the commission has also proposed that the commission should be able to submit a proposal to the council for a regulation on the establishment of a european fisheries control agency (efca). as you know, since 2006 there has been a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna which is due to end in 2022 and fishermen have made a huge effort to adjust their respective catches to the reduced catch volume, complying with the strict conditions set out in the plan. as a result, bluefin tuna biomass showed a very positive trend in 2008 and in 2014 the regional organisation decided to increase the initial catch volume until 2017, as there is sound scientific evidence that the stocks are at a healthy level of abundance. in my view, the spectacular recovery in bluefin tuna stocks in recent years could justify a decision by iccat to increase these volumes even further, and we have asked for this. it is difficult to explain to fishermen who are fishing for bluefin tuna in a completely sustainable way - as is clearly the case in the canary islands, for example - that within 24 hours of the fishery opening they have to withdraw because the quotas are completely exhausted. the legislative initiative we are discussing today is designed to ensure that this plan is uniformly and effectively implemented throughout the european union. the proposal contains technical measures, such as those relating to live transfer and caging operations of bluefin tuna, including also measures relating to the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate bluefin tuna quantities and releases, catch reporting requirements and the implementation of the iccat regional observer programme. the commission proposal generally transposes the relevant recommendations of the icao correctly and we believe that in certain cases it goes a little further than what was decided by this body. i would like to remind you that the aim of the transposition of the icao recommendations is their uniform application throughout the european union. it is not therefore intended to start a new debate on what has already been decided. the uniform application aims to ensure a level playing field for all operators involved in the tuna fishery, including, in particular, operators from third countries. otherwise, if different rules are applied to foreign fleets, all the efforts made and all the restrictions applied to european union fishermen will have been in vain. on the other hand, and this is a very important point, the commission proposes to transpose future amendments to the present recovery plan by means of delegated acts, and here we are in total disagreement. we believe that the transposition of these recommendations should remain a shared competence between the european parliament and the council under the ordinary procedure and that they should therefore be adopted in codecision. i have always asked this parliament to have that codecision and not to violate or use practices to try to circumvent parliament's intervention. finally, we welcome the fact that the iccat recommendations take account of the specific characteristics of the different tuna fishing gear. in this context, the role of artisanal fishing gear - such as those used in the canary islands or traditional fishing gear - in the conservation of stocks should be underlined. that is why we place particular emphasis in this report on this allocation of quotas and on paying particular attention to traditional activities. i would like to thank all those members who have taken part in the amendment process to improve this report and i hope that we will finally have a document that is satisfactory to all.

the next item is the debate on the report by barbara matera, on behalf of the committee on women's rights and gender equality, on external factors that constitute obstacles to entrepreneurship for european women (2015/2111 (ini)) (a8-0369/2015)
mr president, i would like to thank mrs matera for the work she has done and i would like to say that entrepreneurship, self-employment and the activities of the so-called selfemployed women are another aspect of economic activity marked by inequality. women find these options less attractive than men, develop them under worse financing conditions and, in general, in sectors with less added value. they also have to overcome more conciliation and personal problems, so that the contribution of women in this field does not take advantage of all the existing potentialities and we lose talent and opportunities. so we need objective data to enable better diagnoses, specific policies in education, funding, reconciliation and guidance, to tackle the most obvious problems and to continue to fight stereotypes. the first is to think that inequality only hurts us women. and that is the first mistake, because with inequality, commissioner, we all lose. i therefore expect us to act accordingly.
member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to start by thanking ms matera for the work that she has done with this report. as we have heard, and as we know, it is smes which will be the engine for job creation in europe, and to unlock the full potential of our economy we need to unlock the creativity and entrepreneurial potential of our whole workforce of women and men – and yet we know that entrepreneurship is less popular among women than men. sixty-three percent of women say that it has never crossed their mind to start a business, compared to 52% for men, and as we heard, among the key barriers that hinder women there are stereotypes, sometimes lack of confidence, and difficulties in accessing finance and business networks. that is why the role of education is so important and why it makes sense for member states to include entrepreneurial learning at all levels of education. studies show that women are different not only in the motivations that drive them into business but also in the way that they manage an enterprise. in particular, women take more calculated business risks than men, and usually, of course, such economic behaviour leads to a lower rate of failure and to more sustainable enterprises. yet despite that, women find problems in getting hold of the financing that they need. one way forward could be specific programmes for investors to understand women’s entrepreneurship, and also the use of role models has been shown to produce great results, especially when it is linked to tailor-made mentoring and support services. to encourage women to enter the entrepreneurial world, the commission has already taken a number of steps, such as the european network of female entrepreneurship ambassadors and the creation of a network of mentors. but we want to do more, so this year we will launch an online platform for women of all ages who want to start, run and grow a business. the platform will provide training, mentoring, advice and business networking opportunities for women. it is meant to be a one-stop shop for female entrepreneurs. it will enable them to get in touch with other organisations, to enter into existing networks and to find information on funding. thanks to a pilot project from parliament, we also want to increase access to alternative sources of funding by creating a network of women business angels. in addition, as we have heard, women can play an important role in social entrepreneurship, and the commission, via its expert group on social entrepreneurship, is working with interested parties to improve the situation of social enterprises in europe. finally we all know that, to support female entrepreneurs, we need to create an environment within which they can make the most of their potential. that is why we work together with member states to ensure that issues like childcare and facilities for care of the elderly are addressed across europe. europe needs all of its talent, and i can assure you that the commission will continue to work hard to promote and support female entrepreneurship and that this report from parliament will help guide us in that task.

in writing. to recover growth and achieve a high level of employment, the eu needs more entrepreneurs and, above all, more female entrepreneurs, because the differences between men and women are enormous: women account for only 31% of all employees in the eu. the two main obstacles faced by women entrepreneurs are the difficulty of reconciling family and working life and the problems of access to finance, which in some cases involve gender discrimination and often follow from sexist stereotypes that consider leadership as an exclusively male quality. once again we must stress the importance of more and better conciliation policies to facilitate the integration of women into the world of work. it is also essential to facilitate and simplify access to finance. it is also necessary to create european networks for women entrepreneurs, to exchange best practices and to promote an entrepreneurial culture in education and training that fights against gender stereotypes and encourages women to choose careers in science, new technologies and finance.
the next item is the debate on the report by mr marek plura, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on skills policies to combat youth unemployment (2015/2088 (ini)) (a8-0366/2015)
member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to start by thanking mr plura for his report. as we have heard, youth unemployment is obviously one of the biggest challenges that we face in europe, and if we are going to fight it effectively, we clearly need to get better at matching young people’s skills to what employers need. the commission agrees that better cooperation – better partnership, as was said – between businesses, between education and training providers and local authorities, could help make skills training more relevant to what employers actually need. and with that in mind, increasing apprenticeships and workplace training is key. high-quality traineeships can help smooth the transition from education to employment, and we need to find ways that, for skills acquired outside traditional education, for example through volunteering or on-line learning, can themselves be better recognised. the youth guarantee remains a priority for the commission, and the commission will report on its implementation in october, and this will include an assessment of how well member states have met the requirements of a quality framework for traineeships. to help member states speed up the fight against youth unemployment, the commission has proposed to increase the pre-financing for the youth employment initiative from 1%-15% to 30%, and this was quickly accepted by the council and parliament and represents an advance payment to member states of around eur 1 billion. other concerns set out in the report include the importance of promoting equal opportunities, of entrepreneurship and flexibility in education and training provision. these are all areas and concerns that the commission shares, and work here is in progress. last year we set priorities to improve cooperation on vocational education and training, and in the education and training 2020 framework. in november the commission launched a cooperation initiative with businesses and other interested parties on a pact for youth. with business help, over the next two years this pact will deliver 10 000 business education partnerships and 100 000 new opportunities for young people: entry-level jobs, mr president, the fraud committed by the volkswagen company in rigging hundreds of thousands of vehicles to falsify their pollution figures is probably the biggest fraud in the history of the european union. it is a monstrous attack on the environment and public health. it's a scam for buyers, who thought they were buying a model vehicle. and it's a big scam against public administrations. fifty thousand of these rigged cars were sold in spain alone, and since they were supposed to be clean vehicles, they were exempt from various taxes. the amount lost by the administration has not yet been determined, but it will be in the billions. volkswagen has received eur 300 million in direct public aid for its two plants in navarre and catalonia. money from citizens, suffering cuts in essential services, for a fraudulent company. the committee of inquiry of this parliament must go to the bottom of the matter and demand accountability. it is no use apologising, because our credibility with the public is at stake.
mr president, tomorrow, tuesday 19 january, the trial against photojournalist raúl capín will begin in madrid. the prosecution is asking for two years in prison. clearly we are facing a persecution, a criminalization that is part of a strategy that the spanish state is following against media and journalists who are critical. the same repression that social activists and trade unionists are suffering; it is an attack on the right to information and freedom of the press that adds to the attacks on freedom of demonstration and expression that we are experiencing, with the "gag law" as the maximum exponent. raúl capín is being tried because, with his photos, he has brought to light the police repression that has been experienced in the spanish state in recent years. a brutal crackdown that has tried to silence protests and demonstrations against unjust and cruel policies. raúl capín is being judged because he has published photos like these (the speaker shows several photos). because reporting is not a crime, because without photographers you can't see it, we demand an end to repression and an end to the persecution of those who denounce this repression.
mr president, i wanted to draw the attention of this house to the terrible fires which ravaged northern spain in december and, above all, my constituency, asturias. more than 453 fires, most of them caused on the night of 19 to 20 december there were 150 active fires in the territory of asturias, which had a great effect on the whole region. i was able to see from the ground, during my visit to the municipality of el franco, the situation after the end of those fires, but i do not want to focus on el franco, because the east, the west, the centre of asturias, the whole region was ravaged by hundreds of fires - as i say - to a large extent, many of them, caused. the government of the principality of asturias is trying to find ways to compensate the people, the households who have seen their homes, their lands, their livestock destroyed. and i am convinced that the government of the nation, which is responsible for processing that aid from the european union, will do the same. and i, as the european parliament, hope to help in any way i can to at least alleviate to some extent the effects of these terrible fires in asturias.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the spanish authorities unilaterally decided ten days ago to put at risk more than 500 species of birds and fish, as well as the economy of the approximately 60 000 inhabitants of the ebro delta. the late approval of the watershed plans is an affront to the authority of the european commission, which has already warned on several occasions of the repeated problems encountered by the spanish authorities with the implementation of the water framework directive. in view of the approved hydrological plans, we are faced with a case of premeditated re-incidence because despite the commission's warning that the planned ecological flows do not meet the needs of protected areas such as the delta, the government maintains them in the new plans. in our opinion, the commission should act immediately by returning the projects to the spanish authorities. as i said at the beginning, the survival of not only an ecosystem but also the daily lives of 60,000 european citizens is at stake. so we must act now.

mr president, the achievements of the luxembourg presidency have been discussed in this debate, but not enough has been said about the issues that have been dragging their feet and blocked in the council, not only for more than a year, but for several years. this is the case with the proposal for a directive on combating fraud affecting the financial interests of the european union through criminal law, which unfortunately has not been able to be unblocked in the luxembourg presidency. the key issue is the discussion on value added tax, which the council considers to be a matter for the member states, while the commission and the european parliament, above all, consider it to be a major resource of the european union. and this has been confirmed by a recent judgment of the court of justice of the european union, the taricco judgment, handed down in december, which states that fraud against the interests of the union must be prosecuted by the member states through criminal law. this has to have a consequence and impact on the proposal for a directive on the fight against fraud affecting the financial interests of the european union (the 'pif directive') and we therefore urge in this trio dynamic, which now links the dutch presidency, that this proposal for a directive on the protection of the financial interests of the union be unblocked.
mr president, commissioner, a lot has been said and i am going to focus my speech on one aspect which is crucial for the digital economy and therefore for the digital market, which is the big context, the big scale in which this economy can be developed in europe, and that is data. data is essential in the development of the digital economy; the analysis of massive data: the big data. the exchange of data is the fundamental axis, the fundamental pillar, to the point that the profession of data analyst is now the most demanded in the world, according to a study of a few weeks ago by the world economic forum. in this sense, it is necessary to take into account the transport of data: data is transported, circulates, arrives via networks; networks that are the infrastructure of the digital economy. transport used to be by road, it was by air, it was by sea. in the digital economy, transport is carried out by means of networks based on radio spectrum and priority must be given to the development of mobile networks through pro-innovation, pro-investment policies in a context of competitive markets.
mr president, digitalisation has flooded everything and europe must exploit the full potential of the digital society. we need to promote the portability of services and content and remove unjustified geoblocking online, as we have done with the elimination of 'roaming'. we need to plan uses and allocate spectrum bands without delay. we need to push industry 4.0 or the internet of things and create a secure and reliable network. we must help our smes to make the most of digitalisation and we must protect and promote our creators and our cultural production, without which we cannot speak of europe itself. we therefore have a chance. and europe cannot afford to let it go.
in writing. electronic commerce is worth billions of euros a year. and it will continue to grow in a global market without borders. except in the canary islands, where imports and exports are subject to the payment of the single administrative customs document. this tax increases the final amount of the product purchased online by up to 40%, thus restricting electronic commerce in the archipelago. only 27% of the canarian population bought online in 2013, compared to 37% of the spanish average and 50% of the european average. as a consequence, many companies have decided not to sell through the network in the canary islands, despite the fact that european and spanish legislation requires that any company trading within the eu do so throughout the national territory. measures are therefore needed to remove the existing obstacles to electronic commerce in the canary islands so that the same conditions apply to the movement of goods as in the other member states. the outermost regions cannot be a barrier to competitiveness and are crucial to achieving a true digital single market.
in writing. the expansion of large shopping centres had a devastating effect on local production and on small and medium-sized businesses, leading to the destruction of thousands of jobs. the european digital single market is now a major objective for us as an instrument to promote competitiveness and create jobs in the european union. we know from experience that the competitiveness proposed by the european union is totally incompatible with employment and labour rights. this proposal is designed to encourage ultra-consumerism by making available to consumers the products of the large companies which will be the ones with the capacity to do business. it is totally irresponsible for the commission and the council to continue to pursue proposals of this kind and it is a travesty for them to present themselves as job creators when what they are doing is destroying jobs. it is concealed that the jobs that can be created by this type of trade for large companies and large multinationals are always much less than those that are destroyed in small and mediumsized enterprises, in trade and in local production.

mr president, it is a little difficult to speak here, with so much noise and so little respect for the people who have to intervene at this moment, but what i wanted to stress, although the adoption of this report has been delayed, is that the bluefin tuna stocks have improved considerably and that, however, the quota will not do so in the same way, because it seems that the work that fishermen do at sea every day is not important to many of the people who vote and decide here the future of everyone. that, not to mention the distribution of quotas that the popular party does in the state after the quota for fishermen arrives. because if we talk about bluefin tuna today, we could also talk about the fence or we could talk about other fisheries that are drowning every day, like longliners. it is not honest to pat oneself on the back with its fisheries policy and, moreover, i think the word 'sovereignty' is too big for those who approve this type of measures against and behind the back of the general public. we found in this report that there was no position that valued the socioeconomic weight of fishermen and, moreover, we found it shameful precisely because of this. the report will now be studied further and we are pleased, but we will continue to fight for the red tuna fishermen of the mediterranean, the canary islands and the atlantic to recover a share which is their rightful share.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it proposes a strategy for the recovery of bluefin tuna involving the fishing communities that depend on the exploitation of this fishery resource. many towns in southern europe have historically been involved in the exploitation of tuna, and they are the main stakeholders in the recovery of their population. in this connection, the report makes several specific references to the art of the almadraba and the need to protect it in the context of conservation plans and the allocation of quotas for this species, favouring these traditional arts rather than industrial exploitation which is much more damaging to the populations and which is not linked to any territory. the absolute need to restore this important species and the need to do so with the communities that live off it is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ although there was no vote, we would vote for little more than the transposition into european law of the bluefin tuna management plan produced by iccat. we do not agree with the quotas that are being allocated and we believe that the states can put pressure on the commission and the council to have the eu's position in the iccat be to propose the highest possible quota depending on the state of the tuna stock, given that our fishing fleets are in a critical socioeconomic situation.
in writing. ‒ in order to ensure its uniform and effective application throughout the eu, this proposal aims to incorporate into the union's legal order the latest measures, adopted between 2012 and 2014, corresponding to the bluefin tuna recovery plan adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccaa). while the commission has correctly transposed the icao recommendations in most cases, it has sometimes gone beyond what was decided by the icao and what is provided for in union legislation, and it has not been possible to penalise eu operators by means of stricter measures than those agreed. the socialist amendment calling for a quota system for bluefin tuna that is fair to small-scale fishing would be incorporated into the report. the absence of the european parliament from international negotiations is also discussed. in short, i support the initiative to revise the current rules in this area, which were obsolete in relation to the iccat recommendations of recent years, while solving some technical deficiencies, and which was therefore dealt with with by broad consensus in the committee on fisheries of the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, considering that the european union is responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas. a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna was adopted in 2006 and will end in 2022. however, the spectacular recovery of bluefin tuna stocks in recent years could justify a decision to advance to 2016 the total allowable catch for 2017 (23 155 tonnes), which would still be well below the tac in force before the entry into force of the recovery plan. we must continue to work towards the sustainability of fisheries resources while ensuring that an important economic activity such as fishing is maintained, without forgetting other players in the sector who need detailed attention.
in writing. ‒ this project is about transposing the iccat (international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas) convention. the european commission, wanting to act very quickly, has asked for the possibility of adopting delegated acts, but the rapporteur rightly defends the codecision procedure in order to safeguard the prerogatives of the european parliament. some problems are not solved by this plan: there is a great deal of waste, for example, through the technique of sending boats to feed tuna with mackerel. similarly, only a few tuna fishermen benefit from the stocks; the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem. the allocation of quotas is still unfavourable, particularly in the mediterranean. on this point, however, i note that an amendment in favour of rebalancing the quotas in favour of small-scale fishing, similar to an amendment which i myself tabled in committee, was adopted. the european commission and the members of the committee on fisheries want to protect traditional fishing methods for bluefin tuna, such as madrague. these fishing methods are very selective and therefore respectful of the environment. they should benefit from a special favourable scheme.
in writing. ‒ ‒ although there was no vote, we would vote for little more than the transposition into european law of the bluefin tuna management plan produced by iccat. we do not agree with the quotas that are being allocated and we believe that the states can put pressure on the commission and the council to have the eu's position in the iccat be to propose the highest possible quota depending on the state of the tuna stock, given that our fishing fleets are in a critical socioeconomic situation.
in writing. ‒ this report is of some importance as bluefin tuna is the most important species regulated by the iccat (international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas). in this context, it should be noted that in 2006 the iccat adopted a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna which will end in 2022. in order to replenish the stock, the plan provides for a progressive reduction in the level of the total allowable catch. the fishermen have made a huge effort which has resulted in a spectacular recovery in the bluefin tuna population. for the same reason, an increase in the volume of catches would be justified. in 2014, the regional organisation decided to increase the level of the total allowable catch by 20% for the following three years. it is considered necessary to ensure uniform implementation by the eu as a whole. if different rules were applied to foreign fleets, all the efforts made and the restrictions imposed on fishermen would have been in vain. on the basis of the events since 2006, i consider it necessary to approve this report, which will benefit fishermen for the efforts they have made in the past.

in writing. ‒ as we know, spain is a country with a long tradition of fishing and consuming bluefin tuna. however, in view of the alarming decline of this species in recent years, it was decided to control its catch by setting fishing quota limits throughout the eu. in view of the success of these multiannual plans for bluefin tuna, which have resulted in the species having grown much more than expected, i think it is entirely legitimate to ask for an increase in the quota limit for this species and i fully support this report. i also strongly agree with the need for the eu to promote a plan to standardise the conditions in all member states in this respect and, in particular, those outside the european union. otherwise, all our efforts would have been in vain. finally, i would also like to see the different fishing methods taken into account, with particular attention to the traditional practices used in the fishing fleets or in the canary islands, which have always been sustainable and have certainly been adversely affected by the restrictions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on competition policy because it has succeeded in including key objectives for the socialist and democratic group, such as calling on the commission to take a more belligerent stance against social dumping in the labour market (paragraph 5), that services of general economic interest be excluded from the competition rules (paragraph 46), that the problem of the fragmentation of the eu digital market be addressed (paragraphs 55 to 59 and 79), that the commission maintain a priority approach in relation to tax evasion or illegal corporate tax practices (paragraphs 62, 68 to 89) and, finally, that parliament be able to co-decide in the latter field (paragraph 110). useful references have also been made in the report to the need to incorporate flexibility in the enforcement of competition rules for the outermost and island regions. the report also includes, on a proposal from mr fernández and mr jáuregui, a reference to the need to regulate the fees charged by atms, since this is the price of a service whose market value is difficult to determine, which is very relevant for spain at the moment.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, despite its very positive aspects, it continues to develop the neoliberal conception of the economy which sees the market as the main actor in the european economy. this report has included many amendments tabled by my group and other aspects of central importance for the european economy: from support for decisions to punish multinational companies for tax evasion, to the crisis caused by the end of milk quotas or the investigation of the connections between certain former governors and the large electricity companies. however, it does not recognise that services of general economic interest must be provided by the state, and calls for the internationalisation of public procurement and the whole of the european economy in clear reference to the atci. that is why, despite the important positive aspects, i could not vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, despite its very positive aspects, it continues to develop the neoliberal conception of the economy which sees the market as the main actor in the european economy. this report has included many amendments tabled by my group and other aspects of central importance for the european economy: from support for decisions to punish multinational companies for tax evasion, to the crisis caused by the end of milk quotas or the investigation of the connections between certain former governors and the large electricity companies. however, it does not recognise that services of general economic interest must be provided by the state, and calls for the internationalisation of public procurement and the whole of the european economy in clear reference to the atci. that is why, despite the important positive aspects, i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it is based on the need to guarantee the internal market and is based on an open market economy with free competition. it is necessary to give parliament powers in relation to competition law, since the commission cannot be both responsible for establishing the legal framework in the form of guidelines and then be responsible for enforcing its own guidelines. the commission should also incorporate new criteria for the digital economy. unfair tax competition between member states is another source of concern, as it distorts the internal market of the union to a great extent and we must therefore work towards its elimination. similarly, we must investigate the presence of ex-politicians on the boards of directors of the large energy companies, something that causes great rejection in our society.

in writing. ‒ i abstained from voting on the european parliament's annual report on competition policy. it maintains a globally neoliberal view of competition policy, focused on the single market and with hardly any specific references to the various economic sectors. while it devotes considerable attention to the taxation issue, it does not propose any coercive measures to combat tax evasion or avoidance. some amendments tabled by my group were nevertheless included, such as those concerning abuses in the distribution of food or downward social competition. i do not think the report is very negative, but we still do not share the general approach.

in writing. ‒ as we know, on the basis of the tfeu, our internal market is based on an open market economy with free competition. the fundamental objective of eu competition law is to protect the eu from market-damaging commercial activities. for this reason, it is essential to achieve effective competition as a condition for finally enjoying a free and dynamic internal market. to achieve this, coordinated efforts are needed from the commission, through the competition commissioner, the european parliament and the member states. one of the demands made in the report is that the commission should be obliged to give an oral and written opinion on specific proposals which parliament approves by a large majority, and not just through the annual report which it already produces. i think this report is very important because its approval is essential to prohibit agreements between undertakings which are contrary to free competition and which adversely affect trade between member states.
in writing. ‒ my support for the report on eu competition policy in 2014, in which the european parliament wishes to stress that, thanks to the work done, eu competition policy is able to consolidate its important role in the realisation of the market economy and competition in europe, promoting it at international level, and does not give rise to a myriad of sectoral and national exceptions and uncontrollable exception thresholds. we also point out that, in addition to fines imposed for illegal price fixing, it is important to supplement this work in the future by fines to the managers and directors of the responsible companies, in order to be able to prevent this practice more effectively.

in writing. ‒ all in all, the report is of good quality. although it contains few problematic elements, many green amendments were integrated. on that basis, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ this report addresses key issues in eu competition policy, such as the need to withdraw support for the financial sector during the crisis, the need for competition policy decisions to take into account the social impact of the sector in remote or isolated regions, the need to update the rules on infringements, and the importance of competition policy in the digital economy, a fast-growing area where abuses against european consumers must be prevented. i therefore think it necessary to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ following the terrorist attacks in france and denmark in 2015, the eu member states' education ministers adopted a declaration aimed at promoting the values of freedom and tolerance through education. this report is along the same lines. although the report has been improved by the amendments tabled by my group which reiterate the value of social justice, point to the need to promote cultural diversity especially among young people through culture and the media and promote training in multiculturalism among teachers, i have had to abstain because the text gives religious denominations a representative role which i do not think is compatible with the values of secularism which are essential for the development of individual beliefs in freedom.
in writing. ‒ this report is an attempt to build on the common agreement of the ministers of education, signed in paris on 17 march 2015, on the need to make combined efforts to prevent and combat marginalisation, intolerance, racism and radicalisation, and to preserve a framework of equal opportunities for all. the report identifies both opportunities and challenges and proposes concrete recommendations for action at all levels of government as well as at eu level, especially through education. it includes a broad approach that encourages new reflections on the nature and processes of political violence, starting from the premise that radicalisation is a dynamic relational process and an unforeseen and unpredictable consequence of a series of disturbing events. the gue/ngl group was very impressed with the original report. the amendments tabled by our group were also included in the commitments and approved with them. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the role of intercultural dialogue, cultural diversity and education in promoting the union's fundamental values. i am grateful to the rapporteur for her work in reaching agreement. i want to stress the importance of timely integration and education of segregated communities. i also voted against the reference to the fact that these communities are behaving contrary to the fundamental european values.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this motion for a resolution which calls for strengthening the role of intercultural dialogue, cultural diversity and education as a vehicle for peace and as a tool in conflict resolution by promoting human rights, freedom of thought, mutual respect, integrity, cultural diversity, inclusion and social cohesion. the text stresses that genuine intercultural and interfaith dialogue fosters positive and cooperative interactions, promotes understanding and respect between cultures, fosters diversity and increases respect for democracy, freedom and human rights, as well as tolerance with universal values. it also considers it essential that intercultural dialogue be an eu objective and that investment be made in inclusive, accessible and quality education at all levels, which will enable ethical and civic values to be developed. it also calls for renewed attention to the promotion of an intercultural society based on solidarity, especially among young people. it called on the member states and the commission to prevent extremist tendencies such as xenophobia, racism and all forms of discrimination and marginalization by means of measures to strengthen community cohesion and to successfully counter socioeconomic inequalities.
in writing. ‒ following the terrorist attacks in france and denmark in 2015, eu education ministers adopted a declaration aimed at promoting the values of freedom and tolerance through education. this report is along the same lines. i voted in favour because the report has also been improved by the amendments tabled by my group which reiterate the value of social justice, point to the need to promote cultural diversity, especially among young people, through culture and the media, and promote multicultural training for teachers.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report as it makes specific recommendations for action at both european and national level to promote intercultural dialogue and the use of culture as a tool for peacebuilding, conflict resolution and crisis prevention. i believe it is essential that cultural dialogue and diversity are integrated horizontally in all policy areas, such as child and youth policy, education, mobility, employment and social affairs, home affairs and security, and women's rights and gender equality, and regional development. i therefore welcome the commitment set out in the report to mainstream intercultural dialogue in the eu's external relations, including in the union's development agenda. the promotion and protection of cultural diversity on the international stage can benefit the eu and its member states in their relations with the rest of the world. in conclusion, i support the increased exchange of good practice and the holding of an enhanced intercultural dialogue, as they will undoubtedly help to find solutions to the common challenges facing the eu today.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i am convinced of the importance of working towards a pluralist, non-discriminatory, tolerant and fair society in line with the eu's fundamental values of human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights. achieving such high goals requires a positive approach and it is important to work towards intercultural dialogue and the celebration of cultural diversity. there is no doubt that intercultural education and learning in its various settings is fundamental to ensuring sustainable progress in the field of active citizenship.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution on the role of intercultural dialogue, cultural diversity and education in promoting the fundamental values of the european union is typical of the totalitarian ways of the european union. it is a very clear call to politicise the sports, associative and educational circles, while inviting member states to legislate to punish behaviour which appears to be contrary to the spirit of the resolution. by targeting, without saying so and using allusions, patriots and sovereignists concerned about the identity and sovereignty of their nations, the resolution seeks to close any political debate on immigration, integration and multiculturalism. for these reasons, and to denounce the pernicious nature of this draft resolution, i voted against the report.

in writing. ‒ this report is the result of the current situation in which, unfortunately, the notions of identity and eu membership are being questioned or redefined. this is why the member states must commit themselves to actions that strengthen the role of intercultural dialogue in education. among other things, this report aims to prevent and combat marginalization, intolerance, racism and radicalisation, and to preserve a framework of equal opportunities for all. intercultural dialogue should be seen as a positive two-way process that benefits both parties by allowing them to put themselves in the other's shoes. today we can find several examples of these eu-funded cultural exchange practices, one of them being the erasmus+ programme, for example. we also need to develop inclusive learning in which differentiated approaches are implemented to respond to specific community needs. finally, i consider the adoption of this report to be of great importance because it presents measures which will contribute to building a strong and coherent europe. to make this possible we need cooperation in policies at european, national and local level.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report as it calls on the commission to study the impact of the financial market legislation adopted in recent years and to encourage the creation of a capital markets union which should help to improve the channelling of liquidity into the economy. thanks to the work of our group, this report does not call into question the view that sovereign debt is a risk-free asset. however, we still do not have a risk-free pan-european financial asset, which would be solved by the issuance of public debt of the union. the hypothetical issuance of union bonds is not contrary to article 310 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. i therefore call on the european commission to take advantage of the ultra-low interest rates to create a european treasury. i also welcome the inclusion in this report of amendments from the delegation concerning the need to incorporate the consumer and small investor perspective in the capital markets union and the non-discrimination for having an iban code other than the issuer of the receipt.
in writing. ‒ i voted against because it implies the implicit ratification by the european parliament of the european commission's proposal on the capital markets union. this proposal, put forward by mr juncker as the solution to the problems of access to credit and financing in the european economy, is merely a strategy to introduce speculative capital into the direct financing of small and mediumsized enterprises. this proposal is absolutely contrary to the interests of europe's smes, which need to be guaranteed credit through the traditional banking system and not through increasingly complex mechanisms that leave all risk in the hands of small entrepreneurs, who will now have to become shareholders in their own companies. this absurd proposal will cause more problems for small businesses than it is intended to solve, as it is designed to serve the interests of big business. that is why i voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which is intended to assess the eu's legislative work on financial services, in order to address the shortcomings identified. financial stability and consumer protection should remain the eu's priorities in this area, while taking into account the interdependencies with international standards.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it asks the commission to study the impact of the financial market legislation adopted in recent years, and to encourage the creation of a capital markets union which should help to improve the channelling of liquidity into the economy. thanks to the work of the socialist group, this report does not call into question the view that sovereign debt is a risk-free asset. however, we still do not have a risk-free pan-european financial asset, which would be solved by the issuance of public debt of the union. the hypothetical issuance of union bonds is not contrary to article 310 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. we therefore call on the european commission to take advantage of the ultra-low interest rates to create a european treasury. finally, the spanish socialists have managed to include amendments concerning the need to incorporate the consumer and small investor perspective into the capital markets union, and non-discrimination for having an iban code different from that of the issuer of the receipt.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report as it calls on the commission to study the impact of the financial market legislation adopted in recent years and to encourage the creation of a capital markets union which should help to improve the channelling of liquidity into the economy. thanks to the work of our group, this report does not call into question the view that sovereign debt is a risk-free asset. however, we still do not have a risk-free pan-european financial asset, which would be solved by the issuance of public debt of the union. the hypothetical issuance of union bonds is not contrary to article 310 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. i therefore call on the european commission to take advantage of the ultra-low interest rates to create a european treasury. i also welcome the inclusion in this report of amendments from the delegation concerning the need to incorporate the consumer and small investor perspective in the capital markets union and the non-discrimination for having an iban code other than the issuer of the receipt.
in writing. ‒ the balz report addresses the challenges of financial regulation since the 2008 crisis. it repeatedly raises concerns about the increasing complexity of regulation and suggests some interesting ideas, such as the creation of a european public rating agency for sovereign debt. other proposals, which are initially positive, are for the moment the responsibility of the profession of faith: this is the case, for example, of access for smes to the financial markets, which would nevertheless have the advantage of complementing and competing with bank financing. however, other recommendations in the report are not supported by us, such as the break between the states and the banks at national level, with the aim of limiting the risks linked to sovereign debts. we are also wary of the revival of securitisation, since it was partly due to poorly managed securitisation that the 2008 crisis was triggered. finally, the report omits the need to separate deposit banks from commercial banks, a measure which would increase the security of the banking system.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this own-initiative report which reviews the various european legislative acts on financial services that have taken place in the previous mandate, trying to assess achievements and problems. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european parliament. the report welcomes projects such as the juncker plan and the capital markets union, and is overly positive about the legislative achievements of the previous legislature.

in writing. ‒ in the wake of the financial and debt crisis that erupted in 2007, the eu has taken a number of initiatives in the area of financial services to restore financial stability and strengthen consumer protection, among other purposes. the report aims to assess this legislative work in order to apply the lessons learned during the crisis and to establish less complex financial services legislation. it also stressed the importance of coordination, time-scale planning and transparency in the legislative process in order to achieve consistent and high-quality regulation of financial services. among other challenges, it establishes the obligation for european legislators to take into account interdependencies with international standards to avoid contradictions. i think this report will be very helpful in correcting any mistakes made in the past or not dealt with properly and using them as a reference for the future.
in writing. ‒ the legislative changes that had to be made, often in an urgent manner, following the financial and debt crisis from 2007 onwards, were in many cases decisive in dealing with very complicated situations. the time has come, however, to review those acts with a view to articulating a framework for financial regulation and a more efficient capital markets union in the eu. i support the report by mr balz, which points to the need for a detailed assessment of the impact of the financial services framework and for that assessment to be regularly followed up. work should be done to ensure that financial stability and consumer protection remain the priorities of policymakers, with greater emphasis on the application of a coherent risk-based approach.

in writing. ‒ i voted against because it implies the implicit ratification by the european parliament of the european commission's proposal on the capital markets union. this proposal, put forward by mr juncker as the solution to the problems of access to credit and financing in the european economy, is merely a strategy to introduce speculative capital into the direct financing of small and mediumsized enterprises. this proposal is absolutely contrary to the interests of europe's smes, which need to be guaranteed credit through the traditional banking system and not through increasingly complex mechanisms that leave all risk in the hands of small entrepreneurs, who will now have to become shareholders in their own companies. this absurd proposal will cause more problems for small businesses than it is intended to solve, as it is designed to serve the interests of big business. that is why i voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ before making a big leap forward with the capital markets union, it is fundamental that we are able to assert where exactly is europe in terms of financial markets legislation. i hope that this report is useful in this regard and enables the commission to take a broad view on the current state of play and build a cmu that further diversifies and integrates our financial markets.

in writing. ‒ following the financial crisis, several legislative texts have been adopted within the union framework. the report notes that financial stability and consumer protection remain the top priorities of policymakers. it also identifies the competitiveness of european legislation and the financial sectors in the union as a key challenge in the regulation of financial services and calls on the european commission services to complete the first assessment in this regard before 2016, with the aim of having a comprehensive review of the state of financial services. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of this report.

i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, women are not a pawn in society, nor do we submissively wait to be told, let alone in a society ruled by the great economic powers to the detriment of the citizenry, what we should do. women, like men, have the right to decide about our future, whether we want to be entrepreneurs or wage earners, mothers or not, married or single. entrepreneurship is a job option like any other, but it is by no means the magic solution to solving the family reconciliation and the inequality of rights and opportunities that we women suffer. the european union must promote policies that eliminate inequality and the wage gap; that genuinely facilitate family reconciliation by building a network of public services, by helping women to develop their full human and work potential, whatever they want to do, and not through incentives to cover economic sectors, as the economy is interested in at the moment. the austerity policies implemented in recent years by the union and many of its member states have severely punished the living conditions of many citizens and women bear the brunt of the burden in the family, at work and in poverty rates. it is time to abandon once and for all the idea that women, through their effort, dedication and submission, are the wild card that serves to patch up this economically and socially unjust society and that only brings us the growth of inequality in society, and we are seeing it every day. so, female entrepreneurship, yes; and help for whoever wants it and all the necessary support, too; but exploitation of women, no. that is why our group abstained.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to address the existing concern about the barriers to self-employment for women, given that only 34.4% of self-employed people are women. however, while the report highlights the importance of the commission collecting data to assess the causes, or mentions the importance of work-life balance 'reiterating once again the need to improve the current maternity leave directive', the report takes a strongly paternalistic approach by highlighting stereotypes and focusing on the glorification of entrepreneurship as a way of combating discrimination and inequality towards women without addressing structural reasons such as symbolic violence, the unequal impact of austerity policies or the destruction of employment and public services. i have therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it identifies in a precise and clear way the main obstacles to the achievement of entrepreneurship by european women. the work-life balance that entrepreneurship can offer women also represents, however, the first hurdle, as it can put women in a vicious circle in which women have fewer opportunities to gain management experience to run their businesses, build their credit history and gain the trust of investors. i would also like to stress the importance of paragraph 22, which mentions the empirically refuted criterion on the proposal to the commission to introduce gender quotas in all types of specific aid for underrepresented and disadvantaged groups, in order to ensure that progress is made towards business parity.
in writing. ‒ this report indicates that the rate of female entrepreneurship is lagging behind in many member states and that there is indeed untapped potential for growth and prosperity. the report calls for concrete strategies to be put in place to exploit fully the potential of women as entrepreneurs. although the focus is mainly on the private sector and entrepreneurship, positive references to the fight against gender stereotypes and a call for member states to achieve the barcelona objectives can be recognised. while there are many obstacles to women entrepreneurs, this report takes the approach that encouraging entrepreneurship among women is key to achieving gender equality, something not shared by a progressive feminist perspective. references to the important role of the public sector and the negative effects of the austerity policies of recent years are completely absent. i am afraid that this report could be used to legitimize measures to increase women's entrepreneurship as the only solution to improve women's living conditions by giving more weight to the financial and private sectors, so i abstained.
in writing. ‒ this report provides a detailed analysis of the different factors that hamper women's entrepreneurship in the european union. although entrepreneurship has been a political priority since the adoption of the lisbon treaty, the european union is still significantly behind: in 2009, the rate of entrepreneurship in the eu-27 was 12%, compared to 27% and 21% in china and the united states respectively. in this regard, female entrepreneurship deserves particular attention, as economic independence is not yet guaranteed in the eu, and the female employment rate, at 59,6% in 2014 in the union, is below the employment target of 75% defined in the europe 2020 strategy. the two main obstacles faced by women entrepreneurs are the difficulty of reconciling family and working life, and the problems of access to finance, which in some cases involve discrimination on grounds of gender. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the female employment rate is below the eu employment line. this is why attention should be paid to the financing needs of women entrepreneurs, to the particularities of women social entrepreneurs and to addressing issues such as indirect discrimination faced by women at the beginning of their business creation, taking into account the obstacles to female entrepreneurship. the european institutions must also encourage women's entrepreneurship, given that europe needs more entrepreneurs to expand and create new jobs. the european union must offer women the opportunity for greater integration into labour markets, as well as the opportunity to strengthen their role as business leaders, fostering a cultural change within and outside their companies that will serve as an example to girls and young people.
in writing. i voted in favour of this very good report, in which my colleague barbara matera has taken the care to reflect a precise analysis of the obstacles to european women's entrepreneurship, taking into account indirect and direct factors. the emphasis on gender stereotypes, both as barriers to women's internalization and as barriers to access to finance, is particularly relevant and the report offers interesting solutions at european, national and regional levels. awareness-raising among investors and financial circles more generally is an important priority. i also welcome the special attention paid to entrepreneurship in the new information and communication technologies sector. to encourage and support female entrepreneurship in this sector, efforts to reduce the impact of gender stereotypes must be doubly important. finally, the report also has the merit of recalling that it is possible to mobilise the european structural funds to help reconcile work and private life, which is also an underlying element that determines women's participation in the labour market and even more so in entrepreneurship.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, bearing in mind that the european union is still lagging behind in terms of entrepreneurship, as the rate of entrepreneurship in the eu-27 is significantly lower than that of other global players. to strengthen europe's recovery and create quality jobs, the european union needs more entrepreneurs. in this context, female entrepreneurship is particularly important, as the female employment rate is below the 75% employment target defined in the europe 2020 strategy and the male employment rate. the work-life balance that entrepreneurship can offer women also represents, however, the first hurdle, as it can put women in a vicious circle where they have fewer opportunities to gain management experience to run their businesses, build their credit history and gain the trust of investors. we must therefore work tirelessly within the eu institutions to promote european women's entrepreneurship and to remove the obstacles to their progress.

in writing. ‒ i believe that one of the major challenges for the european union remains gender equality in all areas, and particularly in the workplace. there are still clear differences between the employment rates of men and women. these differences are reflected in eurostat statistics, which show that in the eu 70.1% of men are in the labour force, compared with 59.6% of women. on the other hand, it has also been shown that those countries with a higher diversity and equality rate in enterprises are, in many cases, those that have achieved higher levels of economic well-being and social cohesion. in view of these statements and the high level of academic preparation and experience of a large percentage of women, i consider it absolutely necessary to close the gap in employment opportunities between men and women. i therefore strongly support this report and consider it essential to promote all the necessary action to support women entrepreneurs.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it gives a good picture of the youth unemployment problem in the eu member states, the solutions to tackle it are far from adequate in my view. instead of promoting the creation of public, stable and quality employment for young people, it proposes to encourage entrepreneurship and to focus training on market needs. that is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to identify the reasons for the structural obstacles young people face in finding employment and to propose solutions. while most of the content of the final report is positive, calling for more support for young people in skills development and employment, including increased public investment in education and more specifically in the school-to-work transition, these aspects in the report are mere statements of intent, and the real impact on policy will be limited. the report overemphasizes the role of entrepreneurship as a solution to reducing youth unemployment. the continuous references to the need to 'better match skills to labour market needs' and the call for closer links between education and vocational training institutions and enterprises to promote this match between skills and labour market distort the content in our view. that is why, although i cannot support the neoliberal approach to the text, i abstained from voting on the report in order not to block important progress and positive aspects of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on skills policies to combat youth unemployment. individual skills development and the dissemination of knowledge and skills are one of the key elements of integrated social and employment policies and can allow long-term growth, european competitiveness, the fight against unemployment and the building of a more inclusive european society, provided that skills development policies recognise the multiple dimensions of the needs and skills of unemployed young people.
in writing. ‒ after many years of crisis, europe has not been able to put a stop to the drama of youth unemployment. despite the fact that the union institutions have launched initiatives such as the youth guarantee and the youth employment initiative, it is urgent to tackle this tragedy from all angles in order not to frustrate the opportunities of a whole generation of young europeans. active employment policies certainly have a role to play in helping to solve this problem. as this report points out, the learning, acquisition and recognition of skills and competences by young people, whether they are studying, working, unemployed or inactive, plays a key role both in facing a faster and more stable integration into the labour market and in improving study-to-work transition pathways and the quality of jobs and careers that the younger generations of our society will develop. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ while there are 24 million unemployed people in europe, of whom 7.5 million are young people who are neither working nor studying, there are also around two million job vacancies in the eu. in addition, there are many skilled and unemployed young people whose skills do not match the demand for work. to correct these mismatches, strong partnerships need to be built between education, employment and services authorities, the social partners and the business community to support the development of action plans and strategies for quality employment. the report stresses the need for education systems to be more flexible and to provide knowledge and skills at all stages of the career to meet the needs of the labour market and the level of youth unemployment. it also stresses the creation of businesses and self-employment as an opportunity to participate in the labour market, the importance of traineeships, the need to incorporate new technologies into the learning process, better qualification of public employment agencies and an efficient use of european funds by the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour with the intention of bringing solutions to the alarming level of youth unemployment, with almost 15 million young people out of work. this situation poses a serious threat to the social cohesion and economic development of the eu. more flexible education systems are needed to complement and develop knowledge and skills at all stages of the career to better adapt to a changing labour market. at the same time, it is necessary to link higher education institutions with the economic sector.

in writing. ‒ i support any measure that will help reduce youth unemployment. whereas the micro, small and medium-sized enterprises represent more than 80% of all jobs, it is important to facilitate and simplify the creation of these businesses. it is also necessary to continue improving the education system, to facilitate the mobility of young people in europe, improving the efficiency of public administrations and improving the relationship between training and business.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour as reducing employment policies for young people to skills policies is not enough to combat structural youth unemployment. we need to shift from a debate about labour supply and labour demand and focus on changing economic policies which increase unemployment and inequality. this includes investing in the creation of quality jobs for young people.
in writing. ‒ this is a particularly important issue. youth unemployment is an issue we must combat to ensure opportunities for a generation of young europeans who are currently facing great employment difficulties. the development of the youth employment initiative, support for the creation of small businesses, the promotion of youth entrepreneurship in all sectors, the promotion of training measures for the unemployed young people and coordination between local, national and european authorities through employment offices in order to facilitate the finding of professional opportunities seems vital today. it is necessary to continue to promote actions to help young europeans find career opportunities, especially those aimed at helping those who neither study nor work. this report is intended to identify policies which can help to combat youth unemployment, and i think it is necessary to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it gives a good picture of the youth unemployment problem in the eu member states, the solutions to tackle it are far from adequate in my view. instead of promoting the creation of public, stable and quality employment for young people, it proposes to encourage entrepreneurship and to focus training on market needs. that is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ although the youth unemployment rate has improved over the last year, it remains remarkably high at around 20.7%, according to eurostat data. this high number of young people out of work has a negative impact on both economic growth and productivity and effective measures must be put in place as soon as possible to bring this situation to a halt. among the main risks of youth unemployment are the loss of young people's talents and skills (as they are unable to put them to work), the reduction of output and gdp, and the increase in economic costs, as more investment in social subsidies is needed and there is less money coming from tax payments. i therefore fully support this report, as i am confident in an economic recovery and in the eu's ability to offer young people decent work commensurate with their knowledge and skills.
mr president, i was happy to support this report. i consider the digital single market to be one of the main topics of the european parliament and the commission for this term. if we could get some of the principles, like boosting the online sale of goods and services across borders, to work, then i would be very happy. in short, we have schengen, we have no internal borders between states, but in the area of digital markets we still have borders and these must be broken down. the research that has been done clearly shows that today, for example, companies sell a lot of their goods online within their national states, but across borders, the number is very small. so for the czech republic, where i come from, i can say that 26% of czech smes sell online in the czech republic, but only 7% also sell cross-border. it is therefore clear that the rules need to be adapted to allow cross-border sales within the european union to operate online, and this material is intended to do so. that's why i supported him.
mr president, we abstained on the report on the digital single market because, while we are committed to the decision to adapt the economy to the new digital age, we do not share the eternal mantra that greater competition and a single market are always the solution for the european economy to create sustainable and quality jobs. this report risks favouring large companies more than smes and citizens. we have advocated amendments to make the digital market reflect the society we want today. we must therefore guarantee data protection and go further in defending net neutrality as basic principles for digital equality of citizens. the internet must be a global space for communication, participation and democratic transformation today, as it was in the arab spring. the internet should not just be a new business space.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it represents a clear, progressive and ambitious roadmap to the realisation of a true digital single market, through the removal of barriers to create new online opportunities for citizens and businesses, especially smes. the digital revolution is radically changing europe and has great potential for creating millions of new skilled jobs and new opportunities for consumers. i therefore welcome the fact that this motion for a resolution is promoting legislative and non-legislative measures for the benefit of consumers and to preserve the competitiveness of our social market economy. as a socialist i am particularly pleased with the request we have sent to the commission to give serious consideration to working conditions in the sharing economy and the parcel sector, as we cannot accept low levels of protection for workers. we also ask the commission to assess what consumer protection is required in this area and to ensure that the regulation is adapted to the digital environment. the report also contains powerful text on data protection, culture and media issues, digital skills, infrastructure and investment.
in writing. ‒ the digital agenda is one of the juncker commission's least coherent proposals, a drawer that holds everything from copyright to working time, from digital platforms to industrial automation, from the reform of audiovisual directives to parcel delivery. in this way, its more controversial initiatives are diluted among others subjected to less public scrutiny. our proposals in this area are well known. we will support the commission in its harmonization initiatives which improve the protection of workers, access to cultural production and fair remuneration for authors. on the contrary, we will continue to oppose new digital monopolies, the liberalisation of sectors such as parcel delivery and the deregulation of services by unfair competition from networked companies, whether in transport (such as uber) or in any other area, public or private. the parliament's report contains improvements on the commission's proposals, but its general orientation remains unclear. that is why i have decided to abstain in the final vote.

the conclusions of the last council have caused my group concern and disappointment, a feeling which has been repeated in council after council. and it is not because decisions have not been taken, because agreements have not been made. it has been done on important issues: emigration, terrorism, economic and monetary union. the problem is that when you read the conclusions of the june council, the october council or the informal meetings of september and november, you have to read very carefully to see that they are not the same conclusions. it seems that we are condemned to follow the same sequence over and over again: the commission prepares and proposes, the member states meeting in the council take decisions, and the member states in their countries ignore and fail to implement the decisions they have taken in the council. this is the myth of sisyphus: we are continually returning to the original point. let's talk about the issues: terrorism. the question of information exchange remains unresolved. this morning mr juncker pointed out that we are as we were in 2001 after the attacks in new york. it is true that i welcome the proposal announced this morning by mr juncker to combat the financing of terrorism. if we talk about emigration, the 'hotspots' are not working, relocation is not working and the moral, social and political climate within the union is deteriorating. if we talk about the economy, it is not in the council conclusions, but unemployment remains high, investment continues to fall and inequality continues to grow. so, are we going to settle, like sisyphus, who knew he was doomed to return again and again to the starting point? let us take the example of toynbee, whom you yourself have just quoted: let us avoid our own suicide. if we do not prevent our own suicide, the myth of sisyphus will also be fulfilled in us. we will be unable to move forward and that will be our political death.
