mr president, madam commissioner, the report we are discussing today is intended to assess the first two and a half years of negotiation of the agreement on trade in services, but to make clear recommendations to the commission. we must give the commission the necessary room for manoeuvre to continue negotiations, without giving up on improving european union legislation. we support maintaining the parties' right to regulate and transparency in negotiations. this agreement is of vital importance to the european union. we are the largest exporter of services with 25% of world exports - in 2013 we had a trade surplus of €170 billion in this sector. in addition, exports of services to the european union have doubled in the last ten years. it is important to us that the agreement be as multilateral as possible and that it have the capacity to regulate and manage public services of general interest, the capacity to regulate in favour of the consumer and the guarantee that social and consumer protection standards will not be lowered. and congratulations to mrs reding on the magnificent work she has done.
mr president, i would like to thank you. welcome to the police station. we believe that it is essential to update the global rules of trade. we cannot be regulating the most important part of international trade with pre-internet rules. it is essential to update them and to stop social dumping, to guarantee data privacy, to regulate online trade, roaming and, of course, to obtain reciprocity. because trade must be an instrument at the service of consumers and, of course, also of our businesses. i support this resolution because i think it makes clear what the european parliament's demands are to the commission in order to get the negotiations on the track we think they should go. it is essential to say loud and clear that we demand the total exclusion from all public services, respect for the social and labour rights of workers, data protection, regulation of financial and banking services and, of course, also the right to cultural diversity. i think that the commission - and you as a commissioner who is here in this parliament - must take very much into account the opinion expressed in this resolution. because the commission has the power to negotiate, but in the end parliament has the power to approve or reject an agreement, and we want a good agreement, because we need good acp negotiations, progressive and respectful of people and small businesses.

in writing. the protocol of accession of china to the wto, signed in 2001, does not recognise china as a market economy, allowing the eu and other trading partners to apply anti-dumping and anti-subsidy measures to mitigate state intervention in the costs and prices of products exported by the asian country. the possible granting of market economy status to china in december 2016, arising from the legal effects of the accession protocol, could lead to the disappearance of anti-dumping and anti-subsidy measures on chinese products, with dramatic consequences for industry and employment in europe, especially in sectors such as steel, chemicals, ceramics or mechanical engineering. before taking any decision, the european commission should carry out an in-depth impact assessment looking at the effects of this situation on employment, consumers, investment and the competitiveness of the eu and its smes. the commission has not established that the chinese exporting producers are in a position to export to the union market.

member of the commission.– madam president, first and foremost, i would like to thank my colleague, the rapporteur, mark demesmaeker, for his report on the biodiversity mid-term review. it is an honour for me to contribute to this discussion on the eu’s progress towards achieving its 2020 biodiversity targets. the european parliament’s report, which is being put forward for adoption tomorrow, delivers a strong message about the importance of biodiversity and ecosystem services for human welfare and socio-economic development, but it also delivers a message of concern about protecting this essential natural capital. i believe that this report can help steer and accelerate progress towards the difficult task of achieving our 2020 biodiversity targets. the commission’s biodiversity mid—term review revealed that, while we are mid-term – and here i agree completely with mr demesmaeker – we are not mid-way to achieving our targets. we are continuing to lose biodiversity, and this has very serious implications for our ability to ensure food security, for our quality of life and sustainable socio-economic development, and for mitigating and adapting to climate change and delivering on our international commitments, including the recently-adopted agenda 2030 for sustainable development. without any doubt, the commission will carefully consider parliament’s recommendation for action at eu level. i agree that, in addition to completing the eu policy framework, there needs to be much strengthened implementation on the ground. we need to mobilise the efforts of actors at all levels and across many sectors in order to deliver on our biodiversity commitments. we need, in particular, to fully implement the eu nature legislation, focusing our efforts on completing the natura 2000 network, especially for the marine environment, and on ensuring effective management and financing of natura 2000 sites. the ongoing fitness check of the eu nature legislation provoked the highest ever number of responses – over half a million – to a commission public consultation, demonstrating the level of importance of nature and biodiversity to european citizens. it has also generated a huge amount of evidence. here i would like to stress that the fitness check is an opportunity to consider how we can better ensure that the nature directives, which are key instruments in achieving our biodiversity goals, are both effective and efficient. there are issues about implementation, resources, sharing of knowledge and experience, and also the issue about the engagement of all stakeholders. all these issues deserve our full attention. i would like to inform this parliament that the commission is on track to deliver its conclusions on the fitness check exercise in the spring and to propose follow—up action later this year. yes, the nature directives play a central and critical role in halting biodiversity loss in europe, but they are not enough on their own. we need to do more to effectively protect and restore biodiversity and ecosystem services both within and beyond the natura 2000 network. focusing on the positive economic gains through recognising and accounting for biodiversity will also be key. we must deliver on the broader goals of the eu biodiversity strategy, and this will ultimately depend on society’s commitment to sustainable production and consumption. it is very clear that we need to raise awareness about the value of nature and biodiversity, not only because nature and biodiversity are valuable in themselves and important for citizens, but also because they underpin our well-being and socio-economic development. this must be better understood and integrated into planning and decision—making. our mid—term review particularly highlighted the importance of agriculture and forestry, which together cover no less than 80% of the eu landmass. it also highlighted the importance of marine fisheries development and trade policies. these sectors must therefore be at the heart of any solution to halting biodiversity loss. there are many excellent examples of local improvements as a direct result of good practices, and these carry an important message about the achievability of the 2020 biodiversity targets. i would like to note that the adoption of the eu regulation on invasive alien species was a very significant achievement, and its implementation will enable the launch of targeted measures on the ground. this will go a long way towards tackling one of the main causes of biodiversity loss in the european union. as you all know, the commission wasted no time in developing a first list of species of union concern and is already carrying out preparatory work with a view to updating this later this year. finally, at global level, we need to deliver on our international financial commitments whilst addressing the underlying causes of global biodiversity loss, including the impacts of eu consumption, production and trade. i hope that we can do all of this together so that by 2020 we will have a positive result, which will be a significant stepping stone towards our 2030 sustainable development goals.

in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on the amendments to the 1998 protocol to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution in respect of heavy metals. the convention aims to protect the human environment against air pollution. to date, the convention has been extended by eight protocols identifying specific measures to be taken by parties to reduce their emissions of air pollution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of granting approval to the amendments to the 1998 protocol to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution concerning heavy metals. a number of studies carried out between 1972 and 1977 had shown that air pollutants could travel several thousand kilometres before being deposited, so that the problems arising from air pollution must be addressed on an international scale. the convention, signed in 1979 and entered into force in 1983, was the first legally binding international instrument in this field and has been extended by eight protocols laying down specific measures, including the one on heavy metals. this amended protocol sets stricter limit values for particulate emissions from certain large stationary sources, as well as flexible transitional provisions that will benefit parties acceding to the amended protocol before the end of 2019, including countries in eastern and south-eastern europe. the ratification of the amendments will be an important step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution.
in writing. ‒ this report deals with the acceptance of procedural amendments updating the scope of international conventions already approved by the parties at international level and now incorporated into the framework of eu law. i voted in favour because i consider that ratification of the amendments is a step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment against long-range transboundary air pollution caused by heavy metals.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the convention because i want to protect the human environment from air pollution, as several studies have shown that air pollutants can travel several thousand kilometres before they are deposited. it is therefore essential to address this problem at international level. the amended protocol sets stricter limit values for particulate emissions from certain large stationary sources as well as flexible transitional provisions.
in writing. ‒ the aarhus protocol is an international convention under the auspices of the united nations. its objective is to deal with environmental issues, including crossborder heavy metal pollution. these pollutants have serious effects on health and biodiversity. for example, migratory birds lose their sense of direction, which explains the rapid decline in their populations in the americas and asia. the member states of the european union are already signatories to this protocol and apply very strict standards. these are almost the only ones, and the big polluting powers are ignoring them. this recommendation of parliament is not binding on the member states. it will, however, enable the commission to justify future directives to limit polluting emissions, without putting pressure on third countries which are much more polluting than european countries. on the contrary, every free trade agreement between the union and third countries, such as the transatlantic treaty, is designed to increase transport flows and pollution without any environmental prerequisites. the member states are already signatories to this protocol and have no need for the recommendation which is being put to us. i therefore voted against this unnecessary recommendation.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report because the inclusion of these amendments implies acceptance of an improvement in legislation on heavy metals adopted in international conventions and now transposed into the framework of european union legislation.
in writing. ‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution (signed 1979, entering into force 1983) is intended to protect the human environment against air pollution. the convention was the first international legally binding instrument in this area. to date, the convention has been extended by eight protocols, which identify specific measures to reduce their air pollutant emissions. the aarhus protocol on heavy metals is one of these amending protocols. it aims to cut emissions from industrial sources (iron and steel industry, non-ferrous metal industry), combustion processes (power generation, road transport), and waste incineration. the accession of the eu to the protocol was approved on behalf of the community by council decision 2001/379/ec of 04/04/2001. the protocol, which entered into force on 29/12/2003, has been transposed into eu law through several instruments. the protocol put to the vote today sets out stricter limit values for dust emissions from certain major stationary sources, as well as flexible transitional arrangements that will benefit those parties that accede to the amended protocol before the end of 2019. in view of this positive amended protocol, which not only tightens up values for dust emissions but also reaffirms that waste incineration plants damage human health and the environment, eh bildu has voted in favour of this la via report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to accept the changes to the last protocol to the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution in respect of heavy metals. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road. we will therefore be taking a further step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment against transboundary air pollution.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to control and reduce the harm caused by transboundary air pollution to human health and the environment. this report refers to one of the eight protocols to the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution. specifically, it refers to the 1998 aarhus protocol on heavy metals, which focuses on the reduction and control of emissions into the atmosphere of lead, cadmium and mercury. the protocol obliges the parties concerned to reduce emissions from industrial sources, combustion processes and waste incineration. for all these purposes, it sets limit values. as a strong advocate of social welfare and environmental protection, i fully support this report, which aims to set stricter limit values for particulate emissions from certain large stationary sources.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of granting approval to the amendments to the 1998 protocol to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution by persistent organic pollutants. a number of studies carried out between 1972 and 1977 had shown that air pollutants could travel several thousand kilometres before being deposited, so that the problems arising from air pollution must be addressed on an international scale. the convention, signed in 1979 and entered into force in 1983, was the first legally binding international instrument in this field and has been extended by eight protocols setting out specific measures, including one on persistent organic pollutants. this amended protocol includes seven new substances, updates the implementation requirements for various substances, updates the restrictions on emissions of cpd/cdpe from various sources and adds pcbs to the list of substances subject to total annual emission restrictions and reporting obligations. the ratification of the amendments will be an important step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution.

in writing. ‒ this report would ratify an agreement between eurojust, the agency specialising in the fight against organised crime and terrorism, and ukraine through police collaboration and data exchange. it should be remembered that ukraine is a state where the human rights of the population are systematically violated and whose current government has approved measures that violate the rights of the russian-speaking population, and has even outlawed left-wing political symbols and parties. we have opposed the approval of it as we are radically against strengthening our relations with ukraine at a time like the current one when there is a conflict in the country after the coup d'état of 2014 that had european and north american support. this agreement is in the geopolitical interest of the european union to strengthen its ties with the ukrainian authorities and to try to isolate russia, which we will not support.

in writing. we voted in favour of the request for the waiver of florian philippot's immunity, considering that the purpose of immunity is, as the juri report proposed, to enable the legislature to carry out its constitutional tasks without undue interference from outside, in particular from the executive. in this case there is no political persecution or anything that could be the subject of criminal proceedings to the detriment of the member's political activity. i therefore have no problem voting in favour of the request that the investigations be continued in the appropriate areas.
in writing. ‒ i have supported the proposal of the juri commission, whose report finds that the french judicial authorities have requested the suspension of florian philippot's immunity in relation to a criminal action brought by a third state, qatar, which accuses him of having defamed that state in the course of a radio programme on 9 january 2015 and a television programme on 19 january 2015, insinuating that that state had financed terrorism. the juri committee has, however, considered that parliamentary immunity covers not only the views expressed by the member in official meetings of parliament, but also those expressed in other forums, such as the media, where there is 'a link between the opinion expressed and parliamentary functions', and has therefore decided not to waive the parliamentary immunity of florian philippot.

mr president, it is difficult to quantify undeclared work, but it is estimated that in some member states, such as spain, it amounts to some 20% of gross domestic product. it is a scourge with significant negative effects on workers, the state and society as a whole. however, the increase in undeclared work has not occurred by chance, but has been increasing with the economic crisis and austerity policies that have increased precariousness in employment. this is a precarious situation that particularly affects the most vulnerable workers, such as women, migrants, young people and the so-called 'false self-employed'. the platform is a positive first step and that is why we voted in favour. it is important to know the phenomenon, to approach it in a coordinated way, and it contains very interesting aspects. however, the roots of the problem remain intact and the threat of further labour reforms to countries like spain is going in the opposite direction to its solution. we are committed to continuing to work to put an end to the economic policies that have contributed to deregulating the labour market and making working conditions for european workers more precarious.
in writing. ‒ today, the eu has taken a very important step towards tackling the multiple challenges of undeclared work. this is a serious blow to the european economy, accounting for some 18% of gdp, although in some member states it can reach 35% (20% in the case of spain). but it does not only affect the economy, it poses a serious risk to the workers concerned, since they are often exploited, suffer more dangerous conditions and worse wages, and their labour rights are violated. we socialists have led the creation of this platform which aims to improve working conditions, reduce fraud to social security and integrate workers from the shadow economy into the labour market. the platform will tackle all types of undeclared employment, from the bogus self-employed to shell companies, by bringing together the efforts of a wide range of stakeholders, including member states and social partners. for all these reasons i have voted in favour of this initiative which i hope will be the first step in creating more incisive measures to combat this scourge of our economy and our society.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a platform to strengthen cooperation on the prevention and discouragement of undeclared work by the commission in order to provide a stable framework for cooperation and exchange of good practice between states, open to the participation of social partners. i welcome the fact that, through negotiation with parliament, the definition of 'undeclared work' has been extended to include falsely declared work and false self-employment, and the involvement of trade unions, the relevant european agencies (eurofound and osha) and the ilo has been strengthened. although the proposal is far from establishing a coordinated and binding framework for the fight against employer abuse (an undoubtedly european problem after integration into the single market), it is an important first step, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a european platform to combat undeclared work can be a good instrument to help reduce the current figures: undeclared work accounts for 18% of gdp on average in the eu. spain is close to the average, at 18.6%, which translates into more than eur 190 billion. undeclared work undermines the social and economic progress of countries and is a problem for all citizens, not just governments and companies. fighting undeclared work is about improving access to health care, guaranteeing labour rights or pensions. this platform would add value to the work already being done by the different member states, which need a supranational structure like this to facilitate coordination and exchange of information between all countries.
in writing. as regards the creation of a platform to combat undeclared work, we voted in favour of the report presented by the empl committee with the aim of it being passed as an amendment to the commission document. as positive aspects of the report we highlight the following:- the platform should not only prevent and deter undeclared work but also address proactive policies and measures aimed at regularizing undeclared work;- national and eu tools to address common problems such as the phenomenon of the false self-employed and undeclared work in subcontracting chains are to be explored;- the tasks are to include the identification of gaps and/or deficiencies in union legislation; - the operational aspects of the platform are to be strengthened: operational cooperation is to be strengthened with joint training sessions, staff exchange and joint inspections, as well as the exchange of data between national administrations; - common principles and guidelines for inspections addressing undeclared work are to be developed; - european and regional or european wide strategies are to be implemented.

in writing. ‒ the creation of this european platform aims to improve cooperation in the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work in the eu. the exchange of good practice and cooperation between police authorities in the member states is intended to prevent and discourage undeclared work and to raise public awareness of this issue. the aim is to improve the technical capacity of member states to deal with undeclared work across borders and to achieve a european-wide exchange of analysis, opinions and good practice. it is a major eu employment agreement, which will have repercussions on future benefits and which fully respects the principle of subsidiarity and the competences of the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, bearing in mind that closer cooperation and increased labour inspections are essential to combat undeclared work at eu level. i therefore regard the commission's decision to create a european platform to improve cooperation at eu level in this area as an important step in this direction, especially since undeclared work causes serious damage to working conditions, fair competition and public finances, and we must therefore be proactive in its eradication.

in writing. ‒ i believe that the commission's proposal to create a european platform against undeclared work is a positive step in the fight against this social and economic problem, which will help to combat one of the economic phenomena of our society which, in the case of spain, represents 20% of gdp, but in other states may reach 35%. the main victims of this phenomenon are the workers themselves, without security or rights. but it's also a problem for our economy because it distorts the labor market, and it's a very big problem for public coffers in many of our countries. among the most relevant elements of this platform, which will bring together the commission, the social partners and the national eu authorities responsible for combating undeclared work, such as labour inspectorates and social security authorities, are the inclusion of the law on fraud in recruitment, the fact that all states will be part of it and that all social partners will have a leading role in this cooperation. for these reasons i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it calls for better implementation of the relevant legislation to halt biodiversity loss, mainly the habitats and birds directives, while calling for better implementation of these policies and paying close attention to the agricultural and forestry sectors. the report also stresses that member states and the commission must focus on halting the loss of biodiversity in europe, warning that the 2020 biodiversity targets cannot be met unless member states and the eu make a serious commitment to this end.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report because it is a further step towards achieving the objectives of the eu biodiversity strategy 2010-2020. the mid-term review shows that the commitments on biodiversity are unlikely to be met if we continue on the current path. in this report we propose a number of improvements to be made in order to achieve the commitments by implementing ambitious legislative proposals rather than continuing the immobility and decay of existing legislation. at the same time, we must maintain high standards of biodiversity and care for nature and the environment without falling into demagoguery and putting scientific and technical criteria ahead of ideological arbitrariness.
in writing. we voted in favour of the report on the mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy because its content reviews each and every one of the six objectives of the strategy, highlighting the need to improve the implementation of all legislation aimed at halting biodiversity loss, in particular the habitats directive and the birds directive. it also stresses the need for member states to make an effort to better integrate environmental legislation into other areas, such as agriculture and forestry.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank mr demesmaeker for his work in getting this report on the mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy adopted today. i have supported this report as it emphasises, among other things, the strategic importance of the 'state of nature' and soer 2015 reports for the achievement of the eu biodiversity objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which expresses parliament's concern about the continued loss of biodiversity and which notes that the targets set for 2020 will not be reached without additional efforts. the 2011-2020 strategy sets six broad objectives: full implementation of the birds and habitats directives; maintenance and restoration of ecosystems and their services; increasing the contribution of agriculture and forestry to maintaining and enhancing biodiversity; sustainable use of fisheries resources; combating invasive alien species; and strengthening the eu's contribution to preventing global biodiversity loss. the report estimates that only considerable progress has been made on the objectives relating to fisheries and invasive alien species, while the others are insufficient. it therefore calls on the commission to submit to parliament two annual reports in which the council and the commission explain the situation, the reasons for non-compliance and the strategy to ensure future compliance, and calls on both to urgently give higher priority to meeting the 2020 targets and to provide greater financial support for the protection of biodiversity.

in writing. ‒ the report includes the european parliament's proposal for the mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy for 2020. the report stresses the need to halt the loss of biodiversity and the degradation of the eu's ecosystem services by 2020 and to restore them as far as possible, for which the involvement of local and regional actors is essential. that is why i think it is necessary to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ for spain, the protection of biodiversity is a matter of great importance and significant efforts have been made; this is why we are the country that contributes the most to the eu natura 2000 network. in addition, spain's efforts in the protection of the marine environment are widely recognised and we also collaborate on the eu biodiversity strategy with the declaration of the zec (special areas of conservation) and on the policy of protection of genetic resources (nagoya protocol). i believe that the implementation of the legal framework on biodiversity has been very positive in spain and does not need any amendments, as this would be a setback for the eu strategy for spain. i therefore believe that the solution could be to improve its implementation, because i believe that the eu biodiversity strategy is very good.

treaty on european union and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union oblige the commission to implement policies on equality between men and women, because we are talking about a fundamental principle and value of the european project. the current strategy ended in 2015. in june 2015, this house already took a position on this, with a debate on what the content and guidelines should be that the european commission should put forward in the new gender strategy, in the new strategy for equality between men and women. a public consultation was also launched, with over 90% of respondents stating that it was essential, fundamental and urgent that this political priority should be made a commitment by the european institutions and therefore that a new gender equality strategy should be launched. since june 2015, when this house took a majority position and urged the european commission to develop this work, we have been waiting for the commission's response. and the commission's response has been that, in december 2015, it adopted a working document prepared by the commission services, which we think is very respectable. we think that it has a content which must be taken into account, but we think that it completely misses the commitment which should be made on a political level. because a working document has no budget. because in a working document you cannot see how the measures put in place will be implemented. because a working document cannot be evaluated. and for policies to succeed, you need to have budgets and you need to have evaluation mechanisms. we therefore insist on the need for the college of commissioners to adopt a gender equality strategy, because this has to be a commitment of the whole college and it has to be debated and approved by the european commission, which is currently responsible for launching gender equality policies. because we are talking about fighting gender violence. we're talking about the wage gap. we're talking about work-life balance here. we are talking about fundamental issues on the political agenda of the european union, and we have an obligation to be able, together with the member states, to put them into practice. because in recent years we have seen that, alongside all the crises that have occurred within the european territory - the economic crisis, the refugee crisis, the social crisis - women have been the main victims of all of them. and so losing the gender perspective in all policies and being able to understand that transversality is fundamental is an indispensable issue and one that we will continue to demand from this parliament. we therefore also take this opportunity to ask the commission why it has not adopted a new communication on a strategy for gender equality in a public and transparent manner. we want to know why this document has not been adopted, why it has not been discussed, why it has not been approved by the college of commissioners. and we want to know what the commission is waiting for to make this happen, so that you can also discuss how, through the different policies, through the work of the different commissioners, the principle of equality between men and women can be advanced. we also want to know how the european commission will work with the presidency and the trio of presidencies to present a strategy for equality between men and women in 2016. i'm finished. it is fundamental. it's enforceable. we would have liked to have had mrs jourová here today, the person responsible for this matter in the college of commissioners. but i still insist, this is not a compartmentalized policy, this is a transversal policy and political commitment must be at the core of the whole european commission.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution as i considered necessary the call for the unblocking of the ratification of the marrakesh treaty so that member states implement a series of measures to facilitate access to printed works for blind people, people with visual impairments or people with other printing difficulties. although the eu and the member states signed the treaty in april 2014, a minority of seven member states (including the uk, germany and italy) are blocking its entry into force in the european council. i consider this resolution to be positive as a further mechanism of pressure to get final ratification unblocked and these measures implemented as soon as possible - including the approval of exceptions to state copyright laws aimed at facilitating the distribution and reproduction of braille works - which would positively affect almost twenty-five million european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it is essential that all the member states of the european union ratify the marrakesh treaty as soon as possible. only 5% of literature published in europe is made with the accessibility of the format for the blind, the visually impaired or the deaf in mind. we need to ensure access to audio books, braille and apps that allow us to move towards true equality of opportunity. the european parliament has also called for the establishment of a european union-wide network of information centres for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. we voted in favour of ratifying the marrakesh treaty, as the treaty has already been signed by eu member states, to facilitate access to published works for blind or visually impaired people, and we welcome the eu's ratification of the marrakesh treaty. we believe that all member states must respect the right of access to culture for all people on equal terms and facilitate access to culture for those with disabilities, in this case visually impaired people, and that intellectual property rights cannot be a barrier to discrimination against this group. we therefore support the eu's ratification of the marrakesh treaty, also within the framework of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and the signing of this treaty.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this resolution on the marrakesh treaty which recalls that articles 24 and 30 of the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities highlight the right of persons with disabilities to access education without discrimination, in accordance with the principle of equal opportunities, while ensuring that laws protecting intellectual property rights do not constitute an excessive or discriminatory barrier to access by persons with disabilities to cultural materials. in addition, there are seven eu member states which form a blocking minority which is impeding the process of ratification of the treaty, which causes me deep indignation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution by which parliament urges the council and the member states to speed up the process of ratification of the marrakesh treaty, since the eu and the member states signed the treaty in 2014, but seven member states have not yet ratified it, which keeps its entry into force blocked. as it has done on previous occasions, parliament called for the treaty to be ratified as soon as possible in order to facilitate wider distribution and easier access to books in accessible formats for the over 26 million blind and visually impaired people in the european union, who are restricted in their right of access to culture by the fact that only 5% of books published in developed countries are in accessible formats.

in writing. ‒ as vice-chair of the european parliament's committee on petitions, i was one of the driving forces behind this resolution in my political group. the marrakesh treaty requires all signatory parties to introduce exceptions to copyright law to meet the needs of visually impaired people, through the creation of special national authorities responsible for providing, in collaboration with ngos, accessible content. ratification will facilitate access to copyrighted works for visually impaired persons or persons who cannot read printed formats. the european parliament has contributed greatly to the development and success of this treaty, which, based on international copyright conventions, has been designed to also respect the rights of authors and their creators. after ratification and entry into force, visually impaired persons will have access to the same books as the general public. millions of blind people will have access to copyrighted works in the future, which in turn will enhance and broaden their educational and training options and therefore allow them to opt for better job opportunities in the labour market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution, bearing in mind that the world health organisation estimates that in 2010 there were 2 550 000 blind and 23 800 000 partially sighted people living in europe, which represents a total of 26 350 000 visually impaired people. only 5% of books published in developed countries and less than 1% of books published in developing countries are in accessible formats, so we need to work to make books and culture more accessible to this important group, especially as the eu and its member states signed the marrakesh treaty in april 2014 and have therefore made a political commitment to ratify it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, which aims to ratify the marrakesh treaty as soon as possible. this treaty allows for exceptions to copyright to facilitate the reproduction, distribution and making available of works for the blind or visually impaired. this also applies to persons with physical disabilities who are unable to hold or handle a book. it seems that some member states of the union have been an obstacle to the ratification of the treaty. the resolution calls on the council and the member states to speed up the ratification process without making it conditional on the revision of the union's legal framework or the decision of the court of justice of the european union. in any case, the non-ratification of the marrakesh treaty illustrates europe's failure to defend the disabled. the text has not yet been ratified, probably because it restricts copyright (somewhat). it therefore goes against the interests of important people: authors, publishers, translators...
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of ratifying the marrakesh treaty, as the treaty has already been signed by eu member states, to facilitate access to published works for blind or visually impaired people, and we see the eu's ratification of the treaty as positive. we believe that all member states must respect the right of access to culture for all people on equal terms and facilitate access to culture for those with disabilities, in this case visually impaired people, and that intellectual property rights cannot be a barrier to discrimination against this group. we therefore support the eu's ratification of the marrakesh treaty, also within the framework of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and the signing of this treaty.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament is an institution at the service of the citizen and this motion for a resolution is a clear example of this, as it is the result of numerous petitions submitted by european citizens who have difficulty accessing printed texts and books due to visual impairment. according to the world health organisation, in 2010 there are estimated to be 2 550 000 blind and 23 800 000 partially sighted people, or 26 350 000 visually impaired people. however, today, only 5% of books published in developed countries are in accessible formats for all audiences. the main purpose of the marrakesh treaty is to end the shortage of books faced by blind or visually impaired people. intellectual property should not be a barrier to access to cultural materials that discriminates against persons with disabilities. in my view, the adoption of this proposal is necessary to guarantee the principle of equal opportunities enshrined in the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities.

in writing. ‒ this gmo was submitted by bayer cropscience ag to the competent authority in belgium. it is a type of gm soybean tolerant to glyphosate and isoxaflutol based herbicides. on 20 march 2015, the international agency for research on cancer, a specialized agency of the world health organization, classified glyphosate as a probable carcinogen for humans. despite this, the european food safety authority (efsa) has issued a positive opinion. the standing committee has taken the following position: 'no opinion', as has become the custom with regard to gmos. it is clear that the current procedure for authorising genetically modified food and feed is not working properly and that the ep's role on these issues should be linked to delegated acts and not to implementing acts. i therefore support this and any objection that is put forward in relation to the authorization of gmos, and i have voted accordingly.
in writing. we voted in favour of the objection to the authorisation of genetically modified soybean fg72 because we consider that, given the nature of the acts implemented, this measure is more of a purely political act and therefore the european parliament should be able to participate in the legislation. in october 2015, the european commission's proposal on gmos for food and feed was rejected by different political groups in the european parliament, who felt that the decision of each member state to authorise or not the use of gmos on its territory should be respected, but that there is no regulation to ensure the correct implementation of this measure.
in writing. ‒ i would like to explain that i voted against the line of my group in this report on the objection to the authorization of genetically modified soybean fg72. the basque country is a gmo-free region and, as i did in 2015, i voted in favour of the envi commission's motion for a resolution which considers that the draft commission implementing decision is not consistent with union law as it is incompatible with the purpose of several regulations. i therefore support the request to withdraw the draft implementing decision.

in writing. ‒ this gmo was submitted by bayer cropscience ag to the competent authority in belgium. it is a type of gm soybean tolerant to glyphosate and isoxaflutol based herbicides. on 20 march 2015, the international agency for research on cancer, a specialized agency of the world health organization, classified glyphosate as a probable carcinogen for humans. despite this, the european food safety authority (efsa) has issued a positive opinion. the standing committee has taken the following position: 'no opinion', as has become the custom with regard to gmos. it is clear that the current procedure for authorising genetically modified food and feed is not working properly and that the ep's role on these issues should be linked to delegated acts and not to implementing acts. i therefore support this and any objection that is put forward in relation to the authorization of gmos, and i have voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection on the grounds that the draft commission implementing decision lays the foundation for ensuring a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, the environment and consumer interests in relation to genetically modified food and feed, while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ the european commission wants to allow the import of three new gm soybeans, all of which are tolerant of glyphosate. one of them is a soybean from bayer cropscience. i supported this objection in committee and in plenary, not least because glyphosate herbicides are carcinogenic according to the world health organization. it should also be noted that the efsa assessment is unsatisfactory and does not take into account the comments of the competent agencies of the member states. nevertheless, the european commission can override these objections, since the authorization of gmos is within its sole jurisdiction. it has already demonstrated this last december, when it authorised a new gmo maize, nk603xt25, despite opposition from the european parliament. that is why it is necessary that these authorisations now be under the democratic control of parliament, which i have proposed by amendments to amend the gmo authorisation regulation and replace the implementing acts with delegated acts. the objections voted by parliament can effectively veto commission decisions. but when it comes to demanding genuine democratic measures, especially when it comes to gmos, this parliament is decidedly absent-minded.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the objection to the authorisation of genetically modified soybean fg72 because we consider that, given the nature of the acts implemented, this measure is more in line with a purely political act and therefore the european parliament should be able to participate in the legislation. in october 2015, the european commission's proposal on gmos for food and feed was rejected by different political groups in the european parliament, who felt that the decision of each member state to authorise or not the use of gmos on its territory should be respected, but that there is no regulation to ensure the correct implementation of this measure.
in writing. ‒ even though as this vote is an objection to an implementing act, and this objection might be more of a political move made by different groups in the chamber, eh bildu has maintained a coherent position on matters related to gmos and always votes against those, or, as in cases such as last december with maize nk603*t25, vote in favour of objections to allowing the authorisation of gmos. the genetically modified mst-fgø72-2 soybean, as described in the application for authorisation, expresses the 2mepsps protein which confers tolerance to glyphosate herbicides and hppd w336 protein which confers tolerance to isoxaflutole herbicides; whereas the international agency for research on cancer – the specialised cancer agency of the world health organisation – classified glyphosate as probably carcinogenic to humans on 20 march 2015. therefore, eh bildu has voted in favour of this objection, and will keep voting in the same way to any future objection concerning authorisation of gmos, as we would like to put pressure to the commission to come up with a legislative proposal that is more satisfactory than the one rejected by parliament last october.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection to this implementing act by which the european commission authorises bayer cropscience ag to introduce the genetically modified soybean variety fg72 into belgium. with this objection, we ask the commission to refrain from authorizing the marketing of any gmo until a new regulation is presented, as this parliament has requested.

madam president, we voted to prevent the lowering of the emission standards for light vehicles simply because the directives and laws are for the benefit of people, and not for the benefit of companies. in the wake of the volkswagen scandal, known as 'dieselgate' and affecting much of the european car industry, the commission's proposal only represents the wishes of the same people who have been cheating on emissions for years; the same people who have put the sustainability of this sector, millions of jobs and, above all, the health of european citizens at risk. air pollution by nitrogen oxides and harmful particles causes almost half a million premature deaths in europe each year. we tell the commission that the way to avoid closures and relocations is to promote an industry which is both innovative and ecologically sustainable, looking to the future and the long term. do not yield to the pressures of those who put their own interests ahead of the common good of the people.
madam president, nitrogen emissions are currently five times the permitted limit. we have to stop now. i would like to see more ambition from the commission and the council. but if the objection were to be accepted, we would not reduce pollution, we would increase legal uncertainty and prolong non-compliance with the rules, with the consequent risk to health. with this decision, emissions will be reduced by less than half and europe will be the only region in the world to test in real driving conditions. only by implementing these tests will we be able to enforce regulations, protect the environment, protect health, give guarantees to consumers and users, and boost investment and employment in the automotive sector, a very important sector for countries like my own, spain.
madam chairman, i voted against the objection. i am convinced that the rules prepared by the commission, which are to apply from 2017, provide a solid basis for a real-world testing system. the same position is held by my country, the czech republic. for us, for the czech republic, the car industry is extremely important, it employs thousands, tens of thousands of czechs and we want there to be clear rules that apply to the car industry, so that it has stable and clear rules for what the individual types of cars should look like. i therefore voted for the commission and i hope that the commission will do everything possible to ensure that the whole system is working smoothly from 2017.
madam president, we voted in favour of this objection because the most intolerable thing of all is that the commission intends to decide without consulting parliament, again putting our health and that of the planet at risk. doubling the limit on nitrogen dioxide emissions is an absolutely intolerable concession to the large multinationals in the motor vehicle sector. we have not forgotten the volkswagen case, in which the commission knew more about car tricks than it said it did and by its silence and complicity helped to make an unprecedented fraud even bigger. we must prevent such cases from happening again, and to do this we need to promote democratic control and transparency. this is not a trivial matter because, ladies and gentlemen, it is our life - our own and that of future generations - that is at stake in taking care of this planet.
in writing. ‒ as recent studies by independent bodies have shown and as the commission has acknowledged, nox emissions are now up to five times higher than the limits set. this situation cannot continue, as 75 000 premature deaths are attributed to these emissions in europe. the socialists deplore the lack of ambition in the proposal drawn up by the commission and the council, and we have been belligerent in demanding from both an unequivocal commitment to set a date for compliance with the 80 mg/km limit. this has produced results: the limits will be met by 2023 at the latest. however, the proposed measure will already reduce emissions by less than half and make europe the only region in the world with real driving tests. only by implementing these tests can we enforce the regulations, protect the environment, protect health, give assurances to consumers, boost investment and employment in the sector and prevent any emissions fraud in the future. a vote in favour of the objection would therefore have been a vote in favour of keeping things the same, hence our abstention.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because this regulation developed by the commission goes beyond the mandate of the delegation of power granted in the basic act. the commission is once again using the delegation of powers in the interests of multinationals, in this case in clear collusion with the multinationals in the car industry, which has been affected by the volkswagen scandal. the resolution rejects this regulation because it seeks to circumvent parliament by legislating against the opinion of the democratically elected institutions and therefore against the interests of european citizens. it is precisely after the volkswagen scandal that the peoples of europe must give their opinion on this type of requirement for industry. i have therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. we voted in favour of the objection on the measures implemented by the european commission in the rde (real driving emissions) report to object to the conformity factor of 2.1 and not to the rde procedure itself. the basic legislation was adopted in 2007 and published as regulation 692/2008 to set the emission limit at 80 mg/km. now, with the new proposal, which introduces a conformity factor of 2.1, a 110% overrun is allowed. this is unacceptable, regardless of the recent scandal about the failures of co2 emission controls in the automotive sector (volkswagen case). the objection is to withdraw this preliminary proposal to increase the emission levels and to submit a new one by 1 april 2016 that respects the emission limits.
in writing. ‒ i wish to express that i voted differently from my group in this report, as i voted against the envi resolution which considers that the draft commission implementing decision exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 715/2007. i therefore supported the european commission's initial proposal.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection on euro 6 because we must indeed be demanding with industry, but we cannot forget that the letter of the law cannot go ahead of technology, because in that case, in the end, the result is never success but failure. we must be the guarantors of legal certainty in europe in order to be able at the same time to be demanding 'reitero' with industry and to guarantee thousands and thousands of jobs. we must be realistic and build a europe that is a world leader and a benchmark in green growth and that is competitive in creating jobs with high added value. a europe which also respects the agreements reached in paris a few weeks ago. this is the europe we want.
in writing. as recent studies by independent bodies have shown and as the commission has acknowledged, nox emissions are currently up to five times higher than the established limits. this situation cannot continue, as 75 000 premature deaths are attributed to these emissions in europe. the socialists deplore the lack of ambition in the proposal drawn up by the commission and the council, and we have been belligerent in demanding from both an unequivocal commitment to set a date for compliance with the 80 mg/km limit. this has produced results: the limits will be met by 2023 at the latest. however, the proposed measure will already reduce emissions by less than half and make europe the only region in the world with real driving tests. only by implementing these tests can we enforce the regulations, protect the environment, protect health, give assurances to consumers, boost investment and employment in the sector and prevent any emissions fraud in the future. a vote in favour of the objection would therefore have been a vote in favour of keeping things the same, hence our abstention.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the objection on the measures implemented by the european commission in the rde (real driving emissions) report to object to the conformity factor of 2.1 and not to the rde procedure itself. the basic legislation was adopted in 2007 and published as regulation 692/2008 to set the emission limit at 80 mg/km. now, with the new proposal, which introduces a conformity factor of 2.1, a 110% overrun is allowed. this is unacceptable, regardless of the recent scandal about the failures of co2 emission controls in the automotive sector (volkswagen case). the objection is to withdraw this preliminary proposal to increase the emission levels and to submit a new one by 1 april 2016 that respects the emission limits.

in writing. ‒ the european citizens' delegation supports greater demand and ambition on emissions from passenger cars and light commercial vehicles. however, we also believe that a new directive, which would shorten the time limits for adjusting the emissions of these vehicles, would directly affect the employment and economy of european countries where passenger cars and light commercial vehicles are manufactured. in the case of spain, around 60% of the vehicles manufactured are passenger cars and light commercial vehicles (according to figures from anfac, the spanish association of automobile and truck manufacturers). therefore, in defence of jobs and considering that the deadlines defined by the commission's proposed directive are consistent with the time needed by industry to adapt its manufacturing processes towards the production of less polluting vehicles, european citizens will vote against revising the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 692/2008 as regards emissions from passenger cars and light commercial vehicles.
in writing. the text we have just voted on is opposed to the european commission's draft measures, which define how the new pollutant emission tests will be implemented in real vehicle use circumstances. the draft regulation introduces so-called conformity factors, which add a margin of flexibility between test results and emission limits. the reason i voted in favour of the objection is that these factors have set levels which allow manufacturers to continue to significantly exceed the nox emission limit defined by parliament and the council in the basic legislation. the recent volkswagen scandal should serve to take the necessary measures in a matter which is not only of technical or economic relevance. as i have said on many occasions, this type of fraud affects us all: the deceived buyers, the administrations, but above all the citizens in general, who see how money is being gambled with our air, our oxygen, our life and our future. i can therefore only vote in favour of the objection.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because this regulation developed by the commission goes beyond the mandate of the delegation of power granted in the basic act. the commission is once again using the delegation of powers in the interests of multinationals, in this case in clear collusion with the multinationals in the car industry, which has been affected by the volkswagen scandal. the resolution rejects this regulation because it seeks to circumvent parliament by legislating against the opinion of the democratically elected institutions and therefore against the interests of european citizens. it is precisely after the volkswagen scandal that the peoples of europe must give their opinion on this type of requirement for industry. i have therefore voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i am fully in favour of the automotive sector reducing its emissions of polluting gases into the atmosphere and i am aware of the urgent need for this to happen. however, i reject the objection, because i believe that this is the only way that the new controls under real conditions can be established and therefore the only way that emissions into the atmosphere can start to be reduced as soon as possible. moreover, these reductions must be made compatible with the maintenance of our industry in europe. i therefore firmly believe that my position is to strike a balance between the protection of human health and the prosperity of the motor industry.
in writing. ‒ the socialists voted in favour of this resolution which calls for a change of course in the acp negotiations. the acp can be an opportunity to regulate globalisation but it must be subject to a number of conditions set out in this resolution. greater transparency in the negotiations, the unambiguous exclusion of public services from the scope of the agreement and full respect for the labour and social rights of european workers are indispensable conditions for european socialists. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the acquis in the field of data protection and the protection of personal data. this resolution does not determine a final position of the european parliament or the socialist group on the acp. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's trade in services is not affected by the trade in services agreement.
in writing. ‒ in izquierda plural we have positioned ourselves from the beginning against the different trade agreements, such as the atci or the aecg, with which democratic power is being undermined to hand it over to the big corporations. this report endorses the negotiations on the acp, a trade in services agreement being negotiated by 23 countries, including tax havens such as switzerland and non-signatories to ilo agreements such as the united states. in addition, services are being promoted to be owned by large international corporations, encouraging privatisation and full liberalisation of services. the report approves the privatisation of the postal services, which have been public in spain until now. the report also advocates removing the ability of municipalities to re-municipalise, or taking into account criteria such as gender equality or job creation during the negotiation of the agreement. it is also worth noting that we voted in favour of the negotiations when we do not know the content of the negotiations, since they are being held in absolute secrecy and we have only learned of their existence thanks to the wikileaks revelations. we cannot therefore support the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendations to the european commission for the remaining negotiations on the agreement on trade in services (acs) because meps have succeeded in setting sufficiently ambitious and consistent levels of requirements, limitations and transparency. it is essential to leave public services out of this agreement and to ensure that european data protection laws are not compromised. this report sets out the guidelines which parliament recommends to the commission. they are not binding but they are essential if the final result of this agreement, once the negotiations have been concluded, is to have any chance of being approved by this parliament.
in writing. we have voted against this report because, despite considerable progress in relation to the original report and the current conditions of negotiation, it is still contrary to the interests of the citizens of the signatory countries and, even more so, of the developing countries which are excluded from the agreement. we are not prepared to vote in favour of an agreement which favours the liberalisation of services and free trade in areas which include sectors which are very sensitive to welfare and development. it would be contrary to common sense in a context where we are still experiencing the consequences of a crisis caused to a large extent by liberalization.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution containing the european parliament's recommendations on the negotiations on the agreement on trade in services (tsa) for several reasons, but above all because i believe that parliament must send a clear and well-founded message on the importance of international trade and the need to remove barriers to trade and protectionism in order to achieve a more integrated europe with more growth and progress. trade in services is becoming increasingly important as a crucial driver of job creation. this agreement should increase access to external markets, but europe cannot impose its rules and values on countries, nor introduce protectionist, destructive and very unsolidarist factors. paragraphs such as paragraph 1 (d) (i) are contrary to the freedom of movement, which i consider to be fundamental. i do not agree, among other things, that one of the parties should be allowed to withdraw from the agreement. the automatic exclusion of public services should be reviewed: no one guarantees that a service is better, more efficient and safer for consumers simply because it is provided by the state.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i am convinced that the acp negotiations can ensure greater reciprocity in market access, create a level playing field on a global scale and bring tangible benefits to consumers. however, public and cultural services, fundamental rights to data privacy and fair working conditions, and the right to legislate are non-negotiable and should be unequivocally excluded from the scope of the agreement. the european parliament must work constructively to achieve a good agreement in the interests of european businesses and consumers.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report containing the european parliament's recommendations to the commission on the negotiations of the agreement on trade in services (tsa). the agreement aims to extend the liberalisation of services in all sectors. it is designed in principle to win markets in third countries, but its main aim is to level down international standards, taking particular inspiration from american standards. in fact, in order to liberalise the market, the european commission is constantly pushing for the opening of borders and the privatisation of public services, while weakening social and environmental standards. this imperative overrides all others and leads europe to open its borders ever wider without any real reciprocity. although the report is intended to be reassuring and protective, the european commission is not obliged to follow the recommendations it makes. in fact, to protect our jobs and our public services, the enf group is calling for the cessation of the negotiations on the csa.

in writing. ‒ firstly, it should be noted that the agreement on trade in services is a trade agreement whose main purpose is to open up markets, improve licensing rules, financial services, telecommunications, etc. this report is a step forward on the road to reciprocity in market access and to the creation of a level playing field on a global scale. it also means providing tangible benefits to consumers. the european parliament is working constructively and pragmatically to ensure that the negotiations under way are successful. the present report assesses the two and a half years and 13 rounds of negotiations on the agreements on trade in services in order to make a number of recommendations to the commission. finally, i believe that the adoption of this report is necessary in order to achieve a solid agreement which will benefit european consumers and businesses alike.
in writing. the recommendations we have voted on today are important in that they set out the red lines that this parliament is setting when giving a negotiating mandate to the commission on behalf of the union on the agreement on trade in services. there are many shadows surrounding the negotiations, not only in terms of transparency and information but also in terms of political content. this text is, precisely, decisive in all the above. transparency and information are a basic requirement in any negotiating process, whether in relation to ceta or the att, and we therefore call on the commission to be rigorous in its information. we also demand that the agreement to be negotiated should avoid social, environmental and economic dumping and ensure respect for the eu acquis. we call for the right of member states to regulate and exclude sensitive sectors, such as public service markets, to be safeguarded, which means respecting the political, social and cultural models of the eu and its member states. in short, i voted in favour of a balanced and demanding text in defence of european interests.

in writing. ‒ the non-legislative report by mrs reding sets out a number of guidelines for negotiators which i believe are beneficial for europe, such as the reciprocity of european services in the face of the opening of the market, limits on restrictive practices applied by third countries to european companies or a reduced bureaucratic burden for smes. similarly, red lines for negotiation are identified, such as exclusion from public services such as education, health, social services, social security systems or audiovisual services, respect for current and future european data protection standards or the inclusion of a review clause allowing a signatory to the agreement to withdraw from it if labour and social standards are breached. we are therefore talking about a report which contributes constructively to the negotiations, and i think it is necessary to vote in favour of it.
