in writing. ‒ the trade in services agreement (tisa) is of vital importance to the eu, the world's largest exporter of services. given the growing role of the services sector in the community economy, an agreement with the remaining 23 members is clearly a priority interest for the eu. the rapporteur, mrs reding, has also done a good job of balancing the text and gaining the support of the various political groups. this plurilateral agreement, with a view to becoming multilateral, is fully in line with the objectives of the wto and can serve as a development lever for the countries negotiating tisa or for those acceding to it ex post facto. i have no doubt that if this agreement is carried through, its implementation can bring great benefits to the economy and employment in the european union.
madam president, the commission has presented us with a working document, not a strategy for gender equality. it has no objectives; it has no budget; it has no measurement indicators and no subsequent evaluation. this commission proposal not only ignores the european parliament's june 2015 resolution and the results of the citizens' consultation in october of the same year, but may represent a regrettable step backwards on the road to equality. yesterday the commission told us that it has all its political support for gender equality, but the facts are showing that it has no political will and is falling back on its patriarchal deafness. we cannot accept the commission's indolence. the fight for women's rights, for equality between men and women, must be at the heart of our policies, at the heart of the policies of the european union. that is why we voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because it contains an express mandate from parliament and, previously, from the committee on women's rights and gender equality, for the european commission to continue, through a new strategy to succeed it, the so-called strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015, whose scope was already clearly limited by not fully achieving any of its five main lines of work. the commission is thus asked to take more seriously one of the fundamental principles of the treaties, that of equality between women and men, and to adopt a strategy in the form of an official communication rather than a mere working document. in my view, this is some of the evidence that the current european commission has no interest in highlighting such unjust realities as the scourge of gender violence, the persistent wage inequality or the lack of policies to reconcile personal and professional life (as shown by the withdrawal of the proposal to extend the maternity directive).
the eu had a strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015 which came to an end last december. earlier, in june, parliament adopted a resolution calling on the commission to draw up a new strategy for 2016-2019. the public consultation also showed that europeans are in favour of this new strategy. however, unfortunately, on 3 december 2015 the commission published a mere staff working document entitled strategic engagement for gender equality 2016-2019 which is not only a minor internal document, but is also limited in scope and reflects a lower level of institutional commitment. we therefore voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution calling on the commission to draw up urgently, in addition to the working document, which is clearly insufficient, a strategy with objectives, measures, measurement indicators, budget and evaluation, which will make it possible to implement actions for gender equality and demonstrate the commission's genuine commitment to gender equality in a transversal way.
in writing. ‒ i have fully supported, even signed the resolution on the new strategy for gender equality and women's rights in europe after 2015 agreed by four parliamentary groups. we need to have a legislative proposal from the european commission that sets out a clear and pioneering 21st century strategy for gender equality. it's a requirement of society.
in writing. ‒ the strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015 was concluded in december. in its resolution of 9 june 2015, parliament stressed the need and urgency for the commission to present a new specific strategy for gender equality and women's rights in the eu. however, on 3 december 2015, the commission presented a mere working document which has no interinstitutional value. a genuine strategy is therefore required in the face of the commission's intention to reduce its level of action in this area, since it neither sets specific benchmarks nor allocates a budget, and it will therefore not be possible to assess the progress made towards the objectives. for these reasons i support the resolution adopted by the european parliament to correct these shortcomings.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because it contains an express mandate from parliament and, previously, from the committee on women's rights and gender equality, for the european commission to continue, through a new strategy to succeed it, the so-called strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015, whose scope was already clearly limited by not fully achieving any of its five main lines of work. the commission is thus asked to take more seriously one of the fundamental principles of the treaties, that of equality between women and men, and to adopt a strategy in the form of an official communication rather than a mere working document. in my view, this is some of the evidence that the current european commission has no interest in highlighting such unjust realities as the scourge of gender violence, the persistent wage inequality or the lack of policies to reconcile personal and professional life (as shown by the withdrawal of the proposal to extend the maternity directive).
in writing. ‒ gender equality is a fundamental value of the european union and is enshrined in the treaties and the charter of fundamental rights. the importance of equality between women and men leads us to continue working on new strategies for the next five years with the aim of eliminating all the barriers that impede the development of women, both at the workplace and in the professions within society. ending all forms of discrimination and violence against women must be our main objective when developing new strategies. women, like men, must be assured that they will not suffer any prejudice because of their ethnic origin, sexual orientation, sexual identity, disability, region, nationality or age. we must see gender equality as a strategic and universal objective that will help us achieve europe's economic, social and employment objectives.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from voting on the resolution, considering that gender equality is a core value of the eu and that, as a strategic objective, it is fundamental to achieving the eu's overall objectives. there is still a lot of work to be done to consolidate women's rights and gender equality, we have a lot of legislation passed, and we must ensure that the states transpose into their domestic regulations what is already the norm in europe. i therefore believe that it will be much better to facilitate legislative simplification and to have the legislation implemented in the member states than to develop new directives which can be used as measures to block the implementation of the measures for gender equality and women's rights already adopted.
in writing. this parliament already stressed in its resolution of 9 june 2015 the need and urgency for the european commission to present a new specific strategy for gender equality and women's rights in the eu. the previous strategy has been insufficient to help advance gender equality at european and international level while failing to effectively deliver on its intended objectives. i regret that the european commission has not yet presented such a strategy, and i therefore vote in favour of a text which demands and insists that it be done urgently.
in writing. ‒ the strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015 was concluded in december. in its resolution of 9 june 2015, parliament stressed the need and urgency for the commission to present a new specific strategy for gender equality and women's rights in the eu. however, on 3 december 2015, the commission submitted a mere working document which has no institutional value. a genuine strategy is therefore needed in the face of the commission's intention to reduce its level of action in this area, since it neither sets specific benchmarks nor allocates a budget and it will therefore not be possible to assess the progress made towards the objectives. for these reasons i support the resolution adopted by the european parliament to correct these shortcomings.
in writing. ‒ the eu had a strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015 which came to an end last december. earlier, in june, parliament adopted a resolution calling on the commission to draw up a new strategy for 2016-2019. the public consultation also showed that europeans are in favour of this new strategy. however, unfortunately, on 3 december 2015 the commission published a mere staff working document entitled strategic engagement for gender equality 2016-2019 which is not only a minor internal document, but is also limited in scope and reflects a lower level of institutional commitment. we therefore voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution calling on the commission to draw up urgently, in addition to the working document, which is clearly insufficient, a strategy with objectives, measures, measurement indicators, budget and evaluation, which will make it possible to implement actions for gender equality and demonstrate the commission's genuine commitment to gender equality in a transversal way.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because it contains an express mandate from parliament and, previously, from the committee on women's rights and gender equality, for the european commission to continue, through a new strategy to succeed it, the so-called strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015, whose scope was already clearly limited by not fully achieving any of its five main lines of work. the commission is thus asked to take more seriously one of the fundamental principles of the treaties, that of equality between women and men, and to adopt a strategy in the form of an official communication rather than a mere working document. in my view, this is some of the evidence that the current european commission has no interest in highlighting such unjust realities as the scourge of gender violence, the persistent wage inequality or the lack of policies to reconcile personal and professional life (as shown by the withdrawal of the proposal to extend the maternity directive).

member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– madam president, on behalf of the vice-president/high representative, i welcome the opportunity to join you today to discuss haiti and the serious political and institutional crisis the country is going though. the situation in haiti is of great concern and we believe it is fully justified that we address this issue today. the recent postponement sine die of the second round of the presidential elections, originally scheduled for 27 december and subsequently for 24 january, has opened a phase of instability and created the risk of an institutional vacuum. above all, it risks depriving the haitian people of the right to democratically choose their leaders. against a background of a general lack of confidence in the haitian institutions and low voter participation, preparation of the second round of presidential elections took place in a polarised environment, characterised by accusations of electoral fraud by a number of actors. the provisional electoral council, faced with the resignation of several of its members and the danger of further escalation of violence, which tragically has already cost several lives, decided to postpone the voting. i do not need to stress the risk that this situation generates, especially in a country like haiti, affected by widespread poverty and many vulnerabilities. this crisis could jeopardise the reconstruction efforts and the results achieved after the disastrous earthquake which hit haiti in 2010. these results were achieved thanks also to the major contributions made by the european union to the development of the country. in july 2015 the eu fielded a large electoral observation mission, headed by honourable member elena valenciano, and i would like to take this opportunity to pay tribute to the sterling work carried out by ms valenciano and her team. they provided an invaluable service to haiti and to the eu through their vigorously independent and professional observation and analysis. the eu election observation mission reported several irregularities but also concluded that no massive fraud took place at the 25 october election, and that results announced in the first round of the presidential elections were substantially correct. unfortunately, the candidates who did not come first in the first round of the presidential election refused to accept this result. they made known substantial accusations of massive fraud and increased the widespread lack of confidence in public opinion. this led to the current deadlock. the haitian voters could not exercise their political rights in full. as a consequence, there will not be an elected president by 7 february when, according to the constitution, president martelly will step down. the constitution does not precisely provide for this, but of course it contains provisions for cases of incapacity with guidance given. negotiations are currently ongoing in haiti. we are all following the developments very closely. the organization of american states (oas) sent a special mediation mission, and a similar mission by the community of latin american and caribbean states (celac) is also planned. we hope that a general consensus will emerge in favour of a swift completion of the electoral process on the basis of the will expressed by the haitian people on 25 october and with practical improvements to the process. the work of the eu electoral observation mission could again be extremely valuable in this context. there is, however, the risk that an agreement may not be reached in the short term and that the transitional government finds itself faced with a legitimacy issue. this could have serious consequences for democracy and for the country. the eu is a long-standing and committed partner to haiti. in these difficult times we call on all stakeholders to refrain from violence and to accept political responsibility in a democratic way. democracy is necessary for sustainable development. i very much look forward to hearing the views of the honourable members.
the first thing i would like to do, madam president, is to confirm the european commitment to the people of haiti and to their constitutional authorities, a european commitment which we translate and which is the solidarity of the citizens of the european union with that country which has suffered so much. so, first, commitment to haiti. the second thing i want to say is that i have had the honor, i have the honor, of leading a team of very high-quality professionals, very committed to democracy in the world, who have done an excellent job in monitoring the electoral process that, unfortunately, has gone off the rails, for the time being, in haiti. the work has been serious, rigorous. all honourable members can rest assured and if not, you can check our website and our reports to see that we are able to say that the elections of 25 october, the first round of elections in haiti, were certainly the cleanest and least violent elections haiti has had throughout its history. and so we confirm that the result of those elections, of the first round, could have accompanied the holding of a second round. right now, there is an institutional crisis in haiti, there is a political impasse in haiti that haitians must resolve. it is up to the haitian authorities and the haitian people to resolve this important impasse, which mrs crețu has analysed perfectly and on which i shall not dwell. that's a stalemate the haitians have to solve. hopefully they will do it through dialogue and consensus, but our recommendation - humble recommendation - based on serious, rigorous and committed work, is that the second round of elections in haiti be held. it'll be the most legitimate thing we can do. let us wait for the solution that the haitians will give us and, if there is a second round of voting, the european union's election observation mission will be there to give its testimony.

the delegation from venezuela, and i would like to thank you for putting venezuela on the agenda today. two months after the legislative elections of 6 december, it is timely to debate what impact – or lack thereof – the very significant result of those elections has had on the political and economic course taken by this important country in its very difficult situation. let me first thank parliament for the continuous attention you have been paying to the worrying situation over the last two years since 43 people died during the violent street protests of february and march 2014. the resolutions adopted on three occasions since then gave a strong expression of our common conviction that the current crisis can only be overcome by means of a peaceful and constructive dialogue and in respect of human rights and the venezuelan constitution. the elections of 6 december, with a high turnout, produced an unequivocal result. a strong majority of the venezuelan people have given a clear mandate to parliament for taking political decisions in order to address the country’s challenges. the people of venezuela are suffering. they suffer from rampant violence and insecurity, with caracas being a city with one of the highest murder rates per capita in the world and an even higher number of kidnappings and other violent attacks. they are suffering shortages of basic goods and food, medicines and medical care. with their peaceful and clear vote on 6 december, the people have requested a political response to these challenges. all political actors and institutions need to respect this democratic vote for the national assembly as well as the legitimacy of the current government. now is the time to work together in finding pragmatic and workable solutions to these difficult challenges. ideological confrontations or institutional standoffs will not bring these solutions, and there is not much time left to lose in political manoeuvring as economic and financial resources are running out, the oil price is not likely to recover soon and inflation and shortages are getting more acute by the week. initiatives for a national economic dialogue and for a certain process to address the issues of the victims of 2014 have been put forward by the executive. they will be useful if they are inclusive and conducted in a spirit of genuine openness for compromise and new solutions. this requires careful and critical reflection about what has not worked. it is important not to forget the plight of several dozen protesters who are still in jail or have been sentenced in questionable trials. i will only mention the most publicised case of leopoldo lópez. victims of violence must be protected. to achieve this, it is essential to ensure that those accused of having committed acts of violence during the protests get a fair and speedy trial based on objective evidence. all of these issues together form a complex reality that must be tackled. these initiatives should now be embraced as opportunities by both sides – executive and legislative, government and opposition – in a spirit of constructive cooperation and in full respect for the venezuelan constitution. it is the constitution that offers a lawful, peaceful framework in which the venezuelan body politic can operate as a democracy. those on either side who feel tempted by non-constitutional methods or parallel structures must know that they have a heavy responsibility. let us be clear. if the current absence of real dialogue persists, there is a distinct risk of new street protests and violent confrontation, which can easily get out of hand. we know that society is polarised, and there is no escaping that fact. there is a history. both sides must accept that the other side has a role to play. neither side is in a position to solve the multiple crises on its own. this is the message that europe has been giving to our venezuelan friends. dialogue and compromise are the only way forward. the european union and its member states are working closely together in brussels and caracas to convey this message, and we join the considerable number of regional organisations and partner countries that have voiced the same call for national dialogue. europe has legitimate concerns. there are more than half a million eu citizens living in venezuela. eu companies are important investors and the european union is also concerned about regional stability and the negative impact the worsening situation will have on the region. europe has close ties to the region, and we are cooperating in many ways: from trade to security and from the fight against drugs to education and human rights, to name just the main areas of our cooperation with the region. we stand ready also to step up our cooperation with venezuela. we know that many venezuelan citizens are looking to the european union as a good friend that can help to rebuild constitutionality and economic prosperity. this is the offer we have been making in various ongoing contacts both in caracas and brussels. that is also the message that i have expressed in quite a few public statements. let me take this opportunity to thank you for the strong support that i have felt from the house in taking these positions, and i thank you for your attention.

in writing. ‒ the resolution is based on an act that the spanish state does not recognise: the unilateral declaration of independence of kosovo in 2008. the resolution therefore encourages the five eu member states which do not recognise kosovo to do so. spain did not recognise the unilateral declaration of independence as it was contrary to international law and violated the principles of sovereignty and territorial integrity recognised to serbia and guaranteed by the helsinki final act. this position is also consistent with that of the united nations, since there is a security council resolution in force (resolution 1244 of 10 june 1999) which opposes such a unilateral act. moreover, recognition of such independence would not be consistent with the international community's action in bosnia and herzegovina in relation to the republika srpska or in other similar situations such as ossetia, abkhazia and crimea. of course, all the positive aspirations for the people of kosovo contained in the report could be supported, but they cannot lead to the acceptance of unilateral independence for kosovo. i have therefore voted against this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution after analysing the progress made by kosovo and the signing of the eu-kosovo stabilisation and association agreement (saa), which paves the way for kosovo's integration into the eu and will provide a powerful incentive for the implementation and institutionalisation of reforms and will allow for the establishment of cooperation with the eu in a wide range of areas, with a view to strengthening political dialogue and trade integration, as well as strengthening relations with neighbouring countries and contributing to ensuring regional stability. the government of kosovo should continue to work on the implementation of the overall reforms necessary to fulfil its obligations under the saa.
in writing. ‒ we abstain in this vote because, although the international court of justice concluded that the unilateral declaration of independence of kosovo did not violate international law or un security council resolution 1244, and although the process of state formation of kosovo is irreversible, the opinion does not imply that the former province has a well-founded right to be recognised by third parties. the situation in kosovo has a complex political background and must therefore be addressed and resolved politically, by means of an agreement which in any case includes serbia, which neutralises serbian and kosovar nationalism which constitutes a permanent internal threat to peace, which safeguards the rights of the ethnic minorities in the area and which ensures in the medium term the withdrawal of foreign military powers from the area.
in writing. ‒ the resolution is based on an act that the spanish state does not recognise: the unilateral declaration of independence of kosovo in 2008. the resolution therefore encourages the five eu member states which do not recognise kosovo to do so. spain did not recognise the unilateral declaration of independence as it was contrary to international law and violated the principles of sovereignty and territorial integrity recognised to serbia and guaranteed by the helsinki final act. this position is also consistent with that of the united nations, since there is a security council resolution in force (resolution 1244 of 10 june 1999) which opposes such a unilateral act. moreover, recognition of such independence would not be consistent with the international community's action in bosnia and herzegovina in relation to the republika srpska or in other similar situations such as ossetia, abkhazia and crimea. of course, all the positive aspirations for the people of kosovo contained in the report could be supported, but they cannot lead to the acceptance of unilateral independence for kosovo. i have therefore voted against this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the situation in libya, because it defends the nato military intervention in 2011 and considers that the bombings and the death of thousands of libyans, the situation of chaos and destruction in the country, the risk of fracture and the progression of the evil so-called islamic state (is) five years later, the destabilisation of countries and the uncontrolled flow of arms in the region were worth it. not only does it not recognise western responsibility for the conflict, it is seeking to add pressure for a swift implementation of the libyan political agreement which, far from succeeding, has proposed a government that has already been rejected by the tobruk parliament. the eu intends to press for the rapid formation of a single puppet government with international legitimacy which can, on the one hand, admit that the eunavfor med sophia border-externalisation and obstacle to the arrival of refugees in the eu patrols in libyan territorial waters and, on the other, even justify a new foreign military intervention in the country, this time under the pretext of fighting is. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. the libyan parliament rejected the un resolution which sought to implement a stabilisation plan in the area including a unity government. the european commission itself has publicly lamented the irresponsible attitude of the libyan representatives. we are voting against because we believe that the resolution of the libyan political conflict and the formation of a unity government must be a sine qua non for any eu resolution or action.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank those who have worked on this resolution on the situation in libya for the work they have done. i have supported this resolution condemning the destabilising terrorist attacks perpetrated by daesh against the libyan population, including minorities and infrastructure. the focus must be on the reconstruction of the country, for which collaboration between different institutions and bodies is essential.
in writing. ‒ since the nato military intervention and the overthrow of muammar gaddafi in 2011, various political parties, tribes and militias have been vying for power and control of the country's oil and gas fields. in december, an agreement was reached to form a national unity government through the mediation of the un, the united states and italy. the compromise was signed by members of both sides, but many still oppose the pact. despite these tentative advances, anarchy continues to have enormous costs and the number of people killed, kidnapped or imprisoned without due process of law continues to rise. in addition, libya is a transit country for refugees and migrants from africa and the middle east; the uncontrolled trafficking of arms and fighters through the sahel is also a cause for concern. in the face of this chaos, this resolution strongly condemns the recent terrorist attacks in zliten and urges the presidency council to form a government of national unity as soon as possible, as this is the only way for libya to return to the path of peace, stability and prosperity. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, bearing in mind that after the fall of dictator gaddafi, a political vacuum was created without a stable government, a fact which has been exploited by daesh, which exercises full control over an area of over 200 km around sirte and which also has a training base west of tripoli. there is no doubt that the libyan political agreement aims to guarantee democratic rights, establish a consensus government based on the principle of separation of powers and strengthen the institutions of the state. we must support the government of national consensus formed by consensus among the libyan parties as the only legitimate government in the country and contribute in every possible way to the stabilization of the country.

in writing. ‒ the situation in libya, where there is a difficult economic situation and intense violence, requires the eu and the international community to support the country so that it can move forward. i support the resolution adopted in this parliament, in which we express our satisfaction with the political agreement signed in december 2015. i hope that the government in this country will be able to tackle the problems it is currently facing and be able to take measures that will lead to the construction of a democratic, peaceful, stable and prosperous country.

in writing. ‒ i support this resolution. with this vote, i condemn the destabilising terrorist attacks by daesh against the people of libya. i call on the commission and the european external action service, which is coordinating member states’ action in libya, to focus their support on state—building and institution—building and, together with the member states, the un, nato and regional partners, to assist in the reform of the security sector and the creation, under the control of the gna, of effective national army and police forces able to control the entire libyan territory and its waters and secure its borders.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the resolution on libya, a fragmented country, in the throes of a serious political crisis and threatened by the increasingly strong presence of daesh. the government of national unity, which was rejected by the parliament in tobruk a few days ago, is recognized by the resolution as the only legitimate government in the country. the international community urgently needs a new unity government, which would help to halt the increasingly violent advance of the islamic state in libya.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution to support the european institutions in working towards specific funding and measures to address the particularities of island regions which, due to their extraordinary geographical conditions, tend to suffer more from economic problems, regional development and population loss, which clearly goes against the objective set out in the treaties of reducing disparities between the different regions. the resolution calls for a comprehensive study of the additional costs of island areas, improved sources of funding and a white paper to monitor and consult best practice from the various actors. however, i should like to stress that this resolution does not include the criticism that must be made of a global economic model that has damaged sustainable development in island areas, especially those belonging to the southernmost countries, where in general almost exclusively leisure tourism has been promoted, without taking into account protected natural areas, or opportunities for economic diversification and quality employment. anyway, my vote has been in favour.
in writing. we voted in favour as we agree that, in accordance with council directive 2006/112/ec, certain european islands (including the outermost region of the canary islands) should be granted special tax treatment to correct inequalities due to multiple causes related to their insularity.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this resolution on the special situation of islands - islands other than the outermost regions - because i think it is very important. it encourages the commission to provide a clear definition of the type of permanent geographical, natural and demographic disadvantages which island regions may suffer. i would encourage the commission to do so.
in writing. ‒ the island regions, classified as nuts-2 and nuts-3 regions, have common characteristics and peculiarities which are permanently manifested and clearly distinguish them from the mainland territories. article 174 tfeu recognises that island regions as a whole face permanent handicaps requiring special attention. however, in the framework of the preparation of the financial programming period 2014-2020, eu island regions at nuts-2 and nuts-3 levels did not receive any specific funding, but only the possibility to modulate the co-financing rates for certain island types, in accordance with article 121 of regulation (eu) no 1303/2013. for these reasons, i support the resolution adopted by the european parliament to correct these shortcomings.

in writing. ‒ the island regions, which i know well from the balearic islands, have peculiar common and permanent characteristics which clearly distinguish them from other continental areas. in this regard, the commission should provide a clear definition of the type of permanent geographical, natural and demographic disadvantages that island regions may suffer, pursuant to article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). the problems arising from insularity are reflected in multiple areas, such as access to regions and connections within islands, transport costs and energy supply. these are also regions far from the main administrative and economic centres, where balanced territorial development must be supported through innovation and competitiveness. in-depth studies and analyses on the impacts of island status and the possible creation of an eu strategic framework for islands articulating instruments that can have a significant territorial impact should be promoted.
in writing. i voted in favour because i am convinced that there is a need to provide a clear definition of the type of permanent geographical, natural and demographic disadvantages that island regions may suffer, in accordance with article 174 tfeu. it is important to bear in mind the importance of providing support to combat the trend towards considerable depopulation in island regions. the commission should establish an eu strategic framework for islands with the aim of linking instruments that can have a strong territorial impact.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour because we agree that, in accordance with council directive 2006/112/ec, certain european islands (including the outermost region of the canary islands) should be granted special tax treatment to correct inequalities due to multiple causes related to their insularity.
in writing. ‒ island regions need special treatment and solidarity from the european union as a whole to compensate for the differences that cause their inhabitants to have fewer opportunities than those living on the mainland. europe must continue to work to promote the harmonious development of all its territories and that is why measures must be taken for those regions which suffer from geographical disadvantages, as is clearly the case with the islands. the islands which are also ultraperipheral regions, such as my own country, the canary islands, require special sensitivity in this respect. i therefore support this motion for a resolution in which we take up a good part of the challenges facing these territories and the need for the eu to continue to support their development.

in writing. ‒ in accordance with article 174 tfeu, island regions should be the subject of a thorough study and analysis by the european commission in the coming months, in order to better understand the current situation in order to be able to adapt future relevant actions to a changing reality. i think this is an important request and therefore i think it necessary to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the resolution presented today makes it possible to take a further step towards the correct and more efficient allocation of the european structural and investment funds by local and regional authorities, through increased participation in all project phases, including through new tools such as integrated territorial investments or participatory local development. however, it is always good to remember that cohesion and regional development policy must be subject to the principle of reducing disparities between european regions. however, the need for synergies between these funds and the european fund for strategic investments (juncker plan) is becoming more frequent, as the new dutch presidency of the council is pushing for a pact that gives preference to large urban areas, which will undoubtedly tend to widen the disparities if not remedied. i believe, however, that the resolution itself is positive and can lead to improved communication and administrative and financial cooperation between local, regional and state authorities, as well as with the european institutions. i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. we voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, as it calls for the role of regional and local authorities in the management of the esi funds, as these are the bodies which are closest to the citizens and have the powers to carry out much of the policies for which these funds are designed. we believe that citizen participation is key to the management of these funds and to european policies in general, and that the esi funds are of great importance in the pursuit of development and cohesion between different regions and peoples. we are, however, reluctant to vote against paragraph 2, which leaves a veiled door open to reducing these funds on the basis of criteria of coherence and effectiveness. this is contrary to our view that these funds should be increased and always be guided by criteria of social cohesion, development and redistribution, giving more resources to local entities so that they can pursue these objectives.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this motion for a resolution on the role of local and regional authorities in the management of the european structural and investment funds. these bodies play a key role in shaping and implementing the eu strategy. in addition, synergies and complementarities between the esi funds and other eu programmes can be very useful for local and regional authorities to play a key role in european integration.
in writing. ‒ regional and local authorities with a federal structure have greater latitude to develop national policies that have an impact at regional and local level. as regards cohesion policy, the level of development of consultations with regional and local authorities has increased over time. however, this level of development varies between countries. regional and local authorities are closer to citizens and have a better understanding of their own needs to improve citizens' lives and to promote economic growth and sustainable job creation. these entities therefore need more budget support and a higher level of co-financing of projects. for these reasons, i support the resolution adopted by the european parliament to correct these shortcomings and to define what concrete support is proposed to be provided to regional and local authorities in the management of the esi funds during the period 2014-2020, as well as to launch a public consultation on how to strengthen the role of regional and local authorities.

in writing. ‒ for too long, yemeni governments have not fulfilled the democratic, economic and social aspirations of the yemeni people. i express my deep concern at the ongoing violence in yemen and the resultant humanitarian crisis affecting millions of innocent men, women and children i strongly support the efforts of the un special envoy, ismail ould cheikh ahmed, to find a lasting and peaceful resolution to the current crisis. i believe that saudi arabia and iran hold the key to resolving the crisis, and urge both to work to improve bilateral relations and to seek to work together to end the fighting in yemen. the only long-term solution to the crisis in yemen is via inclusive political dialogue, in line with the framework provided by the gulf cooperation council initiative, the outcomes of the national dialogue conference, and the various un security council and european council conclusions.

in writing. ‒ we abstained in this resolution because the text appeals to the responsibility to protect (r2p), which is at the origin of the disastrous military interventions that have caused destabilization in the region. those who supported r2p also supported the jihadist "rebels" who today attack religious minorities. we strongly condemn the killing of civilians, including religious, ethnic and other minorities, but we are against the eu's exploitation and use of certain religions. we have opposed the extension of the powers of the eu's external action by creating a high representative for freedom of religion or belief, because we believe that his work would overlap with that of the high representative for foreign affairs and security policy and could be counterproductive if it reproduced the parliamentary reality, which prioritizes attention to certain faiths over others, which can contribute to islamophobia. that is why we have abstained in this resolution.
in writing. we abstain in the vote on this resolution because we believe that: 1) the call to accept the jurisdiction of the international criminal court must also be addressed to the united states, china, india and all states, and not limited to syria and iraq; 2) any authorized intervention must be of a civil and humanitarian nature and not military; 3) the use of the concept of genocide with a much wider spectrum than that granted to it in the framework of the international criminal court (apart from the case of the yazidis) is problematic; 4) abstention is intended to avoid affecting ethnic or religious discrimination against the victims of this atrocity which, of course, we condemn. pointing to certain religions as victims (such as the christian) and others as culprits (the muslim, even though most of isis's crimes are committed against muslims) only serves to fuel the interreligious hatred and clash of civilizations that the promoters of texts like this one seek to base and justify their self-serving warmongering on.

madam president, we have presented a good report from the committee on employment and social affairs, a very good report which contrasts, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen of the council, with the reality you describe, with a reality which is very much in line with the reality of citizens in the vast majority of the countries of the european union. the truth is that we've had two years of recovery, but it's true that it's a slow recovery, it's a weak recovery and, above all, it's a deeply uneven recovery. we're told that in all the international reports. for example, the oecd - i never tire of saying this - is telling us that the gap between the poorest 10% and the richest 10% has increased sevenfold since the beginning of the crisis, in some countries like mine. and you paint, as i say, a picture too flattering, even with the reality we are seeing, with the new economic and social uncertainties that are hitting us. and to that end, we in the committee on employment and social affairs, the socialist group, ask you to do three things. first, they should boost investment. secondly, that they correct the excesses of the policy of excessive austerity which has been carried out in both labour and structural reforms, and above all, which have attacked the european social model. and thirdly, to build and strengthen the euro area, the social dimension of our common currency. we need to reinforce investments. if we don't invest, if we don't create countercyclical policy in this new climate of economic uncertainty, we will not have learned from the mistakes of the past. we have the juncker plan, but the juncker plan is not having the effect of increasing investment in the euro area. do you know that compared to, say, the united kingdom or, say, the united states, which have increased investment in the last two years, last year in the euro area we continued to decrease overall investment compared to, say, the 2013-2014 period? that social policy matters fall within the competence of member states. they do not wish to give in on national sovereignty through the semester process. however, all member states – and this is the good news – stress that a revamped european semester should continue to ensure that necessary structural reforms are implemented to address social and employment challenges and continually improve social and employment outcomes, taking into account the targets set in the europe 2020 strategy with regard to increasing employment, fighting poverty and social inclusion. many of you also emphasised in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation by which parliament gives its consent to the accession of austria and malta to the hague convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters. the hague convention of 15 november 1965 establishes a system whereby documents may be served on or transferred to another signatory state. of the 28 member states, 26 already apply the convention. since the eu has acquired exclusive competence for the service and transmission of cross-border documents, it is necessary for the union to give its authorisation to these two member states for their accession to the convention.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 seeks to harmonise legal rules by establishing a system whereby documents from one state can be used in another signatory state, covering for example different matters such as the law applicable to maintenance obligations, road traffic accidents, liability in tort or in matrimonial matters and succession. at present, 26 of the 28 eu member states are already applying the convention, and the remaining two, austria and malta, have indicated their wish to join. the committee on legal affairs adopted the report on the draft council decision authorising austria and malta to sign and ratify the convention. since this convention has proved useful and it is in the eu's interest to establish a single regime for the transfer of documents in crossborder relations with third countries, i am in favour of parliament giving its consent to the proposal for a decision to allow austria and malta to accede to the convention.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation by which parliament gives its consent to the accession of austria and malta to the hague convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters. the hague convention of 15 november 1965 establishes a system whereby documents may be served or transferred to another signatory state. of the 28 member states, 26 already apply the convention. since the eu has acquired exclusive competence for the service and transmission of cross-border documents, it is necessary for the union to give its authorisation to these two member states for their accession to the convention.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which is a recommendation for accession to the hague convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters. all the member states, in addition to malta and austria, have already signed this convention, which is of a procedural nature.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation that austria sign and ratify the hague convention and that malta accede to it, as these two member states are not yet parties to the convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters. as this is a convention which facilitates procedural aspects and has already been ratified by all the member states except these two, i have had no problem in voting in favour of malta and austria signing it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this purely technical report which allows austria and malta to apply the convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters.
in writing. ‒ we are talking about a decision that would bring the two countries that have yet to join the convention into the convention, out of the 28 member states. the eu as a whole would thus have a single regime for the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters. by this decision parliament would give its consent to the proposal for a council decision, and i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this international agreement with san marino on the automatic exchange of tax information because it is a major step forward in the fight against tax evasion and avoidance, particularly in third countries by natural or legal persons who are nationals of a member state of the union.
in writing. ‒ the text of the agreement obliges san marino to apply financial account reporting standards equivalent to those of the european legislative framework, which will allow for stronger controls on tax fraud and tax evasion. it is not enough, but it is a step in the right direction, and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which establishes an agreement between the union and san marino establishing a cooperation framework for the exchange of convergent tax information which already operates between member states. this agreement relates only to taxes on interest received by savers as creditors. the agreement makes progress in combating tax avoidance and tax evasion and facilitating transparency.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the eu-san marino agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts. this will mean that from 2017 onwards they will exchange information on the bank accounts of european residents in the country and sanmarinese residents in the eu and it will be more difficult for eu citizens to evade taxes by opening bank accounts in that country. the agreement will also enable tax authorities in the 28 member states to correctly identify the taxpayers involved, enforce tax rules in cross-border situations, assess the possibility of tax evasion and avoid unnecessary investigations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution by which parliament approves the conclusion of the agreement with san marino on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts with a view to improving tax cooperation and compliance with international tax obligations. the agreement takes further steps in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion by establishing an automatic exchange of information on the financial accounts of their respective residents between the parties as from 2017. this will help to deal with situations where a taxpayer tries to conceal assets representing income or assets on which taxes have not been paid. it is also proposed to ensure that the information exchanged does not only relate to income such as interest or dividends, but also to account balances and income from the sale of financial assets. the agreement also ensures the unconditional exchange of information on request, in line with the latest developments in oecd and eu work in this area.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because, with croatia's accession to the convention, the european union's financial resources invested in the country are better protected against irregularities and potential fraud. the convention on the protection of the interests of the union provides for the inclusion in national criminal law of offences against resources and investments made by the eu in that country. that is why the accession agreement involves a better use of public resources, their defence and criminal prosecution in the event of fraud occurring within the borders of the state of croatia, obliging the national authorities to prosecute any type of crime in this area. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the treaty of accession of the republic of croatia of 2011 introduces a simplified system for the accession of croatia to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states on the basis of article 34 teu. the act of accession provides that croatia accedes to these conventions and protocols and sets out in annex i the list of conventions and protocols concerned. that list includes the convention of 26 july 1995 on the protection of the european communities' financial interests, the protocol of 27 september 1996, the protocol of 29 november 1996 and the second protocol of 19 june 1997, which are intended to establish a common basis for the criminal protection of the ec's financial interests. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it approves the agreement with the council to launch a series of measures to improve the intra-european labour mobility platform called eures, which has been in existence since 1993. among the advances to be achieved, thanks to the socialist group's push, are the fact that the eures web portal will finally become a european platform for the exchange of job vacancies and cvs; that the new intelligent database, with the new it platform, will allow the automatic cross-matching of cvs with job vacancies; and that all vacancies published by public or private employment agencies will be published throughout the eu. eures will also involve the social partners at all levels of the network, eliminate fees for basic services for workers and ensure that traineeships and apprenticeships offered under it comply with eu standards and member states' social and employment rules. i believe that the agreement as a whole is in line with the objectives and priorities of the socialist group and represents progress for the workers and citizens of europe.
in writing. ‒ the eures platform should serve to support the fair mobility of european workers by facilitating the exchange of information on job offers and demands and by creating a stable structure of support and information services for migrant workers within the eu. both the involvement of social partners and the central role reserved for public employment services act as a brake on possible abuses such as those recorded in the past. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative proposal which aims to facilitate workers' access to services supporting intra-european labour mobility, to support fairer mobility and to increase access to employment opportunities in the union through the revision of eures. the report ensures the recognition of crossborder agreements with their own objectives and special competences, in particular for frontier workers; the social partners are included in the eures bodies at european and national level, and eures will provide information, with special tailored guidance for workers. information to be provided to workers (on the country to which they move, placement options) will generally be free of charge, while employers may be charged for special services (eures may offer post-employment services but for a fee). employees must also give their consent to the posting of job applications and cvs on the network and can withdraw their consent. for all these reasons, amongst others, i think it is a positive report and i have voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ this proposal for a regulation aims to improve workers' access to mobility support services within the eu by maintaining the eures network as an effective tool for jobseekers. it must be borne in mind that it must also continue to respect the fact that labour market policies remain the responsibility of the member states. moreover, the purpose of the regulation is not only to facilitate the exercise of freedom of movement for workers within the union but also to eliminate any discrimination based on nationality between workers of the member states as regards employment, remuneration and other conditions of work and employment in the union. in this connection, the agreed text lays down specific rules and provisions concerning the mobility of workers in border regions, services provided to jobseekers to ensure fair mobility and the effective promotion of the eures network at union level through intensive communication measures adopted by the commission and, in particular, by the member states.

madam president, tunisia has made very important democratic progress in recent years. it is a key partner of the european union for the development of democracy and human rights in the maghreb, an example of validation of the arab spring. that is why we must give it our strongest support in this road to recovery and that is why i voted in favour of introducing emergency trade measures in tunisia, but i do not agree to incorporate the amendments which were intended to give a protectionist and healing approach to oil. as a member of this parliament originally from spain, i of course see the need to be careful, to see the impact and to establish the measures already envisaged in this resolution as far as protection is concerned, but we have to support everything that means its development, and that is why i also want to reflect that i miss a permanent appeal to tunisia to defend human rights at the highest level and, specifically, to stop harassing the lgbti community, because it is a lackey that does not have to allow itself on this path to democracy.
madam president, i voted against because i am sure that these measures are not helping the people or the farmers of tunisia: the commission has already taken measures to reduce the cost of olive oil, which will be harmful to small and mediumsized producers in the southern countries and also in tunisia. there is also no guarantee that this olive oil will not be brought to the european market below the real costs of production and there are also no guarantees that there will be no ecological and social dumping.
in writing. ‒ the socialists in the ep believe that tunisia's geopolitical situation deserves full support and solidarity from the eu. however, we are not in favour of the burden of this being borne exclusively by farmers in southern europe and without any minimum guarantees for the european olive oil sector, on which the economy of large parts of the eu depends. the duty-free quota enjoyed by that country is supplemented by a supplementary quota of 35 000 tonnes of olive oil for the years 2016 and 2017. we are concerned that this type of measure is being taken without prior impact studies and by abolishing the monthly certificates that step up the entry to the eu oil market. we have won support for two amendments which deal with the solely tunisian origin of the oil and reinforce the temporary nature of the tonnage increase, by disconnecting this emergency measure from the ongoing negotiations on the eu-tunisia association agreement. the final vote was postponed in order to negotiate with the council the two new texts put forward by the spanish socialist delegation.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the introduction of autonomous emergency trade measures for tunisia because i am convinced that these measures are not to help the people or the tunisian farmers, but are measures to lower the cost of olives, which will harm small and medium-sized producers in the countries of southern europe and also in tunisia. nor is there any guarantee that this oil will not enter the european union at a price below the real costs of production or that there will be no ecological or social dumping. for these reasons i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted against these extraordinary trade measures because i believe that, firstly, they do not correspond to the original meaning of the council's mandate, since they do not favour the whole of the tunisian economy and society but only olive oil producing companies with export capacity. the report also does not provide for sufficiently guaranteed compensation mechanisms in the event of a fall in olive oil prices in europe, which could have a negative impact on european olive oil producers, particularly italian and spanish. finally, these extraordinary measures appear to open the door to a permanent increase in the quota of tunisian oil imported under the eu-tunisia free trade agreement, which is currently being negotiated.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work she has done on the report and i welcome the adoption of the proposal for a regulation on the introduction of emergency autonomous trade measures for tunisia. i should also like to point out that i did not follow the group's line on amendments nos 11, 12, 13 and 14, which referred to olive oil. i have supported more duty-free olive oil imports to help tunisia, but guarantees are needed.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to ensure that urgent measures are taken to improve tunisia's economic situation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, as it allows the mobilisation of eur 1 095 544 following the dismissal of 412 workers following the closure of a production plant in roux (hainaut) owned by agc europe sa and of another 268 following the closure of the production plant in auvelais (namur region) owned by saint-gobain glass benelux, both plants located in belgium. this mobilization of funds is aimed at mitigating the disastrous social consequences of the economic crisis of the capitalist system. while these funds are not able to solve the problems of these belgian workers, given the high unemployment rates in the region, they at least offer the possibility of alleviating a small part of the human drama. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it calls for funds to compensate and provide compensatory measures in cases of relocation or closure of companies due to structural changes in markets due to globalisation. the funds will be used to help workers made redundant and young people without education or employment in two regions of belgium (haianut and namur) following the closure of two glass factories. these are measures which, if they were not taken, would leave the workers concerned in a worse position. the vote in favour, however, does not hide the fact that this type of measure is 'bread for today and hunger for tomorrow', while the question of employment and relocations should be approached differently. on the one hand, europe needs an investment plan that is very different from juncker's and another employment policy to act on employment. secondly, this alternative should consist in investing in activities for the future, especially in a change of production model.
in writing. ‒ i have supported, as on other occasions, the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, this time for hainaut-namur glass in belgium, where the beneficiaries would be 412 workers made redundant in the manufacture of other non-metallic mineral products. the redundancies were due, according to the belgian authorities, to the transformation which has taken place in the european glass sector and especially in that country in recent years. i hope that the mobilisation of this fund will help to alleviate somewhat the situation of those affected.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to approve the mobilisation of eur 1 095 544 from the globalisation adjustment fund for 412 workers who have lost their jobs at hainaut-namur glass, which operates in the glass production sector in the walloon region. these redundancies are due to the changes in the european glass sector, and especially in belgium, in recent years, which have had a major impact on the glass production sector in wallonia. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the aid is compatible with the internal market. the personalised services to be financed by the egf include guidance actions, job search assistance, integrated training, transfer of experience and support for the creation of businesses and collective projects. individual services will also be provided to 100 young people under 25 from the hainaut region who are not in employment, education or training.

in writing. ‒ voted in favour of this document relating to the use of the european globalisation adjustment fund (established to provide additional support for workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns) in response to the proposal for a decision to mobilise the egf in favour of belgium to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant in two enterprises operating in nace revision 2 division 23 (manufacture of other non-metallic mineral products) in the nuts level 2 regions of hainaut (be32) and namur (be35) in belgium.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mobilising this fund to help alleviate the economic effects of globalisation and, in particular, the loss of jobs due to relocations.
in writing. ‒ we are talking about a fund which is responsible for processing transfers of funds to cover maximum redundancy payments for the cessation of different business activities in the member states. in this case we are talking about a transfer that comes to cushion to some extent a 19% fall in employment in the period 2007-2012 and 1 236 jobs lost in 2013 in the walloon region of belgium. it is therefore appropriate to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that in the context of the global economic slowdown, the union must strengthen its domestic demand more than ever to achieve higher economic growth, reduce inequalities, create more quality jobs and improve social cohesion. less competitive countries should invest more in improving their productivity, rather than competing with falling wages and reducing public services. at the same time, the eu member states with stronger economies must step up their efforts to support domestic demand through increased public and private investment and higher wages. the euro area is a large economy which must be treated as such and must work towards upward convergence, with employment and social indicators at the same level as existing indicators. finally, i voted in favour of this report because it states the need for further reforms, yes, but reforms to improve the quality of education systems, invest in innovation, modernise public administration and make a more efficient use of natural resources.
in writing. ‒ due to the growing resistance to the economic governance framework and its harmful effects on the popular classes, several proposals insist on making up the european semester by augmenting it with redistributive social policies or elements of democratic supervision while maintaining the 'deepening' (in the union's jargon) of its economic policies. since the neoliberal keyword 'individualisation of labour relations and the orientation of public policies towards private profit' is not in question, i have voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report from parliament. the european semester is the mechanism by which the union is currently trying to make effective compliance with the stability and growth pact deficit and debt control, in addition to other metrics. i am opposed to these objectives, which are to restrict the economies of the various states on the basis of neoliberal criteria. the european semester is a procedure whereby the commission reviews national budgets before they are adopted by parliaments and issues country-specific recommendations to be implemented in the budgets of the following year. i am also opposed to this method which clearly infringes the sovereignty of the member states.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of this report on the european semester for economic policy coordination. unlike my group, i have supported this report and i have supported certain amendments which i believe have improved the text. i agree with the concern that the proposed policy mix does not adequately address the problem of increasing poverty, inequalities and social exclusion in the union. i also abstained on an amendment referring to the request for the suspension of the ongoing negotiations on the atci and acp. not because i do not agree with it, but because the second part of the amendment was about granting china market economy status. this would have a negative impact, for example, on the european steel industry and more specifically on the basque steel industry.

in writing. ‒ due to the growing resistance to the economic governance framework and its harmful effects on the popular classes, several proposals insist on making up the european semester by augmenting it with redistributive social policies or elements of democratic supervision while maintaining the 'deepening' (in the union's jargon) of its economic policies. since the neoliberal keyword 'individualisation of labour relations and the orientation of public policies towards private profit' is not in question, i have voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ i have voted against this report as it is quite biased against surplus countries without taking into account that most of their surplus exports are outside the eu. with china’s slowdown and the arrival of 1 million refugees, the surplus will go down by itself. moreover it includes a mention in the commission communication that enables member states to get fiscal flexibility just by announcing reforms (not approving/implementing them as would be logical) and lastly, it misrepresents the objectives of efsi and does not clarify that only economically viable projects should receive its financing to avoid having more airports without planes, motorways without traffic and high speed trains without passengers.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it imposes a vision of economic governance based on austerity and structural reforms which involve a massive loss of social rights.
in writing. ‒ the annual growth survey 2016 proposes to relaunch investment through the investment plan for europe, boosting investment projects, completing the banking union and accelerating work on the capital markets union, boosting investment in human capital and reforms of education and training systems to boost employment and sustainable growth, continuing the implementation of structural reforms to modernise the economy and implementing responsible fiscal policies. we are talking about a series of proposals which seek to return to a path of sustainable long-term growth in order to create jobs in europe, and i therefore think it necessary to vote in favour of them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that economic recovery must be fair, create quality jobs, reduce inequalities and fight poverty and social exclusion. we need an upward social convergence in europe, with socially responsible reforms based on solidarity, social integration, social justice and a fair distribution of wealth. investment in social development should not simply be a means to enhance economic growth, but an end in itself. we need more investment in social protection systems to combat poverty and to fight against growing inequalities. it also treats the euro area as one economy in need of deeper integration, with a strengthened social dimension, better social protection and minimum wage floors, and a strong pillar of social rights. finally, i have supported this report because it shows us the reality of the data and forgets the complacency of the commission. employment is being created, but it is precarious, with unfair wages, unfair working conditions and precarious jobs. there is no greater betrayal of the social model than the fact that poverty in the workplace is one of the main problems in europe today.
in writing. ‒ the timid social reforms proposed in this report are incompatible in practice with an economic framework whose guiding principles will remain the neoliberal economic policies, to which they serve as a legitimization mechanism. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ while this report on the annual growth survey sent by the commission as part of the european semester on employment and social aspects mentions three positive social indicators from my point of view activity rate, youth unemployment and long-term unemployment in the alert mechanism report 2016, it does follow the economistic logic of the european semester and focuses on neoliberal recipes for the dramatic problem of employment and poverty. that is why i voted against. concepts that place economic benefits above quantity, quality and dignity in employment are recurrent, such as: competitiveness, productivity, entrepreneurship, flexicurity, legislation on the labour law system, deregulation of the labour market, reduction of taxes and wage costs, skills to boost innovation and competitiveness, segmentation of the labour market and simplification of labour protection legislation (which would affect, among other things, unfair dismissals), etc. in the commitments, both the most critical aspects of the annual growth survey process as a whole and the most progressive amendments in specific aspects have not been incorporated, which underlines my refusal to support it.

i supported this report, which concerns the single market within the eu. personally, i regard the single market as one of the main benefits of european integration, apart from the political aspects of the 28 countries working together. i think that even those who are not in favour of further building a federal europe should see that the unification of the internal market is a clear advantage for citizens and for businesses, and i therefore also hope that we will be able to remove the obstacles that still exist in the single market in the future. i would personally consider it a great success if we were to push through some aspects of the digital single market in this election period, regulate the sale of goods online across national borders, solve the issue of geoblocking, etc. this is all the subject of this report, which is why i supported it, and as i said, i am convinced that by strengthening the single market we will increase the efficiency of the european economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it stresses that if the european semester is to be a successful instrument for promoting economic growth and acting as a stabilising tool for economies, it must also include the single market and the policies aimed at its full realisation. the single market is the cornerstone of member states' economies and the european integration project, bringing economic benefits such as increased competition and a level playing field for 500 million consumers in the eu, in particular greater choice of quality products and services at lower prices. as a socialist, i believe that the key to unlocking the full potential of the estimated €1 trillion single market lies in the respect and application of existing union law in our member states, and i believe that better governance and greater transparency of their integration process are vital for job creation, sustainable growth and competitiveness in our influential single market.
in writing. ‒ the deepening of the single market, following the recommendations of the european semester, will continue the regression in social and democratic rights experienced in recent years, by placing pseudo-market freedoms against labour rights and the sovereignty of the european peoples. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted against, because the report sees the single market as the only way to create jobs, growth and competitiveness, and it can only be done within the framework of the european semester. the european semester and the five presidents' report represent a frontal attack on national and economic sovereignty - any tax reform or wage policy measure must be approved by national competitiveness committees, which are tools created for budgetary union - and represent an oligarchic and authoritarian institutional architecture with an absence of absolute democracy. i therefore reject any measure within the framework of the european semester and the report of the five presidents.
