in writing. ‒ today, the consumption of fresh fruit, vegetables and dairy products is declining, especially among children. in addition, the trend toward eating highly processed foods high in sugars and fats is causing an increase in overweight among them. the european parliament therefore intends to provide a series of grants to the member states to finance the supply of a selection of products to schools which promote healthy eating habits. these grants will be allocated to each member state according to the number of children aged between six and ten years in that member state and the level of development of that member state, in order to ensure greater support for those regions which are less developed. i have always considered investing in children to be a priority, and i believe that the adoption of this report is necessary because it will soon enable european children to benefit from milk, fruit and vegetable distribution systems in the best-funded schools, supplemented by programmes to teach them healthy eating habits.
in writing. ‒ fruit and milk consumption programmes are vital to promote the consumption of foods beneficial to public health. these programmes have also proved to be effective in terms of teaching people how to adopt healthy habits. the strengthening of the educational dimension is one of the novel elements of this new proposal, which will allow for further in-depth study of agricultural, nutritional and environmental issues. i can only vote in favour of a proposal which is fundamental for all the reasons mentioned above and which comes at a time when child poverty and, paradoxically, child obesity are reaching really worrying figures in europe.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this dossier because, among other reasons, the council conceded to parliament that all budgetary measures relating to this file should be decided by co-decision (article 43(2)) and not by the council alone. this is an important procedural victory, after the council refused to negotiate on the budgetary aspects of cap reform, and we intend to use it as a precedent for future files. i also voted in favour because the text also provides a number of important safeguards. firstly, the eu will only pay for the milk part of the product, i.e. the added flavouring would have to be paid for by the member state. secondly, national health authorities must approve the list of products to be distributed. thirdly, added salt, sugar and fat can only be added to the extent that they are technically necessary to manufacture the product, and must be approved by national health authorities. finally, and for the first time, added sweeteners and added flavour enhancers (e620 to 650) are banned entirely from the programme.
in writing. ‒ we are talking about a proposal that reorients the current organisation of the two programmes currently in force towards the achievement of long-term objectives and that allows for the reinforcement of the educational dimension of both regimes and helps to connect young europeans with food and its sources, as well as unifying and consolidating the legal and financial frameworks of both programmes, currently separate, and increasing the visibility of eu intervention, maximising effectiveness, management and coherence with the cap. it is a very positive proposal to promote the consumption of these products of great importance to the eu and to help european children to acquire healthier eating habits. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ as the report points out, the consumption of fruit, vegetables and dairy products has declined considerably among the young population in the eu in recent years. this is worrying, because it means that this sector of the population is not getting a very healthy diet, which will undoubtedly have a negative influence on their health and their school performance. i therefore have full confidence in the proposal in this report, because it will not only improve the quality of life of students, but will also be very positive for producers. the latter will have a new niche of customers, which will contribute to the increase of their income.
in writing. ‒ the parliament's report contains substantial improvements on the commission's proposal: for the third time, this house is opposed to the liberalisation of the port sector (although we fear that a new proposal in this regard will come in the coming months). in addition, work with european trade unions has introduced recognition of the rights to training, health and safety at work for port workers, although weaknesses remain in the effective implementation of this rule and in aspects such as the protection of labour rights in the event of port services being transferred. however, some aspects of the commission's initial proposal (in the financial transparency sections) open the door for competition policy to attack essential aspects of the public financing and management of ports. i have therefore decided to abstain, pending the final proposal after the negotiations with the council.
in writing. ‒ we abstained in the final vote on the third attempt to liberalise port services because, despite the improvement of the social aspects and, in particular, the staff subrogation, the text adopted still raises a number of reservations. we welcome the socialist proposal for greater transparency in the sources of financing for ports, which will help to verify the state aid received by ports in central and northern europe, all the more so as this adoption coincides with the new commission proposal to exempt aid for port infrastructure from ex ante competition control. in addition, and in the face of the commission's interest in deregulating port tariffs, the spanish socialists are following the mandate of the current spanish constitution to adopt these tariffs by the congress, since it maintains in a solidarity-based way the current network of our ports, which would otherwise see their presence in the territory reduced, without thereby improving competition with european ports. we are, however, voting for the rapporteur's abstention, who has recognised the peculiarity of spanish working in tripartite dialogues with the council.
in writing. ‒ i believe that this proposal for a regulation on market access for port services and financial transparency of ports can be positive in some respects, such as the one aimed at improving the performance of ports in the european union. however, other aspects, such as article 14 (3) of the commission proposal, are contrary to spanish interests. this article provides for the autonomy of the managing body of the port to establish various matters such as the structure or level of port infrastructure charges in accordance with its own commercial strategy and investment plan. in spain, this type of port charges is required for the special use of the public port domain. the constitution provides that their establishment is subject to the principle of reservation of law and, therefore, they must be fixed by the congress of deputies. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ we have voted in favour of the fleckenstein report. the commission's original proposal (2013), widely rejected by trade unions and port managers, was substantially amended in this legislature, given commissioner bulc's position not to include the opening of the market for port services. in this respect, the rapporteur has produced a report which differs significantly from the original proposal in that it addresses the demands of the different sectors involved. the negotiations on the commitments included aspects which, although not meeting all our objectives, represent important progress in social and labour matters, as well as improvements in the efficiency and transparency of port management, which could be lost in future legislative initiatives if the report is rejected. it is also a good basis for further negotiation with the council.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is particularly necessary for the eu to regulate the union's ports definitively. it is important to advance policies to modernise port operations and services, while combating possible market abuse, to improve port services performance and transparency and to set port tariffs autonomously in each port. this will avoid an additional burden for those ports that are already functioning well, while at the same time creating the conditions for other ports to be able to cope with their structural challenges. it is important that the european parliament should recognise the good management of some ports and should be committed to their autonomy.

in writing. ‒ we reject the proposal to improve the functioning of eu ports, as we consider that it may be harmful for spain. this proposal is not in the general interest and, moreover, it interferes with the powers of the member states, which are an essential part of their organization and their economic system.
in writing. ‒ the objective of this proposal for a regulation is to remove restrictions on the provision of port services and to increase transparency in funding. the aim is to liberalize port services. although i agree with the content of this proposal in general, there are some legal problems with regard to port infrastructure charges. in spain, ports are public property and the fees are those charged for the use or exploitation of the public port space. in short, we have a state port policy which would be strongly affected by privatisation. i think that the proposal does not take account of the different realities and does not maintain the requirement of the principle of subsidiarity in the determination of rates. i cannot therefore support the proposal for a regulation as it stands.
in writing. ‒ we have voted in favour of the fleckenstein report. the commission's original proposal (2013), widely rejected by trade unions and port managers, was substantially amended in this legislature, given commissioner bulc's position not to include the opening of the market for port services. in this respect, the rapporteur has produced a report which differs significantly from the original proposal in that it addresses the demands of the different sectors involved. the negotiations on the commitments included aspects which, although not meeting all our objectives, represent important progress in social and labour matters, as well as improvements in the efficiency and transparency of port management, which could be lost in future legislative initiatives if the report is rejected. it is also a good basis for further negotiation with the council.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this regulation because i believe that real competition among ports is fundamental in order to achieve real and sustainable economic growth. only if every region is able to compete will europe regain its lost economic strength. the state monopolies from the south like puertos del estado in spain and their centralised management are a drag on the economic growth of europe.

in writing. ‒ i abstained from the final vote on this report. the report is generally very negative in terms of environmental regulation of ports and certain social criteria. but it contained an important and very positive element for decentralised port management, namely the decentralisation of the tariff system, introduced by an amendment of the committee on transport which i voted in favour of in the plenary. it is precisely because of this positive element that i abstained from voting, since the report is negative because of its content, which is both left-wing and environmentalist, and we hope that it will be improved in the tripartite dialogues.
in writing. ‒ we abstained in the final vote on the third attempt to liberalise port services because, despite the improvement of the social aspects and, in particular, the staff subrogation, the text adopted still raises a number of reservations. we welcome the socialist proposal for greater transparency in the sources of financing for ports, which will help to verify the state aid received by ports in central and northern europe, all the more so as this adoption coincides with the new commission proposal to exempt aid for port infrastructure from ex ante competition control. in addition, and in the face of the commission's interest in deregulating port tariffs, the spanish socialists are following the mandate of the current spanish constitution to adopt these tariffs by the congress, since it maintains in a solidarity-based way the current network of our ports, which would otherwise see their presence in the territory reduced, without thereby improving competition with european ports. we are, however, voting for the rapporteur's abstention, who has recognised the peculiarity of spanish working in tripartite dialogues with the council.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation updating the statistical methodology for the compilation of a harmonised index of consumer prices, as this is essential to have accurate data on the inflation rate, both in the eu and in the eurozone. the regulation also recognises, on the initiative of the spanish socialists, that consumer price statistics are a public good.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote against this report because it leaves the european commission with a number of powers to define the key details in relation to the definition of this price index which is fundamental to the living conditions of workers in the european union. the report gives the commission the power to amend the list of products to be considered in the compilation of this index, even mentioning the possibility of including products such as certain types of drugs or activities such as prostitution. given the effects that such inclusions can have, and especially the legitimizing effect on these activities that decisions like these would have, i have decided to vote against this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation because of the need to update the reference period for price indices so that they are comparable and relevant. the harmonised indices of consumer prices are a key tool for achieving the price stability objective of the european system of central banks and therefore for defining the monetary policy of the euro area countries.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report which amends the criteria used for monitoring consumer product prices in the eu. these indices are a fundamental tool for the adoption of certain macroeconomic decisions. we find it problematic that the commission is given a high degree of discretion to modify these criteria by means of delegated acts, and that the door is opened to the inclusion of concepts such as prostitution, gambling, narcotics and others in the indices.
in writing. ‒ i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his work in reaching agreement on this regulation on harmonised indices of consumer prices. it establishes a uniform legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of consumer price and house price indices data at union, national and sub-national level. there will be experimental studies funded by the commission where appropriate and, in addition, every five years the commission will have to submit a report to the co-legislators assessing the main results of these studies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. this document aims to update the statistical methodology for the development of a harmonised index of consumer prices in the european union. the current regulation dates from 1995 and with the latest developments in consumer price statistics, a revision of the current framework was necessary to ensure maximum compatibility for the main users of the hicp. this update is also important for the stability and growth pact, as early provisional information on inflation is essential, especially for the management of monetary policy.

in writing. ‒ this report arises from the need to revise the 1995 regulation on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) in order to achieve maximum harmonisation among the main users of hicps. the fundamental role of hicps should be emphasised, as they provide information that is more than relevant to deflate economic values such as wages, rents or interest rates. they are also very useful for economic and monetary policy decisions. among other measures, the report calls for euro-area member states to provide monthly advance hicp indicators so that the european union can have early provisional information and be guided by it to conduct proper monetary policy management. in my view, this report should be adopted in order to establish a legal framework to support the production, development and dissemination of hicp and house price (hpv) data at union level.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on harmonised indices of consumer prices. i am confident that the new regulation will be a breakthrough in measuring prices, vital information which needs to be measured uniformly across europe to ensure that it has the effects we are looking for.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this first reading agreement because the regulation includes two key proposals suggested by the greens, namely:1) the commission shall prepare a report by the end of 2018, which shall address the suitability of the ooh price index for integration into hicp coverage. depending on the results of the report, within a reasonable timeframe, the commission shall submit, if appropriate, a proposal for amending this regulation with regard to integrating the ooh price index within the hicp framework. if the report establishes that further methodological developments are required for the integration of the ooh price index within the hicp framework, the commission will pursue the methodological work and report back to parliament and the council as appropriate;2) in addition to the hicp, research on a harmonised cost of living index should be initiated, although no specific details were provided on how such research will be carried on.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this legislation is to establish a common legal framework for the production of harmonised indices for the member states, which means collecting, compiling and processing harmonised consumer price indices. this will enable us to monitor the results of the eu's monetary policies and to make progress on price stability. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ the report contains several proposals to improve the fight against fraud and corruption in eu budgets, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ 80% of the union's budget is implemented by the member states and the commission. in addition to legislative and budgetary powers, meps have an important supervisory role. the report is critical to the management of expenditure and revenue of the union budget. of the total of 16 473 irregularities notified to the commission in 2014, 1 649 were fraudulent, i.e. eur 538,2 million. although i believe that the union's budget is being spent efficiently, there are still too many irregularities and therefore, as we ask in the report, the commission and the member states must take responsibility for them. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the report by the greens includes interesting elements in the control of the european institutions' spending, such as the development of results-based budgets including multiple indicators (also based on environmental issues). also the promotion of the european prosecutor, eppo, to fill the gaps of the current agencies. but the report also includes measures to require the harmonisation of the calculation of irregularities or fraud, with the aim of ranking countries according to the ratio of irregularity and fraud they achieve. the solution he seems to propose is to demand that payments from the european programmes to the countries concerned be stopped without making any distinction between the beneficiary population, civil servants, businesses and government. it also takes the side of the olaf monitoring committee, which reports to the council, which has been unprofessional and self-interested in its monitoring behaviour. in this balance we weigh abstention against whether it would remove the penalty for the countries or these considerations biased against olaf. the vote in favour was not mixed up because these are not the measures we would have proposed, apart from the mention of neoliberal elements in the model. it was proposed that this be done by separate votes. however, these points were not withdrawn and the vote was against.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report on the protection of the union's financial interests and the fight against fraud. it contains sections on the detection and reporting of irregularities, revenue and own resources, expenditure, the need for improved information and controls, among other things. the commission is asked to develop rigorous indicator systems and easily applicable uniform criteria based on the requirements of the stockholm programme to measure the level of corruption in the member states and to assess anti-corruption policies.
in writing. ‒ investing european taxpayers' money well is a requirement. we must therefore protect the eu's financial interests by fighting fraud and irregularities by all means possible. in the light of the data provided by this report, we must remain vigilant and redouble our efforts in this area, since the total amount of eu funds that have been misappropriated amounts to eur 3 240 million. the report stresses the need for simplification of procedures by the member states and the commission and for better information to the public in order to reduce non-fraudulent irregularities. the commission also commits itself to submitting a biannual report on the fight against corruption and to establishing a strict policy on suspension and interruption of payments in the event of a threat to the interests of the union. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because fraud and corruption are an obstacle to the eu's competitiveness in the global economy and put the well-being of all citizens at risk. the commission should continue to work to recover funds unduly paid from the eu budget and to improve the perception of own resources. the commission should also support the member states' actions in the fight against fraud and corruption.

in writing. ‒ in 2013, irregularities related to expenditure considered as fraudulent increased by 76%. in 2014, this figure was reduced by only 4%. that is why we believe that we have made efforts that are bearing fruit, but we still have a long way to go. the report calls on the commission to develop a system of uniform and easily applicable criteria, based on the requirements set out in the stockholm programme, to measure the level of corruption in the member states and thus to be able to assess the policies to be developed against corruption. another of the proposed measures is to simplify the rules, since many non-fraudulent irregularities are linked to insufficient knowledge of the rules. the rapporteur also calls on the member states to encourage the exchange of good practice and welcomes the fact that ex ante and ex post community controls are increasingly detecting cases of fraudulent irregularities. i believe that, given the importance of the subject under discussion, the adoption of this report is essential to achieve a more transparent and more homogeneous european union.
in writing. ‒ the 2014 annual report on the protection of the european union's financial interests the fight against fraud reminds us that corruption affects all member states and costs the eu economy around €120 billion a year. in order to combat fraud, it proposes measures such as improving information and controls, better regulating public procurement, budgeting on the basis of performance and profitability or strengthening the fight against tobacco smuggling and counterfeiting of products, which i fully share and for that reason i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ corruption costs us 120 billion a year and is linked to the financing of organised crime. this own-initiative report presents data on irregularities notified to the european commission which highlights the need for urgent and effective measures to help us in the fight against fraud. that is why it is important to support this text. the council is called upon to give new impetus to the negotiations on the pif directive in order to strengthen the existing legal framework by establishing common minimum standards for the definition of criminal offences affecting the financial interests of the union. the commission is also urged to harmonise and simplify the framework for reporting suspected fraud and to develop a system of rigorous indicators and uniform criteria, among other measures.
in writing. ‒ investing european taxpayers' money well is one of our priorities. that is why we must properly protect the eu's financial interests by fighting fraud and irregularities by all means possible. in the light of the data provided by this report, we must remain vigilant and redouble our efforts in this area, since the total amount of eu funds that have been misappropriated amounts to eur 3 240 million. the report stresses the need for simplification of procedures by the member states and the commission and for better information to the public in order to reduce non-fraudulent irregularities. the commission also commits itself to submitting a biannual report on anti-corruption and to establishing a strict policy on suspension and interruption of payments in the event of a threat to the interests of the union. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the report calls for stronger governance, transparency and control of the european bank and investment bank and recalls the responsibility of the european commission for the recovery of funds unduly paid from the community budget. in this context, the report also calls on the commission to make full use of its executive powers in areas such as vat fraud, to work more closely with member states to collect accurate data and to maintain a strict policy on interruptions and suspension of payments. i therefore think it is necessary to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is important to mainstream the gender perspective in the work of the european parliament and in all aspects of eu intervention, as well as in the preparation, design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, legal provisions and spending planning, in order to achieve equality between women and men. i also believe that the standard practice of each parliamentary committee appointing one of its members as responsible for gender mainstreaming, thus creating a 'gender mainstreaming network' which meets several times a year, and the high level group on gender equality, which also meets regularly, make an effective contribution to achieving this objective. both bodies are supported by the report, which also emphasises the need for 'gender mainstreaming amendments', which are being drawn up by the femm committee to incorporate the gender perspective into reports of other parliamentary committees. the report also advocates gender impact assessments and gender budgeting.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it proposes to mainstream the gender perspective in all policies and thus to continue to take steps forward in favour of gender equality, through specific measures to eliminate, prevent or remedy gender inequalities. the resolution stresses the need to develop amendments for gender mainstreaming, a gender situation assessment and a gender budget in order to mainstream gender in all policies. it also stressed the need for greater cooperation between committees. the report calls for a roadmap on gender equality, indicating how to increase female representation in middle and senior management positions to 40% by 2020. it also calls on the commission to assess the gender perspective in new policy or legislative proposals in order to ensure that the european union supports women's rights.

madam president, i still have in my ears the words of donald tusk last thursday, when he recommended that what he called 'illegal economic migrants' should stay in their countries and not come to the european union. these words are a death sentence for thousands of people fleeing war, horror and deprivation of rights, but, moreover, people are not illegal. on the contrary, they are protected by international law. as of january, 55 per cent of people fleeing are refugees, who face risks in their countries of origin, during transit and in the country of destination, such as violence, trafficking, exploitation, health risks, among others, which are aggravated in the case of women. it is necessary to open humanitarian corridors and facilitate entry through legal and safe channels to avoid these risks. i voted in favour of this report because it is a further step towards incorporating a human rights approach and protecting women by addressing their specific needs, but it is also essential to establish measures to ensure the integration of refugees.
madam president, we voted in favour of this report because today, 8 march, with thousands of women trapped at the borders, we must remember that the europe of walls, the europe of fences, the europe which condemns illegal migrants is the europe which is complicit in the labour and sexual exploitation of these women. women who are fighting to survive bombs, poverty, misery; women who are stopping evictions in spain, like the pah comrades; women who are fighting against the occupation of their territories, like the palestinians and the saharawis; women who are fighting against daesh, like the kurdish militiamen; or all those who in latin america are fighting against the criminal practices of the multinationals, like the indigenous leader berta cáceres, murdered in honduras. rebels and feminists, because without equality there is no emancipation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is important that asylum policies and procedures are gender sensitive. 55% of refugees arriving in europe are women, girls and boys. to ensure that women's specific needs are taken into account, it is necessary to promote gender-specific training, including gender-based violence, for staff; have gender-segregated health facilities and rooms; guarantee the right to request female interviewers and interpreters; ensure access to women's health services; provide childcare during examinations and interviews; inform women of their right to make an independent asylum application, etc. it is also urgent that there should be no more internments of children, pregnant women and survivors of rape, sexual assault and trafficking. and of course, measures are needed to integrate refugee and asylum seeker women into the labour market. the solution to the refugee crisis is not to send them back to turkey, but to create legal pathways for immigration and to implement integration policies. the dignity of the european project based on the principles of solidarity, justice and equality is at stake.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it sets out the policies needed to address the needs of asylum seekers and refugees. it contains various measures to ensure that women are given specific attention during the asylum process and in reception centres. as unicef reported last month, 60 percent of the refugees and migrants arriving are now women and children, while, in mid-2015, men made up 73 percent of the total displaced. the gender dimension of this massive displacement of people is therefore an essential factor that needs to be taken into account in order to provide an adequate and effective response. the report calls, inter alia, for special protection for the lgbti community and urges the member states and the eu to sign and ratify the istanbul convention. it also called for irregular migration not to impede access to eu asylum procedures and expressed deep concern about forced returns.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report on the situation of women refugees and asylum seekers in the eu. the report is positive in that it considers that asylum policies and procedures and the evaluation of applications should include a gender approach. it includes as grounds for asylum in the eu gender-based violence, rape, sexual violence, female mutilation, forced marriage or gender-based violence. it also includes the persecution and violence against lgbti groups. the report calls for measures to ensure that women's needs are met during the asylum process. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. it stresses that immigration policies and legislation should not prevent access to the eu asylum procedure. it stresses the importance of measures to promote employment. it calls for solidarity to be maintained between the eu countries and for the responsibility not to fall solely on the countries of first destination, which we believe is necessary.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it aims to correct the extremely vulnerable situation of refugee women within the european union. women fleeing persecution in their home states must face an extremely dangerous journey, facing risks such as attacks, rape, fraud, human trafficking and even death. these women, already extremely vulnerable in their home countries, face additional obstacles on their arrival in the european union, which increases their vulnerability. the report proposes that asylum procedures and policies, including the assessment of applications, should be gender sensitive, and calls for all issues of gender-based violence, such as rape, sexual violence, female genital mutilation, forced marriage or domestic violence, to be considered as valid reasons for asylum in the european union. it also focuses attention on the protection of the lgbti community and calls for an end to the detention of children, pregnant women seeking asylum, or survivors of rape, sexual violence and human trafficking. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament was the first international body to recognise, in its resolution of 13 april 1984, the need to carry out a gender-based interpretation of the refugee convention. these considerations have subsequently been taken into account by organisations such as unhcr and by many countries. approximately half of the world's refugees are women and girls. these groups are the most vulnerable and face specific risk situations such as trafficking or sexual violence. this report is of crucial importance because it reflects the specific situation of women and girls and calls for a broader reform of migration and asylum policies that takes into account the gender dimension. these include such important proposals as the signing and ratification of the istanbul convention, improving the safety and reception conditions of refugees, and providing additional resources to tackle trafficking in women and girls and sexual violence.

mr president, madam high representative, the cessation of hostilities is good news, especially because it leads to what we want, which is a political settlement that gives way to a lasting peace that guarantees the existence of the syrian state and that is not broken like other precedents. we have always supported mr. de mistura, but we must remember who did not. you should look at the log of sessions from two or three years ago or the statements of some leaders who said how well al-nusra was doing, that is al-qaeda, or the anti-daesh coalition 65 countries that did not change anything. now the tide has turned and we are seeing that an independent role for the european union is needed and the best way is to tell our partners in quotes, the saudi arabian and turkish governments, to stop financing, to stop tolerating and, above all, to tell the turkish government to break the truce, as it did just yesterday. we must go to geneva, as we have always said, with the government and the non-terrorist opposition present.
mr president, the ceasefire agreement in syria is a hopeful step and i hope it will be strengthened by the forthcoming talks in geneva. the ceasefire is not absolute - as has been said - but the violence has decreased considerably. anyway, this is good news. it is true that a ceasefire is not the solution to the conflict either. we need the upcoming negotiations to allow for progress towards a political solution in the terms agreed in the 2012 geneva communiqué and security council resolution 2254. the lack of progress in the political field would favour the consolidation of groups like daesh and the worsening of the humanitarian crisis, which has had such a negative impact on the european union. we are at a crucial moment and i welcome, mrs mogherini, your commitment to supporting and promoting the geneva talks and to alleviating the serious humanitarian situation afflicting the syrian people. but we also know that it is necessary for the syrian parties to the conflict and for international and regional actors to rise to the occasion so that the conflict in syria can finally move towards a stable solution and put an end to five years of confrontation.
mr president, our inaction has in this case caused a situation to collapse in syria. we have prolonged the war, there has been no solution to the problems that exist, and today we are faced with something that none of us likes, but it is the reality. in a war, the protagonists are not the ones we want, but the real ones. and today the protagonists are, on the one hand, the al-assad regime, which is simultaneously, contradictorily, the guarantee of its own security for the sunni middle classes, for the alawites certainly, and also for the christians, confronted with the wahhabis, either terrorists of jabhat al-nusra or - let's say - the allies of the west, ahrar al-sham, who are exactly the same, with more yaish al-islam. we have an absolute need to go to a peace process and we have a consequent need to recognise that it was the russian intervention which ultimately caused us to agree. to take a primary anti-russian position is to deny evidence: five years of war have ended with a ceasefire within months of russian action, which meant the reinforcement of a criminal but existing regime, that of al-assad. let us push forward the peace negotiations, let us have a proactive presence on the part of europe and let us fight effectively against terrorism, which we strategically do not do.
the first ceasefire in five years of war in syria came into force on saturday, 27 february, following the unanimous adoption of un security council resolution 2268. it is essential that it is fulfilled to allow unhindered access and distribution of humanitarian aid throughout syria. this truce will allow the united nations to re-convene the syrian talks in geneva and begin to create the conditions for the political transition agreed by the security council. the international community and the parties to the conflict have a responsibility to uphold the minimum agreements to save lives, and to bring syria to a peaceful solution. the war has already produced more than five million refugees, who must be taken into account. the eu, together with the us and russia, should share information to monitor compliance with the ceasefire and cooperate with syrian parties, excluding terrorist organisations, to focus on the reform roadmap towards a new syria. we join and support the united nations in declaring the need for a 'marshall plan' for syria.

president-in-office of the council.– madam president, i am very happy to be back in this chamber. the issue up for debate is one where we, as institutions, have come together and demonstrated our firm intent to strengthen our cooperation. i am pleased to mark this important step forward in our interinstitutional relations. with this new agreement we have jointly established a set of rules on how to ensure a better delivery for our citizens and businesses together. i will not repeat the content of the agreement, but let me mention a couple of points that demonstrate this. we will have a joint discussion on our legislative priorities and also select those that, according to the three institutions, should be at the top of the agenda for the upcoming year. and yes, at a time when the eu is perceived as fragmented, it is important to show unity, to send a signal of common purpose and to tackle the big challenges ahead of us in a joined-up way. concerning impact assessments, we agree that eu legislation must be based on informed decisions, while acknowledging that the legislative process is political and not technocratic. as co-legislators, we have a responsibility and a duty to our citizens to ensure that when we decide we have all relevant information in front of us and we take that information into account. in this regard much emphasis has rightly been put on having a particular regard for our smes as they are key to fostering growth and jobs in europe. we have committed to avoiding overregulation and administrative burdens. the commission’s fitness and performance programme is firmly anchored within the agreement framework. this agenda should not be seen as being all about lowering standards for protection. rather it is about thinking twice before we legislate and casting a critical eye on existing regulation. the annual burden survey that, on the suggestion of parliament, found its way into the agreement will help us to focus our minds on this matter. it will be a common platform for a discussion on how we can better ensure that we have legislation fit for purpose but without unnecessary burdens being put on citizens, businesses and administrations. we have also agreed to enhance the transparency of our work for citizens, and here i would like to highlight that we will have a joint database on the state of play of legislative files. this may sound to some of you like a technical issue, although it is quite important. people have to be able to understand how we work, so more active joint communication is needed. then – and this is highly significant – parliament and council have agreed on a number of points where we, as co-legislators, can strengthen our cooperation, such as being better at ensuring an efficient process, while safeguarding the quality of legislation and respecting each institution’s prerogatives, such as working closer together at an early stage to better understand each other’s points of view and thereby, hopefully, facilitating negotiations. in this context, i would like to express my appreciation for the constructive approach of both parliament and the commission in establishing measures to instil greater confidence in member states in the use of delegated acts. i am confident that this agreement will contribute to ensuring a framework and an atmosphere for negotiations that are conducive to finding constructive solutions to our common problems. we are all aware that the agreement is the result of a compromise, and not all issues were settled to the full satisfaction of each institution. some points were hard fought, touching on sensitive issues and the balance between institutions. however, i believe that the deal represents a fair balance. the council has welcomed the agreement reached and next week, on 15 march, the general affairs council will formally adopt the agreement. we then have to turn swiftly to implementation. we have to seize the momentum to put all the good words into practice, to make a real difference in how we deliver to our citizens and businesses. the presidency has therefore placed implementation and follow-up high on the agenda of the council. already next week we will kick off by deciding on how the council will organise its work in relation to the commission’s annual work programme, also paving the way for the three-way talks on the joint annual priorities. we are only at the start of our discussion within the council on implementation, but the presidency in particular intends to look at how the council deals with impact assessments and how to take forward the overall ‘better regulation’ package presented by the european commission. and yes, the presidency also intends to put transparency on the agenda. in closing, i would like to underline that the presidency and the council will of course continue to work in close cooperation with both parliament and commission on ensuring an effective application and implementation of this important agreement.
first vice-president of the commission.– madam president, when we reached an agreement on this in december, i was in two minds about it. i was happy that we had an agreement which takes us quite a number of steps forward, but i would have liked to see a more ambitious agreement in many areas. but realism took over and it was impossible to convince people to go the extra mile, so we settled for an agreement that is still much better than what we had before. so for me the glass is still half full with this agreement. why is it important? because we needed to look at the whole policy cycle. we needed to review everything we – the three institutions directly involved – do when we legislate. all three institutions were unhappy with the status quo, so we wanted to bring improvements. let me a mention a few substantial and meaningful, and let me repeat that, from our three different perspectives, none of us got a hundred percent of what we wanted. on implementing acts and delegated acts, the proposed approach should facilitate future discussions between the co-legislators and unblock the current impasse on many individual files. the commission will also provide greater transparency by allowing stakeholders to see the text of delegated acts and implementing acts before they are adopted. on annual and multiannual programming, the interinstitutional agreement provides for intensive collaboration between the institutions in setting priorities through annual and multiannual programming and on identifying the priority files for the legislative procedure. on regulatory fitness, each new act will set out how the legislation will be monitored and evaluated in the future so that we can check whether it is working as planned. the commission’s regulatory fitness programme will also play a central role in simplifying the body of existing legislation and reducing unnecessary regulatory burdens, but without weakening any of our important social and environmental goals. one of the biggest fears when we started this exercise was that this was just cutting red tape at the expense of our standards. this is not what we are doing. we are maintaining, and even improving, our standards, while still cutting red tape. on transparency, in some cases working jointly across the institutions to build common it platforms for delegated acts – and later perhaps for the codecision procedure – will help open up decision-making to public scrutiny. it is important to remember that the framework agreement between parliament and the commission continues to apply in full, and the commission remains committed to it as the bedrock of the cooperation between our two institutions. this is a balanced outcome. i repeat that, although not all my ambitions were realised, it is balanced for the institutions. i hope that parliament can support the outcome agreed by its negotiators, as this is good for the public and for business. i would like to thank mrs hübner very much for her outstanding report on this. we have a strong political message from the three institutions that they take seriously better regulation and the concerns of small businesses and the man and woman in the street – how can i say ‘man in the street’ on 8 march? – about unnecessary regulation. we have support for better regulation from all the institutions as a means to deliver societal objectives in the most efficient way. if parliament approves the new agreement, the commission is ready to start work immediately with parliament and council to ensure its timely and effective implementation so that together we can start delivering concretely for our citizens and our businesses. in particular, the commission can start to deliver on its commitments on the alignment of existing empowerments with the lisbon treaty, and we can work together to deliver the new register for delegated acts, which is something parliament also wants.

mr president, twenty years ago the trade unions were calling for a directive to guarantee the protection of posted workers. we have not got it because the european union has placed the provision of services above labour rights. in other words, competition in the single market is competition between workers, it is the erosion of their labour rights and it is wages for the benefit of employers. the commission is feeling the pressure to implement changes, but we are a long way from juncker's 'equal pay for equal work in the same place' commitment. the introduction of a 'necessary' remuneration is ambiguous and expressly excludes deferred wages from social security. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. we oppose minimum legislation that consolidates an unprotected workforce, which now numbers almost two million, having grown by 45% as a result of forced mobility and the widespread erosion of working conditions since the start of the crisis. we need - and this is a challenge - a thorough harmonization of work.
mr president, the obsession of the member states of the european union has been to achieve greater levels of economic integration. in the meantime, they left the most important convergence in the background: social convergence. when the needs of european citizens are not met by a truly social europe, we cannot turn a deaf ear or look the other way. we must build a europe where rights are equal, taking as a reference the most democratic and socially developed countries and not the other way round. we need an administration that is concerned with reducing inequalities rather than increasing them. as long as this asymmetrical model continues to operate, we will be creating a fraud on the values of the european union. in this respect, all measures to curb social dumping should be supported. we will therefore support a revision of the directive on posted workers which really addresses the labour rights of those who work outside their borders and combats unfair business practices.

much welcome parliament’s recognition that, with needs growing and pressures on the budget increasing, we ought to focus more on the results of our work. that budget focus on results will be a centrepiece in our work for 2017. let me make four points. first, on the migration and refugee crisis, we have been stretching all flexibilities of the budget, for which we are very grateful to the parliament. it is you that delivered it and we would have been lost if we did not have it. we will continue to do so. as you can see, we anticipate challenges, the most recent one being the necessity to create the new instrument to provide humanitarian assistance inside europe. we will fund the turkey facility in the budget for 2016. we already have projections. i am pleased to say that eur 95 million, our first investment, is now already working there and of course we have an obligation to secure the funds in 2017 and most likely also in 2018. my second point is on another priority we should not forget. it is to continue to wipe out the unpaid bills that have accumulated from the previous financial period. we melted it down to eur 8.2 billion and we will have a chance to present our analysis on the drivers for this more accelerated shrinkage of the unpaid bills and the consequences for future years when we have our first meeting of the interinstitutional dialogue on payments and outstanding commitments on 14 march, just before the discussion on our 2017 guidelines for the budget. my third point concerns what is ahead of us that is very important in 2017. in line with the mff regulation, article 7, we will have to review the cohesion policy envelopes, and that will lead to a revision of the commitment and the payment ceilings decided by the commission on technical grounds. we will have the analysis of the youth employment initiative and very important decisions to be taken on the basis of this analysis. we will have this in mid-april, in other words in about a month’s time. in 2017 we will have the obligation to complete the 5% reduction of staff and i take this opportunity to again urge all of us to do that with discipline. since today is international women’s day, let me finish by recognising that the parliament has placed in the guidelines encouragement for the commission to work on gender mainstreaming in the budget. last, but absolutely not least, in 2016 we are faced not only with the draft 2017 budget, but also with the review and revision of the multinannual financial framework. while these two events will not necessarily be combined, we will have to think of both as we work on the 2017 budget and it will of course have implications.
on behalf of the green group, madam president, this is a report, a good report, mr geier, commissioner, which confirms that this parliament is trying to be - and i believe it is succeeding once again - the best representative of the general european interest in the face of a national interest which continually, and these days more so, calls that european interest into question. it is a report which also admits a risk of obsolescence, because the evolution of events every day adds to our concerns and uncertainties. but i would like to point out some of the coincidences and values in the report: the connection with the revision of the multiannual financial framework, in the sense of the necessary increase in resources, the need to conclude the own resources report with the greatest possible ambition and, as has been mentioned, the risk of returning to the accumulation of outstanding payments. it also contains, on the positive side, a call for the recovery of horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility and a much-needed call to states on the youth employment initiative, with a very positive climate change text and, on the other hand, a red line in relation to iter that will prevent our group from being able to cast the favourable vote that the rest of the report certainly deserves.
mr president, two months ago mr rutte and mr tusk said that we had two months to put the solution to the migration problem into practice. the two months are next week. i think that we must raise our voices in this parliament to say a few things clearly to the heads of state and government before the council next week. the first is that we care about what they agree with others, but we're ashamed of what we do in here. let us ask the heads of state and government to make it clear that the men, women and children who are wandering, lost in the european winter, are of the same condition, have the same dignity as the men, women and children who escaped the spanish civil war, the second world war in its various stages, the fascist and communist dictatorships, the wars in the balkans. let us tell the heads of state and government not to fall into the temptation of populism, not to give in to fear, to defend the values and fundamental laws of the european union before public opinion; and above all let us also ask them to respect the principles of humanitarian action and international humanitarian law in all their agreements with third countries. but above all, let us not remain silent in the face of this epidemic of inhumanity which we are witnessing in so many countries of the union. parliament has a large majority which cannot accept that this inhumanity is being exercised in its name. not on behalf of parliament. not on behalf of our house. no, of course, in my name.
mr president, many arguments have been put forward. i just want to stress two things. firstly, that the member states of the union are responsible for helping refugees. that means that even if turkey is given a mandate, we still have the obligation to monitor it, to control it and to give it guarantees. and we have an obligation to find other solutions for the thousands of afghans, iraqis, libyans, etc. who are not covered by the syrian agreement with turkey. secondly, we must not make the same mistake now. the aid turkey can provide is humanitarian and of convenience. we cannot pay for it with political facilities for turkey's accession to the european union, which is an entry with its own mechanisms and standards and demands respect for human rights. in short, we must continue to assume our political and moral obligations. helping refugees should not mean kneeling before an authoritarian state that does not respect basic human rights.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal for an agreement proposes to return people who are entitled to asylum without even allowing them to apply for it, making it a legal requirement to return people in cold blood, which is not only unfair and immoral, but also violates international and european law, as the united nations high commissioner denounced yesterday in this very house. with this agreement europe is denying itself, outsourcing the management of our borders and our responsibilities of welcome, and hiring the turkish gendarmerie to do it. no person may be returned to a country where his or her human rights may be violated. turkey is not a safe country. with this agreement the european union legitimizes and becomes complicit in the turkish government's attacks on freedom of the press and of demonstration, in the systematic violation of human rights and the repression of minorities and in the bombings in kurdistan. with this deal, they're accomplices. if you want to put an end to the mafia, open safe passageways to europe. if not, you'll have blood on your hands.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think there are four main points in the treatment of this matter, in addition to the many interesting things that have been said. firstly, there is a principle that must not be forgotten: this situation can only be tackled by joint action, and that makes the european union more valuable than ever. secondly, in situations like these, regional alliances are essential, as in this case with turkey or the countries of north africa, however great our differences. we must make some good agreements, but the principle is that these regional alliances are essential - in this case, of course, with turkey. thirdly, i think it is important to ensure that the aid for refugees actually reaches the refugees and that there is no risk of some of it being left behind. and fourthly, a subject which i think is also linked to this: more than ever, it is essential to strengthen the european economy because it is a factor in dealing with the situation of uncertainty, the crossroads and the challenges we are facing and it will help a great deal to make this possible. in this context, the strengthening of the internal market is fundamental, but so is the free movement of persons, because it is not just the free movement of goods and services. without the free movement of persons, the single market will be 'collapsed', it will have a major deficiency. the commission's roadmap for the schengen area to be fully operational by the end of 2016 should therefore be supported.
mr president, a few minutes ago a member of parliament said that she wanted to feel confident and that europe has been built from one crisis to another. i can't feel confidence right now. the immediate mass deportation of all new syrian refugees to turkey seems to me to be a historical mistake which we are watching helplessly in this parliament. the governments have de facto destroyed respect for the value of solidarity which unites us europeans; they think they are protecting our states, but they are not: their panic and neglect in this globalised world mean that we too face a future of greater uncertainty, because we cannot remain on the sidelines of the great problems of our planet. we are told that this agreement will remove the incentives to cross the sea irregularly, but we will return people who have the right to exercise an asylum claim without allowing them to apply for it, after months of promises and false words. the problem is that, in this dark time, our countries have not fulfilled their previous commitments to relocate, to finance and, when it comes to making the commitment with turkey - an indecent commitment - they will certainly not provide the funds either. we cannot continue to trust you or the council, or even, if we are to believe it, the commission. please react!
mr president, the eu-turkey agreement, with turkey acting as a wall to europe, is a sell-out of human rights. for six billion euros, we sell people. how much is each one worth? a thousand? two thousand? three thousand euros? what is it? what's the price? this agreement condemns refugees and migrants to survive in a black hole. nobody knows what's going to happen to these people. we pay and forget. you can keep them in camps in inhumane conditions, send them back to war, or starvation, or do whatever you want. we pay the bill, and turkey does the dirty work. turkey will, of course, close the border in return for the european union looking the other way when the kurdish people are massacred or when there is a lack of freedom and repression in turkey. this agreement buries the geneva convention forever. you can't take people from syria, afghanistan or sudan and send them back to turkey. that's against the law. this agreement is contrary to international human rights standards, and i hope those who sign it will one day be brought to justice.
mr president, a week ago we heard the president of the council, mr tusk, warning migrants not to come to europe. we were all shaken up, and now we understand the content of those threats. the failure to manage the refugee crisis for months has culminated in an agreement that violates human rights, treats people as commodities and uses turkey as a huge wall of containment; we are washing our consciences with billions of euros. we have seen cruel images: children dying on our beaches, women attacked by tear gas, parents losing their children on the crossing; a real human tragedy. and what is the solution of the heads of state? return them to turkey. what a shame and what a shame! we're on time. this parliament has today demonstrated with many voices that it is possible to change this decision. please think of the people and think of restoring to europe the little dignity that is left to it today.
mr president, i would like to say that i find it very regrettable that president tusk and president juncker are not present in this debate. unfortunately, at a time when many of us here feel that europe is abdicating its principles and its responsibilities. the agreement we have heard about in a bad way, certainly not from the information the council has offered us, is of dubious legality, of dubious effectiveness and of dubious morality. you can tell president tusk that it is incredible that respect for persons and human rights is not mentioned even once in that text. how could they have forgotten that little detail? and my only interest today in this house is that the council and the commission and the member states hear that there are people here who do think of others and who do tell the european citizens that there is another europe than the one you are drawing up in those european councils.
mr president, madam minister, next week at the agriculture council, when you talk about employment, remember the crisis in the european agricultural sector, a crisis which is currently affecting sectors such as fruit and vegetables, pigs and dairy. the failure of commissioner hogan to find solutions to the european milk crisis shows the failure of his policies. i would ask you to come back to the real world at the next council and open the door to the regulation of production in the dairy sector. that will stop the destruction of jobs. it is not only the jobs that are created that count, but also the jobs that are destroyed. so take account of the situation in the agricultural sector, stop this bleeding, to contribute to job creation and a vibrant rural environment in europe.
mr president, mrs hennis-plasschaert, commissioner, turkey is certainly a problem. but it is not turkey that is the problem here today, it is europe. europe cannot be the sum total of national interests. who is representing europe in this debate? the council certainly does not. the council is acting in an intergovernmental logic, abandoning the community principle. we pay a police state, turkey, to not take responsibility, and we do so in open contradiction to international law. we punish one member country, greece, and turn it into a prison state, so that the balkan walls we have already erected cannot be breached. the hope for europe is what this parliament represents. this is the seat of the 29th member state, a member state called europe. we're going to exercise our veto. we are going to prevent europe's suicide. we're going to prevent you from taking europe back to the 1930s. you can continue this debate with impassioned indifference. they know that decisions are taken elsewhere, but we are going to recover, from the hands of the citizens, the strong, united, generous and welcoming europe that you are liquidating. don't forget that when you meet next week.

in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it represents a technical improvement in legislation on emissions from certain liquid fuels. specifically, this act sets out amendments to the regulation affecting fuels mainly used in shipping and brings together all the obligations of the member states in the control and monitoring of these emissions within their waters. the legislative framework for transport emissions needs to be improved to ensure that scandals such as those in the automotive sector do not occur. as this is a technical codification incorporating the basic act and its subsequent amendments in a single legislative act, which in this case does not involve any substantial change in its content, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report, which refers to a proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the reduction of sulphur in certain liquid fuels. the new directive will replace the various acts incorporated into it; the proposal fully respects the content of the codified texts and therefore merely compiles those formal amendments required by the codification operation itself. according to the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, the proposal in question contains a direct codification of the existing texts without any substantial amendment to them. the proposed directive aims to reduce sulphur dioxide emissions from the combustion of certain types of liquid fuels and thereby reduce the harmful effects of such emissions on man and the environment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative resolution, which is simply a codification of existing acts, without any substantial changes.

in writing. ‒ a large number of provisions in the field of union law remain, having undergone various, often substantial, amendments, and are scattered between the original act and subsequent amending acts, making them difficult for citizens to access and understand. in this regard, the purpose of this proposal is to codify council directive 1999/32/ec of 26 april 1999 relating to the reduction of the sulphur content of certain liquid fuels and amending directive 93/12/eec, in order to provide greater clarity and accessibility to union law. this codification provides legal certainty as to the law applicable in this area and will help to determine the provisions in force.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this international agreement with andorra on the automatic exchange of tax information because it is a major step forward in the fight against tax evasion and avoidance, particularly in third countries by natural or legal persons who are nationals of a member state of the union. the european and spanish socialists are firmly committed to the permanent abolition of tax havens in the world, and particularly within or on the margins of the european union, because they erode the financing of the welfare state and, ultimately, social justice.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it presents a tax cooperation agreement between andorra and the eu which improves the current legislative framework and extends the exchange of information in tax matters. while the exchange of information cannot be the only way forward in tax matters at eu level and we consider it necessary to abolish completely this type of tax haven, the agreement voted here unquestionably improves the current functioning of the exchange of information with andorra, allowing us to clarify responsibilities in the huge tax evasion that takes place through this tax haven. despite its obvious inadequacy, the formalisation of such agreements is necessary to know the real dimension of fraud and tax evasion by european taxpayers in such jurisdictions. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative resolution by which parliament approves the conclusion of the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the principality of andorra providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. this agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information improves tax cooperation and compliance with tax obligations, while taking an important step in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. under the new agreement, the member states of the union and andorra shall automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of their respective residents as of 2018 for information collected since 1 january 2017. the purpose of the agreement is to resolve situations where a taxpayer attempts to conceal assets representing income or assets on which taxes have not been paid.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive on procedural guarantees for minors who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, as i believe that it represents a step forward in establishing procedural safeguards aimed at protecting the right of minors to a fair trial and at preventing their reoffending by promoting their social integration. in the process of negotiations with the council, parliament succeeded in including in the directive its main demands, such as the strengthening of the right of the child to information, as well as the obligation for the child to be assisted by a lawyer, to have the right to appear at trial and to medical follow-up, and for deprivation of liberty to be considered as a last resort. i therefore voted in favour of this directive, which i regard as a positive step towards protecting the procedural guarantees of minors in criminal proceedings.
in writing. ‒ this directive is part of the eu's agenda for the rights of the child and the stockholm programme. its main purpose is to establish common minimum standards and to ensure procedural guarantees throughout the european union in relation to the rights of children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. i believe it is essential to guarantee the same rights for minors throughout the union. the rapporteur agrees with the general outline of the text and introduces some amendments to strengthen and extend the procedural rights and guarantees contained in the proposal. that is why i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the chinnici report. the rapporteur proposes amendments to improve, extend, strengthen or clarify the rules on the various rights affected by a commission directive which aims to define a small but organic catalogue of the rights of minors suspected or accused in criminal proceedings (or subject to a procedure for the execution of the european arrest warrant), through a structured body of 'minimum rules', linked to each other and adapted to the specific needs of minors throughout the process. its approval represents a significant development in the procedural guarantees for minors who are suspects or accused in criminal proceedings.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on procedural guarantees for minors who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. the proposal reflects the agreement reached with the council after lengthy negotiations in the tripartite dialogue, which reinforces the commission's proposal by broadening its scope and strengthening legal assistance, including 'the child will receive such assistance ex officio, without having to request it', the individual assessment of the processing and the medical examination of the defendant.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive on procedural guarantees for minors who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, as i believe that it represents a step forward in establishing procedural safeguards aimed at protecting the right of minors to a fair trial and at preventing their reoffending by promoting their social integration. in the process of negotiations with the council, parliament succeeded in including in the directive its main demands, such as the strengthening of the right of the child to information, as well as the obligation for the child to be assisted by a lawyer, to have the right to appear at trial and to medical follow-up, and for deprivation of liberty to be considered as a last resort. i therefore voted in favour of this directive, which represents a positive step forward in the protection of the procedural guarantees for minors in criminal proceedings.
in writing. ‒ a european-wide study shows that the rights of minors who are subject to criminal proceedings in the european union are currently not sufficiently guaranteed. in fact, there is no legal definition of the basic elements of a 'fair trial for minors'. this is not an isolated incident, as the commission estimates that more than one million minors are subject to criminal proceedings in the eu each year. the main purpose of this report is to establish a set of rights of minors who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings through a structured body of minimum standards tailored to the specific needs of minors facing a trial. within this body of minimum standards we would find the right to be assisted by a lawyer (right to free legal aid), right to an individual assessment and right to the minor's participation in the process, among others. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that it is necessary to establish a framework which guarantees the necessary legal certainty to minors facing criminal proceedings and not to leave these cases to fragmented jurisprudence.
in writing. ‒ we must ensure that minors who are suspected or accused of a crime have a fair trial. for that reason, i support the directive which recognises the right of anyone under 18 to be assisted by a lawyer and to be accompanied by the holder of parental responsibility (or another appropriate adult) during most proceedings. we have established a catalogue of rights and safeguards as a common european model of fair trials for minors, which will ensure that in all proceedings there are safeguards for minors, ensuring that the best interests of the child are always the primary consideration.
