mr president, we voted today on the first lines of the 2017 budget. there is still a long process of concrete funding to go through and that is why we have abstained, in order to keep the dialogue open before the budget is finally closed. however, it seems that this 2017 budget has not learned much from the experience. we must work for a larger european budget and a budget with a better distribution of revenue, based above all on the per capita income of the member states. in the coming days an agreement will be concluded for the return of refugees and for their literal storage in third countries. it's not something you can just sweep out, we understand. the unhcr representative told us yesterday that these agreements are illegal. we are ashamed of the increase in the budget for the militarization of the aegean sea and not for rescue and humanitarian reception. i think we still lack the flexibility to adapt to humanitarian emergencies and the firmness to be solidary and supportive. we do not reject the values of the european union, ladies and gentlemen.
mr president, i voted against this report because it confirms the neoliberal orientation of the european budgets, starting with their increasingly regressive financing and the lack of democratic control of them. i find it serious that the european budget is directed towards strengthening the structures of economic governance, supporting measures of liberalization and individualisation of labour relations with public budgets, which result in the loss of social rights for the majority of europeans. equally dramatic is the fact that the same funds are increasingly used to strengthen market mechanisms, rather than to constitute an autonomous pole of public investment, so that the state ends up subsidizing private investments, rather than contributing to the creation of a different production model. we need europe to strengthen its funds in support of the democratic and sovereign decisions of its states, rather than blackmailing them, and we need the agricultural and industrial development investment items to be allocated to social and regional cohesion rather than being a crutch for the market.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the report on the guidelines for the 2017 eu budget because we need a strong 2017 budget that gives us the tools to respond to the multiple challenges we face. first, it means that we need to equip ourselves with the resources to deal effectively with the migration and refugee crisis. we need to make sure that we have the resources and the flexibility to react to a situation that is changing rapidly, like the current one, while making sure that the budget allows us to show solidarity with the countries that are facing the worst of the crisis. moreover, the solution to the refugee crisis must go hand in hand with boosting european growth and competitiveness. the eu needs more investment in areas such as education or infrastructure to compete in the 21st century. too many young europeans are still struggling to find a job and we need more action at eu level to meet this challenge. we therefore call for more funding for the youth employment initiative to ensure that no young people in the eu are left behind.
in writing. ‒ these budgetary guidelines for 2017 consolidate, on the revenue side, an unambitious policy of resources that limits the ability to develop ambitious policies in the core areas of the european budget, such as agriculture and cohesion. on the contrary, it delves into the neoliberal management of spending, with its link to the european semester and its market orientation being particularly serious. in addition, they support an aggressive foreign policy that is contrary to human rights, as is the case with the funds lent to turkey to turn it into a prison for refugees who wish to seek asylum in europe. i have therefore voted against.

in writing. ‒ this report is the first step in the european parliament's annual budgetary procedure. it is intended to give the commission a political message on the european parliament's budgetary priorities for 2017, before the commission presents its draft budget for the european union at the end of may. i voted in favour of the report because the budget has proved to be a key resource in the fight against the recent crises and to respond to needs that had not been foreseen during the negotiation of the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. i would like to clarify, however, the meaning of my vote on amendment no 26. although i have already spoken in favour of raising real wages in the countries most affected by the eu's austerity policy, such as spain, this amendment is worded in a simplistic way and far from reality. the budgets cannot and should not be used for this purpose alone. i therefore abstained on the amendment.
in writing. ‒ the geier report lays the foundations for the ep's position on the eu budget for 2017, while providing an overview of the current budgetary situation. addressing the economic and refugee crises are the main priorities, which will require a real review of the multiannual financial framework. a contribution of 1 billion to the refugee fund is planned for turkey, together with the remaining 2 billion that member states have committed to contribute. the report also addresses, among other priority issues, the youth employment initiative, the child guarantee against poverty or the european fund for strategic investments, beyond the global perspective on economic growth or climate change. the s&d group supports flexibility in the member states' budget contributions under the stability and growth pact. we also believe that solidarity, as a fundamental principle of the eu budget, must also be respected in dealing with the refugee crisis.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the report on the guidelines for the 2017 eu budget because we need a strong 2017 budget that gives us the tools to respond to the multiple challenges we face. first, it means that we need to equip ourselves with the resources to deal effectively with the migration and refugee crisis. we need to make sure that we have the resources and the flexibility to react to a situation that is changing rapidly, like the current one, while making sure that the budget allows us to show solidarity with the countries that are facing the worst of the crisis. moreover, the solution to the refugee crisis must go hand in hand with boosting european growth and competitiveness. the eu needs more investment in areas such as education or infrastructure to compete in the 21st century. too many young europeans are still struggling to find a job and we need more action at eu level to meet this challenge. we therefore call for more funding for the youth employment initiative to ensure that no young people in the eu are left behind.
in writing. ‒ these budgetary guidelines for 2017 consolidate, on the revenue side, an unambitious policy of resources that limits the ability to develop ambitious policies in the core areas of the european budget, such as agriculture and cohesion. on the contrary, it delves into the neoliberal management of spending, with its link to the european semester and its market orientation being particularly serious. in addition, they support an aggressive foreign policy that is contrary to human rights, as is the case with the funds lent to turkey to turn it into a prison for refugees who wish to seek asylum in europe. i have therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the guidelines for the eu budget for 2017. the eu needs to be equipped with the necessary budgetary mechanisms to enable us to open the way to economic growth and job creation. we must use the eu's resources as effectively and efficiently as possible, bearing in mind that they are limited. we must also stress to the member states that the eu budget can never be considered a burden, as it makes a decisive contribution to the economic and social progress of all europeans.

in writing. ‒ we are refraining from supporting the jens geier report because we want to give an opportunity for dialogue, inviting people to look reality in the eye. we welcome the recommendations in the outline of the 2017 budgets that include a gender perspective, or greater flexibility in the budgets in the face of economic or refugee crises, and recommendations on the environment. but we must criticize the budget as a whole; its cut is still neoliberal, the current model is a failure and a thorough review of the scheme and the eu budget model is urgently needed. the budget is insufficient, with a poorly distributed revenue system, which should be based on the per capita income of the member states. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (aema) is a step in the right direction. we do not think that is enough to overcome the constraints imposed by the mff. a more comprehensive, more social and more equitable review of these budgets is therefore necessary if we are to be able to meet the challenges ahead.

in writing. ‒ the 2017 budget comes at a crucial moment in the evolution of the migration and refugee crisis. we must therefore have the budgetary means to meet this challenge and find the best solutions. a thoughtful and consistent review of the annual financial framework can help us in this. in these guidelines we also call for a thorough investigation into the case of the 10 000 missing children reported by europol. support for these guidelines is not only an exercise of responsibility but an obligation; that is why i have supported this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this interinstitutional agreement on better law-making which aims to ensure that eu legislation better serves the interests of citizens and businesses. the european and spanish socialists are in favour of reducing the administrative burden on citizens and businesses, especially smes, and of strengthening close cooperation between the institutions, particularly in the field of legislative programming. it is also essential that the new agreement reinforces impact assessments of new initiatives and assesses the cost of non-action at eu level. finally, i welcome the fact that for the first time a procedure is being established whereby the commission has to respond to proposals for acts coming from this parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this agreement, negotiated behind parliament's back by the irregular appointment of the leader of the liberal group as its representative, because it represents a tremendous democratic revolution. parliament's powers vis-à-vis the commission are being reduced, which will consolidate technocratic and neoliberal control over the legislative process. furthermore, the quantitative targets for reducing legislation and combating 'over-regulation' contained in the text are tools to reduce the harmonised protection enjoyed by european workers and citizens (as has already been demonstrated by refit), which is a disturbing development that we must oppose.

in writing. ‒ the ordinary legislative procedure is not characterised by being a rapid process. that is why the european union is making efforts to coordinate its institutions and to achieve more synchronised and less bureaucratic legislation. the parties to this interinstitutional agreement are the european parliament, the european commission and the council of the european union. the three institutions will exchange views on their priorities and objectives for the coming legislatures. they should also agree to draw up an indicative timetable. one of the measures adopted in this report would be for the european parliament and the council, as co-legislators, to maintain close contacts at a stage prior to interinstitutional negotiations. this would lead to a better understanding of their respective positions. on the basis of the above, i support this report as it will help to achieve synchronisation of legislative proposals and to put in place a fully harmonised legal framework.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the agreement between the community institutions to improve the planning, quality and transparency of the legislative process. we will improve the public's understanding of how the eu makes its laws and also the quality of new and updated eu legislation.
in writing. ‒ legislation is not an easy job, but legislating for the 500 million europeans in 28 countries is certainly very difficult. this agreement is about understanding the rules, about better collaboration between co-legislators, about the applicability of the legislation we are about to adopt, about forecasting the impact, on the one hand, and the cost of non-europe in legislation, and about taking account of smes, which are in fact forever forgotten in many european regulations and policies. the institutions are equipped with very sophisticated technical equipment, and the fact is that many european citizens sometimes see us as if we were stationed in a galaxy far away. with this agreement, parliament has lowered some of the barriers we have identified and has successfully negotiated a broader and more balanced approach to better lawmaking. and with that aim in mind, we will work to provide the european union with the most solid legal framework possible. that is why i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ we are talking about a major agreement which will replace the existing 2003 interinstitutional agreement on better lawmaking and the 2005 interinstitutional agreement on best practice between council, parliament and commission. the agreement covers the three main areas: better regulation, interinstitutional relations and legislative processes, including programming, delegated acts and implementing acts. this agreement has been reached after much negotiation and consensus between the parties, and i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ i think this report is very positive, because it reduces bureaucracy and thereby speeds up all the processes and decision-making, which will be very positive for the optimal functioning of the eu. there is currently an excess of laws in the union, the level of detail of which is in some cases too high and, instead of contributing to the agility of decision-making processes and good governance, this excess ultimately slows down the activity of the eu. the formal adoption of the interinstitutional agreement will make the european union's legislative activities much more coordinated and therefore much more effective. this will undoubtedly be of great benefit to all citizens and i therefore support this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it supports the need not to renew the agreement between the eu and philip morris international, while maintaining the need to act on tobacco smuggling and its associated problems. we share the need to act on tobacco smuggling because of the enormous tax revenue that member states lose from their budgets. the multinational pmi is the major beneficiary of this smuggling which causes so many problems both to the coffers and to public health and therefore action is needed on the subject. but this bilateral agreement places a multinational company, the main beneficiary of smuggling, as a legitimate party against the public authority, which is what this resolution is trying to avoid. it is because of this that i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ we voted against renewing the tobacco agreement with pmi because, although it has in principle helped to reduce the firm's illegal tobacco by more than 85%, it has not served to combat new forms of illegal trade. the agreements, as they were signed in 2004, have not been able to respond to the ever-changing smuggling and counterfeiting, where cheap white tobacco is now predominant in the market. the legal framework has also changed since the first agreement was approved more than ten years ago. at that time we did not have the legal instruments to prosecute the major tobacco companies. fortunately, thanks to the tobacco directive and the who protocol, we will be able to legally prosecute illegal tobacco from any producer from 2019 onwards. to avoid a legal vacuum, we demand that the commission put in place an action plan against the smuggling of white labels, that it take all the necessary measures to trace and locate pmi tobacco products, and that it take legal action against the illegal seizures of pmi products.
in writing. ‒ meps have voted for the commission to focus on implementing the 2014 eu tobacco directive, which includes more effective instruments than the current pmi agreement to fight against counterfeiting and smuggling, such as the tracking and tracing system for cigarettes, from 2019. member states should also ratify the who framework protocol on tobacco control, which provides for an equivalent system at international level. the parties to the protocol are obliged to protect their public health policies against the commercial interests of industry, and no responsibility in this area can be delegated to companies. to cover the period when the provisions of the european tobacco directive are not yet applicable, we ask the commission to prepare new rules to deal with the issue of cheap unbranded cigarettes, to monitor and track them and to initiate legal action in the event of seizures of the cigarettes of the company. we are thus putting an end to the current agreement which was raising some ethical problems, such as the use of part of the tobacco industry's funds to finance the european anti-fraud office (olaf), which could have been a conflict of interest.
in writing. ‒ the tobacco agreements were a pact with the devil, the tobacco corporations - in this case phillip morris international - to turn a blind eye to their involvement in illegal tobacco circuits, in exchange for some revenue from the part of tobacco recognised by these same companies that circulates in these circuits. we have supported the gue/ngl resolution which called not only for the cessation of these agreements but also for elements of transparency and tough intervention. he didn't come out. however, a resolution has been passed, which was also supported, led by efdd and greens, which at least proposes the termination of these agreements.
in writing. ‒ the illegal tobacco trade challenges public health policy against smoking by removing the main disincentives to consumption, is a crime against public finances and costs the eu more than eur 10 billion a year in lost excise duties on tobacco products. the eu and philip morris international (pmi) ratified an agreement in 2004 to fight cigarette fraud and smuggling more effectively, which expires in july 2016. but since it was signed, the legal framework has evolved radically and today we have powerful legal instruments to fight the illicit tobacco trade. the tobacco directive will allow for greater control of tobacco companies in the eu and a traceability system, and the who protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products will also make it possible to fight illegal tobacco from the international level. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution which asks the commission not to renew, extend or renegotiate the agreement with pmi after its current expiry date.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it supports the need not to renew the agreement between the eu and philip morris international, while maintaining the need to act on tobacco smuggling and its associated problems. we share the need to act on tobacco smuggling because of the enormous tax revenue that member states lose from their budgets. the multinational pmi is the major beneficiary of this smuggling which causes so many problems both to the coffers and to public health and therefore action is needed on the subject. but this bilateral agreement places a multinational company, the main beneficiary of smuggling, as a legitimate party against the public authority, which is what this resolution is trying to avoid. it is because of this that i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because smuggling, contraband and counterfeiting of tobacco within the eu is a growing problem. the resolution calls on the competent authorities to take action against these practices, which represent a public health problem even greater than that of cigarettes. it is therefore not appropriate to renew, extend or renegotiate the agreement with pmi.
in writing. ‒ we voted against the renewal of the tobacco agreement with pmi because, although it has contributed to a reduction of more than 85% of pmi's illegal tobacco, it has not prevented new forms of illegal trade. the agreements, as signed in 2004, have not been able to respond to the ever-changing smuggling and counterfeiting in a market where cheap white tobacco is currently predominant. the legal framework has also changed since the first agreement was approved over 10 years ago. at that time, we did not have the legal instruments to prosecute the major tobacco companies. fortunately, thanks to the tobacco directive and the who protocol, we will be able, as of 2019, to legally pursue illegal tobacco from any producer. in order to avoid a legal vacuum, we are calling on the commission to draw up an action plan against contraband of white labels and to initiate legal action against the illegal seizure of pmi products.
in writing. ‒ the tobacco agreements were a pact with the devil, the tobacco corporations - in this case phillip morris international - to turn a blind eye to their involvement in illegal tobacco circuits, in exchange for some revenue from the part of tobacco recognised by these same companies that circulates in these circuits. we have supported the gue/ngl resolution which called not only for the cessation of these agreements but also for elements of transparency and tough intervention. he didn't come out. however, a resolution has been passed, which was also supported, led by efdd and greens, which at least proposes the termination of these agreements.
in writing. ‒ we voted against renewing the tobacco agreement with pmi because, although it has in principle helped to reduce the firm's illegal tobacco by more than 85%, it has not served to combat new forms of illegal trade. the agreements, as they were signed in 2004, have not been able to respond to the ever-changing smuggling and counterfeiting where cheap white tobacco is now predominant in the market. the legal framework has also changed since the first agreement was approved over 10 years ago. at that time we did not have the legal instruments to prosecute the major tobacco companies. fortunately, thanks to the tobacco directive and the who protocol, we will be able to legally prosecute illegal tobacco from any producer from 2019 onwards. to avoid a legal vacuum, we demand that the commission put in place an action plan against the smuggling of white labels, that it take all the necessary measures to trace and locate pmi tobacco products, and that it take legal action against the illegal seizures of pmi products.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it supports the need not to renew the agreement between the eu and philip morris international, while maintaining the need to act on tobacco smuggling and its associated problems. we share the need to act on tobacco smuggling because of the enormous tax revenue that member states lose from their budgets. the multinational pmi is the major beneficiary of this smuggling which causes so many problems both to the coffers and to public health and therefore action is needed on the subject. but this bilateral agreement places a multinational company, the main beneficiary of smuggling, as a legitimate party against the public authority, which is what this resolution is trying to avoid. it is because of this that i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ tobacco smuggling is estimated to cost the european union around 10 000 million euros and we are all aware of its link, at times, with organised crime. binding agreements such as the one we are dealing with here with the tobacco company philip morris (pmi) have certainly had their effect, achieving important achievements in the fight against smuggling. this agreement expires in july 2016 and we're debating whether or not to renew it. i believe that since the signing of this agreement the situation has changed considerably at the regulatory level in the european union. we have the tobacco products directive 2014/40/eu. the fact that it has not yet been transposed is alarming to many, who believe that a legal vacuum will be created until then, with a setback in the achievements of the pmi. i do not think there is any reason for such alarm. the who framework convention on tobacco control and its protocols already provide for mechanisms in the fight against smuggling. there are no excuses and there should be no room for fear. we have the tools, we just have to commit to applying them.
in writing. ‒ the illegal tobacco trade challenges public health policy against smoking by removing the main disincentives to consumption, is a crime against public finances and costs the eu more than eur 10 billion a year in lost excise duties on tobacco products. the eu and philip morris international (pmi) ratified an agreement in 2004 to fight cigarette fraud and smuggling more effectively, which expires in july 2016. but since it was signed, the legal framework has evolved radically and today we have powerful legal instruments to fight the illicit tobacco trade. the tobacco directive will allow for greater control of tobacco companies in the eu and a traceability system, and the who protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products will also make it possible to fight illegal tobacco from the international level. i have therefore voted in favour of this resolution which asks the commission not to renew, extend or renegotiate the agreement with pmi after its current expiry date.

mr president, mr prime minister, the refugee crisis is the worst humanitarian emergency we have had in europe since the second world war and we are not going to solve it with inhumane solutions. mr. prime minister, building a wall or closing a border does not end the migrant crisis. the only thing that makes it more inhuman is the desperate flight of men, women and children, and it dehumanizes us europeans. we europeans are equal in the difficulty and we must be equal in the responsibility. that is why we support a common policy on immigration and asylum, and why we support a common management of our external borders, to protect the schengen area. national solutions do not solve the problems of europe. that is precisely why europe exists, because national solutions do not even solve national problems today. for example, your government unilaterally decides to reintroduce border controls, even forcing private transport companies to carry out tests, to identify those who transport. for example, your government has approved the possibility of suspending schengen for three years, whereas the rule only allows a two-year suspension. these, mr prime minister, are national, popular, defensive solutions, and they are insufficient solutions which, in your opinion, are certainly good for sweden, but, i say to you, are bad for europe. the socialists in this house, like the greens in this house, like us, are in favour of a europe without frontiers. even this morning they have spoken very strongly against the agreement with turkey. your government, however, has again raised the bar in the face of the migrant crisis, in the face of the refugee crisis. which of the two is the real socialist speech? which one is the real green speech? europe must be built gradually, because when we stop building europe, nationalism grows again, and with nationalism always xenophobia, with nationalism always fanaticism and populism grow. europe's motto is 'united in diversity', but today it must also be 'united - not divided - in adversity'. mr president, you have called for a more social europe, but it strikes me that, at the same time as you call for a more social europe, when faced with the most social of problems, which is the flight of refugees, you are rebuilding your borders. maybe if what we say matches what we do, the populists wouldn't be right.
prime minister of sweden.– mr president, i wish to thank everyone very much for the discussion and all the interventions. naturally, i cannot answer everyone but i will do my best to give my view on the different things that have been raised. first, to gunnar hökmark. my point is not to deliver a lot of new rules that will burden companies, when i talk about social europe, but my point is this: we have a common economy, we have a common labour market and in this labour market we need a future for those who are working, those who are actually delivering the wealth that we are trying to distribute, and i cannot see the smart thing in showing people a negative future – your wages will perhaps go down, your working conditions might worsen. that is not the future that the european people are looking for. we have a common interest, a common responsibility to make sure that the european labour market is guided by some very important values and, at the same time, give the different countries the possibility to rule in the way they see fit. but the laval case we saw in 2007 – the ruling on the laval case showing that the swedish trade unions could not defend collective agreements – that was wrong. it would have been very easy to say, of course, if sweden has collective agreements then protect them as long as you do not discriminate against anyone who comes into the country, but if the workers, the employees of europe, are looking at a future when they are supposed to compete with lower wages, then i can assure you that those people will not be in favour of this cooperation. so let us promise ourselves, one another, that we should develop a labour market in europe that is a promising future, and let us realise that those women and men who go to work every day, they are the ones who really make a difference and they are the ones to whom we should be giving good conditions and a future. there have been a lot of interventions of course about the refugee crisis. my message is this. we have and we will have refugees in the world, unfortunately. the problem, as some say, is that this is sweden’s problem; sweden has caused the problem because we received refugees. the problem is the crisis in syria and the crisis in the middle east that forces people to flee because they are afraid, they are terrorised, they are in the middle of a war. that is the real problem. and i think it is a human thing to say to people who are fleeing for their lives that yes, we need to help you. we can do that in different ways. we need to help to solve the problem that causes the people to actually have to flee. that is the root thing. you have to help people in the neighbourhood, yes, but those who actually arrive – are you going to shut the door? some parties think so. i think it is human to say that we also need to help people who are fleeing for their lives. and we are in this organisation together, 28 member countries, and if we had done this together we would have solved it. it would not have been a problem. we are 508 million inhabitants on this continent. we could have solved it together. and it is alright for some to say that they will not participate. if they choose to do that, my point is that i think it is fair to say that if you do not participate in this system, the asylum system, perhaps you should not participate in the schengen system. you cannot just choose the good things, the easy things, and sit in the quiet easy corner. you need sometimes to step up and also do the tricky things, the difficult things. we want a future system that actually distributes the responsibility amongst 28 member states. someone asked whether i believed this would happen. i am not sure, i do not know, because i hear the resistance, yes, but this is the only way for the european union to function well: that we help one another, we assist one another, and those who do not want to participate should consider another thing. if this does not work it will affect the whole european union, also affecting those who are now sitting in the backseat doing nothing. it will affect them as well. if we want an efficient, really working european union we need to cooperate also on these difficult issues. that is my point, and i think we need to be clear with one another. regarding the agreement with turkey, yes, i think it is right to do this. i think we need to find a solution, to find that and to have that cooperation with turkey, otherwise i would not have supported it. i cannot answer all the detailed questions but what would that mean? president tusk is now being given a mandate, we gave him a mandate, to negotiate on these principles that we want this trafficking of human beings to stop. we need to do something about it, because those who are against everything also need to show the alternatives. the reality right now is that thousands and thousands of people are risking their lives on the water, in the sea, and we have people that are selling these trips who do not care at all about these lives. we have at least so far, more than 400 people, perhaps 500 people today who have died so far this year, and i think we need to stop it. this is one way of going. it is not the only solution. no, it is not the only solution but it is one of the things that we need to do and now let us see what the negotiations will bring. we will see that result and then we will discuss it, but i think it is the right thing to do. i was asked also about the posting of workers directive and the changes, and will that solve everything, if i understood the question correctly. no it will not solve everything but it is a very good step forward, to show the employees, and the employers i would say, of europe, that we can develop a european labour market that is functioning and that respects collective agreements, or legislation or whatever we choose to develop in our respective countries. but no matter what way we choose as individual countries the european union should give that platform, should give that possibility. for our country it means respecting the collective agreement. this is a path that we have chosen. it has been a good path, it has been a very efficient one with wealth, with growth, but also with quite a fair distribution between the citizens of our country and i would like to stick to that path. therefore, i think what the commission has proposed now is very good. it is a step forward. it will bring more hope to the employees, the workers of europe and i think that is a very good start. in writing. in 2012, the swedish parliament passed a resolution urging the swedish government to recognize the sahrawi arab democratic republic, a courageous decision in the face of economic pressures and the hostile reaction of morocco. sweden has repeatedly demonstrated its consistency in defending international law in the case of palestine. like israel, morocco is an occupying state which prevents the saharawi people from exercising their right to self-determination by maintaining a colonial system of exploitation of their lands. the european united left/nordic green left supports the recognition of the sadr, as has been the case with the state of palestine before the united nations, and we will welcome the fulfilment of the mandate of the swedish parliament to recognise the sahrawi arab democratic republic. it is a matter of justice and international law protects it, so we call on the swedish government to take this significant step which would be a step towards resolving the conflict of a people who have been suffering under moroccan occupation for more than 40 years.
president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, it is indeed important to exchange views on the situation in eritrea. this very small country in the horn of africa is – or continues to be, i have to say – in the headlines because many people are fleeing the country on a monthly basis, many of them to europe, seeking a better life without political oppression, a better life and better employment opportunities. and yes, we are deeply concerned about the gross human rights violations. respect for human rights is a basic principle of the eu’s foreign policy and it is part of our political dialogues with governments around the world, including with the eritrean authorities. through this dialogue, but also publicly, we raise our concerns about violations of human rights obligations and reaffirm the need for eritrea to respect fundamental democratic rights. we have also repeatedly requested concrete gestures, such as freeing prisoners detained incommunicado since 2001, among them mr dawit isaak, a swedish eritrean citizen, and we will continue to do so at all levels and on all occasions. the eu also raises issues related to the human rights situation in eritrea in international fora, notably at meetings of the un human rights council. we appeal to eritrea to cooperate with the un special rapporteur and the un commission of inquiry on eritrea and give them access to the country. let me underline that we believe that a critical engagement with the country is still the best option for the eu for a number of reasons. firstly, because critical engagement creates the possibility to stress the need for concrete changes and progress across the board, and it gives us the possibility to insist on the importance of adhering to international standards on human rights. isolation rarely helps in these circumstances. a second reason why we think that critical engagement with the country is useful is the fight against poverty. regardless of the nature of the political regime, the eu is committed to supporting the population and improving its living conditions through development projects; so no budget support. a lot needs to be done to alleviate the huge stress upon eritrea’s population. eritreans are facing a problematic food security situation and lack of economic opportunities. their despair translates into a constantly high rate of people, especially young people, trying to flee the country. they often venture on a dangerous journey, mainly towards europe, by illegal means and are easy prey for traffickers. this is why eu development aid under the 11th european development fund (the edf) will support social and economic development in eritrea. the programme foresees increasing access to renewable energy and supports economic governance, which will in turn contribute to economic growth and the creation of job opportunities. under the edf programme eu engagement also foresees measures to improve the human rights situation in eritrea. there is a third element to take into account. the country has a strategic position in the horn of africa, bordering sudan, ethiopia and djibouti, as well as the red sea with its access to the arabian peninsula. a peaceful and stable eritrea and an eritrea that respects its neighbours will have a positive impact on the overall situation in this region. the conflict in yemen and the tensions in the arab world are changing dynamics in the horn of africa and our critical engagement should therefore also be seen in this regional context. the policy of isolation has not worked. direct eu support to improve the living conditions of the populations also make them less prone to radicalisation and violent extremism. it is also in this framework that we want to engage with eritrea, thus contributing to regional peace and stability. let me conclude by addressing the issue of migration and asylum. the constant high outflow of migrants and asylum seekers from eritrea is a major challenge. eritrea is a key country of origin. eritrean asylum seekers are generally recognised for international protection in the eu with a very high acceptance rate – understandably so – but eritrea is also an active partner in the khartoum process which addresses, among other things, human rights issues, as well as border management and migration management. by discussing the human rights record and improving the livelihoods of the people of eritrea, our engagement is expected to address some of the push factors for migration. this is part of our comprehensive response to the current migration crisis. let me say clearly that we engage with eritrea for the sake of its people and i would like to stress that once again. yes, the critical engagement is also in our own interest. it is the only way to try to help move things in the right direction. in eritrea or elsewhere, critical engagement based on a good understanding of the dynamics and challenges is a pragmatic way to help promote positive change.

madam president, commissioner, i too would like to congratulate my colleague mrs grossetête, of course: she has had a huge number of amendments, but her great spirit of consensus and her good work have made this report a great report and a good report. the need to clearly differentiate the different forms of treatment in this regulation has been addressed: curative, control and preventive or prophylactic. the administrative burden must be reduced because this does not favour administration, but guarantees of quality, efficacy, safety and correct information on veterinary medicinal products must also be maintained. as regards the availability of veterinary medicines, this is no small matter and solutions must be sought for certain species and pathologies which we call 'minor species' and 'minor uses'. in these specific cases, it is important to support measures to encourage innovation. finally, it is very important that the proposal has been amended to enable veterinarians to use medicinal products for species and indications which are not included in the manufacturer's recommendations. in short, i believe that we must maintain a cascading prescription system and even resort to medicines for human use; as a last resort, yes, and only when there is no better alternative. i think this is vitally important and it is a task which should be done by the veterinary expert.

madam president, why thalidomide? because it's a drug invented by the nazis that a german lab sold until 1961. because it causes irreparable malformations in newborns. because no one stopped it from being produced and distributed among pregnant women. because countless gynecologists have received gifts for prescribing it. because more than 10,000 children had to be born without limbs, or with short limbs, before any authorities reacted. because, it sounds like a lie, but it's true, the victims have had to wait 50 years before anyone apologizes to them. because the governments of the european countries closed their eyes. because it is the greatest health tragedy in european history. because the mothers who took the medicine advised by their doctors have been the only ones to feel guilty, and many are already growing old without any authority saying to them: "ma'am, it was our fault". because all mothers are innocent victims and no one loves their children more than they do. because we have never had this debate in the european parliament. because we are facing a human drama that requires a political solution. because it is a shame that after 50 years there is still no political solution. because in my country, under the franco dictatorship, the drug was withdrawn three years later. because in spain there were 500 victims and only 24 have been recognized. because in spain no government of any party, not even the governments of my party, has wanted to solve the problems of all those affected. because it cries to heaven. because in spain the victims were hidden by the dictatorship and forgotten by democracy. because the vademécum continued to list drugs containing thalidomide until 1975. because everyone in my generation could have been a victim of thalidomide. because the european union must mediate with the german and spanish governments. because i've never felt more confident about what i stand for from this seat. why thalidomide? because the victims are feeling their health deteriorating, without any remedy or repair. because tomorrow will be too late to repair so much pain. because it's about justice.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's financial instruments are used effectively. many citizens who are following us will wonder what has happened in all this time. the answer is that, half a century later, many of the victims of thalidomide are still demanding justice, they are still demanding a guarantee of a life of minimum dignity. the thalidomide tragedy changed the history of medicines in europe, enabling legislation with higher levels of quality and safety to be passed and preventing further pharmaceutical disasters, although the current model of research and clinical trials still suffers from the transparency it should manifest. however, no progress has been made in repairing the damage suffered by many of the poisoned children who today live to a precarious old age after a lifetime of suffering. in many cases, the necessary care and medical care cannot be afforded. within this drama, the injustice committed against the spanish victims must be highlighted. in 1972, the contergan foundation was created by a law establishing the universal nature of aid. the reality is that aid has been granted to 3 000 german citizens and only to one spanish citizen. those affected in other countries have received aid from the foundation or their governments - including in australia. in the case of the spanish, neither the state nor the pharmaceutical industry has paid any attention to them: they have condemned them to a situation of helplessness and marginalization. from the very beginning of my parliamentary activity, i have known firsthand the heroic struggle of the members of avite, the spanish association of victims of thalidomide. commissioner, it is time for action, it is time for concrete measures. it is time to put an end to the discrimination suffered by the victims and, without a doubt, it is time to establish a protocol in the european union, as this oral question raises, whereby all european citizens affected by thalidomide receive the same compensation. we must act without delay simply because we have to, simply because it is just and because there is nothing more contrary to the european union than discrimination.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the pharmacovigilance system in europe is properly functioning. but the response received by the victims was not proportionate (five hundred in spain and hundreds more in the united kingdom, sweden, etc.). there are not many of them anymore, but the suffering they still have is great, especially when they think they have been forgotten. we must not only persevere and try to appeal to the social responsibility of the company, but i also believe that the member states have an ethical and political responsibility. and that is what i ask the commission to do: to promote and coordinate this necessary response that we have to give to these victims. in spain, the socialist government, in 2010, made a decree to recognize these victims and try to give them compensation as far as possible. but it is clear that today it has been shown that it was not enough. i would therefore like to insist and appeal to the commission to promote this necessary coordination from the member states and to all the member states in europe to give a fair and adequate response to all these victims.
mr president, it is now more than 50 years since the thalidomide holocaust: 50 years of shame. the drug was sold under the slogan "as harmless as a lump of sugar" and caused disabilities in thousands of babies. in spain, francoism covered it up. democracy did not answer. the judges spoke of prescription, as if human rights violations meant prescription. the laboratories - in this case, the german laboratory - have been trampled underfoot: economic interests have taken precedence over human dignity, over health; and that responsibility, of course, has to be shouldered by someone. and that is why we are asking for the commission's help. of course, it is the responsibility of the pharmaceutical company which invented, designed and marketed the product; the responsibility of the german government which also marketed it abroad and allowed it to go out; the responsibility of the governments of the member states which allowed it to enter. we are one of the countries in spain where the victims have not yet received any compensation. today, from the european parliament, we can do a great deal because we have the opportunity to defend the equality of all and to say that we belong to a europe which does not forget its innocent people. when a human being - and, in this case, many (and many who are no longer there) - is suffering an injustice, is enduring suffering, you have to take a stand, because neutrality only aggravates injustice, and in no way helps the victims. and that is why i ask the commission to take a stand, not to stay in a debate and to give a solution to the victims.
mr president, i would like to join my colleagues in defending the victims of this great tragedy of thalidomide, but i would particularly like to join the voice of the victims of thalidomide in spain, who suffer double discrimination because they have not received any compensation; and especially the voice of these victims and their association, avite, which is constantly defending their rights and working to ensure that this great tragedy is not forgotten. it is incredible to hear here in this house mr gonzález pons and some other representative of the popular party government, who has not helped at all. the socialist government in spain did something 'not enough, it is true', but the governing popular party has done nothing. i'm not worried. more than 50 years later, there is a great deal of discrimination against the victims of thalidomide in europe and a european response is needed. if they do not, they suffer double discrimination and that is absolutely unfair. the commissioner has to intervene with sensitivity in the face of the tragedy of these victims, especially the spanish victims, who, because they were born in spain and were born sick - not through their fault - have to face double discrimination.
in writing. the thalidomide crisis led to the launch of the european pharmacovigilance system, which has just turned 50. however, despite the fact that the crisis affected many eu countries, it did not bring about either recognition of the victims or support measures for them at european level. the company reached an agreement with the german government in its day and compensated the german victims but never acknowledged the spanish victims. the spanish government passed a decree in 2010 establishing a scale and financial compensation for spanish victims. the possibility of revising it is not excluded. however, the consequences are so significant and serious that the company's involvement is essential to be able to compensate for them. on september 23, 2015, the supreme court of spain ruled that the approximately 500 spanish survivors of thalidomide are not entitled to compensation from the pharmaceutical company due to the statute of limitations.

on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, commissioner, what are we talking about here, in this session of the european parliament? we are talking about a matter of the greatest urgency and seriousness, because it raises great concern: the protection of fundamental european rights and the privacy of europeans. but we also need to consider the protection of what is known internationally as the english phrase 'whistleblower', which, translated into spanish, would be the whistleblower, the whistleblower of a situation that affects cases of corruption, attacks against national security, environmental crimes, fraud, economic crimes that therefore require active cooperation with law enforcement agencies. and that's what we're talking about. why has it become so topical? the european parliament has been asked to vote on the report by mr genscher, and i am sure that the commission will be able to do so. and so it speaks to us of the need to protect whistleblowers who can bring to the attention of the judiciary or the security forces tax fraud, tax havens, environmental crimes, crimes affecting health, abuses that undermine the full enjoyment of fundamental rights, which european law is obliged to guarantee. the european parliament has dealt with this. in 2013, i chaired a committee on mass surveillance on the fundamental rights of europeans in the committee on freedoms, justice and home affairs, whose conclusions were adopted in october 2013. and in 2015, we held a hearing in the libe committee - the committee on freedom, justice and home affairs - to conclude that we need a protection framework that builds on the rights set out in articles 11, 30 and 41 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, that is consistent with the council of europe and the oecd, but above all that provides regulated and safe channels to secure the confidentiality of these whistleblowers of crimes that we care about and want to prosecute. this is what we have to do in the european parliament: how to improve the protection of whistleblowers with a uniform statute throughout european law, with european legislation that fulfils the mandate of the conclusions of the committee of inquiry that i chaired as chairman of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs. this is the task before us and we must take it up. we must complete it and we must carry it out.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, commissioner, i agree with mr lópez aguilar that we need a protection framework. we are talking about white-collar criminals, who can hide their crimes; in fact, because of their sophistication and their technical and intellectual capacity, it is very, very difficult to detect them, and it is much more difficult to prove the crimes. when the crimes are committed by large corporations, who are doing them, because they are doing illegal espionage work, or by some politicians within their parties or in local, regional, national or european power, it is extremely difficult to punish them. so whistle-blowers are the key to not getting away with it. the united nations convention against corruption, which entered into force in 2005, recognizes the importance of the issue among the 167 countries that have ratified it. however, many of them continue to fail to provide whistleblowers with adequate legal protection. most countries do not go beyond general declarations of principles, because it is very uncomfortable, very difficult, very sensitive, and only four member states have extensive legislation on whistleblower protection. creating a healthy culture of transparency is just as important as designing specific whistleblower protection legislation. my own country, spain, is lagging behind many other countries in this respect. and i can assure you that we could have gotten rid of a lot of the corruption if we had had good whistleblower protection legislation. protection surely comes through the establishment of a legal status. it is clear that when someone decides to dare to report a serious crime within a large corporation, a state or a political party, if his anonymity is not protected, he will suffer from isolation and harassment, with possible risks to his career and personal peace of mind, as we have said. they need the protection of their physical integrity and they need secure reporting protocols, which in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 726/2004 is the eu regulatory framework for the manufacture, authorisation and distribution of veterinary medicinal products. treatment is of the utmost importance, as it can seriously affect public health. legislation is needed to harmonize between the different member states. the european commission intends to remove from the regulation the provision for granting and maintaining marketing authorisations for veterinary medicinal products, which are transferred to the new regulation. the european parliament's proposal is to include the european parliament itself in the co-decision procedure within the ema, through a centralised procedure in which the ema will retain its role in the authorisation and control of veterinary medicinal products, guaranteeing its services by setting up a reserve fund. parliament should be fully involved in the setting of the agency's fees through the above-mentioned decision-making process. a cross-reference with the new veterinary medicines regulation and the role of the ema in the authorisation and control of veterinary medicines is also necessary. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ data production is growing at an unprecedented rate. various studies indicate that the volume of data is increasing at an annual rate of 236%, and this trend will increase with millions of devices exchanging information with each other. europe cannot remain outside the big data revolution, a revolution which is already affecting every sector of the economy and every area of our lives. it is therefore urgent that the european union takes a step forward by creating a framework favourable to exploiting the opportunities that this new reality offers for economic development and job creation. as this resolution, which i have supported, states, it is necessary to encourage and support investment in r & d, to open up public and private funding, to invest in broadband networks, to promote the digital adaptation of smes and to train and equip workers in this area, but it is certainly crucial to ensure data protection and network security, as well as to safeguard respect for intellectual property rights.

in writing. ‒ eritrea is a country which, after thirty years of war, gained its independence in 1993. its subsequent development continues to be linked to border conflicts with its neighbours, especially ethiopia. the framework for cooperation between the eu and eritrea is set out in the cotonou agreement, which covers cooperation in areas ranging from trade to the fight against poverty, the protection of human rights and good governance. despite all efforts, the human rights situation has, according to the united nations, been progressively deteriorating. free elections have never taken place in eritrea, and the separation of powers of the state is unclear. citizens are deprived of freedom of expression and arbitrary detention for indefinite periods, ill-treatment and torture are common. this report calls on the eritrean authorities to make immediate improvements in these areas to promote peace, development and sustainable prosperity through unwavering respect for human rights, and that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. ‒ we in this parliament are very concerned about the situation in eritrea, as we have seen that the deplorable human rights situation persists and that the rule of law and freedom of the media are completely absent. that is why i support the resolution calling for all these shortcomings to be addressed and supporting the allocation of eur 200 million from the european development fund to promote poverty reduction and socioeconomic development, to address the economic and political root causes of migration and to fund projects related to renewable energy, energy efficiency and economic governance.
in writing. ‒ eritrea is a country which, after thirty years of war, gained its independence in 1993. its subsequent development continues to be linked to border conflicts with its neighbours, especially ethiopia. the framework for cooperation between the eu and eritrea is set out in the cotonou agreement, which covers cooperation in areas ranging from trade to the fight against poverty, the protection of human rights and good governance. despite all efforts, the human rights situation has, according to the united nations, been progressively deteriorating. free elections have never taken place in eritrea, and the separation of powers of the state is unclear. citizens are deprived of freedom of expression and arbitrary detention for indefinite periods, ill-treatment and torture are common. this report calls on the eritrean authorities to make immediate improvements in these areas to promote peace, development and sustainable prosperity through unwavering respect for human rights, and that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this resolution because we consider it essential to condemn the eritrean regime and to call on the eu to put an end to its growing complicity with the regime for geostrategic reasons and to control migration flows.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this resolution because we consider it essential to condemn the eritrean regime and to call on the eu to put an end to its growing complicity with the regime for geostrategic reasons and to control migration flows.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this resolution because we consider it essential to condemn the eritrean regime and to call on the eu to put an end to its growing complicity with the regime for geostrategic reasons and to control migration flows.
in writing. ‒ the resolution agrees with the allocation of 200 million over the next 6 years to the national indicative programme under the 11th european development fund to promote poverty reduction and socioeconomic development. it also addresses the underlying political and economic causes of migration and proposes to fund projects related to renewable energy, energy efficiency and economic governance. it also urges eritrea to show evidence of transparency and good governance, expresses deep concern about the human rights situation in the country and calls on the international community and eritrea's partners to put pressure on the eritrean government to allow foreign aid in support of vulnerable communities to prevent the current crisis from worsening. we are talking, in short, about a constructive resolution for the country, which goes into the depth of the current needs, and i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the progress of the eu accession process of the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, among other things because it refers to the dispute with greece over the name as a 'bilateral' issue, when i understand that this is a matter which should be resolved within the framework of the united nations and in accordance with international law. moreover, our group opposes the neoliberal agenda, the privatisation policies and the economic model that comes with eu membership, which have proved to have catastrophic effects on the european population, and i have therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ this proposal recommends opening accession negotiations with macedonia, which has been a candidate country for eu membership since 2005 and has seen this process constantly interrupted as a result of political instability and non-compliance with eu accession requirements. i voted in favour because i support macedonia's accession to the eu and because this document makes progress in its accession conditional on considerable progress being made in the urgent reforms which are a priority to bring the country up to community standards. however, i do not share the measures taken by the macedonian government during the refugee crisis. unilateral decisions that have endangered security and, in many cases, violated the rights of refugees. the macedonian authorities must respect and implement the geneva convention and cooperate with the european institutions in this crisis. i also hope that the next elections on 24 april will be held in a fair, free and transparent manner. the elections are an opportunity for macedonia to strengthen the democratic character of its institutions and to meet the copenhagen criteria in order to make progress towards eu membership.
in writing. ‒ we voted against the report as it does not reflect the real situation in the country with regard to the backwardness in critical areas and the extent of non-compliance with the copenhagen criteria. although references are made to political problems, the lack of progress in obligations for fair elections, ongoing corruption and the lack of accountability for the phone tapping scandal, the text could have been much more blunt. the authorities of the former yugoslav republic of macedonia have not been able to avoid irregularities in ensuring the independence of the media.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this resolution on the 2015 report on the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, which calls on the country to break the political deadlock, hold free and fair elections soon and return to the path of reforms to start negotiations on its accession to the european union. the country faces a critical moment as it has not only waited too long at the eu door as a candidate but also faced the challenge of thousands of refugees at its borders, but the time has come to take new steps that will benefit all its citizens.
in writing. ‒ the former yugoslav republic of macedonia submitted its application for eu membership in march 2004. despite repeated requests from the commission and parliament to open negotiations, the council has blocked such an opening because of the name dispute with greece, a dispute which should not constitute an obstacle to the official opening of negotiations and which should be resolved as soon as possible in accordance with the principles of the united nations. this report, which i voted for, considers that the prospect of eu accession is a great incentive to introduce reforms in the country and to promote political stability, highlighting the former yugoslav republic of macedonia as the most advanced candidate country in terms of the level of adaptation of the acquis. however, several problems persist in the accession process: lack of constructive dialogue between government and opposition, deterioration of media freedom, corruption and nepotism in public administration and high unemployment rates. greater efforts are needed to depoliticize the public administration and the judicial system and to fight against corruption in the state apparatus and discrimination against minorities such as the roma.

in writing. ‒ this report notes montenegro's progress in the nine chapters opened in the last year towards its eu accession, while being vigilant in the current climate of polarization and the implementation of the new electoral law. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that montenegro is making great efforts to bring its legislation and institutions into line with the criteria and requirements for membership of the eu. i also think it is good that this text stresses the need to ensure fair and free elections in the face of growing social polarization and to fight corruption more forcefully and effectively. the government must take exemplary action on this last point in cases involving the cabinet itself. i have supported the amendments to clarify that montenegro's eu accession process is independent of that of nato. while admitting that montenegro's accession to the north atlantic treaty organisation is positive for the eu's strategic and geopolitical interests, the two accession processes are different as the criteria for entry are not and should not be the same.
in writing. ‒ we abstain from voting on this report because, although we agree with some of its considerations, we believe that it ignores the social problems that weigh on the citizens of montenegro. the group does not agree with the privatisation process imposed in the context of the accession process, nor the implicit pressure and interference of the eu on the country's foreign policy and its foreign relations decisions which the report endorses.
in writing. ‒ i have supported the fyrom report as i have supported the montenegro report. montenegro's progress and reality are very positive and in 2016 it will be ten years since its independence. parliamentary elections will also be held and the country will hold crucial negotiations for its potential entry into nato. despite montenegro's progress on its path to the eu, corruption remains a serious concern, especially in public procurement, health, education or the construction sector. it is therefore necessary for montenegro to make the fight against corruption one of its priorities.
in writing. ‒ montenegro was designated by the council as an official candidate for accession in december 2010. the stabilisation and association agreement entered into force in may 2010 and the negotiation phase was opened in june 2012. it is currently the country with the most progress in the accession process, with a total of 20 chapters open for negotiation, two of which have been provisionally closed. however, the criteria for opening negotiations on the competition and environment policy chapters are still far from being met. this report, which i voted for, reiterates that greater cooperation between the ruling coalition and the opposition is needed to make further progress in the accession process and expresses deep concern at the extreme polarization of montenegrin politics. it also urges the government to fully implement the new electoral legislation before the holding of new elections in 2016 and to ensure the transparency of the elections. further efforts are needed to improve mechanisms for consultation of civil society organisations, media freedom and access of the roma community to social services, among other areas.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this first report on banking union because i agree with the positive assessment of this new step in the construction of europe, which is essential to form a genuine economic and monetary union in a federal key. i think the assessment of the single supervisory mechanism since its launch in november 2014 and the support for the proposed european deposit guarantee scheme, the fourth and absolutely necessary leg of the banking union, together with the single regulation for the 28 countries, the supervision by the european central bank for the 19 countries and the restructuring and/or liquidation of financial institutions domiciled in the euro area, is appropriate. in this connection, it is very important that parliament does not delay the processing of the proposal on the european deposit guarantee scheme for the benefit of the more than three hundred million citizens living in the euro area, nor that it is linked to other matters that are not relevant. the report therefore in no way supports the introduction of limits on the purchase of sovereign debt by financial institutions outside the basel framework.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i believe that the banking union has only served to extend the exceptional policies developed with financial rescues to the european periphery on a continental scale. in particular, we are witnessing the strengthening of institutions lacking democratic legitimacy, such as the ecb, while promoting an oligopolistic and transnational banking market that consolidates the power of finance over the european economy. the positive aspects, such as european solidarity in the event of bank failures, have not been developed, so that once again the construction of europe serves only to institutionalize neoliberal policies.

in writing. ‒ we voted against this report, which describes the first year of the banking union as a success. in our view, the main problem facing the project, the existence of systemic banks (too-big-to-fail), has not been solved at all, with the addition that some of these banks (such as deutsche bank) are now in a state of insolvency that again threatens the stability of the union as a whole. as regards the supervisory body, the ssm, we believe that its performance during the greek crisis, as well as the ecb's violation of its own assessments, deserved the investigation and condemnation contained in the report. the report also calls for the creation of a european banking system, which would be able to cover the costs of the banking sector and the financing of the public sector.

in writing. ‒ banking union is an indispensable component of a genuine economic and monetary union. the committee on economic and monetary affairs draws up an annual report on the banking union. this report assesses the performance of some of the instruments used, such as the single supervisory mechanism (ssm) and the single resolution mechanism (srm). parliament welcomed the establishment of the ssm, which had produced good results since its inception, both from an operational point of view and with regard to the quality of supervision, and considered it an important achievement given the complexity of the project and the limited time available. it also welcomed the effective launch of the single resolution board and the establishment of national resolution authorities in the member states. these achievements, unthinkable five years ago, show that the policies designed in the wake of the financial crisis are bearing fruit. closer coordination between national competent authorities across the eu and at international level is essential to ensure effective regulation and supervision. i therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ europe must move towards a stronger banking union, creating a single deposit guarantee scheme that offers greater protection. and we must work to reduce banking risks. the report on the banking union for 2015 goes into all these issues and for that reason i am voting in favour of the proposal.

subsidiarity and proportionality are basic principles for a harmonious construction of the european union. the mechanisms put in place to comply with them are insufficient and formalistic today and offer the parties concerned, especially the european regions with legislative powers, clearly insufficient time limits. in addition, in some states, such as my own, the procedure for being able to form the opinion of the state on this does not guarantee that the voice of the regions, if it does not coincide with the view of the state, is included in the early warning reports. if we have this gap in subsidiarity, imagine what will happen to the substance of the issues on which legislation is being made. everything that is lost along the way distances the european institutions from the citizens and undermines transparency and participation. the experience of recent years has shown that the procedure must be corrected and i believe that, as the report says, an ex ante control is not enough, but it seems appropriate to make at least a report assessing the ex post operation of the union's rules from the perspective of proportionality and subsidiarity. in short, we must take this seriously if we really believe in a federal europe and in the concept of union and what it means: a voluntary sum of its members. and nothing better to encourage it than to treat all the institutions affected by european policies as adults.
mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate you on this agreement. the principle of subsidiarity and the principle of proportionality are essential to the proper functioning of the european union and are the starting point of european policies. there is no doubt that the principle of subsidiarity brings european policy closer to the citizen and determines when the european union has the power to legislate. the same applies to the principle of proportionality, which makes any action by the european union meaningful and appropriate to the objective pursued. the report is important because it seeks to ensure the effectiveness and also the democratic legitimacy of decision-making and in some way it strengthens the european project. it is true that since the treaty of lisbon a whole series of cards have been created for the use of national parliaments to establish mechanisms for properly monitoring the application of these principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. it is important to note that this has been done normally, but it is true that all these mechanisms have to be agile, they have to be really simple and they have to be effective. the most important thing in these cases is cooperation between all national and european administrations and ensuring and reinforcing these two principles.
