member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to thank ms kaufmann for the report on refit. the conclusions of the report are a strong encouragement for the commission’s work in this area and also for me personally. making eu law more effective and efficient, reducing the costs of its application and working with member states to ensure that it is implemented well: this is a task for all european institutions. our success in this area will make a positive contribution to growth and jobs and, therefore, help to fight the ‘eu fatigue’ we are too often confronted with. this common endeavour is reflected in the interinstitutional agreement for better law-making which you approved on 8 march 2015. the report we are discussing today dates from before that agreement, so many of the issues it raises have in fact already been resolved between us. the commission adopted the better regulation package on 19 may 2015 with a view to ensuring an effective and efficient regulatory environment for businesses as well as for other stakeholders. the package included several measures, one of which, the new regulatory scrutiny board, is already in place. half of its members are external to the commission, and its prerogatives have also been extended to cover the review of ex-post evaluations. this includes new comprehensive guidelines and tools to cover the application of better regulation throughout the entire policy cycle. it means planning, impact assessments, legal drafting, implementation, monitoring and evaluation as well as stakeholder consultation. this is the first time that such integrated guidance has been prepared in the commission. a new refit platform has been established. a first meeting took place in january, and i hope that first results can be presented by the summer. our new interinstitutional agreement on better law-making includes a number of important achievements. on implementing acts and delegated acts, the proposed approach should facilitate future discussions between the co-legislators and reassure them. the commission will also provide greater transparency by allowing stakeholders to see the text of delegated acts and implementing acts before they are adopted. on annual and multiannual programming, the interinstitutional agreement provides for intensive cooperation between the institutions in setting priorities through annual and multiannual programming and on identifying the priority files for the legislative procedure. on regulatory fitness, each new act will set out how the legislation will be monitored and evaluated in the future so that we can check whether it is working as planned. the commission’s regulatory fitness programme will also play a central role in simplifying the body of existing legislation and reducing unnecessary regulatory burdens but without weakening any of our important social or environmental goals. on transparency, in some cases working jointly across the institutions to build common it platforms for delegated acts – and later perhaps for the codecision procedure – will help open up decision-making to public scrutiny. after formal adoption, the commission will immediately start working with parliament and the council to ensure the timely and effective implementation of this agreement so that together we can start delivering even better legislation for citizens.

group in 2006. this report by mrs nicolai, whom i would like to thank very much, is very timely, as the first preparatory committee, which opens the negotiations on this international instrument, has just taken place in the last two weeks, between 28 march and 8 april. it will be followed by a second meeting at the end of august, between 26 august and 12 september. the report rightly points out that the new legal instrument will address a package of elements. these will include marine genetic resources, including questions on the sharing of benefits, area-based management tools including marine protected areas, environmental impact assessments, capacity-building and the transfer of marine technology. one of the main aims of this new agreement will be to establish a mechanism which will enable the creation and management of marine protected areas. this will help the global community meet the commitment it made at the third rio conference on sustainable development to protect 10% of oceans in this manner by 2020. the european union would also like this agreement to make the unclos provisions on environmental impact assessments operational. this is necessary to prevent or to member of the commission.– mr president, let me start by expressing my thanks to our rapporteurs ms metsola and ms kyenge for this comprehensive report. they and the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe) have invested a great deal of serious work to achieve this result. we all share a common objective. we all agree that the time has come to replace chaotic, irregular and dangerous migratory flows with organised safe and legal pathways to europe. like the european agenda on migration, your report rightly stresses the need to work on all aspects of migration in order to reduce the incentives for irregular migration, assist migrants in need of protection, secure our external borders and attract skills to support our economic growth. we cannot work on one of the aspects and ignore the others. we cannot pick and choose what to focus on. we need to enhance all aspects of our policy in parallel, to coordinate with all key players and be both realistic and ambitious looking ahead. the agreement reached between the european union and turkey should also be seen in this broad context. implementing this agreement is a challenge. we are working tirelessly to put in place all the legal, practical, logistical and financial arrangements to implement it. we are doing so with the greek and the turkish governments, as well as with international organisations and ngos to ensure that the european union and international law is fully respected. people who apply for asylum in greece will have their applications treated on a case-by-case basis in line with eu law. i was in ankara last week to discuss how the eu-turkey agreement is being put into practice. discussions are still ongoing on the protection guarantees for both syrian and non-syrian asylum seekers. as a result, the first promising steps have been taken. in the short time since its implementation, which started on 4 april, 74 syrians have been resettled in europe and more than 300 migrants returned to turkey. we have started to finance projects to support turkey in hosting millions of refugees. more generally, the current crisis has shown that the present system is not working, and many elements are reflected in your report. in particular we need to overhaul the asylum system. currently, the first place of arrival of a person in the european union decides which member state should handle an asylum claim. this is neither fair nor sustainable, as we have seen in the last months. last week’s communication presented two options for the establishment of a sustainable and fair system for determining the member state responsible for examining asylum claims. the first alternative is to add a corrective fairness mechanism to dublin: what i would call ‘dublin plus’. we would keep the current criteria and supplement them with adjustments enabling redistribution to other member states in specific circumstances. the objective would be to have a threshold that is not too high. redistribution should start before the asylum system of a member state is over-stretched. the second, alternative, line of thought we are proposing is changing the basic criteria. in this scenario, responsibility for an asylum claim would be decided from the very start and for every case on the basis of distribution between member states. both options would provide the much-needed solidarity and fair sharing of responsibilities between member states. indeed, under both options, the distribution mechanism should be activated automatically. but a reformed dublin mechanism alone will not make our asylum policy more fair and efficient. this is why the commission will present complementary initiatives in order to achieve greater convergence in the eu asylum system and to limit secondary movements across the european union. the eurodac system will be reinforced. the asylum procedures and the qualification directives will be replaced with fully-harmonised regulations. targeted modifications will be proposed to the reception conditions directive and a new reinforced mandate will be given to the easo. we also need to enhance safe and legal pathways to europe to stop migrants from embarking on dangerous journeys. this is why we will put forward a horizontal mechanism for resettlement. right now there are many differences between member states’ approaches to a settlement. it would be more efficient if eu member states pooled their offers and use the same methodology. we also agree that in the future we will need migration to fill the skills gap and to address the demographic challenge that all our nations in europe face. we will propose a reform of the blue card scheme for highly skilled migrants, as well as measures to attract and support innovative entrepreneurs. i also want to emphasise that we are working on an action plan on integration for all third-country nationals. this will be a crucial element to increase acceptance in our societies. all these actions are complementary to the actions initiated to protect our borders and reduce incentives for irregular migration. last week we proposed making our borders smarter and stronger. we created an eu entry/exit system to improve our external borders management by better monitoring over-stayers. the commission is pursuing its efforts, together with member states, to improve arrangements for the return of irregular migrants not in need of protection, especially regarding sub-saharan countries. let me assure you once more that the commission is working very hard with all actors to ensure that the current deficit in the migration system is being addressed. the refugee crisis has been a catalyst for the acceleration of these changes. the picture sometimes looks very dark. i will not hide from you that my first thought every morning is whether we as europeans will overcome this crisis and turn it into an opportunity instead of a disaster. but i still want to believe that we are all now realising the need to adapt to a new era, which is characterised by human mobility. most importantly, we have started realising that we can only face this new reality united and based on our common values of respect for human rights, and it is true that this parliament was the first to show the way ahead and this commission’s mission was from the beginning to tackle the issue in a comprehensive way. in this framework, i welcome the fact that many constructive proposals can be found in your report, which shows our common understanding of the challenges and potential solutions. i am looking forward to a constructive debate.

in writing. ‒ this report proposes to approve the codification and recasting of the various changes made to the regulation of the european parliament and of the council applying the arrangements for products originating in certain states belonging to the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states in the agreements establishing, or leading to the establishment of, economic partnership agreements. although this is a technical report, i do not agree with the content of the regulation which is being proposed, since it concerns the eu's economic association agreements with third countries, in this case the acp countries. these agreements do not usually have positive agreements on the eu counterpart and reinforce asymmetries. i therefore could not vote in favour and abstained.
in writing. ‒ we abstained on this report which proposes the regulation for trade in products from acp countries (africa, caribbean and pacific). it is a procedural reformulation, however, the market access facilities for the signatory countries of the agreement, will decrease the development potential of non-signatory countries.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work on the adoption of the regulation on goods originating in certain acp states, which regulates imports of products from that area. this transitional instrument provides tariff- and quota-free access to the eu market. it also aims to ensure the transparency, clarity and simplification of eu legislation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation codifying and recasting regulation 1528/2007 regulating imports of products from certain acp countries. this transitional instrument provides tariff- and quota-free access to the eu market for products originating in the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states or in the least developed countries (ldcs) in the phase prior to the conclusion and application of the respective wto-compatible economic partnership agreements (epas) before 1 october 2016. the purpose of the codification exercise is to ensure the transparency, clarity and simplification of eu legislation when an original legal act has been subject to numerous amendments. since its adoption in 2007, the market access regulation has already been amended nine times. codification is therefore essential to ensure its clarity and legibility.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of granting approval to the new protocol establishing fishing opportunities and financial compensation between greenland and the eu. this new protocol promotes a framework for cooperation to develop, for the benefit of both parties, a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fishery resources in the greenland fishing zone. it grants fishing opportunities to union vessels in the greenland fishing zone, in accordance with the relevant conservation and management measures and within the limits of the available surplus.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour because in recent years the european union has signed a number of fisheries cooperation agreements and protocols with 'third countries'. through these agreements, the eu grants financial and technical assistance in exchange for fishing rights in relation to a wide range of stocks in the exclusive economic zone of the partner country. in this case, a specific fisheries partnership agreement has been concluded with the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland, hereinafter referred to as 'the eu-greenland fisheries partnership agreement'.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for his cooperation in the committee on fisheries in order to be able to approve this fisheries partnership agreement with denmark and greenland on fishing opportunities and financial compensation. following three rounds of negotiations, the protocol to the agreement has been renewed for a period of five years from 1 january 2016. the eu's financial contribution is estimated at 17.8 million. i welcome this new agreement, which will be very important for the european fleet.
in writing. ‒ the new protocol resulting from the negotiation between the commission and the governments of denmark and greenland was initialled on 20 march 2015. this new protocol covers a period of five years and is in line with the objectives of the fisheries partnership agreement by granting fishing opportunities to union vessels in the greenland fishing zone, in accordance with the relevant conservation and management measures and within the limits of available surpluses. cooperation between the union and greenland shall be strengthened and a framework for cooperation shall be promoted to develop a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fishery resources in the greenland fishing zone. this protocol provides for an annual financial contribution of eur 17 799 978 during its period of validity, of which eur 13 168 978 corresponds to access to the greenland fishing zone, eur 2 931 000 to the additional allocation paid by the eu in support of greenland's fisheries policy and eur 1 700 000 to the reserve for new additional fishing opportunities which may be accepted by the eu, subject to scientific advice and surplus resources. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ the new protocol is in line with the objectives of the fisheries partnership agreement, strengthens cooperation between the union and greenland and promotes a framework for partnership to develop, for the benefit of both parties, a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fishery resources in the greenland fishing zone. it grants fishing opportunities to union vessels in the greenland fishing zone, in accordance with the relevant conservation and management measures and within the limits of the available surplus.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of granting approval to the new protocol establishing fishing opportunities and financial compensation between greenland and the eu. this new protocol promotes a framework for cooperation to develop, for the benefit of both parties, a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fishery resources in the greenland fishing zone. it grants fishing opportunities to union vessels in the greenland fishing zone, in accordance with the relevant conservation and management measures and within the limits of the available surplus.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation. it should be borne in mind that in recent years the eu has signed a number of fisheries cooperation agreements and protocols with 'third countries', which provide financial and technical assistance in exchange for fishing rights in the exclusive economic zone of the partner country. the current protocol provides for a financial contribution from the eu of eur 17.85 million per year. the renewal of the protocol will be in the interest of both the eu and greenland.
in writing. ‒ this five-year agreement sets out the fishing opportunities for eu vessels in greenland, an autonomous government of denmark. this type of agreement has existed since 1985. the financial counterparts are as follows: the european union will pay approximately eur 17.8 million per year, including eur 13.1 million for the right of access to greenland's fishing zone, almost eur 3 million for the sectoral policy and eur 1.7 million for additional fishing opportunities. the new agreement has positive developments: on the one hand, the contributions of shipowners are increased by 40 to 50%; the commission has also proposed that the quotas be reduced in order to reduce the cost of the agreement. the european union has traditionally bought more quotas than it has fished. finally, the agreement also allows for the introduction of additional species and quotas if stocks permit. so it's a win-win deal for both parties.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour because in recent years the european union has signed a number of fisheries cooperation agreements and protocols with 'third countries'. through these agreements, the eu grants financial and technical assistance in exchange for fishing rights in relation to a wide range of stocks in the exclusive economic zone of the partner country. in this case, a specific fisheries partnership agreement has been concluded with the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland, hereinafter referred to as 'the eu-greenland fisheries partnership agreement'.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of granting approval to the new protocol establishing fishing opportunities and financial compensation between greenland and the eu. this new protocol promotes a framework for cooperation to develop, for the benefit of both parties, a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fishery resources in the greenland fishing zone. it grants fishing opportunities to union vessels in the greenland fishing zone, in accordance with the relevant conservation and management measures and within the limits of the available surplus.
in writing. ‒ this recommendation gives the green light to the signing of the fisheries agreement which the european union has been negotiating for some time with the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland. since 1985 we have signed successive agreements between the eu and the danish and greenlandic governments, which have proved to be extremely beneficial for both parties and in which the commitments and agreements established have been respected - although there is always something to improve. as regards the economic magnitude, it should be noted that this agreement is the third most important for the eu. the analysis of the implementation of the previous agreements shows that the impact on the eu's fisheries sector, as well as on our production and processing industries, has been enormously positive. in addition, from the point of view of environmental protection, these agreements ultimately aim at the european union developing a sustainable fisheries policy and, to this end, thanks to the european financial contribution, the greenland government is improving the management, conservation and control of its fisheries and also investing in scientific research. i shall therefore vote in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the eu's fisheries agreement with greenland is the third most important in terms of its economic value. i agree with the rapporteur that the new protocol strengthens cooperation between the union and greenland. it promotes a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the greenland fishing zone. this is in the interest of both parties, in line with the relevant conservation and management measures and within the limits of the available surpluses.

in writing. ‒ in 2003, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with third countries to replace certain provisions in bilateral agreements with an agreement at eu level, which i consider to be a positive development. the eu-macao agreement on certain aspects of air services is one of the outcomes of these negotiations. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report. the commission has negotiated on behalf of the union an agreement on certain aspects of air services with the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china replacing certain provisions of the existing bilateral air service agreements.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this recommendation on the eu-macao agreement on certain aspects of air services. international relations between member states and third countries in the field of air services have been regulated by bilateral agreements, but in 2002 the court of justice of the european union ruled that traditional designation clauses infringe union law. the ec has therefore negotiated the agreement replacing certain provisions of the 15 bilateral air services agreements concluded between the states of the union and macao.
in writing. ‒ i have given my support to the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the macao special administrative region on certain aspects of air services. this agreement replaces certain provisions of the 15 bilateral air services agreements concluded between member states of the union and the macao special administrative region, after the court of justice of the european union ruled in 2002 that the traditional designation clauses of member states' bilateral air services agreements infringe union law. those clauses allow a third country to refuse, revoke or suspend the authorisations or permits of an air carrier designated by a member state but not essentially owned or effectively controlled by that member state or its nationals. this is considered to be discrimination against union air carriers established in the territory of one member state but owned and controlled by nationals of other member states.
in writing. ‒ a number of judgments of the court of justice in the early 2000s concluded that the european union has exclusive competence over various aspects of external aviation which have traditionally been regulated through bilateral agreements between member states and third countries. following this case law, in june 2003 the council mandated the commission to open negotiations with third countries with a view to replacing the 47 existing bilateral agreements with community agreements. the agreement with macao extends to all eu states the rights already enjoyed by 15 states with which macao had bilateral agreements and allows the right of establishment and access without discrimination on grounds of nationality for airlines wishing to establish routes to macao.

in writing. ‒ on the basis of decisions of the european court of justice and the transport council, the commission is mandated to negotiate with third countries agreements on air services (‘open skies’), coordinating eu external air transport relationships and bringing bilateral agreements by single member states into the eu—line. after a series of other agreements, the commission has now achieved such agreement with macao. the main aspects are the avoidance of discrimination between air carriers (designation clause) and obligatory commercial agreements between airlines. therefore, i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ value added tax (vat) is one of the main taxes in the internal market and is partly a very important source of financing for the union. that is why i voted in favour of extending the current minimum rate of 15%, so that in the meantime the european parliament and the council have time to examine the new proposal for a directive on vat, which is very complex and where we will have to tackle a new anti-fraud strategy, in particular, but not only, that of a cross-border nature. in particular, i am particularly pleased that parliament has supported the extension of the extension to 31 december 2018, instead of 31 december 2017, as proposed by the commission, which is the result of an amendment tabled by the spanish socialist delegation. this achievement is further proof of the added value of parliaments, and as this is a consultation procedure, i hope the council will support the decision.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because the present legal framework, which sets a minimum vat rate of 15% at european level, raises a number of problems, but because of the lack of definition in the new commission proposal, it is necessary to prolong this regime in the interests of legal certainty. in 2017, the commission will propose the new vat regime which is likely to deepen the regressive aspects of vat by seeking to link it further to the economic governance framework. this system gives the european commission the power to set reduced rates on basic products, a power which has created many problems. however, the specific recommendations of economic governance insist on the transfer of direct to indirect taxation, with the clear intention of increasing inequalities. that is why, despite the need for extension, i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ we abstained in this vote to extend the minimum vat rate to 15% pending a proposal from the committee. while we believe that indirect taxes are regressive and should be able to be reduced, in this case it is a formal decision pending the commission's final proposal which will have to be debated.

in writing. ‒ the following directive provides that the standard rate may not be less than 15% as a common base for all member states. the aim is to achieve the legislative harmonisation necessary to ensure the establishment and functioning of the internal market, avoiding as far as possible any distortion of competition. i support this initiative because this minimum level of tax rate provides a useful safeguard for the proper functioning of the internal market, ensuring that crossborder purchases are not made below a certain threshold. i am voting in favour because this is one of the first steps needed to establish an action plan which the commission will publish to achieve a definitive vat system which is simple, efficient and fraud-proof, designed for the single market.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the approval of the strategic cooperation agreement between europol and brazil, which aims to improve judicial cooperation in the fight against serious crime, in particular organised crime, illegal immigration and trafficking in human beings, drug-related crime and credit card fraud, as well as other activities related to cybercrime and the fight against terrorism. the exchange of personal data has been excluded from the scope of the agreement, so the issue of data protection is not relevant in this case. the information exchanged could include expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods and training activities, as well as advice and support in specific criminal investigations.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the agreement is to improve judicial cooperation in the fight against serious crime, in particular organised crime and terrorism. this agreement contains provisions on operational cooperation between eurojust and brazil, including the exchange of crime prevention practices and staff training. important needs have been identified that justify operational cooperation between brazil and europol. brazil is a key country for europol in the prevention of trafficking in human beings and drugs and in activities related to cybercrime. the fact that the 2016 olympic games will be held in brazil may lead to an increase in crime, a factor that has been taken into account when reaching the agreement.

in writing. ‒ i support the adoption of this cooperation agreement, whereby the council, after consulting the european parliament, encourages the exchange of information and personal data with brazil in order to improve strategic cooperation between the latter country and europol. i support this agreement because it also encourages the exchange of expertise, results, strategic analysis and information on crime prevention methods. it promotes training and counselling activities between the two and provides support in different criminal investigations. the importance of this agreement lies in the relevant role that brazil is acquiring in the fight against organized crime, terrorism and data recovery. in view of the above considerations and since cooperation with brazil will contribute to the fight against crime, strengthening it and establishing a closer link at international level, i vote in favour of its approval.
in writing. ‒ my support for the report giving the house its approval for the conclusion of a strategic cooperation agreement with brazil. i am sure that it will contribute to the fight against organised crime by strengthening it and to closer police cooperation at international level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the approval of the strategic cooperation agreement between europol and brazil, which aims to improve judicial cooperation in the fight against serious crime, in particular organised crime, illegal immigration and trafficking in human beings, drug-related crime and credit card fraud, as well as other activities related to cybercrime, and the fight against terrorism. the exchange of personal data is excluded from the scope of the agreement, so the issue of data protection is not relevant in this case. the information exchanged could include expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods and training activities, as well as advice and support in specific criminal investigations.

in writing. ‒ i would like to thank my colleague norica nicolai for her great work in approving the agreement on marine biodiversity in areas outside national jurisdiction, the united nations convention on the law of the sea. marine activities are developing and multiplying rapidly, so the pressure on sustainability and conservation of marine biodiversity is constantly increasing. more coordinated action is needed in the field of marine biology. the new agreement must include instruments for accountability by all actors involved, since without these instruments effectiveness and real progress are difficult to predict.
in writing. ‒ in the united nations convention on the law of the sea (1982), in its fish stocks agreement (1995) and in agenda 21, the united nations has addressed the importance of protecting the world's waters. in this context, a working group was set up to explore the possibility of promoting international cooperation and coordination for the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity outside areas of national jurisdiction. the group recommended the development of a legally binding international instrument. on the basis of this recommendation, the united nations general assembly decided in july 2015 to establish a preparatory committee with a view to drafting the text of an internationally legally binding instrument by the end of 2017. the report by the european parliament comes ahead of an intergovernmental conference on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ the law of the sea negotiations aim to fill the gaps in the montego bay treaty on the high seas, in order to defend biodiversity. the nicolai report proposes marine protected areas, the registration of ships worldwide, and scientific monitoring of new activities to exploit marine resources. the objective is commendable, but the fight against illegal fishing is the most important. it is the one that seriously damages biodiversity. for the time being, the nicolai report is simply encouraging international cooperation. this is not enough, but the negotiations are just beginning and should not be concluded until around 2022. we can then judge this report by the results it produces.

in writing. ‒ the refugee crisis has shown that the current approach to immigration in the eu is not sustainable. this holistic report seeks to give a global answer and that is why i voted in favour of it. immigration is perhaps the most important challenge the eu has to face because, like the refugee crisis, it confronts us with the question of solidarity as the basis of the european model. how we treat people who come to the eu in search of a better tomorrow says a lot about who we are. the importance of this report lies in its addressing the main issues that characterize the migratory challenge. the most important of these include the reform of the dublin system, rescue operations at sea to prevent the mediterranean from becoming a seabed and the establishment of a permanent and legally binding mechanism establishing a quota for the distribution of refugees among the member states. it is also important to include humanitarian visas and promote legal and safe access routes to the eu, as well as to redouble our commitment to fighting the mafia that exploits people and to improve reception and integration policies.
in writing. ‒ this report is a missed opportunity for the libe commission to put on the agenda the problems currently faced by people trying to get to the eu. instead of requiring the issuing of humanitarian visas or the guarantee that mass expulsions will not take place (which are prohibited by international law and enshrined in the eu-turkey agreement), it has been decided to maintain the current aggressive policy imposed by the commission and the council. although the agreement includes positive things, such as the need to create safe access routes, or the need to overcome the dublin system and to welcome states, these issues appear to be mentioned without concrete measures, so they are again empty statements. however, it details the plan for the militarization of the mediterranean with the help of nato, the need for returns, cooperation with military and security forces of third countries, or the drawing up of a list of safe countries from which asylum applications will not be accepted, in clear violation of the geneva convention. for all these reasons, we have not had to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ we abstain from voting because we consider that, despite some progress with respect to the original text and the current terms of the eu's migration and asylum policy, the text enshrines the validity of the unacceptable and illegal eu-turkey agreement, which involves the irresponsible outsourcing of the management of the european migration, asylum and refuge system to countries where the disregard for human rights is evident and systematic.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report in view of the serious humanitarian situation facing the eu. member states must understand that it is essential for the eu to have the capacity and the means to fight against trafficking in human beings and irregular immigration, and to have a common asylum policy capable of responding to the challenges posed by the exodus of several million syrian refugees. we must protect those entitled to international protection, while showing our determination to control our borders, preventing the illegal entry of economic migrants and returning all those who are not susceptible to international protection. the only real solution to ensure the survival of schengen is the creation of a genuine common european external border, with increased powers for frontex, as well as a common asylum policy. if we are not able to guarantee external control of the eu's borders, the schengen area of free movement is in serious danger of disappearing in the face of the migratory pressure on the eu.

in writing. ‒ for this report on immigration, particularly illegal immigration, the left and the right have agreed to join forces and finally show their honesty by showing that their positions are identical: the union must welcome as many migrants as possible, even if the europeans do not agree and even if these migrants are dangerous. this report fortunately has no legislative effect, but it will serve as a basis for future binding measures to be taken by the member states under the commission's auspices for the mandatory distribution of migrants in all countries. the report proposes, among other things, the creation of direct air bridges, the granting of asylum on the basis of sexual orientation, but not the rape of european women by migrants who are self-proclaimed homosexuals. it obviously supports family reunification and transforms every rescue attempt (asylum for unaccompanied minors or circumcised women for example) into a new immigration route to be exploited by smugglers at the expense of local populations. by following the proposals in this report, the union would not only go against the will of the peoples of europe, but would itself become an accomplice to the trafficking it encourages. i have of course voted against this report, the sole purpose of which is to encourage mass immigration.
in writing. ‒ we abstain from voting because we consider that, despite some progress with respect to the original text and the current terms of the eu's migration and asylum policy, the text enshrines the validity of the unacceptable and illegal eu-turkey agreement, which involves the irresponsible outsourcing of the management of the european migration, asylum and refuge system to countries where the disregard for human rights is evident and systematic.
in writing. ‒ the refugee crisis has shown that the current approach to immigration in the eu is not sustainable. this holistic report seeks to give a global answer and that is why i voted in favour of it. immigration is perhaps the most important challenge the eu has to face because, like the refugee crisis, it confronts us with the question of solidarity as the basis of the european model. how we treat people who come to the eu in search of a better tomorrow says a lot about who we are. the importance of this report lies in its addressing the main issues that characterize the migratory challenge. the most important of these include the reform of the dublin system, rescue operations at sea to prevent the mediterranean from becoming a seabed and the establishment of a permanent and legally binding mechanism establishing a quota for the distribution of refugees among the member states. it is also important to include humanitarian visas and promote legal and safe access routes to the eu, as well as to redouble our commitment to fighting the mafia that exploits people and to improve reception and integration policies.

in writing. ‒ this report is a missed opportunity for the libe commission to put on the agenda the problems currently faced by people trying to get to the eu. instead of requiring the issuing of humanitarian visas or the guarantee that mass expulsions will not take place (which are prohibited by international law and enshrined in the eu-turkey agreement), it has been decided to maintain the current aggressive policy imposed by the commission and the council. although the agreement includes positive things, such as the need to create safe access routes, or the need to overcome the dublin system and to welcome states, these issues appear to be mentioned without concrete measures, so they are again empty statements. however, it details the plan for the militarization of the mediterranean with the help of nato, the need for returns, cooperation with military and security forces of third countries, or the drawing up of a list of safe countries from which asylum applications will not be accepted, in clear violation of the geneva convention. for all these reasons, we have not had to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to assess the different policies involved and the latest data from different agencies and associations, on the situation of migrants and refugees who have arrived or are trying to reach the eu, as well as the applications that have been submitted requiring international protection. it also assesses the damage caused by the lack of resources, such as disappearances and deaths, of men, women and children who risk their lives every day in order to seek a better life. this report also considers the trafficking in human beings and labour exploitation that arise from such extreme situations and awareness of the need to take measures to prevent it. i support its adoption because it also discusses the various measures that the commission is implementing and/or proposing to improve border management and stresses the need to create safe routes so that both refugees and economic migrants can have the protection they need. in view of the above considerations and the importance of cooperation and coordination in this field at european level, i am voting in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the report on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a comprehensive eu approach to migration that we have adopted in this parliament makes it clear that we need to address the terrible situation we are experiencing at the moment from a united position and with an approach that takes into account all the factors involved in this crisis. only in this way will the eu be able to give a response that is worthy of what is expected of us, because there are no easy ways out or shortcuts, but we must be courageous and take decisions that reconcile the rights of people living in europe and those who are trying to reach our continent fleeing war.
in writing. ‒ what is happening in the mediterranean is a disgrace. this report, which is very comprehensive, is parliament's hope that the council and the member states will stop turning their backs on all the tragedies that are happening every day. because we don't just need texts and we don't need money, that too. we need political will. it is a very difficult situation which will mark the eu for the future.

in writing. ‒ we are talking about a report which is the result of more than a year of work in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs and which aims to assess the various policies put in place in the area of migration, asylum and border control and to develop a set of recommendations to be implemented in the short, medium and long term.
in writing. ‒ the refugee crisis has shown that the current approach to immigration in the eu is not sustainable. this holistic report seeks to give a global answer and that is why i voted in favour of it. immigration is perhaps the most important challenge the eu has to face because, like the refugee crisis, it confronts us with the question of solidarity as the basis of the european model. how we treat people who come to the eu in search of a better tomorrow says a lot about who we are. the importance of this report lies in its addressing the main issues that characterize the migratory challenge. the most important of these include the reform of the dublin system, rescue operations at sea to prevent the mediterranean from becoming a seabed and the establishment of a permanent and legally binding mechanism establishing a quota for the distribution of refugees among the member states. it is also important to include humanitarian visas and promote legal and safe access routes to the eu, as well as to redouble our commitment to fighting the mafia that exploits people and to improve reception and integration policies.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it jeopardises the delicate balance, which is essential for the proper functioning of the union. the report calls for the creation of additional procedural steps in our legislative process which slow down the already heavy bureaucratic burden on our institutions and make it almost impossible for the legislative process to take place. under these principles and outside areas of exclusive competence, the european union should only intervene if it is able to act more effectively than eu countries at their respective national or local levels. these principles require that the means used by the eu to achieve the objectives set by the treaties may not go beyond what is necessary. the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality must be balanced with the need for the efficiency of the work of our institutions. this balance must be balanced by measures. we must say yes to these principles, but not at the expense of the effectiveness of the union for its citizens.
in writing. ‒ this report rightly notes how the principle of subsidiarity can be invoked to stop proposals that are very harmful to the working class, such as the monti ii directive in the past (which limited the right to strike in the states) or, in the present, the inclusion of isds (which sanction states that regulate against the interests of multinationals) in trade treaties. it also sees it as a democratizing element, allowing national parliaments to have a greater say in european decisions. it also notes the importance of proportionality in legislation (which, as the report's accompanying employment opinion argues, should not be used as a pretext for reducing social rights). however, the text resists explicitly denouncing how the ambiguity inherent in the concepts of subsidiarity and proportionality is being used by the eu to reduce its legislation to its neoliberal core (competition, governance, single market, trade agreements...) and to contribute to a deregulatory agenda, respectively. the complicit silence on the issue of governance, which represents a clear attack on subsidiarity with its blackmail of public finances, is particularly serious. i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ we abstained on this report on subsidiarity and proportionality because, although it has some interesting aspects in terms of transparency and evaluation of the legislative process for the protection of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, the overall view of the text is conservative, and proposes to regulate international litigation systems between investors and states, which we reject.
in writing. ‒ the subsidiarity principle aims to determine the most relevant level of intervention in areas of shared competence between the eu and eu countries, whether at national, regional or local level. in any event, the eu can only intervene when its action is more effective than that of the national, regional or local administrations of the member states. the principle of proportionality, applicable to all eu action, provides that union action must be limited to what is necessary to achieve the objectives set out in the treaties. applying these principles helps to determine when the eu has the power to legislate and helps to ensure that decisions are taken as closely as possible to the citizens. the european parliament draws up annual reports on the application of these principles in the union. i have decided not to support the reports for 2012 and 2013 used by the british conservative rapporteur to put forward his anti-european and eurosceptic agenda. these reports are intended to strengthen the powers of national parliaments to obstruct decisions taken by the union, to reduce their legislative capacity and to weaken the european project.

in writing. ‒ the principle of subsidiarity and the principle of proportionality are fundamental to the proper functioning of the european union and are the starting point of european policies. the principle of subsidiarity brings european policy closer to the citizen and determines when the european union has the power to legislate. the same applies to the principle of proportionality, which makes any action by the european union meaningful and appropriate to the objective pursued. this report is very important because it seeks to ensure the effectiveness and also the democratic legitimacy of decision-making and in some way it strengthens the european project. it is true that since the treaty of lisbon a whole series of cards have been created for the use of national parliaments to establish mechanisms for properly monitoring the application of these principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. it is important to note that this has been done normally, but it is true that all these mechanisms have to be agile, they have to be really simple and they have to be effective. the most important thing in these cases is cooperation between all national and european administrations and ensuring and reinforcing these two principles.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, fully convinced that the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are fundamental principles of the european union. we must therefore always bear in mind that, wherever possible, the administration closest to the citizen should be responsible for developing policies. this means that the regions must play a key role in shaping and implementing european policies.

in writing. ‒ subsidiarity and proportionality are the two fundamental principles which should ensure that the european union is built in a way that respects the sovereignty of the member states. the annual reports on these issues are therefore important as they aim to expose abuses of commission powers. the report points out that few national parliaments are exploring the possibilities of appeal (the so-called 'yellow card') and that when they do, the commission does not follow up as expected. it is regrettable, however, that this report does not propose the introduction of a red card to oppose a commission act which is detrimental to its vital interests. my personal experience of objections to implementing acts (on the authorization of gmos or chemicals), which are genuine decisions without appeal by the commission, shows that the european parliament itself is not inclined to exercise its role of monitoring and defending the interests of citizens. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ the annual reports for 2012 and 2013 are produced to ensure that the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality protected by the teu are respected when the eu institutions make use of their devolved powers. however, they clarify that much remains to be done to strengthen its consideration. it suggests that the ec should participate in annual debates with each of the national parliaments in order to strengthen the dialogue with them. i support the adoption of this report, which also examines the reasoned opinions of national parliaments in recent years expressing their concern to the commission about the lack of respect for these principles. it also stresses the value of certain instruments used by the ec, such as impact assessments, which support decision-making during the legislative process, and thus give due weight to issues relating to subsidiarity and proportionality. i therefore vote in favour of the adoption of this report and underline the importance of political dialogue as a tool to improve and ensure respect for these principles.

i have supported this report because i believe that any action taken by the commission to review and improve the quality of european legislation is the right one. in my experience of national legislation, i am convinced that when legislation is adopted, less is always more, and this is doubly true of european legislation. so if the european commission is setting up a programme to examine the quality of individual legislative proposals and then evaluate the application of these laws, then i think that is right. i also welcome the fact that one of the juncker commission's key points was to slow down the legislative process and really downgrade it. this is also evident from the fact that, compared to the number of proposed legislation under the previous commission, the juncker commission is proposing fewer regulations. i think that is right and that we should be much more concerned with how the legislation is subsequently implemented and how it works in practice.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it represents a breakthrough in legislation, a step forward in simplifying eu rules and reducing the costs it entails. in this connection, and with a view to promoting employment in europe, reducing bureaucratic burdens seems to us to be an appropriate means. employment standards cannot be lowered and job insecurity must not increase, so the idea of 'better regulation' must not become an excuse to eliminate regulation and reduce the eu's legislative capacity. it is about putting the whole eu regulatory apparatus in shape, while assessing the performance of regulation emanating from the european institutions. the protection of social dialogue and the role of consumers and social partners, as well as environmental, social, health and safety standards, were also ensured. the commission has also succeeded in rejecting the conservative and anti-european calls.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because, despite its technical appearance, it provides political support for the commission's strategy to increase its legislative power and avoid scrutiny of its decisions. ex ante, the commission politically reinforces its neoliberal agenda with consultations and technical studies tailored to its interests, which allow it to set the limits of the political discussion. ex post, it reserves the right to withdraw legislative proposals which parliament has modified (as was the case with the maternity directive) or to introduce changes in their application which end up emptying their content (as has happened with the new parameters for nox emissions or chemical toxicity, reach). both changes, under the slogans of 'better', 'more appropriate', 'more informed' or 'more effective' regulation, cannot hide the anti-democratic bias that characterises the european construction.
in writing. ‒ this report is in line with the refit programme (regulatory adequacy and effectiveness programme). although we are critical of many aspects of its implementation in the regulatory framework of legislative procedures, we abstained because the regulatory framework is not aimed at undermining the rights of workers.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for her report on the adequacy and effectiveness of the regulation. in this report i differed with my group on the vote on paragraph 47, which refers to the nutritional profile and nutritional and health claims in food and particularly the problems of distortion of competition. it is requested that the scientific basis, usefulness and feasibility of regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 be reviewed.
in writing. ‒ refit is the european commission's regulatory fitness and performance programme. the programme includes measures to simplify eu legislation and reduce the costs it entails. the refit programme is part of a wider concept of 'smart regulation' or 'better regulation'. this improvement of legislation consists in designing eu rules and policies so that they achieve their objectives at the least cost. for the socialists, the idea of 'better regulation' must not become an excuse to eliminate regulation and reduce the eu's legislative capacity. with this report, led by the socialists, we have succeeded in ensuring, within the framework of this programme, the protection of social dialogue and the role of consumers and social partners, as well as environmental, social, health and safety standards. we have also succeeded in rejecting the conservative and anti-european calls for the creation of an independent advisory body for better regulation, and in limiting the attempts of eurosceptic groups to impede the union's legislative capacity. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it represents a breakthrough in legislation, a step forward in simplifying eu rules and reducing the costs it entails. in this connection, and with a view to promoting employment in europe, reducing bureaucratic burdens seems to us to be an appropriate means. employment standards cannot be lowered and job insecurity must not increase, so the idea of 'better regulation' must not become an excuse to eliminate regulation and reduce the eu's legislative capacity. it is about putting the whole eu regulatory apparatus in shape, while assessing the performance of regulation emanating from the european institutions. the protection of social dialogue and the role of consumers and social partners, as well as environmental, social, health and safety standards, were also ensured. the commission has also succeeded in rejecting the conservative and anti-european calls.

in writing. ‒ the refit programme was launched in december 2012. it is the continuation of a project to reduce administrative burdens that was implemented between 2007 and 2012. since then, work has continued, simplifying and reducing burdens in a whole range of fields, such as patents, public procurement, electronic vat invoicing, etc. until we created this refit platform. the objectives pursued, as regards simplification and improvement of regulation, are to improve regulation to increase the competitiveness of enterprises, to ensure legal certainty and to contribute to market unity and to reduce the bureaucratic burden of administration, by removing obstacles and increasing simplification to facilitate administrative processing by citizens and entrepreneurs for a better exercise of their rights and fulfillment of their obligations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report. we must bear in mind - as president juncker announced at the beginning of his mandate - the need to legislate better to meet the expectations of citizens. the objective of better law-making should cover the need to simplify legislation and should include the implementation and enforcement of union acts at european, national, regional and local level. similarly, the eu institutions must always bear in mind in their actions the need to maintain an open, transparent and regular dialogue with representative associations and civil society.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it represents a step forward in legislation, in particular in simplifying eu rules and reducing costs. in this connection, and with a view to promoting employment in europe, reducing bureaucratic burdens seems to us to be an appropriate means. employment standards cannot be lowered and job insecurity must not increase. the idea of 'better regulation' should not therefore become an excuse for eliminating regulation and reducing the eu's legislative capacity. it is about strengthening the whole eu regulatory apparatus, while assessing the performance of regulation emanating from the european institutions. the protection of social dialogue and the role of consumers and social partners, as well as environmental, social, health and safety standards, were also ensured. finally, the rejection of the conservative and anti-europeanist appeals was achieved.

in writing. ‒ the refit programme aims to establish recommendations for more effective european regulation. we can highlight positive points in this report, including the recommendation for a more judicious use of delegated acts (which parliament can oppose and force the commission to revise its proposal) and implementing acts (which parliament can oppose but without any power of constraint on the commission). the report also calls for more impact studies, particularly in terms of the competitiveness of our companies, which is often sacrificed on the altar of the fight against pollution without ever questioning the globalist model that transforms our industries into soldiers without agility. the report recommends, however, that the regulation, which is directly applicable in national law, should be used more often, in particular to promote the internal market. we are certainly opposed to these provisions. in view of all these points, i therefore abstained on this report.
in writing. ‒ this report is in line with the refit programme (regulatory adequacy and effectiveness programme). although we are critical of many aspects of its implementation in the regulatory framework of legislative procedures, we abstained because the regulatory framework is not aimed at undermining the rights of workers.

in writing. ‒ i believe that the refit instrument is an essential element for improving legislation at european level, for better lawmaking, for simplifying eu law and for reducing administrative burdens. this is the beginning of a path towards good governance, where impact assessments and ex post controls have the relevant role that i believe they deserve in policy making. i support this report as it includes the updates that the ec has made on the refit programme and assesses all the progress made in the different policy areas and on the initiatives selected by the commission, including the measures adopted by parliament and the council. i also consider it necessary since the 2003 interinstitutional agreement on better law-making has become obsolete following the creation of the current legislative environment under the lisbon treaty. i therefore vote in favour of this report because i believe that this legislative instrument is important and will also help to establish a coherent work programme and policy approach, which will make the eu more transparent and more acceptable to its citizens.
in writing. ‒ we are all clear that our legislation needs to be further improved. it is not a question of making more legislation just for the sake of it, but of doing a few things well and improving the existing ones. in this parliament we are clear that the refit programme must not be used to undermine sustainability or any social, labour, environmental or consumer legislation. and we believe that every effort should be made to improve transparency and facilitate the participation of stakeholders in the whole legislative process.
in writing. ‒ efit is the european commission's regulatory fitness and effectiveness programme. the programme includes measures to simplify eu legislation and reduce the costs it entails. the refit programme is part of a wider concept of 'smart regulation' or 'better regulation'. this improvement of legislation consists in designing eu rules and policies so that they achieve their objectives at the least cost. for the socialists, the idea of 'better regulation' must not become an excuse to eliminate regulation and reduce the eu's legislative capacity. with this report, led by the socialists, we have succeeded in ensuring, within the framework of this programme, the protection of social dialogue and the role of consumers and social partners, as well as environmental, social, health and safety standards. we have also succeeded in rejecting the conservative and anti-european calls for the creation of an independent advisory body for better regulation, and in limiting the attempts of eurosceptic groups to impede the union's legislative capacity. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ my vote was against since i am concerned that the regulatory simplification (refit) might lower in the legislation the level of ambition on issues related – i.e. to the well—being of people and the protection of environment by not properly distinguishing between the reduction of administrative burdens and the reduction of regulatory burdens, as reducing regulatory burdens questions the very existence of the laws and the protection provided by those laws.
in writing. ‒ the regulatory fitness and performance programme (refit) has as its main objectives the reduction of red tape and administrative burdens on the one hand and the simplification and improvement of legislation on the other in order to achieve the policy objectives and respecting the legality of the treaties and the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. we are talking about a report which is sending an important political signal today by supporting the commission's 'better regulation' agenda. i am glad that the commission has taken this opportunity to make a statement on the subject.

this report builds on the previous report. it is again about the quality of the legislation, in this case the single internal market. i personally consider the single market to be one of the main positive aspects of european integration, and it is therefore good that this topic is dealt with separately, especially in contrast to the previous report, which generally evaluates the implementation and application of european legislation. it is important to be aware of the importance of the quality of european legislation, especially in this area. if european legislation is very general, then the implementation in individual member states, in each country, is different, and we are left with 28 different national legal regimes. it is therefore good to look at the quality of the individual directives and regulations governing the eu's internal market, and i am therefore pleased that the european commission has given us clear figures showing how implementation is progressing.
in writing. ‒ the report makes it clear that the development of the single market must not run counter to fundamental rights, while stressing the need for dialogue with organised civil society and the need to protect social, environmental and safety and security standards contained in european regulation. however, it continues to interpret the deepening of the single market as a priority in the face of 'over-regulation' and 'barriers' that would plague the european economy, ignoring those of us who believe that the improvement of the living conditions of europeans must prioritize the upward harmonisation of social legislation and the democratisation of the institutions governing the single market. that is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ although the report has some positive elements in terms of the implementation of the single market - especially in terms of transparency, the role of national parliaments or market surveillance, which we voted in favour of - it does not significantly correct the profile of the single market dominated by the commodification of all socio-productive relations, without elements of redistribution or compensatory. the report does not substantially correct the structural inequalities in the european union, which are reinforced by the single market mechanisms. that is why we are voting against.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report on improving the regulation of the single market, a responsibility shared by each of the union's institutions. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu concerning the definition of the criteria and mechanisms for determining the union's macro-financial assistance to third countries and international organisations, in particular the european investment bank and the european banking authority. the institutions must be firm in this fundamental objective.
in writing. ‒ we believe that the single market is a key instrument for boosting economic growth and job creation in the union, but we believe that a number of crucial issues, such as promoting better regulation and greater subsidiarity, should be emphasised. we also want to achieve more accessible eu legislation, balanced against the prerogatives of the member states, to achieve harmonised european standards on social, labour, environmental and consumer protection standards. that is why i voted in favour of the report entitled 'towards better regulation of the single market'.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to introduce a european dimension in school education in order to restore citizens' confidence in the european union. but the report does not explain why citizens' distrust and discredit of the present eu has increased. the report is cynically promoting the principles and values enshrined in article 2 of the eu treaty, but fails to criticise the systematic violation of these principles within the eu itself. for these reasons i could not vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ most of the points we have opposed are due to the vagueness of the concept of the european dimension used. we are not opposed to more information about the eu being given at different levels of education, but rather we believe that greater knowledge of the procedures and powers of the eu bodies is something that is positive in every way. however, we do not think that training should be confused with propaganda, and in this sense this report does not envisage or incorporate the causes or responsibilities of the authors causing the situation of inequality in which we live in europe today, while on the contrary it is full of additional precisions on the term euroscepticism. we note that there are some positive and relevant contributions, but we believe that the general spirit of the report is aimed at remedying a lack of legitimacy, such as that suffered by the european project in different regions, rather than making the population aware of the operation, causes and consequences of the european project. that is why we abstained.
in writing. ‒ i wholeheartedly support this report on learning about the eu in school. this presents two fundamental and interrelated aspects. the first is the acquisition of knowledge, and the second is based on the idea of the legitimacy and stability of the entire democratic political system which is largely based on civic engagement. there is a limited understanding of what the eu is, with a negative view, and of what it represents and has represented since its constitution. this is a legacy that our future generations must know.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which defends the need to integrate a european dimension into education as a key element to help citizens better understand the eu ‒ and reconnect with it ‒, to deepen the role of the union's fundamental values and to promote adherence to them. as the report points out, knowing and understanding the history and common values of the eu and its member states is key to mutual understanding, peaceful coexistence, tolerance and solidarity, as well as to understanding the union's fundamental principles. the report reviews and proposes specific measures for curricula, teacher training, teaching methods, mobility, research and the use of new technologies. it also recognises the role played by social partners and civil society organisations. at a time when the eu is facing serious challenges, the integration of a european dimension into education should enable pupils to acquire knowledge and develop a sense of belonging, but also to initiate critical reflection on the eu, in particular through learning about the eu's core values based on the rule of law and human rights.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to ensure that children from an early age take the european union flag as a banner worthy of allegiance. the report is a veritable propaganda tool against the clear and growing wishes of another europe, and it does not hesitate to propose the homogenization of school curricula by incorporating a component on european citizenship and, above all, to argue that the union would be better placed to define the curricula than the member states. education is one of the few areas where member states still have exclusive competence, which has angered pro-eu meps, often the same ones who promote gender education. this point is also addressed with the demand for an education that promotes multiculturalism and non-discrimination. our group tabled an alternative resolution recalling that education is the exclusive responsibility of the member states and that basic knowledge must take precedence over ideology. i supported the proposal of dominique bilde and voted against the draghici report.

in writing. ‒ unfortunately, a large majority of europeans are unaware of the functioning and relevance of the european institutions and tend to perceive a certain democratic deficit in them. this has two terrible consequences: on the one hand, the low participation of european citizens in european electoral processes and, on the other, the growth of so-called euroscepticism. that is why, through this report, parliament is proposing that european schools should be given a better understanding of the european union, that children should develop a sense of european citizenship, that they should understand what it means to be european and that they should share the fundamental values of the rule of law and the defence of human rights. to this end, we propose that the commission, among other things, continue to maintain and increase funding for education and mobility programmes and develop a common framework for learning about the union. we also ask the member states to use all the means at their disposal to promote a high profile of european union knowledge among their teachers. from what i've seen, my vote will be in favour.

we support this erasmus+ report, mr president, because it will enable students in vocational training to have access to european mobility programmes during their studies. the commission's proposal is to be incorporated in the treaty of rome, and the council's proposal is to be incorporated in the treaty of rome. today, cities such as london, paris or berlin are full of young spaniards in precarious jobs because of the lack of job expectations in their country. there has to be a strict surveillance on this programme and the status of the apprentice has to be regulated. we know that in recent years many workers have been laid off and many workers have been replaced by trainees with lower pay and fewer rights. in no case can internships replace stable jobs. in no case may the practices be used to dismiss workers and used as a regular form of work. in the southern countries where this is the case, we know the disastrous consequences for the quality of employment. so mobility for training, for opportunities, fighting discrimination and promoting equal opportunities, yes. labour mobility as an obligation, as an alternative to quality employment, no.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is clearly european in its approach to unifying the representation of the member states of the european union in international financial institutions such as the international monetary fund or the oecd. the overall weight of the union cannot be effectively projected if the member states continue to resist giving up their seats in international organisations. in particular, the eurozone should be represented as such in the international monetary fund, while all the member states should concentrate their shares in development banks such as the world bank in a european chair (a proposal which is not covered by the report). it also makes no sense that the european central bank is not the only eurozone institution represented in the bank for international settlements, a matter which will have to be addressed in the future. the report also contains important guidance on the kind of positions the eu should take in international organisations in which it participates (promotion of sustainable development, combating climate change, promotion of human rights, etc.) which i fully share.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it transfers fundamental powers of representation to the european commission, which will be able to take decisions in different international economic forums such as the international monetary fund, the oecd or the world bank on behalf of the member states of the european union. the commission has shown, especially in the field of economic policy, that it is pursuing policies which are contrary to the will of the people of europe. the orientation of many developed policies has shown the unequal treatment of the central and peripheral economies of the continent. with this experience the transfer of additional powers, in this case representation in international economic forums, is detrimental to democratic participation in economic decisions. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report, which, based on the current or ongoing european economic and financial integration (monetary union, capital market union, banking union, etc.) advocates that the european union should have a single representation in international forums dealing with financial matters. in our view, economic integration is the opposite of integration based on solidarity and redistribution and not on financial markets. we also think that given the enormous inequalities within the union, it is wrong to think that the union can have a single voice representing its interests.
