the next item on the agenda is the brief presentation of the report by kostadinka kuneva on domestic workers and carers in the eu (2015/2094 (ini)) (a8-0053/2016).
mr president, i would first of all like to thank mrs kostadinka kuneva for the enormous work she has done on this report and for the close cooperation she has had with the committee on employment and social affairs, whose opinion on this report i have asked for. domestic workers and carers are one of the most unprotected groups of workers in the european union, and already in 2011, the international labour organization tried to provide us with an international framework, with its convention no. 189, to guarantee decent work for domestic workers and carers, without much success in the european union, since only six member countries have ratified it. these workers suffer from conditions of absolute unprotectedness and vulnerability: very long hours, very low wages, and no guarantees of safety and health at work. we need a legislative framework to guarantee the professionalisation of care and, in addition, we need public investment to develop active information and professionalisation policies. as we know, it is a job that is 88% done by women, which suggests that there has not been much interest in regulating it. their professionalisation would be a boost for women's equality and an opportunity to create jobs and put care at the centre of our societies.
member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mrs kuneva, for her report, which sheds light on a sector that employs at least 53 million people in the world, with around 2.5 million in the eu, according to the international labour organisation’s figures. as is rightly stressed in the report, this is a highly feminised sector: 83 % of all domestic workers are women. i have read the report carefully and i share several concerns: for example, the need for recognition of the profession of domestic workers and carers, reducing undeclared work in the sector, promoting labour market integration and raising awareness and sharing good practices among member states. given the rapid ageing of the population, the demand for care and household services is expected to increase in all member states. i am glad that parliament welcomes our approach for a ‘new start for working parents and care—givers’ because our aim is to take account of recent developments and the needs of the families – those with elderly or dependent relatives, not only parents – and make more equitable use of family-related leave arrangements between partners. several commission studies show the importance of the professionalising of domestic work and care. in this regard, the commission financed three projects to explore the cost—effectiveness of public support for this sector, the quality of services and the productivity gain. the european quality framework for long-term care services, launched in 2012, aims to improve the quality of life for older people in need of care and assistance. i also note the request for further analysis on the added value of a professionalisation of the sector of domestic work. i agree that the professionalisation of household service workers and care workers will increase the attractiveness of the sector and the quality of the service provided because it can create jobs. the commission staff working document on ‘exploiting the potential of personal and household services’, published in 2012, recognised the potential for job opportunities for the relatively low skilled, in particular as far as housework services are concerned, at a low cost for public finance. to this end, the provision of housework services in the formal economy, rather than in the shadow one, should be encouraged. some member states have already put in place a policy on personal and household services: for example, france and belgium with service vouchers, finland with tax credit for domestic help or sweden with tax deduction for service acquisition. promoting the professional recognition of skills and qualifications is also a priority for domestic workers and carers. all people in europe must have the right skills for jobs. this can improve their life opportunities. this is why the upcoming skills agenda will have a particular focus on improving the transparency of skills and qualifications. this could be very relevant for people with a migrant background or for refugees’ labour market integration. as regards the international labour organisation convention on fair and decent work for domestic workers (no. 189), the commission has regularly promoted its ratification. in december 2015, together with the luxembourg eu council presidency, we invited member states to an expert meeting on the ratification of this convention. we acknowledge the plea for an appropriate level of health and safety at work for the workers of this sector. the question of the exclusion of domestic servants from the scope of directive 89/391/eec on safety and health at work will be examined in the light of the outcome of the ongoing evaluation of the eu acquis in the area of occupational safety and health. as is mentioned in the report, there has been an increase in recent years in the proportion of female domestic workers who are migrants. i also take note of the recommendation, both to the commission and the member states, to ensure the availability of legal avenues for migration to the eu and to introduce targeted legal migration programmes. the commission has launched a global action programme on migrant domestic workers and their families, which entails pilot projects supporting migrant domestic workers including in europe. i share the concerns about undeclared work, which is particularly high in this sector and has a negative impact on these people’s working conditions, the quality of their services and, more broadly, the economy. the formalisation of their work would provide adequate social protection and create additional revenues for public finance. it would also increase the quality of their services, which is strongly linked to their working conditions and the recognition of their qualifications. i am confident that the newly—established european platform to enhance cooperation in the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work will contribute to raising awareness and sharing good practices, analysis and experiences to find solutions to the challenges faced by this sector. i am glad that parliament stresses the important role social partners can play in addressing sector—specific challenges in the care work sector. we will be interested in following their activities in that domain, while of course respecting their autonomy. in conclusion, i would like to recall that it is the commission’s firm intention to steer the union more strongly towards social fairness. no one should be left behind, and that includes domestic workers. the report is therefore both timely and helpful to move forward on several policy files and help us connect the dots between them.

in writing. there are 2.5 million domestic and care workers in europe (88% are women). the vast majority do not contribute to social security, do not enjoy retirement, do not have health insurance, earn a meagre wage in the dark and work long hours, without the right to rest or paid holidays. many are illegal immigrants. others are family members who care for dependents without salary or entitlement. the eu must address this unfair situation by introducing a legal framework for the professionalisation of domestic work and care, and by introducing a directive to regulate the situation of non-professional carers who care for dependent family members. states should define a specific legal framework to allow for the regular recruitment of domestic and care workers and to establish the rights and duties of employers and workers. these people take care of our children and dependent family members and also of us so that we can develop our jobs and vocations outside the home, whose maintenance they take care of. how will they live when they reach retirement age? when will they be able to enjoy the rights of the welfare state? when will they stop being second-class workers with no labor rights?
the next item on the agenda is the brief presentation of the report by terry reintke on gender equality and the empowerment of women in the digital age (2015/2007(ini)) (a8-0048/2016).
member of the commission.– mr president, i am happy to have the opportunity today to discuss with you the current situation regarding gender equality and empowering women in the digital age. this is a topic that deserves our undivided attention. the fact that women are under-represented throughout the ict sector is a key challenge that we need to tackle. the report by mrs reintke very much contributes to raising awareness of this challenge and offers solid recommendations that are aimed at strengthening women’s participation in the ict sector. the report brings us a step closer to closing the gender gap in the sector, and for this reason i would like to thank the rapporteur of this excellent and forward—looking report. the commission is fully committed to take further action in this area, as outlined in the ‘strategic engagement for gender equality’. the grand coalition for digital jobs, for example, is a multi-stakeholder partnership, which tackles the lack of digital skills in europe. some of the pledges target only women. the strategic engagement includes a key action that focuses on using the grand coalition for digital jobs to support measures enhancing digital skills among women and girls and promoting female employment in the ict sector. the commission has been active in promoting opportunities for girls and women in the sector as well. the ict sector is rapidly growing, creating around 120 000 new jobs every year. in view of the good job and salary prospects, we would like to see more women take advantage of this situation and consider a career in the sector. women active in this sector generally enjoy higher flexibility to arrange their working schedules and will be less susceptible to unemployment. when considering economic arguments for increasing female participation in the ict sector, the commission’s study on women active in the sector found that more women entering the digital jobs market can create an annual eur 9 billion gdp boost in the eu area. furthermore, women working in the sector earn almost 9% more than women in similar positions in other service sectors. in order to increase women’s opportunities in the digital age, it is of the utmost importance to tackle women’s under-representation in the sector. at this moment, only nine in 100 european app developers are female; 19% of ict managers are women and less than 30% of the ict workforce is female. when we look at the educational aspect we see that, today, only 29 out of every 1 000 female graduates have a computing or related degree. the commission supports several initiatives that promote getting more women into digital jobs and encourage girls to pursue ict-related subjects. for example, the european network of women web entrepreneurs hubs (wehubs) is the first network of partners which specifically supports women to create and scale-up their web enterprises, building links between women entrepreneurs, investors and the web entrepreneurship ecosystems. the digital single market with its e-society dimension constitutes a great opportunity for women in digital. but we need more role models, mentoring, greater engagement of business and industry by offering even more targeted programmes to study and work in the ict sector. more grass-root initiatives like the code week are needed – during the 2015 eu code week half of the almost half a million young coders were young girls! we also need to get men involved in the debate on diversity. i strongly believe that tackling gender stereotypes will contribute to creating equal opportunities in the workplace and will attract more women to the sector. as also highlighted in the report, the increasing digitalisation of society also poses some threats to gender equality, including cyber—bullying, cyber—harassment, cyber—stalking and sexist forms of hate speech. the fundamental rights agency survey on women’s experiences of violence shows that one in ten women has experienced sexual harassment or stalking through new technologies. all forms of violence against women and girls, including cyber-violence, are rooted in gender inequalities and reinforce them further. the eu is committed to fighting against such violence as affirmed in a number of strategic documents. an important action that the commission has undertaken in this area is the proposals for the european union to sign and conclude the council of europe’s istanbul convention, a comprehensive international treaty on combatting violence against women and domestic violence. this includes provisions to encourage the participation of the information and communication technology sector in combating this phenomenon, also in the online sphere. considering the excellent recommendations outlined in the report, it is clear that there are significant challenges ahead of us. let us take advantage of the new and great opportunities and explore ways to advance women’s empowerment in the digital age. i look forward to tackling the challenges together in order to break down gender stereotypes and use the technological innovations as drivers of progress towards gender equality.

mr president, last week hundreds of people went back to the castilian town of villar de cañas, in cuenca, to demand that the construction of a nuclear waste repository be stopped. in response to questions i have put to the european commission, it has been acknowledged that this project does not have the mandatory reports required by the euratom treaty, which spain has signed. the technical staff of the nuclear safety council also denounce political pressure and the fact that reports are approved with which they do not agree. and to make matters worse, the site is considered inappropriate by many experts. but the spanish government continues and does not cease in its efforts to place in villar de cañas a nuclear cemetery built without the minimum guarantees and with a total lack of information to the citizens. and i ask here: is castile also europe? can the european union contemplate the construction of a high-risk nuclear facility in this way and not get involved? castile wants security, it wants respect and it wants investments that will stop the bleeding of its population and not become the dump of what nobody wants.
mr president, in order to meet the deficit set by the european commission for 2016, last week the spanish ministry of finance asked the autonomous governments to take on the entire amount of the necessary cuts. centrifuging the deficit is unfair in terms of territorial equity. the autonomous communities are responsible for more than 50% of social spending in spain, and more than 60% of the catalan budget, for example, is devoted to this chapter. these cuts would cost catalonia 1 billion euros, which is like closing for a year the prisons, the entire administration of justice and three large hospitals. yes, the public accounts must be kept in balance, but under no circumstances can we accept further cuts in education, health or social services. why does the spanish government not consider reducing its public defence expenditure, which currently amounts to more than 1% of gnp? does it make sense to keep the ministry of culture, when the autonomous communities have competences in this area?

i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. madam president, the eu-turkey agreement, which is deporting thousands of people to turkey, is inhuman and cruel, but it seems that the human question is of little concern to rulers who have already been making policies for many years that force those who flee wars to risk their lives at sea. so today we're going to stick to the legal issue, which seems to matter to you more. the agreement violates the directive on common rules and procedures in the member states for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals, the directive on common procedures for granting or withdrawing international protection, the directive on reception conditions, the geneva convention, the international covenant on civil and political rights, the european convention on human rights, the charter of fundamental rights and the constitutions of the member states, and we could go on, because it violates many other international and european regulations. and of this agreement, it must be said that there are those responsible with names and surnames, namely those heads of state or government who signed it on 19 march - from the 28 member states - but all of us here - the european parliament - will be complicit if we do not stop it. article 263 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union gives us that possibility. the european parliament may bring an action before the court of justice of the european union for failure by the council to comply with legislation or for a breach of the treaties. i repeat: if we do not do this, if we do not bring this matter before the court of justice of the european union, the european parliament will be complicit in these crimes.
madam president, in less than a month the first world humanitarian summit will be held, which, by the stroke of fate, will be held in istanbul. in the process of preparing for this summit there have been eight regional meetings around the world and one global meeting and the common point has been that the key to humanitarian action is respect for international humanitarian principles and law. that is absolutely necessary in a world where there are 120 million refugees and where conflicts are multiplying and lasting longer and longer. parliament will send a delegation, which i will chair, to that international summit, and when i chair that delegation and speak on behalf of parliament, i want to be able to assure the international organizations, in particular the united nations refugee agency, that we treat refugees as human beings, with all their rights - it seems unnecessary to stress this, but unfortunately it is not necessary - that we apply international humanitarian law and the relevant legislation when repatriations occur and that we protect those on our territory by providing them with shelter, food, health care, especially children, the most vulnerable. i think the example of the european union a few years ago would have been more convincing. let us make the implementation of this agreement allow you to regain that conviction in the rest of the world.
mr president, commissioner, i am reading on the screen the title of this debate: legal aspects and democratic control of the agreement between the european union and turkey. this parliament is not here to control turkey, but to control what the commission and the council do and say, and the first thing we know is that it is not an agreement, but a deal with a press release. is this to be seen as an attempt to escape the rules of international law? because not calling it an 'agreement' may prevent the procedure of international law from being followed, but it does not exempt it from the rules of international humanitarian law or from the scrutiny of this parliament. we may not have the power to decide whether to accept or reject it, but we do have the right and the duty to debate it and to criticize it because, first of all, it contains absurd and impossible-to-enforce clauses, such as the one-for-one clause -- one irregular migrant returned to syria for every refugee relocated, as if irregular migrants and refugees were indistinguishable categories, when they are not -- or as the one that does not guarantee the principle of non-refoulement for non-syrian refugees -- iraqis and afghans -- who are exempt by turkey from international humanitarian law. so this deal is a sham. i don't recognize myself in this deal. and if i had the power to decide that with the red button on my seat, i would reject it: it degrades the standards of the european union and deals an irreparable blow to the union's prestige in the field of asylum and humanitarian law.
in writing. on 18 march, an agreement was reached with turkey to manage the 'refugee crisis'. a controversial agreement for applying a mercantilist logic to resettlement. among other things, it is not clear what will be the fate of those refugees who are not covered by turkey's territorial exception to the geneva convention, what the impact of this agreement will be on the planned reform of the dublin system or whether turkey will respect our human rights standards. the first world summit on humanitarian action is due to take place in may, and by chance it will be in istanbul. in a world where there are already more than 120 million refugees and where conflicts are multiplying and becoming more protracted, the key to humanitarian action is respect for international principles and law. at that summit, the european parliament must assure the world that the eu treats refugees as human beings with all their rights. it seems unnecessary to emphasize this, but unfortunately it is not. let us make sure that the implementation of this agreement restores confidence in the eu's role in the rest of the world.

the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, first of all i would like to thank all those who have been involved in this difficult report on rail interoperability throughout this time for their its field and a current and future source of quality jobs. the fourth railway package seeks to remove the major obstacles which affect it from a political and technical point of view. there have been permanent attempts to divide both pillars. we have strongly opposed this idea because only the complete package can build the common railway space we need. we welcome the agreement recently reached on the political pillar, but we regret that it is not as ambitious as the sector needs. as rapporteur for the report on interoperability, i have to remind you that at present the railway agencies in the member states have more than 11 000 different standards and a system of authorizations and approvals for fixed and rolling stock in place and in operation, which makes it an adventure to start up a business in this sector. the bureaucratic costs and complexity of procedures are in fact a tool of protectionism and discrimination which makes it extremely difficult for new operators to emerge and affects the business of vehicle and fixed equipment manufacturers. companies manufacturing railway equipment, for example, bear huge administrative burdens which increase the final price of their products by between 10% and 30%. in this context, competition is affected and the first to suffer are users in the form of supply restrictions. to remove these obstacles, our report proposes to strengthen the role and powers of the european railway agency, which will prevent manufacturers and operators from having to submit multiple applications to different bodies. the afe 'european agency' will authorise vehicles for crossborder services, while those concerned will be able to choose between national agencies and the european agency for domestic traffic. there will be a network of agreements between the tfa and the national agencies to clarify roles and a one-stop-shop system to be in place within a maximum of three years. this coordination tool will simplify and increase transparency in the administrative process, allow it to be followed from any member state and ensure that all similar authorisations are dealt with with under the same criteria and deadlines. a european vehicle register will complete the design of a more transparent administrative system, shielded against duplication and arbitrariness. afe will also deal with safety and traffic management systems (ertms), which it will undertake before any tender for such equipment is published. in short, we want to ensure that entrepreneurship is not held back by administrative or bureaucratic problems, without this reducing the security of the sector in the slightest. i hope that the member states will comply and that we will not have to adopt a 'fifth railway package', because this development is essential for more sustainable mobility. europe convinces citizens when it is useful, when it solves problems, when it forms the backbone of common services and makes decisions that improve people's lives and the conditions for entrepreneurship and development. that is the aim of the directives and regulations which make up this fourth railway package.
mr president, i would like to congratulate the three rapporteurs and thank them for their availability and energy in bringing this technical pillar of the railways not to a good port but to a good station. i am glad that the vote on this pillar follows the agreement reached on the political pillar, which we shall vote on in a few months' time and which assures us of the political will to overcome the national selfishness of the state monopolies. i am also pleased that the principles have been applied in safety to urban rail systems in memory of the victims of the valencia metro, that accessibility and victim support plans have been included in tribute to the victims and their families of the angrois accident, and that the foundation stone has been laid for a new rail safety culture, such as exists in aviation, by allowing confidential reporting of incidents by workers on board. in the area of interoperability, we have made progress, particularly in making it more accessible to people with reduced mobility, and we have strengthened the consultation of workers, through their trade union representatives, where technical standards directly affect them. it is up to you, mrs bulc, to ensure that national governments comply with it, and you can count on this parliament to do so.
member of the commission.– mr president and honourable members, this is a really great moment, and i would like to thank you for this very constructive and positive debate. it shows clearly that the proposal is important and that the compromise text strikes an important balance. allow me just to quickly respond to two points that were raised as questions. the first is related to duration, by ms kyllönen, who is really asking era to try to anticipate and speed up the process of the implementation to allow benefits to materialise as soon as possible. the cooperation agreements between era and national authorities are under preparation as we speak. another comment i would like to make, related to additional costs, was raised by ms aiuto and ms seymour: era will allow savings, pooling resources and allowing national safety authorities to focus on the supervision of their local markets, and this will further improve rail safety as well. before concluding, please allow me to refer to the agreement reached last week on the market pillar of the 4th railway package, which complements the technical pillar we are debating today. while this second pillar of the rail package will only be tabled in plenary at a later stage, i would like to take the opportunity already now to express my warmest appreciation for the work that was done there as well. if the technical pillar brings greater synchronisation of rules, the market pillar will ensure better and new services addressing real passenger needs. so thanks to parliament we have managed to negotiate on all proposals as a package and ensure the coherence between them. this is no doubt for me that each proposal will maximise the impact of the others. citizens, railway undertakings and railway manufacturers are eagerly awaiting them, so i am really pleased to confirm to you that the council just endorsed our trilogue agreement. i am looking forward to your support and a positive outcome of the vote today. commission statement statement by the commission on explanatory documents "the commission recalls that the european parliament, the council and the commission acknowledged in their joint political declaration of 27 october 2011 on explanatory documents that the information member states supply to the commission as regards the transposition of directives in national law 'must be clear and precise' in order to facilitate the achievement by the commission of its task overseeing the application of union law. in the present case, explanatory documents could have been useful to this end. the commission regrets that the final text does not contain provisions to this effect. " statement by the commission on non-opinion clause "the commission underlines that it is contrary to the letter and to the spirit of regulation 182/2011 (oj l 55 of 28.2.2011, p. 13) to invoke article 5, paragraph 4, second subparagraph, point (b) in a systematic manner. recourse to this provision must respond to a specific need to depart from the rule of principle which is that the commission may adopt a draft implementing act when no opinion is delivered. given that it is an exception to the general rule established by article 5, paragraph 4, recourse to second subparagraph, point (b) cannot be simply seen as a "discretionary power" of the legislator, but must be interpreted in a restrictive manner and thus must be justified." statement by the commission on necessary budget resources "the 4th railway package gives era new competences, in particular the power to issue vehicle authorisations and safety certificates directly to the sector. it cannot be excluded that in the transition period fees and charges are not yet available to era while the staff needs to be recruited and trained. in order to avoid disruption to the railway market, the commission will endeavour to reserve the necessary budget in order to cover the costs of relevant staff." statement by the commission on the era management board and the selection and dismissal procedure of the executive director "the commission regrets the fact that compared to the original proposal presented by the commission, the agreed text on the new era regulation deviates from the key provisions agreed under the common approach on eu decentralised agencies, by the european parliament, the council and the commission in 2012. this concerns the number of representatives of the commission within the management board and the selection and dismissal procedure of the executive director. the commission emphasises in particular that the appointment of an observer among the members of the management board to follow the selection procedure applied by the commission for the appointment of the executive director should not result in a duplication of roles in the selection and appointment procedures (article 51(1))."

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the protection of the best interests of the child throughout the european union on the basis of petitions to the european parliament. i am glad that the resolution contains many of the demands that have been put to the european parliament by citizens from different member states in the form of petitions. for example, a clear call for the automatic recognition of adoptions between member states, always in accordance with the principle of non-discrimination. the call for countries to designate specialised courts for crossborder disputes involving children, for greater efforts to ensure judicial cooperation in cases of crossborder disputes involving minors, and for the establishment of minimum criteria to ensure that minors are always heard in national judicial proceedings, is equally positive. i have voted in favour of this resolution because i believe it is a positive call to the european commission to take account of a number of important points in view of the forthcoming revision of the brussels ii regulation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, put forward by the chair of the committee on petitions, cecilia wikström, which aims to ensure the best interests of the child in crossborder custody disputes with different instruments and guarantees. children cannot suffer the consequences of a lack of cooperation between member states in family matters. the current community legislation is not in keeping with the europe of today, where the free movement of persons coupled with the growing cultural and academic exchange has given rise to a large number of marital relationships giving rise to societies where families with members of different nationalities are common. we have received dozens of petitions in the committee on petitions concerning minors. it is an unmistakable sign that something is wrong and that many citizens need a solution. the resolution contains a number of measures and provisions, such as the creation of specialised chambers within family courts to deal with transnational disputes involving minors, the prevention of separation of siblings, the preservation of cultural and linguistic links between minors and calls on the commission and the member states to ensure automatic recognition of adoption decisions.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this resolution, as we believe that the main objective of 'safeguarding the best interests of the child throughout the eu on the basis of requests to the european parliament' is to bring to the commission some concerns related to the regulation on the recognition and enforcement of family law, and that these should be taken into account in its next review. the poor practices of the authorities in child welfare, protection of children's rights, child custody, child abduction and cross-border childcare are recurrent themes in many petitions to the ep. although in our view some more specific references to migrants and some statistical data are missing, we consider the resolution to be positive and that it is well balanced between the protection of children and the rights of parents.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this resolution, which is necessary for the protection of the best interests of the child in the union. the interests of the child must always be given priority in crossborder judicial proceedings on parental custody and adoption decisions and advocate for specialised chambers within family courts to expedite the processing of these cases. member states must improve their judicial cooperation and the european commission must provide citizens with clear information in cases of dispute, for example on parental rights in different countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the protection of the best interests of the child in the union on the basis of the numerous petitions concerning the practices of the authorities responsible for the welfare of children, the protection of children's rights, the custody of children, the removal of children and childcare that the committee on petitions has received in recent years from several member states of the european union. the resolution calls for all child protection systems to be equipped with transnational and crossborder mechanisms that take account of the specificities of crossborder conflicts and calls on the member states to introduce monitoring and evaluation systems, within a framework of national coordination, on crossborder cases involving minors. it also recommended that the commission coordinate the transfer of information between the competent authorities of the member states and recalled the obligation of national authorities, laid down in the brussels iia regulation, to recognise and enforce judgments given in another member state in cases relating to children.
in writing. ‒ the principle of this motion for a resolution is to apply the best interests of the child in all areas, including in the field of adoption. this includes the right of parents to maintain contact with the child. the problem with this resolution is that its final version includes an amendment which removed the possibility for states not to recognise adoptions contrary to their public policy. even if the motion for a resolution adopts a cautious wording, in particular in paragraph 22, by merely stressing that there is no automatic recognition, it nevertheless calls on the states and the commission to regulate the recognition of cross-border adoptions. i am opposed to this wish because the states must be able to define what is and is not within their public policy, particularly in family law. moreover, article 81 (3) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) provides that measures relating to family law with cross-border implications are to be adopted by the council, acting unanimously after consulting the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, as cross-border family issues have become more and more a relevant matter of concern within the eu, given the current level of integration and following the significant level of free movement of workers between member states, which has generated an ever-increasing number of mixed couples, many of them with offspring. matrimonial disputes are a sensitive matter, particularly when they involve determining provisions for the custody of children in the event of divorce. given the growing european dimension of these eventualities, and on the basis of the article 81(3) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, some provisions of civil law have been introduced into the acquis communautaire, such as council regulation (ec) no 2201/2003 of 27 november 2003 concerning jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters and matters of parental responsibility, more commonly known as the brussels iia regulation.
in writing. ‒ we are talking about a report which deals with several issues of great importance in the field of child protection, such as the protection of children, judicial cooperation in this field in the european union, the role of social services in the protection of children, judicial procedures relating to childcare, the reception and adoption of children or the crossborder abduction of children by their parents. i believe that the report touches on a particularly important issue at an important time when children are also protagonists in the current refugee crisis. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ despite references to the european social charter, the existence of the charter of fundamental rights and the mandatory ratification of the european charter of human rights (paralysed by the current commission), the single market is constitutionalised in the treaties in such a way that 'economic freedoms', which favour big business over workers, take precedence over social rights. the creation of a new pillar for the european union is a call for european trade unions to reverse this situation. the nature and importance of this issue (as well as its ambiguities) require extensive consultation with the social partners. that is why i have supported this request for consultation of the european economic and social committee.
in writing. ‒ in january 2016, in juncker's state of the union address, the idea of establishing a european pillar of social rights was launched. this pillar should be a framework document for analysing the social and employment changes that are taking place as a result of the convergence process in the euro area. in march this year, the commission launched the explanation of this initiative and its intention to launch a consultation with all stakeholders to receive their views on the matter. in this context, the economic and social committee is requested to be consulted as the employment committee believes that it can contribute with its experience in social and inclusion policies and put forward interesting measures for a european pillar of social rights. we voted in favour of the eesc's exploratory opinion on strengthening the european social model, to be delivered by september 2016. the empl committee will then produce an ini report on the subject, in which we will be able to take a more informed view of the matter thanks to the eesc's study.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the request for consultation with the european economic and social committee on the establishment of a european pillar of social rights as requested by the committee on employment and social affairs following commission communication com (2016)127 of 8 march 2016.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the technical pillar of the railway package because it will make it possible to reduce drastically the number of redundant rules, barriers and procedures which still persist today and which prevent trains from crossing borders and manufacturers from marketing them in a single railway area without technical barriers. i am also pleased that in a few months' time it will be succeeded by the agreement reached on the political pillar which guarantees us the will to overcome the national selfishness of the state monopolies. we have also succeeded in applying the principles of the railway system to urban railways in the field of safety, in memory of the victims of the valencia metro, and in including emergency and accessibility plans and victim support plans in recognition of the victims and their families of the angrois accident. we have also succeeded in laying the foundation stone for the new railway safety culture, as it exists in aviation, by allowing confidential reporting of incidents by workers. in terms of interoperability, we have made progress, particularly in making the rules more accessible to people with reduced mobility, and we have strengthened the consultation of workers, through their trade union representatives, when the rules directly affect them.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the adoption of the technical pillar of the 4th railway package because we believe that harmonising safety and interoperability standards at eu level allows the rail sector to gain agility in cross-border journeys and connections. although the text is not perfect, it is balanced and addresses key issues for developing a sustainable alternative that can compete with the airplane and the road for passengers and goods. but let's not forget that this is the good side of the fourth railway package. in the coming months we will have to decide on the market pillar and, if the text remains as it is now, they will not find an outstretched hand from us. the total and mandatory liberalisation of the railway sector in the eu will only bring management problems and financial losses to the state, and a deterioration in the public service provided to citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for the second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european union agency for railways and repealing regulation (ec) no 881/2004, which provides for the agency to be the single window for the certification of railway equipment and safety authorisations for operators, and for a single vehicle register to be established. this will reduce technical and administrative barriers to the placing of vehicles on the market in the eu, eliminating the need to submit multiple applications and giving the tfa a greater role in the development of ertms, as well as providing for the possibility of creating a sanctions regime to prevent and prosecute incumbents blocking the possibility of authorising a vehicle to operate on the network. this will increase the economies of scale of railway companies and manufacturers across the eu and avoid any covert discrimination against new companies, creating an integrated, dynamic and cross-border railway system.

in writing. ‒ this fourth package of measures arises from the continuing problems facing the railway sector, it is vital to work towards a more liberalised and dynamic environment, favourable to business and competition. the fragmentation of the rules at national level only hinders this development and the efficiency of rail services. there are three proposals in this package. the first proposal is for a regulation on the european union agency for railways (afe), which will allow it to have more efficient authorisation and certification procedures tailored to the needs of companies. i think it is really important to have a single interlocutor who cooperates with the national authorities. in view of the above considerations and the fact that rail transport contributes sustainably to european jobs and growth, i am voting in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ in europe we have been working for years to achieve a more efficient railway union. the railway agency in the eu will help to move this forward, so i am voting in favour of the proposal to adopt the new regulation to improve performance and competitiveness and to increase the quality and efficiency of rail services in europe. we believe we have reached a good agreement to improve the efficiency of the system and to improve cooperation to advance the common objective.

in writing. ‒ this is one of the three reports which form the technical pillar of the fourth railway package proposed by the european commission. these reports are basically aimed at preparing the infrastructure, by removing the so-called technical barriers, to liberalise the sector and leave it in private hands through the creation of the single railway market. that is why i voted against, although i am not opposed to the harmonization of railway safety standards at european level if this would improve and increase them. but the main purpose of these regulations is not that, but the one mentioned above, and i believe that the railway should continue to be a public service serving the population, not in the hands of private companies for their profit.

in writing. ‒ i was and remain in favour of a single european railway agency with sufficient staff and resources to do its job. we cannot continue with 28 member states’ national railway agencies, often blocking progress and cross-border competition. the elimination of regulatory barriers and bureaucracy should be our objective. the 4th railway package is not as ambitious as we wanted it to be. many of the arguments are the same as those in relation to the recast of the 1st railway package. in the rail sector, progress is very slow by comparison with developments in the aviation sector in the past 30 years. there are always excuses for not increasing competition and making progress, which, at the end of the day, will benefit consumers.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation for the adoption of the european parliament and council directive on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union, a directive which will bring europe closer to a single european railway area, in which administrative costs will be reduced and procedures accelerated, while maintaining the current high level of safety. in particular, the need for companies to submit multiple applications will be avoided, a single window system will be created, clear deadlines for the different stages of the procedures will be established and the interoperability of the european rail traffic management system (ertms) projects will be ensured. the tso shall assess the technical solutions envisaged to ensure that the different ertms are effectively compatible and to avoid technical barriers from the emnes. this will result in a significant reduction in the number of national rules in those areas where harmonised eu-wide rules are being introduced.

in writing. ‒ i abstained in this report because, although it facilitates the creation of new standards in view of the liberalisation and privatisation of rail services contained in the european 'fourth railway package', some of its measures are necessary to improve the functioning of the european rail corridors.
in writing. ‒ this fourth package of measures incorporates the interoperability directive, which is designed to remove the remaining obstacles in the railway market and thus lay the foundations for a single railway area. this directive is mainly aimed at removing the barriers, not only administrative but also technical, which still drag the european railway sector along, in order to be able to boost the economies of scale of railway companies working at european level. if we reduce administrative costs and speed up procedures, we will be able to increase competitiveness, transparency and market security in this sector. the fragmentation of legislation at national level only feeds an outdated system which is out of step with the current situation and needs of industry. in view of the above considerations and the fact that these measures will ensure consistency and a clear division of responsibilities, i am voting in favour of their adoption.
in writing. ‒ my support for the draft legislative resolution with a view to the adoption of the european parliament and council directive on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union. we want to put all the instruments at the eu's disposal to improve the railway system, increase the number of users and establish common safety and operability standards, which will help to improve the economies of scale of railway companies operating in the eu.

in writing. ‒ this is one of the three reports which form the technical pillar of the fourth railway package proposed by the european commission. these reports are basically aimed at preparing the infrastructure, by removing the so-called technical barriers, to liberalise the sector and leave it in private hands through the creation of the single railway market. that is why i voted against, although i am not opposed to the harmonization of railway safety standards at european level if this would improve and increase them. but the main purpose of these regulations is not that, but the one mentioned above, and i believe that the railway should continue to be a public service serving the population, not in the hands of private companies for their profit.

in writing. ‒ i was and i am in favour of a single european railways agency with sufficient staff and resources to do its job. we cannot continue with 28 member states’ national railway agencies, often blocking progress and impeding cross-border competition. the elimination of regulatory barriers and bureaucracy should be our objective. the 4th railway package is not as ambitious as we had wanted it to be. a lot of the arguments are the same as those made around the recast of the 1st railway package. in the railway sector, progress is very slow by comparison with what has happened in the aviation sector in the past 30 years. there are always excuses for not introducing more competition and for making progress which, at the end of the day, will benefit consumers.

in writing. ‒ this proposal aims to reform the existing regulatory framework to define the new tasks that the european union agency for railways will carry out in the field of interoperability and safety. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the railway sector is able to compete with the other railway sectors. i therefore think it is appropriate to vote in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation by which parliament gives its assent to the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of the european parliament and council directive on railway safety. this directive takes a further step beyond the progress already achieved with directive 2004/49/ec by migrating towards a single union safety certificate replacing the current two-part system. the european railway agency (era) will thus play a key role as it will be competent to issue safety certificates to railway undertakings operating in more than one member state. railway undertakings operating in a single member state may choose to be certified by the afe or by a national safety authority. the afe may also establish a tool for the exchange of information on security risks between relevant stakeholders. this will facilitate the cross-border exchange of information.

in writing. ‒ in order to continue to support the establishment of a single market for rail services, i consider it necessary to establish a common regulatory framework for railway safety. the commission proposes to revise the previous directive on this subject, to move towards a single safety certificate, leaving behind differences and technical barriers, with the ultimate aim of harmonising the content of these standards at european level. i also think it is appropriate to establish a system for exchanging information on safety risks between the parties concerned and to improve the coordination of emergency services. in view of the above considerations, and that these measures will facilitate technical assistance, reviews and will ensure the independence and efficiency of the sector, i vote in favour of their approval.

in writing. ‒ the spanish socialist delegation voted in favour of this regulation which sets strict rules on the benchmarks used in financial contracts following the libor and euribor scandals in 2013. on 25 november 2015 the agreement between the commission, council and parliament took place, of which we would like to highlight the following aspects:- it extends the consideration of critical index, allowing critical indices to be declared according to qualitative criteria and opening the possibility to raw material indices. - it ensures that national supervisors can also require compliance with the requirements set out in the regulation for non-critical indices;- it improves the transparency and robustness of the methodology used for its preparation. - strengthens the role of esma in the supervision of critical indices. this regulation is certainly a decisive step in the fight against the manipulation of indices and we hope that the strengthening of the supervisory role of the national and european authorities will completely remove any doubts about their integrity.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because the outcome of the trilogue maintains the european system of central banks' exemption from complying with its provisions. this regulation will regulate the economic benchmarks, following the very serious libor and euribor scandals which have allowed a real transfer of income to the banking sector for years and which have led to the execution of hundreds of thousands of evictions both in spain and throughout europe. we have tried to cancel the escb exemption which, in practice, renders this legislation ineffective. but the negotiations with the council and the commission have decided to maintain this exemption, which will allow the ecb to continue to operate without transparency in this area. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.

in writing. ‒ we voted against this report, which deals with the indices on which interest rates for various financial products are based. one of the best known is euribor and libor, which are applied to mortgages. last year, several scandals exposed the ability of large financial institutions to manipulate these indices. we believe that the proposed legislation is not sufficient to prevent such practices and that is why we have opposed this report.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank my colleague from the cora group for her work on this dossier which we are voting on today on indices used as a reference in financial instruments and financial contracts. the new rules are aimed at preventing the manipulation of benchmarks such as the libor and euribor following the scandal of several major banks rigging interbank interest rates to artificially influence the prices of derivatives. the new legislation aims to bring transparency to the process of setting these indices and to avoid conflicts of interest.

in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation on benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts comes in the wake of the libor and euribor manipulation scandals. the aim is to regulate conventional stock market indices such as the cac 40, but also indices on monetary rates, commodity prices and energy prices. this regulation is designed to increase transparency and better control by regulators. it also entrusts the main control functions to the national regulators. i therefore voted in favour of this report because it is high time that the controls on financial operators were improved.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report, which deals with the indices on which interest rates for various financial products are based. one of the best known is euribor and libor, which are applied to mortgages. last year, several scandals exposed the ability of large financial institutions to manipulate these indices. we believe that the proposed legislation is not sufficient to prevent such practices and that is why we have opposed this report.
in writing. ‒ the spanish socialist delegation voted in favour of this regulation which sets strict rules on the benchmarks used in financial contracts following the libor and euribor scandals in 2013. on 25 november 2015 the agreement between the commission, council and parliament took place, of which we would like to highlight the following aspects:- it extends the consideration of critical index, allowing critical indices to be declared according to qualitative criteria and opening the possibility to raw material indices. - it ensures that national supervisors can also require compliance with the requirements set out in the regulation for non-critical indices;- it improves the transparency and robustness of the methodology used for its preparation. - strengthens the role of esma in the supervision of critical indices. this regulation is certainly a decisive step in the fight against the manipulation of indices and we hope that the strengthening of the supervisory role of the national and european authorities will completely remove any doubts about their integrity.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation which provides for strict regulation of the benchmarks used in financial contracts following the libor and euribor scandals in 2013. on 25 november 2015 the agreement between the commission, council and parliament took place, of which we would like to highlight the following aspects:- it extends the consideration of critical index, allowing critical indices to be declared according to qualitative criteria and opening the possibility to raw material indices. - it ensures that national supervisors can also require compliance with the requirements set out in the regulation for non-critical indices;- it improves the transparency and robustness of the methodology used for its preparation. - strengthens the role of esma in the supervision of critical indices. this regulation is certainly a decisive step in the fight against the manipulation of indices and we hope that the strengthening of the supervisory role of the national and european authorities will completely remove any doubts about their integrity.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because the outcome of the trilogue maintains the european system of central banks' exemption from complying with its provisions. this regulation will regulate the economic benchmarks, following the very serious libor and euribor scandals which have allowed a real transfer of income to the banking sector for years and which have led to the execution of hundreds of thousands of evictions both in spain and throughout europe. we have tried to cancel the escb exemption which, in practice, renders this legislation ineffective. but the negotiations with the council and the commission have decided to maintain this exemption, which will allow the ecb to continue to operate without transparency in this area. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ benchmarks have become public goods in practice. i therefore believe that it would be necessary to maximise their social benefits by subjecting them to more written control and to criminal sanctions if they cause damage to the real economy or to society as a whole. the report aims to promote the reliability of the assessments of price reporting agencies and to ensure that they comply with the standards and methods proposed in this regulation. it is essential to prohibit any trading of any commodity derivative contract referenced by one of those agencies, unless such assessments are in line with the applicable legislation. in view of the above considerations, and the fact that it is essential to ensure the quality of benchmarks and, above all, to take into account the detrimental effect that they may have on users among market players, i am voting in favour of their adoption.
in writing. ‒ the financial crisis of recent years has made us realise the importance of issues we previously barely thought about, such as benchmarks, which are fundamental to the stability of european financial markets, such as libor and euribor. the eu must therefore work to ensure that these indices on which so many businesses and households and the economy in general depend are transparent and sound. i support the proposal to establish clear and detailed legislation in this respect, to prevent any kind of manipulation and to ensure the credibility of the bodies setting the indices.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report. the final text agreed between the co-legislators falls far short of what is needed to restore confidence in the integrity of benchmarks and prevent new manipulation scandals. recent experience has demonstrated that benchmark manipulation can cause significant losses to consumers and investors, distort the real economy, and undermine market confidence. for example, the manipulation of the london interbank offered rate (libor) and the euro interbank offered rate (euribor) has resulted in multi-million euro fines on several banks in europe and the us, and allegations of manipulation of commodity (e.g. oil, gas and biofuel) and exchange-rate benchmarks are also under investigation. the prices of financial instruments worth trillions of euros depend on benchmarks, and millions of residential mortgages are also linked to them. hence, the need to create strong rules for what is a largely unregulated part of the global economy.
in writing. ‒ we are talking about a regulation introducing a common framework to ensure the accuracy and integrity of the indices used in the union's financial instruments and contracts. its main objectives are to improve governance and avoid conflicts of interest, to improve the quality of data and the methodology used in designing these instruments and contracts, to ensure proper control by those responsible for the indices and to ensure adequate protection of the users of the indices by increasing transparency. i therefore think it appropriate to vote in favour of this regulation.
in writing. ‒ i did not vote in favour of the discharge to the european commission and its executive agencies because, despite meeting the formal and procedural requirements, the commission continues to develop an agenda contrary to the interests of the european working classes. i voted in favour of the resolution because it approves the formal aspects of the management of the commission and its various executive agencies and their directors during the financial year 2014. the commission meets all the requirements of financial auditing in the implementation of its expenditure and that is why we voted in favour of the resolution. but we cannot approve the discharge because the political direction of the commission during 2014 has been guided by a neoliberal project that we do not share.

in writing. ‒ under the treaties, the european parliament has the right to scrutinise the legality and regularity of the implementation of the expenditure of the european institutions and agencies each year. the main objective of exercising this right is to ensure that public funds are used in the best possible way. this scrutiny is based on the report of the european court of auditors, a written question and answer procedure and, finally, the public hearings of the institutions and agencies before the european parliament. parliament has not detected any irregularities in the implementation of the european court of auditors' budget, which is why i voted in favour of approving the management of the court of auditors' budget and of parliament's resolution.
in writing. ‒ management and closure of accounts approved as no significant irregularities.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2014 as regards the european ombudsman, in view of the court of auditors' report in which it observes that no significant deficiencies were found with regard to the examined issues relating to human resources and public procurement, and that the payments made in the financial year 2014 for administrative and other expenditure in the institutions are free from material error. furthermore, it is to be welcomed that the ombudsman has undertaken inquiries on his own initiative in relation to complex matters falling within his remit. however, the ombudsman is requested to include in his annual activity report a table of all available human resources.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the 2014 discharge for the european ombudsman. it was in 2014 that the european ombudsman asked frontex to set up a complaints procedure for migrants, when they are allegedly victims of violations of their fundamental rights. this measure is not intended to curb illegal immigration, but on the contrary to encourage illegal immigrants to enter and stay in europe. it seems to me that the european ombudsman should rather defend the rights of european citizens and legal residents in europe, rather than focus on promoting migration flows. i also note that the report raises concerns about the ombudsman's staff selection policy. short-term posts were filled directly by trainees and temporary staff were recruited without any selection procedure. these recruitments may be justified, but it is important that the staff of this institution be selected in a transparent manner and in accordance with the principle of equal opportunities in access to the public service.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of these reports as they contain important votes on the single seat for this house. my position is that two seats is a waste of money and therefore we should try to save. pieper report: stresses that the court of auditors’ report adopted on 11 july 2014 states that the potential saving for the union budget would be about eur 114 million per year if parliament centralised its activities; reiterates its call on parliament and the council to address, in order to create long term savings, the need for a roadmap to a single seat, as stated by parliament in several previous resolutions; czarnecki report:22. takes note of the ombudsman´s calculations with regard to potential savings of eur 195 000 should the institution only have one seat; takes into account that the seat of the ombudsman is tied to the seat of parliament and therefore deems it necessary that the ombudsman be included in any debate on centralisation of the parliament´s seat; stresses that such centralisation should be actively promoted. i voted in favour of these 2 points!

in writing. ‒ i have supported this report, which reiterates the importance of the work of the agencies and their direct impact on the lives of the citizens of the union and recognises the efforts made and the progress achieved in terms of governance, efficiency and accountability. the report notes that, according to the court of auditors, the high level of carryovers of committed appropriations remains the most frequent problem in budgetary and financial management, with 28 agencies affected, although it acknowledges that these are often justified by the multiannual nature of operational programmes. the report also highlights that the final accounts of all decentralised agencies present fairly, in all material respects, their financial position as at 31 december 2014, their results of operations and cash flows for the year and that the transactions underlying the annual accounts of all agencies were legal and regular in all material respects. it is concerned, however, that some agencies are partly financed by fees paid by industry, which could affect their independence and calls for safeguard measures.

in writing. ‒ under the treaties, the european parliament has the right to scrutinise the legality and regularity of the implementation of the expenditure of the european institutions and agencies each year. the main objective of exercising this right is to ensure that public funds are used in the best possible way. this scrutiny is based on the report of the european court of auditors, a written question and answer procedure and, finally, the public hearings of the institutions and agencies before the european parliament. parliament has not detected any irregularities in the implementation of the budget of the translation centre for the bodies of the european union, which is why i voted to approve the management of the budget and the resolution of parliament.
in writing. ‒ the discharge and closure of accounts were approved as there were no significant irregularities.
in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this report approving the management of the director of the translation centre for the bodies of the european union in the implementation of the centre's budget for the financial year 2014 in the light of the court of auditors' report, in which it states that it has obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the centre's annual accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions and in which it notes that the budgetary surveillance work during the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 79,34%, representing a decrease of 4,13% compared to the financial year 2013. however, it highlights the synergies created by the centre by sharing services with other agencies, in particular the cooperation agreement between the centre and the european union agency for railways.

in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this report approving the management of the director of the european centre for disease prevention and control in the implementation of the centre's budget for the financial year 2014 in the light of the court of auditors' report, stating that it has obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the centre's annual accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions and noting that budget monitoring efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a high budget implementation rate of 98,77%, representing an increase of 5,81% compared to the previous financial year. it also welcomes the development of an anti-fraud strategy in 2014 following the guidelines published by the european anti-fraud office.
in writing. ‒ the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) has a mission of providing information and expertise on human diseases. its budget is €60 million, financed entirely by the union. in terms of the centre's activities, 2014 was marked by the outbreak of the ebola virus in west africa. over a third of the center has been devoted to this outbreak, and some officers have gone on the scene, risking their lives. however, while the ecdc investigated the outbreak as soon as it occurred, it, like who, took it too seriously far too late. moreover, while she herself stressed the ineffectiveness of temperature screening at departure airports, she never proposed to end flights and trade in risky products between contaminated areas and europe. we can therefore consider that it has not fulfilled its protective role and i have therefore voted against the motion for a discharge.
in writing. ‒ the discharge and closure of accounts were approved as there were no significant irregularities.

in writing. ‒ the discharge and closure of accounts were approved as there were no significant irregularities.
in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this report approving the management of the executive director of the european chemicals agency in the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2014 in the light of the court of auditors' report, stating that it has obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions and noting that budget monitoring efforts throughout the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 97,08% and that the payment appropriations execution rate was 87,46%. it also congratulated the agency on the development of its reporting processes and on the optimisation of its financial processes and appreciated that the agency had implemented the recommendations contained in the court's special report no 15/2012 on the management of conflicts of interest and that the agency regularly reviewed and updated its conflict of interest policies.
in writing. ‒ the european chemicals agency is responsible for the proper application of chemicals legislation. it is thus responsible for registering and even authorising chemicals, for example plasticisers suspected of being endocrine disruptors or nanomaterials. the number of products under his care is in the hundreds of thousands. it has a budget of €113 million and employs 587 people. like the medicines agency, only 6% of its budget comes from the union, the rest from the chemical industry, which is applying for authorizations and registrations, jeopardizing its objectivity. the court of auditors' report validated the accounts, but its 2014 activity revealed surprising and completely prohibited practices: the agency completed on its own at least one application for marketing authorisation, that of dehp, an endocrine disruptor. it informed the applicant of the uses for which the product was intended, the classification of the substance as a substance of very high concern, the uses which condition the risks and therefore the authorization... following questions from meps, she has to review 700 authorisations, which is quite astonishing. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ the discharge and closure of accounts were approved as there were no significant irregularities.
in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this report approving the management of the executive director of the european chemicals agency in the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2014 in the light of the court of auditors' report, stating that it has obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions and noting that budget monitoring efforts throughout the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 97,08% and that the payment appropriations execution rate was 87,46%. it also congratulated the agency on the development of its reporting processes and on the optimisation of its financial processes and appreciated that the agency had implemented the recommendations contained in the court's special report no 15/2012 on the management of conflicts of interest and that the agency regularly reviewed and updated its conflict of interest policies.

in writing. ‒ our group pushed for very critical and constructive approached on the discharge reports and therefore my vote was positive. the financial year 2014 is the first year of the new multiannual financial framework (mff 2014-2020), thus this first discharge aims at verifying whether the new eu budget has been properly and efficiently used and spent, whether the simplification of the legal bases reduced the error rate and whether the new eu budget is more efficient and effective than the previous one.

in writing. ‒ i am not in favour of this discharge to the european fisheries control agency and the resolution accompanying it because, although it formally meets a large part of the established accounting requirements, it does not represent a change of direction or the correct implementation of the provisions towards a socially and environmentally sustainable fisheries system in the eu. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common fisheries policy' to cover all fisheries, including the fisheries in the baltic sea. that is why we have not voted for discharge or the resolution on the financial year 2014.
in writing. ‒ the discharge and closure of accounts were approved as there were no significant irregularities.
in writing. ‒ the european fisheries control agency has an exemplary record of budgetary compliance. commitment and payment levels are improving year on year to reach 99% and 88% respectively in 2014. the results achieved since its creation and its contribution to the implementation of the reformed common fisheries policy are also exemplary. the room for improvement is very small. in particular, the reduction of staff and the freezing of the budget. i have therefore voted in favour of this report. however, the financial and human resources at its disposal must be increased so that the agency can continue to fulfil the responsibilities assigned to it in the reform of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors considers that the european fisheries control agency's 2014 budget has been implemented correctly: its implementation rate for commitment appropriations is 99% and that for payment appropriations is 88%. these rates are improving every year. these results have been achieved despite the fact that the agency's budget has been frozen since 2013. i oppose the request in the report to increase the appropriations for this agency because i am opposed to 'agencyisation', that is to say the increase in the number of european agencies and the extension of their powers, which is precisely what is driving the increase in their budget. i am also opposed to the european fisheries control agency adding to its mandate, like all other maritime agencies, the cooperation of coast guard functions. this new function will distort its mission by making this agency a contributor to managing migration flows. increased financial resources and synergy between maritime agencies will only result, in the light of current migration policies, in encouraging illegal immigration by increasing the repatriation of migrants to europe. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ the committee voted in favour of clearance of accounts and closure of accounts as there were no significant irregularities
