in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this report giving a discharge to the executive director of the european food safety authority in respect of the implementation of the authority's budget for the financial year 2014, in view of the court of auditors' report, stating that it has obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the authority's annual accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions, and noting that budget monitoring efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 99,69%, representing an increase of 0,86% compared to 2013. it also notes that the authority has launched a project aimed at improving efficiency and compliance in the processing of transactions through a centralised strategy, the introduction of centralised planning, control and reporting processes and structures, and centralised financing and procurement processes and structures.
in writing. ‒ the european food safety authority is responsible for the evaluation and monitoring of foodstuffs subject to authorisation, such as gmos, additives and sweeteners. it also gives opinions on food contact materials or nutrition claims, for example. it has a budget of eur 79 million, fully financed by the eu, and employs 449 people. the parliament's report proposed to grant discharge, despite the risk of conflicts of interest affecting almost a third of the experts requested. when it comes to the food security of europeans, and therefore their health, these conflicts of interest are unacceptable. there are also some curious recruitment practices with the recruitment of a former food industry lobbyist as communications director. the daily practice of efsa is also questionable: it takes little account of the opinions of national agencies, especially in the case of gmo evaluations. it can also be blamed for being unwise in its opinions, for example on bisphenol a. in these circumstances, i felt that its mission was not being carried out in the interests of the european people and i voted against the discharge for the efsa budget.
in writing. ‒ the vote was in favour of postponing the discharge and closing of accounts as its communications director is linked to the private food industry and there is a clear conflict of interest.

in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this report approving the management of the director of the european institute for gender equality in the implementation of the institute's budget for the financial year 2014 in the light of the court of auditors' report, stating that it has obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the institute's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions and noting that budget monitoring efforts throughout the financial year 2014 resulted in a high budget implementation rate of 99,04%, indicating that commitments were contracted in due time. it also stressed that the institute, in the context of the implementation of its internal control rules, focused on adopting the quality management framework, the implementation of an ex ante control system, the strengthening of the anti-fraud and anti-harassment environment and the development of its business continuity plan.
in writing. ‒ the european institute for gender equality's mission is to inform and ensure the good dissemination of eu policies related to the promotion of equality between men and women and to combat discrimination based on sex. however, the institute deviates from its mission to conduct research on lgbt people. it employs 46 people and is asking for an increase in its budget, although it consumes only 72% of the 7.3 million euros allocated to it. the decrease of 3,08% in the 2014 budget compared to 2013 can and must be continued. the proposed report also notes that the institute cooperates closely with the femm committee and has synergies with other bodies, including frontex. cooperation with the femm committee affects its work by politically orienting it towards a communitarianism which i do not wish to support, while cooperation with frontex does not go in the direction of the fight against illegal immigration. the institute is not very well managed from a budgetary point of view, and it is also too close to the femm committee, which undermines its independence. i therefore voted against the motion for discharge.
in writing. ‒ the discharge and closure of accounts were approved as there were no significant irregularities.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this discharge in favour of the european medicines agency because, despite meeting the formal and procedural requirements, this authority is responsible for defending the interests of the european pharmaceutical industry which maintains strong barriers to access to generic medicines. i abstained in the resolution because it approves the formal aspects of the authority's management and points out some shortcomings in its functioning during the financial year 2014. but we voted against the financial discharge because the political direction of this agency in 2014 has been the systematic blocking of access to new generic medicines that would have allowed to guarantee access to numerous treatments to european citizens.

in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this report giving a discharge to the executive director of the european medicines agency in respect of the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2014, in view of the court of auditors' report, stating that it has obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2014, the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions and noting that budget monitoring efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 94,32%, a decrease of 2,44% compared to the previous financial year. it also notes that the agency increased the transparency of its staff selection procedures by publishing the status of the external procedures in progress and the status of the reserve lists on the agency's external website, and also improved the documentation related to these procedures.
in writing. ‒ the european medicines agency issues marketing authorisations for specific medicines (anti-cancer, anti-hiv, genetically engineered medicines such as the controversial cervical cancer vaccines, gardasil and cervarix, etc.). it is also responsible for so-called 'biosimilar' medicines, generic medicines produced by biotechnology. it also carries out pharmacovigilance at european level. it has a 2014 budget of €282 million and employs 580 people. only 12% of its budget comes from the union, the rest from the pharmaceutical industry, which is already problematic in terms of independence. the court of auditors points to several points of concern, such as the failure to meet the deadlines for calling for payments from laboratories and settling national agencies, and shortcomings in management control. there is also a serious conflict of interest. professor nistico represented parliament for three terms (9 years) on the administrative board, without updating his declaration of interests. he thus 'failed' to specify that he held senior positions for an english company and a chinese company, whose products depended precisely on the agency. in these circumstances i voted against the discharge for this agency.
in writing. ‒ the discharge and closure of accounts were approved as no significant irregularities were found.

in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this report giving a discharge to the executive director of the european maritime safety agency in respect of the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2014, in the light of the court of auditors' report, in which it states that it has obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the agency's annual accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions, and in which it notes that budget monitoring efforts carried out throughout the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 94,78% and that the payment appropriations execution rate was 93,77%.
in writing. ‒ according to the court of auditors, the 2014 budget of the european maritime safety agency has been implemented correctly, with a rate of implementation of commitment appropriations of 94,8% and payment appropriations of 93,8%. i welcome the fact that the agency was able to fulfil its mission, with a budget decreased by 9.37 per cent in 2014. it is important that the european union, which is advocating austerity, should apply this principle to its own agencies. i am therefore opposed to the regret expressed in the report about the budget cuts. i also oppose the involvement of the agency in the management of the refugee crisis, as stated in the report. this agency must not be put at the service of smugglers, facilitating the repatriation of migrants to europe. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this report approving the management of the executive director of the european railway agency in the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2014 in the light of the court of auditors' report, stating that it has obtained reasonable assurances on the reliability of the agency's annual accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions and noting that the budget monitoring efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a high budget implementation rate of 97,34%, representing a decrease of 0,53% compared to 2013. it also stressed that the fourth railway package includes a review of the agency's role and its powers, and stressed the need for the agency to be given the financial, material and human resources necessary to enable it to carry out its new or additional functions effectively and efficiently.
in writing. ‒ the european railway agency, set up in 2004, is principally responsible for ensuring the safety of european railways and for ensuring the interoperability of rail systems in europe. nevertheless, the european commission is using this agency to force member states to liberalize rail, first in the freight sector, without any clear results, and soon in the passenger sector. it is reasonable to expect that this liberalization will weaken the public service and worsen security conditions. in fact, the agency could in future become the sole body competent to issue the necessary technical certifications and commercial authorizations in all the member states, tasks which must remain the sole responsibility of the national agencies if a safe and high-quality public service is to be maintained.

in writing. ‒ under the treaties, the european parliament has the right to scrutinise the legality and regularity of the implementation of the expenditure of the european institutions and agencies each year. the main objective of exercising this right is to ensure that public funds are used in the best possible way. this scrutiny is based on the report of the european court of auditors, a written question and answer procedure and, finally, the public hearings of the institutions and agencies before the european parliament. parliament has not detected any irregularities in the implementation of the budget of the european union agency for fundamental rights, which is why i voted in favour of approving the management of the agency and of parliament's resolution.

in writing. ‒ i have abstained in this report because, while it contains many of our group's demands to the eib (for example, the use of its funds to ensure effective social and regional cohesion or to finance projects for which the market does not seem to be interested), it lacks a critical reflection on how the eib often behaves, like any other bank, disciplining the european economy (and also those in its neighbourhood) to adapt it to the service of globalisation.
in writing. ‒ we voted against the 2014 annual report of the european investment bank for several reasons. the report makes reasonable praises and recommendations, but it also lacks a critical perspective. the eib is an intergovernmental institution which has proved incapable of stimulating investment in europe sufficiently, managing, among other things, the investment plan known as the juncker plan, which we have been criticising in its design and implementation. it has concentrated its resources, 55% of them, in just five countries, concentrating its profits in countries which themselves need it much less than other less developed regions.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done on this report on the eib's activity in 2014. unlike my group, i did support the amendment which referred to the fact that in 2014 59.4% of all projects signed by the eib went to the top five eu economies while the percentage for the other 23 member states was only 30.3%. a more balanced distribution of eib lending to member states is needed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this parliament's report in response to the 2014 annual report of the european investment bank. the report calls for complementarity with the structural funds and other public funds and calls on the eib to implement and further develop the efsi through cooperation with the co-legislators, respecting the timetable for the conclusion of an agreement still pending between the european parliament and the eib. we also call for the development and implementation of a comprehensive approach to the existing challenges posed by the increase in migration flows to europe. it is imperative that operations in the countries of origin of these flows as well as in the neighbouring countries affected by them should be included. other highlights of the report include prioritising investments to foster recovery as well as improving productivity, improving environmental sustainability in the fight against climate change, improving the governance structure, transparency and scrutiny of the eib and strengthening parliamentary accountability over the eib.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it calls for an urgent reaction by the european union and the international community as a whole to the alarming increase in attacks on civilian infrastructure and facilities, such as schools and hospitals, which has occurred especially in recent months in conflict zones such as syria, yemen, afghanistan and the gaza strip. on the same day as we adopted this text, there was yet another attack on a hospital in syria, in this case in aleppo and again on a facility supported by the ngo doctors without borders. the bombing has caused dozens of deaths, including children and the last pediatrician in the city. these are acts which constitute war crimes but which go unpunished because the international community is not putting in place the existing mechanisms to ensure that they are investigated and that those responsible are brought to justice. the resolution we have adopted, in addition to condemning these attacks, calls on the union and its member states to support the un's efforts at the forthcoming world humanitarian summit to put an end to impunity for violations of international humanitarian law.
in writing. ‒ on the same day we voted this resolution on "attacks on hospitals and schools, a violation of international humanitarian law", more than thirty people were killed in a bombing of a doctors without borders hospital, this time in aleppo. this bombing is yet another example of the urgent need for the eu and the rest of the international community to strengthen the mechanisms that ensure compliance with international law. i voted in favour of this resolution because i share its condemnation of the attacks on hospitals and schools and the need for transparent, independent and impartial investigations into these attacks. i also welcome the call on the eu and the member states to advocate that the un security council use existing mechanisms such as the international criminal court to deal with such attacks. i also welcome the request that no member state of the security council should veto decisions on humanitarian matters or the call for eu member states to ratify the main instruments of international humanitarian law.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs because i consider positive and necessary the call for greater transparency and access to documents and the criticism of the blocking and lack of transparency in numerous cases during the period 2014-2015. among other things, i share the rejection in this report of the secrecy and lack of transparency surrounding all eu negotiations of international agreements, its criticism of the excessive use of opaque trilogue procedures or its commitment to the need for a mandatory register of lobbyists. i also supported this report because it reflects some of the demands expressed by the gue/ngl in its amendments, such as the need to achieve greater transparency in the internal bodies of the european parliament, such as the conference of presidents or the bureau, the criticism of the secrecy surrounding decision-making in european institutions and bodies such as the european central bank or the european investment bank, or the need to review regulation 1049/2001, which was blocked in the council with the help of the commission.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report in order to guarantee the right to good administration under article 298 tfeu, where transparency has been established as one of the basic pillars on which the union is based. it is a key tool for greater citizen participation in decision-making, for the legitimacy of administration and for efficiency, ensuring democratic control over the actions of public administrations and enhancing the confidence of european citizens. we must continue to improve transparency, since the right of access to documents is a fundamental right protected by the charter of fundamental rights and the treaties, while respecting privacy and data protection. we need to adopt a proactive approach, including measures to harmonise the classification of documents, translation into the official languages of the union, and an ambitious action plan to improve the transparency of trilogues.

in writing. ‒ i support this report as it promotes the transparency of the institutions by facilitating public access to their documents. i believe that these measures can bring citizens closer to the work we do in the european union, thereby helping to increase their confidence in the european union, while at the same time raising their awareness of their private rights. it is equally important that european citizens know and become familiar with the union's decision-making process so that they are informed of how they may be affected by it. in addition, full access to these documents is a fundamental right enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the union, which we must protect and promote, thus ensuring more democratic control over the activities of the institutions. in view of the considerations set out above, and the fact that the actions and policies of the union's institutions must be based on representative democracy, i vote in favour of its adoption.

in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution as it urges the eu institutions and bodies to be more transparent and appoint a transparency officer from within their existing management structures, to be responsible for compliance and for improving practices. it also considers that the institutions, agencies and other bodies of the european union still fail to take fully into account, and to comply with, the rules and the changes provided for in the lisbon treaty and the charter of fundamental rights when applying regulation (ec) no 1049/2001, especially as concerns participatory democracy. it underlines the fact that any decision denying public access to documents must be based on clearly and strictly defined legal exemptions, accompanied by reasoned and specific justification, allowing citizens to understand the denial of access and to make effective use of the legal remedies available. among many other things it also urges the commission to designate a commissioner to be responsible for transparency and for public access to documents.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that action is needed to try to remedy the unfair situation facing domestic and care workers, a group of 2.5 million people in the eu (88% of whom are women). the vast majority do not contribute to social security, do not enjoy retirement, do not have health insurance, earn a meagre wage in the dark and work long hours, without the right to rest or paid holidays. many are illegal immigrants. others are family members who care for dependents without salary or entitlement. the eu must address this precarious and unacceptable situation by introducing a legal framework for the professionalisation of domestic work and care. the commission also needs to submit a proposal for a directive to regulate the situation of non-professional carers who assist dependent family members. states should define a specific legal framework to allow for the regular recruitment of domestic and care workers, establish the rights and duties of employers and workers and provide legal certainty for both parties. it should also include such workers in labour, health, insurance and anti-discrimination legislation enacted at national level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that ratification of ilo convention 189 and its recommendation 201 are essential to improve the working conditions of domestic and care workers, who are tireless fighters for their rights and dignity.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by the committee on women's rights and gender equality because it contains a number of requests for the european commission to take steps to adopt legislative and non-legislative initiatives to regulate the profession of domestic and care workers in the eu. some 29.9 per cent of domestic workers are completely excluded from national labour legislation. the result is that they are often working in precarious conditions and are discriminated against and without any protection. the situation is even worse for immigrant women. the report therefore calls for an end to this precarious situation and for measures to be taken to tackle the problem at its root.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report to defend the protection of the labour rights of domestic workers and carers in the eu. this is a job that is 88% done by women, who are engaged in tasks traditionally done by women such as housekeeping or care, and who suffer from precarious and unfair working conditions. as early as 2011, the ilo tried to provide us with an international legislative framework with its convention 189 to guarantee decent work for these workers, but only 6 of the 28 countries have ratified it. the people who work in care also work in deplorable conditions, and yet they suffer from the same situation of unprotectedness, long hours, very low wages, lack of and no guarantees of safety and health at work. with this report we are voting in favour of professionalising the sector, a european directive on permits for the recognition of the status of non-professional carer who guarantees them a remuneration. we believe that the situation of these workers must be regularised and that we must have sufficiently strong tools at eu level to prevent abuse and exploitation from finding a place in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report by the equality committee which calls for a statute to improve the employment situation and social protection of domestic workers and carers, and to combat precariousness and undeclared work in these areas. the need for appropriate inspection methods and sanctions to prevent exploitation and trafficking in human beings is also stressed, given that many of these workers, mostly women, come from third countries. the commission is also proposing that the eu should give them an official status.

in writing. - women domestic workers, housekeepers and childcare workers in the eu (kuvena). the report recommends that domestic work be given a new lease of life, in particular by removing it from the often illegal situation in which it finds itself and thus making it possible to grant social rights (unemployment, pension, etc.) to those who carry it out. it points out several facts: 88% of the jobs of housewives and domestic helpers are held by women; these jobs are often precarious and difficult. these jobs are often undeclared. immigrants/clandestines are often confined to these posts and are sometimes reduced to slavery in this context. the report has the merit of being quite at odds with the general propaganda: it states that many migrant women are in these jobs precisely because they require a priori little training and skills. some of the proposals are positive: professionalizing these trades, which will grow due to demography; introducing tax incentives such as the employment service to take this market out of the underground economy. however, i do not support his proposal to regularize illegal immigration and create legal migration routes. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ domestic workers and carers represent more than 2.5 million people in the sector across the eu, 88% of whom are women. this is not just a matter of respect for people, but also respect for women and their dignity. these workers are in various institutions as well as in private residences, generally without adequate recognition and with their labour rights unprotected. the commission is therefore calling for the profession to be recognised and the value of this kind of work to be recognised, so as to reduce undeclared work and to be able to establish common standards by establishing guidelines and a framework for the professionalisation of the sector. we also call on the commission to come forward with a proposal for a directive on carers' leave and a framework for the recognition of the status of non-professional carer, guaranteeing remuneration and minimum standards of social protection. finally, msm are encouraged to ratify ilo convention 189 on decent work for domestic workers and promote regulatory programmes. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the report aims to reflect existing inequalities in women's access to, training, employment and use of digital media. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. it is also recognised that the trend towards more flexible working practices can result in unstable forms of employment. it also advocates the right of workers to "work disconnection". however, given the nature of the new gender equality policy 2016-2020 set by the european commission, there is little hope that this institution will address coordinated and in-depth programming on issues such as those mentioned. in addition, it is obvious that austerity policies have widened the gender pay and employment gaps in the new technology sector. that said, my vote has been in favour.
in writing. ‒ in europe, only nine out of 100 developers are women, and in the ict sector only 19% of managers are female (compared to 45% in other service sectors). in addition, women represent only 19% of entrepreneurs (compared with 54% in other service sectors). we therefore aim to improve women's access to vocational and educational opportunities in relation to information and communication technologies and computer skills. i have therefore voted in favour of this report which calls on the commission to take advantage of and better target the digital agenda and the digital single market strategy in order to address the serious gender gap in the ict sector and to promote the full integration of women and men in the ict sector and in general to take account of this inequality in all its programmes and policies relating to this issue.
in writing. ‒ we consider our vote in favour of this report to be broadly in line with the direction of our group. we highly value efforts to address issues related to harassment on social media towards women. the report also makes a bold contribution to the field of work, combining access to technology with the breaking of the glass ceiling for women and the possibilities that technology offers for reconciliation. this report emphasises the value of equality education and the continuing focus on maintaining research and information centres on this issue. for all these reasons, and save for a few secondary points, we shall vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs for their work. i have supported this report on gender equality and women's empowerment in the digital age, which calls on the commission and the council to fully exploit the potential of the information society, ict and the internet in promoting women's empowerment and their rights and freedoms, as well as gender equality, irrespective of age, disability, genetic traits, gender and sexual orientation, among others.
in writing. ‒ the progressive incorporation of icts is constantly creating new opportunities in areas such as participation, the labour market or education and training. however, as the report stresses, we must not lose sight of the gender perspective in the actions promoted under the digital agenda and the single market strategy. we must take full advantage of the potential of the information society in terms of women's empowerment and their rights and freedoms. in the european ict sector, only 19% of managers are women, a figure that is repeated at the level of female entrepreneurs in this sector. the impact of sexism and gender stereotypes is undoubtedly an obstacle to equality between men and women in the union. the empowerment of women contributes to the improvement of the socioeconomic conditions of society and to the competitiveness of the union, and that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the report reflects the need to fully exploit the potential of the information society, ict and the internet to promote women's empowerment, women's rights and freedoms and gender equality. measures in this regard should be advocated, such as gender mainstreaming in digital initiatives and plans to increase women's access to the information society, improve and increase women's use of ict, including women on an equal footing in the digital and information sectors. at european level, the report also promotes the inclusion in the next strategy for equality between women and men 2016-2020 of specific actions to support the integration and participation of women in the information society.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the entry of more women into the ict sector would provide a boost in a labour shortage market where women's equitable participation would amount to €9 billion a year in the eu's gdp. women remain very underrepresented in ict studies, professions and entrepreneurship. it is very important that the eu fully exploits the potential of the information society, ict and the internet to promote women's empowerment and their rights and freedoms, women's participation in decision-making, for example through electronic voting, and gender equality. the report again calls on the commission to present as soon as possible a european strategy against gender-based violence containing a legislative instrument and addressing new forms of violence against women and girls, such as cyberbullying, the use of degrading images online, the distribution on social networks of private photos and videos without the consent of the people involved, etc.
in writing. ‒ in the name of women's empowerment, this report laments that few women are deploying their talents in the ict sector, figures to back this up. it thus sets aside all studies, and all common sense, showing that men and women are complementary and not equivalent or interchangeable. it reveals a new criterion of discrimination in addition to the usual criteria of "age, disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, race, social or ethnic origin, religion or belief, and economic status". this is discrimination on the basis of "genetic characteristics"! the concept of "positive balance" is also created when a situation is unbalanced to the advantage of women. it also states that the family policy of the member states should not include any measure allowing women to choose whether or not to work. for this to happen, women must necessarily work outside the home. they have no choice. this report is yet another monument to the propaganda against genuine freedom of choice for women. i voted against it, of course.

mr president, integrated territorial investment and participatory local development are important tools for territorial development, but they are not sufficiently applied. it is said that it is urgent for the member states to make greater use of them, but that is precisely where the problem arises. without much more real and effective involvement of local and regional actors, politicians and the social sector, the effectiveness of both tools loses its effectiveness, meaning and quality. and this is particularly relevant if we are talking about crossborder cooperation. although it is a question of questioning the existing framework, and in line with what several members have just said, local and regional actors must be involved and act before the implementation phase, that is, in the design, selection and decision-making, not just in the consultation. we need more information and training, but also a clearer and more ambitious policy direction.
mr president, alternative routes must be offered to europe to provide new supplies at a better price, with the setting up of new infrastructure as part of the energy corridors. in a context of energy interdependence such as the present one, the lack of a long-term strategic vision favours uncertainty in the markets. the southern corridor, with the potential to meet up to 20% of the european union's gas needs, should therefore be given priority. the european union must diversify its gas supply so that all regions have access to at least two different sources of supply. in this way we will make progress in consolidating the union's energy security, guaranteeing a stable supply and transit of energy in the long term.
mr president, the worst thing about this debate is that we are not talking about access to energy, nor about climate change, but about pure and simple geostrategy, about conflicts over access to fossil fuels. energy agreements with third countries directly condition the kind of relationship we want to build with them. in this case, the german government, guided by the low price of russian gas, prefers to override the interests of the eastern countries. this project is an economic and environmental aberration. different studies show a continuous decline in gas demand. the european court of auditors itself has acknowledged that the commission's gas demand forecasts are persistently overestimated, so that there is no need to increase the current gas supply capacity. however, there are german companies investing in this project, as a consequence of leaving the energy future in the hands of the market. the 'no' to this project without economic or climate justification is fundamental, as is the commission's intervention to stop it.
in writing. beyond the undeniable negative effects on marine ecosystems of the construction of a new gas pipeline in the baltic to link russia and germany again, and beyond the geopolitical circumstances in ukraine, this installation is not at all necessary: it does not improve security of supply, as there are several gas pipelines fulfilling that function; it would give a dominant position to a single supplier company, and to a single member state. moreover, it would increase russia's already high transport capacity without justification. at present, only about 50% of russia's transport capacity is used and the available capacity far exceeds the eu's needs. it would jeopardise routes through romania and bulgaria, negatively affecting the diversification of supply to the eu. all this raises serious doubts as to the compatibility of the project with the internal energy market, in particular with the third energy package. natural gas can be a backup fuel in the transition to a new energy model based on the use of renewable energy sources, but in no case should it be a substitute fuel. increasing supply capacity would delay the entry of clean energy into europe.
member of the commission.– mr president, i would first like to thank ms engström and the committee on fisheries (pech), in particular alain cadec, for the opportunity to discuss this very important issue, which, as was mentioned, concerns consumer information and the traceability of fishery and aquaculture products. significant efforts were made in the approval of the reformed common fisheries policy to improve consumer information and the fisheries policies control regulation has critically strengthened traceability. the motion for a resolution linked to this oral question identifies the key issues, and the commission shares with you the sentiment that we still have to do more. but we must act on the basis of evidence, rather than on the basis of emotions. the results of one study should not be generalised, especially if we have other, broader studies published during the same period which indicate that significant progress has been made. it is the case of the eu-coordinated control panel for fisheries and aquaculture products, which covers not only three eu canteens and some restaurants around the eu institutions, but also covers 29 countries with more than 3 900 samples. i would also like to restate that this discussion about mislabelling only covers a specific item of consumer information: the name of the food and the risk of species substitution. concerning the study reference, it must be stressed that its authors do not take into account the applicable legislation in its findings. mislabelling, particularly in the case of fish substitution, does not always result from an intention to commit fraud. incorrect labels may also be the result of mistakes or mismanagement, and these situations occur much more often than fraud. so taking into account all these elements and the relevant eu and national laws, the commission is of the view that the actual level of mislabelling is much lower than the figure published by oceana. so we must be careful of the evidence we use, but having said that, this is an excellent opportunity to make the point that we need a proper understanding of traceability. traceability is a tool for transmission of information from the ship’s deck or the farm to the plate. if a solid traceability system cannot avoid misconduct of operators or human errors, it can permit us to trace back to the moment when the misconduct or error occurred. only extensive controls by member states can avoid misconduct of operators and more generally reduce mislabelling. funding has already been made available through the european maritime and fisheries fund to support the development, purchase and installation of components to ensure the traceability of fisheries and aquaculture products and also to support the implementation of a union control inspection and enforcement system. since 2010, the commission has assessed control systems put in place by member states to monitor the traceability of fishery and aquaculture products. possibly deficiencies are being addressed through appropriate means. moreover, the commission has started a project on compliance and control of labelling and traceability. the commission has also been proactive in the fight against mislabelling and fish substitution. in cooperation with 27 member states and two efta countries, we recently completed a coordinated control plan for white fish. as i already mentioned, more than 3 900 samples were collected, representing a broad range of products and species. this demonstrated a level of non-compliance of 6%. just a couple of weeks before the publication of the results of the coordinated control plan, the eu-funded label fish was also completed and this finding made public. here again, out of more than 1 500 samples from different species, countries and products, less than 5% were found to be mislabelled. so while the commission agrees that we can and must do more, we must also not portray a misleading image of a sector that is highly non—compliant. we should not risk increasing mistrust by eu consumers, particularly as we see from evidence that the level of irregularities is generally low. it is important to mention here the different testing protocols that can be used to identify species and aquaculture products officially. it is true that dna-based methods represent the most promising approach. the commission’s joint research centre is actively working in this field, and the experience gained in conducting the eu-coordinated control plan for fishery products will be very useful. concerning the potential of eco labels, i note that you consider these as one among possible solutions to avoid mislabelling, but please be aware that an eu-wide eco label would not necessarily strengthen traceability. having clarified these points, i am glad to inform you – as also mentioned by ms engström, that the commission is finalising the feasibility report on options for a union-wide eco label scheme for fishery and aquaculture products. this feasibility report is based on an external study as well as on a public consultation and interviews of stakeholders. it analyses various options. i hope that this feasibility report will provide useful information and ideas to feed the debates that will take place both in this house and with member states and stakeholders.

as will be discussed in the course of the debate, this new agreement with mauritania fills some of the gaps in the previous protocol, which left much to be desired. the restrictions imposed on the member of the commission.– mr president, it is a pleasure to jointly debate the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement (sfpa) and associated protocols with liberia and mauritania. i would like to take the opportunity to thank both rapporteurs, mr wałęsa and mr mato, for their reports. i am pleased to note that the committee on fisheries also recommends that parliament give its consent to both agreements. let me now say a few words on each one of the agreements. i will start with liberia. the new sustainable fisheries partnership agreement with liberia is not one of our largest agreements in terms of fishing opportunities and in terms of financial layout. however, it is a very significant agreement because it expands the eu’s regional network of tuna agreements into west africa. the protocol to the agreement will last for five years and will allow up to 28 eu tuna seiners and six surface long liners to fish in the liberian fishing zone. these vessels also operate under other agreements in the region. therefore, the agreement with liberia will contribute to extending the geographical coverage of fishing activities without increasing the fishing capacities. this agreement with liberia also fully respects the principle of sustainability of fishing activities. it is based on the best and latest scientific data and the principles of transparency and non-discrimination with other foreign fleets. a human rights clause has also been included. the agreement also sends a strong signal that liberia is open for business despite the difficult situation in the country after last year’s ebola outbreak. the fisheries agreement is a real partnership. it not only brings fishing opportunities for eu vessels and steady financial revenues for liberia, but it also forms a framework for developing the liberian fisheries sector and to fight illegal fishing together. the sectoral support available to liberia under the agreement will be used to help reinforce its monitoring, control and surveillance capacities. this will enable it to control the fishing operations of all fleets operating in its waters and of its own fishing and carrier vessels, wherever they operate. additionally, recent discussions with the liberian authorities have opened the way to a complementary action under our development cooperation programme with liberia to enhance the sectoral support under this agreement. while this is at an early stage, the liberian authorities have requested additional support for, in particular, capacity-building, artisanal coastal fisheries, post—harvesting handling and local markets. i am confident that this new agreement with liberia will develop into a long lasting partnership. let me now turn to the protocol with mauritania. the fisheries agreement with mauritania is the european union’s biggest sustainable fisheries partnership agreement in financial terms. it provides fishing opportunities to up to 98 eu vessels from 11 member states and is therefore of crucial importance for the european union fleet. the new protocol is the result of intense negotiations. it is a significant improvement compared to the previous protocol and can be considered an example to be followed for the negotiation of future sfpas with other countries. the new protocol is fully consistent with the external dimension of the reformed common fisheries policy, as was also mentioned by mr mato and mr wałęsa. it respects the principle of sustainability and confirms the principles of transparency, preferential access for the eu fleet and non—discrimination between foreign fleets. the protocol will ensure good returns on eu taxpayers’ money and gives the eu fleet stability and predictability with improved technical conditions. it will ensure better implementation of sectoral support through more conditionality. the focus now is on ensuring the smooth implementation of the new protocol. i can assure you that the commission will monitor closely the state of all the stocks covered by the protocol in order to ensure the sustainability of fishing activities. we will also check whether mauritania respects the principles of transparency and non-discrimination. i think this is crucial to ensure that the eu fleet is not operating under less favourable technical and financial conditions than other foreign fleets. i consider it a very positive sign that mauritania recently adhered to, and took a leadership role in, the fisheries transparency initiative. i know many of you are interested in the first meeting of the joint committee, scheduled to take place at the end of may. i hope that at the meeting we can approve the sectoral support programming under the new protocol and wrap up sectoral support from the previous protocols. but we also intend to raise with mauritania the possibility of creating a new demersal fishing category. such a new category could benefit the trawlers which are currently unable to fish for octopus and other cephalopods due to the bad state of the stocks. we will also discuss the possibility of relaxing the obligation for eu pelagic vessels to trans-ship 100% of their catches exclusively in nouadhibou. let me thank you again for today’s opportunity to debate these fisheries agreements with you. i look forward to your support in the future on these agreements.

mr president, our main task as members of parliament is to defend the interests of our citizens, our companies and our workers. fifteen years have passed since the start of the protocol of accession of china to the wto and we have seen no willingness on its part to make the necessary reforms to meet the five criteria defined by the union. this is precisely why we must refuse to give china the status of a market economy. this concession would have very negative consequences for europe and would prevent us from continuing to fight unfair competition. we must protect our companies and our workers from all kinds of dumping, whether fiscal, social or environmental. if we want to be respected internationally, we must send a clear message: we will not open our markets to those states which do not respect the principles of reciprocity or balance in economic relations.
mr president, we were supposed to take a decision on granting china market economy status in december and this parliament still does not know what we are going to be proposed. the socialists are in favour of strong trade relations between the european union and china but on a balanced and fair basis, and the reality is that we are not competing on equal terms. china doesn't respect the rules of the wto. it is not a market economy and practices social, environmental and price dumping. if china wants to be treated as a market economy, it has to behave as such and meet the required criteria and requirements. my group therefore opposes the automatic granting of market economy status. i am very concerned, commissioner, that the public consultation launched by the commission seems to be aimed at concessions and that the proposed protective measures are insufficient. chinese prices do not reflect costs and therefore the standard methodology cannot be applied to them. the european union needs new, powerful, effective and rapidly deployable trade defence instruments and i therefore call on the council to unblock the situation now. innovative sectors such as steel, textiles and ceramics, which employ millions of people, are in danger and i believe that the european union cannot afford to lose a single job by giving china a trade status it does not deserve.
mr president, any free-market economic status with any country must be based on respect for bilateralism, fair trade and also on safeguarding the interests of the parties. china is the opposite of a fair and free market with the european area, because chinese products - dumping of those chinese products - goes against the interests of the industrial and steel sectors in the european area and puts hundreds of jobs at risk, such as the basque steel mills in sestao or zumárraga in spain and elsewhere in europe. the european parliament and the european commission must therefore urgently take precautionary anti-dumping measures to protect the european steel industry, and these measures include setting a minimum selling price per tonne of coil, establishing a border adjustment for steel, introducing green tariffs on imported steel or subsidising steel produced by recycling scrap.
mr president, pending the outcome of the public hearings and the legal studies being carried out on china's status in the wto (which i hope will be resolved by recognising the reality that china is not a market economy today), i would encourage the commission to come up with faster mechanisms to solve the problems we have today with the dumping of chinese steel. and i want a unanimous response from the member states. because no one can save themselves alone. in the basque country, two plants have already closed: zumárraga and sestao. and there are hundreds of jobs at stake, as in many other european regions. i also call on european steel companies to take more responsibility and to commit themselves to society through investment and innovation in order to become more competitive through the circular economy and sustainability. these are the keys to a determined commitment to its strategic role and its permanence in the european economic fabric.
in writing. let me put this debate in its true context, which is the commission's intention to further liberalize trade between the eu and china. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we will not fall into the trap of those who use the threat of non-recognition of china as a market economy as a weapon to demand privatizations and to push the penetration of their own transnationals. but we also do not think it acceptable that the use of anti-dumping measures should be eliminated, since their disappearance will lead to a serious deterioration in the overall conditions of the industry. any new progress in international trade integration cannot be made as if the market were an institution independent of its social structure; it requires, on the contrary, full recognition of international labour and environmental standards. otherwise, it will be the working classes who bear the cost of the biggest profits of the multinationals.
madam president, commissioners, yesterday we celebrated europe day and we talked about the future of europe. the future of europe is today's young people. that's a fact and no one can change it. what are we doing with them? well, we're dealing with growth with employment here. the problems of youth unemployment vary from one part of europe to another. in some it is an intolerable rate of unemployment for a long time; in others it is the quality of the work; in others it may be the remuneration of the work. but they all lead to the same solution. the solution is that it is a european crisis and it has to have a european approach. and for that, if we talk about growth, because growth must make it possible to finance education, not just training; to finance vocational training and mobility of vocational training at european level in particular; to launch investments preferably in the areas, not in the countries, in the areas of large youth unemployment pools and, of course, to strengthen mobility. there's no need to look any further. (the speaker agrees to answer a question put under the 'blue card' procedure (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure))
the answer is 'blue card'. of course, dear colleague, i mean, everything helps. one of the aspects i wanted to sum up is that of vocational training, education and investment promotion. 'social investment also counts' and of course a focus on research and a priority approach to the areas of the future will certainly help. but we must not forget the young people who cannot have access for a thousand reasons and who are just as valuable to europe as those who cannot have access to higher education.
madam president, commissioner, the youth guarantee programme is the great european disappointment. firstly, because you have not financed it sufficiently and secondly, because the member states which are implementing it are wasting it on programmes which do not help to combat youth unemployment. but we have two problems here: one is the problem of job creation and the other is the problem of job quality. youth unemployment is always twice the average of general unemployment and that means we have to grow twice as much to absorb all youth unemployment, and for that you have to change the economic policy of the european union. there has to be more investment. if there is no economic growth, there will be no job creation and there will continue to be rising youth unemployment. and the second, the quality of employment, has to do with the structural reforms that have also been promoted in the framework of the european semester. young people today are working in jobs which have nothing to do with their training; many are earning 20% less than the average wage of the general population; they are living on part-time contracts which are totally involuntary. we need to change, change to grow more and change to integrate a new generation of young people decently into our labour markets; otherwise, they will unplug from the european union, and that is what we have to avoid.
madam president, the economic crisis has left us with a more unequal society, with more poverty, less protection and more precariousness in our labour markets. it is only necessary to look at the different impact it has had on disposable income between germany and spain: in the years of crisis it has increased by 20% in germany and decreased by 20% in spain. and above all, this poverty and exclusion, what has caused is that many people today are disconnected from european institutions and support eurosceptic or euro-phobic forces. we have put forward some programmes, the youth guarantee, the youth employment initiative, but these are programmes, not a complete policy in the face of a phenomenon which is now plaguing the whole of europe. that is why we need a policy of economic growth, sustainable, inclusive growth, which is a real pact between states, a real pact between classes and a pact between generations. because a society without a future is doomed to failure.
in writing. since the end of 2013, economic and labour data in the european union indicate some recovery. this is a slow and uneven recovery between countries and with still excessively high records in terms of unemployment and poverty. the council and the commission are trying to convey an optimistic view of the results achieved, insisting that this proves that economic measures, structural reforms and austerity have worked. the reality is very different for the majority of the population, who are in worse conditions today than they were ten years ago and without any prospects for the future. the youth guarantee, for example, has not delivered the expected results and needs reforms to improve its financing, its implementation and to ensure its use by the states and by young people themselves. the union's economic policies, which have been a failure in economic, social and political terms, must therefore be changed. if we want to preserve the future of the european project, we must promote progressive structural reforms, starting with a major public investment programme that stimulates demand, generates sustainable growth and creates quality jobs, especially with a view to young people.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this fisheries agreement, because it will allow eu vessels to catch 6,500 tonnes of tuna a year for a fee of eur 3,25 million over five years. the financial contribution shall be divided equally between an amount intended for access to fishery resources and an amount intended for support of the liberian fisheries policy. in addition, other elements of the reform are also included, such as the exclusivity clause, a human rights clause, and the principle that no country fishing at high altitude should be subject to more favourable conditions than those applied to the eu. as regards transparency, a key element to promote sustainable fisheries is included: a provision similar, but less detailed, to that in the latest agreement with mauritania, which requires the publication of any agreement (whether public or private) allowing access to liberian waters by foreign flagged vessels.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is the first fisheries agreement with liberia by the european union. despite our firm commitment to a fisheries policy based on the responsible management of local fisheries resources, we believe that a small share in the responsible exploitation of certain fisheries resources is possible and that this will maintain jobs in the sector. this is the first agreement with the country, which means that for the first time vessels operating in these waters will be subject to an agreement with the local authorities and will be liable for it. the development of such agreements in a way that respects the full sovereignty of countries and takes into account the care of marine resources is fundamental to the sustainability of fisheries in general. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ we voted away as we consider these agreements to be inconsistent with the type of sustainable fishing we advocate. while reports often indicate that they point to an improvement in fish production in the eu and the country concerned with which the agreement is concluded, the beneficiaries are usually large fisheries corporations, not small producers or the local population. there are improvements for liberia in relation to previous treaties, but there are insufficient controls on the management of the funds in the recipient country and to date there have been no improvements in the population resulting from these agreements, but poor management of the funds.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of international fisheries agreements is always good news. they are a key element for the sector in many member states. the agreement provides for eu vessels to be able to fish 6 500 tonnes of tuna per year in return for financial compensation intended partly to promote sustainable fishing and improve food security in liberia and partly to provide access to fishery resources for community vessels. the commission also welcomes the fact that the council has adopted a new resolution on the situation in the democratic republic of congo. it is vital for the future of the sector to renew fishing agreements and to find new alternatives in other waters, of course in accordance with the sustainability of the activity within the framework of the principles of the reformed common fisheries policy and its external dimension. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation in the belief that the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement with liberia will clearly contribute to the achievement of the eu's objectives in the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and to the promotion of the common fisheries policy objective of sustainable management of fisheries and aquaculture activities. the protocol provides for a financial contribution from the eu of eur 715 000 for the first year, eur 650 000 for the second, third and fourth years and eur 585 000 for the fifth year, which will have a positive impact on the local economy and coastal communities.
in writing. ‒ this agreement allows eu fishing vessels access to liberian waters. signed on 5 june 2015 for a period of 5 years, this is the first fisheries agreement with liberia. it concerns 28 tuna seiners (16 spanish and 12 french) and 6 surface longliners (spanish). in return, liberia will receive eur 715 000 in the first year; eur 650 000 in the second, third and fourth years; eur 585 000 in the fifth year, based on a reference tonnage of 6 500 tonnes. support for the development of the sectoral fisheries policy (support for small-scale fishing, combating illegal fishing, monitoring and control) accounts for half of these amounts. the european financial contribution will decrease from year to year, as shipowners will pay €55 per tonne in the first year of application, €60 per tonne in the second and third years, €65 per tonne in the fourth year of application and €70 per tonne in the fifth year of application. after periods of civil war and the ebola epidemic, the liberian economy is getting back on its feet and this fisheries agreement supports this development. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which is beneficial to both parties.
in writing. ‒ we voted away as we consider these agreements to be inconsistent with the type of sustainable fishing we advocate. while reports often indicate that they point to an improvement in fish production in the eu and the country concerned with which the agreement is concluded, the beneficiaries are usually large fisheries corporations, not small producers or the local population. there are improvements for liberia in relation to previous treaties, but there are not enough controls on the management of the funds in the recipient country and to date there has been no improvement in the population resulting from these agreements, but poor management of them.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement which will allow eu fishermen to fish in mauritanian waters. the protocol, which has been provisionally applied since 16 november 2015, provides for fishing opportunities for crustacean vessels, except for lobster and crab; non-freezer trawlers and bottom longliners for hake; demersal fishing vessels; tuna seiners; pole-and-line tuna vessels; pelagic freezer trawlers and pelagic fresh-water fishing vessels. the largest category is freezer trawlers for pelagic fisheries, for which a quota of 247 000 tonnes is envisaged, out of a total of 281 500 tonnes fixed for the whole fleet. this new protocol represents a major step forward in relation to the previous one and the new commitments made by mauritania on transparency and preferential access for the european fleet. however, i stressed in my speech the need to include the galician cephalopod fleet as soon as scientific data support the sustainability of the stocks.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because it goes beyond certain lines of international law which must be taken into account when justifying the exploitation of fisheries in other territories. there is a clear risk that the territorial provisions will not be respected in respect of the occupied territories of western sahara, which as a nation must be represented in the negotiations on the exploitation of its natural resources. these types of agreements include environmental and social provisions, so they are a preferable situation to unregulated exploitation. however, the fact that such treaties are made in territories in conflict or with occupying forces, in accordance with international law, implies that the right of peoples to decide on their own resources is not being respected. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the adoption of international fisheries agreements is good news. they are a key element for the sector in many member states. however, they have been experiencing serious difficulties, as in the case of mauritania, the most important fishery of the union, to which the european cephalopod fleet has not been able to access since august 2012. this is particularly true in my region, galicia. the economic interest and employment of the community ports of la luz and las palmas are also affected, where landings are still being refused. that is why i abstained. it is vital for the future of the sector to renew outstanding fisheries agreements and to find new alternatives in other waters, of course in line with the sustainability of the activity within the principles of the reformed common fisheries policy and its external dimension.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, convinced that the agreement will be very favourable to both parties. the new protocol represents a major step forward in respect of mauritania's commitments on transparency and preferential access for the fleet. the union's sectoral support will also be increased to improve european support for the implementation of the new sectoral strategy for the sustainable development of fisheries in mauritania and for improving the living conditions of the citizens of mauritania.
in writing. ‒ this agreement allows european union fishing vessels access to mauritian waters. the agreement, which was signed on 10 july 2015 for a period of four years, is one of the largest fisheries agreements signed by the european union. in return, mauritania will receive eur 59 125 000 per year, based on a total allowable catch of 281 500 tonnes. this financial contribution includes support for sectoral policy (support for small-scale fishing, combating illegal fishing, monitoring and control) amounting to eur 4 125 000 per year. the european union will also monitor mauritanian waters, as certain third country vessels are suspected of illegal fishing. this agreement is beneficial for both sides, which is why i voted for its renewal.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement because it offers fishing opportunities in mauritanian waters to european union vessels, taking into account the available scientific assessments, in particular those of the committee for fisheries in the eastern central atlantic (cpaco), taking into account the scientific opinions and recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccaa) within the limits of the available surpluses. the aim of the agreement is also to intensify cooperation between the european union and mauritania in order to establish a framework for cooperation that will promote the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fishery resources in mauritania's fishing zone, to the benefit of both parties. sectoral support has increased compared to the previous period to assist the islamic republic of mauritania in implementing its new national sectoral strategy on sustainable development of fisheries activities. the new protocol represents a major step forward compared with the previous protocol and the new commitments made by mauritania on transparency and preferential access for the european fleet.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it calls on the european commission and the member states to provide more funding and to share good practices in implementing the two new instruments with the structural and cohesion funds in the period 2014-2020, namely participatory local development (ldl) and integrated territorial investment (iti). i am in favour of asking the member states to encourage the use of these instruments to improve the management of the funds, even in a complementary way, while increasing the bottom-up approach, in order to tackle the problems of structural unemployment, the integrated development of the less developed regions, the fight against youth unemployment and to provide solutions to the lack of financing of small and mediumsized enterprises, the main economic engines and creators of stable employment. these two instruments can only work within the framework of a fairer cohesion policy, not subject to so-called macro-conditionality, and which promotes economic diversification in the poorest areas, especially in the south of the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to give a guideline to the new territorial development instruments in cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020. these instruments are participatory local development (pld) and integrated territorial investment (iti). the main aim is to increase the involvement of the social fabric in rural development, improve financing and give greater flexibility to it to allow an integrated use of funds and an increase in the participation of local actors. cohesion policy has been and is essential for the economic and social progress of spain and europe. the instruments adopted should enhance this policy, which is essential to achieve a sustainable economy and reduce territorial inequality as set out in the europe 2020 strategy. communities such as extremadura, andalusia and asturias have the possibility of developing their economies thanks to these funds. at the same time, these instruments require a high degree of transparency as well as good governance between the different institutions and governments. a challenge which, if successfully tackled, will help to achieve a fairer and more cohesive union.
in writing. ‒ territorial cohesion is a key objective in the eu treaties. we vote in favour of this because these two instruments for territorial development, participatory local development and integrated territorial investment, are heading in the right direction. we believe that a bottom-up, bottom-up approach to cohesion policies is necessary and that it includes the participation of both the institutions at various levels and civil society. the report also covers problems such as youth unemployment in many regions, inequality, joint action in border regions, etc. on the other hand, we stress the failures in their application and the lack of knowledge of these tools, which, together with their excessive bureaucratization, would be problems to be tackled promptly. while these tools should be further explored within the cohesion policies, we believe that the report positively addresses the issue in question and proposes a line of citizen participation which we consider essential in cohesion policies.

in writing. ‒ territorial cohesion is one of the types of cohesion referred to in article 174 tfeu. the 2014-2020 cohesion policy strategy aims to use integrated and local-based approaches to further economic, social and territorial cohesion in the union in line with the 2020 strategy. participatory local development and integrated territorial investment are two of the new tools of cohesion policy which bring fundamental changes in the ability of local authorities to properly target their initiatives and sources of funding. the empowerment of local authorities is one of the central pillars of this policy, which aims to correct development imbalances between regions and to implement integrated actions in favour of development that is also sustainable. i voted in favour of this report to continue to tackle the many challenges which, as the document points out, remain unresolved in the area of cohesion policy.

in writing. ‒ the main objective of this text is to strengthen the reporting and publication obligations in order to improve the transparency and level of detail of the various economic statistics. in addition to regulatory innovations related to the fight against money laundering and tax evasion, methods are proposed to improve the reporting of financial accounts. however, all these mechanisms provide the commission with a lot of information, including strategic data on financial flows. this commission governance in the economic field is imposed on the member states. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the methodology for the compilation of balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment statistics needs to be updated. high-quality economic statistics are very important for european public policy making and also for academic research. in this sense, european statistical information is a public good which must be properly supplied and whose importance for the deepening of the internal market, the completion of economic and monetary union and the political construction of europe cannot be underestimated.

in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, despite consistently improving the content of the initial proposal for a regulation, it assumes the authority of international institutions with no democratic control. this report contains a number of proposals which will enable the production of such statistics, for example it sets out the distinction between foreign direct investment in the real economy and investment of a speculative nature, which may allow for differences between the two flows in the balance sheet of the member states; it also includes greater requirements in the area of regional breakdown of statistics which can be very useful for the development of a true cohesion policy. however, the report makes it abundantly clear that the provisions adopted by the imf and the oecd in this area must be introduced into european legislation, and that is why i was unable to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ community statistics form part of the overall eu framework for monitoring economic developments in each member state and in the union as a whole. i therefore believe that the production of reliable statistics helps to monitor key aspects of our economy, such as the development of current accounts or flows within or outside the union. these are equally fundamental in the monitoring process. i support the amendment of the statistics regulation because i believe that given the complexity of capital flows in recent years, we must ensure the transparency and granularity of statistics and thus ensure that they are a valid tool for political decision-making. with this revision we also give the commission powers, through detailed and implementing acts, to ensure the updating and adaptation of the regulation in certain non-essential elements. for the reasons stated above and because of the importance of the financial market to the european economy, i am voting in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the production of reliable statistics in areas such as balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign investment is essential to monitor key aspects such as the evolution of current accounts and financial flows within and outside the eu. these statistics help to ensure the consistency of the economic policies of the member states with the eu's broader guidelines as well as with the legal constraints arising from the eu's economic governance framework. they are also the fundamental basis of the supervisory process which sets the context for macroeconomic imbalance procedures. for this reason we must support an improvement in the development and use of these instruments as we have called for, with my support, in the report on the proposal for a regulation on community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, following the conclusion of the trilogue with the council, of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on community statistics relating to balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment, as regards the conferral on the commission of delegated and implementing powers to adopt certain measures. this is a technical report updating the methodology for the compilation of balance of payments, foreign direct investment and international trade in services statistics.
