in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it emphasises the way in which the eu's mountain regions could contribute to its objectives, such as europe 2020. the natural resources of these areas can boost job creation in the eu, in particular through 'green jobs' that help fight climate change. the rich variety of renewable energies could contribute to the achievement of the eu's renewable energy targets. at the same time, poverty and social exclusion within the least developed mountain regions could be reduced with the help of union funds. mountain regions can also become engines of sustainable growth in the eu as centres of 'green growth'.
in writing. ‒ the resolution deals with the consequences and challenges facing mountain regions in relation to european cohesion policy. the report calls for a clear definition of mountain regions in the framework of an 'agenda for the eu's mountain regions' proposed by the european commission. the development objectives for mountain areas should be integrated into the various funds alongside this agenda. the text also contains some positive elements, such as calls for greater use of the instruments for participatory local development (ldl) and integrated territorial investment (iti) or for priority to be given to the territorial dimension of cohesion policy. it also states the need for the european commission to encourage pilot programmes to restore traditional economic activities. however, development of areas cannot be stimulated through public-private partnerships; nor does it help to ask for a higher level of volunteering for the provision of public services. in short, this resolution seeks to reduce the burden on public administration, which in practice is a serious threat to the objectives of territorial cohesion set out in the treaties. i have therefore decided to abstain on the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the cohesion policy in the union's mountain regions. its main objective is to strengthen the community's mountain regions. these regions account for a large proportion of the european territory. to ensure the success of cohesion policy in mountain areas, a differentiated approach is needed which takes account of their special characteristics and the unique socioeconomic context in which they develop. in this respect, i consider the future development of an 'agenda for the eu's mountain regions' and a long-term strategy to be a very important point in the resolution. all policies in this area should aim to protect the environment, boost local economies and improve collaboration between member states.
in writing. ‒ the eu has not yet had a coherent strategic approach to mountain regions. although there are some elements with this specific focus (e.g. in the european agricultural fund for rural development), there is no definition or guidelines for a regional policy in mountain areas and interventions are usually specific, linked to specific results. we voted in favour because, although not perfect, the overall content of the text is constructive and balanced: it highlights the specificities of mountain regions and calls for a comprehensive approach, including the call for a european agenda, to guide eu investments and actions and to facilitate greater coordination between member states in cross-border mountain areas.

madam president, i cannot help but smile when i hear the popular bench lecturing the greek government after it has sunk the country's economy and rigged the national accounts to enter the euro zone. i think that's a little forward. in any case, i would like to say that i believe that greece is in these last days facing a kind of impossible sandwich, between the irrationality of its european creditors not wanting to restructure the debt, when everyone knows that it has to be done, and the suicidal recessionary measures that the international monetary fund wants to impose. we took a small step yesterday, but i think it is frankly insufficient. i would ask you, commissioner, to do two things: to make debt restructuring more ambitious and to speed it up now. we've known since 2010 that this is not sustainable and we need to do this as quickly as possible. and the second thing, and i'll end with this: to a country that is currently one point higher in primary surplus than the program was targeting, and is just beginning to emerge from recession, to ask for more recessionary measures is suicide. so it seems to me that the contingent measures go far beyond what we should; it seems to me that we are asking for a kind of preventive austerity that is out of place, but in any case let us give the greek economy a breathing space and not impose further recessionary measures on it. (the speaker agrees to answer a question put under the 'blue card' procedure (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure))
blue-card answer.– i think that would be the ideal situation, but it would require having rational terms, in the sense that we need debt restructuring that and the europeans do not want to accept that we need that, and we need to avoid more recessionary measures. but we need both of those things. if on those two grounds we could find a common agreement, of course that would be ideal. but those two things are necessary and, until now, both the imf and some of the european creditors have been blocking them.
madam president, first of all i would like to thank commissioner moscovici for the work he has been doing for over a year now, after we saw that last spring, at the last minute, call for a referendum when we were about to reach an agreement. we have probably lost a year and it is true that we have now reached an agreement which i think is reasonable; even though people in this parliament - like my colleague, mrs eva kaili - rightly question the confidence we can have in the syriza government, it is true that we have reached a reasonable agreement. i would like to recommend in some way that the reforms should be focused on a few areas which really unlock the potential for growth, for example in the export sector, taking into account rodrik's idea of major reforms, reforms which really unlock growth. and, as mr paul tang said, we must now tackle the debt issue. the compromise is on that issue, but we cannot wait any longer, because the greek people cannot continue to suffer from cuts and adjustments without a hopeful future that will enable them to regain growth and enthusiasm for europe.
i would like to point out first of all that this summit comes at a time of great organizational difficulties and the presence of actors such as this parliament, which is having difficulty in being at the appropriate level at the istanbul summit, but at the same time - as the commissioner has just pointed out - it comes at the right time, at the most appropriate time. because right now we have the greatest accumulation of humanitarian crises of the highest level in the world, from iraq to syria, south sudan, the central african republic, but also in ukraine or also in yemen, also in libya and also in other parts of the world. because right now we have the largest number of people displaced from their homes - about 120 million, from 37 different countries - almost half of them children. because at the moment there is the biggest gap between the need to serve people and the funding we have; we have around a 40% funding gap. and because right now, too, there are more and more violations of the principles of humanitarian action and attacks on facilities and actors. so, it's time to address a strong call, a serious push to address the humanitarian crises in the world. there has been a lot of consensus in the various global dialogues and in the various regional dialogues, and i think that the position expressed by the commissioner and the council representative also reflects this consensus on what needs to be done. however, there is less determination in the commitments to be made. the commission presented its proposals with its priorities; parliament supported it; parliament, in turn, drew up a report in which we called for a global consensus on humanitarian action, in which we also called for the need for better protection in connection with development cooperation policies; we also called for a greater role for local actors and for women; we spoke to the displaced, to whom the minister referred, and we also called for consistent funding. what i am asking the commission and the council to do now is to make istanbul the first step, and to follow istanbul with serious commitments by the commission, by the member states, towards a global consensus on humanitarian action, towards a new initiative that brings together development policy and humanitarian policy, and towards commitments to denounce violations of humanitarian principles, attacks on the various humanitarian actors. i would like to conclude, madam president, by saying that istanbul must be the first step towards restoring dignity to a proper level in this world.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, humanitarian crises are unfortunately becoming more frequent. the causes are not just climate change or natural disasters, but often armed conflicts of economic interest; political decisions, such as closing the borders to the arrival of thousands of refugees, have created a humanitarian crisis in our own territory. that is why we are extremely sceptical about the real possibilities of this summit. what good are vague humanitarian aid commitments if their policies are aggravating the humanitarian crises themselves? unless the real aim of the istanbul summit is to make up the policies of the european union and, above all, those of our new turkish partner. ladies and gentlemen, it is no use giving away stickers with the left hand while handing out axes to human rights and international law with the right. if you want to provide solutions, you can do so tomorrow: open safe routes and open a humanitarian corridor for the arrival of refugees; otherwise your hands will still be stained with blood.
madam president, thank you very much, commissioner, for being here today. attacks on humanitarian aid structures and organisations have increased in recent years. in 2015 alone, médecins sans frontières has already reported at least seventy-five attacks on its facilities. last week, in the refugee camp of sarmanda, in syria, 30 people were killed in an attack that can hardly be considered an accident. there's a code of conduct. as the french foreign minister has said, we are talking about a war crime, a crime against humanity. the world humanitarian summit, the first in history, must give an urgent and joint response against impunity. compliance with international humanitarian law and the protection of humanitarian workers must be at the heart of european humanitarian aid policy. the safety and survival of those who suffer most, who are precisely those we want to help, depend on this premise. as the european union, we have a duty to strengthen the crucial role of the international criminal court. we must use all our european influence to put an end to this abominable and unacceptable situation.

member of the commission.– madam president, first of all allow me to thank you for these very constructive and fruitful discussions. i always appreciate the views and position of parliament and this is particularly true as we are getting ready for such a unique multi-stakeholder event as the world humanitarian summit. this is why i insisted on increasing the number of places for the european parliament at this big event. my services and i did our best so that this parliament has a strong presence there and i am pleased to announce today that we secured two additional places in the eu delegation for the european parliament. we have common priorities: more efficiency; more effectiveness in the humanitarian system; respect for international humanitarian law and, of course, humanitarian principles also; more support for education, emergencies, and many more in the humanitarian field. this is why we have this very strong collaboration because we are in the same boat. this summit will complete a cycle of events – the sdg summit with agenda 2030, sendai, addis ababa and cop21 – that have provided a vision for the future. their outcomes provide a solid framework for the future, but real progress can only be achieved if we now turn to the poorest and most vulnerable and look at how we can help them thrive. this is the mission of the world humanitarian summit. i hope that when we look back in 2030, we will be able to say that this event was a true game changer. through the long consultation process it lent a voice to everyone: from leaders to members of affected communities, from academics to the private sector. it involved thousands of people across the world. it introduced a new way of discussing some of the toughest problems we face at a truly global forum and it generated momentum to bring about systemic changes in how we could prevent, respond to and recover from crises. it delivered on the ultimate goal: that by 2030, fewer people require life-saving emergency assistance. this is our common goal. on thursday, i hope that the council will adopt a second set of conclusions on the summit. we have worked with the presidency and member states on a strong position. this will guide us in making commitments at the summit but also beyond that. i count as always on your continued support and cooperation during the follow-up so that we can show leadership and deliver on our commitments. thank you very much for your collaboration.
president-in-office of the council. – madam president, the world humanitarian summit is not an end point, but is in a way a starting point for a global community to restore humanity, as the secretary—general of the united nations has said several times. we hope to see many, many meaningful and sincere commitments by all stakeholders at the highest possible level. yes, we have to make sure that the summit is not perceived as a western—dominated event. so outreach was, and is, being coordinated in particular by many states outside the union. i also agree with mr guerrero salom that, from the very first day after the summit, we will have to show that we are serious about our commitments. as the presidency of the council, we are ready to play our full part in this endeavour, and we very much count on our cooperation in the coming weeks.
member of the commission.– madam president, i am not sure i can solve the political crisis in brazil during this short time but i want to thank mr lange and the plenary for putting this question because it is indeed a very topical issue and we are, of course, aware of the huge political importance of reconnecting with mercosur but it also has, as you said mr lange, great potential economic use. we have long historical and cultural ties with mercosur, many shared interests and, of course, we have, on both sides, economic interests. so in terms of trade mercosur countries offer eu exporters and investors a very attractive market and this is still subject to significant tariffs and barriers. eu exporters pay annually more than eur 4 billion in tariff duties alone, so the potential gains of a free trade agreement are of course evident. we are committed to those negotiations and we are encouraged by the interest that has been seen lately in the four mercosur countries in moving forward, and a very large majority of eu member states also welcome this movement and the work towards an exchange of offers. this exchange has been carefully prepared on both sides, given the importance of moving the negotiation process forward, because there has been a long history to this and now we need to look forward. we have kept you and member states informed about this. the timing of the exchange of offers: i had a meeting with mr nin novoa, who is the foreign minister of uruguay and the current president of mercosur, and we agreed to exchange offers in this week of may, so we are fine tuning the very last formulas here, and making the final checks with member states, of course. we are looking forward to studying the mercosur offer when it comes. we will study it very carefully and of course share the results and our analysis with member states and with members of the european parliament. the exchange will be a first step in this new phase and mercosur has already indicated that it is a first phase and that they are ready to improve offers during the negotiations, and we will set a timing for negotiations when we have analysed each other’s offers. we have set out with the uruguayan minister a very ambitious agenda for the rest of this year, so we are both aiming to advance the negotiations quite rapidly. we hope to make progress on all areas with the aim of obtaining a balanced, comprehensive and ambitious agreement with mercosur. the eu is aware and the commission is aware that we have strong offensive interests with mercosur but there are also some specific defensive interests in the agricultural sector. following the various impact assessments conducted during the course of the last negotiations, we will conduct a new impact assessment and a new sustainability impact assessment for the trade part. that will of course also cover key issues such as human rights and economic impacts of the agreement. with regard to the impact on the agricultural sector we have already conducted two studies in 2011 on the impact of a potential deal between ourselves and mercosur which examines a range of scenarios and we take account of those conclusions in the calibration of our offer. in addition, as has been announced by commissioner hogan, the commission is also conducting now a general study of the cumulative aspects and impacts of the different free trade agreements on our european agricultural sector and we expect conclusions later this autumn and will of course share them. investment protection was one of the parts in the question as well. the mandate for this negotiation dates from 1999, which was well before the lisbon treaty; there is therefore no chapter on investment protection foreseen in the mandate. there will the rapporteur. madam president, good morning, commissioner, and dear colleagues, friends and comrades. i have been working on this mandatory regulation for over three years. as rapporteur, i have had the same intention from the beginning: to provide europol with a regulation that has the necessary tools to fulfil its tasks and objectives effectively. the main objective of the european union agency for police cooperation is to support and strengthen the action of the competent authorities of the member states and their mutual cooperation in preventing and combating terrorism, serious crime and thirty other crimes, such as drug trafficking, trafficking in human beings, illicit organ trafficking, kidnapping, illegal detention, hostage taking, racism and xenophobia, blackmail, counterfeiting of currency and means of payment, computer crime, illicit trafficking in arms, ammunition and explosives, sexual abuse and so on. we have already succeeded in preventing the merger of europol and ecpol at first reading, which was supported by this house by 610 votes in favour. this result was also achieved thanks to the good cooperation and the work of the alternative rapporteurs, to whom i pay tribute with gratitude. the second reading procedure has again been marked by the degree of cooperation and consensus of my colleagues. i would therefore like to reiterate my gratitude for all the efforts you have made during these three long years of negotiations. i have had a total of ten tripartite dialogues: three under the italian presidency, three under the latvian presidency and four under the luxembourg presidency, with which i reached a good agreement on 27 november. i also want to thank all of them. i would also like to highlight and thank the great work of victoria amici, the commission representative, for her high level of professionalism. the result of this second reading is that europol has a key role to play in combating the terrible scourge of jihadist terror. the regulation will therefore provide it with better capacity and tools in this area. notable was the creation in january of the ectc 'european counter-terrorism centre', a unit combining information, intelligence and support resources to counter terror. it will also provide a legal basis for the iru internet content notification unit. it is a fundamental tool for combating terrorist propaganda and extremist activities online. this unit within europol will identify extremist content online and will contact internet service providers to get it removed as quickly as possible - removed, i mean the content, of course. the agency, in order to be able to tackle all forms of crime for which it is competent, collects, stores, processes, analyses and exchanges information, including criminal intelligence. it also produces threat assessments, strategic analyses and operational analyses, all under the aegis of the police agency, i.e. the national units and liaison officers, who are the link between europol and the competent authorities of the member states. for example, it will be mandatory for national units to be notified without delay of any information and links between criminal acts affecting them. europol also has the possibility to coordinate, organise and carry out investigations and operational actions to support and strengthen the 'keywords' actions of the member states. for the first time, europol will be able to process data from private entities, always with a high degree of privacy, but this will allow europol to better fight against such terrible crimes as the abuse of minors. this will always be done under a robust data protection architecture, thanks in particular to the role of the european data protection supervisor, who, as an independent body, will always cooperate with national data protection authorities. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data. the new mandate will also improve the governance of the agency, increasing its effectiveness, in particular as regards the management board and the director of europol. and this regulation will set a precedent for the other agencies as far as parliamentary control is concerned. article 88 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union clearly requires that europol's activities be scrutinised by parliament, together with national parliaments. that is why we have set up a joint parliamentary monitoring group. finally, i would like to stress that the prevention of organised crime is fundamental, the best operational cooperation between existing agencies. europol shall therefore allow eurojust to access and consult its data. it has been a long legislative journey, but the result has been satisfactory and will allow europol to continue working 24 hours a day, every day of the week.
on behalf of the green group, madam president, commissioner avramopoulos, europol is the european agency responsible for supporting national police and judicial authorities in the fight against international crime and terrorism. the most recent terrorist attacks have increased the need for a stronger european police agency with increased capacity to facilitate cross-border cooperation and the exchange of information between member states. in this context, it was necessary to adequately equip europol to support member states in the prevention, analysis and investigation of crime across the union. however, the more powerful europol is, the greater the parliamentary scrutiny of its activities must be and the greater the legal safeguards to prevent unlawful mass surveillance of citizens or indiscriminate sharing and analysis of personal data, which could be disproportionate, unnecessary and contrary to the fundamental rights of those it serves. europol carries out its activities within the european union. however, organized crime does not stop at our borders. this is why better cooperation with third countries and international organizations is also needed. the regulation we are discussing today is intended to strengthen europol and to avoid certain risks of police interference in our lives. i should also mention that there are points in the text which are still displeasing to my group. for example, to name just two: the fact that the executive director of europol is not directly accountable to the european parliament for the exercise of his functions, but to the council; or the way in which the legal basis has been introduced so that the iru (internet referral unit) can continue to exercise functions that it already started to develop on 1 july 2015. that is why we have maintained our amendment in this respect, to recall that, as was agreed to the end, the iru would be the subject of a separate legislative proposal. i would like to thank mr diaz de mera for his efforts to improve various aspects of the text. my group will of course vote in favour of the amendment we have tabled, but it also supports the text as a whole, and it does so because it is a necessary instrument and there is no alternative in sight at the moment to achieve better and more effective crossborder cooperation between the european union law enforcement agencies and to improve the exchange of information with third countries in the fight against transnational crime.
madam president, i would first of all like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr agustín díaz de mera, and the other rapporteurs. the police, professional and democratic, are one of the pillars of our security, but they are also one of the keys to living in personal and political freedom. they risk their lives when it's necessary for us. in this globalised world, the approval of the new europol is good news if governments do not put the brakes on the agency's new capabilities. we must ask the member states to send the best people for the board of directors' duties, not bureaucrats or lobbyists. we appeal to your responsibility. we in parliament must ensure that our new roles are scrutinized with fairness and without partisan pretences, because we need it, because we owe it to the victims of the most serious crimes, to the most vulnerable and to all citizens.
madam president, i would first of all like to congratulate mr díaz de mera and the other members on their tenacity in seeking the most powerful instrument possible to combat crossborder organised crime and terrorism within the european union and in relation to third countries. the latest attacks within our borders, in paris and brussels, but also the previous ones in madrid and london, have highlighted the dramatic and urgent need to provide a sufficiently solid legal framework agreed by all to give decisive support to our police, civil guards and european law enforcement forces, who needed this european backing to strengthen and improve their work. this regulation for europol means more investment in prevention through risk analysis and cooperation, but also more intelligence sharing, including the necessary infiltration, ending sanctuaries and more capacity to fight not only terrorism, but also those other crimes that underlie terrorism: the dramatic trafficking of people, money laundering and tax evasion and tax evasion, and also cyberattacks in a society like ours.

member of the commission.– mr president, i do not need to repeat why it is really important that we have agreed to revise and update eu rules on foreign students and researchers. as the context on migration and mobility evolves, it is understood that so should our rules and policies. the agreed text is a very important element of our overall migration approach. it sends the important signal that the european union is a globally competitive and welcoming destination for much—needed students and researchers from abroad. at the same time, it provides for a clear legal framework which does not mix up other categories such as asylum seekers or refugees, and it does not touch on member states’ competences to grant access to the labour market. this agreement is ambitious and balanced and will allow europe to attract more talented students and researchers in the future who can contribute to our societies and to our economies. as many of you have insisted on this, i will repeat that the commission has insisted, together with you, that member states’ discretionary powers with regard to rejecting an application may only be used when strictly necessary and justified, and we will of course be monitoring this. as i mentioned earlier, let us not forget that migration and mobility are also about empowerment, creativity and socio-economic development. commission statement joint declaration by the european parliament and the commission on the grounds for rejection (article 20) the european parliament and the commission understand point (f) of article 20(2) of this directive as allowing member states to reject an application only on a case-by-case basis and taking into account the specific circumstances of the third-country national and the principle of proportionality and on the basis of evidence or serious and objective reasons. the commission will ensure that member states implement this provision in line with this interpretation when transposing the directive, and will inform the parliament and the council thereof, in the framework of its obligations under article 39. the european parliament and the commission consider that the inclusion of this provision in this directive should not constitute a precedent for future legal migration instruments.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the new regulation which will govern europol, in compliance with the provisions of the treaty of lisbon for its adaptation to it. europol is an institution of great importance in shaping the european union's area of freedom, security and justice. as security functions are the exclusive responsibility of emts in their respective territories, europol has an important role to play in coordinating the action of emts in the fight against certain forms of crime. europol acts in practice as a 'pool' of information sent by mscs on criminal areas under its management that require specialised analysis from a european dimension. its objective is to prevent and investigate the activities of criminal groups operating in different member states. the new regulation will make it possible, for example, to combat terrorism more effectively, which is being developed and carried out on the internet.
in writing. ‒ we have rejected the council's proposal for a new europol regulation. we protest against this agency being given greater powers while maintaining a significant opacity that leaves it completely outside of public scrutiny. the new rules remove the principle of subsidiarity, leaving the agency responsible for all matters relating to european policy, which would allow europol to carry out its activities independently, without cooperating with the security forces of the member states, in addition to cross-border cooperation. in addition, it will have the ability to collect and store data independently, which may conflict with the data protection laws of different states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the european police agency europol will be able to step up its efforts in the fight against terrorism and cybercrime and to respond more quickly to threats thanks to the new operating rules that parliament has approved. the new powers are accompanied by strict safeguards on data protection and democratic control tools. the draft legislation, agreed by parliament and council negotiators in november 2015, strengthens europol's powers to ensure that it has the necessary tools to deal with the threat of cross-border crime and terrorism. among other innovations, the agency will have more facilities to create specialised units to respond to imminent threats.
in writing. ‒ during the passage of the european commission's proposal on the european police office (europol) by the libe committee, a problematic text was improved, thanks to amendments by the left-wing groups. for example, by means of more stringent data protection, in line with the recently adopted libe directive, a broader parliamentary control mechanism or a better definition of the limits of europol's action. however, in its passage through the trilogue the text has returned to a swamp as it alters the original purpose of europol to help national police and judicial authorities to combat international crime and terrorism by extending its scope of action to the point of compromising the principle of subsidiarity. the lack of a precise definition of the scope of action, the reduction of parliamentary control, the ability of the internet content notification unit to exchange data directly with individuals without the participation of the member states, among other provisions, seriously calls into question a text that should regulate an agency whose actions affect civil liberties in a decisive way. we therefore voted in favour of rejecting the council's position.

in writing. ‒ this report, the result of several years of hard work, aims to increase the supply of information from member states to europol so that it can provide comprehensive support to member states' law enforcement services. this is why it is given increased responsibilities such as the creation of a new department to support and coordinate the training of law enforcement officers at strategic level. in addition, this report also establishes a robust data protection regime, introducing elements of joint supervision of data transferred to europol. europol also has the responsibility to periodically review the need to retain personal data. finally, it is also intended to introduce a mechanism for scrutiny of europol's activities by the european parliament and national parliaments to ensure democratic legitimacy. in my view, the adoption of this report is crucial as it will serve to adapt europol to the requirements of the lisbon treaty, as well as to ensure greater data protection which will help prevent crime.

mr president, i support this proposal because i believe it is right to promote the principles of mobility of young people, students and researchers. i think it is extremely right that we should try to establish uniform rules for students and scientists from third countries to be able to study and carry out scientific research in the european union. in short, the influx of high-quality brains into the european union is clearly a positive trend, it enhances the quality of european research, the quality of european education and of course, subsequently, if these people remain in the european union, it affects the quality of european industry and other sectors where these educated, qualified people can take hold and can thus increase the competitiveness of europe as such in relation to other powers such as the united states of america, japan and so on.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this early agreement at first reading on a directive covering the categories mentioned in the title, which takes the form of a consolidated text in which several directives are brought together in a new one which addresses together issues previously regulated by means of separate legal acts. the aim of the new directive is to extend the material scope of the existing directives, to provide greater legal certainty for different groups of third-country nationals coming to the eu to carry out the activities falling within the categories envisaged.
in writing. ‒ in the current situation where the european authorities are applying such aggressive immigration policies at our borders, they are simultaneously presenting this directive of a markedly elitist nature for the migration of the members with higher academic qualifications. during the whole negotiation, our proposal to extend this administrative category to highly discriminated sectors such as au pairs was ignored, and the possibility remained that the states would not accept a candidate without giving any explanation, which could lead to discrimination on the grounds of origin. we have voted against the rejection amendment, however, because we believe that despite these major weaknesses, any legislation which favours freedom of movement and migration with rights is a positive one.
in writing. ‒ we voted against the two amendments tabled by two political groups, which would have meant the rejection of the council's position and, consequently, the failure of the legislative proposal. we believe that this report contains very positive aspects for people who wish to pursue their higher education or research in the eu. this is a second reading of what was agreed in committee and there was no vote in plenary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this directive which recasts several directives on the entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purposes of research, studies, traineeships, volunteering, pupil exchange and au pair placement, by merging them into a new regulation. the aim of this legislation is to provide greater security for third-country nationals coming to the union to carry out any of the activities envisaged, and to achieve a fully homogeneous system. the commission has also proposed that the directive be amended to include the possibility of a voluntary scheme for the recruitment of au pairs. in addition, intra-community mobility of students and researchers has been improved and the minimum number of hours that students can work part-time has been extended, and the period for which students and researchers can remain in the union after completing their studies or research has been set at 12 months. the union must make further progress on legal migration.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal that amends and brings together council directive 2004/114/ec (‘students’ directive’) and council directive 2005/71/ec (‘researchers’ directive’) as it proposes that the existing rules for students and researchers should also apply to trainees and, although only optionally, to au-pairs. these account for a much needed broadening of instruments establishing a legal framework for third country nationals to enter and reside in the eu under equal regulated conditions.
in writing. ‒ the new directive aims to bring together the directive on students and researchers from third countries and to improve certain aspects of both groups, such as granting them the right to stay for at least 9 months after finishing their studies or research in order to look for work, facilitating their movement within the european union during their stay, requiring notification only to the member state of destination, allowing researchers to bring their family members and allowing students to work 15 hours a week. we are talking not only about simplifying legislation but also about improving the situation of third country nationals who are subject to regulation. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of this text.
i am sorry to abstain, mr president, but we cannot dissociate the debate on regional cohesion from the construction of another economic model. we cannot ask for flexibility in public funds, acknowledge the burdens that the crisis and austerity have imposed and at the same time insist on the implementation of new structural reforms, which are the main cause of the growing inequality in europe. because let us not be fooled, european funds are increasingly tied to promoting the integration of the european economy into the global market, without compensating for the effects of liberalization and privatization on workers in the peripheral states. european policy can use the market, but not to replicate its priorities, the priorities of big capital. on the contrary, it must be a public pole for the definition of a different social and productive model. we must denounce the way in which the right wing, and also the member states and regions, have managed the funds without taking account of the social partners and favouring the fragmentation and disintegration of public investment at the hands of private interests.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the resolution is to ask the european parliament to speed up the implementation of cohesion policy funds, given the delays in payments by the european institutions to beneficiaries (regions and subnational entities). it therefore called on the commission to report to parliament on the implementation of the payment plan and on the acceleration of the implementation of the payment plan. it also called for an assessment of the impact of the fulfilment of the preconditions for project financing, given the problems arising from confusing regulations and lack of information to the public actors concerned. i cannot, however, support the institution's declaration that it is in favour of 'promoting structural reforms', which means nothing more than accelerating the dismantling of public services and reducing public spending and investment, with fatal consequences in terms of social and territorial inequality, contrary to the treaties. i have therefore decided to abstain from voting on this resolution.
in writing. this resolution aims to promote and improve the community's cohesion policy by pointing out its main shortcomings, calling for the correct implementation of all programmes and instruments, and promoting better use and management of the european structural and investment funds (esi funds). the esi funds are the main investment tool in european policy. the eu has a budget of €454 billion for the period 2014-2020. their effectiveness and good management are essential to meet the guidelines of the europe 2020 strategy, modernise our union and facilitate entrepreneurship. cohesion policy must make possible one of the eu's fundamental values, solidarity, by ending territorial differences. this is particularly so in a time of economic crisis which has increased social inequalities and economic disparities between member states. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the resolution on speeding up the implementation of cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ the resolution aims to speed up the implementation of cohesion policy in all eu regions and improve its effectiveness, a key issue given that this instrument has a budget of over eur 350 billion until 2020 and is the main source of funding for public investment in several member states. we agree with many of the things that are proposed: recommendations for simplifying procedures, improving information, reducing deadlines, putting in place tools for analysing and evaluating the use of funds, etc. but there are references to deepening structural reforms and to the use of mechanisms of the stability and growth pact which we find problematic because they support the austerity policies we have been suffering for years in spain and other eu countries. in line with the position of denunciation of these instruments, we have voted against.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this resolution because, in addition to insisting on simplifying procedures and deepening the study of the problems caused, it focuses on the problems that the crisis is creating in the investment capacities of some states and the effects that these states have on the use or participation in these cohesion programmes. i also agree that in some member states local and regional authorities are still considered 'minors' and often function much better than the member states to which they belong. the recommendation against centralism contained in the resolution is very timely.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is the eu's main instrument for reaching out to citizens, as well as the main investment and development policy of the union and the main source of public investment for some member states. the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy can be achieved through a coherent interaction between growth, development and structural reform policies. cohesion policy thus plays an essential role in integrating and developing these objectives. there is a significant concern about the delay in the implementation of cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020, in view of what happened in the previous programming period, in which insufficient information, lack of administrative structures or complexity in the procurement processes made implementation of cohesion policy difficult. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the application of the principle of subsidiarity to the member states is a good one.

in writing. ‒ the resolution aims to speed up the implementation of cohesion policy in all eu regions and improve its effectiveness, a key issue given that this instrument has a budget of over eur 350 billion until 2020 and is the main source of funding for public investment in several member states. we agree with many of the things that are proposed: recommendations for simplifying procedures, improving information, reducing deadlines, putting in place tools for analysing and evaluating the use of funds, etc. but there are references to deepening structural reforms and to the use of mechanisms of the stability and growth pact which we find problematic because they support the austerity policies we have been suffering for years in spain and other eu countries. in line with the position of denunciation of these instruments, we have voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because eu cohesion policy is the main source of public investment in some member states. the objectives of promoting growth and creating jobs can be achieved through a coherent interaction within the union's economic policy mix of structural reforms and growth-enhancing investments, all of which are facilitated and accelerated by cohesion policy investments. the fact that the n+2 rule of the 2007-2013 perspective has been extended to n+3 for all member states is positive. however, there is a clear concern about the significant delay in the implementation of cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020, including the deadline for the adoption of operational programmes. this resolution sets out how the implementation of cohesion policy is to be accelerated and what measures are envisaged to facilitate the implementation of operational programmes and to avoid the release of funds.
in writing. ‒ investment policy is considered to be the main investment and development policy of the union. this proposal arises from the need to coordinate and harmonise cohesion policy with other union policies, such as the digital single market or transport policy, in order to meet the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the report calls for the implementation of the relevant structural reforms, including investment-friendly policies and the fight against fraud. it also aims to reduce territorial disparities by establishing a plan in which all regions are able to develop their competitiveness. i support this proposal because a good interaction between cohesion policy and growth and development policies would ease the way towards achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is the eu's main instrument for reaching out to citizens, as well as the main investment and development policy of the union and the main source of public investment for some member states. the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy can be achieved through a coherent interaction between growth, development and structural reform policies. cohesion policy thus plays an essential role in integrating and developing these objectives. there is a major concern about the delay in the implementation of cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020, and the commission is asked how it intends to accelerate the implementation of cohesion policy. i welcome the fact that a joint debate has been held in the house on these matters. that is why i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the resolution aims to speed up the implementation of cohesion policy in all eu regions and improve its effectiveness, a key issue given that this instrument has a budget of over eur 350 billion until 2020 and is the main source of funding for public investment in several member states. we agree with many of the things that are proposed: recommendations for simplifying procedures, improving information, reducing deadlines, putting in place tools for analysing and evaluating the use of funds, etc. but there are references to deepening structural reforms and to the use of mechanisms of the stability and growth pact which we find problematic because they support the austerity policies we have been suffering for years in spain and other eu countries. in line with the position of denunciation of these instruments, we have voted against.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the resolution is to ask the european parliament to speed up the implementation of cohesion policy funds, given the delays in payments by the european institutions to beneficiaries (regions and subnational entities). it therefore called on the commission to report to parliament on the implementation of the payment plan and on the acceleration of the implementation of the payment plan. it also called for an assessment of the impact of the fulfilment of the preconditions for project financing, given the problems arising from confusing regulations and lack of information to the public actors concerned. i cannot, however, support the institution's declaration that it is in favour of 'promoting structural reforms', which means nothing more than accelerating the dismantling of public services and reducing public spending and investment, with fatal consequences in terms of social and territorial inequality, contrary to the treaties. i have therefore decided to abstain from voting on this resolution.

mr president, mr commissioner, we socialists have said many times in this european parliament that the dublin regulation is obsolete and is blatantly unenforced and we have therefore called for its abolition and replacement by a genuine european mechanism, a european system worthy of the name, a european system that lives up to the commitment of the lisbon treaty, with a common european asylum system. and for exactly the same reason we are now critical and deeply disappointed at the stingy insufficiency of the commission's proposal, which offers only a creative make-up of the current dublin regulation rather than establishing a truly binding mechanism governed by the principle of solidarity, reception and registration of asylum seekers on european soil. what's he do? a corrective mechanism exclusively designed for emergency situations or extraordinary flows, and economic sanctions that are not a sufficient deterrent mechanism to compel states to comply with their obligations under humanitarian law. the spanish case is a shocking one; unfortunately, my own country, which is said not to be a country for refugees because it is in flagrant breach of the agreements adopted by the council, but which would be prepared to pay the fines proposed by the commission. no, it's not enough. we need not only economic mechanisms but also political ones and, where appropriate, legal sanctions. we therefore say very clearly that we must move towards a european asylum system governed by dignity in reception and registration, by a dignified reception and by sufficient resources to honour the european vocation of the asylum system.
in writing. the commission has proposed a revision of the regulations governing the european asylum system. we socialists have long been denouncing the ineffectiveness of the present dublin system and stressing the need for a thorough reform of it to give rise to a genuine european asylum system worthy of the name. a system based on solidarity between member states in meeting the challenges posed by the current dynamics of asylum and refuge. a system including a mandatory compliance allocation key, with corrective mechanisms that take into account the particularities of each state in terms of size, gdp and absorption capacity. the socialists have got the commission involved in the reform and from today we will work hard to improve the proposals presented because we believe that what the commission has put forward does not meet our expectations. we welcome the initiative to impose sanctions on countries which do not support the eu and which fail to comply with their asylum obligations or do not accept their share of responsibility for receiving and handling asylum applications in accordance with the allocation key.

on behalf of the alde group. madam president, commissioner, much of what i am about to say is perhaps very much intended for your former colleague, mr moscovici, because the unequal dynamic we are in is ultimately destructive for economic growth. that's a classic. and we also enter a vicious circle. why would you do that? because it affects economic growth negatively, then there will be more unemployment, then there will be more financing problems, more pension costs, and so on; then there will be less growth. that has to stop now, because we've gone too far. but we must look at it from the point of view of economic policy. both the oecd and the international monetary fund have said that this is going too far. and here comes the crux of the matter. you see, the indispensable social policies are for relief: to alleviate poverty, to alleviate unemployment, and so on. they don't solve the structural problems. the structural problems must be solved by appropriate economic policies, fiscal policy, redistributive policy, income policy, policy on essential investments, sectoral policies, etc. those are the ones that are going to break an unequal economic dynamic. and that is measured, commissioner. it's the palma indices, the gini indices. i'm talking to you about very basic economics. what the commission and the member states, which the commission must help, must do is to focus from now on on the unequal dynamics with the same interest with which they have focused on financial balance or even on the opening up of the single market. why not include in the commission's semiannual evaluation, in the famous european semester, a series of objectives relating to the gini or palma indices and see how this destructive dynamic of inequality develops?

on behalf of the alde group. mr president, mrs jourová, i would first like to extend my warmest congratulations to my british liberal colleague, catherine bearder, for the outstanding work she has done on this report. human trafficking robs millions of people of their dignity around the world. it is important to remember that not only is it a violation of human rights, as recognised by the charter of fundamental rights of the union, but it is one of the most lucrative illicit businesses in europe. the traffickers make millions, billions a year of profit on our continent. men, women and children are deceived as the main motive for sexual exploitation, but thousands of victims are destined for begging, forced labour or organ harvesting. 80% of trafficking victims are women. most are young people deceived with false promises of employment and then raped, drugged, threatened, blackmailed, stripped of their passports, loaded with debts... in europe, some 140 000 women are victims of sexual exploitation and trafficking. for a problem of european scale we need european solutions, of course. cooperation between europol, eurojust and national authorities and authorities of third countries, with a systematic exchange of information between member states, is essential. let me say one last thought: we still don't know the whereabouts of at least 10 000 unaccompanied minors who entered the union last year. it is not unreasonable to fear that many may be in the hands of human traffickers. perhaps the commissioner could answer the urgent question i put to you three months ago today: what records do you have on these children? do you know its age, do you know its origin? what is the new global strategy announced in the european agenda on migration to strengthen the functions between frontex and europol in order to combat the mafias that also traffic in refugee children?
on behalf of the green group, mr president, every year thousands and thousands of people fall victim to traffickers. the phenomenon is now one of the most lucrative illicit businesses in the world and we have a legal instrument at european union level, but unfortunately it is being applied very badly: in the matter of identifying victims, in the matter of what article 18 provides, for example, to give the necessary training to public servants and police officers who are in contact with victims of trafficking; in the application of article 8, for example, which calls for persons who commit an offence who are victims of trafficking not to be penalized, and fines are still being imposed at the moment on persons who are considered victims; and also, for example, in giving international protection for reasons of trafficking as required by the directive. countries like spain, for example, are not doing that. we have a serious problem with the implementation of the directive and we also have a problem, mrs jourová, i have to tell you, with the information we are given, because the commission has not yet given us the report on the implementation of the directive. and with that, we have had to make a report - i want to thank the rapporteur, mrs bearder, because she has done an excellent job - but we have a serious problem in the application and in the information, too, that you give us.
on behalf of the enf group. mr president, 80% of the victims of human trafficking are women. it is time to combat effectively the increasing proliferation of pimping, forced begging, forced marriage, forced labour and organ harvesting in europe. what does the report suggest to remedy this? the commission has also proposed that the member states should take measures to ensure that the rights of women are protected. have we considered the consequences of such a move? i'll tell you this: to get papers, women will be systematically prostituted, enslaved or forced into marriage by the criminals who exploit them. the cure would be worse than the disease, that's for sure. what is the solution? it is obviously not automatic legalisation of trafficking victims. the solution is to fight hard against smugglers, to control our national borders, to tackle the causes, not the consequences, and finally to use common sense and firmness. i shall therefore vote against this report because it does not tackle the mafia networks which exploit women, but rather, in a way, supports them.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, two out of every three victims of trafficking are girls, girls like this one who, despite all the efforts we make to get them back, will be irrecoverable after being sold and exploited to the point of being stripped of all their dignity. almost 80% of trafficked women cross a border and the vast majority of them end up in europe, victims of criminal organisations who, under false promises of work, force them into prostitution. if they are not fortunate enough to be released by the police, many of them end up sick or dead. we can't keep our eyes closed. i therefore ask the commission to assess the member states' compliance with this anti-trafficking directive, to see whether they are really taking action against the impunity surrounding the sale of human beings, preferably women and girls. the main measure is prevention. action must be taken against traffickers, by increasing prosecution and protecting victims who cooperate with the police. secondly, we must strengthen the protection of victims, by identifying and protecting them so that they can escape the hell they live in, by offering them a dignified life so that they do not fall back into criminal networks. finally, i believe that we need greater judicial cooperation and information exchange between member states. and so that girls like this don't end up dead alive, we're forced to discourage the demand that increases trafficking. if sexual exploitation wasn't a business, this little girl wouldn't end up in a brothel, think about it.

on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – madam president, in march, two years after the illegal annexation of the crimean peninsula by the russian federation, the eu and its member states reaffirmed their deep concern at the worsening of the human rights situation in the crimean peninsula. this includes the denial of freedom of expression, freedom of peaceful assembly, freedom of religion and belief, and the persecution of persons belonging to minorities, in particular the crimean tatars. high representative/vice-president mogherini discussed these issues in person with the leaders of the mejlis of crimean tatars during her last visit to kiev in november 2015. the decision of 26 april by the so-called supreme court of crimea to prohibit the activities of the mejlis, which is a self-governing body of the crimean tatars, and labelling it an extremist organisation, represents a grave attack on the rights of the crimean tatars as a whole. furthermore, it constitutes an additional very negative deterioration in the human rights situation on the crimean peninsula since its illegal annexation by the russian federation in 2014. let me reiterate once again the eu’s long-standing call for full, free and unrestricted access for international human rights actors to the whole territory of ukraine, including crimea and sevastopol. in the light of recent developments this remains absolutely vital. in less than one week, 18 may will mark the anniversary of the deportation of crimean tatars in 1944. last year the crimean tatar community was not allowed to hold peaceful public events on the peninsula to commemorate this historic tragedy. the occasion is a stark reminder to all of us that the crimean tatar people have suffered too much in their history and their persecution must stop immediately.

in writing. i could not vote on this report because, despite the fact that it represents a clear improvement in the exchange of tax information between eu member states, the limit set excludes most companies from this type of obligation. this report is part of the numerous tax scandals which have been the subject of the european parliament's work over the last few years. it proposes very important measures for the control of the tax activity of multinational companies which should be integrated into the european regulatory framework. however, the limit of eur 750 million (as consolidated turnover) excludes the majority of such companies which may continue to operate without being subject to this regulation. it is because of this major flaw that i have not been able to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this text proposes country-by-country reporting, i.e. the possibility for the tax authorities of the different member states to ensure that multinational profits are properly taxed where they are made. this commercial strategy is already being applied to banking institutions. once implemented, the directive would require multinational groups to report their turnover by country, pre-tax profits, taxes paid, salaries and all subsidies received. we could then fight more effectively against fictitious, abusive addresses, but also against the so-called 'mailbox' companies. member states will retain the right to sanction abuses in the event of failures on the part of multinational groups. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which seems to me to be in the direction of greater transparency.
in writing. the report amends the committee's proposal for the exchange of information on multinational corporations' profits and taxation, aimed at reducing tax avoidance. we consider the report to be clearly inadequate and have made a point of ensuring that information is not only exchanged between member states but also regularly communicated to the commission and, above all, made public. unfortunately, the latter point has been rejected by the major groups.
in writing. country-by-country reports are key to the commission's anti-avoidance package in the wake of the luxleaks (and now panaleaks) scandal, as they reveal where multinationals make their profits and where they actually pay their taxes. the european parliament has already taken a position in favour of imposing an obligation on multinationals to publish country-by-country reports under the shareholders' rights directive (cofferati report) although the council has strongly opposed this. the commission has recently put forward a legislative proposal on the mandatory publication of country-by-country reports, so this proposal to exchange country-by-country reports of multinationals between tax administrations, which i have supported, is only a first step, albeit an important and positive one. however, i do not share the relatively arbitrary turnover threshold for the application of the directive (eur 750 million per year) which means that only 1,900 companies would be covered, whereas the accounting directive indicates a lower threshold for identifying large companies and if applied, the new standard would cover 20,000 companies.

in writing. ‒ this legislation amends directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation in the field of valuation, requiring multinationals with a consolidated turnover of more than eur 750 million to report their country-by-country tax returns to the authorities of the member state in which the parent company has its tax domicile. that country will have to share the information with the countries in which the company operates. the company must report on income, profits, taxes paid, capital, tangible assets and number of employees. this is therefore an essential step in the fight against unfair tax practices, as it will increase transparency and reduce unfair competition. i therefore think it appropriate to vote in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ we socialists are opposed to china being granted the status of a market economy automatically. china and the eu are not competing on equal terms, as the asian country does not respect wto rules, is not a market economy and practices social, labour, environmental and price dumping. to address these unfair trade practices, the eu needs to have renewed, more effective and faster to implement trade defence instruments and an anti-dumping methodology that takes into account the distortion of chinese prices and production costs until the 5 criteria set by the union to be considered a market economy are met. this resolution, which was led by the socialist group and adopted by a very large majority, covers all these issues and i have therefore voted in favour of it. the eu cannot afford to lose a single job by giving china a trade status it does not deserve. if china wants to be treated as a market economy, it has to act like one.
in writing. ‒ as i have stressed in the vote on the amendments, i consider it necessary to take a firm stand against the commission's intention to further liberalise trade with china after 2016. the joint motion put to the vote, although it acknowledges that the present situation would not justify such a procedure, merely repeats the commission's arguments. it thus endorses a poor public consultation and leaves the door wide open to eliminating anti-dumping protection in exchange for privatisations and deregulation in the chinese economy. we cannot defend economic meddling in china or an intensification of global competition which would seriously damage social and environmental standards in industry and the jobs it creates in europe. that is why i voted against.

in writing. ‒ we abstained on the grounds that the possible recognition of china as a market economy would threaten millions of jobs in the european union. we consider the resolution to be ambiguous in that it does not explicitly call on the european commission not to grant this recognition to china. we tabled two amendments which asked the commission to do the same in a very specific way, but unfortunately they were rejected in the plenary.

in writing. as i have stressed in the vote on the amendments, i consider it necessary to take a firm stand against the commission's intention to further liberalise trade with china after 2016. the joint motion put to the vote, although it acknowledges that the present situation would not justify such a procedure, merely repeats the commission's arguments. it thus endorses a poor public consultation and leaves the door wide open to eliminating anti-dumping protection in exchange for privatisations and deregulation in the chinese economy. we cannot defend economic meddling in china or an intensification of global competition which would seriously damage social and environmental standards in industry and the jobs it creates in europe. that is why i voted against.

in writing. ‒ in the resolution on the granting of the market economy status to china, ehbildu's position has been abstention. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat dumping, and it is not the commission's intention to take action against china. otherwise, the impact on the economy is serious, as we are seeing in the steel sector in euskal herria. however, trade relations, under the rules of the world trade organisation, follow neo-liberal patterns which, in the interests of free competition, hinder any action by the public authorities in favour of the strategic productive sectors of the countries and consequently prevent the defence of employment and labour and social rights in our countries. the motion for a resolution does not make a strong defence of the affected productive sectors in europe, and accepts the neo-liberal scheme of free competition, although in this case it is reluctant to grant market economy status to china.

in writing. ‒ i have voted against granting china market economy status because china is simply not a market economy. already now without this status chinese products have flooded european markets. think about the steel industry or textile products. under section 15 of the chinese wto accession protocol, china can be treated as a non-market economy (nme) in anti-dumping proceedings if chinese firms cannot prove that they operate under market economy conditions. the main implication of nme status in anti-dumping proceedings is the possibility to use other methodologies to determine the normal value of the good, instead of using domestic prices to compute the dumping margin. china will invade our european economies with cheap subsidised products that will kill our european smes and manufacturers. china does not have the same social and economic costs as in europe. i want to protect european quality products made in europe. european quality and health standards are the highest and chinese products would undermine safety for health and the environment. we should stand behind european companies and jobs on this file.

in writing. ‒ in this resolution, parliament states that as long as china does not meet the five criteria set by the eu to define a market economy, its exports should be treated differently. we are talking about a subject of great importance and magnitude and which would have economic, political and social consequences throughout europe, and it is therefore necessary that this house send a clear message through this resolution for the next steps that the european commission will take in this matter. that is why i think it is appropriate to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ as demonstrated, china's export prices are not determined by supply and demand; as a result of its overproduction, it sells its products at lower prices, so that it can reduce it. for this reason, it is clear that it is not a market economy and that therefore to consider it as such would only harm the union. in addition, another reason why we cannot consider china a market economy is as simple as that it does not meet the five criteria of the european union. i therefore do not support the granting of market economy status to china and i fully expect to continue to strengthen and improve trade defence instruments to defend our companies against unfair practices.
in writing. ‒ last september, the united nations adopted the 2030 agenda for sustainable development, which includes very positive elements for us when it comes to achieving global goals such as the eradication of hunger, gender equality, or the promotion of peace. however, the european commission has not taken any concrete action to implement this agenda. we have supported this resolution because it calls on the commission to take specific measures to achieve these objectives, which requires a real economic commitment to cooperation policies, which establishes the obligation of 0.7% of the budget for this purpose. it also calls for a reorientation of existing policies, so that they take into account cross-cutting criteria such as environmental sustainability, health promotion, or universal access to basic resources such as water. we hope that this resolution will be taken into account and will not be added to the long list of failures in this matter, because due to the lack of will of the governments of the global north these objectives have not been met, which initially set 2015 as a target.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the european commission to take concrete action on the sustainable development goals. since the adoption of the so-called 2030 agenda for sustainable development at the united nations last september, the european commission has done little or nothing to adapt its policies to this new development agenda. we believe it is essential that the commission should draw up a road map in this respect as a matter of urgency, as the resolution rightly points out.
in writing. ‒ the sustainable development goals (sdgs) of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development, adopted in september 2015, entered into force on 1 january 2015. countries will need to step up their efforts over the next 15 years to end poverty in all its forms, reduce inequality and combat climate change. since they are not binding, it is up to governments to adopt them as their own and to establish national frameworks for their achievement. as the resolution states, which i supported, it calls for the adoption of a joint strategy by the european union for the implementation of the sdgs, and for the agreement and development of indicators to assist in the process of monitoring the achievement of the objectives, and for the provision of sufficient resources, by calling on the eu and its member states to commit themselves without delay to achieving 0.7% of gdp in development aid.

in writing. ‒ as we know, the 2030 agenda is an action plan for people, planet and prosperity, which aims to strengthen universal peace and eradicate poverty once and for all. in this area, we must emphasise the role played by the union and its institutions, as well as by its member states, as the main actors in achieving these objectives. the aim of this proposal is to have the developing countries set periodic targets, which will be examined by the commission and transmitted to parliament so that it can take the necessary measures. it also recalls that a substantial allocation of financial resources is necessary to achieve the objectives effectively. on the basis of the above, i consider this resolution to be of great importance, since the eradication of poverty in the world is an urgent challenge and a priority for the union and for citizens.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this parliament's motion for a resolution following the statements by the council and the commission on the follow-up to and status of the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals. we need to constantly monitor the 2030 agenda and the sdgs from within the european institutions to ensure that we make progress in the fight against poverty and correct the course of action where necessary, ensuring that there is proper implementation of the three dimensions of sustainable development: economic, social and environmental.
