in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the strategy for the single market, which calls for the removal of unjustified obstacles and the promotion of social economy enterprises in internal market policies, since they represent approximately 10-12% of european enterprises. the council must swiftly adopt the package of measures on product safety and market surveillance and the commission should play a facilitating role in this respect. the importance of providing adequate information on products intended for retail sale and in particular the indication of the country of origin should be emphasised. it should be stressed that the principle of equal pay for equal work at the same place is an important tool in the fight against market distortions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it supports the overall objectives of the commission's new strategy to achieve a fairer and more competitive single market in line with title ii of the tfeu, and appreciates its actions in key areas to exploit the full potential of the single market for the benefit of consumers, workers and businesses, especially start-ups, in order to increase the number of sustainable quality jobs and to foster the growth of smes. the report also calls on the commission to submit without delay a legislative proposal for the establishment of a single european system for the protection of geographical indications for non-agricultural products in the union, which will have many positive effects for the whole european business and social fabric. it also reiterated its call for the council to adopt swiftly the package of measures on product safety and market surveillance, stressing the importance of the indication of the country of origin on products intended for retail sale.

on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, commissioner, the un conference will take note of the many advances that have taken place in this field over the last fifteen years: advances in information that have led to better prevention of the disease, medical and pharmacological advances in responding to it, greater activation of civil society and health systems that have responded in a coordinated way to this infection, which has taken so many millions of people around the world by storm. but more important than the progress we have made is the commitment to continue fighting this disease that still afflicts 40 million people in the world, which killed more than a million people in 2015, which continues to infect different parts of the world and which africa - the continent of poverty and also the continent of pain - is losing many of its girls and women. the important thing is therefore the commitments we have for the future. and in this commitment, the most important thing is to assume what is identified with the three 90 percent: that 90 percent of those who have the virus end up being diagnosed by health systems, that 90 percent of those who are diagnosed end up being treated, and that 90 percent of those who are treated end up being free of viral infection. i therefore believe that the european union should push the member states to establish coordinated national plans, strategies to prevent infection, to ensure treatment, but also to fight discrimination. and those plans have to prevent the national strategy from weakening in some countries, as in spain, and the data relating to the fight against aids are now showing, as in europe as a whole, an increase in infections, although in the rest of the world they are decreasing.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, hiv has become a global epidemic. between 1981 and 2007, it killed nearly 25 million people, and today, there are still more than 30 million people affected worldwide. the joint united nations programme on hiv/aids coordinates international efforts to address the epidemic and it is essential that the european union reinforces its support for this institution. but supporting with words alone is useless. for it to be a real support, we should rethink our model of drug development to put it at the service of the people and not the interests of big pharma. we must be consistent and not undermine access to medicines for people in developing countries through trade agreements with stringent intellectual property clauses that are reproduced over and over again, and we continue on this path. and patent protection is the reason why the newest and most effective drugs are not available to 95 percent of the people affected by aids, who live in the global south. it's not my data, it's un data. finally, i would like to remind you that the most common way of spreading hiv is still sexual transmission, that is, the most effective protection - despite the fact that some fanatics continue to deny it and continue to preach abstinence - is condoms. and that is what this european parliament said in its 2011 resolution, where we advocated - and i read literally - for access to means of protection such as male and female condoms, and the strengthening of women's rights and autonomy in sexual relations. in short, more coherent policies and more informed and safe sex, especially for women.
mr president, the truth is that, according to the united nations report, and we can all see this, there has been very, very significant progress in the treatment and prevention of aids. however, as the report says, we cannot be complacent because the progress made in the last 15 years can be lost if we do not make the effort required to bring an end to what we might call the aids epidemic. almost 40 million people are still infected, and 22 million of them still lack access to treatment. we are opening a debate here in parliament on access to medicines and of course we must incorporate this aspect into the whole of development cooperation policy. women and girls are particularly affected, so a gender approach is essential. in europe, low and middle income countries still face the challenge. i would also like to warn that we may be seeing a resurgence in this economic crisis, where the pattern of drug use is changing from cocaine to heroin, which is cheaper and, as you know, carries so many infectious diseases. therefore, we cannot let our guard down. the european union has to take the lead, it has to have an ambitious target to eradicate this epidemic by 2030, we have to aspire to national plans to eradicate and prevent these viral diseases as a whole and, of course, we have to strengthen our health system, in which it is so important to ensure universality for all citizens in order to combat this and all the epidemics that we have ahead of us.
the european union and the participants in this high-level meeting must make binding commitments to: end the discrimination and social stigma still suffered by people with aids and to eliminate existing laws in some countries which criminalize people with the virus, ensure universal access to public health and sexual and reproductive health services and medicines, end the monopoly of the pharmaceutical industry and the shameful business of patents, and prevent further contagion. to eradicate the disease, much more is needed in the field of prevention and much attention to young people and adolescents. research should be public and be in the service of the people, rather than handing public money to an industry that uses it to advance its interests over the right to health. the answer is 'blue card'. thank you for your question, mr arnott. i think i have already made it quite clear in my speech that the european union and the industrialized powers must commit themselves to putting an end to the patent business and to allowing the production of medicines at affordable prices and costs.
mr president, promoting the support of the european union and its citizens for the united nations objectives of eradicating aids as a public health threat by the year 2030 is for me reason, but also excitement. because in the '80s, in bermeo, the little fishing village where i was born, this disease killed too many people with whom i shared the pulpit, adolescence, that i treated you. too many people who, in shared spaces and times, discovered the drug and suffered the disease, the death associated with those two fearsome syllables whispered at every funeral. but i also experienced a rebellion that was started by mothers, women, denunciation, social and institutional involvement, hope, rigour and victory. and i want the same opportunity, the same relief, for each and every one of us who face an enemy today already visible and known who can only rearm if we waste what we've already gained. aids today survives in poverty, with marginalization, with prejudice and with inequality. mostly a woman's face. and it's a ticking time bomb ambushed in what we call the third world, but also in eastern europe. let's deactivate it by avoiding the vetoes that fundamentalism wants to impose on the most active and useful associations at this summit; by 2030 at least 90% of those who are hiv positive know they are hiv positive, at least 90% of them are on treatment and 90% of those on treatment have an undetectable viral load. that's why i call for zero cuts against aids, active citizens, laws that do not make it harder for at-risk populations to access treatment, more equality, more empowered women and humanity. a final effort to achieve a goal that is within our reach.
member of the commission. – mr president, policy coherence for development is, indeed, of fundamental importance in our joint efforts to promote and support global sustainable development. ensuring that all european union policies contribute to our shared development objective is not only common sense but also a necessity. in the commission we have put policy coherence at the heart of our work, both in terms of ensuring coherence of our general policies and actions and in making sure that our policies indeed support our development cooperation objectives. but we cannot do this alone: we need to join forces. it is a shared responsibility. it is very encouraging to see this parliament’s strong interest in and support for policy coherence for development, as manifested by this debate. let me thank the rapporteur, mr preda, for steering the preparation of the report, which we welcome. the european parliament has a key role to play in making policy coherence for development a success. you have consistently underlined the importance of the topic, including by establishing the post of standing rapporteur and by issuing several important resolutions. this debate is both useful and very timely. it provides an important contribution not only in our daily business of implementing policy coherence for development but more importantly for the implementation of the watershed 2030 agenda for sustainable development. the universal character of the 2030 agenda marks a fundamental change of paradigm. it calls for a whole-of-government approach and for development sensitivity in policy making across a very broad range of inter-connected sectors. the most important challenge for all of us in this room and well beyond is to make it happen, putting all means at our disposal to good use. this is what we are currently working on in the context of the revision of the european consensus on development. a public consultation was launched last week and will be open until 21 august. we count very strongly on your input and support. despite some critical remarks, which we note and also appreciate, i welcome the overall positive assessment by this house of the commission’s work on policy coherence for development (pcd). we have made significant progress over the last years. let me give you some examples of where our work has successfully influenced political decision making in favour of development objectives. first, we have placed pcd firmly as a part of impact assessments within the better regulation framework. it is still early days, but the systematic development check, through development specific guidelines and a toolbox for assessing potential impacts when elaborating new initiatives, has the potential to be a game changer. we have introduced country-by-country reporting, increasing transparency in extractive industries. the last common agricultural policy reform of 2013 was mindful of potential trade distortions vis-à-vis developing countries. and, finally, the commission communication on ‘trade for all’, from october 2015, was drafted with significant pro-development considerations as guiding principles. in short, we are making progress and this is confirmed by the 2015 pcd report and by your report today. we should be encouraged by that. we should continue to step up our joint efforts to make full use of policy coherence for development as a tool for implementing the 2030 agenda and guaranteeing the shared prosperity of the european union and our partner countries.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. mr president, policy coherence beyond a principle enshrined in the treaty on the functioning of the european union and in the united nations' own sustainable development goals is pure common sense. consistency must or should be the cornerstone of all our foreign policy. some members of this house talk a lot about efficiency and effectiveness of resources, but, ladies and gentlemen, policy coherence is a key issue for efficiency. if we are not consistent in our external action, we are wasting the money for official development aid and deceiving the citizens who finance this aid with their taxes. because while we are allocating development aid, the rest of our policies, especially trade, continue to impoverish the countries of the south. and so, what we give with one hand we take away with the other. that is a totally cynical and hypocritical stance. it is now, with the sdgs approved, time to move from policy to action. the universal nature of the new development framework means that we, the developed countries, must put the emphasis on policy coherence. it is time to be ambitious, to go beyond fine words and to commit ourselves to really effective and above all binding measures, such as committing ourselves to international taxation, combating austerity policies and privatisation of public services, demanding civil and criminal liability from large companies and ending their unbearable impunity, reformulating trade and investment policy so that it is at the service of the people, or ensuring access to medicines as a universal and fundamental right. we are facing a very important opportunity for the european parliament to become aware of the principle of policy coherence for development and to call for the urgent need to take effective and, as i said, binding measures to ensure full compliance with article 208, which, ladies and gentlemen, we have given ourselves and are not fulfilling. it is regrettable to see how the conservative group and the people's group, through separate votes, are trying to dilute the most necessary elements of this report.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, after reading this report, i am struck, as a first impression, by the constant link that is made between development and security, often involving the european external action service in the middle. the report is also full of nice words and good intentions: it proposes, for example, impact assessments on the coherence of development policies, but without demanding any legally binding policy or decisions. the report also stresses the concern about the current migration crisis (as the report calls it) and proposes a security solution to this phenomenon, rather than addressing the causes of this increase in migration and, moreover, without taking into account the economic, cultural and social benefits that immigration brings to our countries, as various studies have shown. anyway, a lot of nice words and not so nice words and few acts. a "more of the same".
mr president, commissioner, the coherence of development policies is enshrined in the lisbon treaty and is therefore a constitutional mandate for the european union, something we are politically obliged to implement. however, this is not the case. we're not getting it started. each union policy is its own thing, and yet we need that coherence at institutional level within the union and in connection with national policies. we must strengthen our ties with national parliaments to monitor the development policies of their governments more closely. 2016 is a key year to get to work, because it's the year we have to start implementing the sustainable development goals. we must implement the decisions of the world humanitarian summit in istanbul and other commitments on the effectiveness of debt. here, as in the bible text, it is not proper for the left hand not to know what the right hand is doing. on the contrary, it is the two hands that have to work together on trade, development and taxation.

mr president, the chernobyl tragedy directly affected over two million belarusians and indirectly the whole planet. nuclear pollution knows no borders, it affects everyone and that is why we must have this debate. we seem to be failing to learn from our mistakes anywhere, when belarus is building a new nuclear power plant without carrying out the planned stress tests with the european commission and the necessary impact assessments. the commission would do well to urge belarus not to go down a path of which it is already aware and has already suffered, but above all it must contribute to a radical change in the energy model here in the european union. half of the world's nuclear power is produced in europe. we have the technology and the resources to change this model, and also examples like germany, which is already doing it. it is time for other countries to do the same and for the commission to push the member states along this path. let's start by setting an example. let us start by dismantling the power stations which have already outlived their useful life and are a potential danger, like garoña and almaraz in spain, and which pose a potential danger to our lives and to the earth.
in writing. technological solutions in agriculture have always created mechanisms of dependence of the farmer on large companies producing and selling plant protection products, seeds or chemical fertilizers. the challenge of feeding a growing world population is not to increase crop yields by more application of fertilizers, genetically modified organisms or more insecticide pressure, but to reduce food that is thrown away. the fao estimates that 33 percent of the food produced in the world ends up in the garbage. technical agriculture results in the offshoring of production from consumption centres, by the requirements of expansion and cheapening of labour, which means further destroying local jobs and increasing co2 emissions. in a world transitioning to energy sustainability, it's time for agriculture to start its journey towards truly sustainable production, and organic farming is the future of sustainable production. furthermore, growing continuously despite the economic climate, both in number of farmers and in area, driven by an increasingly responsible citizenship, makes organic farming the environmentally sustainable solution that europe must promote.
madam president, we are talking about something as important to agriculture as innovation. this is certainly one more element, but not the only one, in the attempt to get the sector out of the crisis in which it is immersed and in which the policies adopted by the european commission have a lot to do with. innovation can have many perspectives, and that is why i would like to thank the rapporteur for making it clear that innovation and sustainability are not at odds. innovation also means committing ourselves to an agriculture that is less dependent on agrochemicals, that allows the farmer to be more independent and produce cheaper and that takes advantage of all that respect for biodiversity provides us. to commit to sustainable agriculture is not to go back to the past. it is to look to the future with responsibility, with research and with the aim of making effective and sustainable agriculture a secure and permanent source of food. probably the most revolutionary and the most innovative thing is to re-take all the power that nature gives us and that we have been so long estranged from.

member of the commission. madam president, mr rapporteur, ladies and gentlemen, i am delighted to be here today to debate the proposal for a directive on tax evasion. step by step, and we also see it, debate by debate, we are moving towards a profoundly renewed, more modern and also more ethical european tax landscape. i have already had the opportunity to put a proposal before you and will not go into further detail. i simply want to remind you of our political objective - and i know how much the european parliament shares it - to put an end, quite simply, to tax evasion in the european union. the current situation, in which some companies can avoid paying their fair share of taxes in the union, is simply not tenable any more. like you, i was shocked by the new revelations in the press about the panama papers and, as you pointed out, the news provides us with more every day. like you, i know that the citizens of europe have had enough and, like you, i feel a deep sense of urgency to act. that is why, from the beginning of its mandate, this commission has been constantly working to reform the taxation of our companies and will continue to do so until the end of its mandate. i now turn to mr bayet's report. this excellent report recognises the directive as a positive step in the fight against tax evasion, and i welcome that. i thank all those who have contributed to its drafting and, of course, i congratulate the rapporteur first. this report proposes a number of amendments. i shall briefly review some of them, but i will not go into them in detail. firstly, to emphasize that in many cases the commission fully agrees with the points suggested. secondly, we believe that the objectives pursued by certain amendments would be better addressed in the context of other initiatives or other instruments. many of these relate to issues covered by previous or lateral initiatives of the commission. i will take two examples, if i may, mr rapporteur. the june 2015 action plan first confirmed that the commission will provide guidance to member states for adopting the so-called modified link approach for the patent-friendly tax system. it also indicated that the transfer pricing rules should be adapted. the directive on tax evasion discussed this morning does not therefore appear to be the right legislative instrument to deal with these issues. at that time the commission had chosen to follow a non-binding approach and we still believe that this approach is sufficient to achieve our objectives. however, the commission has made it clear, and i repeat it here, that it could consider legislating on these matters, as you have suggested, if necessary, but again in a legislative instrument that would be different from this directive. second example: you propose that the question of tax havens be dealt with in the framework of this directive. to be frank, we do not think this is desirable, not that we do not want to fight tax havens; the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat tax havens, and i am sure that the commission will take them into account in its proposals for the future. however, as you know, the commission has also initially opted for a non-binding approach. the external strategy we recently adopted has thus defined a common approach to assess, list and, where appropriate, sanction third countries which refuse to apply internationally defined tax rules. we are working to establish, in a short time, a european blacklist of tax havens - which does not exist today and which is needed - with common methods, common approaches and common sanctions. i welcome the support given by the member states to our proposal for a blacklist, with the selection of a first set of countries this summer. i therefore agree with you on the objective, the aim, the ambition and the requirement. i think that again is an approach which must be disjointed or dealt with elsewhere or otherwise. as you know, this text is currently being discussed in the council. we had a first meeting at the last ecofin council, which allowed us to both note a number of points of agreement and to see in which areas we still needed to make progress in order to reach an agreement. the council has also amended the proposal in some respects in the way suggested by this house. i am thinking, for example, of removing the rule of limitation of interest from public infrastructure projects or introducing a definition of associated enterprises. the commission approves these changes, which are undoubtedly improvements to the proposal and are included in your report. again, this is a sign of its quality. i want to make my position very clear here: we need an agreement and we need it now. we must seize the opportunity of the dutch presidency, which has been ambitious and vigorous in this matter. we must also take into account the political situation we are in, in the wake of the panama papers, to conclude now. i do not want this debate to be sandblasted or to take any longer. the member states are very close to an agreement, in fact. i therefore welcome the timing of this debate, because i think it is an opportunity for parliament to send a very clear and very strong message to the finance ministers of the 28 member states. you must always remember - and you are even better placed than i am to know this - that although the commission proposes and parliament legislates or makes decisions, the member states have a power of decision, including blocking, which must be reversed. the political pressure we exert together is extremely important in this respect. the message you are sending, as i understand it, mr rapporteur, ladies and gentlemen, is that the rapid adoption of this directive, namely next week, at the ecofin council, to be held on 17 june in luxembourg, is essential to better combat tax evasion. we have a sort of obligation to succeed. that is how i understand this report. these are the main points i wanted to make today, as a quick introduction to our debate. the time does not allow me, in this introductory speech, to go over each of the amendments contained in your report, but of course we can discuss them in more detail in this debate, to which i am ready as always, with the conviction that the commission and the european parliament are, in this fight against tax evasion, partners who share the same aim and the same will.
i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr moscovici, for his report, and i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr cervantes, for his report. you see, this is a key economic and political issue at the moment we are living, and of the greatest importance for the system on which we all base the european construction, which is liberal democracy, because civil society - and we are the highest representatives of civil society - can no longer tolerate the lack of ethics in certain business. the european parliament, therefore, mr commissioner, sends you and the council a very strong message, a very strong support for all that is being done to rationalize and make the functioning of the economy more ethical in this respect, in which, indeed, the commission has recently shown itself sensitive to popular indignation. i would therefore like to say that, beyond the technical terms which mr bayet has very well explained here, and on which we have fortunately reached agreement with a large majority of the house, we must also understand what is at stake. because sometimes it is said that this is against the companies, that this is an anti-business attitude. we are not going to go against the companies. you're not going to get away with this. but it is a question of companies, at best centring more and more investment - as has been said here - linked to production, linked to their real activity, than paying large law firms. it is not only to combat evasion and fraud; it is also to combat avoidance. that's what we want to stop. and, while we make these large companies focus more on production, we are fairer to all medium or small companies that do not have the option of finding investment in law firms to escape tax networks. that is what it is all about, to protect a greater competitiveness and a greater efficiency of our companies at the same time that, if we can collect a little more, the tax burden will be more just and will have a better response from the potentiality of the agents and the taxes. that is what it is all about, it has nothing to do with attacking companies. it is a question of making europe more just, more ethical, but also more efficient, and that is what we are asking for with all our force, mr commissioner.
madam president, commissioner, the economic crisis has required very considerable efforts on the part of the european citizens. in this context, the fight against tax avoidance - particularly by large multinationals - must be a top priority for the european institutions. these practices reduce government revenues, revenues that could be earmarked for education, health or public investment. and not only that: tax avoidance by multinationals leaves small and mediumsized enterprises, which are undoubtedly the engines of growth and job creation, in a much more unfavourable position. in this sense, the european union is actively working to promote the measures needed to reduce the so-called fiscal gap, and we must continue in this direction. i have no doubt. i would like to thank the european commission and its commissioner moscovici for their proposal here today, and i would ask the council to look up and listen to this house. the oecd has been working for the last few years on the so-called beps project. the oecd and g20 countries have committed themselves to the project and have made a political commitment to adopt its conclusions. let's do this, your honor. the directive we are discussing today is an appropriate instrument for transposing the conclusions and recommendations of the oecd beps programme in a coordinated and coherent way throughout the european union. we must all - i repeat, we must all - show our commitment to actively cooperate in the promotion of these measures.
madam president, commissioner, maintaining the capacity of our institutions to make policy, to promote productive investment and innovation, to maintain the european social model means ending tax avoidance, through what we call aggressive tax planning, and enabling companies to pay their taxes where they make profits. a coordinated and harmonised approach to the functioning of tax systems, integrating all tax administrations, is also needed. when i say all, i also mean the regional systems which meet the criteria of the luxembourg court of justice to be considered autonomous systems because they have institutional, regulatory and economic autonomy. the proximity of these systems has been shown to promote control, prevent corruption, support the real economy and is an effective antidote to deficits which occur more easily in those administrations which have less responsibility for their revenue than they do for their expenditure. let us bring up strategic coordination and approaches, and below, experiences that have proved their usefulness and we will move in the right direction. it is not acceptable that many multinationals pay tribute to the letter, that public administrations lose between one hundred and two hundred and forty billion a year in this way. to put an end to this we need another fiscal governance at european level. it requires the clear and unconditional commitment of the 28 member states and, in line with the answer given to our question on the fiscalis programme, also the autonomous regional tax authorities, such as the basque concert or the navarre convention, which show their commitment to our objectives.
mr. president, i'm sorry for your words. the billions that are lost every year are jobs, schools, hospitals, public housing that will never be built. an organized robbery of the rich from the poor and the working classes, on whom the tax burden ultimately falls. today's report is right to point out the mechanisms which facilitate this avoidance at international level: the false transparency of tax havens, the complicity of double taxation treaties. but in its concrete aspects the improvements it proposes are very modest. we would like to see the minimum tax rate for companies established abroad set at 15%. but it's not enough. nor are we satisfied with the indifference to the tax avoidance of companies within the european union itself. and worse, it is endorsed that it is the haciendas complicit in tax evasion and even tax avoidance - as demonstrated by today's revelations about the bourbons - that certify that risky practices, such as asset transfers from one country to another, should not be taxed, or the perception that foreign income should not be taxed either. the final result is uneven and not satisfactory; it only adds gaps where there should be an effective commitment to link production and taxation. we are again sending a disappointing signal to the people of europe.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the protocol on the elimination of illicit trade in tobacco products of the framework convention on tobacco control of the world health organisation (fctc). i have done so because it is the first global health treaty. it was developed in response to the global tobacco epidemic and aims to address some of its causes, including illicit trade in tobacco products. it entered into force on 27 february 2005 and to date 180 parties have acceded to it. illicit trade in tobacco products, in particular cigarette smuggling, is a criminal activity that poses a serious threat to public health, as it undermines tobacco control policies and facilitates access to tobacco products that are often cheaper. in addition, it causes huge revenue losses for the union as a result of unpaid taxes and customs duties. it is estimated that the union and the member states lose more than eur 10 billion each year.

in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products of the who tobacco control convention. it is the first global health treaty. the protocol is the world's leading initiative in this field and also includes a complex set of measures, rules and policies in the field of combating illicit trade in tobacco products. it aims to improve the security of the tobacco supply chain, tobacco products and manufacturing equipment by creating a global tracking and tracing regime. the rapporteur supports the view that ratification of the protocol will benefit public health and contribute to the international fight against illicit tobacco trade, tax evasion and organised crime.
in writing. ‒ the world health assembly adopted the framework convention on tobacco control (fctc) in 2003, which aims to reduce tobacco-related deaths and diseases globally. this protocol, which builds on and complements article 15 of the fctc, which seeks to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products, such as smuggling, illicit manufacture and counterfeiting, is an essential component of tobacco control, and obliges the parties to adopt and implement effective measures to eliminate illicit trade, which is why i have supported its ratification. illicit trade in tobacco products, and in particular smuggling of cigarettes from third countries into or within the eu, is a criminal activity that causes huge revenue losses for the eu and its member states as a result of unpaid taxes and customs duties, estimated at over eur 10 billion per year. the tobacco products directive already contains provisions on tracking and tracing which were developed in line with the fctc protocol.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation whereby parliament gives its consent to enhanced cooperation in two regulations establishing a common european framework for the rules applicable to property regimes in international marriages or civil partnerships. the decision to use enhanced cooperation in the area of competition, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions on international couple's matrimonial property regimes, both in the area of matrimonial property regimes and the property consequences of registered partnerships, follows the stagnation of negotiations between member states on the initial proposals made by the commission in 2011. in a decision of december 2015, the council recognised that unanimity among the 28 member states was not possible for the adoption of the two regulations. eighteen member states asked the commission to propose a text for a decision authorising enhanced cooperation between them to regulate uniformly the property regimes of international couples, a proposal which it submitted at the beginning of the year. the recommendation is strictly formal and merely gives its consent to the procedure, since parliament will later vote on the commission's proposal for regulations.
in writing. ‒ this report authorises enhanced cooperation in the field of competition, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions on the matrimonial property regime and the property consequences of registered partnerships. i voted in favour of it because it will make it easier to recognise the marriage arrangements of crossborder couples.
in writing. ‒ a number of studies have highlighted the high number of transnational couples in the union and the practical and legal difficulties these couples face, both in the day-to-day management of their assets and in their division when the couple separates or one of their members dies. these difficulties are often the result of the wide disparity in the applicable rules, both substantive and private international law, governing the property effects of marriage. the aim of this proposal is therefore to establish a clear legal framework in the european union for the determination of jurisdiction and the law applicable to matrimonial property regimes and to facilitate the circulation between member states of decisions and other acts in this field.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the enhanced cooperation recommendation, considering that 23 member states agree in principle to adopt these acts, which do not harm the internal market or economic, social and territorial cohesion, do not constitute a barrier to or discrimination in trade between member states, and do not distort competition between them. the acts to be adopted shall not infringe the rights of non-participating member states. this enhanced cooperation in the area of the property rights of international couples is clearly in line with the objectives of the union and is in the interest of its citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because its purpose is to give the council its consent to the opening of enhanced cooperation in the field of competition, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions in property regimes of international couples, covering matters of matrimonial regimes and the property consequences of registered unions. these measures will make it easier for international couples to manage their affairs.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because since 2013 there has been an overall eu strategy to fight cigarette smuggling which proposes action in four key areas: (a) reducing incentives to smuggle; (b) improving supply chain security (in particular by ratifying the cmct protocol); (c) strengthening enforcement by tax, customs, police and border control authorities; (d) strengthening sanctions. the union has also strengthened the legislative base with the tobacco products directive, complemented by binding and enforceable anti-fraud agreements concluded between the union and the member states, on the one hand, and the four major tobacco manufacturers, on the other (philip morris, japan tobacco international, british american tobacco holdings limited, and imperial tobacco limited). it is therefore an international agreement which develops and complements article 15 of the cmct and is currently the only multilateral regulatory initiative in this field. the commission has participated in the negotiations of the cmct protocol on behalf of the union.

in writing. ‒ the anderson report calls for the adoption of the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the union, of the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products to the who framework convention on tobacco control, as regards its provisions on obligations relating to judicial cooperation in criminal matters and the definition of criminal offences. the stated objective of the protocol is to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products. this is done by targeting the supply chain of tobacco products through a range of government measures, for example, a comprehensive tracking and tracing regime, prevention of money laundering, the introduction of licensing and record keeping, and regulation of internet sales, duty-free sales and international transit. it also aims to encourage and strengthen international cooperation, the exchange of valid information, police and technical cooperation and mutual legal and administrative assistance. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ i am in favour of this report for a number of reasons. firstly, the illicit trade in tobacco poses a threat to public health, as it undermines tobacco control policies and in turn encourages the entry of new, cheaper tobacco products, which hinders the responsible competition sought by the euro area institutions. this illegal activity also causes a large loss of revenue for the union as a result of non-payment of the taxes established, as it is estimated that member states lose more than eur 10 billion each year. i am confident that through effort and coordination between member states we will succeed in overcoming this obstacle which is so damaging to the tobacco industry in europe and to other parties concerned, in order to ensure fair and transparent trade within the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, mainly because it approves the delay, by one year, of its implementation, which will not be effective until 2018. this delay in its implementation is not accidental and is in line with the interests of the sector. despite the complexities created by the financial sector, with the connivance of member states, which have completely deregulated the financial sector, political will is needed to end the opaque and speculative practices that prevail in the sector. the delay of one year in the implementation of this directive will allow the main financial institutions to continue operating in the opaque world of speculative operations to which they are accustomed, without having to comply with any regulation. these speculative activities have resulted in the explosion of the crisis that europe has been facing since 2008 and, in order to tackle it, it is necessary to put an end to these practices. because to approve this delay undermines the credibility of this institution, which claims to be trying to find solutions to the crisis, that is why i have decided to vote against it.

in writing. ‒ i have supported this report because it proposes, broadly speaking: - a more dynamic correlation of policies and actions between the sdgs and the cdp. - greater involvement of local and regional governments, civil society organisations and expert groups. - setting quality objectives and developing clearer indicators for dpc. - ex ante impact assessments and the establishment of a complaint mechanism. - more resources in the union delegations and in the focal points of national ministries to implement national and european strategies in terms of cpd. - a specific european council on the cfp and its coordination with the sdgs. the eu's external relations are now more closely linked to the eu's external relations, and the eu's external relations are more closely linked to the eu's external relations.
in writing. ‒ the principle of coherence for development, first enshrined in european law in 1992, states that no union policy, whether trade, economic or migration, can be contrary to international development objectives. although i regard it as positive, i have not been able to support this report because it contains a constant link between security and development and a greater inclusion of the union's external action service in development policies. similarly, all references to the need for assessments of the impact of union policies in third countries should have been in line with making them binding and mandatory. on the other hand, i do not share his approach to the migration phenomenon, which focuses on the security aspects and not on the human right of every person to migrate. however, the report contains positive elements such as the need to improve coordination between the union's institutions and also between them and the member states in order to improve compliance with this principle, which should be at the heart of any union policy.
in writing. ‒ one of the biggest challenges we have in the field of development cooperation is the coherence between our policies. although positive steps have been taken, we are still far from achieving real coherence between the policies that most affect development, international trade, foreign affairs, financial and agricultural policy. the report is critical of the current situation and contains some interesting initiatives. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ considering that the union must take the lead in promoting policy coherence for development, as stated in article 208 of the treaty of lisbon, we voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the european commission to effectively step up its efforts through concrete measures to coordinate and coherence its external policies so that they are aligned with the union's objectives (eradicating poverty and reducing inequalities).
in writing. ‒ i supported this report on policy coherence for development, which stresses the need to put more emphasis on institutional coordination, both between the eu institutions and with the member states. in addition, an adequate level of resources and staff will be necessary for the proper development of policy coherence for development. moreover, it should not be forgotten that aid alone is not enough and it is considered necessary to take into account innovative and diversified sources of funding such as the financial transaction tax, the carbon tax, the solidarity tax on airline tickets and the income from natural resources, among others.
in writing. ‒ as the lisbon treaty states, the eu must ensure coherence in development policies in order to link internal and external policies more effectively. following the adoption of the 2030 agenda on sustainable development goals (sdgs), there is a need for the eu to continue to take into account the new development goals set out in its policies and to continue to generate synergies between its policies, to benefit developing countries and to increase the effectiveness of cooperation. this report proposes greater involvement of regional and local governments as well as civil society organisations to help with these issues. it also proposes setting quality objectives and developing clearer indicators to assess the coherence of development policies. in line with the proposals, it is called for the european union delegations in third countries to be given more resources to enable them to carry out these tasks and to strengthen the dpc as one of the key elements of foreign policy, and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the coherence of european policy and the search for a more prosperous and dynamic future for the european union will require a thorough reform of the european budget, which cannot continue to depend on member states' contributions alone. it is important to incorporate new revenue in order to move towards a union capable of absorbing economic disruption and offering a minimum degree of income convergence. the reason why i voted against paragraph 30 is not because of the specific use that the financial transaction tax or the co2 tax is intended to make, but because i believe that the revenue from these taxes should be used to create a more effective european budget.
in writing. ‒ the principle of coherence for development, first enshrined in european law in 1992, states that no union policy, whether trade, economic or migration, can be contrary to international development objectives. although i regard it as positive, i have not been able to support this report because it contains a constant link between security and development and a greater inclusion of the union's external action service in development policies. similarly, all references to the need for assessments of the impact of union policies in third countries should have been in line with making them binding and mandatory. on the other hand, i do not share his approach to the migration phenomenon, which focuses on the security aspects and not on the human right of every person to migrate. however, the report contains positive elements such as the need to improve coordination between the union's institutions and also between them and the member states in order to improve compliance with this principle, which should be at the heart of any union policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i am convinced that pro-development policies are essential and indispensable, and that they are the responsibility of all eu countries. in 2015, there was a positive development in development policy as the sustainable development goals were adopted. now it's time to move from words to deeds. the eu must continue to work to improve the effectiveness and coherence of development policies.
in writing. ‒ this report on the coherence of development policies is nothing but a moralizing text that announces great intentions without ever calling into question the failure of development policies of the past decades. while some principles seem to be contrary to common sense (for example, aid to fix populations by development), the report has clear anti-sovereignty intentions: the adoption of a binding legal act to integrate the member states into the cpd, in particular. moreover, the mention of 'new budget appropriations' makes it clear that once again it is the member states that will have to pay for the change, and not the adjustment of european policies. for these reasons i opposed this text.
in writing. ‒ considering that the union must take the lead in promoting policy coherence for development, as stated in article 208 of the treaty of lisbon, we voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the european commission to effectively step up its efforts through concrete measures to coordinate and coherence its external policies so that they are aligned with the union's objectives (eradicating poverty and reducing inequalities).
in writing. ‒ policy coherence for development (pcd) is a simple but powerful premise: no policies should detract from a country’s international development goals. this pcd report takes into account the outcomes of the september 2015 un summit, where the 2030 agenda for sustainable development was formally adopted, including a target to ‘enhance policy coherence for sustainable development’ (target17.14). hence, the report reiterates that pcd is a key element for delivering and achieving the new sustainable development agenda and calls for proactive action based on a common understanding of pcd, while pointing out that a hhrr-based approach should lead to a deepened understanding of pcd. moreover the report acknowledges the impact of trade and investment issues and recalls that trade liberalisation is not per se positive for poverty eradication, since it can have negative effects on sustainable development; and notes the importance of development effectiveness and of gender equality and focused on migration-related issues. nonetheless, the report contains some references to the security and development and poverty eradication nexus that, although being framed on the pcd logic, are problematic for eh bildu as we aren’t in favour of the cfsp and militarisation in general; and hence we have abstained in the final vote.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. some other political groups’ attempts to weaken the report failed, except on one request unfortunately, namely its calls for a un body on tax matters to enable developing countries to participate on equal footing in the global reform of existing international tax rules. nevertheless, paragraphs that highlight the challenge of harmful tax competition; the need to develop innovative sources of financing (through an ftt; carbon tax; ticket levy; rents from natural resources, etc.) were maintained, as in the case of the paragraph that trade liberalisation is not per se positive for poverty eradication.
in writing. ‒ this report takes stock of progress made in development policies, identifies areas where existing mechanisms can be improved and stimulates debate on the future of development at european level, calling for development policies to be discussed and coordinated at community level and between member states, highlighting the need to promote interinstitutional debate between the commission, the eeas, the council and the european parliament, as well as debate at national level. we are talking about a constructive report and it has been the subject of a broad consensus, so i think it is necessary to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it highlights several critical aspects of the new partnership for food security and nutrition in africa, which was sponsored and promoted in 2012 as a mega public-private agreement and which has led to structural liberalisation reforms in african countries, being one of the main mechanisms responsible for land grabbing, marginalisation of small producers and support for an unsustainable model of agriculture and livestock farming, contrary to the principles of food sovereignty. the report also criticises the negative impact on the development of public-private partnerships and, although it does not reject them, it does include the need for strict regulation. another positive aspect is the call for support for local economies and small farms, the references to the positive aspects of agroecology and the commitment to support these practices with an explicit rejection of the introduction of gmos in africa. the report also makes clear the need to combat land grabbing by recognising traditional forms of community ownership of land, including the rights of indigenous peoples.
in writing. ‒ considering that the new partnership for food security and nutrition in africa aims to improve food security and nutrition, helping 50 million people in sub-saharan africa to escape poverty by 2020; and that the participating countries have negotiated national cooperation frameworks, setting out commitments to facilitate private investment in the agricultural sector in africa, we voted in favour of this resolution, which warns of the risks of the role that the private sector can play in this regard if it is not well regulated.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on the new alliance for food security and nutrition by the committee on development. agricultural investment policies are mostly focused on large-scale land acquisitions and export-oriented agriculture that is rarely linked to local economies. rural communities, agricultural workers, small farmers, fishermen and indigenous peoples have been deprived of their right to participate in the decision-making process of cooperation. i have voted for others to urge the g8 member states not to support the cultivation of genetically modified organisms in africa.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the new alliance for food security and nutrition which aims, through increased private investment and the stimulation of agricultural growth, to lift 50 million people out of poverty in africa by 2022. the initiative, which already covers 10 african states, will involve an investment of $10 billion and will call for major changes in different regulations to encourage investment. the instruments used to promote development will include the design of cooperation agreements, the creation of new tools to mobilise private capital and the formulation of national investment plans.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report with the firm conviction that the food crisis in many countries can be remedied by the means at our disposal. initiatives such as this, where public-private cooperation for a larger goal is paramount, should be supported by the eu.
in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition (nasan) is a broad public-private partnership including the g8, the african union and 180 companies. this is an african agricultural development programme that has involved about ten countries since 2012. this program promotes unsustainable agriculture on the model of the one that wreaked havoc in asia in the 1970s. however, in this model, smallholders no longer survive. this is why this report seeks to stimulate family farming and the local economy by combating both farmer poverty and food security. the report also defends proximity by favouring short-distance transport and local agriculture. it promotes security of supply by limiting the import of foodstuffs in favour of local foodstuffs in a spirit of self-sufficiency. this security of supply would help to solve the problem of african migration to the european union. in addition, it would enable them to obtain quality products at affordable prices. the report also denounces the fight against the excessive use of plant protection products and fertilizers, which are washing away the soil and causing ecological disasters. for all these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. attempts to weaken the report through split/separate failed. the report sends strong criticisms on mega ppp and covers strong provisions regarding land grab. it warns against pure focus on land titling to ensure land tenure security, but calls for the respect of fao land tenure guidelines. it calls for ex ante impact study on land rights and implementation of free, prior and informed consent (fpic), which shall be obtained from all communities concerned by transfer/control of land prior to the development of the project by the private sector. it also calls on participating countries to new alliance to enact binding legislation against land grabbing. food sovereignty is acknowledged, and the right of african countries to protect their agriculture through tariff and tax regimes is equally acknowledged.
in writing. ‒ the document highlights the need for investment policies in africa to be linked to supporting the development of the local economy, including smallholder farmers and family farms, to help reduce poverty, hunger and malnutrition. it also calls on african governments to invest in local food systems, to boost rural economies, secure decent jobs and labour rights. that is why i think it is necessary to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains positive references to understanding international accounting standards as a public good, it does not go sufficiently into the necessary public regulation. international accounting standards are standards set by the private sector, which have allowed the development of the speculative bubbles that have led to the current financial crisis. this shows the need for public control over these standards and the need for democratic organisations to set them. despite some positive references, the report does not go into the necessary and immediate public involvement in the determination of these and that is why i could not vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this report, which seeks to harmonise common accounting standards for companies at european level. while i am not opposed to this process, the report does include positive references to processes which i am opposed to, such as the capital markets union, which is why i have abstained.
in writing. ‒ international financial reporting standards (ifrs) and international auditing standards (ias) are a necessary component for the efficient functioning of the internal market and capital markets. both rules are in the public interest, aim to enhance accountability, protect investments, provide transparency and enable investors and other market participants to make informed economic decisions, and should therefore not jeopardise financial stability or hamper economic development. in this report, which i have supported, parliament welcomes the report on the assessment of the ias prepared by the commission on the application of ifrs standards in the union and welcomes the conclusion that the objectives of the ias regulation have been achieved. regrets, however, that the commission has not yet proposed the legal changes required to address the identified shortcomings and urges it to submit legislative proposals with diligence and to comply with the maystadt recommendation on the extension of the 'public interest' criterion, i.e. that accounting rules should not jeopardise the financial stability of the union or hamper its economic development.

in writing. ‒ international accounting standards are an essential component necessary for the efficient functioning of the internal market and capital markets. while the evaluation has shown that the objectives of the regulation have been achieved, this report establishes the need for the commission to propose the legal changes necessary to correct the shortcomings identified in the commission's evaluation. we are therefore talking about a report which acknowledges the progress made in the rules and at the same time proposes actions for improvement, and i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ this report on peace support operations aims to increase the eu's contribution to peace operations, and collaboration with the un and the african union. the report calls on member states to significantly increase their contributions of military and police personnel to un missions. i am opposed to this report because, among other things, it calls for the eu to make greater efforts to strengthen international security, and maintains that european security must be the principle of eu interventions. furthermore, the report fails to acknowledge the negative role and destabilisation that 'good western' operations have brought to different parts of the world, and fails to take into account that many of the missions carried out in recent years by the eu have not been at all successful in terms of long-term peace and stability of the countries. for all these reasons, i have voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i abstain in voting on this resolution because, while i recognise the importance of developing certain peace and crisis management missions with eu participation, which have managed to save hundreds of thousands of human lives, i am opposed to the systematic use of the military route for crisis and conflict management, and what this entails in terms of diverting european funds that should be focused on the development of african countries. i believe that peace on the continent cannot depend so much on the presence of foreign troops in these countries and on short-term plans of action as on a structural and comprehensive response based on the revision of the terms of trade, the strengthening through enhanced cooperation of productive and technological capacities and the formulation of development plans adapted to the needs and capacities of the populations of these countries.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on peace support operations as regards the eu's engagement with the united nations and the african union. the importance of the union's instruments in the field of security and in the missions and operations of the common security and defence policy is underlined. strengthening european military cooperation would improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the european contribution to un peacekeeping missions. in addition, a comprehensive approach by the union must be supported, which is the main instrument for mobilising the union's full potential for action in the context of peacekeeping operations and the stabilisation process, as well as for activating different avenues of development support for the african union countries.
in writing. ‒ peace support operations (psos) are a form of crisis response, usually in support of an internationally recognised organisation such as the united nations or the african union (au), with a un mandate, and intended to prevent armed conflict, restore or maintain or consolidate peace, ensure respect for peace agreements and deal with emergency situations. as this report, which i supported, points out, the security landscape has changed dramatically in the last decade, particularly in africa, with the emergence of terrorist and insurgent groups in somalia, nigeria and the sahel-sahara region, and with peacekeeping and counter-terrorism operations now the norm rather than the exception in many areas. the report urges the eu to continue its support for the paos and stresses the need for the eu and its member states not to act in isolation, but to take account of the contributions of other international actors, improve coordination with them, speed up their response and focus their efforts on certain priority countries.
in writing. ‒ this report on peace support operations aims to increase the eu's contribution to peace operations, and collaboration with the un and the african union. the report calls on member states to significantly increase their contributions of military and police personnel to un missions. i am opposed to this report because, among other things, it calls for the eu to make greater efforts to strengthen international security, and maintains that european security must be the principle of eu interventions. furthermore, the report fails to acknowledge the negative role and destabilisation that 'good western' operations have brought to different parts of the world, and fails to take into account that many of the missions carried out in recent years by the eu have not been at all successful in terms of long-term peace and stability of the countries. for all these reasons, i have voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the basis that peace support operations (psos) are a way of responding to crises, usually in support of an internationally recognised organisation, and of contributing to creating stable, secure and more prosperous environments in the long term. the eu has been a forerunner of peace since its foundation, and it is precisely for this fundamental objective that we must actively combat any alteration of this principle.
in writing. ‒ the van orden report on peace support operations offers operational recommendations on missions in africa. these recommendations concern the military and diplomatic means to be used, the exchange of intelligence and technology, the training of personnel, logistical support and the financial assistance that european countries provide or should provide to un and african union operations. france is particularly concerned, with operations such as serval in mali and sangaris in the central african republic. while only 5% of un peacekeepers are from european countries - 5,000 troops out of a total of 92,000 - france trains 25,000 african troops each year and at the same time deploys more than 4,000 men in peacekeeping operations in africa. the french example shows that the european union's action is marginal: it is up to the member states to decide whether or not to commit themselves financially or militarily to resolving these conflicts. in reality, the european union's intervention in this area should be outlawed, so that it does not hinder decision-making and feed unnecessary bureaucracy.

in writing. ‒ we discussed a report highlighting the strategic partnership in peacekeeping and crisis management operations and its priorities for the period 2015-2018, highlighting the contribution of the eu and its member states to the un peacekeeping budget (approximately 37%) and the need for member states to increase their military and police contribution to un peacekeeping operations. we are talking about a balanced report which comes at an important time, given the instability in several african countries. that is why i think it is appropriate to vote in favour of it.
mr president, i abstained on the report on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain because we have to strengthen farmers and livestock farmers against the defaults and price manipulations of the wholesale food distribution, and that cannot be achieved without binding measures. price volatility and falling farm incomes pose a serious threat to the agri-food sector, but the abuses of distribution chains occur within the framework of the european agricultural policy itself, which has intensified competition between farmers by deregulating european production and liberalising global trade. it is these deliberately created conditions which have permanently destabilised agricultural markets and created a structural imbalance between small agricultural producers and large distributors, who are doubly favoured by trade liberalisation. only a return to a cap based on production rather than the market can guarantee a lasting solution to the price crisis in the countryside.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because we socialists are calling for firm and consistent measures to be taken to eradicate once and for all these practices in the food supply chain in the eu, which are the result of economic imbalances in trade relations and differences in bargaining power between the various actors in the chain. the report also calls for the eu to be able to take action to combat unfair trading practices and ensure that european farmers and consumers have the opportunity to benefit from fair conditions of sale and purchase, as voluntary schemes have proved to be insufficient. such legislation should not reduce the level of protection of countries which already have national legislation on the fight against unfair business-to-business trading practices. there are member states which are already regulating such practices at national level, so if we do not do this at eu level we will create distortions in the internal market. as a social democrat, i believe that the solution to this problem is regulation.
in writing. ‒ although i am in favour of the general outline of this report, my final vote was for abstention, because i consider that it does not provide binding elements to set limits on the actions of large multinationals, in order to curb unfair practices in the food supply chain. it is therefore a report with good words but a difficult direct applicability.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this report because it introduces anti-abuse measures for producers and consumers to try to remedy a number of practices that act against small producers. the report also calls on the commission to promote cooperation and legislation at european level. the epp amendments to the text go further in this direction but i maintain discrepancies in form. this report recognises the need for greater cooperation between the weakest links in the food sector and proposes solutions which i believe address the problem. the report was unanimously approved in committee and the amendments by our shadow rapporteur were included, so i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain and the two amendments tabled by the committee on agriculture and rural development, stating that framework legislation at union level is considered necessary to tackle unfair trading practices and ensure that european farmers and consumers have the possibility to benefit from fair conditions of sale and purchase, and that such legislation should not reduce the level of protection of countries that already have national legislation on the fight against unfair trading practices between companies.

in writing. ‒ large retailers, in the absence of any reaction from the public authorities, have acquired a dominant position and have progressively marginalised small businesses. they have also imposed unfair trade practices on small producers. the report presented seeks to defend small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) against these unfair practices by establishing a code of conduct which is relatively binding on the giants of the retail sector. that is why i voted for this report. however, it is regrettable that the unfair competition suffered by our companies as a result of the opening of the frontiers is not mentioned. yet this competition, coupled with deregulation, has upset the balance and destroyed jobs.

in writing. ‒ i support this report. unfair trading practices (utps) are a serious problem, occurring in many sectors of the economy. utps occur where there are inequalities in trading relations between partners in the food supply chain, resulting from bargaining power disparities in business relations, which are the result of the growing concentration of market power among a small number of multinational groups, and these disparities tend to harm small and medium-sized producers. utps can have harmful consequences for the individual entities in the food supply chain, particularly in the case of farmers and smes, which in turn can have an impact on the entire eu economy.

in writing. - we are talking about a matter of vital importance. producers cannot be the main ones affected by price volatility. we cannot tolerate unfair trading practices in the food supply chain which end up harming the weakest link in the chain: the producers. we must make our opposition to such practices clear in this report. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it presents many arguments which i strongly oppose. for example, it uses the promotion of new technologies to justify the intensification and increased industrialization of agriculture, it supports new breeding techniques which are nothing but new gmos which are being tried to be introduced through the back door, and it uses the increase in world population as an argument to justify the increase in productivity, placing on europe the task of feeding the world, instead of opting for the food sovereignty of the peoples.
in writing. ‒ i voted against because i do not share the philosophy and rhetoric of the report, according to which the eu must intensify its agricultural production through greater technological harvesting, in order to produce more and export to third countries without the capacity to feed their own population. i reject the logic in the report that the increase in the world population justifies an intensification of agriculture in the european union. on the contrary, i think that the eu should promote a transfer of knowledge to these third countries, which serves to stimulate production at source, allowing all peoples to move towards their own food sovereignty.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on technological solutions for sustainable agriculture in the eu, which states that it is considered essential to maintain and develop the yield of local species, given their ability to adapt to the characteristics of their native environment, and that, in order to ensure the genetic diversity of european agriculture, the right of farmers to obtain plants autonomously and to store and exchange seeds of different species and varieties is respected. i also voted against the paragraph which states that it is essential not to hinder the application of high-precision improvement techniques or the carrying out of experiments with such techniques without a valid justification and that legislation should be adapted to the aims pursued so as not to be outdated or burdensome.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which focuses on the challenges facing agriculture in the coming years and how technology-based solutions can contribute to more sustainable agriculture in a context of increasing production demand and increasing scarcity of natural resources. the report stresses the need to allocate funds to research, especially in the framework of the european innovation partnership, skills development and knowledge transfer. it also defends genetic diversity as the key to sustainable agriculture and warns against soil degradation as a serious problem for agriculture, calling for efforts to improve soil and water use management.
