in writing. ‒ i am very much in favour of this report, as i believe it is very positive for the eu economy and for the general welfare. the agricultural sector must be strengthened in economic terms to continue creating jobs and to try to consume the greatest number of products produced in the eu. in terms of social welfare, we must try to ensure that agriculture is sustainable, does not harm the environment and, consequently, does not harm health. for all this, innovation applied to technology is a key tool. in spain, for example, innovation has for years been considered an indispensable tool for ensuring the viability of the agri-food sector. i therefore strongly support the initiative to promote the development of technological and innovative solutions to promote sustainable agriculture in the eu.
mr president, european agriculture is not threatened by a lack of innovation. it is threatened by free trade agreements negotiated behind the backs of the citizens, behind the backs of the people. spanish dairy farms are among the most technologically advanced in europe and do you know what is happening? that our cattle ranchers are going broke. innovation in the field, of course, is fundamental to generating wealth. yes, and from europe, of course, we have to create the conditions for people in rural areas to be able to innovate. but the belief that technology will come to our rescue when we're done with everything is a myth. nothing is going to give us as much wealth as the planet, the land and the people who care for it and work it. we have to get to the root of the problem. the crisis in agriculture has to do with our model of economic growth, our model of production, it has to do with our way of life. only by guaranteeing investment in projects linked to the territory and which are committed to food sovereignty and to agriculture with farmers, will we achieve a decent future for our people and our countryside.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i completely disagree with it. i think that the new techniques, new varieties and new machinery proposed in this report will further increase the dependence of the multinational agrochemical companies, industry and banks, widening the gap between the large industrial food producers and small-scale agriculture, with the increasing disappearance of small farms, local varieties, cultural heritage related to traditional forms of agriculture, etc. the solution would come through a change of system, not based on technology and machinery, but on an agroecological production system, the defense of small-scale farmers, local varieties and, in most cases, the recovery of traditional forms of cultivation, short circuits of production-consumption, and food sovereignty. also social participation, and environmental education programs for responsible production and consumption.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i believe that the innovation and development of farms proposed by the rapporteur is contrary to the model of agro-ecological agriculture which we are advocating. the report opens the door to the introduction of robotics on farms, such as the use of sensors to monitor livestock and drones. although i am not against the use of these technologies, it seems to me that this report is designed to benefit large farms which have a high capacity for borrowing to introduce new systems. on the other hand, the report proposes the introduction of more sophisticated risk management systems, which reinforces my suspicion that it is a report designed for agri-food corporations, and not for farmers to improve their working conditions.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report by mr huitema on improving innovation and economic development in the future management of european farms. the spread of precision farming, which offers new approaches to integrated farm management, should be encouraged. further efforts are called for to develop and fully implement integrated management systems for plant protection by supporting research into non-chemical alternatives and low-risk measures.
in writing. ‒ in line with the mcintyre report, the huitema report, on which i voted in favour, also addresses the challenges facing agriculture: how new practices, techniques and production methods have increased yields and improved the adaptability of agriculture to new and changing circumstances, and how technology and innovation open up new ways to optimise resources or to provide solutions in livestock farming that contribute to a higher level of animal welfare and health. the report also calls on the commission to encourage more effective research to better meet market needs and develop sustainable agronomic and agro-ecological practices and to report regularly on the impact of agricultural innovation on the development of the cost and selling prices of agricultural products and on the business viability of agricultural holdings.

madam president, i fully agree that our response to the present humanitarian crisis in europe should be a comprehensive. i agree that africa should receive our increasing political consideration. nevertheless, the first ideas proposed on the migration compact do not mention two extremely important points: firstly, there is no mention of the defence of human rights. we seem only interested in getting rid of present and future refugees. of course, we are ready to pay to get rid of them. the second point is closely related to the first. apparently, we totally trust all african leaders – morally and economically. my question is: are we going, for instance, to trust the countries which were mentioned here as we have trusted turkey? without defence of human rights, without a strong democratic control on our own procedures and on our agreements with third countries, we are about to repeat all the mistakes made in the recent past. (the speaker agreed to take a blue-card question under rule 162(8))
blue-card answer. – i just believe that we should not confuse things. human rights should be accomplished everywhere. if someone does not, well that is not my fault. i am sorry, we should do that.
madam president, in adopting the migration package, the commission has, in my view, taken the right approach, the approach which is based on a strategic and global vision, taking account of the various aspects of the migration situation; which is based on agreement and partnership with the countries of origin and transit and which looks at a medium and long-term project. because when there are 60 million people displaced by conflict in the world, it is clear that being a global actor in conflict prevention and resolution is an essential element in fighting migration. because when there are also 60 million people in the world who are displaced by hunger and humanitarian crises, it is clear that we need investment to end poverty in those territories. i simply stress, as the european parliament's rapporteur on humanitarian aid, that this whole process must be based on respect for human rights, international humanitarian law and the principles of humanitarian action.
mr president, mrs mogherini, mr timmermans, i have no doubt of your good will, more would be needed, but even rhetoric is late in all this. mr pittella has been very elegant, but i do not think it is just shortsightedness on the part of the member states. they have long known that refugees also die on the african journey and they know, of course, that the integral and sustainable development of africa is just and necessary for africa. they've known for a long time and they haven't done anything - well, unfortunately, they've done too much, too much. so i would like to ask you: what guarantees does the european commission have? how will it get the member states to change their foreign, trade, economic, military and cultural policies towards africa? because this is what it's really about. without that change, there will be no plan, no strategic alliance, nothing.
in writing. for the socialists, the community's immigration policy, both in its internal and external dimensions, must be based on solidarity and the equitable sharing of responsibility, respect for the rule of law and human rights. the success of the 'migration compact' will depend on its adequate funding and budgetary resources. we need robust external investment action, with reliable partners and acting at source, in the so-called sending countries, with innovative development initiatives, also from the point of view of their financing. the eu must continue to insist on improved management of migration flows and effective control of its external borders. the eu should help the sending countries with 'training' initiatives and through the supply of equipment and technology, while these third countries should also be actively involved in search and rescue activities. the european border and coast guard should, within its new mandate, step up cooperation with third countries and play a role in coordinating migration flows in full respect of fundamental rights and european values.

in writing. the new skills agenda is a key initiative to get europe back on the path to prosperity. with the right skills, people are better equipped to enter the labour market for the first time, reorient their working lives or re-enter employment after a long period of time. however, the situation is dramatic: more than 70 million europeans have poor reading, writing, arithmetic and digital skills. too many people are working in jobs that do not match their talents, while 40% of european employers have difficulty finding people with the right skills. the socialists therefore welcome this initiative, but we will be very attentive to its development and implementation, since we cannot rely on a programme designed in the eu to be implemented as the member states wish. what we need is a genuine european action programme, with adequate funding and a specific focus on the countries and regions with the greatest needs. europe needs a skills agenda for all: young, old, employed and unemployed. only then can we ensure a just, sustainable and prosperous future for all.

in writing. ‒ the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with a view to the conclusion of a bilateral agreement between the european union and the republic of palau, the purpose of which is to establish a visa-free regime for citizens of the union and their nationals travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than the pursuit of a paid activity. the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver is a further step in the deepening of relations between the european union and the republic of palau and is an additional means of strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report because it is consistent with the letter and spirit of the cotonou agreement. this island republic is a country fully committed to democracy and human rights. the visa waiver will improve euro-pacific relations and in particular can boost the archipelago's economy, which is largely based on the services sector and has a booming tourist industry. it is consistent with the eu-asia-pacific partnership agreement.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this recommendation by which parliament gives its consent to the conclusion of this bilateral agreement in implementation of the amendments introduced by regulation (eu) no 509/2014, which transferred the republic of palau to annex ii, which establishes the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement to cross the borders of the member states. following the adoption of this regulation, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with a view to concluding the bilateral agreement between the european union and the republic of palau, which was signed on 7 december. the agreement signed establishes a visa-free travel regime for citizens of the union and palau travelling to the territory of the other party for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than the pursuit of a paid activity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of visa-free travel for citizens of the republic of palau for trips of up to 90 days to the european union and for european citizens for trips of the same duration to the republic of palau. although this agreement has been negotiated in an opaque manner and without regard to the views of the european parliament, i am in favour of visa-free procedures which allow the right to freedom of movement to be exercised with fewer restrictions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation, in accordance with the agreements signed between the european union and the republic of palau. the agreement, which is based on the short-stay visa waiver, is a breakthrough in the deepening of relations between the european union and the republic of palau and gives political substance to the cotonou agreement, as well as being a means of strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue.

in writing. ‒ this agreement represents a further achievement in the deepening of relations between the european union and the republic of palau. i also believe that it has an important political significance in the context of the cotonou agreement and that it strengthens political dialogue on various issues as well as economic and cultural relations. the republic of palau has proved to be a democratic republic fully committed to human rights, which are enshrined in its constitution. this agreement will have a positive effect on our economy, as it will simplify travel conditions for businessmen, thus facilitating investment and boosting tourism. in addition, the available data show that this country does not represent any threat either in terms of irregular migration or in terms of security and public order. for the reasons stated above and because the visa waiver will also enable citizens to benefit directly from the agreement, with less financial and practical burdens, i am voting in favour of its approval.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on visa facilitation, so that colombians can make short-term trips, without the need to meet this requirement, to any of the countries of the union, with the exception of the united kingdom and ireland, as well as that of the non-european territories of france and the netherlands. the agreement signed by the eu and colombia allows citizens of the latin american country to travel to the european territory for a maximum period of 90 days every 180 days and covers all persons holding any type of passport from ordinary to official. they may enter the union without a visa when travelling for any reason other than work, for which a specific permit is required. we socialists are proud of an achievement in which we have put all our efforts. this is a major step forward in the deepening of relations between the european union and the republic of colombia and a further means of strengthening economic and cultural relations between the two parties and intensifying political dialogue, including on issues such as human rights and fundamental freedoms.

in writing. ‒ this agreement represents a further achievement in the deepening of relations between the european union and the republic of colombia. i believe that this agreement will help to strengthen regional coherence, since the republic of colombia is one of the few latin american countries whose nationals still require visas, and it is a significant factor in bringing europeans and colombians closer together. we must bear in mind, firstly, that the eu is the second largest trading partner of the republic of colombia and, secondly, the potential of this country thanks to its abundant natural and agricultural resources and the development of the hydrocarbon and mining sectors, which are attracting more and more investors. the republic of colombia can also become a key partner in the field of security and the fight against organised crime. the european union and the republic of colombia share many challenges, which justify the importance and the need to strengthen cooperation through an agreement on the short-stay visa waiver. for the reasons set out above, i am voting in favour of this recommendation.

in writing. ‒ the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with a view to the conclusion of a bilateral agreement between the european union and the republic of colombia establishing a visa-free regime for citizens of the union and nationals of these countries travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than the pursuit of a paid activity. the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver is a further step in the deepening of relations between the european union and the republic of colombia, and is an additional means of strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ the expansion of the ita agreement facilitates the technological exchange of semiconductors, machinery, lenses, gps, medical devices, etc. between a total of 54 countries within the wto framework. however, because of the asymmetries between the participating countries, it functions in practice as a mechanism to reinforce the technological and financial dependence of developing countries, benefiting the large european, american and east asian multinationals. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against this report because i believe that the ita agreement, far from helping to bridge the technological gap in developing countries, risks having an adverse impact on these countries, not only by undermining the collection of resources through customs, but also by increasing south/north technological dependence and by exposing the scarce business fabric to lethal competition from highly technological countries. in addition, the environmental impacts of this industry are not covered in the entire document.
in writing. ‒ the agreement on information technology and trade in derived products (itd) is an adaptation to the planned tariff disarmament phasing-in, which will benefit consumers in terms of prices and supply and introduce more competition in some sectors. it is a stimulus for european innovators and our ability to compete in that market. the measures taken to reduce tariffs are expected to boost european exports in this sector.
in writing. ‒ the agreement on trade in information technology products (itp) entered into force in 1997 and today covers some 200 it products, including not only products such as computers or telephones, but also inputs, components and machinery for the production of it goods. however, since its entry into force, technological progress has profoundly changed the information technology sector. 54 states parties to the agreement have therefore completed a review of the agreement to include new products such as the new generation of semiconductors, gps navigation systems, medical devices, printed circuit board tools, telecommunications satellites or touchscreens. the commission has also concluded that the measures provided for in this regulation are in accordance with the opinion of the committee established by article 15 (1) of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 i have supported this revision of the agreement because it will be positive for the eu economy, which currently exports eur 189 million in products covered by the expansion of the ati, for consumers, who will see prices reduced, and for producers, who are dependent on imported components.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation in the belief that a free market system with non-eu countries for importing and exporting it products would be very beneficial both for the eu and for other countries. the union currently exports eur 189 million in products covered by the expansion of the ati, a figure which is expected to increase considerably following the tariff cuts. the most immediate consequences of the agreement are that prices will be reduced for consumers, but also for producers who rely on imported components.

in writing. ‒ the information technology agreement (ita) has improved the regulation of a growing number of product exchanges. but we have not only seen an increase in trade in recent years, but new products have been introduced, which must also be included in the agreement to avoid damage, especially to consumers. as a consequence of this new agreement, prices will be reduced for consumers, but also for producers who rely on imported components. however, some sectors will also experience increased competition, so it is positive that a longer period of escalation has been established for certain products considered as sensitive, while most non-sensitive tariffs will be eliminated on the date of entry into force of the agreement. i therefore support the recommendation for this agreement and i hope that more countries will join it.

in writing. ‒ new psychoactive substances have been identified as having no medical or veterinary benefits and which, according to the who, produce violent behaviour, psychotic behaviour and cardiotoxicity. i voted in favour of complying with the provisions of the 1971 un convention on psychotropic substances, which require that these substances be subject to a series of controls and, if they are considered dangerous or addictive, that the use of them be regulated by the states within a period of no more than 12 months.
in writing. ‒ α-pvp is a psychomotor stimulant first registered in the eu in 2011. it is a derivative of synthetic cathinone, and is commonly referred to as a new psychotropic substance that has, among other things, effects similar to methamphetamine and cocaine. who research suggests that α-pvp is readily available on the internet and in some retailers; it has also been discovered in the illegal market in the form of ecstasy pills. more than 130 deaths have been associated with α-pvp, in addition to non-lethal side effects such as cardiovascular toxicity, violent behavior, and examples of psychotic behavior. the boni report proposes that this substance be subject to eu control measures, in accordance with decision 2005/387 / jha (for the exchange of information, risk assessment and control of new psychoactive substances) of 10 may 2005. if it is adopted, member states will have to legislate within the next 12 months. its implementation would allow the member states' authorities to take whatever measures they deem necessary to prevent the sale of such substances (including via the internet). i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ in view of the deaths caused by this new psychotropic from china in particular the 115 deaths and 91 acute intoxications in eight member states where α-pvp has been detected and the limited data available on its medium and long-term effects, the conditions laid down in the council decision of 10 may 2005 on the exchange of information, risk assessment and control of new psychotropic substances, and in particular article 8 (3) thereof, are clearly fulfilled. this report should therefore be supported.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this draft resolution by which parliament approves the draft council decision to subject α-pyrrolidinovalerophenone (α-pvp) to control measures and criminal sanctions in the member states under their obligations under the 1971 united nations convention on psychotropic substances. currently, 16 member states control α-pvp under their national legislation, in compliance with the obligations imposed by the 1971 united nations convention on psychotropic substances, and five member states apply other legislative measures to control it. the introduction of control measures for this substance across the union will help to avoid the emergence of obstacles to cross-border judicial and police cooperation and will help to protect society against the risks that the availability and consumption of this substance may pose. it is not surprising that in the eight member states where α-pvp was detected, 115 deaths and 191 acute intoxications were recorded.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to give parliament's consent to the council adopting the 2010 protocol to the convention on harmful and dangerous substances relating to the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, with the exception of aspects relating to judicial cooperation in civil matters. since regional bodies cannot do this, it is up to the member states to join. i voted in favour of this report because it proposes to ensure that the specialised international compensation fund for snp is used to ensure that people, property and the environment are compensated for the loss or damage caused by the transport of harmful and potentially dangerous substances by sea.

in writing. ‒ the european union is pending ratification of the 1996 international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, including liquefied natural gas (lng) and liquefied petroleum gas (lpg). i fully agree with the european approach to the problem and with the recommendations that parliament makes to the council in this report to ensure that there is sufficient financial compensation for victims of disasters caused by ships carrying this type of substance and that it is applied uniformly at international level.
in writing. ‒ the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea is a key legal instrument in terms of transport and the environment. the ratification of the 2010 protocol, which effectively represents the ratification of the above convention in its new 2010 terms, is relevant for the eu because it provides enhanced protection for those affected by the transport of dangerous substances by sea. in its decision of december 2015, the council left it to the member states to decide when each of them would carry out the ratification. this possibility could lead to legal uncertainty due to differences in the applicable rule. in addition, some of the provisions overlap with the environmental liability directive 2004/35/ec, which could lead to confusion as to the legal basis of claims. with this interim report, which i voted in favour of, parliament is trying to put pressure on the council to correct its decision by calling for a uniform ratification of the convention and thus clarifying its application.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the approval of this eu-philippines framework agreement because the eu's cooperation and collaboration agreements with third countries are the prelude to a free trade agreement, which we oppose because of its negative effects on the working class of the countries concerned. moreover, such trade agreements pave the way for putting european business interests ahead of those of the peoples of the different countries. the amendments tabled by our gue/ngl group on the growing militarization of the asia-pacific region, the repression of left-wing activists and politicians, extrajudicial killings and our concerns about how this economic agreement will harm the local population were all rejected, so i have no hesitation in voting against this agreement.
in writing. ‒ i abstain in the vote on this own-initiative report which did not include amendments tabled by our group, concerning the growing militarization of the asia-pacific region and the joint us-philippine maneuvers, the repression of civil society activists and members of left-wing parties, the proper implementation of the human rights conventions in the country and the existence of extrajudicial killings by the state security forces and paramilitary forces. while some of these elements are mentioned in the final text, it is ultimately an instrument aimed at moving towards the signing of a free trade agreement between the eu and the philippines, which, like the rest of such instruments in the process of negotiation with other countries since the doha freeze, has a double face: on the one hand the promise of new trade opportunities, to accompany and secure their reform processes and on the other hand the risks that trade liberalization between economies with very different levels of development entails for the weaker party.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of incorporating croatia, as a newly integrated eu member state, into the framework agreement on partnership and cooperation between the republic of the philippines and the eu since 2010, now updated.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the approval of this eu-philippines framework agreement because the eu's cooperation and collaboration agreements with third countries are the prelude to a free trade agreement, which we oppose because of its negative effects on the working class of the countries concerned. moreover, such trade agreements pave the way for putting european business interests ahead of those of the peoples of the different countries. the amendments tabled by our gue/ngl group on the growing militarization of the asia-pacific region, the repression of left-wing activists and politicians, extrajudicial killings and our concerns about how this economic agreement will harm the local population were all rejected, so i have no hesitation in voting against this agreement.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report with the intention that the republic of croatia should immediately accede to all the protocols of the european union as quickly as possible. the accession process has been a fundamental principle for european development and the member welcomes the fact that the republic of croatia is taking steps forward in this respect.
in writing. ‒ i abstain in the vote on this own-initiative report which did not include amendments tabled by our group, concerning the growing militarization of the asia-pacific region and the joint us-philippine maneuvers, the repression of civil society activists and members of left-wing parties, the proper implementation of the human rights conventions in the country and the existence of extrajudicial killings by the state security forces and paramilitary forces. while some of these elements are mentioned in the final text, it is ultimately an instrument aimed at moving towards the signing of a free trade agreement between the eu and the philippines, which, like the rest of such instruments in the process of negotiation with other countries since the doha freeze, has a double face: on the one hand the promise of new trade opportunities, to accompany and secure their reform processes and on the other hand the risks that trade liberalization between economies with very different levels of development entails for the weaker party.

in writing. ‒ the republic of the philippines and the eu have had a framework agreement on partnership and cooperation since 2010 and in december 2014 it was granted gsp+ status, the first asean country to enjoy such trade preferences. the eu also doubled its financial allocation for development cooperation with the philippines over the period 2014-2020 and has also provided substantial humanitarian and emergency assistance to victims of tropical storms. parliament calls on the philippines to ratify and implement all the core international conventions on human and labour rights, environmental protection and good governance listed in annex viii to regulation (eu) no 978/2012. in 2014, the commission considered the possibility of banning imports of fishery products from the philippines if it did not improve the control of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing earlier, and the commission therefore initiated a dialogue to address the weaknesses in its fisheries management and control systems. for all these reasons i voted in favour of this framework agreement.

in writing. ‒ the report proposes to approve macrofinancial assistance to tunisia for a second time up to a maximum value of 500 million. i am not opposed to helping a country like tunisia economically, whose population has been in a difficult situation since 2001, now aggravated by the threat of the islamic state and its allies in the region. but this aid must in no way be through the instrument of macrofinancial assistance, since this economic aid will supplement imf loans conditional on structural reforms, which do nothing but impoverish the population and worsen their living conditions: liberalizations and privatizations. i have therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution, calling for more foreign investment through credits to strengthen tunisia's economy. i believe that the aid that tunisia needs should be given, if possible, in the form of non-repayable aid and not in the form of loans with strict macroeconomic conditionality criteria which not only undermine the country's sovereignty but also increase the risk of debt stress.

in writing. ‒ the democratic transition in tunisia is not going smoothly. this country is going through difficult economic times and also has to face the terrible suffering associated with the terrorist attacks that have occurred, especially in tourist areas. the eu must help stabilise this country, and that is why i am in favour of the proposal to grant additional macrofinancial assistance to that which we have already approved in a first programme. this assistance programme will support the reforms undertaken by tunisia to improve its budgetary situation, balance of payments and create a more favourable investment climate.
in writing. ‒ since the start of its democratic transition in 2011, tunisia's economy has been affected by continuing internal turmoil, regional instability and a weak international environment. in 2014, tunisia requested a first macro-financial assistance operation from the eu, as an accompaniment to the imf assistance programme. the aid, granted by the eu in the form of credits and grants, has been disbursed in several tranches throughout 2015 and the first part of 2016. however, following the terrorist attacks in 2015, tunisia's economy has been hit hard, particularly tourism, transport and investment, with a devastating impact on employment and significant social unrest. the economic instability is having a very negative impact on the balance of payments and the public finances, leaving tunisia in urgent need of financing. the tunisian authorities have therefore requested new assistance from the imf and, as a complement, a second macro-financial assistance operation to the eu amounting to eur 500 million. i have decided to support this new financial assistance to tunisia, as support for its political, social and economic transition efforts.

in writing. ‒ tunisia has succeeded in consolidating its democratic transition. it now has a constitution that safeguards rights and freedoms, with a consolidated judicial system and empowered media. it is led by a broad unity government that emerged from free and transparent elections, with an enterprising and modern civil society, and has rightly been rewarded with the nobel peace prize for the tunisian national dialogue quartet. tunisia is going through very great difficulties. on a number of occasions it has been the target of terrorist murders and attacks which have hit key sectors of the country’s economy, such as tourism. growth, projected at 3% for 2015, has been revised down to 0.5% for 2016; the unemployment rate is 15% on average, 20% for women and 28.6% for young university graduates. the regional security and political context is extremely volatile, moreover, chiefly because of the border it shares with libya. despite all these challenges, tunisia continues to make significant progress, firmly establishing democratic transition in the country, carrying out the reforms needed to modernise its economy and bolstering its relations with its partners, in particular the european union, with which it is currently negotiating a free-trade agreement.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution, calling for more foreign investment through credits to strengthen tunisia's economy. we believe that the aid that tunisia needs should be given, if possible, in the form of non-repayable aid and not in the form of loans with strict macroeconomic conditionality criteria which not only undermine the country's sovereignty but also increase the risk of debt stress.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour as we greens are generally in favour of granting mfa to the countries which participate in the eastern european neighbourhood programme. we regard these countries as in the area of economic influence of the eu which hence deserve support in case of balance of payments problems.
in writing. ‒ we are talking about a proposal that will provide tunisia with macro-financial assistance of eur 500 million in the medium term. the aim of this assistance is to help our neighbour to carry out a number of necessary reforms which will have to be set out in a memorandum of understanding. we are therefore talking about aid which is necessary to help bring greater stability to a mediterranean neighbour, and i therefore think it necessary to vote in favour of this decision.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the commission's proposal. the european union should support tunisia through this new financial aid package to help stabilise the country and achieve growth. in a highly unstable geographical context, tunisia faces numerous economic, political and security challenges. however, we must recognize the progress it is making and the consolidation of its democratic transition and the modernisation of its economic structures. the european union should show solidarity by supporting the tunisian transition process through this €500 million macro-financial assistance package.
madam president, a report by oxfam intermón shows that the largest spanish companies are leaders in tax evasion. the ibex 35 companies tripled their presence in tax havens during the crisis. the bank of santander is the main beneficiary of this tax avoidance. former president josé maría aznar was fined more than €70,000 for using an instrumental company to pay half of what he owed to the treasury. the castellana papers are unveiling decades of tax evasion in the spanish state. in the meantime, people are losing their social and labour rights and public services as a result of, among other things, the bailout of the banks and the budgetary adjustment. the european union must put an end to this by taking strong action, by adopting strong rules against tax evasion and avoidance and by eliminating any loopholes that allow this. this report is not strong enough on this, which is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote on this report because, despite the fact that it represents a major step forward in the fight against tax evasion and avoidance by large multinationals, it does not deal adequately with the mechanisms of large multinationals such as the patent boxes. the report is an undeniable step forward in the development of legislation to combat tax evasion and avoidance, from effective clarifications and definitions to specific measures. however, certain well-known mechanisms are left out and very high limits are set which will prevent these measures from having the real effect they seek. we need a more aggressive fiscal policy to combat the practices of multinationals and to put an end to the growth of inequality in europe. it is because i consider that the report will not achieve its objectives that i have not been able to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this report. the rapporteur tried to build a progressive majority in parliament by taking strong measures to combat tax evasion, but the division in the alde group forced him to seek agreements with the epp, which has substantially reduced the content of the text. i myself have tabled amendments to increase the ability of states to monitor transactions with countries which are not sufficiently transparent, but these amendments were rejected.
in writing. ‒ the aggressive planning practices of large multinationals - as the euphemistic name for the work of some large companies to avoid taxation - deserve, require and oblige a european response. the member states cannot compete with each other with their tax systems to save themselves individually at the cost of undermining the whole of the revenue and the values and principles of fair taxation. this problem needed and deserved a european response and we are giving it. and all tax systems, including those in regions considered to have autonomous tax systems, must be involved in this response.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this consultation report on the proposal for a council directive and which is part of the commission's anti-circumvention package. the commission considers that the aid is compatible with the internal market if it is granted to a company in difficulty. the two major advances in this proposal are the introduction of an exit tax on profits in certain circumstances and the imposition of limits on the deductibility of interest on financial expenses. the rapporteur, mr hugues bayet, a colleague from the socialist group, has succeeded in improving the initial proposal, particularly as regards the limitation on the deductibility of interest and the definition of a permanent establishment. the commission has also included a number of amendments tabled by the spanish socialist delegation during the committee procedure. it is expected that the council will take account of the european parliament's position in this consultation procedure.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i am convinced that tax evasion must be avoided, since it directly affects society as a whole. it is estimated that aggressive tax planning by multinational corporations costs public coffers between $100 billion and $240 billion a year worldwide. this amount represents between 4 and 10% of the worldwide corporate tax revenue. that is why the european union must move from economic and monetary union to harmonization of european taxation. fair taxation should become the cornerstone of the single market.

in writing. ‒ the construction of economic and monetary union must involve the harmonisation of european taxation. fair and effective corporate taxation must become the cornerstone of the single market. i believe that a coordinated and harmonised approach to the functioning of tax regimes is essential to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market and the success of the capital markets union. the main objective of this report is to get companies to tax where they make their profits. to this end, this report has chosen to introduce precise and mandatory definitions of the conditions which demonstrate that a multinational is well established in a country. it's the only way to force these companies to pay taxes fairly. today, multinational companies too often organise themselves to move their profits to tax havens without having paid any tax. to avoid this and the loss of revenue and therefore of investment capacity to promote employment, to fight poverty and to develop effective and universal health systems which this aggressive fiscal planning entails for the states, i am voting in favour of its approval.
in writing. ‒ my support for the report on the proposal for a directive laying down rules against tax avoidance practices which directly affect the functioning of the internal market. we must stop at once the bleeding that is taking place in the public accounts by the system of some multinationals, which have devised a whole mechanism to avoid paying billions of euros, which means less money for public services, for promoting employment, for fighting poverty and for continuing to grow in an equal way. i am firmly convinced that the construction of economic and monetary union must involve a harmonization of european taxation that is fair and effective, and for that we must ensure that companies are taxed where they make their profits.

in writing. ‒ tax avoidance has become one of the worst problems of our society. with our middle class struggling to adapt to globalisation and our welfare state at risk due to the vulnerability of our public finances, it is fundamental that all elements from society contribute their due taxes and do not avoid their responsibility. without a level playing field that makes everyone pay taxes the same way, cohesion policy will suffer.

in writing. ‒ my vote was positive. i had liked that this directive would have gone much further than the oecd agreement. but this directive is absolutely needed in the context of an integrated eu market where tax competition plays an harmful role. my group has successfully managed to include in the report some additional provisions to tackle artificial establishments and transactions that companies uses only for tax purposes and fight against patent boxes.
in writing. the brutal interrogation and torture methods used by the cia after the 9/11 attacks are a stain on the conscience of the united states. the fact that european governments were complicit in their actions is not only immoral but constitutes a violation of our commitments to human rights and the values on which the eu is founded. the us senate report not only exposes the scale of these crimes, but also clearly demonstrates that torture is not effective in preventing and prosecuting terrorist attacks. there can never be any justification for torture from the prism of international law, and we have an obligation to show that we take this matter very seriously by ensuring that those responsible are held to account. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution calling on the member states to take responsibility once and for all for these unfortunate events and to make a formal and factual commitment that such serious violations of human rights can never happen again with the connivance of european governments.
in writing. ‒ following the discovery of the involvement of various eu states in the cia's extraordinary surrender programme, through which torture and other human rights violations were perpetrated outside the us, an inquiry into european involvement in the libe commission was approved. after one year, the right-wing groups in this house do not want this investigation to continue into facts which reveal the subordination of the european union to american interests, to the point of allowing serious human rights violations on its territory. i have therefore voted in favour of renewing the mandate of the libe committee, so that the facts can be investigated and the political responsibility of the eu governments that allowed these shameful acts to be proved.
in writing. ‒ i consider this to be a very positive motion for a resolution as a whole, which goes into detail on various aspects which we believe should be clarified, both on human rights violations and torture, as well as the existence of detention centres in member states of the european union. i think that there should be full transparency on these facts and all the actions that parliament can take to investigate and punish a series of human rights violations over the last decade. i regard this report positively and therefore think it appropriate to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i support this resolution because the best way to strengthen the values on which the european union is founded is to put them into practice and because we cannot afford, at a time when international terrorism is violating the most basic rights, to turn a blind eye to intolerable violations of fundamental rights by the authorities of important partner countries such as the united states. i also believe that it is essential to eradicate these practices from european soil, and i therefore agree to launch investigations in all the member states where, in collusion with american agents, torture of detainees may have occurred.

in writing. ‒ this report advocates strengthening the eu's security and defence policy rather than giving priority to civilian capabilities in conflict resolution. it also considers space capability to be an appropriate instrument for border management, internal security and energy and to enhance the development of the military-industrial complex. he advocates greater militarization of space, as well as of the eu. i am opposed to the report, as it also calls for greater eu cooperation with the us and nato on future space capabilities and services for the csdp; advocates the use of dual-use space technologies in the space sector, which aims to contribute to the development of the european military industry; and calls for the mobilisation of eu resources to increase its space capabilities in security and defence, deepening its militarisation. i believe that military research should not be funded from the eu budget and that conflict resolution should be based on a peaceful, civil and diplomatic approach. that is why i am not only against greater cooperation between the eu and nato, but also call for the latter to be dissolved.
in writing. ‒ i vote against this report. i agree with the rapporteur that the european union's space capabilities must be encouraged and work towards improving innovation and strategic independence in satellite navigation systems. but i do not agree with the military use of these space programmes. galileo and copernicus should be used for civilian purposes only, and the european union should not contribute to the militarisation of space. the increase in funding for these matters should always be reviewed by the european parliament and not be given to the space agencies, which have to coordinate and manage, but should not do so without democratic control or for military purposes. the use of satellites for border control, as well as for the military resolution of the refugee crisis, is not the appropriate way to end this problem. we must therefore always seek solutions based on civil society and solidarity and the values of the founding treaties of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i support this report for three reasons. firstly, because global threats require global responses and space technology is fundamental in this field and europe needs independence and self-sufficiency in this field. secondly, because it is a very appropriate way of turning the many arguments we are dealing with into facts, of getting rid of the concept of 'national security' altogether and replacing it with a european concept where coordination and efficiency are paramount. the third is linked to development, which this strategy will encourage in european companies involved in space technology.
in writing. ‒ as the report points out, the security environment is becoming increasingly complex, both inside and outside the union, with terrorist attacks and mass killings affecting all member states. these challenges call for strengthening eu security by developing and supporting the common security and defence policy to make it a more effective policy instrument and a real guarantee of the security of eu citizens and the promotion and protection of the norms, interests and values enshrined in the teu. space capabilities are key in a multitude of situations, from everyday peacetime use to managing crises and the most pressing security challenges. the potential of satellites could be used to better assess and identify the flow of illegal migrants and their routes and, in the case of those from north africa, to identify embarkation areas, intercept them earlier and save more lives. it is therefore urgent to step up defence cooperation with a view to building up critical capabilities, including through a coherent and efficient use of available union funds and capabilities.

in writing. ‒ in this report, the european parliament stresses the economic importance of developing space capabilities and the need to develop more cooperation mechanisms between european and member states' space programmes. it is important to continue to focus on the development of space capabilities through the existing galileo and copernicus programmes as well as through new programmes. we are talking about key technologies that will enable us to continue to innovate and to apply them in future to productive sectors, with the consequent creation of jobs. i therefore think it necessary to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because space should not be a commodity left to the market, but part of the environment, a public good which should be protected by decisions of democratic institutions and not by the interests of multinationals. in the face of obvious problems such as the presence of space junk, this resolution encourages the market-controlled development of industry, moreover, encourages putting public resources and research in the hands of private actors. the report also refers to the potential military uses of the 'market'. i am opposed to the possible military use of space, the use of public resources for the benefit of private companies, and i am opposed to the privatization of the environment, including space. that is why i have decided to vote against this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against this motion for a resolution, which proposes a market system in the space sector, promoting investment and support for private companies in different space services. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i believe that progress in this sector must always be led by academic scientific research, common interests, and never have a militarization component as they have today. we also regret the 'pre-cooking' in these reports by the 'grand coalition', which leave no room for objections from a sector critical of the use of space capabilities and services for war. using the rhetoric of security and fear to increase the militarization of space.
in writing. ‒ the promotion of a space strategy is essential to end the fragmentation of the digital market, to demonstrate the added value that the union brings to the economy of this region of the world, to ensure europe's independence in the sector, to foster a new source of specialisation and trade and to enable entrepreneurs to have basic infrastructures for new businesses based on knowledge and the exploitation of big data. the space strategy must be given priority in the european strategy for reindustrialising and relaunching our economy. in this context, the cuts in public investments linked to these programmes are a real contradiction to the 2020 development model.
in writing. ‒ the european union has a major source of scientific and technological development in space activities, but also of economic activity, competitiveness and highly skilled employment. according to studies carried out by parliament, between 6% and 7% of the gdp of western countries depends on activities linked to satellite positioning and navigation. the european satellite navigation system is expected to generate economic and social benefits of between eur 60 and 90 billion over the next two decades. and most of that value will be generated by small and medium-sized enterprises. as this resolution, which i have supported, calls for, europe must make a strong effort to develop its space programme so as not to lose its world leadership in this field. the space strategy to be launched in the second half of the year must therefore focus on the development and marketing of products, services and applications in order to maximise the socioeconomic benefits of the community's space programmes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it is a balanced text. the left must denounce the abuses of power and violations of democracy and the rule of law that are being committed in venezuela. and at the same time, the left must firmly bet on the dialogue between government and opposition, executive and legislature, as the only possible, peaceful and legitimate solution to the problems in venezuela. the request for dialogue is in line with the request of most of the international community (unasur, celac, european commission, g7, us and vatican among other actors), and with the mediation work between government and opposition that are being carried out by the three former presidents josé luis rodríguez zapatero, leonel fernández and marín torrijos, with the support of unasur. the resolution also seeks to help to remedy the serious shortage of food and medicines in the country. to this end, it has asked the eu to draw up a humanitarian assistance plan to send and distribute supplies in venezuela and has asked the venezuelan government to accept this aid.

in writing. ‒ venezuela is going through a serious economic crisis and political tension is increasing. in may, the opposition that controls the legislature handed the electoral council 1.85 million signatures asking for a recall referendum of the president, nicolás maduro. this resolution merely reflects the current situation in venezuela, a country with the largest crude oil reserves in the world, but which nevertheless has skyrocketing inflation and suffers from shortages of basic products and electricity cuts. the venezuelan people do not deserve this situation. i therefore think it appropriate to vote in favour of this resolution.
madam president, by failing to adopt by 13 december 2013 the delegated acts to specify the criteria for determining substances that are endocrine disruptors, the commission has breached its legal obligations. i think that this is a serious attack on public health and that the commission is just trying to buy time for the manufacture of doubts, which, as we know, the big companies in the sector are experts in - we can take the example of glyphosate - thus allowing nothing, not even our health - public health - to get in the way of the business of these big companies. the commission knows that by this attitude it is allowing the planet to be poisoned and causing pain, suffering and death. i voted in favour of this report because it condemns the commission's decision and i hope that the commissioner will take responsibility and act accordingly, and now.
madam president, 'let us put commerce before people, let us not investigate the effect of endocrine disruptors on health'. that is the message that the european commission is sending us. some chemicals can have tragic effects on the body's endocrine systems: infertility, cancer, problems during pregnancy, neurological disorders are just some of the consequences they can cause. does the european commission expect that ttip will end health protection and that it will no longer have to investigate anything? the action of the chemical industry lobbies is playing a decisive role in these delays, as has been recently proven in leaked documents. we insist that the european commission has a moral and legal obligation to carry out rigorous and independent scientific research on endocrine disruptors. however, this mandate is being delayed forever and deliberately.
madam president, what credibility can a commission have that violates its own laws, that refuses to publish the list of endocrine disruptors - substances that are linked to hormonal disruption, cancers, infertility, neurological disorders and diabetes, among other diseases - in order to avoid regulating in favour of public and occupational health? we are aware that there is a lot of political pressure in this case, especially from american industry, which wants to remove the precautionary principle from european legislation and prepare the landing of its unsafe products with ttip. but it is an illegal impulse, because delaying a decision violates a legal rule that is very clear. the identification of these substances, pending since 2014, should be based on scientific criteria and protect the public interest. the complicity of the right in this house with the commission and big business, ignoring the fact that the court of justice of the european union itself has ruled against them, does not surprise me. we have therefore opposed their amendments and have supported the text contained in our own motion.
in writing. ‒ the european commission is failing to meet its obligations to determine the endocrine-disrupting properties of active substances and biocides with a view to banning harmful substances. endocrine disruptors are largely responsible for neurobehavioural disorders, breast cancer, endometrial cancer, ovarian cancer, prostate cancer, testicular cancer, thyroid cancer, etc. and are found in food, water, packaging, toys, textiles, cosmetics, pesticides, hygiene products, building materials, clinical materials and in numerous other consumer items, etc. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe it is urgent that the commission should take up its responsibilities and take action in this area.
in writing. ‒ the commission is, in this case, clearly in breach of a judgment of the general court, and therefore the commission is clearly in breach of article 266 tfeu. i think that this attitude is particularly serious, given that human health issues are also at stake. i hope that the commission will honour its commitment and that before the summer it will proceed to detail the scientific criteria for determining the endocrine-disrupting capacities of the disruptors on humans.
in writing. ‒ endocrine disruptors are chemicals that can interfere with the hormones of animal species, including humans, and thus cause many serious diseases e.g. hormone-dependent cancers, infertility, obesity, diabetes, neurological behavioural disorders, etc. i have supported this resolution to demand that the commission comply with the judgment of the court of justice and come forward as soon as possible with strict criteria for endocrine disruptors based on science and not on socioeconomic considerations. under the biocidal products regulation, the commission is obliged to find a way to distinguish endocrine disruptors from other chemicals by establishing scientific criteria for their identification. the list of these scientific criteria should have been drawn up by the european commission in 2013. on 16 december 2015, the court of justice ruled that the european commission had failed to fulfil its legal obligation by failing to adopt delegated acts specifying scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties. according to the judgment, the scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties should be based only on the science related to the endocrine system, independently of any other considerations, in particular economic considerations.
in writing. ‒ the european commission is failing to meet its obligations to determine the endocrine-disrupting properties of active substances and biocides with a view to banning harmful substances. endocrine disruptors are largely responsible for neurobehavioural disorders, breast cancer, endometrial cancer, ovarian cancer, prostate cancer, testicular cancer, thyroid cancer, etc. and are found in food, water, packaging, toys, textiles, cosmetics, pesticides, hygiene products, building materials, clinical materials and in numerous other consumer items, etc. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe it is urgent that the commission should take up its responsibilities and take action in this area.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i am convinced that endocrine disruptors may be a health hazard according to reports by the unep and the who. they can affect the endocrine system in humans and also in animals, as there has been evidence of effects such as infertility, cancers, malformations... due to exposure to endocrine disruptors, there is also increasing evidence of the effects of these chemicals on thyroid and brain function, on obesity and metabolism, and on insulin and glucose homeostasis.
in writing. ‒ endocrine disruptors, which are found in everyday products, interfere with hormones. they cause a whole range of diseases, from obesity to infertility. however, although experts agree on the negative effects of these substances, no definition has been established at european level to regulate endocrine disruptors and their circulation in a precise way. in this context, our group co-signed a motion of censure against the european commission in may, to stop the postponement of the publication of the criteria defining the characteristics of an endocrine disruptor. in the face of the commission's inaction, i have therefore proposed, on behalf of the enf group, a resolution consistent with our objectives, so that member states can ban products they consider to be dangerous themselves. the pro-european parties, out of partisanship, refused to sanction the commission and to defend the health of citizens. the motion for a resolution put to the vote by the socialists only serves to highlight their hypocrisy. since the proposal of our opponents is only a vulgar alibi, i have decided to vote against this measure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution as regulation (eu) no 528/2012 does not approve active substances which, on the basis of criteria to be established or provisional criteria, have endocrine disrupting properties that may cause adverse effects in humans. it also provides that the commission is to adopt, by 13 december 2013, delegated acts specifying scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties of active substances and biocidal products. the commission has not yet adopted those delegated acts. the who report identified endocrine disruptors as a global threat, referring, inter alia, to the high incidence and upward trend of many endocrine disorders in humans and noting that effects on endocrine function have also been observed in wild animal populations; that there is evidence of adverse reproductive effects infertility, cancers, malformations from exposure to endocrine disruptors, and that there is also increasing evidence of the effects of these chemicals on thyroid and brain function, obesity and metabolism, and on insulin and glucose homeostasis.
in writing. ‒ meps have expressed their displeasure at the commission's delay in publishing the scientific criteria needed to identify and address exposure to chemicals that cause hormonal disruption. for that reason, i am voting in favour of the resolution in which meps call for the information to be published now in view of the possible restrictions on the use of these chemicals, which are associated with the deterioration of sperm quality, the early onset of puberty, certain types of cancer and other disorders.

in writing. ‒ condemns the commission’s failure to act not only re scientific criteria for endocrine disrupters, but also for failure to comply with art. 266 tfeu by not complying with the court judgment (para 1; ecr am 10 rejected rcv 72/400/192). has strong wording on the inappropriateness of impact assessments for a scientific matter and of looking at regulatory changes in the context of the ia, as this is beyond the powers of the commission in the context of a delegated act calls on the commission to immediately adopt hazard-based criteria for endocrine disrupters.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection because i am totally against genetically modified organisms and therefore against new authorizations for them. the decision-making process concerning the authorization of gmos for food and feed is not being democratic. the special committee almost never reaches a qualified majority, but the european commission is almost always issuing authorisations, without the support of the member states or the majority of eu citizens. this should be the exception, but with gmo, it's now the rule. at older ages, this maize is tolerant to glyphosate, which makes its authorisation very premature when a qualified majority of member states cannot even agree on the re-authorisation of this 'potentially carcinogenic and endocrine disrupting' herbicide.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because since 22 april 2015, in the explanatory memorandum to its legislative proposal amending regulation (ec) no 1829/2003, the commission regretted that since the entry into force of that regulation, decisions authorising the use of certain substances have been adopted by the commission, in accordance with the applicable legislation, without the support of the opinions of the committees of the member states, and that the referral of the dossier to the commission for the adoption of the final decision, which indeed constituted an exception in the framework of the procedure as a whole, has become the norm when adopting decisions on authorisations of genetically modified food and feed. we consider that the commission's draft implementing decision exceeds its powers. as described in the application, the genetically modified maize mon-øøø21-9 expresses the cry1ab protein which confers protection against certain lepidopteran pests and the mepsps protein which confers tolerance to glyphosate-based herbicides. the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) has classified glyphosate as a probable human carcinogen.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on this matter by the envi parliamentary committee, which considers that this draft implementing decision of the committee exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1892/2003, and i am therefore in favour of the committee withdrawing it.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the objection to this implementing act by which the european commission authorises the company syngenta to place on the market products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize bt11 × mir162 × mir604 × ga21 and genetically modified maize combining two or three of the events bt11, mir162, mir604 and ga21. this authorisation by the commission exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 on genetically modified food and feed. in particular, some of the genetically modified maize concerned confer tolerance to glufosinate ammonium and glyphosate-based herbicides, which could lead to increased use of these herbicides. for these reasons, i have supported the objection.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection, considering that we must have all the information necessary when making decisions on authorisations of genetically modified food and feed. our only interest in this case must be to ensure the safety and health of the food we consume in the eu.
in writing. ‒ the marketing authorisation for products and foodstuffs containing this gmo had already been granted. however, it excluded culture. efsa gave a favourable opinion in 2015 on the extension of the authorisation to all sub-combinations of the genetic modification requested in 2013. the objection is that the authorisation is beyond the commission's powers. this gmo is resistant to glyphosate, which is a pesticide tolerated as there are not enough alternatives and the industry needs a transition period before its definitive ban. in order to protect the citizens of europe, i have decided to vote in favour of this report, in favour of this objection.

in writing. ‒ even though as this vote is an objection to an implementing act, and this objection might be more of a political move made by different groups in the chamber, eh bildu has maintained a coherent position on matters related to gmos and always vote against those, or as in cases as such, vote in favour of objections to allowing the authorisation of gmos. on 9 february 2009, syngenta submitted to the competent authority of germany an application for the placing on the market of foods, food ingredients, and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from bt11×mir162×mir604×ga21 maize; and later on 5 july 2013, extended the scope of the application to all sub-combinations of the single genetic modification events, including bt11×ga21 maize, mir604×ga21 maize, bt11×mir604 maize, and bt11×mir604×ga21 which are already authorised by different commission decisions. however, this draft commission implementing decision exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation(ec) no1829/2003 on genetically modified food and feed. indeed, some of the genetically-modified maizes in question confer tolerance to glufosinate-ammonium and glyphosate-based herbicides, while the international agency for research for cancer (who) classified glyphosate as probably carcinogenic to humans. therefore, eh bildu has voted in favour of this objection, and will keep voting in the same way to any future objection concerning authorisation of gmos.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection because i consider the procedure followed for authorisation to be inappropriate, since it should fully respect the precautionary principle in such a sensitive area as authorisations of genetically modified organisms (gmos). a good example of the lack of democracy in decision-making on the authorisation of gmos for food and feed is that the special committee almost never reaches a qualified majority, yet the european commission is almost always issuing authorisations, without the support of the member states or the majority of eu citizens. this should be the exception, but with gmo, it's now the rule. the main commercial attraction of this variety is its compatibility with glyphosate, on which there is also no qualified majority of member states for the extension of its authorisation as a 'potential carcinogen and endocrine disruptor' herbicide.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection because i am totally against genetically modified organisms and therefore against new authorisations for them. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the transgenic carnation is not used in the field. in addition, the decision-making process concerning the authorization of gmos for food and feed is not being democratic. the special committee almost never reaches a qualified majority, but the european commission is almost always issuing authorisations, without the support of the member states or the majority of eu citizens. this should be the exception, but with gmo, it's now the rule.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this administrative objection, given that in nature cross-pollination of dianthus spp. is carried out by pollinating insects, in particular lepidoptera; the efsa gmo technical committee considers that the risk of lepidoptera transferring pollen from the genetically modified carnation shd-27531-4 to wild dianthus species cannot be eliminated. in its opinion, efsa also states that the technical committee on gmos is aware that some populations have a dietary habit of intentionally consuming carnation petals as a garnish and that the commission has not assessed the consequences of the intended human consumption of genetically modified carnations. the genetically modified carnation contains the surb (als) gene which encodes a mutant acetolactate synthase (als) protein derived from nicotiana tabacum, which confers resistance to sulphonylureas. according to pan uk, 'certain herbicides, such as sulphonylureas, sulphonamides and imidazolinones, are highly toxic to plants at very low doses'. experts have warned that the widespread use of sulphonylureas 'could have devastating effects on the productivity of non-target crops and on the composition of phytocenoses and food chains'.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on this matter by the envi parliamentary committee, which considers that this draft implementing decision of the committee exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1892/2003, and i am therefore in favour of the committee withdrawing it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection to this implementing act, whereby the european commission authorises the japanese company suntory holdings limited to place genetically modified carnation dianthus caryophyllus l., line shd-27531-4, on the market in the netherlands. this carnation is resistant to the sulfonylurea. these herbicides, according to the british herbicide action network pan were highly toxic to plants at very low doses, and their widespread use could have a negative impact on the productivity of other crops and the composition of natural plant communities and wild food chains. finally, sulphonylureas are common treatments for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and are associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease compared to other antidiabetic drugs. the creation of a market for sulphonylurea-resistant plants will encourage the worldwide use of this antidiabetic drug as a herbicide, with potentially harmful effects on biodiversity and chemical pollution of drinking water, so i have supported the objection.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the motion for a resolution, considering that we must ensure that this carnation meets the eu's objective of protecting human health and the environment, which has not been substantiated so far, and that the distribution of this decorative flower could have negative consequences for the health of european citizens and the environment.
in writing. ‒ in march 2013, a request was made in the netherlands for the placing on the market of genetically modified eyelashes. efsa has produced two scientific opinions concluding that these carnations do not present a risk to human health and the environment. the agency stated in particular that the transgenic eggplant plants did not harm other species. the european commission therefore planned to give its authorization for this marketing. however, some of the characteristics of these gm plants are only expressed when they are exposed to sulphonylurea-based herbicides, to which they are resistant. however, the increased use of these herbicides will inevitably have consequences for the development of neighbouring species. therefore, even if gm carnations do not appear to pose a direct risk, they will lead to the massive use of environmentally harmful herbicides. i therefore voted in favour of the objection.
