in writing. ‒ in march 2013 a notification concerning the placing on the market of a genetically-modified carnation (dianthus caryophyllus l., line shd-27531-4) was submitted by suntory holdings limited, to the competent authority of the netherlands; covering the import, distribution and retailing of cut flowers of the genetically modified carnation for ornamental use. on 25 april 2016, with the lack of opinion of the regulatory committee on the draft commission implementing decision authorising the placing on the market, dianthus caryophyllus l., line shd-27531-4 was authorised. however we considered that the draft commission implementing decision does not fulfil the objective of health and environment protection set out in directive2001/18/ec and therefore exceeds the implementing powers provided for in this directive. the reasons: 1. certain populations intentionally consume carnation petals as garnish. efsa had not assessed the possible consequences of the intentional consumption of gm carnations by humans and animals. 2. propagation by rooting, and spreading of pollen of this gm carnation to wild dianthus species cannot be excluded. eh bildu has maintained a coherent position on matters related to gmos and always vote against those, or as in cases as such, vote in favour of objections to allowing the authorisation of gmos. therefore, eh bildu has voted in favour of this objection.

in writing. an estimated 12 million eu citizens live in an eu country other than their country of origin, and many more stay temporarily in another eu country for study, work or simply for holidays. all these people may at some time come into contact with the administrative authorities of their country of residence. the scope of this regulation includes documents relating to marital status and other documents often requested by citizens, such as residence, nationality and criminal records. for those public documents, this regulation provides for exemption from legalisation and apostille, two administrative procedures traditionally provided for for cross-border public documents. provision is also made for facilitated acceptance of certified copies and certified translations. another key development of this regulation is the creation of multilingual standard forms for most of the public documents concerned. the proposal which is to be adopted is a major step forward for the citizens of europe. it eliminates red tape and gives substance to the principle of mutual trust.

in writing. ‒ with these new rules we are moving towards the achievement of a genuine common european area, a genuine political union and not just an economic one. in short, towards the achievement of a bigger and better europe. the ratification of the new rules facilitates free movement within the eu, as it involves simplifying the procedures for proving the authenticity of official documents such as birth or marriage certificates issued in another member state. to avoid the need for translations, a new multilingual form will be attached to the documents in some cases. the simplification will also apply to the documents that citizens living in another eu country must present if they wish to vote or stand as candidates in the european or municipal elections in their country of residence.

in writing. ‒ with the development of the competences of the european union, citizens are increasingly confronted with the union’s institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, without always having their procedural rights adequately protected. in a union under the rule of law it is necessary to ensure that procedural rights and obligations are always adequately defined, developed and complied with. citizens are entitled to expect a high level of transparency, efficiency, swift execution and responsiveness from the union’s institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. citizens are also entitled to receive adequate information regarding possibility to take any further action in the matter. over the years, the union has developed an extensive number of sectoral administrative procedures, in the form of both binding provisions and soft law, without necessarily taking into account the overall coherence of the system. this complex variety of procedures has resulted in gaps and inconsistencies in these procedures. to avoid the growing distance between european citizens and its institutions, urgent actions is need to modernise it, make it more friendly and transparent, a better communication campaign is needed in order to inform people of the positive work being done.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this resolution because its purpose is to ask the commission to draw up an action plan to propose to the parliament and the council a regulation of the procedures of the european union and its administrative function. i am in favour of implementing this type of improvement in administration and forcing the commission to respond to parliament's demands.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. this represents a cornerstone of green objectives and priorities. if the commission will come forward with a proposal on a european law of administrative procedure, as set out by parliament, the regulation will increase transparency and accessibility, enhance trust and improve the relationship between citizens and the union’s administration, thereby also reinforcing the legitimacy of the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because it is not aimed at solving the real problems which have put this important industry in such a difficult situation. the fundamental problem, despite the fact that the european authorities point to china, is the trade and competition policy of the european union. it is the continuing phases of liberalisation of the railway sector and the imposition of strict conditions on public procurement that expose this sector to international competition rather than putting the generation of jobs and growth ahead of competition. although it includes positive references to the participation of trade unions in decision-making and the attempt to propose industrial policy. the lack of any reflection on the liberalization of the sector forces me to vote against a resolution which will not solve the problems of european industry.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this resolution, since its purpose is to ask the commission to draw up an action plan to propose to parliament and the council a regulation of the procedures of the european union and its administrative function. i am in favour of implementing this type of improvement in administration and forcing the commission to respond to parliament's demands.
in writing. ‒ the rail industry is fundamental to creating an integrated mobility system, reducing coal consumption in the transport sector and adding efficiency to the european economy. from an industrial perspective, it is a world-leading sector with great potential for quality employment. the fragmentation of the internal market, unfair competition from certain external competitors and the progressive introduction of origin clauses in contracts awarded in third countries are real obstacles to maintaining and improving our leading position in the world. it is essential to apply the fourth railway package now and to rely on the competitiveness and capacity of our industries, as well as to modernise business models which do not allow the train to take off and to capture passenger and freight traffic in accordance with its virtues and capabilities.
in writing. ‒ the european rail equipment sector is strategically important for growth, employment and industrial innovation and for the transition to sustainable mobility, employing 400 000 workers, investing 2.7% of its annual turnover in r & d and representing 46% of the world market. while the eu maintains a high degree of openness to competition from third countries, there are numerous obstacles in the latter that discriminate against the european rail equipment sector. in addition, some competitors are pursuing an aggressive policy of expansion to other regions of the world with strong political support. the european railway equipment sector thus has to compete internationally with companies in third countries which are heavily backed by state aid, such as favourable export credits. i have supported this oral question and the accompanying motion for a resolution to ask the commission to ensure a better level playing field within the railway equipment sector and to develop an integrated and coherent industrial policy strategy which highlights the specificity and strategic importance of sectors such as railway equipment.

in writing. ‒ while the resolution does have some positive elements reference to the participation of the rail sector in reducing co2 emissions or concern for smes, it does not go against the logic of liberalisation and deregulation of the sector. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the railway sector is not left behind. that is why i voted against the resolution.

in writing. ‒ the european railway equipment sector currently employs 400 000 people. it is therefore an activity which we must take care of, because we are interested in promoting the railways, with interesting advantages for europe. for this reason, i join the resolution in which parliament calls for the maintenance of the european rail equipment sector's leadership in the world, a new agenda for innovation in the european rail equipment sector, the acquisition of the necessary skills to make the rail equipment sector ready for the future, support for smes, the improvement of the european market environment for suppliers and the promotion of demand for rail products, the boost of investment in rail projects and the improvement of strategic political support for the sector.

in writing. ‒ the european rail supply industry (rsi), which encompasses the manufacture of locomotives and rolling stock, and track, electrification, signalling and telecommunication equipment, as well as maintenance and parts services, and which includes numerous smes, as well as major industrial leaders, employs 400 000 employees, invests 2.7 % of its annual turnover in r&d and accounts for 46 % of the world rsi market. the railway sector overall, including operators and infrastructure, is responsible for more than 1 million direct and 1.2 million indirect jobs in the eu. recognising the rail supply industry as a key industry for europe’s competitiveness and capacity for innovation, i urge the ec to take all measures to ensure that europe maintains a technological and innovative advantage in this sector. competition rules with regards to china and other emerging actors should be considered. however i also believe that too many internal market physical and regulatory barriers remain in europe in order to have a single european market in the rail sector. rail is very far from aviation in this regard.
in writing. ‒ while the resolution does have some positive elements reference to the participation of the rail sector in reducing co2 emissions or concern for smes, it does not go against the logic of liberalisation and deregulation of the sector. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the railway sector is not left behind. that is why i voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ voted in favour - the rail supply industry is an important eu industrial actor for the transformation towards sustainable mobility and for meeting climate objectives. a coherent european industrial policy based on sustainability and competitiveness of eu manufacturing industry should recognise the importance of this sector and address the needs for: investing in r&d, innovation, developing skills, increasing demand and investment into (sustainable) rail projects, expanding smes suppliers’ base, and ensuring manufacturing is maintained in the eu. if the eu rail industry is still a market leader in technology and innovation today and an industry rooted in eu territory, it faces several challenges, including unfair competition on the eu and global markets in the participation of public procurement tenders, in particular from china’s giant state-owned and fully subsidised corporation benefitting from generous export subsidies outside the scope of oecd guidelines. the resolution ask for this purpose that the commission re-evaluates its market definitions to take the global market into account and enable itself to address the problem posed by mega-mergers in third countries, and, if desired, enable eu companies to make strategic alliances.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, secrecy, opacity, lack of transparency: that is the policy of the european union's international agreements, because what it wants to hide is the lack of democracy, an imperialist agenda in the political and economic spheres. that is why this parliament has had to fight every document, every note it has taken from the commission. and that is why it has been necessary to resort to the courts to obtain what the treaties provide: automatic and exhaustive access by parliament to all information relevant to the negotiations of the european union's international treaties. it is not surprising that this judicialisation is necessary: we have grown tired of receiving papers with censored content in commissions of inquiry such as luxleaks, not to mention the resistance to which we could see the atci documents. even today, in a partial, biased and secret way, as if we were not accountable to the european people for what the european union negotiates on their behalf. we have to learn from leaks and press reports about the european union's collaboration with morocco and the colonial exploitation of western sahara, the violation of the rights of refugees in turkey, the handing over of our data to american agencies and the sale of our agriculture, our industry and even labour standards through the acp, the ceta or the atci. the situation is particularly serious because parliament is the only democratically elected european institution. it is obvious that the treaties must be opened up so that parliament can express its opinion and decide on european foreign policy, which combines neo-colonial adventurism, subordination to nato and service to economic oligopolies. but in those areas, such as trade agreements, where the right of consultation and decision is already recognised, how can the commission justify that its current practices are transparent, if the information is fragmented and contains only the minutes of one party, preventing a global view of what is being negotiated, if it excludes certain committees of members or if confidentiality is used as a subterfuge so that access is only made in secret rooms where most of the documents, when they are legible, are marked 'confidential' to prevent the debate from being moved to those whom we represent, who are none other than the european people? we therefore do not consider the debate on transparency to be a purely technical one. it is a debate on how the european union has drifted so far from democratic principles that its political activity cannot withstand the light and the stenographers. while parliament is denied information, the media are used to assure us that if there were to be negotiations, they would be to ensure democracy, our social rights, our security, always respecting the will of the people. if so, why aren't we being kept informed? how can we believe that geopolitical considerations are not discussed when it comes to the revision of visas and tariffs? how can we believe that human rights are not the last consideration when discussing migrant and refugee agreements? how do you decide where to send our ships and our weapons to protect multinational interests and not global peace? who is pushing for the maximum liberalization in each and every trade agreement that is born in brussels, spearhead of the dismantling of the european social model itself? who has more voice? the employers, their experts? don't experts have an ideology? or do the interests of the big countries, including the united states, have more say than the 751 members of this house in preparing the meetings and the lines of external action? if not, have no fear, open your doors, your documents, regularly and without curtains, and allow parliamentary teams access to all, absolutely all information, although i fear that what you will show is the degradation of the european project against the rights of workers and peoples, in the world and in europe itself.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, once again in this parliament we have to address, to reject, the situation in the democratic republic of congo. this time, our strongest condemnation of the massacres in the eastern zone. i want to express our support for political and peaceful solutions to the conflict. military solutions bring more death, more pain and more violence to the population. we also want to express our concern about the strengthening of the us military command in africa and its destabilising role in various countries and also in the democratic republic of congo. we call for the dismantling and withdrawal of africom. the european union should also launch an independent investigation into the role of european multinationals in the violation of social and environmental rights and their links to the financing of armed groups in order to continue the exploitation of the congolese subsoil. the deputy executive director of the united nations environment programme in 2015 stated that 2% of the annual profits from exploiting natural resources went to finance these internal armed groups. we also believe that the non-interference and sovereignty of the democratic republic of the congo must be guaranteed. and, commissioner, respect for this political sovereignty means that the population can benefit from its natural resources, for which it is necessary to establish control over the activities of multinational companies by reviewing and abolishing all mining and forestry contracts, as well as respecting the right to food sovereignty and the cancellation of debt, which, we understand, are essential measures to meet the most basic and urgent needs of the population.
on behalf of the green group, we are again here in this house to condemn the terrible situation in the congo - in this case, the massacres in the eastern part of the country - and the commission representative will understand that we are a little frustrated because we have just approved another one, and yet it seems that this has no bearing on the terrible situation of a large part of the congolese people. we welcome this joint resolution, a resolution which we signed in the interests of consensus, but which we would have liked to have been more forceful at some point, especially when it criticises the role played by monusco, the united nations stabilisation mission in the democratic republic of congo, a mission which has been accused by independent actors of being passive, of not playing its assigned role, which is to defend the civilian population against these massacres. we hope that the investigation we are also calling for in this resolution will be carried out and that it will be clarified exactly whether the mission is not being fulfilled and who is responsible. we welcome the fact that some of the key points of the terrible situation in the congo are being brought out. firstly, the fact that women are the preferred victims and that the rape of women and girls is being used as a weapon of mass warfare; that child soldiers are being recruited, who will have no chance in life in the midst of this horror. and above all, let us speak of the conflict over illegal mining. and here the commission has a role to play, because european companies have a great deal of responsibility in this and it would be important for us to go beyond declarations and to take active measures of sanction, of investigation, to find out which european multinationals are involved in this trade which, in the end, is the ultimate justification for the terrible situation that this territory is experiencing. one of the points in the resolution is the possibility of sanctioning those who are directly responsible for these massacres. let's not shake hands! let us also take up this european responsibility and show that the european union is not abandoning the people of the congo.
madam president, i pay my respects to kashetu. the democratic republic of congo is in the midst of one of the longest humanitarian crises in its history. the massacres and attacks, especially in the eastern part, are causing more than three million displaced persons, half a million of whom have already fled to neighbouring countries. the constant kidnappings, disappearances, sexual abuse of women and children and more than a thousand rapes a day: i am talking about indiscriminate attacks, forced recruitment of children. i want to condemn the terrible acts that took place in beni, lubero and butembo, which took the lives of 1 160 people. i want to express my solidarity and support to the victims and their families. i would like to stress, madam president, the need for the resumption of joint operations between the armed forces of the republic of congo and monusco, because this is the only way, in my view, to counter the abominable actions of armed groups such as the democratic forces for the liberation of rwanda or the allied democratic forces, among others. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'customs' in the definition of the concept of 'commercial'. finally, i would like to draw attention to the need for the next presidential and legislative elections, which would be decisive in advancing stability and progress. the country needs to be institutionalised as soon as possible and the military and civil justice systems reformed to end criminal impunity and effectively protect citizens. the hague court's condemnation of bemba should also be exemplary.
on behalf of the alde group. madam president i thank the representatives of the commission and the council, ladies and gentlemen. i keep the selfie of orlando's killer in my office and they ask me why. i don't want to forget the face of banality and cruelty in this age of the internet. i do not think that anyone has any doubts about the need to prevent and stop the capacity of action and expansion of terrorist organizations. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat terrorism, and i am sure that the commission will take them into account. we must be able to effectively question a political logic that walks on human suffering and for this the most important thing in the long term is to disable hatred, dehumanization and the legitimization of cruelty. on the other hand, the ideology that recruits fanatics also generates other forms of hatred. so fighting crime and achieving prevention is crucial, and it's not easy. young people need to get ideas that prevent the legitimization of violence against others. they need to prevent the temptation to hate other human collectives, whether they are invented or real; to prevent the temptation to see their own neighbours, their own family as enemies. in this globalised world, under the domination of communication technologies, it has changed the way we perceive reality. the new generations in particular must develop their own but coherent vision of what the dignity and humanity of each person means. we therefore welcome the new measures taken by the commission, since the european union strategy adopted in 2005 has become obsolete and european jihadists are statistically overrepresented among those who are training from anywhere in the world. experts insist on linking quality studies on the phenomenon of violent radicalisation to public policy making. experts, local authorities and citizens are asking us not to dwell on rhetoric of limited effectiveness. those who aspire to the moral disintegration of our societies in order to bend us and impose their sexual obsessions on us should know that we will defeat them with the law and with respect for fundamental rights.
madam president, if you combine jihadist radicalization with hatred of the muslim community or islamophobia, you have an explosive cocktail. the precedent is there not to repeat itself: the destabilization of the area for geopolitical reasons of control of hydrocarbons, which some of our allies use - or we ourselves use - the divide and conquer, throwing some communities against others... the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force. saudi arabia, moreover, has a bull: from 2008 to 2011, 17.3 billion in arms exports by the european union. solutions: cutting funding, cutting the supply of weapons, deepening the solutions negotiated with regional actors in the framework of the un - that is, non-interference - and also combating, with real plans, poverty and social exclusion in our neighborhoods, turned into ghettos where the wahhabis or takfiris find the breeding ground.
madam president, two opening words: solidarity and rejection. solidarity with the victims of magnanville, uk our friend jo cox, and with the victims of orlando. and i refuse. i reject without palliation any form of terror. i welcome and thank the commission for the communication it published on 14 june on the prevention of radicalisation. we are facing a new and very complex threat. unfortunately, the recent attacks have shown us how easily these individuals can train themselves through social media and the agility and speed of the spread of terrorist propaganda online. that is why i, as rapporteur for europol, and the whole of parliament have given the iru the legal basis it needs to carry out its work. but i also want to say that i think that there is a need for continuing research into the causes and forms of this phenomenon so that we can act consistently and, above all, quickly. support the necessary interoperability of information systems by providing access with due guarantees to state security forces and bodies, in particular by reviewing the schengen information system as soon as possible. we need to make more use of the srs - the radicalisation awareness network - and equip it with more skills and resources, improve the training of prison staff both to identify and prevent and to contribute to the reintegration of prisoners, promote and encourage greater coordination and cooperation between all member states, especially with europol and eurojust, and enhance social inclusion and the values of the union. that is why, commissioner, i support the commission's proposal for the use of erasmus+, education and youth forums for intercultural debate. in conclusion, the union and all states must strengthen and improve all the tools necessary to combat and prevent any form of radicalisation.
madam president, once again, in the minutes of silence, the candles, the tears and the rage at this terrorism which is relentlessly striking us and which we must defend ourselves against without really knowing when it will strike us again. yesterday it was the young people in orlando or a couple of cops doing their duty to protect us. to all of them i want to say a huge "thank you" for giving their lives so that i can exercise my freedom. the terrorists want to scare us. we know this well here in brussels, when they repeat their threats and we do not know where we will be safe. we can't give up our way of life, because that would be the same as telling them that they've won this new war that is terrorism. but if europeans are to continue to live in an area of freedom and security, we need to take measures to prevent terrorism and combat radicalisation. we must do so without any qualms, as the people's party does, which has made the fight against terrorism a priority, contrary to those in this house who do not seem to understand that in terrorism prevention is very important, but so are security measures, the exchange of information and defending ourselves, by all means permitted by law, from those who have only the end in mind. we need to fight online recruitment of those who join isis; we also need to fight radicalization in prisons; and we need to empower education. but above all we need unity and political will to fight effectively against terrorism, a will which fades quickly after an attack, putting the security of europeans at risk. i would like to end by remembering all the european victims, inside and outside our borders, and by asking the commission to do what i have been asking for the last seven years: a european directive on victims of terrorism, because victims of terrorism are killed in order to frighten the whole of society. we are all victims of terrorism.
the recent terrorist attacks in europe have highlighted the urgent need to address the radicalisation that leads to violent extremism and terrorism. the majority of the alleged terrorists involved in the attacks were european citizens, born and raised in the member states, who became radicalized and conspired against their fellow citizens to commit atrocities. preventing radicalisation is a key part of the fight against terrorism, as highlighted in the european agenda on security. the design and implementation of measures to combat radicalisation is primarily a matter for member states. the eu has supported its work in this area for more than a decade. in 2005, the eu's counter-terrorism strategy identified prevention as one of the four pillars of its actions. this latter communication also complements the united nations plan of action to prevent violent extremism presented in january 2016. for these reasons, the commission has launched this communication addressing the eu's contribution to supporting member states in preventing radicalisation leading to violent extremism in the form of terrorism.

madam president, madam commissioner, in the face of some of the catastrophic statements we have heard, i would like to stress that in recent years we have been taking fundamental steps in the european union to ensure a more sustainable and effective management of our seas and our fishing activity. the agreement we are discussing today is not only important in ensuring a good multiannual management plan for cod, herring and sprat fisheries in northern european waters: we are looking at an agreement which will serve as an example and a basis for drawing up other regional management plans, which we will approve in the future, for fish stocks in different parts of the continent. and in this plan, we have talked about many things - fishing mortality range, biomass; also after tacs and fishing quotas - but we have talked mainly about competences. and i want to stress the competence of each institution and that we must strictly respect that. the aim is therefore to establish multiannual plans which take account of all the aspects surrounding the management of this activity, ensuring, on the one hand, a balanced and sustainable exploitation of fish stocks, but at the same time protecting the activity of our fishermen, which is also very important.
madam president, i would like to congratulate mr wałęsa and the negotiating team on their efforts to bring this multiannual plan for cod, herring and swordfish from the baltic sea, the first one after the reform of the cfp, to fruition. i hope that once again transparency and objectivity will be the key to fixing fishing quotas. the council's reluctance to accept that parliament has codecision in this area has already blocked three multiannual plans, the anchovy plan, for which i was rapporteur, the jellyfish plan and the codfish plan. this attitude of the member states, which is contrary to the treaty of lisbon, has allowed the fixing and allocation of fishing quotas to remain opaque. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries sector is not left behind. the victims have been the professionals of the sea and in many cases the state of fisheries. we therefore support the generalization of this system of long-term management plans. it is better for the sea and its balance and for those who live off what they catch in it.
madam president, it is a step forward that we analyse the situation of fisheries in the baltic sea in a joint way and not by species, because that is true and helps to find solutions to improve biodiversity. but we want to stress that it is essential that all these regulations really respond to the specificities of the territories and their people because, unfortunately, the needs of fishermen are not always taken into account by the policies of the union. our fishermen and, above all, low-impact fishing gear must be at the heart of these policies. that is why it is essential to respect their way of life and their culture. fisheries policy cannot be made without the people of the sea to ensure their present and their future. we believe that we need to take a further step towards managing a more sustainable model within the states themselves. we must be vigilant in the allocation of fishing quotas to prevent large vessels, which destroy marine resources, from fishing at their own expense and, above all, to ensure that those who really respect the sea can make a decent living from fishing, namely fishermen.

commitment, it is really timely to debate the impact of the joint comprehensive plan of action (jcpoa) on the relations between iran and eu businesses. this is really important. let me first of all the joint commission overseeing the implementation of the deal. let me assure you that we have faithfully met our commitments, as agreed under the plan of action, by lifting the sanctions and questions. this has demonstrated ongoing commitment to provide clarity to business operators and to keep the guidance a living document. we also invited the director of the office of foreign assets control to inform our finance ministers and encourage him to further reach out to the private sector. in addition, we are planning to hold a symposium in brussels on the lifting of sanctions for business operators, with contributions from both eu and us experts. in the same spirit, the high representative chaired a ministerial meeting on 19 may 2016 with the foreign ministers of germany, laundering and countering financing of terrorism and of course, more needs to be done. cooperation and consultations in the financial action task force framework should be treated as a priority. our visit to iran has served as an opportunity to establish the basis for cooperating and providing assistance in these domains. despite all the challenges, the results of the plan are already positive, with a 22% growth in trade between the eu and iran in the first quarter of 2016, compared to the same period last year. thirty-three iranian banks have been reconnected to swift so far. more recently, it was reported that 200 small and medium-sized international banks, including european ones, have started correspondent relationship with iranian banks. major banks are becoming more comfortable as they start to comprehend the new rules in practice. to enhance the economic dialogue and cooperation, in october we are planning a european economic mission to iran with representatives of european smes and businesses. as an element of the trade promotion role of the member states, another promising avenue is the use of national credit insurance companies, which could provide cover and additional reassurance to investors. all of these issues together form the complex reality. it will still require, of course, some time as the international business community needs to adjust to the new reality of the post-implementation deal. while we cannot force banks or other businesses to take certain decisions in commercial matters, we will continue to be committed to ensuring that iran can reap the benefit of the plan of action. with that in mind, we can better continue our consultations with the us in order to get as much clarity as possible, continue reaching out to the european business community and provide assistance to iran’s banking and financial system. dialogue and persistence are the way forward.

política climática ambiciosa con una política energética sostenible.
the rapporteur. mr president, i thank you once again for the tone of the debate and for the contributions of my colleagues. i want to expand on one of the points of my initial intervention. the question of the development of renewable energies is also a question of energy sovereignty. europe cannot bear the growing bill for its energy imports and plunder the fossil resources of the globe. on the contrary, it should improve energy efficiency and savings and encourage energy production on the continent itself. in these circumstances, conventional fossil fuels in europe have a supporting role in the energy transition, but it will undoubtedly have to be centred on the development of renewable energy. it is also a challenge that must be met for reasons of ecological sustainability, and it is to these issues, which are well reflected in today's debate, that we are trying to respond in this report. commissioner, i disagree with your optimism that some countries will be able to achieve the targets and objectives set by 2020. and by 2030 we will not give up anything that the european parliament sets. among other things, because this house is sovereign over the council. first of all, we have tried to make the past requests of this parliament on the development of renewables consistent with the reality of the member states. but what we cannot tolerate is, in any case, less ambition than we have shown so far. the current renewable energy directive must be fully implemented, and we need more ambitious targets for 2030 than those proposed by the commission and the council. in addition, mechanisms that have proven their efficiency in facilitating investment in renewables and their preferential entry into the market, as well as greater energy democracy of self-consumption of public investment, should be promoted. that must be the message that comes out of parliament today.
in writing. faced with the challenge of decarbonisation and climate agreements, no country can be allowed to backtrack on the path to implementing renewable energy. when the presence of renewable energies increases worldwide, in countries such as spain it decreases by 4% per year. the spanish government has torpedoed any investment in renewable energy with retroactive legislation, which ruined investors, smes and spanish industry in the sector. it is against the promotion of renewable energies to penalize self-consumers by imposing the sun tax or banning collective self-consumption as is also the case in spain. by acting against renewables, we are acting against energy independence and security and against the fight to avoid climate change. on the other hand, the renewables sector is a technological sector with skilled workers. in spain, the attack has led to the loss of more than 80 000 jobs, and this at a time when job opportunities in this sector are increasing in the rest of the world. part of the blame for this decline lies with unambitious targets, and the new targets for a 40% deployment of renewables in europe by 2030 should be revised.

(the following is a transcription of the interpretation of the original speech from arabic into english.) – mr president, in the name of allah, the most merciful, may i first of all thank you for this parliament, so that you have some guidelines in thinking about our situation as we seek peace in our part of the world. i would also like to thank you all for all the different kinds of aid you have given, aiding us in institution-building and helping us establish the bases for a democratic regime which will be stable in the future and which will be able to comply with international criteria for democracy, and in particular we want to establish a proper rule of law and proper respect for human rights. so once again, our thanks to this parliament for the recognition you have given our country. recognise the state of palestine. i would also say this. when talking about a two-state solution, if you believe in a two-state solution you have to recognise both states and not just one of them. a hundred years have passed since the balfour declaration back in 1917. sixty-eight years have passed since al-nakbah, the catastrophe which we suffered when in 1948 the israeli forces were guilty of slaughter and massacre in our part world, and this led to hundreds of thousands of our citizens having to migrate. this turned these hundreds of thousands of people into refugees. more than 485 of our occupation of a country we have not seen elsewhere in the world in the 20th century or in the 21st century. and all this in full view of the international community and in full view of the international authorities. we have been through so many black periods throughout history, and we are still going through a black period. our palestinian people are suffering from occupation, from suppression. we are suffering from arbitrary action by the israelis. we are suffering from racism, hateful racism, and our people are living abroad as refugees. they are living in poverty, in a very precarious situation. now we have decided to resist. we have decided to remain in our country, on our land. we have decided to continue our efforts to put an end to israeli occupation by using political, diplomatic and peaceful means. we have been successful in these efforts at international level, but we are not making progress in terms of our relations with israel. we have used every effort in order to implement the agreements which have been signed. we have complied with our commitments, and we are calling on the israelis to comply with their commitments, but the israelis refuse to respect these commitments and continue to oppress us and to dominate us in every area of life. the israelis are trying to change the situation in the city of jerusalem. they are trying to change its historic identity. they are infringing holy places – christian and islamic and muslim. they are continuing to build their colonies by confiscating our territory, by flattening our houses. israel is still imprisoning thousands of our people. today, israel is still a violent state. every day we see cases of extreme violence for which the israelis are guilty. we have seen the colonists have burned down houses only recently in which people were living. in particular, a young man died in the latest attack from the israelis when his house was burnt down. every day we see murders, extra-judicial killings. and this israeli attitude, this israeli behaviour is such that some israeli politicians have started criticising their own government, for example, mr herzog, leader of the opposition, or ya’alon, a former army leader, and ehud barak, and a former head of the armed forces, and journalists. all these people – israelis – announcing that the israeli government’s behaviour is fascist and racist, and i am quoting them there. resolution 181 of the united nations divided the historic territory of palestine into two states in a more or less fair sharing out of the land, but since then israel has used force of arms to occupy 78% of historic palestinian territory. this was back in 1948, but that was not good enough for israel. it occupied the rest of our territory in 1967. people still quote that united nations resolution– resolution 181 – today and they say that this resolution should not be interpreted literally all the way through, but only certain paragraphs should be implemented. i would say that united nations resolution 181 has to be applied in its totality. despite international resolutions, united nations resolutions and the efforts of the international community to find a solution, a two-state solution, despite all these efforts our state is still not independent, despite the fact that we are now a member state of the united nations, and that since 2012. and we are now a member of a great number of international organisations, as well as the united nations organisation. we have ratified a great number of international conventions, we are recognised by 138 states around the world. in order to make progress towards peace and to put an end to our years of suffering, we have now accepted the establishment of the state of palestine on an area which is less than a quarter of the area of historic palestine; 22% of our historic territory. we have accepted that as a state, respecting the 1967 borders, and that is an enormous sacrifice. since the madrid conference and since the oslo agreements we have made no further progress. we are going round in circles in negotiations. we are just negotiating for negotiation’s sake at the moment. and this is being imposed upon us by israel. they are trying to gain time in this process so that they can change things on the ground, which will make it less and less possible for us to find a two-state solution. today israel is carrying on with its colonisation. it is continuing to expropriate our land. it is building walls and all this is also being done on a racist basis. under our other united nations resolutions calling on israel to put an end to colonisation, these resolutions have called on israel to do away with colonisation, to reverse it, but nevertheless, israel is carrying on with these projects. we are calling on israel simply to freeze this colonisation so that negotiations can properly start, but israel still does not stop colonising. it is carrying on. furthermore, over the last six years, israel has started at least three wars in gaza. it has killed thousands of people. israel has killed dozens of palestinian families. there are hundreds of families which have quite simply disappeared. there is no longer a record of them in our civil registers. these families have quite simply disappeared because of the three wars waged by israel in gaza in the last six years. israel has destroyed houses. it has destroyed factories and since the occupation i can tell you this: one million palestinians have been jailed by israel at some time or another. at the moment we have 7 000 of our people held as prisoners of war. that is the bitter reality and the dangerous reality we are facing and is it not time to put an end to the israeli occupation of palestine? why is international law not being applied? (applause)why is international law not being implemented in the case of israel? you have here a state attacking another state. when that happens normally the whole world stands up and punishes the member of the commission. – the commission expresses concern that the limited powers delegated to it by the co-legislators may hinder the timely implementation in eu law of measures taken by iccat in the future that revise or update the control scheme of this organisation. the commission therefore declares that it considers this regulation to be without prejudice to any future position of the institution as regards the recourse to articles 290 and 291 tfeu for the transposition of regional fisheries management organisation measures. the commission furthermore reserves the right to propose amendments to the regulation increasing the number of measures which should be adopted by delegated or implementing acts in case the transposition through the ordinary legislative procedure leads to delays which would jeopardise the eu’s ability to comply with its international obligations.
member of the commission. – when proposing and adopting delegated acts under the regionalisation provisions of this plan, the commission will comply with the framework set out in the basic regulation (in particular article 18), and the practice established under the basic regulation in implementing the regionalisation process will continue as it has since 2014.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the establishment of this committee of inquiry into money laundering and tax evasion and avoidance, and the appointment of its members. after the scandals of the panama papers, which have revealed not only the passivity of european governments in the face of such practices but also the direct involvement of different leaders, this type of commission is of great importance if there is really a will to reverse such situations. for this, the committee of inquiry cannot serve only to clear up political responsibility, but must propose effective measures to put an end to this type of crime both through offshore companies and in the case of panama and within our own continent. we therefore welcome the creation of this committee and hope that it will be allowed to work without restriction and that its conclusions will be taken into account.
in writing. ‒ we are in favour of the creation of this special committee, set up in the wake of the panama papers scandal to investigate possible omissions by the commission and the member states in transposing european union directives to effectively combat tax evasion and money laundering. we consider that the information contained in the panama papers raises serious questions about the effectiveness and even the will of the european authorities to combat tax evasion effectively, and we believe that it is the duty of parliament to investigate this to the last detail.
in writing. ‒ following the scandal caused by the revelation of the existence of thousands of opaque bank accounts for tax evasion in panama, the european socialists call for the establishment of a committee of inquiry, since very important european citizens have been involved in this scheme and the financial interests of the union may also have been harmed. this commission will investigate, among other issues, whether member states have correctly implemented the anti-money laundering directive to prevent money laundering through the creation of offshore companies, whether they cooperated in relation to the automatic exchange of information, whether the legislation in the audit sector has been well implemented to avoid conflicts of interest, and also to prevent them from being involved in tax havens and whether the legislation on the banking sector (crd iv) has also been well implemented. in order to finalise the constitution of this committee of inquiry, i have voted in favour of the list of members of this house who will be part of it, including, and i congratulate my colleagues, ramón jáuregui and juan fernando lópez aguilar.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the establishment of this committee of inquiry into money laundering and tax evasion and avoidance, and the appointment of its members. after the scandals of the panama papers, which have revealed not only the passivity of european governments in the face of such practices but also the direct involvement of different leaders, this type of commission is of great importance if there is really a will to reverse such situations. for this, the committee of inquiry cannot serve only to clear up political responsibility, but must propose effective measures to put an end to this type of crime both through offshore companies and in the case of panama and within our own continent. we therefore welcome the creation of this committee and hope that it will be allowed to work without restriction and that its conclusions will be taken into account.
in writing. ‒ my support for the proposal with the names of the people who will be part of the committee of inquiry that we decided to set up a few weeks ago to determine whether there has been a breach of eu legislation on evasion and money laundering in relation to the so-called 'panama papers'.
in writing. ‒ following the scandal known as panaleaks, which revealed the existence of thousands of opaque bank accounts for tax evasion in panama, the european socialists call for the establishment of a committee of inquiry, since very important european citizens have been involved in this scheme and the financial interests of the union may also have been harmed. this commission will investigate, among other issues, whether member states have correctly implemented the anti-money laundering directive to prevent money laundering through the creation of offshore companies, whether they cooperated in relation to the automatic exchange of information, whether the legislation in the audit sector has been well implemented to avoid conflicts of interest, and also to prevent them from being involved in tax havens and whether the legislation on the banking sector (crd iv) has also been well implemented. in order to finalise the constitution of this committee of inquiry, i have voted in favour of the list of members of this house who will be part of it, among whom i congratulate my colleagues ramón jáuregui and juan fernando lópez aguilar.
in writing. ‒ we are in favour of the creation of this special committee, set up in the wake of the panama papers scandal to investigate possible omissions by the commission and the member states in transposing european union directives to effectively combat tax evasion and money laundering. we consider that the information contained in the panama papers raises serious questions about the effectiveness and even the will of the european authorities to combat tax evasion effectively, and we believe that it is the duty of parliament to investigate this to the last detail.

in writing. ‒ i support the institution of the committee of inquiry to investigate alleged contraventions and maladministration in the application of european union law in relation to money laundering, tax avoidance and tax evasion. the panama leaks and scandal must be investigated and we should make sure these abuses are not repeated. parliament has its role to play as we represent the european citizens that are the victims of these frauds as most of them pay their taxes according to the law. it is morally wrong to avoid and evade taxes in a period when many european citizens, smes and most big companies pay their fair share of taxes and respect the rules. i am proud to be part of the panama inquiry. my work will focus on all actions to combat economic fraud, capital outflow and money laundering.

in writing. ‒ by these appointments, this parliament is demonstrating its will to fight these practices. it is important that european citizens see us as part of the solution and not as part of the problem, and i think it is appropriate to vote in favour of this decision.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the creation of this committee of inquiry, of which i will be a member, into the so-called panama papers, as it represents a further step by the european parliament towards greater transparency and accountability with regard to money laundering, tax evasion and tax avoidance. as a member of this committee, i would like to argue that this is an excellent opportunity to show the european citizen that his representatives, that is to say, we, want to be part of the solution and not part of the problem. together with my remaining 64 colleagues, we will work together to identify any mistakes that may have been made both by action and by omission. thank you very much.
in writing. ‒ the euro-mediterranean agreement (euromed) promotes economic integration and reform in 16 countries neighbouring the eu, in north africa and the middle east. this partnership aims at greater economic integration in the region and states that the eu can offer its neighbours a privileged relationship that benefits both sides. parliament was asked to adopt three protocols, mainly technical, in order to give its consent to the approval of the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement and to add the names of the countries of the 2004 enlargement and bulgaria and romania since their accession to the eu to the official documents. i could not vote in favour of this report because such agreements lead to the establishment of free trade agreements, which we oppose because of their disastrous consequences for the majority of the population, but on the other hand i recognise the will of the lebanese authorities and respect the decision of a sovereign country. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ we abstain in this vote because we believe that, although this type of agreement is intended to advance an eminently economic and trade integration which excludes fundamental dimensions of integration (such as respect for human rights in general and labour and women's rights in particular, free movement of people, recognition of academic qualifications, dealing with environmental issues of common interest, and others), it is the citizens of the states who must choose the type and degree of association they wish to maintain with the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution by which the european parliament gives its consent to the conclusion of the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of lebanon, of the other part, on a framework agreement between the european union and the republic of lebanon on the general principles for the participation of the republic of lebanon in union programmes. this agreement, and the two protocols voted on in this house, establish economic, financial and technical rules which enable lebanon to participate in certain european union programmes. the specific terms and conditions for the participation of lebanon in each specific programme shall be determined by the negotiation of agreements between the commission and the competent authorities in lebanon.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it represents an indispensable step forward in the exchange of tax information with the principality of monaco. while the exchange of information has proven to be insufficient for member states to take action against the main tax evaders and avoiders on the continent, it is an important step for states to be able to identify such capital and its owners. the provisions contained in this agreement therefore represent an objective improvement in the operation of the exchange of information with monaco. although this type of measure does not pursue the prohibition of the use of tax havens by european capital, it is an important step forward in order to be able to carry out more radical measures to tax the capital where wealth is generated. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report, whereby the eu and monaco agree to exchange information on financial accounts in their respective territories, in order to improve the capacity of the tax authority to identify taxpayers, apply tax law in cross-border situations, and identify possible cases of tax evasion.
in writing. ‒ i think this is an agreement in the right direction to combat fraud and tax evasion and money laundering. the geographical location of monaco, a state of its own embedded in the union, made it incomprehensible that any form of banking secrecy was maintained for the members of the union. the information to be exchanged automatically must be relevant to all banking concepts of the asset holder in monegasque banks, such as account balances or income from the sale of financial assets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it represents an indispensable step forward in the exchange of tax information with the principality of monaco. while the exchange of information has proven to be insufficient for member states to take action against the main tax evaders and avoiders on the continent, it is an important step for states to be able to identify such capital and its owners. the provisions contained in this agreement therefore represent an objective improvement in the operation of the exchange of information with monaco. although this type of measure does not pursue the prohibition of the use of tax havens by european capital, it is an important step forward in order to be able to carry out more radical measures to tax the capital where wealth is generated. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ on 22 february 2016, the european union signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts with the principality of monaco. this is one of the mechanisms established by the european union and neighbouring states to cooperate in the fight against tax fraud and evasion. these agreements will make it possible to share with these states data on account receipts, account balances and proceeds from the disposal of assets. in continuation of my votes in favour of the fight against tax evasion and tax evasion, i voted in favour of this cooperation with the principality of monaco.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report, whereby the eu and monaco agree to exchange information on financial accounts in their respective territories, in order to improve the capacity of the tax authority to identify taxpayers, apply tax law in cross-border situations, and identify possible cases of tax evasion.

in writing. ‒ this agreement represents an important step in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. under it we will ensure that the member states of the union and monaco automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of the respective countries, so that the taxpayer can avoid hiding assets representing income or assets on which taxes have not been paid. the report aims to ensure that monaco applies enhanced measures equivalent to those provided for in the legal framework of the european union and that those measures comply with the procedures for the automatic exchange of information. and here, we are no longer talking only about income such as interest or dividends, but also account balances and income from the sale of financial assets. in view of the above and because i believe that we must enforce tax legislation in crossborder situations, i am voting in favour of adopting this report.
in writing. ‒ my vote in favour of the recommendation in favour of the eu-monaco agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information with a view to improving tax cooperation and compliance with international tax obligations. the agreement represents an important step forward in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion and updates the 2004 agreement, which ensured that monaco applied measures equivalent to those provided for in the eu directive on taxation of savings income.

in writing. ‒ this agreement represents a further step in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion in the european union. it will be more difficult to find cases in which european citizens hide alleged funds initially intended for taxation in banks in the principality. the big breakthrough that i think has been made with this resolution has been to expand the information exchanged between monaco and the european union, because the data that will be transferred from 2018 onwards will include bank account balances as well as income and transfers. greater cooperation, such as is sought in such measures, will strengthen the effectiveness of laws imposed by both the member states and the union, generate more confidence among taxpayers who fairly pay their taxes, and shield the authorities from future strategies to evade their responsibilities. finally, the achievement of such a positive agreement is a clear demonstration of institutional competence and a proof of a constructive reaction to some of the tax scandals which have recently been reported in the press.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report, since it calls for funds to compensate and provide for compensatory measures in cases of relocation or closure of companies due to structural changes in markets due to globalisation. the aim is to help workers made redundant and young people without education or employment in the hainaut region of belgium, which is already suffering from unemployment, in the manufacture of industrial machinery and equipment, following a previous process of redundancies. these are measures which, if they did not exist, would leave the workers concerned in a worse position. such measures have only short-term effects, but do not solve the problem in the long term, since the question of employment and relocations should be approached differently. on the one hand, europe needs an investment plan, which is very different from the juncker plan, and a different employment policy, in order to act in the field of employment. secondly, this alternative should consist in investing in activities for the future, especially in a change of production model.

mr president, today is a great day for tuna fishermen, and especially for those in the canary islands. the european parliament has said, by an overwhelming majority, that the allocation of quotas for bluefin tuna must be more fair and that member states must take account of traditional vessels that are engaged in small-scale and more sustainable fishing. and that's our case. the recovery plan has clearly worked. there is therefore a possibility of increasing the quotas considerably, and this increase should be mainly directed at these fleets. it cannot happen again that a small-scale fleet such as the canary islands, with a miserable quota, has to see this fishery closed down in 24 hours, having consumed its quota. i thank parliament for the majority support for my proposal, and my vote is a resounding yes to sustainable fishing and a much fairer allocation of bluefin tuna quotas.
mr president, i want to support this regulation, which translates the recommendations of the iccat into european legislation, and to support a methodology which, according to scientific estimates, is gradually succeeding in recovering the bluefin tuna stocks at sea. this species is crucial, especially for the delicate mediterranean ecosystem, and one of the most valued in the world. recovery and maintenance of fishing activity must therefore go hand in hand. in this connection, i would like to stress my support for three fundamental points. the first is that i fully agree to give special recognition to the traditional fishing methods used for this species: longline fishing, live bait fishing and trawling. we are talking about gear which has a low impact on marine ecosystems, a high degree of selectivity in catches and, in addition, a considerable capacity to create jobs. the second is to promote a more equitable distribution of fishing quotas between the different fleets, with particular regard to small-scale and artisanal fishing. and finally, to consolidate the powers of this parliament in the implementation of the recommendations of the regional fisheries organisations, which are the responsibility of this house and the council and should not be resolved by means of delegated acts from the commission.
mr president, i would like to take this opportunity to explain why i abstained on this report. it is because in passing this parliament's regulation to the council we have lost something: the explicit defence of additional and specific quotas for bluefin tuna. a reference to the mattresses, as is done in this document, is not sufficient. we must defend and support them, because bluefin tuna represents fishing with rights, fishing linked to a territory and a local economy. it represents environmentally sustainable fishing, although the pp government has forgotten about it in its unfair allocation of quotas. i do not want to go into too much detail, because all this is something which this house is already aware of and which it will have to defend more firmly against the governments of the council in the future. we're not abandoning our commitment. we have presented two pilot projects to the committee on fisheries, with which we seek to protect and defend the production of bluefin tuna by means of specific quotas and a special label for this product, an initiative which i am confident will receive a favourable vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to incorporate into union law the measures of the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean, adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas at its annual meetings between 2012 and 2014, ensuring their uniform and effective implementation throughout the european union. this new regulation will repeal council regulation (ec) no 302/2009, which was already amended in 2014 to incorporate the measures relating to fishing seasons adopted by iccat in 2012 and 2013. i think it is appropriate to support this initiative to revise an obsolete regulation, which solves some technical problems, and which was passed with great consensus in the committee on fisheries. i would like to stress, however, that the text resulting from the interinstitutional negotiations is much less ambitious than the text which came out of parliament itself. although the importance of artisanal fishing is emphasized, specific references to a traditional and sustainable fishing technique such as cod trawling have been removed, which in my view deserves specific mention in this regulation.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because it represents a serious step backwards in favour of industrial tuna fishing and a fair distribution of fishing quotas. this report is the result of the trilogues with the commission and the council on the bluefin tuna recovery plan. the initial position of parliament, which we support, contained provisions in favour of traditional, sustainable and small-scale arts, specifically on the craft of making rugs. the parliament's proposal would have improved the situation of the cages by increasing the quotas for the cages, which would have led to an increase in the sustainable exploitation of tuna. however, all these references have been erased in the process of the trilogues, relegating the almadraba to a mere reference without any binding power. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ we voted against because, while the report underlines the role of artisanal fishing gear such as traditional traps, we believe that when implementing the recovery plan, the eu should place even greater emphasis on the use of traditional traps which contribute to the restoration of tuna stocks and have very little impact on marine ecosystems due to the low level of energy consumption and bycatch. we also feel it necessary to point out that in practice the distribution of quotas among the member states does not apply article 17 of the cfp, which calls for the allocation to be based on 'transparent and objective criteria, including those of an environmental, social and economic nature'.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to incorporate into union law the measures of the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean, adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas at its annual meetings between 2012 and 2014. in this respect, uniform and effective application of these measures is ensured throughout the eu. this new regulation will repeal council regulation (ec) no 302/2009, which was already amended in 2014 to incorporate the measures relating to fishing seasons adopted by iccat in 2012 and 2013. i think it is appropriate to support this initiative to revise an obsolete regulation which was negotiated with great consensus in the committee on fisheries. i would like to stress, however, that the text resulting from the interinstitutional negotiations is less ambitious than the text which came out of parliament itself. while the importance of artisanal fishing is highlighted, specific references to a traditional and sustainable fishing art such as trawling have been removed.
in writing. ‒ thanks to the efforts of fishermen, bluefin tuna stocks in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean have been rebuilt. the report we are debating takes this into account and simply proposes to transpose the iccat convention, that is to say the convention of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas. the european commission, in order to act quickly, has of course tried to introduce implementing and delegated acts in the proposal for a regulation, in order to increase its power to the detriment of the european parliament. but meps voted amendments to remove these provisions, in order to defend parliament's prerogatives. it should also be noted that the new regulation provides greater protection for small-scale fishermen, who use traditional fishing methods such as cod. these fishing methods are very selective and therefore respectful of the environment. in conclusion, the amended draft law preserves parliament's control, defends small-scale fishing methods and does not go beyond the iccat recommendations, i.e. does not impose unnecessary constraints on fishermen. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ following the same line of argument as the rapporteur, i believe that the objective of the transposition of the icao recommendations is uniform application throughout the eu. this uniform application should aim at ensuring a level playing field for all operators involved in the tuna fishery, including operators from third countries. otherwise, if different rules are applied to foreign fleets, all the efforts made and all the restrictions applied to eu fishermen will have been in vain. this transposition is also particularly important because of the role of artisanal fishing gear in the conservation of stocks. i believe that the european union should pay particular attention to them, since they have very little impact on marine ecosystems due to their low level of energy consumption and bycatch. for the reasons described above, i am voting in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i support this resolution. the fishing industry in europe is very important for many coastal areas. the fishermen are the first who want, and should care about, sustainable fishing. the recovery plan should take into account the specificities of the different types of gears. when implementing the recovery plan, the eu and member states should pay particular attention to non-industrial fishing activities and to the most artisanal and sustainable gear types, such as traditional traps (‘almadrabas’, ‘tonnare’), which contribute very positively to the rebuilding of tuna stocks, due to their high level of selectivity and low environmental impact in marine ecosystems, and which are valuable in scientific terms.
in writing. ‒ we abstained because, while the report underlines the role of artisanal fishing gear such as traditional traps, we believe that when implementing the recovery plan, the eu should place even greater emphasis on the use of traditional traps which contribute to the restoration of tuna stocks and have very little impact on marine ecosystems due to low levels of energy consumption and bycatch. we also feel it necessary to point out that in practice the distribution of quotas among the member states does not apply article 17 of the cfp, which calls for the allocation to be based on 'transparent and objective criteria, including those of an environmental, social and economic nature'.
in writing. ‒ this report confirms the political agreement reached by the european institutions responsible for this matter. we are talking about a report incorporating the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean into eu rules, in which the european parliament sends a clear message in defence of these fisheries, and also provides for small-scale and sustainable fishing to be given specific treatment when setting the quota for bluefin tuna. i therefore think it is appropriate to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because it represents a serious step backwards in favour of industrial tuna fishing and a fair distribution of fishing quotas. this report is the result of the trilogues with the commission and the council on the bluefin tuna recovery plan. the initial position of parliament, which we support, contained provisions in favour of traditional, sustainable and small-scale arts, specifically on the craft. the parliament's proposal would have improved the situation of the cages by increasing the quotas for the cages, which would have led to an increase in the sustainable exploitation of tuna. however, all these references have been erased in the process of the trilogues, relegating the almadraba to a mere reference without any binding power. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the multiannual plan for the baltic cod, herring and sprat stocks and the fisheries exploiting these stocks is the first of the multiannual plans submitted following the 2013 cfp reform. these plans are intended to be the tools for the management and recovery of community fisheries. despite the need for plans to manage fisheries in our seas and oceans, i could not vote for this one because the original proposal has been downgraded following the tripartite negotiations between the council and the commission. i am particularly concerned about the real application of an ecosystem-based approach or the correction of overfishing. i have therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ we abstained because we consider the implementation of multi-species management to be a step forward, much more effective than the management of individual species. we believe that management plans must guarantee the balanced and sustainable exploitation of these fisheries, based on scientific advice, and that it is also essential that all these regulations respond to the specificities of the territories and their people, which unfortunately are not always covered by eu policies, so we still do not share the criteria for the application of the cfp in the territories.
in writing. ‒ the multiannual plan aims to establish a multi-species management framework for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, where they account for more than 94% of catches in recent years. on 15 march 2016, representatives of the commission, the council and the parliament reached an agreement for this multiannual plan, which is expected to enter into force before the end of august 2016. this is the first of several plans required by article 9 of the cfp regulation. the agreed plan contains a number of requirements consistent with the new requirements of the common fisheries policy and introduces the concept of 'ranges' for the calculation of fishing mortality. it considered this regulation to be of the utmost importance, taking into account the interactions between the species concerned. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
