in writing. ‒ overfishing is putting the baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat at risk. scientific advice has established that the current exploitation of stocks is incompatible with the objective of maximum sustainable yield, i.e. with the objective of responsible fishing that allows the best possible recovery of resources. it is therefore necessary to act, but not to confuse speed with haste. to speed up the procedure, the european commission did not want to wait for further studies by the ices (international council for the exploration of the sea) before implementing the multiannual plan. fortunately, the draft regulation, as amended by meps, insists that scientific studies be taken into account and that local advisory councils be consulted. it is regrettable, however, that the draft delegates a great deal of power to the european commission, to the detriment of the prerogatives of the european parliament. i voted for this text, however, because fishermen need multiannual plans that give them long-term visibility.

in writing. ‒ the general principle underlying the commission's proposal is the need for a multi-specific management plan in the baltic sea. multi-species management is much more effective than species management alone. this plan should ensure the balanced and sustainable exploitation of those stocks and the stability of fishing opportunities and thus the livelihoods of fishermen. i think it is important to stress that when multiannual plans are drawn up, the voice of the region must be heard and implemented, with the participation of the european parliament at the appropriate time. it should also be borne in mind that the plan is a pioneering proposal in a very sensitive baltic sea ecosystem and the first review will therefore take place relatively soon, precisely because the multi-species management plan is a new and developing concept. i therefore vote in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ this report approves the commission's proposal to regulate competition, the applicable law, the recognition and enforcement of decisions on the matrimonial property regimes of international couples, both in the field of matrimonial property regimes and the property consequences of registered partnerships. i voted for the same because it will make it easier to recognise the marriage arrangements of crossborder couples.
in writing. ‒ when we talk about the importance of the union and how the decisions we take in the european institutions directly affect the lives of citizens, we are referring to measures such as those contained in the commission proposal adopted in this resolution. in europe there are some 16 million 'cross-border' couples who will benefit from the future property rights regulations. these regulations are undoubtedly a step forward that will make life easier for many international couples. however, because of the enhanced cooperation, there will be two europas for these couples: one where their property rights are recognised and one where they are not. i voted in favour of this resolution because it represents progress. but it's not enough. my commitment is to continue working for a europe without barriers for couples and families, including all forms of family that exist in our society, and therefore without discrimination for lgbt citizens. we must guarantee free movement within the eu. in order to achieve this without discrimination, it is also essential that any marriage or registered union of same-sex couples be recognised in another member state.
in writing. ‒ we propose to vote in favour of this report, since its purpose is to open up enhanced cooperation in the field of competition, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions in property regimes of international couples, covering the issues of matrimonial regimes and the property consequences of registered unions. these measures will make it easier for international couples to manage their affairs.
in writing. ‒ freedom of movement within the union has led to a significant increase in international marriages or marriages that have to resolve crossborder issues. however, these couples often face problems related to property, either within the marriage or when dividing property in the event of divorce. this regulation, drawn up under the enhanced cooperation procedure and applicable to 18 member states (belgium, greece, croatia, slovenia, spain, france, portugal, italy, malta, luxembourg, the czech republic, the netherlands, austria, bulgaria, finland and cyprus) which have so requested, is intended to provide clear guidance to help international couples to choose the law applicable to them, the courts having jurisdiction and the conditions for the recognition and scope of application of decisions given in other member states. this regulation will improve the legal status of international couples or those who have to resolve crossborder issues by establishing a clear legal framework for determining jurisdiction, the applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions on property regimes within marriage, which is why i voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ this proposal for a regulation aims to facilitate the management of the economic aspects of international couples within the european union by improving on the commission's initial proposal of 2011 and on the 2013 proposal. the regulation seeks to preserve the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law by excluding certain matters from its scope. it also lays down the court with jurisdiction to rule on applications and states that if a member state does not recognise the marriage in question, the courts of that state may refer the case to those of another member state which does. i believe that this proposal for a regulation is clearly in the interests of the union and its international partners, since it will put an end to many cases of confusion and legal difficulties and make life easier for citizens. i therefore agree that parliament should give a favourable opinion on the proposal.

in writing. ‒ i am in favour of this package of proposals on family law, as i believe that they are all very useful in that they form a reinforced private international law regime, complementing other instruments in this legislative branch. international couples and marriages are a phenomenon that, due to factors such as globalisation and the economic crisis (which in many cases has led to european citizens having to change their place of residence in search of a better working life), are becoming more common. all this certainly requires a revision of the legislation, which allows this profile of couples to have legal support and recognition, so that those in this situation do not feel disadvantaged by this international union and have the same rights and duties as a couple belonging to the same state.
mr president, i have supported both these reports, both these regulations. i did not have time to say yesterday in the debate that it is very good that the regulation has been adopted, but it is a great reminder that after more than five years of debate between parliament and the council, a plan which is not so ambitious in principle has finally been adopted. it only covers certain conflict of laws and procedural rules, and the problem is that it has not been adopted by all the member states of the european union, but by only 18 of them. so this is a great warning, a great reminder for the future. since we do not regulate substantive law itself, and do not interfere with the powers of the individual states, i am a little sorry that we are not able to agree on the conflict of laws and procedural rules governing, for example, the jurisdiction of the court or the law that will be the decisive law. on the one hand, it is a good project, but the fact that only 18 countries have accepted it makes it extremely weak and therefore only partly applicable to the european union. so i have to express some regret.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution initiative of the socialist group because i believe that the international community, and in particular the european union, must do much more in the face of a conflict such as the one that has continued to affect the eastern democratic republic of the congo (drc) for decades, and which, more than its alleged status as a conflict of low tension, suffers above all from the low attention it receives from the rest of the world. over the past 20 years, this conflict has caused six million deaths at the hands of the many armed groups that exercise brutal violence against the civilian population. hundreds of women and girls are raped every day. the massacre of civilians has become routine in the context of inter-ethnic strife and the dispute over control of the region's abundant natural resources. in this resolution we call on the high representative to initiate an international inquiry into the latest massacres in the beni area, in collaboration with the un and the international criminal court. we also call for an assessment of the performance of monusco, whose main objective, the protection of the civilian population, must be strengthened.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in the final vote on the joint resolution mainly because it does not recognise the genocide, calls for the reinforcement of mounsco and in particular through the patrols and mobile bases of operations, even though some paragraphs with which i agree call for an assessment, and does not reflect information on the responsibilities of multinationals in the financial support of the conflict and the illegal exploitation of natural resources
in writing. ‒ we voted against this resolution because, while condemning the recent dramatic events in the democratic republic of congo, it can be considered partial in that it fails to address the root causes of the current instability, namely inequality and the role of the large extractive transnational companies in the territory.
in writing. ‒ i support the text of this joint resolution because the situation in the democratic republic of congo requires intense and immediate action by the international community and in particular by the european union. among the key aspects of this statement i express my particular support for the implementation of an investigation by the international criminal court into the crimes in the beni region, the possibility of applying targeted sanctions, including a travel ban to the eu and the freezing of assets of all those responsible for repression and killings in the democratic republic of congo, and the call for european companies operating in the area to be held accountable. i also consider it essential to call elections and end president kabila's term of office.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution - an initiative launched by the socialist group - because i believe that the international community, and in particular the european union, must do much more in the face of a conflict such as the one that has continued to affect the eastern part of the democratic republic of the congo (drc) for decades, and which, more than its alleged status as a 'low-tension' conflict, suffers above all from the 'low attention' it receives from the rest of the world. over the past 20 years, this conflict has caused six million deaths at the hands of the many armed groups that exercise brutal violence against the civilian population. hundreds of women and girls are raped every day. the massacre of civilians has become routine in the context of inter-ethnic strife and the dispute over control of the region's abundant natural resources. in this resolution we call on the high representative to initiate an international inquiry into the latest massacres in the beni area, in collaboration with the un and the international criminal court. we also call for an assessment of the performance of monusco, whose main objective, the protection of the civilian population, must be strengthened.

in writing. ‒ we in this parliament condemn in the strongest terms the massacres and crimes against humanity that continue to be committed in the eastern region of the democratic republic of the congo. it is necessary to put an end once and for all to the criminal activities of all armed groups without exception in the eastern region of the country and to restore democratic control in that country, which requires the intervention of both the government of the democratic republic of the congo and the international institutions responsible for ensuring peace in that region. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally sound use of energy.

in writing. ‒ i fully support this resolution as i strongly condemn what is happening in eastern congo. i call as a matter of urgency for a thorough, independent and transparent investigation to be launched by the international community into the massacres, with the full collaboration of the drc government and monusco. with this vote we ask for an emergency meeting of the team of international envoys and representatives for the great lakes region of africa on elections in the drc with a view to taking appropriate action in this direction, such as mobilising the un security council. i insist that this situation should not prevent elections from taking place as constitutionally planned.

in writing. ‒ it is necessary to condemn the massacres and crimes against humanity that continue to be committed in the eastern region of the democratic republic of the congo and to seek to put an end to the criminal activities of all armed groups without exception in the eastern region of the country, as well as to rebuild the authority of the rule of law in the areas of governance and security and to carry out a transparent and thorough investigation into the massacres and crimes that have occurred as the resolution points out. i therefore think it necessary to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in the final vote on the joint resolution mainly because it does not recognise the genocide, it calls for the reinforcement of mounsco and in particular through the patrols and mobile operating bases. even though some paragraphs i agree with call for an assessment, it does not reflect information on the responsibilities of multinationals in financial support of the conflict and illegal exploitation of natural resources.
in writing. ‒ the strategic framework is a multiannual plan linked to the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy which aims to increase student mobility, equity, cohesion and active citizenship, as well as a focus on creativity and innovation, including entrepreneurship. the results of recent years show that the mercantilist orientation of the education system, the standardization of educational programmes to increase competitiveness between pupils and schools, and the cuts in austerity programmes applied in economies such as spain, have led to a clear imbalance between the objectives themselves set by the commission and the council, which in themselves do not represent my position in favour of free, quality public education. the resolution, which welcomes a joint report from the commission and the council, seeks to legitimize these practices through parliament, adding minor positive aspects (e.g. calling for the promotion of multidisciplinary training of teachers adapted to new social challenges, or the review of evaluation working groups). i therefore voted against the report because it does not address the fundamental problems which lead to increased social inequalities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. it highlights the need to increase cooperation in education and training. from a europeanist perspective, it presents various measures aimed at increasing the mobility of students and teachers within the eu, one of the great achievements of our union which must be preserved and improved. the report contains a progressive approach to the integration of the most vulnerable and disadvantaged groups in our society. it also aims to combat the various discriminations that still exist in our continent today and that affect lgbtqi citizens, the disabled, women or immigrants. the integration of migrants and refugees is another of its priorities. education is a vital tool for ensuring coexistence in our societies and for providing opportunities for those citizens who have come to the union fleeing barbarism, poverty and in search of a better future. in a time like the present, quality, universal, inclusive and accessible education and training is one of the greatest assets we have to have a fairer union and to eradicate the different forms of intolerance.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, the commission took stock of the education and training strategy, et 2020, in cooperation with the member states. on the basis of the conclusions of the resulting report, the commission set out the priorities for the period 2016-2020. while these priorities address such unquestionable issues as inclusive education, equality, equity, non-discrimination, civic competence, welfare, social cohesion, intercultural dialogue, innovation and support for teaching, they are still a wrapper to give prestige to a neoliberal conception of education and training. the krasnodebski report, in line with the commission, does not hide the conversion of education and training into a business object, and directs it towards employability rather than the development of knowledge. the inclusion in the report of aspects such as the reception of migrants, refugees and asylum seekers in this area, as well as the gender perspective, should be acknowledged. however, these necessary inclusions should not be made to pay the price of the commercialisation of education, which is why we voted against.
in writing. ‒ i support the contributions made by this report on the role of education in integrating the hundreds of thousands of people who come to our union fleeing violence, war and poverty. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption. this task must also be directed at overcoming the shortcomings that european education offers to those who arrive. a key to insisting on the humanistic principle of united in diversity. i also welcome the strengthening of mechanisms for sharing good practice, the insistence on supporting parents and families as the basic actors in the educational process and the involvement in this strategic cooperation of all the actors who can contribute and who demonstrate with data that there are policies that give results, even if their protagonists are uncomfortable for some of the member states. this parliament has been witness to, and sometimes accompanied, gratuitous criticism of, for example, the basque education system for its commitment to effective bilingualism, which came to be seen as a sign of support for terrorism. this week the bbc was putting it up as an example of integration, innovation and results.
in writing. ‒ the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training has been revised by the council and the european parliament in order to reinforce its effectiveness, reorder the priority areas for action and increase its added value. this report, which i have supported, stresses the need to achieve long-term objectives while working on specific issues of relevance to each country, such as low participation in adult education, school drop-out, social inclusion or the gender gap, among other issues. thanks to the s&d group, the need to focus on social inclusion in order to achieve the objectives of et 2020, to improve the inclusion and quality of education and training systems with a lifelong learning perspective and to call for better governance and cooperation in this area has been included. it also emphasises the strengthening of digital skills, high-quality early childhood education and inclusive education to ensure equal access and opportunities for all, especially for the most vulnerable groups, while including a specific chapter on migration and education, calling for the proper integration of migrants, refugees and asylum seekers into education and training systems.

in writing. ‒ education and training are important in helping people to acquire the knowledge and professional skills that will enable them to become competitive and innovative employees. urgent action is needed at national and european level, including in the framework of et 2020, in the field of education and training. education is essential for integration and employability, and the failure of national systems to meet this challenge can increase social divisions and cultural segregation. it is also important to prevent the wasting of the talent of highly skilled migrants, as well as to strengthen the link between schools and families, since parents are responsible for their children's education. i think that a good measure would be for the commission to draw up a decision to ensure the horizontal coverage of the migration issue in the mandates of all the working groups and to develop mutual learning activities in order to identify good practices for the effective integration of migrants. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ my vote in favour of the report on the follow-up to the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training (et 2020). so far this strategy seems to be bearing fruit, but we must work hard to strengthen education and training policies and to ensure the quality of the education provided, as education is a key element for integration and employability.

in writing. ‒ the strategic framework is a multiannual plan linked to the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy which aims to increase student mobility, equity, cohesion and active citizenship, as well as a focus on creativity and innovation, including entrepreneurship. the results of recent years show that the mercantilist orientation of the education system, the standardization of educational programmes to increase competitiveness between pupils and schools, and the cuts in austerity programmes applied in economies such as spain, have led to a clear imbalance between the objectives themselves set by the commission and the council, which in themselves do not represent my position in favour of free, quality public education. the resolution, which welcomes a joint report from the commission and the council, seeks to legitimize these practices through parliament, adding minor positive aspects (e.g. calling for the promotion of multidisciplinary training of teachers adapted to new social challenges, or the review of evaluation working groups). i therefore voted against the report because it does not address the fundamental problems which lead to increased social inequalities.
in writing. ‒ i share the majority position of the european parliament in favour of 30% renewables by 2030, through binding national targets, more ambitious than the one adopted by the council. the ppe does not share this view, as it has shown by its vote and by the action of commissioner cañete, who is due to appear in court because of the scandals surrounding him. our amendment in favour of quality employment in renewables has been adopted, despite the opposition of the epp. however, we must regret that the proposal for specific social guarantees for vulnerable consumers, i.e. those in a situation of energy poverty, was rejected. the report responds to the drama of the retroactive measures against aid to renewables approved by the current government of my country, asking the commission to avoid such changes and to guarantee the economic viability of existing assets. it is surprising, once again against the general sentiment of the house, that the ppe is opposed to penalizing self-production and self-consumption of energy with additional taxes or fees. in general, with the exceptions mentioned, the result is positive and deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it represents an important endorsement of the development of the renewable energy sector and an important call to member states that are not meeting the objectives of the directive. the report reflects the progress of the sector but also the problems encountered in certain member states such as the 'sun tax', the retroactivity of support measures, difficulties in accessing the network, etc. the report also refers to the need to create quality jobs and to include trade unions and civil society in the development of these energies. specific proposals are also made on the definition of prosumers, support for modal shift in transport, development of renewable cooling technologies, public investment in the sector, etc. this makes the text an important reference for the development of the next directive, and it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the paloma lópez bermejo report because it provides a good basis for the revision of the renewable energy directive. it emphasises the potential for job creation, the benefits for the economy, and the centrality of renewable energy development in the fight against climate change. it sets ambitious targets and asks for them to be binding. it also promotes self-consumption and the democratization of the energy system.

in writing. ‒ i support the majority position of the european parliament - more ambitious than that adopted by the council - in favour of 30% renewables by 2030 through binding national targets. the european parliament has also called for the commission to be given the right to take action in the event of a dispute between the commission and the member states. despite the vote against the ppe, our amendment in favour of quality employment in renewables was adopted. however, i regret that an amendment which advocated the adoption of specific social guarantees for vulnerable consumers, i.e. those in a situation of energy poverty, was rejected. the report responds to the drama of the retroactive measures against aid to renewables approved by the current government of my country, asking the commission to avoid such changes and to ensure the economic viability of existing assets. it is surprising, again against the general sentiment of this house, that the epp is opposed to not penalizing self-production and self-consumption of energy with additional taxes or fees.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the paloma lópez bermejo report because it provides a good basis for the revision of the renewable energy directive. it emphasises the potential for job creation, the benefits for the economy, and the centrality of renewable energy development in the fight against climate change. it sets ambitious targets and asks for them to be binding. it also promotes self-consumption and the democratization of the energy system.
in writing. ‒ i share the majority position of the european parliament in favour of 30% renewables by 2030, through binding national targets, more ambitious than the one adopted by the council. the ppe does not share this view, as it has shown by its vote and by the action of commissioner cañete, who is due to appear in court because of the scandals surrounding him. our amendment in favour of quality employment in renewables has been adopted, despite the opposition of the epp. however, we must regret that the proposal for specific social guarantees for vulnerable consumers, i.e. those in a situation of energy poverty, was rejected. the report responds to the drama of the retroactive measures against aid to renewables approved by the current government of my country, asking the commission to avoid such changes and to guarantee the economic viability of existing assets. it is surprising, once again against the general sentiment of the house, that the ppe is opposed to penalizing self-production and self-consumption of energy with additional taxes or fees. in general, with the exceptions mentioned, the result is positive and deserves my vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it represents an important endorsement of the development of the renewable energy sector and an important call to member states that are not meeting the objectives of the directive. the report reflects the progress of the sector but also the problems encountered in certain member states such as the 'sun tax', the retroactivity of support measures, difficulties in accessing the network, etc. the report also refers to the need to create quality jobs and to include trade unions and civil society in the development of these energies. specific proposals are also made on the definition of prosumers, support for modal shift in transport, development of renewable cooling technologies, public investment in the sector, etc. this makes the text an important reference for the development of the next directive, and it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i believe that a new approach to renewable energy is needed, making it the cornerstone of the european union's energy model. our main obligation is to combat climate change and reduce our dependence on the rest of the world for energy resources. to meet this obligation i consider the implementation of the renewable energy sources directive appropriate, as it acts as the eu's legal instrument for the transition to a sustainable energy production model. regulation of the sector at european level aims to address the various problems that are holding back the development of the sector, by promoting public investment, democratic control and a stable framework for investment that facilitate collective and democratic energy management to ensure a fully sovereign, efficient and clean energy model by 2050. i am in favour of these budgets.
in writing. ‒ the eu is on track to meet its 2020 targets of reducing co2 emissions by 20%, increasing the share of renewable energy sources in total energy consumption by up to 20% and increasing energy efficiency by a further 20%. but we must continue to develop renewable energy and ensure that this share continues to rise over the next decade, reaching if possible the 30% target by 2030, as the report we have approved, with my support, in this house stresses.

in writing. ‒ i certainly support this report, as it seems to me vital to know the state of play of the production and use of renewable energy in the eu, mainly because the trend of renewable energy continues to rise and it is one of the key resources to be able to tackle pollution and curb environmental damage. in spain, for example, progress in this area is very positive, considering that in 2013 and 2014 there was an increase in the use of renewable energy significantly above the indicative minimum trajectory. this progress has also taken place in relation to electricity, heating and cooling, transport and sustainability for biofuels. i therefore hope that with proposals like this one all the member states will be able to achieve these results and even improve them.
in writing. ‒ i share the approach adopted in this report by the majority of the european parliament in favour of a binding target of 40% energy efficiency by 2030, as advocated at the recent paris climate summit. this is despite the council's position and the epp's vote against, which wanted to limit it to a non-binding 30%. we believe that the implementation of the energy efficiency directive is wrong, and we do not share the rapporteur's approach to greater flexibility, in pursuing a target of 17.6% instead of the 20% target for 2020. the ppe, like the bermejo report, which was also voted on today, is opposed to measures to combat energy poverty, which have nevertheless received the support of the majority of parliament. in this connection, we call on the member states to ensure that measures are taken to help consumers with low incomes. the final result is positive and therefore deserves my vote in favour. i hope that the report will be taken into consideration by the commission, which is always waiting for commissioner cañete to appear in this house because of the scandals surrounding him.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i consider it a necessary step forward to demand a 40% improvement in national efficiency targets by 2030, correcting the council's proposal downwards from 27%. this will also require a review of the way the energy efficiency directive has worked so far, the inapplicability, excessive flexibility and lack of concreteness of which is duly highlighted in the document.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the report because it underlines the need to improve energy efficiency as a way of combating climate change. it proposes binding targets by country. the binding aspect is a key point because it obliges countries to meet these targets while flexibility leaves the door open to insufficient targets. the commission is also proposing to increase the number of member states that have adopted the euro by a factor of two. it also proposes to focus measures on households in energy poverty, which we believe is of the utmost importance.

in writing. ‒ the union is well on track to meet its 2020 targets for environmental protection measures. this development owes much of its success to the progress of the emissions trading system. i believe that the concern on this issue should be focused above all on the bureaucracy associated with reporting in the energy sector and on high energy prices, because the cost reductions achieved through energy savings are offset by the special levies imposed at national level and by the complicated reporting obligations. to solve these problems, i call on the commission to step up its efforts to develop a coherent climate and energy policy and to design a european electricity market. i am voting in favour of this report because of that and because the implementation of the directive will also provide other important innovative stimuli in relation to obligations and incentives in the member states.
in writing. ‒ we have made progress, but we still need to take bold and decisive steps towards greater energy efficiency. our citizens still face obstacles, such as the existence of sometimes contradictory climate protection regulations, the complexity of energy efficiency legislation and the different national approaches to energy policy, factors which can exert a massive influence on european policy. i therefore believe it necessary and i vote in favour of the call from this parliament to the commission to step up its efforts to develop a coherent climate and energy policy and to design a european electricity market. we must strive to ensure that the energy efficiency directive is effectively implemented by making changes to the text that will make it easier to overcome the work that has been done in its implementation.

in writing. ‒ i am very much in favour of this report, as i believe that it is very important to keep in mind the levels of energy used in the eu, which should not exceed certain maximum levels, so that pollution and damage to the environment can be reduced. it is therefore necessary to create a clear and consistent legislative framework in this respect, reflecting the regulation on energy efficiency, so that efficiency levels are common to all eu states and so we can all contribute to the same extent to a common objective of improving the environment. in spain, for example, primary and final energy levels were reported during 2014 to be below the target levels by 2020, which indicates that we are very conscious and further supports my support for this report.
in writing. i deeply regret the tone of the debate in this house: too many threats and a lack of self-criticism. we must respect the will expressed in the referendum and not oppose nationalism and right-wing populism with a hollow cosmopolitanism which defends the same xenophobic and reactionary policies. or is it not the case that the eu is covering up expulsions of european citizens between member states, while militarizing its borders and refusing to take in refugees from the wars it is encouraging in its neighbourhood? or is it not true that the neoliberal policies you advocate are the main cause of the erosion of the living conditions and social rights of the european population? it is these policies, for which the commission and the governments of the member states share responsibility, that have brought us to a situation in which the peoples no longer conceive of a common political space, forced to compete with each other in an integration made by and for the market. the lack of democracy is the real core of a problem which, unfortunately, they refuse to face.
in writing. that a historic member state should decide to blow up the european union project is against the grain of the times. in the 21st century and in a global world, the union of the future united states of europe remains the hope in the face of the disagreement between nations and the armed conflicts that plagued us during the last century. despite the deep sadness felt by most europeans at the decision of the united kingdom to leave the european union, we must take advantage of this event to rebuild, reform and relaunch the project that has brought the greatest period of peace and prosperity to the citizens of our continent in recent decades. as regards the road map to follow, it is clear that if they have decided not only to endanger the unity and solidarity of their country but also to blow up europe, we must try to counter that danger with a departure from the united kingdom as quickly and painlessly as possible for both sides. any expansion can cause contagion in other countries with populist movements as well as greater instability and economic uncertainty.
in writing. ‒ i have voted against this joint motion because i reject a hasty resolution which is only intended to increase political pressure on the people of the united kingdom following the referendum on leaving the eu and which lacks any self-criticism towards the policies which explain the outcome of the vote. we do not identify ourselves with the front which attributes to europeanism the custody of democratic values, because in this europe of perpetual austerity, of the militarization of borders, of imperialism and neoliberalism there is no future for the popular classes.
in writing. ‒ we voted austainable on this resolution because we believe that the will expressed at the ballot box must be respected, starting with the activation of article 50 of the treaty on european union. we defend the right of citizens to freely choose their future in democratic and transparent processes. we do not believe that the united kingdom's departure from the european union will improve the living conditions of its citizens. we do not agree that the exit process should be activated immediately. we believe that the united kingdom should legitimately assess when it is ready to start the process, and in no case should there be any gaps in the rules and treaties to which the country is subject. a process with democratic guarantees is one that guarantees the well-being of its citizens, of all the people who live and work in the united kingdom. we did not vote in favour because we felt it was essential that two amendments were tabled which made it clear that it was essential to reactivate the european process by taking account of inequalities and by defending the democratization of the european institutions. they did not go through and that is why our final vote was abstention.
in writing. ‒ the outcome of the referendum on the uk's membership of the eu is not what we would have wanted. i'm sorry about that. the first consequences of brexit have already been seen in recent days in the fall of the pound, in the announcements of relocations and in the lies that the promoters of the exit told their fellow citizens to break the european bond. it is regrettable that such an event has been triggered by the irresponsibility of the british prime minister. for reasons of purely personal and partisan interest, david cameron has led his country into a consultation which has fragmented the united kingdom, both territorially and generational. however, the british people have spoken and their decision must be respected. however, it cannot be allowed to unnecessarily delay the implementation of the mechanisms set up by the lisbon treaty. it is therefore urgent that europe and the united kingdom negotiate the terms of their new relationship as soon as possible. and above all, it is urgent that europe reinvent itself and build with the citizens of its 27 member states a new project for the future.
in writing. ‒ first of all, i am very sorry that the united kingdom has decided to leave the european union. it is a sad day for the union and for all those uk citizens who feel they are citizens of europe. i voted in favour of this resolution because the most important thing at the moment is to show the unity of the pro-european parliamentary groups in these circumstances. i hope that there will be fair negotiation during this process, but i echo the words of president jean claude juncker during this plenary session: there must be no negotiation until there is notification.

in writing. it is positive to see that youth unemployment figures have fallen in both the eu-28 and the eurozone. but this is no time for complacency or for letting our guard down, because there are still more than four million young people out of work in europe and because many of the jobs that have been created are precarious jobs with low wages. it is now time to make a thorough analysis of the implementation of the youth guarantee. my country, for example, has done it slowly, inadequately and irresponsibly. it's slow because it took over a year and a half to get it up and running. inadequate because, in february 2015, only 60,000 young people had found a job and irresponsible because the system is mainly being used to give bonuses to companies. i therefore believe that the time has come to commit ourselves to a genuine european youth guarantee, with more funds and a minimum framework to guarantee the quality of job offers, the dignity of the grants received and the excellence of the education received.

mr president, this regulation - and i have already said this - on energy efficiency labelling is undoubtedly key to providing the citizen and the consumer with the best information, the best understanding of the impact that certain products on the market can have on the energy bill, on the electricity bill, and, in turn, it is a regulation that will undoubtedly contribute to the objective of reducing emissions. the need for a new approach to labelling is due to the overcrowding of the most efficient classes of certain products, which undermines the scale of the product and the information it provides to the public. the proposal is also sensitive to industries such as heating, which has recently introduced efficiency labelling. finally, this adjustment will seek to avoid new cases such as 'dieselgate', which must occur under real conditions of use and not in laboratory tests.
the use of household appliances is increasing and 85% of european consumers take energy labelling into account in their purchasing decisions, so it is widely accepted in all eu countries. it is a guarantee for the consumer, while at the same time it is an instrument for achieving the objectives of reducing emissions, improving energy efficiency and reducing dependence on fuels. the proposed new labelling eliminates the confusing a+ categories and establishes a single, more simplified a to g scale. it is estimated that by 2020, the fuel savings from the use of energy efficiency labels will be equivalent to 180 million tonnes of oil. the objective of improving energy efficiency by 27% by 2030 is an unambitious target and should be increased to 40%. the unjustified delay of up to five years in the full implementation of the new regulation may lead to lower investments in research and improvements by manufacturers and should be minimised for the benefit of all.
member of the commission. – mr president, let me start by thanking the committee on international trade and especially the two rapporteurs, ms forenza and ms beghin, for their work on these two very important reports. sustainable development in trade policy is an area where parliament and the commission clearly share an interest and a strong engagement. the commission’s new trade policy, the trade for all strategy, has sustainable development at its core. it sets out an ambitious and comprehensive agenda for the eu, underlining the fact that trade is not only about economic growth but also about defending the values that we share in europe: social justice, respect for human rights, and high labour and environmental standards. this strategy builds upon progress already achieved since the adoption by the european parliament in 2010 of the three resolutions in this area: first, the introduction of binding and comprehensive trade and sustainable development chapters in all our free trade agreements; second, the strengthening of the human rights dimension, including gender, in our sustainable impact assessment; and, third, reforming the eu generalised system of preferences, including the flagship gsp+, sustainable development and good governance. we also have developed partnerships with key players to promote change in countries where the situation was acute, for example through the bangladesh compact. furthermore, we are supporting responsible business practices, including enhanced transparency for large companies on non-financial information, as well as the uptake in implementation of internationally recognised guidelines and principles of corporate social responsibility. the eu has been a frontrunner over recent years in pursuing the integration of sustainable development into its policy, and this engagement has also been recognised by many international organisations and our trading partners. but being a frontrunner is, of course, not enough. there is much more work to be done. in this regard we have set some priorities, notably the effective implementation of trade and sustainable development chapters, better linking trade policy instruments to development cooperation, including with a view to supporting the 2030 agenda, and the promotion of responsible supply chains and of private sector engagement to integrate sustainable development objectives as part of core business strategies. the report on a new forward-looking and innovative future strategy for trade and investment underlines the importance of pushing both jobs and growth, as well as the value agenda that focused on human rights, good governance and sustainable development. we have taken very careful note of the request for our future trade policy to have a stronger focus not only on these issues but also on manufacturing priorities and services. trade in manufacturing is, of course, a priority, as it has been in recent decades and will be in the future as well. it is a central pillar of our market access strategy in trade agreements and trade defence. the commission welcomes the attention given to the importance of coherence between trade and other eu policies, and this new commission is working hard, along these lines, to integrate the various policy areas – respect for human and labour rights, protection of the environment, and the development of partner countries, including sustainable development chapters – in all our trade agreements. we very much welcome parliament’s emphasis on the primacy of the world trade organisation (wto) system and the multilateral approach to negotiation. i share the ambition in that regard. we agree that the multilateral route for trade liberalisation is of course the most efficient and the most equitable, when it is possible. moreover, we endorse parliament’s demand for a balanced outcome, including on agriculture, in free trade agreements. we will continue, in this context, to balance the needs of manufacturing, services and agricultural producers in setting our priorities for negotiation. we also take note of the view expressed on market economy status for china. as you know, the commission is currently conducting an in-depth impact assessment analysing the various options with regard to the treatment of china in anti-dumping investigations, and we will hold further political discussions on this in the coming weeks. lastly, parliament’s call for greater reciprocity in opening up public procurement is well noted. it is clearly an area where there is imbalance, and we take this very much into account when we formulate mandates and negotiate free trade agreements, in order to have a more level playing field in the area of public procurement. so i want to thank you very much for these reports. they contain some very valuable comments. much of what you propose is actually already being done by the commission but we can, of course, do more and we look forward to working with you in order to have not only as efficient a trade policy as possible but also a sustainable and responsible one.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this. mr president, i should like to begin by thanking the shadow rapporteurs and the rapporteur for this report for having taken account of the opinion of the committee on agriculture, since the agricultural sector is one of the most sensitive chapters in trade negotiations with third countries. free trade agreements can bring many benefits, but they can also seriously jeopardise the future of certain vulnerable agricultural sectors, for which exclusion clauses or the necessary palliative measures need to be provided for. the accumulation of concessions can be particularly harmful in areas such as fruit and vegetables or in sectors such as poultry and beef. agriculture has already been the currency of trade negotiations with third countries on many occasions, and this should not happen again in the future. the commission's proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs intended for human consumption, which is to be adopted by the council on 1 january 1993, is a very important step towards the achievement of the objectives of the directive. finally, i would just like to stress the importance of the protection of designations of origin and geographical indications in third countries for the image of the european union, and that this should be a prerequisite in agricultural negotiations for trade agreements.

madam president, you have split british society in half; you have deeply divided your country by generations and by territories; you have endangered - perhaps irreversibly - the continuity of the united kingdom as such; you have awakened political cannibalism in your own party; you have weakened the european union and ended your political career, albeit deferred. this is the legacy of mr cameron's political adventurism and these are the first fruits of the first success of the euro-phobes. in the face of this, the european council has dispatched the matter in line and a half, with a timid applause has dismissed mr cameron and has convened itself for two and a half months to try to deal with the matter. this is not what we need. we need to move quickly to trigger article 50 and start negotiations for a new relationship between the uk and the eu. we need the european commission to lead this negotiation and not let it fall into the hands of governments on a bilateral basis. we need a good agreement, satisfactory for both sides, but one which cannot consist in the one who leaves retaining the advantages of the one who stays without assuming any of the commitments. we need predictability and clarity, not confusion. mr juncker said in his speech that truth cannot be found in paraphrasing or repetition, and i remind him of what the british philosopher bacon said: 'truth emerges more easily from error than from confusion'. and right now we're in a state of confusion. the answer is 'blue card'. mr ujazdowski, yes, i think that the irresponsibility comes from those who have set this diabolical process in motion, but in any case i did not say in my speech that we should not reach a good agreement with good relations: i stressed that this cannot be at the expense of the european union. this referendum shows that we can get out, but now we have to show that the 27 can and must move forward, and that is what must be done.
madam president, reading the council conclusions one might think: 'what kind of world do they live in in the council?' a line and a half for brexit and the word "refugees" is gone, but not the problem. hungary has just announced a referendum in october on the relocation of refugees, which is another storm. the council is naked, mr tusk. national selfishness and fear of populism have paralysed the council. mr verhofstadt has said that the european union must change or it will collapse. i will make it clear: either the council changes, or the european union will collapse and all the nations will do so, piece by piece.
madam president, we cannot pretend that nothing has happened: brexit is very serious. we cannot go ahead and start the european accelerator. the united kingdom and europe are now projects that will run in parallel. the negotiation that is opened must be transparent and swift. we cannot give the impression that we are incapable of making difficult decisions with a very slow negotiation, with a very long negotiation. a bureaucratic negotiation would confirm all the brexit arguments. we cannot allow the united kingdom to use this negotiation to obtain better conditions for another referendum, or better conditions outside the european union than within the european union. the future of the european union is not a replica of the united kingdom. that is why more europe is not yet the answer: more europeanism is the answer. without europe, there is no europe, just as there is no fatherland without patriotism. we cannot accept that the british people were lied to during the referendum campaign; but it is also true that we were silent during the referendum campaign. the council, the commission and parliament said nothing to the british people during the election campaign. there is no divorce where the fault is 100% on one side. in this case, the european union will also have to accept its share of responsibility. we cannot avoid self-criticism: governments fail when they use europe to justify unpopular decisions, and institutions fail when they take cruel decisions without looking the europeans in the eye. we have to make the united kingdom the last to leave the european union, not the first, and for that we have to build a better europe, which in my view is a europe with a heart.
madam president, i would like to express my full agreement with the main lines of the speech which president schulz made at the summit last week. deciding to leave is to leave, and staying means to make a real commitment to unlocking the full potential of our union for economic revival, employment and investment and to make real progress towards a political union which my party, the basque nationalist party, has supported since the first decades of the 20th century, as you can see from this poster, which is from 1933 (the speaker shows an electronic tablet with the image of a poster), or by checking the role played by our first lehendakari in the new international teams or at the hague congress in 1948. this week we have heard a lot of reproaches against europe for the decisions it has taken in the face of our great crises. the terrible thing is that those who formulated them were the same ones who took them from the council, states that hide their fears and evade their responsibilities by pointing to one culprit: europe. we must change our attitude and the best way to defend the interests of one or another state here is to assume that what is good for that common project is good for all its members.
madam president, those of us who feel europe in our hearts are saddened by the present situation. with respect, as it could not be otherwise, to the decision of the british people, we are free to express our concern, but also to be firm in the decisions we have to make at this moment. of course europe must change, of course there is a large part of the citizens who today feel let down, but the solution cannot be a europe à la carte, where each one decides how he wants to be part of it, where only the particular benefits are sought and not the common welfare. we cannot defend the free movement of goods and at the same time reject the free movement of citizens. the message from this parliament must be clear. the union must change, of course, but the solution cannot be to break with the values that created our project: more common policies, a more social and more inclusive europe, leaving selfishness behind. together, united in our diversity.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of approving the agreement between the european union and the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver, as it is a very satisfactory agreement for which the spanish socialists have been working for a long time. the agreement represents a further step in the deepening of relations between the union and peru, as well as being a supplementary means of strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. the agreement will thus help to strengthen regional coherence, as peru is one of a minority of latin american countries whose nationals still require a visa. peru is a relatively stable democracy which, like the european union, upholds the values and principles of democracy, good governance, respect for human rights and the rule of law, and remains an important partner in this field in latin america. human rights and democracy are essential elements of the relationship between the european union and the andean country.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement in line with our favourable position on visa exemption. although i disagree with the way the negotiation procedure has been conducted, in a non-transparent way and without including democratic institutions such as the european parliament in it, i agree with the proposed measures, which facilitate the freedom of movement of both peruvian citizens to the european union and european citizens to peru, thus reducing the restrictions that still exist on freedom of movement.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement which will allow peruvian citizens to travel without the need for a visa to thirty european countries. a decision that will have a direct impact on many citizens and that will undoubtedly bring two continents even closer together, with the aim of increasing their collaboration in the coming years. the fact that peruvians can travel to europe without a visa is a testament to the good bilateral relations with a reliable and secure partner such as the republic of peru. relations based on trade, with the union being the second largest destination market for peru's exports and the fifth largest source of peru's imports. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties. on the political side, the recent election observation mission by the european union on the occasion of the presidential elections, and its welcome by the peruvian authorities, is another indicator of the state of these relations.
in writing. ‒ the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with a view to concluding a bilateral agreement between the european union and peru, among other countries, to establish a visa-free regime for citizens of the union and nationals of these countries travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than the pursuit of a paid activity. this agreement on the short-stay visa waiver is a further step in the deepening of relations between the european union and these countries, as well as a further means of strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ air quality control is a key priority of environmental policy. the amendments incorporated in the proposal extend its focus to public health, strengthen parliament's role in implementing the directive and ensure an improvement over current emissions. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the report is aimed at reducing emissions from non-mobile combustion engines. it is a very technical, specific report on the characteristics of machinery which does not have a specific wheel to move around: commonly used in agriculture, on some railway tracks, on some cotton farms, machinery such as snow-clearers and specific tractors. the aim was to harmonise their life cycle potential by replacing them with less polluting engines that could contribute drastically to reducing co2 and other pollutant emissions. i voted in favour of the report because the negotiations in the trilogue were positive for the eug and the council and the european parliament agreed to give due attention to any consequences that could be brought about by the replacement and to mitigate the economic impact, mainly in the agricultural sector.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur, mrs gardini, for her work in reaching agreement on the regulation on emission limits for non-road mobile machinery. the main objective of this report is to strike a reasonable balance between concern for health and the environment and the competitiveness of eu manufacturing industry and the related jobs and know-how. in this respect, the agreement has struck the much-needed balance.
in writing. ‒ engines installed in non-road mobile machinery are responsible for about 15% of the nitrogen oxide emitted and 5% of the eu's particulate matter emissions. in september 2014, the european commission published a proposal for a regulation with measures to reduce emissions of the main air pollutants from engines of non-road mobile machinery. this proposal also reduces the complexity of the legal framework for the sector. the proposal introduces new emission limits reflecting technological progress and eu policies in the road sector, with a view to achieving eu air quality objectives; it extends the scope, in order to improve market harmonisation (eu and international) and minimise the risk of market distortions; and it introduces measures to simplify administrative procedures and improve compliance, including conditions for better market surveillance. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ air quality control is a key priority of environmental policy. the amendments incorporated in the proposal extend its focus to public health, strengthen parliament's role in implementing the directive and ensure an improvement over current emissions. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because i am convinced that we need to legislate to help tackle the public health problem posed by studies attributing carcinogenic properties to ultrafine particles, to improve air quality in general and to create a barrier-free market not only within the eu but also with our main trading partners around the world. i have also taken into account that, thanks to technological progress, regulations can be tightened up without imposing an excessive burden on manufacturing industry.
in writing. ‒ according to the commission, non-road mobile machinery (nmme), such as cranes or mowers, is responsible for 15% of nitrogen oxide emissions and 5% of particulate matter emissions in the european union. these emissions are limited by directive 97/68/ec, as last amended in 2004. over time, technological developments have made it possible to be increasingly strict in the field of energy saving, which can have a positive effect on the competitiveness of industries. however, this legislation is generally binding on manufacturers. it places additional constraints on the already weak industrial sector in europe, whereas there is an urgent need to support european production. i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ the report is aimed at reducing emissions from non-mobile combustion engines. it is a very technical, specific report on the characteristics of machinery which does not have a specific wheel to move around: commonly used in agriculture, on some railway tracks, on some cotton farms, machinery such as snow-clearers and specific tractors. the aim was to harmonise their life cycle potential by replacing them with less polluting engines that could contribute drastically to reducing co2 and other pollutant emissions. i voted in favour of the report because the negotiations in the trilogue were positive for the eug and the council and the european parliament agreed to give due attention to any consequences that could be brought about by the replacement and to mitigate the economic impact, mainly in the agricultural sector.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this report, which has as its main objective to strike a reasonable balance between, on the one hand, concern for health and the environment, as proposed by the commission, and, on the other, the competitiveness of the eu's manufacturing industry and the jobs and know-how associated with it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because this report sets stricter emission limit values for internal combustion engines installed in non-road mobile machinery. at the same time, it establishes harmonised rules for the marketing of such engines on the eu market. in addition to improving air quality across the eu, the new proposal offers the sector a predictable and stable regulatory framework. this ensures a level playing field for european industry and avoids unfair competition from low-cost imports of unregulated machinery. on this basis, the new proposal comprises the following main lines: introduction of new emission limits reflecting technological progress and eu policies in the road sector, with a view to achieving eu air quality objectives; widening of the scope, in order to improve market harmonisation, both eu and international, and to minimise the risk of market distortions. introduction of measures to simplify administrative procedures and improve compliance, including conditions for improved market surveillance.
in writing. ‒ air quality control is a key priority of environmental policy. the amendments incorporated in the proposal extend its focus to public health, strengthen parliament's role in implementing the directive and ensure an improvement over current emissions. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the proposal of the european parliament and of the council on limitation and type-approval requirements for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery is based on the report analysed by the commission on 20 november 2013 on the economic and environmental advantages and disadvantages and the comparison of possible options. i believe it is essential to promote these legislative initiatives, which are aimed at ensuring air quality, and the health and environmental responsibilities of the union towards its citizens. the aim is to ensure that this regulation reflects the technological advances made by the european union in the field of emissions, environmental protection and public health. that is why i am voting for it.
in writing. ‒ it is necessary to update the type-approval rules and emission limits for internal combustion engines for certain machines such as lawnmowers, excavators, diesel and inland waterway locomotives. that is why i support the proposal adopted by this parliament, in which we have sought a balance between environmental protection and the competitiveness of enterprises.
in writing. ‒ non-road mobile machinery covers a wide range from gardening tools to heavy construction or agricultural machinery and is responsible for about 15% of the nitrogen oxide emitted and 5% of the particulate matter in the union. remember, these particles have carcinogenic properties, so we're talking not just about air quality but public health. this regulation will replace the various national legislation on the subject, thus providing the industry with a unique opportunity to market such engines in the union market, increase competitiveness and information for users. we are in fact faced with a text which strikes a proportionate balance between concern for health and the environment and the competitiveness of the sector itself, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ engines installed in non-road mobile machinery are responsible for about 15% of nitrogen oxide emitted and 5% of the eu's particulate matter emissions. in september 2014, the european commission published a proposal for a regulation with measures to reduce emissions of the main air pollutants from engines of non-road mobile machinery. this proposal also reduces the complexity of the legal framework for the sector. the proposal introduces new emission limits reflecting technological progress and eu policies in the road sector, with a view to achieving eu air quality objectives; it extends the scope, in order to improve market harmonisation (eu and international) and minimise the risk of market distortions; and it introduces measures to simplify administrative procedures and improve compliance, including conditions for better market surveillance. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i supported this text because it is in line with the eu’s air quality policy, the objective is to progressively reduce the emissions from new engines being brought on the market and, thereby, replace the old, more polluting ones over time. the proposal is also expected to alleviate the pressure on member states to take additional regulatory action that could hamper the internal market. finally, the proposal seeks to remove obstacles to external trade through harmonised rules and by reducing the regulatory barriers that result from diverging emission requirements. in particular with a view to bringing eu and us requirements closer together. we should focus primarily in urban conglomeration where there is a higher concentration of people that are affected by air pollution.

mr president, i voted in favour of the report in order to promote the social inclusion and integration into the labour market of people seeking refuge in europe from the situation of war or threat in their country of origin, because it is urgent to find solutions to deal with more guarantees in a situation for which we were not prepared, but to which we cannot turn a blind eye. it is therefore necessary to take immediate action, always applying the principles of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility necessary to tackle this problem common to all europe and which therefore requires a common response from all europe.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that respect for human rights and international law must go hand in hand with the dignified integration of refugees and asylum seekers into our societies. in this sense, we are convinced that social and labour integration is the spearhead to achieve this. the report calls for increased investment by the union in social and labour policies to tackle this situation, and to prevent it from being to the detriment of those european citizens who are already in a vulnerable situation in our countries. it therefore called for the european social fund's share in the structural and investment funds to be increased to 25%. it calls for the maximum time for a refugee to acquire the right to participate in the host country's labour market to be reduced to just six months. and that their access to training, housing, health, education, as well as recognition of their skills and family reunification, can be guaranteed. a comprehensive and robust report with recommendations that can be key to the long-term management of the crisis we are suffering.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to make a number of recommendations to facilitate the inclusion of refugees in the workplace. this is a good way to end the precarious situation in which most refugees in the european union live, as well as to fight for their empowerment and against the xenophobia that continues to spread across the continent. i therefore voted in favour of the report, which contains a number of elements which we regard very positively, such as the demand for access to rights such as housing, health care, education, or the involvement of social organisations and trade unions in the process. the commission is also proposing that refugees be given access to the labour market after a maximum of six months in the union and that they be paid the same minimum wage as the rest of the population. these are two key elements for the review of the directive 2013/33/eu on the reception of asylum seekers, one of the main european regulations that needs to be amended to ensure that refugees living in our society enjoy effective equality.
in writing. ‒ as stated in the universal declaration of human rights, everyone has the right to work. work, in addition to being a right, is the fundamental instrument for the integration and development of any person. the union must not only comply with the common asylum policy by allowing refugees to be admitted, but also facilitate their inclusion in the labour market as the necessary pathway to their full integration into our society. this report contains a large number of measures aimed at achieving this objective. it also pays special attention to vulnerable groups such as women and children. i welcome the fact that it denounces the situation in the refugee camps, stresses the importance of education as a vital factor for integration and access to the labour market, and seeks to avoid any discrimination against asylum seekers. from the beginning of the refugee crisis i have always advocated the need for a solidarity response to it and the implementation of the common european asylum system. i believe in a europe where there is room for those who suffer from the conflicts and misery that plague their countries. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it is a first step towards improving the policies of social inclusion and integration of refugees. the text speaks of guaranteeing access to housing, education and training, social protection, health and family reunification, all of which are inalienable rights of people seeking international protection and which our delegation defends. increasing public investment with an increase in the esf, as the report says, is good news, as is ensuring that refugees can enter the labour market no later than 6 months after applying and that they have a minimum wage equal to that of other nationals, avoiding dumping and exploitation of the most vulnerable. in the paragraph on the blue card, however, i voted against because we must avoid rewarding some refugees over others on grounds of origin or education. however, on the whole it is a positive report and i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for her work on this report on the social inclusion and labour market integration of refugees. i voted differently from my group on paragraph 79, which deals with the recommendation that additional language classes be provided for refugee children in the language of their country of origin. i have also supported the recital in which reference is made to the inhuman conditions in which refugees live in camps, without access to sufficient quality resources and services to meet their basic needs. i am glad that this report has been adopted by a large majority.

in writing. ‒ this report deals with the integration and inclusion of 'refugees', a term which is inappropriate in this case, since a refugee is in principle supposed to return to his country once the conflict has been resolved. in reality, the text refers to migrants, whom the commission considers to be a boon for the member states, as they would be the miracle solution to the demographic crisis and the ageing of the population. the commission prefers to welcome millions of migrants, without worrying about whether they will integrate and especially assimilate, rather than developing natalist policies. the commission also intends to put in place provisions to offer refugees a job within six months of their application, at a time when most european countries are in crisis and unemployment persists, particularly among young people. for these reasons our group tabled an alternative motion for a resolution and i naturally voted against this report.
