mr president, we in this parliament have adopted a motion for a resolution calling for the implementation of the recommendations we made in 2010 on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate civil liability. in the european union we do not have a regulatory framework on how companies must respect human rights obligations and respect social and environmental standards. but i think we all agree that the private sector must contribute, together with the public sector, to sustainable development and that companies must act in a responsible way from all points of view, but, fundamentally, from a social point of view and also - why not say - from an ecological point of view.
in writing. ‒ this report looks at the implementation of three previous ep reports with recommendations on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate civil liability in the union's trade agreements with third parties. i voted in favour of it because it clearly points out the shortcomings in parliament's previous recommendations, while at the same time going further and introducing new aspects which i consider to be extremely positive and important, such as the requirement that the human rights clause in these agreements be binding.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report which makes clear the need to make the human rights clauses in trade agreements binding. other elements that we have considered positively are the granting of official observer status to the ilo in the wto. finally, we believe that the call for all parties to multilateral and bilateral agreements in which the union is involved to ratify and implement the ilo core conventions can have a great impact in the context of the tisa and ttip negotiations (since the us has not currently acceded to these conventions).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate social responsibility. and i have also supported the call for mandatory human rights and sustainability impact assessments to be started at an early stage so that they can be taken into account in the negotiating positions.
in writing. ‒ we socialists believe that trade policy should be another tool for sustainable development and, to be effective, it must be linked ineluctably to binding and fully enforceable objectives in the areas of social, labour, environmental and human rights, with appropriate accountability for both governments and businesses. this own-initiative report gives us a new opportunity to remind us that it is the responsibility of everyone, public and private, men and women, to ensure that international trade benefits the world's population equally, putting the general interest of society above any other objective. that is why i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ this report looks at the implementation of three previous ep reports with recommendations on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate civil liability in the union's trade agreements with third parties. i voted in favour of it because it clearly points out the shortcomings in parliament's previous recommendations, while at the same time going further and introducing new aspects which i consider to be extremely positive and important, such as the requirement that the human rights clause in these agreements be binding.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is important and very beneficial for international treaties to incorporate environmental, social and human rights clauses, in line with the 'trade for all' strategy. i believe that trade agreements are also a good tool for promoting european values and for helping to raise both social and environmental standards worldwide. this needs to be done through specific clauses and not as an ex post exchange of information, as was common in previous trade agreements.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i am convinced that we must continue to ensure that companies maintain and improve social and environmental standards, human rights and civil responsibility. this means ensuring effective taxation in the countries where they carry out their economic activities, including clauses on respect for human rights and the environment in trade agreements, etc. the union can and must contribute, together with civil society and business, to improving the living conditions of millions of people, not just in the union but around the world.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report which makes clear the need to make the human rights clauses in trade agreements binding. other elements that we have considered positively are the granting of official observer status to the ilo in the wto. finally, we believe that the call for all parties to multilateral and bilateral agreements in which the union is involved to ratify and implement the ilo core conventions can have a great impact in the context of the tisa and ttip negotiations (since the us has not currently acceded to these conventions).
in writing. ‒ the forenza report on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate civil responsibility assesses the implementation of the european parliament's recommendations adopted in 2010. it also stressed the importance of respect for human rights, gender equality, environmental protection and sustainable development, the defence of labour rights and the eradication of child labour. it also recognises the right of people to access water, healthcare and education, promotes the elimination of fossil fuel subsidies, supports the energy transition and the development of renewable energies and requires strict compliance with the civil responsibility of companies. eh bildu therefore supports the report and voted in favour, despite the doubts that may arise from the mention that trade and foreign investment increase the prosperity of the poorest countries and are essential for economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and the protection of human rights. the experience of the current business model shows us that this is not the case and it is essential and urgent to implement the recommendations made in the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe it is essential to establish mandatory traceability systems, which enable companies of all sizes and throughout the production chain and, at the end of the process, the consumer, to obtain sufficient information to be able to assume their share of responsibility. but the first responsibility must lie with governments, as guarantors of the welfare of their people, and with the big multinationals, because of the obvious impact of their activities. the report calls on the commission to: take the lead in reforming the world trade organisation (wto), strengthen its legitimacy and enable more effective global trade regulation that is more consistent with the goals of sustainable development, with responsible and sustainable management of global supply chains; ensure that the gender perspective is mainstreamed in trade policy; include strong corporate social responsibility and human rights legislation in all trade agreements, with ambitious, binding and fully enforceable trade and sustainable rights chapters; and call for the reinforcement of parliamentary and civil society participation in all trade negotiations, promoting these goals within and beyond our borders.

in writing. ‒ trade plays an essential role in promoting employment opportunities, social development and economic progress, it is important that businesses find support in the union to carry out their activities safely. trade and investment agreements have direct consequences on human rights and sustainable development and should therefore be designed to reflect european standards. this is reflected in the 'trade for all' strategy, which has finally established the link between them and thus crystallized the need for action by the european union to help its citizens. since the european parliament made some recommendations to the commission, some of which were not implemented, and since there are still companies established within the union's borders which do not respect human rights, i am voting in favour of this report which calls for the highest level of ambition from the commission.
in writing. ‒ trade and human rights can be mutually reinforcing. elements such as the sustainable development goals demonstrate that it is possible to use trade to promote the defence of human rights, and trade diplomacy and trade agreements are one of the ramifications that the european union has to firmly protect social rights and environmental protection. if we allow these weapons to lose their meaning and become something that is predatory, we will not only be failing in our international responsibility but we will be going against the past and the spirit of the union. the european union has at its disposal a tool such as trade, which is important in order to export the common values, values which are sorely needed in many places outside our borders. if we are responsible and fair, we can gain a lever to give a decisive boost to the defence of human rights outside the union.
in writing. ‒ we socialists believe that trade policy should be another tool for sustainable development and, to be effective, it must be linked ineluctably to binding and fully enforceable objectives in the areas of social, labour, environmental and human rights, with appropriate accountability for both governments and businesses. this own-initiative report gives us a new opportunity to remind us that it is the responsibility of everyone, public and private, men and women, to ensure that international trade benefits the world's population equally, putting the general interest of society above any other objective. that is why i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ the report calls on the european commission and the member states to adopt an approach in all their policies that integrates issues of major importance such as the achievement of the 17 sustainable development goals of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development adopted by the united nations general assembly, the need to ensure access to commons such as water, healthcare and education to ensure social rights and respect for human rights, and the importance of promoting corporate social responsibility (csr) and forging cooperation at unilateral, bilateral and multilateral levels on social, environmental and human rights standards to advance these goals. i therefore think it necessary to vote in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i very much agree with this report, as i think it is very important to take environmental and social aspects into account when establishing any type of trade agreement. it is a job the union has been doing for years, so all its agreements include provisions on trade and sustainable development, enhancing transparency and dialogue with civil society. the union is also currently applying the generalised system of preferences (gsp) and its equivalent for developing countries (gsp+) simultaneously, with the aim of further enhancing the role of the environment and the role of green technologies, which are key in negotiations with other countries. i therefore believe that the union is playing a role which can certainly make a positive contribution to sustainable development by including clauses on the aspects i have mentioned.
the report we adopted this morning on an innovative strategy points to the need to adapt more rapidly to the rapidly changing trends in world trade. we need to support a transparent trade policy and greater citizen participation and achieve greater coherence between the union's trade objectives and other aspects of its external policy in the area of trade for development. we support the promotion of world trade from a multilateral approach within the world trade organisation and the right to decide, in our own interests, which free trade agreements to negotiate in the future. in this proposal too we make clear once again our opposition to the granting of market economy status to china and the need for more effective trade defence instruments.
in writing. ‒ the report deals with the latest commission communication: 'trade for all'. i voted against it because this new communication reaffirms the union's trade policy orientation towards accelerating the liberalisation of public services. i could not vote in favour of the report because i believe that the union's trade policy should be a 180-degree turn, respectful of the asymmetries within and between the blocs, and based on fair trade rather than on the best interests of europe. i have therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ we abstained because, although there are some very positive aspects in this report, it is ambiguous in supporting a strategy which is essentially pro-free market at any price such as 'trade for all'. we welcome the fact that it draws attention to issues that the free market dogma tends to camouflage in most debates (i.e. 'considering that there has been no serious debate in the eu on free trade policies'), publishes negotiating mandates immediately, reinforces policy coherence for development, and makes the labour, social and environmental rights chapters of trade agreements binding. however, we cannot vote in favour because the underlying logic is support for the commission's strategy, and to promote foreign trade as a solution to european problems and support for the commission's 'trade for all' strategy, which proposes a strategy for the future that can only lead the eu and its partners to deepen the inequalities, the increase of which we have been witnessing for decades.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report on the new forward-looking and innovative trade and investment strategy and voted for greater protection of the full spectrum of intellectual property rights and for the commission to develop legislation to ban the import of products manufactured through any form of forced labour or modern slavery. i have also supported the reference to the union's manufacturing industry which is too often neglected in favour of the services sector.
in writing. ‒ the new eu trade and investment strategy calls for a more effective trade policy, to generate new economic opportunities, more transparent, opening trade negotiations to greater public scrutiny through the publication of their key texts, and more responsible, redoubling efforts to ensure responsible management of supply chains, safeguarding the european social and regulatory model within the union and promoting european values such as sustainable development, human rights, fair and ethical trade and the fight against corruption in the world. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of workers' health and safety at work, the protection of workers' rights in the event of accidents at work and the protection of workers' rights in the event of serious accidents. the report also calls for greater efforts to use trade negotiations as a tool to promote gender equality worldwide. for all these reasons, i have supported the report with my vote.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because the report gives a positive assessment of the union's new trade and investment strategy and brings to the table some of the shortcomings of the commission's communication. the report calls on the commission to implement the recommendations made by the european ombudsman on access to documents relating to all trade negotiations. it called for the recommendations of parliament in its resolutions on the ttip and tisa negotiations to be respected and for a multilateral solution to investment disputes to be found in the medium term. the report opposes the granting of market economy status to china. it stressed that labour and environmental standards must be respected throughout the supply chain and called on the commission to introduce legislation aimed at prohibiting the import of products manufactured by any form of forced labour or modern slavery. it requires that no trade agreement should result in a lower level of regulatory protection, that any change in the level of protection should only be upwards, and that the right of public authorities to regulate should be fully protected, while maintaining european standards.

in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal is a new trade and investment strategy for the eu entitled 'trade for all - towards a more responsible trade and investment policy'. it is very important that this new strategy responds to citizens' concerns about globalisation. greater transparency, participation and accountability in relation to all parties involved is needed. the commission is therefore asked to ensure that transparency is promoted in future negotiations and the council is asked to publish all negotiating mandates. as regards the external challenges facing the union, i consider that consistency between trade objectives and other aspects of its foreign policy is a priority. trade agreements need to be defined and human rights, labour and social standards and environmental sustainability promoted. for all these reasons, i am voting in favour and urge the commission to update the commercial strategy regularly and to present a detailed annual report to enable european citizens to check whether the commission is complying with what has been agreed.

mr president, in this house we strongly denounce and reject human trafficking, which is a growing business at the expense of human suffering and affects all societies and economies in a profound and persistent way. we are certainly facing an extremely lucrative business and it will take unity, collaboration and firmness to eradicate these practices and the different forms of exploitation. the union's policy on trafficking in human beings, as we have agreed in a report in this parliament, must therefore be linked to the community's external action in order to establish more coherent and effective cooperation in developing systems to identify, protect and assist victims, to improve the prevention of trafficking, to facilitate the prosecution of traffickers and to create a network to enable rapid response to difficulties that may arise.
in writing. ‒ it is a well-intentioned initiative, but it does not offer concrete and specific solutions that contribute to the real fight against trafficking in human beings. urgent measures that must involve actions by transit countries that are crucial to combating this scourge are not given priority. that is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this report. although the text contains elements which i support, as far as the effective protection of persons in situations of forced mobility and especially the most vulnerable is concerned, i do not share the general approach of the text, which absolves european countries of all responsibility for the root and structural causes and the dramatic consequences of mass migration by concentrating action solely on trafficking networks, which are the consequence of a failed asylum and immigration system. nor do we share the security vision in the face of the humanitarian crisis, which on the one hand doubly victimizes refugees and on the other generates a very lucrative business linked to the large arms companies, whose expansion is linked to the prevalence of wars that cause mass exodus.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for her work and good work on this report on the fight against trafficking in human beings in the eu's external relations. it considers that governments should encourage dialogue and partnerships between different stakeholders in order to take joint action against trafficking in human beings and to ensure respect for workers' rights. the commission is also proposing to introduce legal measures to ensure transparency and traceability of products in the supply chain. it is necessary to ensure that products are free from exploitation throughout the supply chain and to establish responsibilities in cases of trafficking in human beings occurring at any point in the chain, including subsidiaries and subcontractors.
in writing. ‒ trafficking in human beings is one of the worst forms of human rights abuse, reducing people to mere commodities, violating the dignity, integrity and rights of the victim and affecting entire families and communities, deliberately exploiting situations of vulnerability such as poverty or isolation. it is also an extremely lucrative business, with its revenues being injected back into the global economy and financial system. in view of this situation, the report, which i have supported, calls on the commission and the member states, among other things, to strengthen cooperation with third countries in order to investigate all stages of trafficking in human beings, to improve the exchange of information and to undertake operations, (financial) investigations and preventive legal action. it also called for cooperation with third countries to be adapted to the new situation created by the development of trafficking on the internet and for national child protection regimes in europe to be strengthened as part of the union's strategy to combat trafficking. it also encourages the eu to develop a new anti-trafficking strategy for the period after 2016 with a strengthened and more selective external dimension.

in writing. ‒ the lochbihler report has many positive proposals on how to combat trafficking in human beings. it contains many good ideas but the overall language and spirit of the report, when it comes to migration and asylum issues, is very much that of fortress europe. the gender perspective is present and a clear link is made between prostitution and human trafficking. the problem is the ‘hidden’ support in the text for a fortress europe policy. the eu’s inhumane and increasingly restrictive refugee and migration policy pops up in several places in the report. efforts to combat human trafficking are used as an excuse for cooperation with dictatorships, under the khartoum process, and to legitimise eu military operations in the mediterranean (eu with nav). this is not acceptable. therefore, since there are many positive points but also some which are not that positive, eh bildu abstained in the final vote on this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it highlights that trafficking in human beings is a highly lucrative business and the proceeds of this criminal activity are returned to the global economy and the financial system. the report reviews the different forms of exploitation. it describes the rights of victims, including the right to compensation or damages. the report also deals with cooperation against trafficking in human beings at regional and global level and the union's policy in its external relations. a clear link is established between the illegal trafficking of migrants and human trafficking in general.

in writing. ‒ the report deals with the union's responsibility in its work to combat trafficking in human beings and aims to improve coordination relations between institutions and to promote the creation of joint actions. the aim is not only to implement these measures within the european union but also to improve relations with third countries in order to facilitate the identification of victims and thus protect and assist them. it also includes the need to put in place means to control cases of forced marriages, as these can sometimes be transnational in nature and have a direct link with trafficking. the report also states that people with disabilities are particularly vulnerable and can therefore be the target of these groups. because of the need to adopt a coherent policy both internally and externally, and to ensure that it reflects the union's fundamental values, i am voting in favour of its adoption.

in writing. ‒ it is a well-intentioned initiative, but it does not offer concrete and specific solutions that contribute to the real fight against trafficking in human beings. urgent measures that must involve actions by transit countries that are crucial to combating this scourge are not given priority. that is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i very much agree with this report: human trafficking is a phenomenon comparable to modern slavery and one of the worst forms of human rights abuse. with globalization, this type of crime has been increasing, as it has provided new tools to facilitate their crimes and make their prosecution more difficult. for this reason, it is increasingly necessary that european legislation be as forceful and decisive as possible. i believe that the eu strategy for the eradication of trafficking in human beings (2012-2016) should provide continuity to the policy lines for their review. i believe that the key aspects are identifying the most vulnerable groups, widening the channels of action against traffickers in human beings and recovering the proceeds of this crime.

mr president, for almost a decade now, each successive presidency has had to face a new crisis, but at the same time it inherits all the previous ones: the financial crisis, the euro crisis, the security crisis, the refugee and migrant crisis. their specific crisis is brexit. we had a debate in this parliament yesterday. i think the majority position is in favour of immediate triggering of article 50, negotiation led by the commission and the search for the cleanest possible outcome and a win-win agreement, but at the same time maintaining that whoever leaves cannot keep the advantages of whoever stays without also taking on their own responsibilities. but there are some causes of the crises that have been there for a few years: insufficient growth, high unemployment - especially unacceptable among young people - poverty and inequality, growing lack of cohesion within the union, inhuman reception of refugees and alienation of citizens. all these crises, all these causes, must be answered positively. fear and hate are more intense, stronger human reactions than trust and solidarity, but only trust and solidarity promote cohesive and progressive societies. we therefore need positive proposals that reach the citizens, that strengthen confidence and solidarity. otherwise, fear and hate will drag us down.
mr president, as has been said many times, we are entering this presidency under a certain shock, the shock of the united kingdom's withdrawal as a result of the referendum result. but it should be noted that emotions should not cloud judgment or analytical ability. decisions must be made, but we must never lose the capacity for calm reflection, either on this or on other matters. i believe that there is one question, which is fundamental in the end: that the european union must always follow the path of responding clearly and efficiently to real needs. this means responding to all those economic issues that allow for more growth and more jobs; this means that in a world of global transformation, together with digital transformation, digital transformation in all its aspects is at the forefront of the 'digital' decisions of the european union. you have said that the digital single market is an urgent need. we must break this legislative fragmentation. we have a number of dossiers, such as the one on the wholesale market, which affects the end of roaming. you say that there are three principles which will guide you: tangible results that affect the lives of citizens, improvement of living conditions, breaking with fragmentation and restoring confidence in the european project. three fundamental foundations that require leadership for this to be effective. we trust you to develop it.
mr president, prime minister fico, you have heard in this house the expression of good wishes for the slovak presidency, but you have also heard concern about those outbreaks of racism and xenophobia which have become apparent in the immediate aftermath of brexit in the united kingdom, but which are sweeping europe. because europe needs advocates for its cause and, in particular, prime ministers and heads of government who defend the european cause, its values, the common asylum policy, the policy of free movement of persons, the schengen system - and who do so with a european dimension and that also happens, of course, through the slovak presidency - and a commitment to the achievement of the objectives of the lisbon treaty. and so i ask you to dispense with those statements which have led many in europe to think that there is a rotating presidency of the european union with a prime minister who thinks that you are not slovak enough if you profess another religion, you are not european enough if you profess another identity. because slovakia is a success story, it is the story of european integration that embraces its own diversity and reconciles with the identities of its neighbours. we asked him to do that in the slovak presidency.
mr president, two years ago president juncker presented the commission's priorities for this period. since then, the european union has been rocked by crises: the financial crisis, the euro crisis, the refugee crisis and the security crisis, all of which have interfered with the commission's work in some way, but it is true that the commission has been working continuously on some issues that are less visible, that are insufficient, but which are basically positive. what this motion for a resolution does is to define the major challenges we face and to call for european action to meet those challenges: the insufficient growth of our economy, which is a growth that is for a long time insufficient and lower than that of other competitors or other large economies; the maintenance of sustained, unsustainable youth unemployment; the growing inequality within the union; the deterioration of territorial cohesion; the loss of labour rights and social protection; the breakdown of respect for democratic rules in several countries of the union; solidarity with respect to territorial cohesion within the european union; and the alienation of citizens. and we hope that these european responses, which the commission has promoted, will have the support of parliament and the council.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have the impression that when i read a commission text on the future of europe, i have to read it in code: where it says 'governance', we should read 'inequality', and where it says 'cohesion', it means 'preferential treatment'. there is certainly something wrong between the plans they propose and the objectives for 2020, which should be to deepen european integration, putting social cohesion first. but this contradicts the commission's obsessive mantra of "austerity and cuts". it is unacceptable, unacceptable, that the commission is proposing to impose a penalty on spain and portugal for not complying with the deficit. it is unacceptable because there have been other countries which have failed to do much more than spain and portugal, but they are doing it to spain to justify the anti-social policies which the spanish government is willing to implement, because they are using public institutions to defend their political projects, which put the citizens of europe in the last place. and it is unacceptable because the reason why there is no economic recovery in spain is precisely that we have implemented those policies which are drowning out the citizens and which in europe have already generated more than 123 million poor people.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft amending budget on the surplus for the financial year 2015. the dossier recommends that, given that there was a surplus of 1 350 million in the budget last year, that, although it is legally required that member states' contributions for the coming year be discounted, that this money be used in a finalist way for the purpose of dealing with immigration in humanitarian terms. the regulation says that the discount must be made the following year, and parliament has no power to prevent it. we think it is good that parliament is speaking in these terms, because it would be ideal if this money did not return to the states and were used for such a laudable purpose.

in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 2/2016 returns to the 2016 budget the surplus of eur 1,3 million resulting from the implementation of the 2015 budgetary year and consequently reduces the total contribution of the member states to the financing of the 2016 eu budget. parliament called on the member states to honour their pledges in relation to the refugee crisis and to make the contributions to which they have committed in relation to the african and madad trust funds respectively. it also considered that the eu budget should be able to reuse any surplus resulting from under-utilisation or fines in order to meet its financing needs and hoped that this issue would be resolved during the negotiations of the next revision of the multiannual financial framework. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ this report on the proposal for a directive on measures to ensure a high common level of network and information security in the union supports the council's favourable position on the proposal. the proposal contains a number of measures whose common objective is to ensure a high common level of security of network and information systems in the union. security must be synonymous with cooperation. without the exchange of information between all member states, without a collective effort to do so, and without the trust that this requires, we will not succeed in solving the major challenges in this area. we must give cybersecurity the importance it deserves at a time like the present, characterized by the rise of new technologies and the different threats that put our security at risk. i voted in favour of this strategy because i share the aims of ensuring a secure and reliable digital environment. but i will not forget to defend the compatibility of these objectives with the promotion and protection of fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the security of network and information systems, as it has several points of interest. a key element of the directive is that member states should ensure that public bodies and certain market operators adopt appropriate technical and organisational measures to manage security risks in network and information systems, which should ensure a level of security appropriate to the risks and prevent and minimise the impact of security incidents affecting the basic services they provide. it is for member states to ensure that digital service providers inform the competent authorities. the result of the three-way dialogue is weaker than the original proposal in that the scope has been limited and fewer digital service providers are included than in the original commission proposal. however, there are still a lot of positive issues in the outcome and the directive will create an obligation to report, which until now did not exist. we therefore regard it as positive as a whole.
in writing. ‒ in 2013, the commission presented the proposal for a directive to ensure a high common level of network and information security (nis directive). parliament adopted the proposal for a directive at first reading on 13 march 2014. after more than a year of negotiations, a political agreement was reached with the council on 7 december. the nis directive represents the first union-wide legislation on cybersecurity and its main objective is to improve security in the eu online environment and to strengthen cooperation between member states and european institutions in this area, overcoming the current fragmentation. the negotiations have not been easy given the fear of some member states of losing their prerogatives in the field of national security and of sharing information on their national strategies to prevent cyberattacks and other related threats. however, the nis directive will improve cybersecurity capabilities in member states, enhance their cooperation in this field and require different operators of essential services as well as key digital service providers to take appropriate security measures and to report security incidents to national authorities. i have therefore voted in favour.

madam president, it looks like we're about to debut new energy-efficient labeling for home appliances. energy efficiency is a key to reducing our consumption and our energy bill. the new regulation restores the original scale, which was from a to g, and removes those categories which were a and a series of crosses, of +, which was quite confusing. today, technology is evolving very rapidly. we therefore proposed that the labelling should be adjusted every three years. unfortunately, the ppe group, in an attempt to protect industrial firms, proposed that this should be done every eight years. we strongly believe that large companies should adapt to environmental legislation, not the other way around. contrary to popular belief, investment in improvements of this kind creates jobs and sustainable growth. we therefore believe that this report is a useful tool to promote and make more understandable the devices that consume less energy. at the same time, it allows citizens to be actors in the energy transition towards a more moderate energy model.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it represents an improvement in consumer information in terms of the energy efficiency of the purchased product. in a context where the response to the problem of climate change is crucial for all of humanity, any progress towards reducing energy consumption is key to the future of humanity. this report, which deals specifically with the ways in which certain goods can be labelled as energy efficient, is a step forward in improving the information distributed to consumers and enabling better informed consumption. the report substantially improves on the european commission's proposal by making binding proposals to bring about a real reduction in the energy consumption of goods produced in the union. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work on this report on energy efficiency labelling which i have supported. it sets out the labels and related documents and the challenge of readjustment, the product database as the real driver of change, surveillance, safeguards, conformity assessments and additional tools for the regulation to work. it is a good agreement which will serve as a good basis for negotiation in future trilogues with the council.
in writing. ‒ the labelling of household appliances enables consumers to make informed choices about their carbon footprint. the current system is outdated, hence the current simplification to make it easier for the consumer to identify those products with higher energy efficiency, saving on the electricity bill and contributing to a better environment. article 7 is noteworthy, since it provides for a period of 5 years as a general rule for the change of scale for all labels, with the exception of dishwashers, refrigerators, washing machines, televisions and lamps, which have 21 months, and heaters (6 years). we socialists believe that this 're-scaling' reflects the real use of household appliances and is not the result of laboratory tests which, as with 'dieselgate', may result in higher energy consumption under real conditions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road. we also advocated, without success, that member states should direct their incentives towards low-income consumers at risk of energy poverty.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because i am convinced that since its creation, the label has helped citizens to better understand the environmental impact and the life cycle of products. the evaluation of directive 2010/30/ec identified a number of shortcomings which, once addressed, can lead to significant additional energy savings. to achieve this we must bear in mind that a balance needs to be struck between citizens, industry and other stakeholders.
in writing. ‒ energy efficiency is a key to reducing our consumption and energy bill. the new labelling model proposed takes account of technological advances and eliminates the problems of the old model. the new regulation restores the original scale from a to g and removes those categories of a and a series of + that were quite confusing. we think it's a useful tool to push and make more understandable devices that consume less energy. at the same time, it allows citizens to be actors in the transition to an energy model that is at least more cost-conscious. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the labelling of household appliances allows consumers to make informed choices about their carbon footprint when buying new products, in order to contribute to reducing emissions and saving on the energy bill. the proposal aims to simplify the current system so that consumers can more easily identify the most energy-efficient products on the market. in this way, the labelling will reflect the actual use of the appliances and not be the result of laboratory tests which may result in higher energy consumption under real conditions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it represents an improvement in consumer information in terms of the energy efficiency of the purchased product, substantially improving the european commission's proposal by incorporating binding proposals for the reduction of energy consumption.
in writing. ‒ in order to achieve the commission's target of reducing pollution levels by 27% by 2030, set in october 2014, a number of measures have been taken, including the creation of information labels on products to help citizens better understand the environmental impact of what they use and their life cycle. but the labelling process is undergoing a readjustment and this is a delicate point as it requires a lot of objectivity and precision, although because the new labels are necessary to improve certain aspects of this procedure we should not stagnate, but know how to adopt the new changes, using the circular economy as the main tool. the new approach is the guarantor of the adaptation of the existing regulations to the needs of the new society, characterized by the technological progress which we must take advantage of and use in our favour. for the reasons outlined above, i am voting in favour of this report, so that well-designed social awareness can be the real driver of the change we need, making citizens the real protagonists of the eu's energy transition.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the proposal for a regulation establishing a framework for energy efficiency labelling. we have introduced some amendments which i believe will improve the text and with which, i am sure, we will improve the regulation of labelling, which has helped citizens to understand better the environmental impact and the life cycle of products. we are trying to correct a number of shortcomings in the previous directive which, once resolved, can lead to significant additional energy savings.
in writing. ‒ one of the keys to economic development for the promotion of the so-called green economy. it is clear that there is much work to be done and that there is a lack of development in terms of energy sufficiency, saving and efficiency. energy labelling is a key part of the energy efficiency policies to be developed. this regulation proposes simplification of the labelling of household appliances, which will help citizens to better understand the environmental impact and life cycle of products, with the resulting energy savings, not to mention the positive impact on information and communication technologies. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this proposal for a regulation.

in writing. ‒ this decision replaces directive 2010/30/eu by a regulation which maintains the same scope but modifies and strengthens some of its provisions, taking into account the rapid technological advances for energy efficiency of products achieved in recent years. the legislation needs to be adapted so that consumers have as much information as possible when buying their products. that is why i think it is necessary to vote in favour of this decision.

madam president, the creation of the european border and coast guard reinforces the idea of building a fortress europe, it is just another step in the closure of frontiers. we are responding to the greatest humanitarian crisis in our history in a security way, with a closure of borders that makes us complicit in the thousands and thousands of deaths in the mediterranean, of all those people who are turning the mediterranean into the greatest mass grave. this border and coast guard is just increasing the process of outsourcing of borders that has been seen with the agreement between the european union and turkey. if we do not want to have blood on our hands any longer, we must respond to the construction of fortress europe by opening safe passageways for refugees and by adopting measures of welcome, not security and militarism. i believe that this step, this building of this european border and coast guard, is wrecking the european project morally and politically. we will not be complicit in this shipwreck.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation because it extends the agency's prerogatives in the field of migration management, the fight against crossborder crime and because it strengthens search and rescue operations. thanks to the intervention of the socialists, the safeguards of fundamental rights and the agency's accountability to the european parliament and the council have been strengthened. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european union border control system. the european border and coast guard should deploy its action building on the mandate and experience of frontex, but overcoming its limitations and the malfunctions identified over its years of experience and above all reinforcing the protection dimension of fundamental rights. parliamentary control, democratic scrutiny, has also been established over the work of the agency, which must now be filled with content and meaning. we cannot allow this parliamentary control to become an empty procedure.
in writing. ‒ the new european border and coast guard agency, the new body to replace frontex, is a key building block for the construction of fortress europe. the process of militarizing the union's borders is being advanced with a new agency whose tasks also include internal security, thus assuming the dangerous xenophobic discourse of the extreme right which links migration with insecurity. we have opposed the creation of this agency, which for the first time will have its own staff and resources and will be able to act even without the consent of the states in which it operates, because what is intended is to make a single migration policy from the most aggressive postulates against migrants. it will take over the removal of detainees from the member states and will have the capacity to intervene in third countries. it therefore prevents the creation of humanitarian corridors and safe access routes, perpetuating the current model that makes the union's borders the places with the highest death rates in the world.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation to create a european border and coast guard (ebcg) is, along with shameful bilateral treaties such as the one with turkey, the european union's response to the migration crisis. instead of turning to a foreign policy which is tirelessly seeking stability and respect for human rights in the areas of origin of these desperate migratory movements, combined with a policy of welcome worthy of the essential values of this union, what is proposed is, once again, a policy of rejection. the gefc is the multiplication of frontex, in capacity and autonomy, to prevent the entry of migrants fleeing war and misery. the pabriks report welcomes this proposal, which is intended to meet the expectations of the most unsolidarist governments. in so far as it goes against the values that define us, such as the defence of the right to a life of dignity for all people, regardless of their origin or status, i am voting against the pabriks report.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this proposal because i believe that sharing responsibility for the guarding of external borders among all member states is key to separating economic immigration from refugee flows, ensuring more humane treatment for all people fleeing poverty or war and preventing and intervening to prevent further tragedies at sea and fighting human traffickers. it is also wise to coordinate the work of these new european agents with the resources and knowledge of the european maritime safety agency and the european fisheries control agency. it would have been a real blunder to double the expenditure and to extend the time needed to implement this instrument. it is one, but it is one of the essential tools for a european solution to the refugee crisis.

in writing. ‒ in the face of the flagrant failure of the frontex agency, which is responsible for securing the union's external borders, and the massive immigration we have been experiencing for the past two years, the european commission has proposed the creation of a new agency to replace frontex. the new agency will be called the european border and coast guard agency. this agency will bring together frontex and the national border management authorities. it will have the task of controlling the external borders but also of helping to control the internal borders. this dual vocation alone shows the intended failure and incompetence of the agency: why should there be a problem at internal borders if we really control external borders? in reality, this system is essentially aimed at saving schengen and its sacrosanct principle of free movement of persons, european citizens or illegal immigrants. the report endorses the commission's proposal to strengthen the european union's grip on border management. this project will be presented as a miracle solution to the problem of uncontrolled immigration, when it will solve nothing as long as the eu refuses to apply the firm policy of the australian government: to refuse all illegal immigration. i voted against it, of course.

in writing. ‒the new european border and coast guard agency, the new body to replace frontex, is a key building block for the construction of fortress europe. the process of militarizing the union's borders is being advanced with a new agency whose tasks also include internal security, thus assuming the dangerous xenophobic discourse of the extreme right which links migration with insecurity. we have opposed the creation of this agency, which for the first time will have its own staff and resources and will be able to act even without the consent of the states in which it operates, because what is intended is to make a single migration policy from the most aggressive postulates against migrants. it will take over the removal of detainees from the member states and will have the capacity to intervene in third countries. it therefore prevents the creation of humanitarian corridors and safe access routes, perpetuating the current model that makes the union's borders the places with the highest death rates in the world.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation of the ep and the council on the european border and coast guard is necessary as the migration crisis requires an increase in the level of effectiveness in the control of the administration, due to the growth of the migratory flows faced by europe in recent years. this regulation addresses the issue of the role of the european border and coast guard and the changing protocols of action needed to support those responsible and to know how to intervene immediately. it arose because some european border countries have been overwhelmed by migration flows, partly because controls within the eu's borders are very scarce and, given the scale of the migration crisis, this can pose a danger to both security and public order. in order to be able to improve border control, to monitor the crossing successfully, and to be able to meet the challenges of this mass migration, i am voting in favour of this proposal for a regulation. we are also helping to combat crime with crossborder dimensions and to safeguard security and freedom of movement within the schengen area.
in writing. ‒ my support for the proposal to create a european border and coast guard to ensure adequate control of the schengen external borders, while safeguarding the free movement of persons within the union. this is a new body which would replace frontex, but for it to work, it is essential that we ensure that it has the necessary border guards and equipment at its disposal whenever it needs them and, above all, that it can deploy them in a short timeframe when needed. in addition, while its main task will currently be to manage migration effectively at the external borders of the union, the role of the agency should also include the possibility to address threats such as crime with a cross-border dimension.
in writing. ‒ the new european border and coast guard has introduced positive measures; it will have its own resources, will step up rescue of people in distress at sea and a complaint mechanism has been set up if fundamental rights have been breached in an agency operation. now, we do not want the changes to be articulated in floating prisons. without a common system of asylum and economic migration, without solidarity between countries and governments, without better legal migration mechanisms in an ageing europe, frontex will be nothing but our ugly face. member states have resisted giving up sovereignty, which has undermined the effectiveness of all initiatives. i want a strong and resolute agency, but i want it to make a policy real consistent with the values we proclaim. no one can stop desperate people fleeing unless, in addition to a police model of border rejection, we hire third countries to carry out repression that we do not want to witness. the loss of the soul of europe will mean the ruin of us all in the short term.

in writing. ‒ i agree with this report because i believe that, given the current situation in the union, with a large influx of refugees and migrants, it is necessary to have controls on the external borders. this will not ensure a reduction in the number of people crossing our borders, but it will increase security, as we will be able to identify those who are seeking asylum and thus reduce to some extent the potential risk that could result from the entry of unidentified persons.
in writing. ‒ this report is part of the package for the creation of a european border and coast guard and seeks to amend the regulation governing the functioning of the european maritime safety agency so that it cooperates with that body mainly in the management of the union's external borders. i voted against this amendment in line with my opposition to frontex and the new proposal for a european border and coast guard to replace it, to the way in which they are dealing with the refugee problem and, in general, to the migration policy of the commission and the council.
in writing. ‒ this report is part of the package of measures proposed by the commission to renew the frontex agency. it provides for the european maritime safety and fisheries control agencies to make their technical, technological, human and (therefore) financial resources available for maritime border control tasks. it is recommended that we vote against, thus linking up with our support for the rejection am which we have tabled together with the greens in the main libe report.
in writing. ‒ the proposal is part of a package of measures presented by the commission to strengthen the protection of europe's external borders. the proposal amends the basic regulation of the european maritime safety agency (emsa) and introduces a new article authorising it to cooperate in the field of coastguards. it aims to strengthen european collaboration on coastguards and to improve cooperation and coordination between the relevant eu agencies in order to enhance synergies between their respective services and with the more than 316 national and regional authorities carrying out safeguarding functions, avoiding duplication of effort and ensuring that the main actors act in a coherent and efficient manner and develop synergies. i support this report as originally proposed by the commission.
in writing. ‒ this report is part of the package for the creation of a european border and coast guard and seeks to amend the regulation governing the functioning of the european maritime safety agency so that it cooperates with that body mainly in the management of the union's external borders. i voted against this amendment in line with my opposition to frontex and the new proposal for a european border and coast guard to replace it, to the way in which they are dealing with the refugee problem and, in general, to the migration policy of the commission and the council.
in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to develop european cooperation in coast guard functions by developing forms of cooperation between europe's border and the coast guard, the european maritime safety agency and the european fisheries control agency to improve synergies between agencies, in order to provide more efficient and cost-effective services to national authorities for the performance of multi-purpose coast guard functions. emsa will in particular lead to a significant improvement in surveillance capacity to reinforce the control of the european union's external maritime borders
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the creation of the european maritime safety agency, which will help to strengthen the exchange of information and cooperation on coast guard functions and emerging risks in the maritime domain.
in writing. ‒ the report presented aims in principle to strengthen the cooperation between frontex, which will become the european border and coast guard agency, and the european maritime safety agency. in reality, it is a question of involving the latter in the management of migration flows. it is clear that the aim of this cooperation is not to combat illegal immigration but rather to facilitate the work of smugglers by organising the rescue and then the repatriation of migrants to europe. my colleague marie-christine arnautu had amended the commission's legislative proposal so that this agreement would be used to combat illegal immigration and not to facilitate it. but his report was not adopted, as the european union continues to facilitate the flood of migration.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because the creation of the agency aims to strengthen the protection of europe's external borders, includes a proposal to amend the basic regulation of the maritime safety agency (emsa) and introduces a new article enabling it to cooperate in the field of coastguards. this legal change is intended to strengthen european collaboration in the field of coastguards and to improve cooperation and coordination between the relevant union agencies, with a view to enhancing synergies between their respective services and with the more than 316 national and regional authorities carrying out safeguarding tasks. the ultimate objective is to avoid duplication of effort and at the same time to ensure that the main actors (in particular the union agencies, the maritime safety agency and the fisheries control agency) act in a coherent and efficient manner and develop synergies.
in writing. ‒ this report is part of the package for the creation of a european border and coast guard and seeks to amend the regulation governing the functioning of the european maritime safety agency so that it cooperates with that body mainly in the management of the union's external borders. i voted against this amendment in line with my opposition to frontex and the new proposal for a european border and coast guard to replace it, to their handling of the refugee problem and to european migration policy in general.
in writing. ‒ this is part of a set of measures proposed by the european commission in 2014 to strengthen border protection. it arises from the need to improve cooperation and coordination between national bodies and agencies carrying out coast guard services, to establish a set of fundamentals on the roles of the different security bodies, and establishes when the border and coast guard, and the european fisheries control agency, should provide support to the national authorities of each country. what the proposal suggests is that the data underlying functions be shared to improve cooperation, intensify synergies and make these services more cost-effective. these needs are further recognised in multiple legislations, strategies and official agendas. the main objective is to strengthen border protection, as security plays a key role in ensuring the peace of mind of european citizens. aspects such as laying the foundations and changes in this area, such as remote piloted aircraft systems, or support for the exchange and training of personnel, are essential to making the union safe. i therefore vote in favour of its adoption.

in writing. ‒ the amendment of council regulation (ec) no 768/2005 establishing a community fisheries control agency is proposed to strengthen cooperation and information exchange with the european border and coast guard agency and the european maritime safety agency. among the objectives is to strengthen the eu's operational capacity not only in the fight against illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing, but also in the protection of the common borders. i welcome this initiative, as it will undoubtedly increase the efficiency of measures against illegal fishing and will provide significant support for the eradication of trafficking in human beings. to this end, the eu's contribution to the cef is to be increased by some eur 7.5 million per year, as is the recruitment of temporary staff. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the regulation because i felt that we needed to be better equipped, better prepared. the european fisheries control agency contributes to the control of fisheries operations but cannot currently act in other maritime areas. the proposal aims to strengthen the european union's response capacity to maritime threats and risks by improving cooperation between european agencies, but also between all civil and military actors, in order to improve maritime situational awareness and to support coherent and cost-effective action.
in writing. ‒ this amendment to the regulation on the european fisheries control agency (efca) aims to use the agency to facilitate migratory flows, under the pretext of dealing with disasters at sea. the same text was also introduced in the mandates of the european maritime safety agency (emsa) and the european border and coast guard agency. the proposal does not simply coordinate maritime surveillance, prevention and control at european level. it proposes, in particular, the addition of an article on cooperation between border and coast guard functions in the mandate of the european fisheries control agency. this proposal echoes the european parliament's pilot project on the coordination of european coast guard functions, adopted in the framework of the 2016 eu budget. we opposed this project because of its laxity: rescued migrants are never returned to their point of departure, but are instead repatriated to europe, to the point that smugglers no longer even need to reach european shores. they just have to wait for the european ships to arrive.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because this reform seeks to strengthen cooperation and the exchange of information with two other european agencies: the european border and coast guard agency and the european maritime safety agency. among the objectives, the most important is to strengthen the european union's operational capacity not only to combat illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing, but also to protect borders and to prosecute and punish those involved in the abhorrent practice of trafficking in human beings.

in writing. ‒ national authorities carrying out coastguard functions are responsible for tasks in areas as diverse as security, maritime protection and rescue, border control, customs control, environmental protection and general law enforcement. the aim of this proposal is to enable the three european agencies to coordinate and cooperate by pooling their capacity and exchanging surveillance data for the benefit of maritime safety and security. this proposal will enable the three agencies to support national authorities and act jointly to take over control, safety and surveillance operations by providing them with information, equipment and training. i believe that the responsibilities of the different european agencies should be allowed to be adapted as regards cooperation in coast guard functions, since although the means of action are national, the co-ordination of coast guard functions is european. i therefore support the adoption of the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ safety, security and rescue at sea, border and customs control or environmental protection are key functions carried out by our coastguards. however, to do a good job, more cooperation between national authorities and greater cooperation between european bodies working in the maritime field - the european fisheries control agency, the maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency - is needed. we cannot forget that the role of all these bodies is crucial in the current migration context and the european union must redouble its efforts in terms of material and human solidarity. it is therefore essential that it enhances cooperation in coast guard functions by establishing systems for the exchange of information between agencies, improving surveillance and communication services through the use of the most advanced technology, strengthening capacities at european and national level and pooling the capacity of each agency to enable the planning and enhance the execution of multi-purpose operations.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this report, through which the european parliament acts in codecision, is to amend the regulation governing the secretariat of the olaf supervisory committee. since doubts arose from the 2013 and 2014 olaf activity reports concerning the lack of independence of some of its members due to conflicts of interest, it is decided to amend the regulation to strengthen the independence of the members of those bodies. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which seeks to give greater independence, staff and resources to the secretariat of the olaf supervisory committee. this monitoring committee reports to the council and supervises olaf, the anti-fraud agency, with the result that it is less independent. the committee's work has been marked by a number of conflicts of interest and by the interference of certain committee secretaries, who have intervened on behalf of a number of companies. in our opinion, this committee should not exist, let alone be strengthened, because olaf should be controlled by parliament, but not by the council, and especially after its track record in favour of cases of specific companies which have obstructed the work of olaf. olaf does not work perfectly and can be more efficient, but this monitoring committee is not the appropriate body to do so. the eu/ngl group votes in favour of the report because it considers olaf to be an interventionist european agency which takes away the sovereignty of the states. we are in favour of this, and if so, parliament should be given more means of monitoring, even though it has had the competence to do so up to now, and that is the way it should be. strengthening this committee does create conflicts of interest.
in writing. ‒ i support this initiative because it objectively strengthens the independence of the supervisory committee of the european anti-fraud office (olaf), which will result in a more transparent and reliable exercise of a body essential to preventing crimes and practices that have caused serious economic and institutional damage in several eu states. the union institutions must be equipped to prevent this risk as much as possible. the reform will also have no budgetary impact because the material and human resources will be transferred from olaf's budgets.
in writing. ‒ the olaf monitoring committee is responsible for regularly monitoring the investigative work carried out by olaf, especially as regards the correct application of procedural safeguards and the duration of investigations. the ep has repeatedly called on the commission to take the necessary steps to strengthen the independent functioning of the secretariat of the monitoring committee. in the new proposal, the commission will be responsible for the management of the secretariat of the olaf monitoring committee, without interfering with its functioning. our group has always insisted on the need to strengthen the dialogue between the two sides in order to improve their relationship. the proposal also amends the wording of article 10 (4) and (5) so that the competence of the data protection officer of olaf will continue to cover the processing of data by the secretariat. i voted in favour of the report under the simplified procedure provided for in rule 50 (1) of the rules of procedure, without amendments or debate.

in writing. ‒ the objective of this proposal is to strengthen the independence of the olaf monitoring committee secretariat, thus providing for a more efficient functioning of this monitoring committee. this will require an independent secretariat with the appropriate staff. under the new proposal, the secretariat of the monitoring committee will be provided by the european commission, and no longer by olaf. the budget appropriations for the secretariat of the supervisory committee will be transferred from the budget line and the staff of olaf to that of the commission. the data protection competence of olaf (dpo) will continue to cover the processing of data by the secretariat. in addition, the staff of the secretariat will be subject to the same rules of confidentiality as hitherto. as i believe that the independence of the secretariat of the monitoring committee must be strengthened, with all the measures that this may entail, i am voting in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 883/2013, as regards the secretariat of the supervisory committee of the european anti-fraud office (olaf). for us, strengthening the independence of the institution helps to reach our results. the three conclusions aim at remedying weaknesses in the olaf regulation: 1) the secretariat of the supervisory committee will be provided by the commission, and no longer by olaf;2) the budgetary appropriations for the secretariat of the supervisory committee will be moved from the budget line and the establishment plan of olaf to that of the commission;3) olaf’s data protection officer will continue to cover the processing of data by the secretariat. i believe these three measures are on the right path and therefore support the report, but expect us to persist in reform and action towards a fully independent office.

in writing. ‒ this report is a golden opportunity to correct the mistakes made when we adopted the current financial framework, without sufficient funds to deal with the economic crisis, to reactivate investment, to establish a real and effective youth employment plan and with substantial cuts in development cooperation. we need more funds for all this, but we also need a proposal on own resources. in the present context we cannot continue to depend on the goodwill of the member states if what we really want is a project for a future of solidarity. the union also needs to be adjusted and made easier because there are funds which cannot be spent today because it is too complex. and also a little coherence in our policy: we cannot be asking for investment in the union to get out of the crisis and at the same time have half the countries of the union under surveillance, and they cannot co-finance their share in the structural funds and the european youth guarantee. we therefore support this report to review the current financial framework in order to define a new europe with more investment, more revenue, more ease and more coherence.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report provides the european parliament's view ahead of the revision of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. i did not vote for it because the budgetary recommendations are in line with the neoliberal policies which have so far caused the crisis in which we are still immersed. since there is no will on the part of the union to reorient these policies, as is seen in this report, i have voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted against, following the disappointing scope of the document which, despite acknowledging the numerous atrophies and shortages of resources in the face of the enormity of emerging crises to be dealt with, merely calls for greater flexibility between headings and tightening margins, without amending the legal bases of the multiannual financial framework, consolidating the role of the corset of this planning instrument for the european budget.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the preparation of the post-electoral review of the mff 2014-2020. i would like to thank the rapporteurs for their work towards its completion. it says that in 2016 it must take into account a whole series of serious crises and new political initiatives that have their budgetary consequences. i voted in favour of not reducing the allocation to the european maritime and fisheries fund and of the request to introduce one or more new resources which, if possible, have a clear link with european policies which generate added value.
in writing. ‒ this report is a golden opportunity to correct the mistakes made when we adopted the current financial framework, without sufficient funds to deal with the economic crisis, to reactivate investment, to establish a real and effective youth employment plan and with substantial cuts in development cooperation. we need more funds for all this, but we also need a proposal on own resources. in the present context we cannot continue to depend on the goodwill of the member states if what we really want is a project for a future of solidarity. the union also needs to be adjusted and made easier because there are funds which cannot be spent today because it is too complex. and also a little coherence in our policy: we cannot be asking for investment in the union to get out of the crisis and at the same time have half the countries of the union under surveillance, and they cannot co-finance their share in the structural funds and the european youth guarantee. we therefore support this report to review the current financial framework in order to define a new europe with more investment, more revenue, more ease and more coherence.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour considering that the current multiannual financial framework, agreed in 2013, reflects the priorities of the union at the time of its adoption and that the union will continue to face challenges in the coming years that were not foreseen when the multiannual financial framework was adopted. the union's funding priorities have also been multiplied, while the multiannual financial framework has remained unchanged. so if we want to have a positive impact, we must adapt the multiannual financial framework to the current needs of the citizens of the union.

in writing. ‒ the report presents an analysis that concludes that a revision of the mff is absolutely necessary if the union is to be able to effectively address a number of challenges and meet its policy objectives. we recall that the europe 2020 strategy remains the main priority to be supported by the union budget and that adequate resources must therefore be provided to ensure that investments that promote growth and jobs, the achievement of economic, social and territorial cohesion and the promotion of solidarity are effectively secured. these recommendations address a range of issues, including the migration and refugee crisis, low levels of investment, youth unemployment, internal security, environmental challenges, economic, social and territorial cohesion, the growing pressure of development and neighbourhood policies, gender mainstreaming and payment delays. i am in favour of it so that the revision is presented as soon as possible in order to allow for the parallel negotiations on the revision of the mff and the union budget for 2017 as well as a rapid agreement on these issues.
in writing. ‒ the union must update its long-term spending prospects to deal with unexpected crises such as migration, terrorism and rising youth unemployment. i am therefore in favour of the proposal to make the multiannual financial perspective for the period 2014-2020 more flexible in order to allow the union to respond quickly to situations not anticipated at the time of its adoption. we therefore call for a budgetary strategy to deal with sudden crises without having to set up ad hoc instruments, which create problems of accounting and democratic control.
