in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the second report of the taxe special committee because i consider it an important step forward in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, proposing measures such as increased protection for whistleblowers and journalists who reveal necessary information; sanctions against tax havens and non-cooperative jurisdictions in the fight against fraud that are included in the black list, as well as against banks, tax advisers and intermediaries that work or collaborate with them; a uniform legislation on patent-boxes to prevent their misuse; or the publicity of property registers, through the creation of a union property register, with information on the beneficiaries of assets. it is incompatible with the european social model and social justice that we social democrats defend, that those who have money and opportunities shift their incomes to tax havens and that the profits are not taxed where they are generated, wasting billions of euros needed to finance public services and combat growing inequality. the road map is clear in the fight against tax evasion. the member states must act. the time is now.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains substantial elements of our denunciation of tax evasion and avoidance by large multinationals in the union, it does not clarify the political responsibilities, leaving the results of this inquiry without any effectiveness. the work carried out by the taxe2 committee has been very positive, helping to advance knowledge of the tax practices of multinationals and the nature of the real tax havens that are not classified as such by the european authorities. these are very positive recommendations which help to make our traditional proposals in the tax field more common. but we are still a minority opinion in expressing the need to establish real public control of the financial sector, the restriction of international capital movements and the need to discuss the problem of tax havens in a democratic forum such as the un and not the oecd. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this important resolution, prepared by the committee of inquiry set up by parliament in the wake of the 'luxleaks' scandal, which revealed the prevalence of bilateral agreements between certain states (luxembourg, the netherlands) and multinationals to facilitate reduced tax burdens. these agreements were also made in secret and thus facilitated practices of transfer of the declared benefits to the countries concerned. the resolution contains many valuable elements of analysis and criticism of the current widespread practices of evasion, avoidance and money laundering, as well as various legislative and executive proposals to try to tackle them.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteurs for their work on this resolution on tax rulings and other measures of a similar nature or effect. there are important points in it, but i have disagreed with my group on some of the points. the commission needs to consider the creation of a common union list of crossborder tax evaders and avoiders to which everyone could have access. in addition, the commission is requested to prepare binding legislation prohibiting all union institutions from opening accounts or operating in jurisdictions listed in the common list of non-cooperative jurisdictions of the union.

in writing. ‒ i voted more convinced than ever that it is necessary to continue working tirelessly to eradicate tax evasion and tax avoidance, especially considering the revelations of the panama papers and luxleaks. we must move forward in tax integration and cooperation to restore tax justice, making our tax systems fairer and ensuring that corporate taxes are paid where value is created, not just at member state level but also at global level. we must not treat this important issue from a partisan point of view, but we must approach it with the understanding that the european commission estimates the scale of tax evasion and avoidance at one trillion euros a year, resources which we cannot invest in the improvement of european society. so it is a matter of great gravity that concerns us all.

in writing. ‒ in addition to depriving the states of tax revenues, this optimisation is unfair competition against our smes. the multinationals use ingenious arrangements (e.g. by paying royalty payments not subject to tax on the exploitation of patents) and can unduly improve their profitability and competitiveness. some multinationals therefore avoid paying taxes by exploiting the weaknesses in bilateral agreements or the generosity of the tax laws of our neighbours. in tax matters, however, cooperation between states alone is not enough and solutions must be found together. the report suggests that multinationals should publish certain information, such as the distribution of staff by country; it also wants to protect whistleblowers who report abusive tax practices. a country like france, which has a low tax attractiveness due to unstable legislation and very high compulsory levies, would benefit greatly from common tax rules against tax evasion, fraud and optimisation. although this report may raise some reservations, particularly on the creation of an observatory of national tax policies, under the responsibility of the commission, it is a step in the right direction. so i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ my support for the conclusions of the special commission on tax resolutions which makes recommendations for fairer and more transparent taxation. in this parliament we believe that there is a need for a public register of the ultimate owners of companies, a blacklist of tax havens, sanctions against non-cooperative jurisdictions, measures against the abuse of tax advantage schemes, a code of conduct for banks and tax advisors, rules on tax governance in all trade agreements signed by the union with third countries and tax withholdings for profits exported outside the union.
in writing. ‒ the luxleaks and panama papers scandals have highlighted the urgent need for europe to develop a fairer tax system and measures to ensure that large companies pay their taxes where they generate their profits. the fight against taxation must now be a priority for all more than ever, and that is why it is not enough to propose measures but we must be firm in our commitment to implement them. because this debate is not new and because what we are voting on today has been discussed on countless occasions. the report we have just approved calls for such important and basic things as a public register of the beneficial owners of companies, a blacklist of tax havens, sanctions against those tax jurisdictions which do not cooperate, a code of conduct for banks and tax advisers, and a consolidated common tax base, among other things. it should be borne in mind that the phenomenon of tax avoidance and evasion amounts to a billion euros a year at european level. only if we end these kinds of systematic practices can we have any hope of regaining our welfare state.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this important resolution, prepared by the committee of inquiry set up by parliament in the wake of the 'luxleaks' scandal, which revealed the prevalence of bilateral agreements between certain states (luxembourg, the netherlands) and multinationals to facilitate reduced tax burdens. these agreements were also made in secret and thus facilitated practices of transfer of the declared benefits to the countries concerned. the resolution contains many valuable elements of analysis and criticism of the current widespread practices of evasion, avoidance and money laundering, as well as various legislative and executive proposals to try to tackle them.
in writing. ‒ the biggest economic challenge for europe’s policy-makers is how to ensure that taxes are paid by all economic actors without difference. people, smes and big multinationals have to pay their due in order to ensure that taxes can remain the lowest possible achieving the maximum welfare effect. the eu and member states should dedicate all efforts to achieve this objective, and i hope that the recommendations outlined here are followed in the near future. our citizens and our welfare state need it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this important resolution, prepared by the committee of inquiry set up by parliament in the wake of the 'luxleaks' scandal, which revealed the prevalence of bilateral agreements between certain states (luxembourg, the netherlands) and multinationals to facilitate reduced tax burdens. these agreements were also made in secret and thus facilitated practices of transfer of the declared benefits to the countries concerned. the resolution contains many valuable elements of analysis and criticism of the current widespread practices of evasion, avoidance and money laundering, as well as various legislative and executive proposals to try to tackle them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the second report of the taxe special committee because i consider it an important step forward in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, proposing measures such as increased protection for whistleblowers and journalists who reveal necessary information; sanctions against tax havens and non-cooperative jurisdictions in the fight against fraud that are included in the black list, as well as against banks, tax advisers and intermediaries that work or collaborate with them; a uniform legislation on patent-boxes to prevent their misuse; or the publicity of property registers, through the creation of a union property register, with information on the beneficiaries of assets. it is incompatible with the european social model and social justice that we social democrats defend, that those who have money and opportunities shift their incomes to tax havens and that the profits are not taxed where they are generated, wasting billions of euros needed to finance public services and combat growing inequality. the road map is clear in the fight against tax evasion. the member states must act. the time is now.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains substantial elements of our denunciation of tax evasion and avoidance by large multinationals in the union, it does not clarify the political responsibilities, leaving the results of this inquiry without any effectiveness. the work carried out by the taxe2 committee has been very positive, helping to advance knowledge of the tax practices of multinationals and the nature of the real tax havens that are not classified as such by the european authorities. these are very positive recommendations which help to make our traditional proposals in the tax field more common. but we are still a minority opinion in expressing the need to establish real public control of the financial sector, the restriction of international capital movements and the need to discuss the problem of tax havens in a democratic forum such as the un and not the oecd. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
madam president, i was unable to vote in favour of this resolution, mainly because of what it says, but also because of what it does not say. this resolution is about innovation, research, synergies between european union funds, and all of that is very good. but this is not about people and their real problems: cohesion policies are subordinated to the strengthening of the single market, to public-private partnerships and to the logic of the europe 2020 strategy. the cohesion funds were set up to reduce economic, social and territorial inequalities and, more than ever, we are now at a time when these inequalities have been exacerbated by the economic crisis and austerity policies. there is no mention here of employment, social inequalities, economic imbalances between the countries of the union, evictions, the gender pay gap, the integration of immigrants, social inclusion, disadvantaged groups. i believe that the synergies between the funds and the promotion of innovation cannot be used as a means of diverting from the objectives of cohesion.

in writing. ‒ we voted against this resolution on the structural funds. we are following the voting line proposed by the gue/ngl. the joint motion resolution and its call for synergies, conceal possible rationalizations and cuts. it goes without saying that synergies are needed, not to reduce the burden of investment but to ensure that investment increases and its multiplier effects and its cohesion consequences. the gue/ngl resolution is committed to the latter criterion, and the positive vote can only go to this and the green amendment to the jmr of the grand coalition.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on synergies for innovation, the european structural and investment funds, horizon 2020 and other european innovation funds and union programmes. these synergies are integrated directly from the strategic programming phase and require strategic planning and options. it is also stressed that the development of smart specialisation strategies through the involvement of national and regional managing authorities and stakeholders such as universities and higher education institutions, industry, etc. in a process of discovering business opportunities is mandatory for those regions and member states wishing to invest erdf resources in research and innovation.
in writing. ‒ eur 121 billion will be invested in research and innovation, ict and support for smes from the european structural and investment funds (esif) over the period 2014-2020. it is true that the links between cohesion policy and other union policies, programmes and funding initiatives have been strengthened in the current financial period. however, there is room for improvement. this resolution, which i have supported, calls on the commission to monitor synergies between the funds and to publish a communication on such synergies, in particular between horizon 2020 and ris3. it also calls on the commission and the member states to pay constant attention to the needs of smes in the design and implementation of the efsi and horizon 2020 and to synergies between them. it also called on the commission to prepare coordinated calls for proposals to facilitate access to multi-fund financing and to carry out a detailed evaluation of the programmes for smes in terms of budget allocation and the success rate of projects. it also stresses that the european fund for strategic investments should complement and complement the efsi and other programmes such as horizon 2020 and the involvement of the eib, ensuring full coherence between all union instruments.

in writing. ‒ the european structural and investment funds, with €454 billion, and the horizon 2020 programme, with €80 billion, are two vital tools to help create jobs and competitiveness in the union. the effectiveness of programmes does not lie in the quantity but in the good management, eliminating duplications and enhancing links. in this sense, it is our duty to assure all europeans that not a single euro of the union's funds for its projects is wasted because of bureaucratic duplicity. i therefore think it is necessary for the european commission to provide more information on the synergies that have been created between the structural funds and horizon 2020, and i therefore think it is necessary to vote in favour of this document.
in writing. ‒ two years ago, president juncker presented the commission's decalogue of priorities for this period. since then, the european union has been rocked by crises - the financial crisis, the euro crisis, the refugee crisis and the security crisis - which have in some way interfered with the commission's work. what this motion for a resolution does is to define the major challenges we face and to call for european action to meet those challenges: the insufficient growth of our economy, which is a growth that is for a long time insufficient and lower than that of other competitors or other large economies; the maintenance of sustained, unsustainable youth unemployment; the growing inequality within the union; the deterioration of territorial cohesion; the loss of labour rights and social protection; the breakdown of respect for democratic rules in several countries of the union; solidarity with respect to territorial cohesion within the european union; and the alienation of citizens. we hope that these european responses, which the commission has promoted, will have the support of parliament and the council.
in writing. ‒ the commission's work programme shows the profound economic, political and social crisis of the project of european capitalist integration, and the profound contradictions which characterize it, which result from its class nature. a crisis that confirms the growing alienation of citizens from the union itself and its policies of exploitation of the working class for the benefit of big capital. this union work programme for 2017, rather than responding to people's needs and problems, deepens the policies that were at the heart of the social crisis that has dragged millions of people into poverty. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ the work programme sets out the commission's plans for the following year. actions are identified in different themes and work plans for 2017. i have voted against this report for a number of reasons, which point to the lack of coherence between the proposals and the aims they seek to achieve. there is much talk of defending a social europe, reducing unemployment and strengthening public services, as well as of increasing competitiveness and promoting free trade at global level with new agreements. the development of the europe 2020 strategy for sustainable growth, employment, reindustrialisation and the digital economy is advocated. there is also no clear roadmap to combat capital flight and dismantle tax havens, beyond advocating their disappearance. the document also points out the international threats facing europe, the loss of the union's global leadership, for which it proposes to give greater weight to the common foreign policy, migration, proposing in response tougher and shared border control with the european coast and border guard, and international terrorism, through more europol and the european centre for the fight against terrorism.

in writing. ‒ the union needs to update its long-term spending prospects to deal with crises and challenges such as migration, terrorism or the rise in youth unemployment. the report therefore stresses the need to make the multiannual perspectives more flexible in order to respond quickly to unforeseen situations such as the migration and refugee crisis, terrorism, the agricultural crisis and youth unemployment. in this connection, this resolution proposes the creation of a permanent emergency reserve within the community budget and the need to discuss extensively possible new sources of own resources. we are therefore talking about a necessary document in this area and i think it is necessary to vote in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ the commission's work programme shows the profound economic, political and social crisis of the project of european capitalist integration, and the profound contradictions which characterize it, which result from its class nature. a crisis that confirms the growing alienation of citizens from the union itself and its policies of exploitation of the working class for the benefit of big capital. this union work programme for 2017, rather than responding to people's needs and problems, deepens the policies that were at the heart of the social crisis that has dragged millions of people into poverty. that is why i voted against.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on japan's intention to continue whaling activities, as it considers that this constitutes an impediment to the conclusion of the eu-japan free trade agreement, on the understanding that trade policies should serve, among other purposes, to improve respect for human rights, animal welfare and environmental protection, including the protection of marine mammals. the commission has also pointed out, among many other points of interest, that the killing of pregnant female whales can threaten the populations of these animals, since large cetaceans reach sexual maturity very late, have a very low reproduction rate and have a long gestation period.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on japan's decision to resume whaling during the 2015-2016 season, which calls on japan to end its whaling activities and respect the conclusions of the international whaling commission. this resolution was focused on this fact, and i have therefore voted against all the amendments which referred to the current negotiations on the eu-japan trade agreement.
in writing. ‒ on 31 may 2010, australia sued japan before the international court of justice (icj) over a large-scale whaling programme under its antarctic whale research programme (jarpa ii), which violated its obligations under the international convention for the regulation of whaling (circb). on 31 march 2014, the icj ruled that japan, in granting special permits to kill, hunt and kill fin whales, humpback whales and antarctic minke whales in compliance with the jarpa ii programme, had failed to act in accordance with its obligations and therefore should revoke all existing authorisations, permits or licences it had granted and refrain from granting new permits. despite the ruling, in november 2015 the japanese fisheries agency informed the international whaling commission that it would resume whaling under a revised plan. this plan would allow the killing of 333 minke whales during the 2015-2016 season and a total of nearly 4,000 whales over twelve years. in view of these facts, i have voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution denouncing the situation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i support the maintenance of a general moratorium on whaling anywhere in the world and the prohibition of trade in whale products.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, considering that in 1982 the international whaling commission introduced a moratorium on all commercial whaling, which is still in force, in order to prevent the extinction of stocks and allow their recovery. however, despite this moratorium, several countries continue to hunt whales commercially under the special permit for purportedly scientific purposes, and japan has been hunting whales under special permits for decades, killing over 20 0001 whales as of 2014. the union's institutions must call on japan to end its whaling activities and to respect the iwc's conclusions.
in writing. ‒ in november 2015, the japanese fisheries agency informed the international whaling commission that it would resume whaling. japan plans to kill 333 minke whales during the 2015-2016 season and about 4,000 whales over 12 years. the country is thus ignoring the decision of the international court of justice of march 31, 2014 that it should stop whaling in the antarctic ocean. the icj concluded, in particular, that the hunt was not actually conducted for the purpose of scientific research. it should also be remembered, even if it is not mentioned in the resolution, that plastic pollution now appears to be more dangerous to whales than hunting, global warming or increasing salinity and acidity of the water. finally, an important amendment proposed that pressure be put on japan in the negotiations on free trade agreements between the european union and japan. unfortunately, the umps members rejected it, removing from the text the most effective solution to persuade the japanese to give up this hunt. for the umps, the survival of whales must not interfere with the sacred and holy opening of borders.

in writing. ‒ last february, the european council took the decision to reduce the sanctions imposed by the european union on belarus. as a consequence, the commission presented a delegated act to enable belarus to benefit from financing from the european investment bank. some political groups have decided to object to the delegated act in the committee on budgets. since the adoption of this objection would have delayed the partial lifting of sanctions against belarus, which i reject in principle, i have voted against the objection to the delegated act which seeks to give effect to this partial lifting.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of these resolutions, which object to the commission's decision to provide a guarantee for the european investment bank's investments in belarus. according to the treaties, respect for human rights is a condition for granting such investments. however, it is clear that there are systematic human rights violations in belarus, and it is enough to recall that this is the only european country where the death penalty is still applied. i therefore consider the objections to be relevant.
in writing. ‒ on 15 february 2016, the council decided that the union would not continue to apply the important restrictive measures, namely those against 170 persons and three companies in belarus, following the release of all political prisoners still in prison, as requested by the union. however, since the decision to lift sanctions was taken, the overall human rights situation in the country has improved only very slightly and, to date, the belarusian authorities have ignored all the main expectations of the said council meeting. the forthcoming general elections on 11 september offer an opportunity for belarus to put an end to its long-standing practice of fraudulent elections and are a decisive test of the authorities' genuine willingness to reconcile with their own citizens and to cooperate constructively with the union. although it is important to guarantee the eib's investments against possible losses in project financing operations in third countries, it does not seem very appropriate at the moment to grant such a guarantee for the case of belarus, and i have therefore abstained in this vote.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it shows parliament's rejection of the commission's proposal for a delegated act on accounting requirements for minimum own funds and eligible liabilities. the commission proposal does not designate the shareholders and creditors of a financial institution as being jointly and severally liable for any type of write-off prior to the establishment of a resolution fund. in this respect, this report of objection to this proposed delegated act argues that in order to be able to intervene in a systemic entity through a resolution fund, shareholders and creditors must first be liable for a minimum of 8% of the own funds. in this way, adequate legislation can be ensured which does not allow the bailout of the financial sector with public funds, as has been the practice in many member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which sets a minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities. there are several things that require harmonizing the rules on the minimum level of capital of banking institutions (8%) regardless of their size. the commission has also proposed to recover regulations setting a clear deadline of two years to recover that level of capitalisation, so that it does not remain in the air, among other points, so that systemic institutions are treated equally.
in writing. ‒ by means of the delegated regulation supplementing directive 2014/59/eu establishing a framework for the resolution of credit institutions and investment firms, the commission may, following the submission of draft standards by the european banking authority (eba) and in accordance with regulation (eu) no 1093/2010, adopt delegated acts specifying the assessment criteria for the methodology for setting the minimum requirements for own funds and eligible liabilities (mrel). the commission may also approve the draft rules only in part, or with amendments, where the interests of the union so require, taking into account the procedures laid down in article 10 of regulation (eu) no 1093/2010. i voted against this objection and therefore in favour of the application of the delegated regulation, strengthening the commission's powers with regard to the methodology for setting the minimum requirements for own funds and eligible liabilities.

mr president, mrs mogherini, i believe that this revamped common security and defence policy will prove to be the same failure as the previous one. in military terms, for example, it is said that we need a stronger europe, one that defends europeans. but then it says: more cooperation with nato. so, what's the deal? do we defend ourselves or does the united states defend us? and, furthermore, a nato which, as we saw in lisbon, is trying to be global and we are going to see now in warsaw that uses us as a subordinate army to contain certain neighbours. in terms of security, after seeing the misguided neighbourhood policy and the refugee crisis, which has a lot to do with disrespect for international law or the un charter, what are we opposed to? a super-frontex, mass deportations and more power for turkey. no, the answers are different, asymmetrical, with intelligence: support for legitimate governments to stabilize the area and combat the funding or training that many times our neighbors, or even members of the european union, have given to rebel groups that have later become terrorists.
mr president, as the european parliament's permanent rapporteur on humanitarian action, i would like to stress three points: firstly, the need to strengthen our role in conflict prevention and resolution; secondly, the need to bring coherence to our development policies, to ensure that the flow of migrants and refugees is not the only solution in many parts of the world; and thirdly, the need to apply international humanitarian law and respect for human rights. our example here is what gives us strength out there. and i want to point out, following the high representative, that the destructive fury of mars often creates as many problems as it solves, but the charm and enchantment of venus sometimes doesn't work very well in a world surrounded by conflict. so we have to get venus and mars to work together, and that's precisely what a strategy is.
mr president, i thank mrs mogherini for the document she has presented to us today, which is particularly important in view of the complex world in which we live. it is a global and interdependent world, in which nothing is foreign to us europeans, and that is why we need a common, cohesive, coherent and effective foreign policy. i am convinced that together we are much stronger than apart. in these days when many of us are asking ourselves what policies need to be made to make europe better, i would like to remind you that, according to recent polls, foreign policy is an area in which the majority of all european citizens agree that the union should play a more active role. this is striking, but it is so. and for this, what is needed first is political will - as has already been said - and also the proper use of the resources and instruments at our disposal and that strategic vision, and fortunately with your document it will be easier for us to outline that strategy. after brexit, i think it's not the time to be standing still, in any way. moreover, i believe that it may be easier to move forward on some of the elements that have been blocked up to now and to put in place the mechanisms already provided for in the treaties. i am thinking in particular of the defence sector, which has been the subject of so much discussion this afternoon, and even - why not? - of the so-called permanent structured cooperation. if we want to be a global, effective actor, well, soft power is important, but it does not come, as has been said here this afternoon repeatedly. it is a very complex world and the threats to security and defence are very strong. i believe that the role of the european union as a global actor does not correspond to its economic weight. we must abandon the idea of a europe that is withdrawn into itself, afraid, and we want a europe that is a protagonist, as pope francis himself reminded us here almost two years ago. we are in times of uncertainty and the european union must contribute with our partners, in the framework of the united nations, to generating stability and to safeguarding the interests of our citizens.
in writing. three words can define the high representative's proposal and the implementation of the overall strategy for the union's external action: credibility, action and focus. we socialists support this strategy, which is aimed at strengthening and developing the union's external action, making use of all our potential and of the treaties, with the aim of ensuring the coherence of our policies, linking the local, regional and global contexts. we support a strategy which aims to respond proactively, collectively and effectively to the challenges of today, to safeguard the values and the model of society of the union and to transform it into an effective and more strategic actor. we socialists advocate an approach based on joint action and the participation of civil society. the european union is also committed to the full respect and application of international humanitarian and human rights law. our unity, our example, is what gives us strength, what drives our action and our weight in external action.
vice-president of the commission/ high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – mr president, this is not the first time – and it will definitely not be the last – that we will have a debate in this chamber on our initiatives in the middle east peace process. i know very well that there is a widespread feeling that things will never change in israel and palestine and some say there are more urgent crises to deal with. others think the current leaderships are not up to the task. personally, i have always believed that we have a duty to keep working for positive change with patience and courage, and a precise interest in doing so. i know that parliament shares this view. you have shown it by hosting, just a couple of weeks ago, president rivlin and president abbas in the chamber in brussels. one reason why we have a duty to keep working for positive change, and an interest in doing so, is that the status quo cannot hold, and actually there is no status quo. if things do not change for the better, they can only get worse. another reason is the regional context. the other crisis in the region – the spread of terrorism – makes it even more urgent to restart some kind of political process. a new war in the holy land could have horrific consequences in the entire region and we do not want to see daesh take root in israel or in palestine. peace now – or at least a process for peace now – is more urgent than it has ever been. i know this parliament shares the same sense of urgency. the french initiative was spurred in part by your willingness to restart a credible peace process. for exactly the same reason we decided to revive the middle east quartet about a year ago and to work on the report that we presented on 1 july. it is a report on the main threats to the two—state solution, with clear recommendations on the steps needed to rebuild the conditions for meaningful direct negotiations. we all know that the situation on the ground in israel and palestine is deteriorating. the viability of a two-state solution is challenged on a daily basis. people are dying on both sides – almost on a daily basis – and with them hope is also dying. children are dying and children are being killed. unless we do something to reverse the negative trends, this conflict could get out of control and the very chance of peace would slip away. we simply cannot afford further escalation. we cannot afford further escalation, the israelis cannot afford further escalation, and the palestinians, and the entire region, cannot afford further escalation. this is why we issued the report. it was a lengthy process but, as you might have seen, the report is a long, dense text that brings the international community together on substance and in some detail. the report is about our common goal in the international community, which is to start a process and to stop and reverse the negative trends we have seen, to rebuild trust and to advance the two-state solution on the ground in order to create the conditions for peace. we are seeing those conditions slipping away at the moment. the report is a result of complex, collective work and is an integral part of a broader international effort. the report stresses the importance of the arab peace initiative and the opportunity for building a regional security framework. egypt, jordan and saudi arabia, as well as the league of arab states, are essential for peace and, for the first time ever, the arab countries can actually represent an opportunity for, rather than a threat to, israel’s security. we must not waste this historic opportunity. above of all, israel must not waste this opportunity. we are also working closely with france in the same direction and towards the same goal. let me thank president françois hollande and foreign minister jean-marc ayrault for their great commitment and for our close coordination in these weeks. our union and the quartet have welcomed the communiqué issued in paris and its support for a negotiated two-state solution. i was myself at a conference in paris at the beginning of june. all our initiatives can – and must – proceed hand in hand, coherently and in full coordination. together we can pave the way for a return to meaningful direct talks because this is the ultimate goal of the report. let me be very clear on what the report is. i will start with what the report is not. it is not a document on what the final status should look like or on parameters for final status negotiations and it is not a legal assessment of the situation under international law. let me state clearly that the european position on this is very clear and has not changed. what is the report? the report seeks to indicate a way forward, with concrete actions to be taken. it is an attempt, first of all, to save the two—state solution. we had a debate here, in this chamber – a couple of months ago, i believe – on the fact that the two—state solution is fading away. so, first and foremost, we have to make the option of a two—state solution still possible – something about which all of us have serious doubts if the trends continue this way. how? by setting out affirmative measures on the ground to reverse negative trends, to rebuild trust between the sides and to recreate a political horizon. i remember very well that this was exactly the goal we defined for ourselves, as the european union, the first time we debated the issue in this chamber at the start of the new term of this parliament. the report identifies three main trends that are putting at risk the two—state solution and that need to be reversed. the first is the trend towards violence and incitement. the report clearly identifies hamas as responsible for the most explicit and widespread forms of incitement, but it is also a fact that some fatah members have failed to condemn specific attacks. the report also refers to the actions of the israeli authorities: an expansive use of administrative detention, punitive home demolitions, closures of whole districts and the use of excessive force when there was no imminent threat. second, the settlements: for the first time ever, all quartet members have agreed to look at the settlement issue in a much broader and deeper context. we focus not just on the construction and expansion of settlements but also on the designation of land for exclusive israeli use, the high rate of demolitions and the denial of palestinian development in area c. this is the first time this has been done by the quartet as such. this set of negative trends on the ground in area c is steadily eroding the viability of the two—state solution and we clearly say this. the legitimate questions in the international community and in the region about israel’s long—term intentions are also raised. thirdly, there is the situation in gaza. the report not only addresses the dire humanitarian situation – and let me remind all of us that the european union has delivered on all the pledges we made at the conference in cairo two years ago on reconstruction in gaza – but we also focus on something that goes beyond the humanitarian situation. both the continuing military build—up by hamas and the lack of palestinian unity damage prospects for economic development and efforts towards a negotiated solution. so, analysing the situation on the ground was the first step, and you will find in the report things you have not seen said by the quartet as such ever before. but the analysis of the situation on the ground is only a first step because we have also issued clear common recommendations on actions to be taken on the ground. these are steps on which the whole international community agrees – the european union, the united states, russia and the united nations. first, decisive action is urgently needed to reverse the negative trends we have described. the parties must work to de—escalate tensions and maintain security cooperation. palestinians must strengthen efforts to combat terrorism and incitement to violence. the israeli policy of settlement construction and expansion has to come to an end. second, the two—state solution needs to be created on the ground. the palestinians must be able to take control of their lives and to build a future, including in area c. in gaza all militant activity must end. israel should accelerate the lifting of the restrictions of movement to and from gaza with due consideration for its security. the palestinians should unify, based on the plo platform and on democracy, for the benefit of their own people. the third element of the recommendations – you will find 10 recommendations in the report but i will not go through them all – is key. it is that the primary responsibility for peace obviously lies in the hands of the israeli and the palestinian leaders. peace cannot be imposed upon them and only direct negotiations can lead to a solid solution, but the region also has a central role to play. so we strongly encourage further dialogue in the context of the arab peace initiative and its vision for a comprehensive peace because it is very clear that are two overlapping conflicts there that need to be resolved, possibly together: the one between israel and palestine and the one that is still creating tensions between israel and the arab world. the report was presented a few days ago. we have seen the first reactions. we fully expected some criticism from the parties and, in fact, that is only natural because the report challenges the prevailing narratives on both sides. we are telling the israelis and we are telling the palestinians – and we are doing this together for the first time ever – that there are many things each side can do, and should do, independently to demonstrate genuine commitment to the two-state solution. and this is essential to lay the ground for successful direct negotiations. perhaps the most important thing right now is, as we discussed in relation to the global strategy, the follow-up: that both sides engage with the quartet and use this opportunity to advance and to stop trends that might destroy both peoples. all international initiatives can play a role, and it is vital to keep a united international front and a united region connected with the international front we have built. that is why the quartet envoys have worked throughout recent months in close cooperation and close connection especially with the initiators and the key players of the arab peace initiative, because we need to revive that and operationalise it, together with them, and with the united european union at its core.
the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force. the latest report by the quartet recognizes this: israel must stop its policy of building and expanding settlements. israel and palestine cannot, of course, negotiate on an equal footing, there can be no equating between occupier and occupied, and that is why i am calling on you specifically, as high representative, to get really involved in finding a solution to end almost half a century of occupation and colonization. the palestinian people need actors like the european union to end their complicity in israel's continuing violations of international law. freezing the eu-israel association agreement is essential to that and you know it, the same thing happened in south africa.

the committee on petitions has already adopted a number of amendments. mr president, i would first of all like to congratulate mrs helga stevens on her report. it is the first international human rights treaty to be signed and ratified by the union as a whole and is therefore part of the union's own legal order. in august last year, the united nations drew up final observations on the compliance of the member states and the union itself with all the parameters of this convention. this convention is not the end, it is the beginning of the consolidation of the principle of equality of all rights of persons with disabilities. many comments were made in these, mainly that the european union should harmonise all its legislation to bring it into line with the convention. there were also comments on accessibility, access to justice and, ultimately, a principle of equality and diversity that enriches us all. the european union must be a leader on these issues and that is why i again call for the unblocking of the directive on non-discrimination, which needs to be adopted and which has been blocked for many years in the council. the accessibility directive, too, as far as the labour market is concerned, with reasonable adjustments, and also education. and i end by calling for respect for difference and acceptance of people with disabilities as part of diversity and the human condition.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment. mr president, i am speaking because i have been the rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on women for the second time. of the 80 million women and men with disabilities, half are women - almost 46 million, or 16% of the population of the european union - and i would like to speak specifically to them in this second part-session. they suffer multiple discrimination - women and girls: they often face many obstacles to exercising their rights; they are certainly at much greater risk of violence, injury, exploitation and ill-treatment and are therefore often in a more vulnerable situation. their access to employment and education is also undoubtedly more difficult. if we compare the employment rates of women without disabilities and of women with disabilities, there is also a gap; also in their access to education, for which we call in these final remarks for an inclusive education, an education for all. the commission's final remarks are very clear in this case: they call for a gender perspective to be taken into account in all areas where the union is working and, in particular, in the disability strategy and the gender equality strategy. they also have the right to enjoy their sexuality like all human beings and like all people without disabilities and, therefore, we denounce and call for the prohibition of forced abortion and compulsory sterilization of these women; break a spear, therefore, to defend women and girls with disabilities more than ever.
mr president, approximately 15% of the world's population, that is 900 million people, have a disability. but 80 percent of those people live in developing countries. 50% of disabilities are preventable, because they are directly related to poverty. poverty is a barrier to accessing basic needs such as nutrition, health care and water and these factors, in turn, can lead to disability. the 2030 agenda for sustainable development is clear on how to address this issue. however, our foreign policy and, above all, our trade policy impoverishes the developing countries even more by undermining, among other things, public services and, therefore, by undermining fundamental human rights. we must help strengthen public services in developing countries, especially health and education, and not undermine them for the sake of our corporate profits. only then, with quality public services, early health care and less inequality, will we be addressing the real problems of people with disabilities in the world. and in the european union the main enemy of these people is austerity, it is the cuts and privatisations of public services, so let us be consistent, ladies and gentlemen.
mr president, commissioner, mrs stevens, i want to thank you for the pleasure of working with you on this report, for your passion and determination. the committee on petitions believes that this report on the implementation of the convention on the rights of persons with disabilities is a real milestone for the european parliament: it is the first human rights treaty of the 21st century and the first to be signed by the european union in the field of human rights. but let me say that i am particularly concerned about two articles of this convention, articles 24 and 30, which guarantee the right to inclusive education, without discrimination and based on equal opportunities. so why do i care? because the council, with a blocking minority, continues to have disabled and has not implemented either the anti-discrimination directive or the marrakesh treaty. i would like to ask you, from this place, to ratify the marrakesh treaty, which has been in force for three years, and to ensure that these seven countries, led by germany and italy, remove all their barriers, because they are closely linked to the publishing industry and only 10% of the millions of books published in europe are accessible to the visually impaired. so let's do something else to complete this implementation.
mr president, universal suffrage is not a reality in europe. in spain there are 80 000 disabled people who are denied the right to vote because they have a court judgment declaring them incapable of voting. article 29 of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities says that 'political rights and the ability to enjoy them on an equal basis shall be guaranteed to persons with disabilities'. the spanish government ratified this text in 2008. yet he does not. you are preventing the exercise of a fundamental right. the committee on the rights of persons with disabilities of the united nations has asked the spanish executive to amend the electoral law that allows this discrimination. but the spanish government has not done so. it is preventing thousands of people from participating in political life. we are facing an electoral apartheid; they are prevented from exercising their right to vote, to decide on the future of their country, because they have a disability. it is a flagrant violation of international law. does the european commission intend to do anything about it?

the joint resolution we are debating today should send a clear message to african countries, which are the ones where the rights of people with albinism are being violated. people with albinism suffer the worst forms of persecution and human rights violations: they are often verbally and physically assaulted, even mutilated or killed. these unacceptable attacks are not only happening in malawi, but also in tanzania, burundi, mozambique and kenya. people with albinism are socially discriminated against, excluded from access to public services, including healthcare. given the high rate of skin cancer among these people, their exclusion from the public health system is a death sentence. some of these countries have made efforts to remedy this tragic situation, but this is not enough: they must take preventive and training measures and put an end to the impunity of the aggressors. the european union must continue to monitor these acts which violate the most basic human rights and offer our cooperation to those affected in the fight against the aggressors.
author. madam president, in africa, people with albinism face some of the most extreme forms of persecution and human rights violations ranging from widespread social discrimination and harassment to murder, kidnapping, rape and mutilation. these threats stem from superstitions that albino people have magical powers, such as the belief that having sex with them can cure aids. this causes trafficking gangs to murder them for body parts that they believe bring health and wealth. for our part, the union's external action sometimes undermines or deteriorates the public services of the southern countries by encouraging privatization through totally unfair trade agreements. we must be consistent and aware that the most effective measure to tackle this reality is to strengthen the public services of these countries, especially education, to break these myths. universal, quality public education, training and health services is what they need.

in writing. ‒ the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities is the first human rights treaty of the 21st century and the first to be signed by the union as a whole. today we voted on parliament's response to the committee's conclusions on the rights of disabled people and the steps we think should be taken to implement it. and in this report both the content and the form are important, because the organizations of people with disabilities have been involved in the whole process. the participation rate of disabled people in the labour market is 58.5%, compared with 80.5% for non-disabled people. and these figures are even worse for women, at 44%. i would therefore like to highlight, among all the proposals in the report, the one calling for support for people's independent living, equal opportunities and equal access to the digital society. the council must put an end to the blockage of the anti-discrimination directive and the marrakesh treaty once and for all.
in writing. ‒ the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities is one of the most important human rights conventions and the first to be signed by the european union as a whole. the report calls for the implementation of accessibility legislation, the compliance of programmes and projects financed by the union with the convention and the establishment of a structured dialogue with organisations representing disabled people. we believe that these rights are fundamental to achieving a just society with equality for people with disabilities, which is why we voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ this report aims at the implementation of the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. i voted in favour because i think it reflects the ambition with which this issue must be tackled to put an end to the discrimination which millions of disabled europeans still suffer today. disability should be treated in the same way as discrimination on other grounds. at the same time, specific measures are needed for citizens who may suffer double discrimination, such as women and children. in this respect, i like the attention that this document devotes to disabled women who are in a situation of double discrimination, due to the specificities of diseases they suffer from such as fibromyalgia or endometriosis. the report also denounces the damage caused by cuts in social spending, which have negative consequences for the lives of the disabled, and prevent their inclusion and equal opportunities. the european institutions and the member states have a role to play in building a europe that is accessible to all citizens. the commission must urgently come up with concrete solutions, such as the signing of the marrakesh treaty.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it has a progressive and positive approach to people with disabilities, including a gender approach and rights of girls with disabilities and a recognition of the role that the economic crisis has played in devaluing the provision of quality services for people with disabilities. the aim of this own-initiative report is to respond to the list of recommendations of the un committee on the rights of persons with disabilities, ensuring that the views of the european parliament are taken into account in the european commission's report (to be presented in september). the report calls on the eu to ratify the optional protocol to the convention, welcomes the proposed european accessibility act and calls for its rapid adoption, calls on the commission to review the european disability strategy and develop a new eu strategy on the crpd and a review of legislation to ensure full compliance with and implementation of the crpd.

in writing. ‒ the report on the implementation of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities (uncrpd) aims in principle to reduce inequalities between disabled people and other citizens. however, this report is diverted from its objectives in favour of the inclusion of migrants or gender equality. the rapporteur also believes that the european commission is the only body capable of tackling these inequalities: once again, the sovereignty of the states is being undermined. in conclusion, while i support the integration of people with disabilities into society and the improvement of their well-being, i am opposed to their being used to favour migrants or to strengthen the powers of the commission. i have therefore decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it has a progressive and positive approach to people with disabilities, including a gender approach and rights of girls with disabilities and a recognition of the role that the economic crisis has played in devaluing the provision of quality services for people with disabilities. the aim of this own-initiative report is to respond to the list of recommendations of the un committee on the rights of persons with disabilities, ensuring that the views of the european parliament are taken into account in the european commission's report (to be presented in september). the report calls on the eu to ratify the optional protocol to the convention, welcomes the proposed european accessibility act and calls for its rapid adoption, calls on the commission to review the european disability strategy and develop a new eu strategy on the crpd and a review of legislation to ensure full compliance with and implementation of the crpd.

in writing. ‒ the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities is one of the most important human rights conventions and the first to be signed by the european union as a whole. the report calls for the implementation of accessibility legislation, the compliance of programmes and projects financed by the union with the convention and the establishment of a structured dialogue with organisations representing disabled people. we believe that these rights are fundamental to achieving a just society with equality for people with disabilities, which is why we voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ the convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and its optional protocol were adopted on 13 december 2006 at the united nations headquarters in new york, and opened for signature on 30 march 2007. 82 signatures of the convention and 44 of the optional protocol were obtained, as well as one ratification of the convention. never before has a united nations convention gathered such a large number of signatories on the day it opened for signature. it is also the first comprehensive human rights instrument of the 21st century and the first human rights convention to be opened for signature by regional integration organisations. the report gives a clear signal of this parliament's commitment to the full integration of disabled people and can mark a before and after in the recognition of their rights. our commitment is clear, and i therefore call on the member states and the commission to do their utmost to ensure that these rights are respected and to adopt a disability pact that ensures that the rights of people with disabilities are integrated into all union initiatives.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the implementation of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, with special regard to the concluding observations of the un crpd committee. the reports warns that there are an estimated 80 million persons with disabilities in the european union, making these citizens more vulnerable to poverty and all kind of abuses. this text calls upon member states and european institutions to improve accessibility and fully include persons with a disability in society and in employment to enable them to follow a fully independent life and, as a result, ensure the fulfilment of basic human rights within european borders. it stresses the need to introduce european directives and legislation and ensure the implementation of existing measures. as a result and bearing in mind the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and the universal declaration of human rights, amongst others, we fully support the document.

in writing. ‒ the convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and its optional protocol were adopted on 13 december 2006 and the union acceded to the convention in december 2010. the 28 member states of the union have signed the convention and 26 have ratified it. it is in this context that this report is being developed, which deals with those issues which present difficulties at national level and which are therefore best dealt with at european level. the report stresses that the institutions must be a model in the implementation of this convention and the need for no hierarchy of human rights, since discrimination on the grounds of disability must be addressed in the same way as discrimination on other grounds, an aspect especially important for women and children with disabilities, older people and people who have complex support needs, in particular those with an intellectual or psychosocial disability. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection because allowing the health effects of caffeinated drinks to be advertised would undermine the importance and visibility of the negative effects of these drinks on consumers, especially young people (who are the biggest consumers of these drinks). energy drinks, far from having nutritional benefits, are high in sugar and caffeine and are known to cause headaches, sleep problems and behavior problems in young people who consume them regularly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the administrative objection on health claims about caffeine, as it aims to make visible, among other things, that energy drinks generate undesirable consumption habits/patterns among young people. it specifically identifies adolescents as the main sector of energy drink consumption and the undesirable effects on excessive sugar intake according to the who recommended values. in addition to other substances and additives, a recommendation is made for the correct labelling and identification of certain products which may affect proper development at an early age.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which states that labels of sugary and energy drinks should not highlight the mention that they help to increase alertness or concentration, as they could encourage high sugar consumption among adolescents, who are the largest group of consumers of these drinks, and as the transfer to the consumer is fundamental. the aim is also to avoid health claims being made that are not suitable for children and adolescents. it includes both caffeinated drinks and energy drinks which also contain a large amount of sugar. and i don't think these kinds of drinks should carry any health claims.
in writing. ‒ the commission has presented a proposal for a regulation amending regulation (eu) no 432/2012 to add four health claims relating to the effect of high levels of caffeine in food. the four healthy claims are caffeine contributes to an increase in endurance, caffeine contributes to an increase in capacity, caffeine helps to increase alertness and caffeine helps to improve concentration. energy drinks are virtually the only foods that have a sufficiently high level of caffeine to be able to use these health claims. however, children and adolescents are the largest consumers of energy drinks, and they also have a high sugar level per can. regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 required the establishment of nutritional profiles to which foods or certain categories of foods must conform in order to have nutritional or health properties. this would ensure that products containing a high level of caffeine and a high level of sugar cannot use health claims. however, this requirement is not being met. i therefore supported the objection that the commission should withdraw its proposal.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection to the amendment of the regulation establishing a list of authorised health claims for food other than those relating to the reduction of disease risk and to children's development and health for two main reasons. firstly, the european food safety authority has produced a scientific report concluding that energy drinks are not a health hazard in themselves, as long as they are consumed in moderation. secondly, because i do not think that the solution is to mark or label beverage cans any more if we do not educate children and young people properly about the properties of these drinks.
