on behalf of the green group, mr president, we are talking about barriers to food exporters in the european single market, which should be our market. and we valencians know what those barriers are, and the andalusians and the aragonese and the catalans, because we see our trucks stopped when they cross the french border and the fruits and vegetables they contain scattered on the ground. i have reported these attacks to the commission. i have been told that you will act decisively, but we do not see the effects. the cases are repeated: intolerable aggressions within our european union. we cannot build a real single market in this way. the single market must be looked after, protected and made stronger every day. it's not a plant that's left to its own devices. we must work at every moment, we must demand that the states keep a constant watch on it and react firmly to these barbarities and to these obstacles which my colleagues are denouncing, which prevent it from becoming a reality. but there is much more, because the single market does not protect our producers. they are suffering abuse in the supply chain, they are getting miserable prices for their products and we have no european law prohibiting such practices. a single market requires uniform rules, harmonization of social and working conditions, in order to avoid competitions which lead to such clashes. will the commission move in that direction? a single market cannot function with 28 different rules, which, ladies and gentlemen, and we have talked a lot about this in this sitting, will soon be 27 after brexit and there may be many fewer if we do not react. because this situation also explains brexit, it also explains anti-europeanism. because our producers do not feel protected by the european union, our farmers wonder what benefits it brings them, why they encounter these absurd barriers when they just want to do their job well. and unfortunately, ladies and gentlemen, i often do not know how to answer them. i am a profound europeanist, and i do not know how to answer that. i hope the commission will give me that.
mr president, commissioner, i want to acknowledge the opportunity of this debate, it is good that we are talking about what is happening in the internal market. ladies and gentlemen, the internal market is one of the greatest achievements of the european union. we must be aware of the value of this asset, which benefits us so much and is often attacked by national decisions. i agree with what my colleague mr sebastià has said: spanish farmers and cattle farmers are regularly and systematically attacked by french farmers. the strawberries of huelva, the vegetables of almeria, the wine of la mancha and the pigs of castile and leon are being attacked without any response from the french government or the commission. the absence of european legislation against unfair trading practices also means that each member state is developing its own standard, creating differences between countries for the same commercial transactions. the absence of european legislation on unfair trading practices leads to harmonisation and therefore to market abuse. (the president cut the speaker off)
mr president, commissioner, we shall then have to talk about national legislation, which is also emerging like poisonous mushrooms to try to fragment and hinder the free movement of people and goods. in the present debate, i recognize that it is you, precisely in the college of commissioners, who are acting with the greatest interest and determination precisely to avoid these barriers. but i believe that the mandate given to you by mr juncker, namely to consolidate and improve the internal market as an element of cohesion in the european union, should help you and all those commissioners who are willing to avoid all these barriers. in a way that is insidious and unacceptable, through legislation, through action or inaction, an attempt is being made to fragment that common market, which i believe must be strengthened precisely at such a difficult time for the european union. (the speaker agrees to answer a question put under the 'blue card' procedure (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure))
the answer is 'blue card'. i think you have not heard the commissioner correctly, mr coburn. the commissioner has just explained that the rules are going to be changed. ergo, i think it has nothing to do with brexit - i am absolutely against brexit - i think it will rather generate you - it is already generating you - problems. we're all going to die. and of course any fragmentation of the single market and the common market will only lead to a disintegration and confrontation and weakening of both the united kingdom and the european union. so i disagree with that.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, the agricultural crises are giving rise to a resurgence of nationalism in trade matters and i believe there is a growing tendency to compartmentalize markets, which in my view is an attack on one of the greatest achievements of the european union since its birth, which is market unity. i think that this should be avoided by the european parliament and the other community institutions. some member states are considering systems of labelling of the national origin of agri-food products which could be clearly discriminatory against imports from other community countries. moreover, other national measures, such as the 'traffic light' system envisaged by the united kingdom, under which products of recognised nutritional value, such as olive oil, would be considered harmful, could also constitute a barrier to trade in agri-food products. i would also like to call on the european commission not to stand by idly in the face of the attacks on spanish lorries on the french border. these are repeated actions which also call into question the proper functioning of the single market.
mr president, in recent months, at the height of the economic and social crisis, we have seen the emergence of a new silent frontier war based on false social legislation which creates new obstacles to the free movement of people, services and goods. and let it be noted that the minimum wage is always welcome and that we were glad when it was finally introduced in germany, because the immediate effect of its introduction is to raise the general wage level - it was time to mobilize the scandalous german surplus and to put an end to the minijobs that are doing so much damage in the rest of the states. the surprise is that this was not the case and that it has been used to build barriers in the field of road transport. and germany has now joined france, two central states which have distinguished themselves in the past by trying to benefit their hauliers against the rest of europe: the german toll or the threat of jail for overnight in the truck for other hauliers in france. the commission has already taken measures to penalise peripheral hauliers: restrictions on the movement of heavy goods vehicles (weekend bans), the eurovignette, and so on. we do not like sanctions, madam commissioner, and we would prefer to see a clear european legal framework to prevent this unstoppable fragmentation of the market, which benefits...
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, do you know what it means to sleep in a cabin at 50 degrees? working to pay for the truck, no breaks and no going home, in a debt slavery typical of feudalism? to put your health, your life and that of your family, and even that of other people, at risk because the european union does not want to implement legislation against social dumping? if they knew, if they cared, they wouldn't act with impunity against workers' rights. denying minimum wages to international hauliers is the latest of his shameful decisions, violating the principle that all workers, without exception, are entitled to a minimum and decent wage. the european legislation on social rights is being emptied into a hollow shell because of the arbitrariness of the commission. i therefore support the transport operators, the associations and the trade unions in their denunciation of this brutal situation. i hope that the commission will reconsider, listen to mobilisations and campaigns such as fair transport europe and that this parliament will legislate so that workers' social rights are protected and monitored.
mr president, commissioner, the problem of social dumping affecting the road transport sector in the union is not going to be solved by state-to-state measures, as you have already said. it needs an immediate european solution. we therefore welcome the fact that infringement proceedings have been opened against the german and french rules on the minimum wage for hauliers, which, unilaterally, because of the bureaucratic costs and complications they entail, are going to make the situation of the companies worse. we believe that the infringement procedure is incompatible with the decision taken by the french authorities to start monitoring compliance with their rule, even though at this first stage they will not apply sanctions. we therefore call for speedy preparation of specific european legislation on the mobility of transport workers and the suspension of checks in france until it is clear whether this is in line with union law.
mr president, first of all, i do not understand whether the debate is on the application of article 50 or on mr verhofstadt. secondly, i do not understand why a debate is being called on the application of an article which no one has asked to be applied. debating things that haven't happened yet leads to melancholy. thirdly, it is absurd that the british government has asked for two years to decide whether or not to apply article 50 and we have to decide in two days. it's an unfitting disproportion to the serious situation we're dealing with. fourthly, i think it is frivolous that such an important matter should be resolved behind our backs, without warning and in haste, in two days of parliamentary debate. it is not up to the very serious problem facing the european union. there is already a parliamentary procedure, and when the day comes that parliamentary procedure will be activated and this parliament will debate. and let me tell you that you should organise yourselves a little better, because at the same time that you want this parliament to debate article 50 - which nobody has asked to be applied - in another room there is going to be a discussion about the new british commissioner who wants to be part of the governing bodies of the european union. do one thing or the other, but both at the same time is contradictory. we will vote no, to avoid misunderstandings.
mr president, we are laying the foundations for what should be an energy union based on an interconnected market and capable of ensuring the supply of electricity at affordable prices, with the optimum use of resources and energy efficiency as its pillars, and integrating renewable energies and cogeneration by the citizens themselves. this objective requires increasing interconnections in the internal market, the deployment of smart grids that end energy islands, such as the iberian peninsula. mr commissioner, heating and cooling account for about half of the european union's energy demand, hence the importance of improving energy efficiency in this area, to reduce dependence, to reduce emissions and costs for consumers and, in particular, for those at risk of energy poverty. in short, we must put the citizen at the centre of the shaping of the new energy market.
mr president, commissioner, the creation of a single energy market that guarantees security of supply, advances clean generation and provides stable legal frameworks to encourage investment is one of the greatest challenges facing our union. achieving this objective is useful for citizens, first of all as consumers, but also as entrepreneurs, and it is useful for companies and their competitiveness. it is also essential if we are to be able to speak of free competition in the internal market. at the moment, differences in energy prices between member states are one of the main factors of distortion. for these reasons, i insist that this objective is a priority and i recall that the foundations of our common cause, the credibility of our union - the european union - begin with our ability to solve the general, everyday problems affecting all europeans. when we talk about electricity market fragmentation, we are talking about these kinds of problems.
in writing. if there is one sector that requires strategic planning, it is the energy sector. the development of sovereign conventional resources, the need to ensure affordable supply to industry and households, public control over energy commons, the energy transition to an environmentally sustainable model... all these are objectives which the market is incapable of developing, something which the union implicitly recognises by simultaneously pushing for privatisation and liberalisation of the energy sector - a regulation which, however, only reinforces the privileges of energy oligopolies vis-à-vis consumers. the langen report is just another piece of rhetoric in the same direction.
in writing. a new energy market model is needed in a world in transition and the european union must lead the shift towards clean energy. it is time to phase out fossil fuels and give more weight to renewable energy, key to energy independence, diversification and security. all this is done through a safe market for new investors. in this connection, some states such as spain have undermined the legal certainty of any investment in renewable energy by means of a battery of retroactive regulations that have made any investment in renewables insecure, while increasing coal burning by 24% and their co2 emissions, which seriously compromise compliance with climate agreements. in four years, spain has lost 35 000 skilled jobs and the photovoltaic energy sector, in which it was a world leader. at the same time, national coal is subsidized with the commission's approval and self-consumption is restricted by the sun tax. these and other issues, such as subsidies disguised as payments for capacity for fossil and nuclear power generation, are the big issues that the new energy market must address.
the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner crețu, you know that some of the priorities of the european commission in its current mandate are those relating to economic growth on the one hand and the creation of quality jobs on the other. the commission launched a tool based on the so-called smart specialisation strategies. but what is this about strategies for intelligent specialization? the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval, and the council will be consulted on it. the so-called ris3 are therefore designed on the basis of the operational programmes, which also forces the regions to draw up their strategies ex ante, because otherwise it would be completely impossible for them, the regions, to access the funds. we will also say that these strategies are very much participatory in nature. they involve citizens, businesses, universities and, of course, public administrations. we in parliament and in the committee on regional development are preparing a report which is intended, among other things, to encourage the commission to go further with these strategies. we shall say of this report that it is the first to deal with this matter in this legislature and here in this parliament. we should also say that the report was drawn up on the proposal of various associations, many of which are specialised in this sector, and with the broadest possible agreement of the members of the committee on regional development, as i have already said, because i should like to say that when it was presented, the vote was 33 votes in favour, 3 against and, in addition, the report itself was enriched by a series of amendments, which were substantial in number but, above all, substantial in content, bringing the total to 20. i would like to stress the contents of this report, on the one hand, the need for the european union to intensify all possible efforts to achieve such economic growth, which is smart, sustainable and also inclusive. i would also like to stress the importance of research, technological development and innovation being one of the investment priorities if the regional development fund is to turn them into the real basis from which competitiveness can be strengthened and quality employment created. it is also necessary to analyse the capacities, assets and skills of each region, so that new business opportunities can be opened up. i would also like to stress that greater cooperation between regional authorities and between transnational cooperation programmes is needed to avoid duplication of the rapporteur. mr president, almost a year ago volkswagen admitted to the us environmental protection agency that it had used cheating mechanisms to pass emissions tests and thus obtain the type approval of these products in the us. the first question i think we should ask ourselves is why this scandal was not discovered in the european union; why in the european union we were not able to discover a fraud of such a magnitude. obviously, the answer is not easy, but there are many factors, which i'd like to discuss here today, that explain it. firstly, obviously, a lack of europe. the lack of europe is due above all to insufficient integration. i have no doubt that if we had been a true united states of europe, this scandal would not have been possible. but i am sure, without a doubt, that if we had been the united states of europe, our consumers, the millions of europeans who use cars every day, would have been more protected. but i have no doubt that if we had a single judicial system, consumers in the european union would certainly be better protected. there is another factor that also explains why we have come to this situation. there is no doubt that a vague legislation pushed forward in the days of commissioner verheugen also explains why we have not been able to discover this scandal and - more importantly - why this scandal has been able to take place. i also think we have to criticise ourselves, because commissioner verheugen negotiated legislation in this house with some of our colleagues which, as time has shown, has been insufficient. commissioner tajani came in and tried to put the rattle on the cat to try to push through legislation that was ambitious in reducing nox emissions. we were all aware of the discrepancies. this same house approved a report which shows that we were aware of discrepancies between tests in real driving conditions and laboratory tests. the question is, did we then do enough? i think it's time to look to the future. what the european citizens expect from this committee of inquiry, no doubt, is that we will know the truth and, more importantly, that we will make proposals to promote measures to prevent such fraud from ever happening again. and i have no doubt that all my colleagues will agree that we are going to try to get to this point. crises are opportunities and this is undoubtedly the crisis that the automobile sector needed to adapt to a reality of the 20th century that was much more demanding in terms of emissions, much more demanding in terms of finding new forms of mobility. and we have to be aware that the income of 12 million families is at stake. we must be sufficiently rigorous, not only to guarantee the income of these families, but above all to give them a better future. it is no use admitting that we should have known about this fraud; what we have to do now is to discover the truth and, above all, and most importantly, look to the future. it was a pleasure to work with my dutch colleague, with whom i hope to continue to work in the coming months, and with the other colleagues, the alternative rapporteurs.

in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of this report which supports cohesion policies and research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation (ris3). the ris3 contribute to the strategic programming of the cohesion funds and can play a key role in meeting the europe 2020 objectives, in pursuing balanced and sustainable development and in creating quality jobs. it also proposes support for multi-level governance and greater participation at all levels in aid programmes, as well as the creation of positive synergies in the different regions to identify their strengths. although the report contains many 'battles to the wind', i am in favour of technological and social innovation, of the evaluation of the aid system, of strengthening the strengths of each region and of smes, in order to achieve more sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report because i believe that synergies between homogeneous areas of knowledge, production fabric and specialisation have proven to be more effective in stimulating and supporting innovation. the development areas associated with crossborder cooperation, for example, demonstrate this reality and the results obtained by regions such as the basque country that have opted for this model, prove that this way of organizing support for innovation is more effective.
in writing. ‒ the ris3 strategies aim to promote smart, sustainable and inclusive growth based on knowledge, capable of generating quality jobs in all regions, not just in developed areas. these strategies contribute to the thematic focus and strategic programming of the european structural and investment funds (esi funds) and lead to a greater focus on results on the ground. two years after the start of its implementation, this report focuses on the main areas of improvement for ris3. in particular, it underlines the need to promote a coordinated and complementary use of the esi funds with horizon 2020 and the european fund for strategic investments to boost innovation at regional, national and union level, by increasing the attractiveness of research and innovation investments in order to attract private capital as a complement to public funding, and calls on local and regional authorities to make the most of the possibilities of combining these instruments. it also stresses the need to improve coordination between all levels of governance and to give civil society a more active role. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ enhancing the capacity and possibilities of regions to collaborate across borders is the backbone of europe and its building blocks, because it stimulates development, encourages coexistence in diversity and generates potential and possibilities that cannot be curbed by old borders. we also want to simplify the procedures and bureaucracy that affect this mechanism of cooperation and we want to give these policies a leading role in cohesion policy beyond 2020.
in writing. ‒ european territorial cooperation (etc) should be a key element of cohesion policy. it should be remembered that approximately 38% of the european population lives in border regions, and this policy is therefore crucial in promoting further economic, social and territorial development of these regions. however, the etc budget represents only 2.8% of the cohesion policy budget, so as the report indicates, it is not up to the big challenges facing the etc and does not reflect its high european added value. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the structural funds. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it contains some positive aspects which are relevant to improving the conditions of the reference population. it recommends that special attention be paid to projects which aim to adapt municipalities and regions to the new demographic situation, such as: adapting social and mobility infrastructure to demographic change and migration flows, supporting job search for older people, women and migrants, contributing to better social inclusion. it reinforces the idea of simplifying programmes and involving civil society, taking into account transparency and accountability. it calls for local and regional authorities to play a greater role in the proposal, management and evaluation of european territorial cooperation programmes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the need to continue to focus on improving and extending territorial cooperation within the eu. european territorial cooperation now benefits all 28 member states and has become one of the objectives of cohesion policy. it has a budget of eur 10.1 billion: 74.1% for crossborder cooperation (60 programmes), 20.4% for transnational cooperation (15 programmes) and 5.6% for interregional cooperation (4 programmes). european territorial cooperation contributes to strengthening the economic, social and territorial potential of regions, transcending national borders and removing obstacles to improving security, transport, education, energy, health, training and employment. we must therefore continue to make a strong commitment to improving and extending eu territorial cooperation.

in writing. ‒ without prejudice to the jurisdiction of the courts, a commission of inquiry into alleged infringements and maladministration in emissions measurement in the automotive sector was set up on 17 december 2015. the scope of the investigation is limited by article 226 tfeu and the ep's right of inquiry decision, according to which it should focus on investigating the compliance of the commission and states with the obligations of regulation (ec) no 715/2007. in addition to collecting and analysing information on the application of directive 2007/46/ec, determine whether they had evidence of the use of deactivation devices and make any recommendations it deems necessary. while the final report will take place in march 2017, this vote refers to the interim report which, by its nature, cannot advance conclusions before all witnesses have been heard and sufficient evidence has been gathered. it is therefore purely technical in nature, with an emphasis on procedural aspects. the principles of transparency and good cooperation between institutions are recalled and all stakeholders are requested to provide the necessary assistance for the fulfilment of the mandate of the emis commission. i therefore vote in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the progress of the inquiry by the parliamentary committee on measurement of emissions in the automotive sector is needed to assess the more political aspects of the volkswagen scandal. in addition, we are looking at updating existing legislation in the union to ensure that measurements are closer to real driving circumstances. the parliamentary committee investigating car emissions measurements has determined that the german carmaker and its subsidiaries must overhaul 8.5 million cars in europe, 2.4 million of them in germany alone. the report denounces the lack of cooperation by the member states in explaining how this fraud on consumers could have occurred. the european commissioner for the internal market, elzbieta bienkowska, has announced her intention to open cases against those member states which have failed to comply with their control obligations by not taking the appropriate sanctioning measures.

in writing. ‒ i abstained in the vote to withdraw the parliamentary immunity of the hungarian mep, istván ujhelyi, from the group of the progressive alliance of socialists and democrats. this request arises as a result of an allegation of defamation against another public official in hungary. although these events took place before he became a member of the european parliament following the 2014 european parliament elections, i.e. outside the parliamentary activity for which he enjoys immunity, i consider that the elements of judgment do not allow me to take a firm position in this case. at the same time, being a hungarian mp opposed to the government of viktor orbán, characterized in recent years by its increasing authoritarianism, is another reason to be cautious in relation to this request for the withdrawal of parliamentary immunity which, moreover, was promoted by the parliamentary spokesman of the ultra-right party jobbik, tamás sneider, who has been involved in several violent episodes and with racist connotations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the request for the waiver of immunity as proposed by the juri committee. i understand there's no possibility of using the suspension to initiate a political prosecution.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the legal assessments which consider that the statements which have given rise to the accusation of mr uhjelyi, were made when he was not a member of the european parliament, have nothing to do with his status as such, nor with the functions which fall within the competence of members of the european parliament and have a chance to be clarified in the field of hungarian justice.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of istván ujhelyi in view of the report drawn up by the committee on legal affairs, which finds that the central district court of pest has requested the waiver in connection with an ongoing criminal proceeding for a defamation offence relating to the statements made by the said parliamentarian on 25 april 2014 about a person from hungary, when he was not a member of the european parliament, and that therefore the charges against him do not relate to an opinion expressed or a vote cast by him in the exercise of his functions as a member of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of lifting the parliamentary immunity of istván ujhelyi because he has been accused of making defamatory and racist statements on hungarian television, when he was not yet an mep. given the nature of the offence he is charged with, i have decided to vote in favour of the waiver of his parliamentary immunity so that the courts in his country can pursue the judicial process.
in writing. ‒ it is established that members of the european parliament may not be sought, arrested or prosecuted for opinions or votes expressed by them in the exercise of their functions; it must be borne in mind that the statements by which this case was opened were made when mr ujhelyi was not yet a member of the european parliament and, therefore, when he made those statements, he was not acting in the exercise of his functions as a member of the european parliament. the committee on legal affairs therefore recommends that the european parliament suspend the parliamentary immunity of istván ujhelyi.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of protecting the parliamentary immunity of former italian mep rosario crocetta, who was accused in italy of defamation and slander. the committee on legal affairs recommends that the european parliament should protect its privileges and immunities, as the statements made were made in the context of its parliamentary activity as an mep. i believe that the freedom of expression of public officials must be protected, since they must be able to express their views and comments freely on a wide range of issues. mr crocetta, the current president of sicily, has also always been a public figure, renowned for his fight against organised crime and the influence of corruption in the economic and environmental spheres. during his time as an mep, crocetta insisted on the power of the mafia in europe, and therefore proposed the creation of a union antimafia commission. his commitment to freeing italy and especially his region, sicily, from the mafia has earned him numerous enemies and threats.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the defence of the immunity of the parliamentarian rosario crocetta, since he was accused of making statements in a political debate about the mafia. in this case, we understand that his statements are directly linked to his political activity as an mep, and i therefore vote in favour of defending his immunity.
in writing. - i agree with the legal arguments that advise mr crocetta to be protected. the statements which gave rise to the legal proceedings concern issues and activities related to his activity and concern a matter of general interest at european level, namely the influence of the mafia on public procurement. mr crocetta was also a member of the european parliament when this complaint was lodged.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of protecting the immunity of former member of the european parliament rosario crocetta in the light of the report drawn up by the committee on legal affairs, which finds that the criminal proceedings pending against him in the third criminal chamber of the court of palermo concern alleged defamatory statements made when he was a member of the european parliament; that mr crocetta's statements are directly and manifestly related to his parliamentary activity and that, in accordance with article 8 of protocol no 7, members of the european parliament may not be sought, detained or prosecuted for opinions or votes they have expressed in the course of their duties, an immunity intended to protect the freedom of expression and the independence of members of the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on statistics on external trade with third countries. i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work in seeking agreement and reaching this final text.
in writing. ‒ following the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty and the subsequent adoption of regulation (eu) no 182/2011, it became necessary to adapt the rules for decision-making in the field of trade policy to the new regime of delegated and implementing acts. most legislation in the field of the common commercial policy has been harmonised through the trade omnibus i and ii general trade regulations and several subsequent individual harmonisations. regulation (ec) no 471/2009 on community statistics had, however, been left to be adapted. after negotiations and agreement with the commission and the council, the european parliament's inta committee overwhelmingly approved the agreed text, which was put to the vote in the plenary today and which i supported.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report at second reading. an agreement under the 'better regulation' framework already exists, which provides, inter alia, for a horizontal solution concerning the consultation of member states' experts in the preparation of delegated acts. the adoption of the new interinstitutional agreement on better law-making in december 2015 enabled the parliament and council negotiating teams to reach an agreement on the regulation in question.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is simply a matter of adapting to our new legal framework. the rules for decision-making in trade policy matters needed to be adapted to the new regime of delegated and implementing acts.
in writing. ‒ the resolution aims to make compulsory the collection of data on natural gas and electricity prices applied to household users, which the commission has been collecting since 1970, in order to avoid problems in this task as pointed out by several member states. i believe that this measure is necessary to prevent a significant deterioration in quality and to continue to maintain a broad market coverage and a high level of quality of price data. this information is essential to ensure a high level of transparency and information following the process of harmonisation and liberalisation that has taken place in the union's internal energy market. this liberalization should also have an impact on competitive prices and quality service, avoiding the oligopolistic practices which, in the case of spain, have led to a 70% increase in the cost of the bill over the last ten years. spain is now the fourth country in europe with the highest electricity bill. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ while the general idea of the report may seem good at first sight: to oblige member states to report gas and electricity price statistics to eurostat, in the end it is a way of promoting the single energy market at european level. this market is moving towards greater liberalisation of the energy sector, which means a greater role for the market and less power for the states to regulate the sector on the basis of environmental or social considerations. that is why i am voting against.
in writing. ‒ the collection of data on natural gas and electricity prices applied to household users has been carried out on a voluntary basis with a response rate of 100%. the aim is to make this voluntary nature mandatory, as it is for industrial prices, which should not impose an additional burden on the notifying authorities; data will continue to be collected by the competent national authorities. the report aims, among other things, to clarify the objectives, to provide certain provisions for notifying authorities and companies that have to provide data and to avoid incomparable data sets. in accordance with the s&d group's guidelines, i did not vote for the report, as it was written by a rapporteur from the europe of nations and freedom group, including the far-right french national front. the content of the report is not controversial and an interinstitutional agreement was reached at first reading.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it represents a step forward in the implementation of the energy union. although we consider that harmonization of the structure of prices is important in order to improve the transparency of electricity markets and the final price paid by the consumer, this proposal is made with the sole intention of deepening the integration of energy markets. our commitment is against the energy union, because we consider energy to be a public good and not just a commodity. that is why, and because of our opposition to the energy union, i voted against this report, even though i consider it necessary to harmonize statistics in the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, considering that the european commission has been collecting data on natural gas and electricity prices since the 1970s. the methodology was modified in 2007 to take account of the liberalisation of energy markets. meanwhile, the collection of data on natural gas and electricity prices applied to household users has been carried out on a voluntary basis with a response rate of 100%. the aim of the new regulation is to make this voluntary status compulsory, in order to avoid problems in data collection. there is no doubt that this measure is necessary to prevent the quality of the survey on electricity and natural gas price data for the household sector from deteriorating considerably.
in writing. ‒ while the general idea of the report may seem good at first sight: to oblige member states to report gas and electricity price statistics to eurostat, in the end it is a way of promoting the single energy market at european level. this market is moving towards greater liberalisation of the energy sector, which means a greater role for the market and less power for the states to regulate the sector on the basis of environmental or social considerations. that is why i am voting against.

in writing. ‒ i support this report. i am in favour of full transparency and publication of the gas and electricity prices in all member states so that consumers can better be aware and choose/change their providers. since the 1970s the european commission has been collecting data on natural gas and electricity prices. in 1990 the council adopted the directive to define the procedure to improve the transparency of gas and electricity prices charged to industrial end-users, yet not to household consumers. the responsibility to collect and publish the data lies with eurostat. the objective of this regulation is to transform the voluntary basis into an obligatory one, so as to avoid problems in the data collection as having been reported by several member states. in order to not let the quality of the survey of the electricity and natural gas price data for the household sector deteriorate significantly, and in order to continue to achieve a wide market coverage and high quality of price data, this step is necessary.
in writing. while the general idea of the report may seem good at first sight - to oblige member states to report gas and electricity price statistics to eurostat - in the end it is a way of promoting the single energy market at european level. this market is moving towards greater liberalisation of the energy sector, which means a greater role for the market and less power for the states to regulate the sector on the basis of environmental or social considerations. that is why i am voting against.
in writing. ‒ i voted against as greens are in favour or collecting and disseminating high quality and reliable data on the prices and cost of electricity and gas, for both households and industrial customers to bring transparency to the market and enable better energy policy making. however, the proposed framework, by simply distinguishing household and non-household consumers, remains insufficient to enable to provide a good understanding of the market for the different types of customer (ex. smes, energy-intensive industry, households). in addition if fails to provide a transparent picture of the cost of each energy source, by not accounting for direct and indirect subsidies that are not included in the final customer prices, for ex. for nuclear power and fossil fuels.
in writing. ‒ the regulation aims to establish a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of comparable european statistics on natural gas and electricity for households and other european consumers. we are talking about a document which has been widely agreed upon in the committee on industry, research and energy, and i think it is necessary to vote in favour of it.
mr president, last week several spanish citizens came to the european parliament who were affected by the 'sun tax' and the retroactive measures. they explained to us how the design of the energy market harms the self-consumers of renewable energy. this report could have provided a solution for these people, who are living through a real social drama. this report could also have created a legal and legislative framework to help implement renewable energy, with priority for access to the grid, as opposed to energy from burning fossil fuels such as coal or gas, the main cause of global warming. instead, it assumes that all technologies are neutral, both nuclear and solar. another step in blindly guiding ourselves by the needs of the market, that is to say, the needs of the large companies in the energy sector, which, by the way, will continue to receive covert subsidies for fossil fuels and their large infrastructures, as we already know castor, doñana, the south stream corridor, through the capacity mechanisms that this report endorses.
in writing. ‒ on 15 july 2015, the commission presented its communication on the new energy market configuration, ahead of the legislation expected by the end of 2016. for a new energy market design, it is necessary to consider the changing nature of our supplies. we must be more flexible, incorporate renewables and locally generated energy. among the many challenges we face are dependence on oil and gas, lack of diversification and progress in efficiency, high prices, growing global demand, security risks or the fight against climate change. the report lays the foundations for an energy union based on an interconnected european-wide market, ensuring affordable electricity supply, with optimal use of resources and energy efficiency as its pillars, integrating renewables and cogeneration. this requires increasing interconnections within the country and eliminating energy islands such as the iberian peninsula. better market integration offers multiple opportunities to achieve a secure, efficient and environmentally sustainable supply. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it presents a disappointing vision of the design of energy markets and networks in the union, which does not provide solutions to the problems at hand. our group has included amendments in support of renewables and criticising mechanisms such as capacity mechanisms which allow large multinationals in the electricity sector to benefit. this report does not address the need to support small renewable producers, nor the importance of allowing state intervention in the electricity sector. the report calls for the disappearance of regulated prices, which have proven to be one of the best tools to tackle the problem of energy poverty. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, bearing in mind that the eu faces major challenges in the field of energy: dependence on oil and gas imports, lack of diversification, high energy prices, growing global demand for energy, security risks in producing and transit countries, the fight against climate change, lack of progress in energy efficiency, the increase in the share of renewable energy, the integration and interconnection of energy markets and market distortions caused by different aid schemes. i am convinced that better integration and coordination of energy markets in europe is essential to achieve the common european objectives of a secure, cost-efficient and environmentally sustainable energy supply.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report because it is based on market mechanisms and not on social and environmental needs. it leaves aside or deals with the issues of access to the grid for self-consumers, decentralisation of the system or energy efficiency. the report is also based on technology neutrality, which means that energy from renewable sources and nuclear sources are treated in the same way, when we know full well that the environmental impacts are considerably different. capacity mechanisms are covert subsidies to large companies and possibly to fossil fuels. in addition, there is a risk that these mechanisms will lead to the construction of new large infrastructures that will condemn us to continue with the current model for several more decades.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it sets the future rules for the energy market and, in particular, for its marketing and distribution. a new energy market design needs to take into account the changing nature of our supplies, so energy markets need to adapt, evolving from traditional models of centralised generation towards systems more based on variable renewables and with greater flexibility, often also generated at a more local level. it advocates an evolution towards a truly flexible, decentralised, integrated and open electricity market, where improved interconnections can potentially ensure that services and supplies flow freely across national borders, based on local and regional needs and advantages. in short, it is a question of promoting a design of the future energy market, at the service of consumers and industry, which guarantees supply at affordable prices.

mr president, smes generate 71% of employment in the european union, and that is why we believe it is essential to make progress in supporting these enterprises. i voted in favour of this report because we think it is good that it identifies austerity as one of the causes of the weakening of smes and also because it insists on the need to facilitate access for smes to the european union's structural and investment funds. but i would like to emphasize our disgust at the european commission's threat to freeze these funds for the spanish and portuguese states, because, in addition to considering the use of funds to blackmail the people intolerable, we consider that both the adjustments to avoid the freezing of funds and the freezing of funds themselves will create even more difficulties for smes and will therefore further increase the high levels of unemployment, poverty, marginalization and social exclusion that have been caused by the austerity policies, especially in the peoples of southern europe. we also believe that the capital markets union is not the solution for smes - indeed, it could create new difficulties - and that there is no alternative to free trade agreements, which put smes on a path to reducing production costs, while reducing wages and prices at source, destroying jobs and causing many smes to close. this report also addresses the strengthening of smes in the agriculture, fisheries and aquaculture sectors through thematic objective 3. we believe that in order to maintain these smes, which are essential to guaranteeing our food sovereignty and food security, policies to regulate production and markets and a fair distribution of production and fishing rights are also essential.

in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is the main instrument for investment and job creation in the union. throughout this crisis it has become the only investment policy in certain regions. there are 23 million smes in the eu - 99% of all businesses - which make a key contribution to economic growth, social cohesion, innovation and the creation of quality jobs. through the structural funds for the sme competitiveness enhancement programme, the 2014-2020 period is expected to increase job creation and invest in people's skills development, while developing and implementing new business models, developing new products and services and supporting internationalisation. the report, which i have supported, therefore calls on the commission and the member states to take account of the added value of smes' projects for the development and innovation of traditional sectors in order to promote their adaptation to the processes of digitalisation by improving their skills in ict, and calls on the member states and regional entities to study and apply to the full the possibilities offered by the financial instruments.

mr president, we cannot forget the problems facing the alpine region and the people who live there, because they are common to those in other rural areas. these areas are depopulated, schools are disappearing, health centres have to be moved to older towns where there are no jobs. the inhabitants cannot survive on tourism alone. it is clear that this sector must be valued and promoted, but people will not always be attracted to it if the region is not permanently looked after and cared for by those who live there all year round. the strategy proposed by the european union must be geared to the development of agriculture, forestry and other environmentally friendly services and industries. the protection of this region must go beyond economic criteria, and this debate is a good opportunity for us to talk about this, about the need to go beyond that; because the importance of protecting the culture, the life of areas like this - a sustainable and balanced life - is basic. it is a life of respect, respect for its environment, a life and a wisdom that only people living in villages continue to give us.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this report because i am in favour of the macro-regional strategies. until now, these have arisen from intergovernmental initiatives, but thanks to the inclusion of the territorial cohesion objective in the lisbon treaty, the strategies can be more fully integrated into the community approach.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because we believe that it is essential to have a clear strategy. although i do not agree with some of the points that are being raised, i believe that there is an urgent need to put in place a plan to solve this and other problems affecting many rural areas without resources. in these areas, the exploitation of the natural environment or tourist attractions is often given priority over the standard of living of the inhabitants themselves. in addition, the dossier includes amendments that have been incorporated in light of civil society concerns about issues such as carbon emissions, renewable energy, climate change and protection of glaciers, endangered species and biodiversity. the report also supports sustainable tourism and makes interesting contributions to cop21. i am particularly interested in your comments on the more remote areas of the alpine area, which lack access to the most basic social and economic services, lack of job opportunities, lack of connections, depopulation, etc.
in writing. ‒ the eu strategy for the alpine region is developed in a context characterised by the existence of various types of cooperation in the region, in addition to various crossborder interreg programmes. this region, home to over 80 million people, spans 48 regions and 7 countries and has a strong human, natural, economic and cultural appeal. however, the difficulties of connecting and logistics of production have marked the development of mountain territories. in addition, the area is also very vulnerable to the effects of climate change. in this context, the report emphasises that public authorities must address the existing economic and environmental challenges. the report identifies as priorities: improving the competitiveness, prosperity and cohesion of the alpine region; ensuring accessibility and connections for all inhabitants of the region; ensuring sustainability in the alps; or protecting the alpine heritage and promoting a sustainable use of natural and cultural resources. for these reasons, i have voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the eu strategy for the alpine region is the union's fourth macro-regional strategy and can therefore draw on the experience gained with the eu strategy for the baltic sea region, the eu strategy for the danube region and the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region. a legal framework should be established to better define, on the basis of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, the governance system for existing and future strategies, limiting the role of national and union authorities to the initial impetus and coordination, as well as to the monitoring and support functions, leaving the aspects relating to the governance of projects and their implementation to regional and local bodies which should be the real protagonists of the basis of territorial and development policies. for all these reasons i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which analyses the objectives and funding of the trust fund for africa, which was designed to help 23 countries in three african regions (the horn of africa, the sahel and lake chad basin and north africa). this fund is a development instrument which brings together the resources of the different donors to enable the union to provide a rapid, flexible, complementary, transparent and collective response to the different dimensions of an emergency situation. in the area of migration, the fund seeks to address the root causes of irregular migration and displacement in countries of origin, transit and destination through five priority sectors: (1) development benefits of migration; (2) legal migration and mobility; (3) protection and asylum; (4) prevention and combating irregular migration; and (5) return, readmission and reintegration; however, the contributions from the member states are still very limited, and so we in this house are asking for new appropriations and for parliament to be included in the strategic board of the fund. we also ask the member states to respect the commitment to 0.7% of oda.

in writing. ‒ the eu trust fund for africa, implemented by the president of the european commission, 25 member states, plus norway and switzerland, was launched at the valletta summit on 11 and 12 november 2015. the european union's contribution will be €1.8 billion, but funds from member states and other donors will be added for an equivalent amount. the fund's main objective is to stabilise african countries and thereby to control migration. this is to ensure that resilience, economic opportunities, security and development are promoted. in reality, the fund will pool resources from different donors, often already existing, to provide a coordinated, faster and more flexible response. but will the european union control the use of the funds? the report calls for regular and detailed reports from the european commission, but if these reports are based mainly on information from local authorities, ngos, and private partners, this will leave the problem of aid misappropriation unresolved. i therefore abstained because this report is still a waste of public funds, without any obligation to achieve results.

in writing. ‒ the union emergency trust fund for stability and addressing the root causes of irregular migration and displaced persons in africa was established in november 2015 with the aim of contributing to the promotion of stability, with a view to improving migration management, addressing the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and irregular migration, and promoting equal opportunities, economic opportunities, security and development. this report addresses many of the issues raised in relation to the establishment of this fund in terms of funding, implementation and scrutiny, calling for transparency, accountability and policy coherence in defining and implementing projects, while respecting, above all, the principles of development effectiveness. the document also provides a critical assessment of the budgetary aspects affecting the member states. in this context, it should be recalled that spain was the first to support the creation of the fund and one of the first to announce its contribution. i therefore consider it appropriate to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ due to high levels of irregular migration, the eu trust fund for africa was created to support the most affected african countries, to help promote stability in those regions and to promote closer cooperation between africa and the eu on migration management, security and development. the report makes reference to financing, implementation and control. it calls for transparency, accountability and ownership and policy coherence in the definition and implementation of projects, with full respect for development principles and their effectiveness. the report provides a critical assessment of budgetary aspects and shortcomings in terms of funding by member states. it also calls on all parties concerned to meet their commitments and responsibilities on time. finally, spain has already made its contribution and is actively participating in this fund, so i am voting in favour of this report.

on 15 july, turkey suffered a military coup in which more than 250 people were killed and nearly 1 500 injured. the government from the beginning pointed to the gülen movement as the authors of the coup. after the failed coup, the government declared a state of emergency and began a purge with some 80,000 arrests of journalists, judges, police and army officers, businessmen, teachers and the withdrawal of media licenses. 49 337 workers have been suspended. the attack on democracy requires exceptional measures to safeguard democratic institutions. however, the exceptional nature of the measures and the state of emergency must be proportionate and the rule of law must be guaranteed. the council of europe's cooperation with the turkish government in the investigation into the attempted coup in the country and in the trials that will follow is therefore essential to ensure that they are based on the european convention on human rights. last week, a high-level dialogue took place between vice-president mogherini and commissioner hahn, which covered, among other issues, the kurdish question, cyprus and the eu-turkey agreement.

high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy/vice-president of the commission. – madam president, many of you called – well, some of you called – in this room for us to tell the truth, so let’s try to do this exercise once again together. first, as some of you mentioned, migration or human mobility is part of the history of mankind. to tell the truth mankind itself is the result of human mobility, and maybe we should keep that a bit in mind. coming from some countries this might be easier to remember, for others maybe a little bit difficult, but all of us, all of us, are the result of human mobility: truth number one. second truth, others are doing more than the european union is doing, you were saying this perfectly well. this is not a european phenomenon, and even less a european crisis. if you look at the movements of people inside africa, inside asia, they are much bigger than the movements of people towards europe from these two continents, not only combined but also taken alone. and wherever you go in africa or in asia, every single country, or almost every single country, is itself at the same time a country of origin, a country of destination and a country of transit. so we have to get a little bit out, in our public debate, of this eurocentric approach that we are at the centre of the flows of the whole world, and realise that indeed there are many other countries in the world, most of the time countries that are living in conditions that are much more difficult than ours from an economic point of view, from a climate point of view, from a conflict point of view, that are doing much more than we are doing. and indeed that we can lead by example, if we are able to provide some good examples – and let me tell you in some fields we are not. i mentioned things which i am not particularly proud of, but we are in some other fields capable of leading by example. and let me tell you, on a personal note, i had the occasion of briefing the un security council twice, this year and last year, on the eu policies on migration and i have noticed a radical change in the attitude of our global partners to our response, or our policies on both refugee and migration, which means that probably – let me put it this way a bit bluntly – last year we woke up. we woke up in what was for many a surprise, not for me personally, not for many in this room, but for many of us was a sudden wake-up. and this year we managed to elaborate or to react to this shock and put in place policies – finally. i often told you, i told you at the beginning of our debate today, to me it was a shock when i came in, moving from my time being an italian minister to the position of high representative, that migration was not on the table of the foreign affairs council. it was a purely internal matter, as if we had to tackle this issue only from an internal point of view, but where are these people coming from? so we come from there. two years ago, this was not an issue, if not an issue of interior ministers only, so in two years i think we have come a long way. third truth: there are things where we can lead by example. there are solutions we can find only if we do it together, as europeans and globally. and what we can try to do is to manage this complex phenomenon in all these different aspects. i will come to the different aspects in a moment, but let me stress one point that i think mr panzeri mentioned. i refer to this as the need to manage a complex phenomenon. i will never, never personally call this a problem or a burden, because it is people. it is people with names, stories, even when we do not see the photos, it is people. so the language we use is important, the respect we pay to persons is important, especially to children, and the point on non-accompanied children is one that we will for sure bring up in new york. we have to keep that in mind also when the photos are not on the front line, on the front page of the newspapers, and let me tell you with sadness and shock, i never understand the fact that those that claim our christian identity the most are also those who are the first to forget the word and the message of pope francis on migration and refugees. this is a mystery to me. so we can do things to manage this phenomenon together, as europeans and globally. it is different aspects of things we need to do. on the refugees, it is the urgency of supporting globally, first on resettlement programmes, something good, something we need to do more, something we need to encourage our partners to do more, and also financial support, which is what we are doing the most. we need, on migration, to work on the implementation of the sdgs, on agenda 2030, on investments in countries of origin and transit. i am glad to hear also from the right side of the chamber tonight that indeed there is support also from that side to increase our budget for development policies. this is news to me, welcome news, and i think that will need to be tested with coherent and consistent voting, but this is good news if we realise that investing long-term in the economic and social development of countries from where people are coming, is indeed a major step forward in our own policies. then, we also need to work very much on dismantling the smugglers and the people traffickers. this is what we are trying to do at sea. this is also what we are trying to do with our partners in some countries, in full respect of human rights, and in coordination with the iom and with unhcr. this goes together with opening regular channels for migration. the more we open regular channels for migration, the more we manage to discourage the irregular channels, thus preventing the loss of lives at sea the role of civil society and ngos is crucial, as is the role of local authorities also here in europe, in so many cases they are doing much more the national governments, let me tell you. so we need
