in writing. i welcome the un high level summit on large movements of refugees and migrants and the political agreement reached by 193 states. i am particularly grateful that there is a commitment that focuses on both sides: refugees on the one hand and safe, orderly and regular migration on the other. it was absolutely essential that all countries come together to give a global response to a problem that is. i welcome the creation of a more responsible, predictable and supportive system with shared responsibility. in all this, unhcr plays and will play a key role, as initiator and developer of the response, but in coordination with all other actors, such as the receiving states, local and national entities, international organisations, etc. unhcr cannot deal with the problem alone. so i applaud the willingness of these 193 countries to take a global approach to this crisis, but i hope it doesn't stop there, at will. we must study the causes of these mass movements of people in depth, so that we can anticipate them and see them as a development challenge and not just a humanitarian one.
on behalf of the green group, madam president, i welcome this report and thank you very much for the excellent work done by its rapporteur, mr castaldo. the current tunisian president, béji caïd essebsi, told a delegation from this parliament - including the rapporteur - that there was no arab spring, that it was an invention of western journalists. there was a tunisian spring. and it is true, because tunisia is the only country in the region where there has been a popular revolution against a dictator and where fragile democratic structures have been created, which may or may not stabilize. and europe has a lot to say about that. it must be much more involved, not just financially but politically. it must look much further south and help to remove those black spots that are weighing down the tunisian process. some of my colleagues have already commented on this: the restrictions on freedom of expression, the legislation against lgbtqi groups, the exceptional laws. and to do that, our trade agreements with tunisia must prioritize mutual benefit and take into account that we have a very great ally there: civil society. they must also help the country in such basic economic matters as the development of renewable energy and the fight against desertification. and, furthermore, tunisia needs to recover, that we help it recover the money that dictator ben ali stole and that is still hidden in europe. tunisia's future is also ours. a unique opportunity for the mediterranean to become a sea of encounter once again and not that graveyard it is becoming.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, it is often said that tunisia represents a political model of successful transition to democracy after the arab spring in the maghreb. it is, and we admire it. the main challenge for the new president will be to put an end to the country's serious economic and social crisis, which poses a concrete threat to tunisia, but also to the security of the entire euro-mediterranean area. i acknowledge, mr castaldo, the merit of your report in pointing out that a worrying number of young tunisians are being taken by the islamic state or daesh. numerous factors contribute to young people being lured by the false promises of extremists, and one of them could be that one third of tunisia's total working age population is unemployed today. in this context, the protests of young people in tunisia are an alarm that europe needs to hear. we need to put in place concrete measures so that the union can support the country, with policies aimed at young people to integrate them into the labour market and help them plan their careers, and invest in new businesses, and promote the participation of women in the country's labour force.
madam president, i would first of all like to congratulate mr castaldo on his very balanced report. tunisia, despite its great difficulties, is a positive case in the framework of the so-called 'arab spring'. there has been limited violence during the transitional process and, finally, a remarkable degree of consensus among the various political actors, which led to the adoption of the constitution in 2014. the process has now been strengthened following the formation of a new government of national unity, despite regional instability, in particular that generated by the civil war in libya and repeated terrorist attacks. these are hindering the transition in tunisia, and to this must be added the economic difficulties and the high unemployment among young people, which is also the result of the weakness of tourism, as has been said. the union must maintain close political cooperation by helping tunisia to consolidate its democratic transition, as called for in the report we are voting on tomorrow. it must also deepen our mobility partnership, advance the trade and services negotiations now under way, promote economic reforms and maintain our support for security sector reform. tunisia is an important partner, and we must support it in its efforts to consolidate its political position, to develop its economy and society, to ensure its security and to combat terrorism. a partner, and a neighbour too, which is also a political model in the current regional context of the mediterranean and the arab world, which in general is encountering so many difficulties in reaching stable and inclusive democratic political formulas.
madam president, i would like to congratulate and join in the congratulations to mr castaldo, because it is very moving to read a text which is so deeply rooted in the country, in tunisia and its people, and which is also demanding of its government, its parties and its institutions, as if it were, in short, a report from one of our countries. thank you very much. i would also like to congratulate and thank the high representative for her courage and wisdom, for breaking so many austerity reservations and giving her work a new lease of life, to go step by step, with enormous tenacity and intelligence, building a sort of marshall plan - i would rather say a mogherini plan - for tunisia: macrofinancial support of more than 500 million euros; for the commitment to a free trade area that makes a difference and drives the tunisian economy and autonomous development; for the visa facilitation, so urgently needed and clearly needed to make a difference. it would only be necessary to add the euro-mediterranean bank, which this parliament has supported in many of its reports; also the eu global strategy on security, which recognises the peoples, but also the opportunity that is to share such a challenge, and to congratulate that horizon 2020 finally has tunisian resonance as well.
madam president, tunisia was the origin of the arab spring, but also of the humanitarian dimension of what we have wrongly called the refugee crisis. we therefore welcome a report which crystallizes the positive case of a country which has managed to demonstrate that not everything has been an arab hell, but, in fact, a transition to democracy and the constitution, but which reminds the european union of the need to be globally relevant, to have an external policy of positive stimulus and not just of negative gaze and remorse afterwards towards the southern shore of the mediterranean and to also correct the humanitarian policy in the management of this terrible dimension of refugees coming from the southern shore. and the occasion - and i emphasize this - is the visa code for the introduction of humanitarian visas at the origin, at the embassies and consulates of the european union, because they can make a difference and show that not only in the bilateral case of tunisia, but in learning the lessons that come from that experience, the european union has improved as well.
madam president, as the truck drivers who came to the european parliament a few months ago to complain about their situation said, you only have to go to a truck stop anywhere in europe to see what an underworld the road transport sector has become. unfair competition in this sector is spreading to many others, such as agriculture, catering or domestic and care services, creating huge pockets of precariousness throughout the european union. social dumping is a particularly serious problem for cities like avilés and regions like asturias, where i come from, with a heavy weight of steel and heavy industry, which are constantly blackmailed by relocations to countries with lower labour and environmental costs. those who advocate deregulation are leading us into an unstable situation, one that is absolutely unsustainable. that is why we support measures to eradicate shell companies, to combat fraud and tax evasion and to defend decent working conditions.
president-in-office of the council. – mr president, first of all i would like to thank all those who spoke during this discussion. i think the discussion showed that we may have some different views but in general we are united by the fact that we want to have a workable budget, a good budget for european citizens. one of the issues or challenges we have is that we have too many priorities and too little money, and the question is how to use the money in the best possible way. i remember long and painful discussions at the national level in my country, in my government, where we had to go through very painful decisions on where to cut, where to take away and how to adjust the budget. unfortunately there are also similar situations at the european level. i can assure the members, and mr geier, that the cuts which were made by the council were not ritual, were not easy, were not technical, and followed many discussions among the member states and a lot of deliberation. i would also like to put those numbers which came out of the council into some perspective by comparing both the proposal from the commission and numbers from 2016. this comparison shows that in the proposal from the council we are actually talking about increasing commitments by 0.9% in comparison to 2016. there is a drop in payments of 7%, which we believe is justified because of the low absorption of the eu funds in some of the categories. so again the change is not major and it reflects the views of the member states, including the situation in their own countries. if i may, just very briefly, address some of the important points which were made during the discussion. the council fully agrees that the priority of competitiveness, of jobs, of economic growth, is a key issue for europe. europe can survive in the global economy only as a competitive economy. the cuts made to sub-heading 1a were focused on areas in which some investments may be postponed because 2017 may be too soon for them. we also made sure that the council has not proposed any reductions to the programmes that are best placed to achieve the political goal of economic growth, such as efsi, core parts of the horizon 2020, cosme, erasmus+ etc. so we tried to preserve those core elements of the budget which we believe are the main drivers of economic growth. in response to the points made by mr tarand on the european court of justice, this is an issue where we also looked very carefully at the budget. we took into account the increase in the budget of the european court of justice in 2016 and which helped with the process of reform. that increase was eur 21 million. we believe that the further increase requested by the european court of justice for next year is not fully justified. the council is ready to support the reforms but not at the level requested. i think the points made by mr arthuis are very important. they go into the very substance of the budget, its composition, and looking into the future, how we adjust the structure of budget, both in terms of revenues but also expenditure, to the needs of modern europe. this is something that we certainly have to discuss as part of the mff mid-term review, that we have to discuss as part of the post 2020 discussions and of the european commission. i think kristalina is going to present some of the ideas tomorrow, and we look forward to that. it is the common job of all the institutions to gradually adjust the budget in a way which would look into the future for 2017, and we want to keep the main focus of these discussions on the 2017 budget. we believe that we are proposing a budget which is balanced and which also reflects the situations in the member states. lastly, i would like to express my huge appreciation for the discussion today, even at this late hour. as we have seen, views may differ but the goal is a common one, which is to adopt the best budget for europe and its citizens. we will now eagerly await the position of the european parliament on the budget for 2017, and we also look forward to the process of seeking to reconcile those differences together. as in past years, we will count on the commission, and in particular on vice-president georgieva, acting as a honest broker in this in this process, and i would also like to wish mr arthuis, the chair of the committee on budgets, as well as mr geier and mr tarand as rapporteurs the best of luck for their work over the coming months within parliament. i am also looking forward to our cooperation. i wish to assure you that the slovak presidency will do its best to make sure the 2017 budget is achieved and is a good budget.
member of the commission. – mr president, let me start by quoting the trade for all communication that the commission adopted last year, which sets out its beliefs on the direction of future trade policy. it says that: ‘as free trade agreements enters into force, the eu will have to make sure that the provisions on trade and sustainable development are implemented and used effectively’. that is exactly what we will be talking about today in relation to the agreement with the southern african development community (sadc). sustainable development issues are of high importance but they also need to be implemented and monitored and that is why i am very grateful for the opportunity of having this debate and answering the questions here tonight. you will vote tomorrow. as the rapporteur said, and i would like to thank the rapporteur and all the shadow rapporteurs for the work on the economic partnership agreement (epa), with six countries in southern africa. i had the pleasure of signing the agreement when i was in botswana this june. this agreement will start a new relationship between us in the european union and these six countries: botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, south africa and swaziland. why will it do this? well because, while negotiating this deal, we took full account of the economic and societal differences between the countries involved and that has led us to eliminate much more of our custom duties than we are asking our southern african partners to do. so the eu is opening up our market much faster and, furthermore, providing free market access to the african countries involved. the markets of the six african countries are going to be only partially and very gradually opened to european products, and their right to vote on protective measures, to protect nascent fragile industries and for future food-security reasons, will remain. our trade relations will be based on a predictable business environment, getting rid of customs duties for african exporters, big and small, and by then we will have commonly agreed rules in areas such as customer procedures, future sanitary measures, rules of religion, and technical barriers to trade. this will also contribute to diversifying the economies of many countries in southern africa that are seeking to broaden production and include a wider range of products and services, and it will foster regional integration of markets in southern africa. this is a powerful tool for prosperity, stability and growth, and all the countries raised this issue with me when i spoke to them in botswana. let me also underline what the rapporteur said, because i have heard that there are some concerns circulating here about this economic partnership agreement and oranges. the agreement has been available online with all its annexes, all 1 300 pages, on our website for more than a year. nothing has happened since: everybody has been able to read it and we have not heard any of these problems raised before. imports of oranges or citrus fruit during the eu season from december to may will not be liberalised. we are talking only about out-of-season imports and that has been the case since the year 2000: imports of oranges from 1 june to 15 october. the sadc epa adds only six weeks to this period, and that includes the month of november, during which south africa exports less than 1% of its total production. the duties will remain high, there are specific safeguards and we will monitor the process, so i am happy to tell you that some of the concerns i have been hearing are not really grounded. we will continue to monitor this very closely. turning now to the questions that the rapporteur raised on behalf of parliament and the committee on international trade, let me assure you, first of all, that we are obliged to monitor the operation of all the agreements. like other economic partnership agreements, this sadc agreement requires monitoring to assure that all the objectives of the epa, including those of sustainable development, are realised, and that the benefits are maximised for all, especially the most vulnerable. epas are, furthermore, anchored in the provisions of the cotonou agreement and that includes sustainable development objectives, provisions on labour and environment and, very importantly, democratic principles and human rights. the monitoring we will put in place will contribute to assessing whether our partners respect the essential elements of the cotonou agreement and, in the event of breaches of it, appropriate measures can be proposed. the monitoring will also be fed into a review that each epa undergoes every five years. so more specifically: i propose to you that the monitoring will be based on three principles: transparency, objectivity, and openness. transparency in the sense that the results of the monitoring will become accessible to all – to you, of course, but also to a wider audience. objectivity in the sense that the monitoring will be neutral, systematic, and involve independent expertise. open in the sense that the monitoring will involve outside stakeholders. i believe it is very important that outside stakeholders are involved in the monitoring. so i am committed, as is the whole commission, to structural civil-society dialogue, ideally once per year. we will have no problem finding parties, including relevant organisations, to take part in this. we have already started to identify possible civil-society organisations, and we are already planning the first dialogues this month and in october in south africa. with regard to parliamentary oversight, i fully support an interparliamentary dialogue between the european parliament and the parliaments of the six states and i really want to encourage you to establish this already. how will we finance this? well, you have my commitment that we will seek to ensure adequate funding is put aside. one route is a project that the commission’s directorate-general for trade, in collaboration with our service for foreign policy instruments, is drawing up to finance the involvement of civil society in trade agreements. the commission also has other funding possibilities – for instance, under thematic programmes that support specifically the participation of civil society in partner countries and the eu. how will we then take on board this civil-society input? well, we will ensure that the results of the dialogues are made available to the ministerial councils established under the epas to oversee the monitoring process. in the case of west africa and east africa, those epas contain provisions for the civil-society dialogue to work in consultation with the epa institutions. in the case of the sadc epa, the text requires the parties to undertake the monitoring within their respective participative processes and institutions. the last question was on policy coherence. we have a long track record of making trade a tool for development. this is done by granting preferential market access, by providing aid for trade and by addressing any coherence issue that arises, and the epa is, of course, part of this policy. we give full access to our market, but we ask for less in return. we provide for safeguards to make sure that domestic industries are not damaged and we will introduce flexible rules of origin. we will also accompany our trade partners in meeting the commitments on trade and sustainable development in accordance with the provisions in article 11 of the agreement, and this includes assistance through eu development cooperation. in addition, we have made available support under the european development fund. in eastern and southern africa, regional programmes amount to eur 1.3 billion and national programmes to around eur 7.2 billion: these funds are not used entirely for trade-related support, but spending of eur 600 million on relevant infrastructure gives you an idea of how much this can facilitate trade. also the epas provide the structures in which any coherence issue can be addressed. so i think we have a good chance of getting this right. our partners are very keen to start working together as soon as possible under these premises, and we are convinced that the economic partnership and sustainable development can go hand in hand. i am committed to make that happen and i am looking forward to working with you on all these steps.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, commissioner, we are discussing an economic partnership agreement which, as we have seen, opens a new stage in relations between the european union and six countries of the southern african development community. it has been a difficult and lengthy agreement, but i am sure that the end result will be, in general terms, beneficial. hence our support, since we have created a clear legal framework and have also succeeded in extending the previous interim agreement, with south africa joining these talks. that said, we cannot ignore the fact that, in general, all economic association agreements always have some point of friction, and this one does too. as you have heard me say many times, someone has to pay the bill for these agreements and unfortunately this bill is usually paid by the agricultural sector. in any case, we are facing an important agreement, since it is the first one we have signed in the european union with an african region. i hope that this will serve as an impetus for talks to take place soon to strengthen the relationship between europe and africa. on the positive side, the agreement allows for the protection of certain sensitive sectors, the application of safeguard clauses and measures to protect nascent industries, as well as facilitating exports, while providing for clauses on the protection of human rights and a commitment to sustainable development. but not everything is positive. the agreement may have negative consequences for community citrus production, and this could have been avoided despite what has been said here. there are two aspects to consider. i believe that in the negotiations there was not enough information on the concessions granted mainly to south africa, a direct competitor of european union production, nor was there any study of the impact of these measures on our production. we are also extremely concerned about the guarantee, or rather the lack of guarantee, of plant health controls for these products. the commission's answers to the question of the black spot so far do not give us any peace of mind. we are clearly committed to the economic association agreements and to this agreement as well, but we are also committed to the future of oranges in many regions of spain. the two are not incompatible at all.
mr president, i firmly believe that this agreement is a step forward in the strategy of cooperation for sustainable development for the countries of the southern african community and to facilitate their integration into the world economy, because it helps to diversify their economies and, of course, to facilitate cooperation and regional integration between them. but the agreement does contain concessions on exports from south africa which do affect european mediterranean producers. unfortunately, i have to admit that the spanish government has not done its job in defending spanish citrus fruit, and i ask the commission to take care to protect and defend the interests of mediterranean producers. i therefore believe it is essential that the volume of imports and sales of south african citrus fruit be monitored on a monthly basis, applying the safeguard clause if necessary, and also compensatory measures. the extension of the period of entry of exports from south africa, so that it coincides with the european production season, will have an impact, and the important thing is to have assessed it beforehand and to measure it for whether protective measures are necessary. fair trade for all; for citrus growers, too, and for southern agriculture, which also counts.
mr president, i want to speak on behalf of the european agricultural sector and, of course, the spanish. i'm spanish and i'm from andalusia, a region where there are many citrus fruits. citrus fruit is produced, and the season begins on october 15. not only in sicily, but also in my homeland, in andalusia. and so i want to say on behalf of all agriculture - because not only the citrus sector but also the wine sector is being affected - that there has been a clear lack of transparency and of knowledge of the aspects that are most detrimental to exports from a country like south africa, which has been granted an extension of the export period of six weeks, just at the beginning of the european campaign, the spanish campaign and the andalusian campaign. so, of course, it's harmful. in addition, it has been shown that there is no impact study, and that impact study on the extension of the period should be required. in addition, south africa exports citrus products with the black spot disease, which is also very damaging to european production. these interests are therefore in conflict with european agriculture.

madam president, mr juncker, europe is worse off than it was a year ago. the bombings in france, in germany, in belgium, brexit, the mafias, who continue to choose which refugees are the ones who pass. populism is growing, unemployment is growing, skepticism is growing, the feeling is growing that the system is not working. the institutions work. the commission works, parliament works, but what really does not work is solidarity between the states. without solidarity there is no europe, even if there are european institutions. solidarity is the vaccine against nationalist interests. solidarity is what we learned from the war. solidarity is, as you have said, mr juncker, and as mr weber has said, a european way of life, but also a european model of life enjoyed by all citizens equally, not some more and others less. solidarity means that all countries respect their deficit commitments and their budgetary commitments, but solidarity also means that some partners do not seek to punish others. solidarity is for the south to understand that putin is a threat, but solidarity is also for the east to understand that mass immigration is a common problem. solidarity is that the single market means one economy and not twenty-eight economies. solidarity is one for 27 and 27 for one: europe. solidarity is europe, and europe is the only possible future for europeans. i therefore congratulate you on your speech and ask you to count on my support and that of my country, spain. in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a technical agreement to assimilate the situation of croatia, the last member state to join the union, to the same status as the other member states of the union with regard to the movement of persons with switzerland. parliament must be consulted on the conclusion of such international agreements and this resolution gives its consent to croatia's accession. as it represents a technical improvement in bringing the rights of croatian citizens on an equal footing with those of other citizens of the union, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ because of its geographical and cultural proximity, and in particular its political and economic importance, the union, with its 28 member states, is switzerland's most important partner. some 430 000 swiss citizens reside in the union. with the accession of romania, bulgaria and croatia to the union, the internal market has expanded to almost 505 million people and has become even more important for our swiss partner. a series of bilateral agreements (the so-called bilateral agreements) was therefore negotiated, followed by a second package of agreements (bilateral agreements ii) which began to be negotiated in june 2002 and were signed in 2004. for all these reasons, it is appropriate to support this protocol to the agreement and to recommend its adoption.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the conclusion of a protocol to the ec-switzerland agreement to take account of croatia's accession to the eu. it should be borne in mind that because of its geographical and cultural proximity, and in particular its political and economic importance, the eu is switzerland's most important partner. similarly, more than one million union citizens live in switzerland, another 230 000 cross the border daily to go to work and some 430 000 swiss citizens reside in the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of extending the eu-switzerland agreement on the free movement of persons to croatia. an agreement that was blocked by the swiss popular initiative "against mass immigration" approved in a referendum in 2014, incompatible with the same.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the agreement on the free movement of persons gave citizens the right to enter, live and work in the respective territories by mutually abolishing most restrictions. however, in order to enjoy these rights fully, a contract of employment or services or the possession of sufficient and secure financial means is necessary. the aim of the various agreements was to establish between the union and switzerland provisions equivalent to those laid down in the community acquis, allowing entry, residence, work, establishment as selfemployed, study, introducing the right to social security and making it possible to enjoy the same living, employment and working conditions as nationals.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a technical agreement to assimilate the situation of croatia, the last member state to join the union, to the same status as the other member states of the union with regard to the movement of persons with switzerland, facilitating the free movement of workers on the european continent.
in writing. ‒ switzerland, like the member states of the union, benefits from the internal market and its enlargements, as has been repeatedly stated in this country. there is no doubt that croatia and switzerland will benefit from the signing of this protocol iii in the political, economic and cultural fields, thanks to a larger internal market in which free movement is a fundamental element. with this bilateral agreement we have succeeded in setting quantitative limits and in gradually opening up the swiss and croatian labour markets. i therefore vote in favour of this recommendation.

in writing. ‒ this decision extends the agreement on the free movement of persons signed in 2000 to croatia as a member of the union. the european parliament is ratifying the protocol by this decision and i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this recommendation on the sst because it marks the end of a long process in which, although the council's relationship with parliament has not been as efficient and sincere as it should have been, the result is positive, both for the dialogue between the commission and the council with the social partners and for the european parliament's position on the sst. it should be noted, however, that the council has acted during this procedure without respecting parliament's deadlines.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the tripartite social summit for growth and jobs. it is a forum for dialogue between the union institutions and the european social partners, which aims to promote continuous exchange and ensure that the social partners contribute to the union's economic and social strategy. the previous 2003 decision was to be amended by a council decision with the consent of the european parliament. in 2014 parliament only approved an interim report. the situation has finally been resolved and the decision repealed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a proposal to improve the current system of european social dialogue, especially as regards parliament's participation in meetings. parliament must be consulted in the review of the functioning of the tripartite social summit, and the condition for this consultation has been the participation of the chairman of the employment committee of the european parliament in the meetings. once agreement has been reached with the commission and council on this point, his participation in the summit is guaranteed. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ faced with the need to update the legal framework of the tripartite social summit for growth and jobs (sst) due to the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty, the european commission has presented a new council decision on which sst could be based. the proposal is to adapt the 2003 council decision to the institutional changes introduced by the lisbon treaty. it is also reviewing the overall policy framework, replacing the lisbon strategy, the europe 2020 strategy and specifying how osh for growth and jobs should contribute to global governance.
in writing. ‒ the tripartite social summit (tss) includes the presidency of the european council, the presidency of the commission and the presidency-in-office of the council. it was set up in 2003 and meets at least once a year, before the spring european council, to discuss social and employment issues. it brings together the social partners 'recognised by the institutions' and is, in a sense, the moral guarantor of economic governance. the choice of the social partners, fully aware of the relevance of the system's choices, leaves european decision-makers free to act in favour of globalism. this is particularly the case in the area of migration, where the schengen area is considered untouchable and migrants are seen as an 'opportunity for europe'. the proposal itself aims to revise council decision 2003/174/ec, which institutionalises the tripartite social summit, in order to facilitate its contribution to global governance. the patriotic members of parliament cannot endorse this institution, whose functioning leaves no room for national and democratic institutions, starting with the national parliaments, and whose main aim is to 'cheat' the social dialogue. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this recommendation on the sst because it marks the end of a long process in which, although the council's relationship with parliament has not been as efficient and sincere as it should have been, the result is positive, both for the dialogue between the commission and the council with the social partners and for the european parliament's position on the sst. it should be noted, however, that the council has acted during this procedure without respecting parliament's deadlines.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the tripartite social summit for growth and jobs (tss) is a forum for dialogue between the union institutions at the level of the presidents and the european social partners at the level of the management bodies. its task is to promote continuous exchange between the social partners and the union institutions and to ensure that the social partners contribute to the union's economic and social strategy. the last summit was on 16 march 2016 on 'intensive collaboration for job creation and inclusive growth'.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a proposal to improve the current system of european social dialogue, especially as regards parliament's participation in meetings. parliament must be consulted in the review of the functioning of the tripartite social summit, and the condition for this consultation has been the participation of the chairman of the employment committee of the european parliament in the meetings. once agreement has been reached with the commission and council on this point, his participation in the summit is guaranteed. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the tripartite social summit (tsc) for growth and jobs was set up in 2003 with the aim of institutionalising the practice of holding high-level consultations between the different community institutions and the social partners in the union. in 2013, the commission presented a proposal to adapt the organisation of this summit to the new situation in the union, reinforcing it as an indispensable part of the social dialogue. the cst has largely fulfilled its role of facilitating the exchange of views at the highest level between the various actors on the employment and social aspects covered by the europe 2020 strategy. i have voted in favour of this report, considering it essential that the european social dialogue be well organized.
in writing. ‒ the tripartite social summit (tsc) for growth and jobs was established in 2003 by a council decision. the commission proposed the 2003 decision to institutionalise the practice of holding high-level consultations between the eu institutions and the eu social partners. the tripartite social summit, comprising the presidency trio, the social partners and the european commission, meets before the spring and autumn summits of heads of state or government and sets out its position for the summits. i am voting in favour of this report because i consider that a good european social dialogue is essential to promote the european semester process, now complemented by the european social dimension.
in writing. ‒ in the previous phase of committees, we voted in favour of this technical regulation on inland waterway navigation. the objective is to establish a harmonised technical framework ensuring the same level of safety for all vessels operating in the union and to facilitate their adaptation to scientific and technical progress taking into account the guidelines of cesni (european committee for the development of inland navigation standards) and other international bodies. in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure of the union, the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading was adopted without a vote.
in writing. ‒ we support the adoption of common technical standards for inland waterway vessels. they offer more and better guarantees to users by raising the safety standard and the technical conditions that these vessels must meet, including also the environmental aspect. we also congratulate parliament's negotiators for having defended the prerogatives of the house in this field throughout the process and for having defended the council's exclusive power of decision in this matter.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive which aims to harmonise technical standards for inland waterway vessels. parliament and council have agreed on the general objective of the directive, which is to establish a harmonised and coherent framework guaranteeing the same level of safety for inland waterway vessels. the two institutions supported the rationalisation of the use of resources to develop technical standards and to adapt them to scientific and technical progress by using standards developed by international organisations such as cesni. the basic aim of the standard is to align the technical requirements laid down by the commission for the navigation of the rhine, the main navigable canal in europe, with the requirements for other waterways.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it represents a good compromise in the field of inland navigation, aimed at improving the technical requirements for this type of transport. this improvement will result in safety for both workers and end-users of such forms of transport in the union. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ cesni (european committee for the development of common inland navigation standards) was established to facilitate the harmonisation of technical standards applied in the inland navigation sector throughout europe. the objective of the revision of directive 2006/87/ec is to allow progress towards a single uniform set of technical standards through cesni. this would provide greater legal certainty and ensure that appropriate adaptations to technical progress can be introduced in a timely manner, in order to ensure that high safety levels on all union waterways are maintained and that innovation and safety in the sector are not hindered.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation with a view to the uniform application of common technical requirements for inland waterway vessels in the eu, in order to ensure a high level of safety and efficiency in inland navigation, and to streamline the use of resources to develop technical standards and to adapt them to scientific and technical progress by using standards developed by international organisations.

in writing. in the previous phase of committees, we voted in favour of this technical regulation on inland waterway navigation. the objective is to establish a harmonised technical framework ensuring the same level of safety for all vessels operating in the union and to facilitate their adaptation to scientific and technical progress taking into account the guidelines of cesni (european committee for the development of inland navigation standards) and other international bodies. in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure of the union, the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading was adopted without a vote.
in writing. ‒ voted for as generally welcome proposal to harmonise standards for technical requirements for inland waterway navigation to strengthen legal certainty and a common high level of safety. however, i emphasise that the founded committee for the development of technical standards should ensure the possibility of participation for all relevant stakeholders as well as ngos. besides, our aim was to integrate a link to article 16 and article 36 of the ten-t guidelines (reg. no 1315/2013) in order to establish a connection between the development of environmental performance of inland waterway transport and the already adopted priorities regarding existing inland waterway infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ the revision of this directive aims to move towards a uniform set of technical standards to ensure better safety standards in inland navigation. i therefore think it appropriate to vote in favour of this report.
mr president, i voted against this new economic agreement between the european union and the south african countries because it is very damaging to european orange and citrus growers and, in particular, to the valencians, who are the largest producers in europe. the decision to extend the period during which south african oranges can enter europe until the end of november is a very hard blow to our producers, because during that time imported oranges will be matched with oranges produced in our own country. another blow to the orange growers, who are suffering from unfair competition coming in from countries like morocco - where the orange is produced without our standards, neither social nor environmental - and the pressure of the big distribution chains, who pay them a miserable price. another blow that fuels euroscepticism. i don't know how i'm going to explain this to my constituents. frankly, we get the impression that the european union is not working for european agricultural producers.
mr president, i voted 'no' to this agreement because, once again, the european union's foreign policy is against the community's agricultural policy, especially against our producers, in this case citrus fruit. i come from spain, from the south of spain, from andalusia, where citrus fruit, like in valencia, as mr sebastià has said, is very important, and there has not been the slightest sensitivity. i must also point out here to the house that the industry was completely unaware of the latest agreements: the extension of the six-week period, which coincides with spanish production; and the radical elimination of all tariffs. everything has been done behind the back of the agricultural sector. we can't keep doing international politics. this agreement has some laudable aspects, but seriously hurting the agricultural policy and our producers, certainly not with my vote.
mr president, i voted against this agreement because it will seriously damage small and mediumsized farming in the european union, especially in the wine and fruit sector in the southern countries and in the african countries. i also voted against it because it is an agreement which is against the interests of the entire working class. this is an agreement for the big western companies - they are the ones who profit from exports and imports, because behind the oil imported by the eu from angola, behind the diamonds imported from botswana, or behind the coal, precious stones, metals and fish imported from namibia are the interests of the big multinationals. in 2013, the european union imported 31 billion, exported 33 billion, a positive balance of 2 billion, to which we must add the profit of large companies that supply themselves with cheap raw materials and with extremely low production costs.
in writing. ‒ in this legislative resolution, parliament gives its approval to the conclusion of the agreement with the member states of the community for the development of southern africa (botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, south africa and swaziland). this agreement seeks to increase cooperation with this region of africa. it contains provisions to promote trade and development, promote regional integration, and contains clauses on respect for the values and monitoring of the implementation of the agreement. however, this agreement poses a threat to the spanish agricultural sector, especially citrus, because of the unfair competition it allows and the lack of reciprocity. i share the objectives of encouraging interregional cooperation and helping the economic growth of southern africa, but not without transparency, at the expense of the spanish agricultural sector and without taking into account its demands and its possible impact, nor of providing for compensatory measures.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the economic agreement between the union and the countries of southern africa. the instrument offers few real advantages to african countries, since it replaces the logic of non-reciprocity that has existed so far in the epas with one of reciprocity. in other words, it forces the least developed countries to open their markets to european products and thus further increase competition, which has serious repercussions in some sectors such as agriculture. in addition, there has been unfortunate pressure on african countries to speed up the signing of the agreement.
in writing. ‒ in accordance with the general framework described in the agreement. we have abstained in this report because we do not quite understand why the date for allowing oranges to be imported into the european market has been extended until november. in the previous situation, the date of 15 september was much more suited to the reality and needs of european citrus growers. this extension poses a completely gratuitous problem. that is why we have abstained in this vote.
in writing. ‒ i recognise that this agreement is a major step towards contributing to the sustainable economic development of the countries of the community for the development of southern africa, facilitating its integration into the world economy, diversifying its economic structures, strengthening cooperation and intensifying its own regional integration dynamic. however, i abstained on the vote because of the excessive concessions granted to south african citrus exports which could have a negative impact on spanish producers. the ministry of agriculture of mr rajoy's government has not done its job in defending mediterranean citrus fruit, but the spanish socialist delegation has managed to get the commission to commit itself to protecting our producers by carrying out a monthly monitoring of exports and also of sales of citrus fruit from south africa to europe, by applying the safeguard clause in the event that these exports or sales have a negative impact on the production of our regions and by putting in place compensatory measures for producers if necessary.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this economic partnership agreement between the eu and the sadc epa states because it is an agreement that will go against the interests of the popular classes: it is tailored to the big western companies, which are the ones who profit from exports and imports to these states (oil imported from angola, diamonds imported from botswana, coal, precious stones, metals and fish imported from namibia, sugar from swaziland...). the union's own data show that in 2013 it imported 31 billion and exported 33 billion to these countries. the balance sheet is positive by 2 billion, to which must be added the profit of the large companies which source cheap raw materials, with extremely low production costs due to poverty wages. we see that it is not development that is being promoted, but plunder. and as always, this agreement will seriously damage small and mediumsized farming, both in the union, especially in the southern european wine and fruit peoples, and in the sadc countries.
in writing. ‒ i am opposed to ratifying this agreement, not because i am opposed to its laudable objectives of helping the economic development of south africa, but because its implementation has suffered from certain elements which i consider essential to make a sound decision. in particular, no impact study has been carried out on the consequences of the agreement on the community market, in the specific case of extending the period for duty-free export of south african oranges by one and a half months, until 30 november each year. this extension coincides with the start of the marketing year in the south of the union. the european citrus sector has been experiencing difficulties for several years in trying to ensure the profitability of its producers. the new concession for south african orange exports also joins the sector's dissatisfaction with the european commission's inaction in tackling the threat posed by 'black spot' disease affecting south african citrus fruit. the commission is not only not addressing that concern, but has recently relaxed its controls on the ground.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the agreement, bearing in mind that while it is vital to continue supporting developing countries to achieve a level of economic development that will enable them to reduce poverty and social inequalities, it is equally important to protect european producers. trade can and must play an important role in achieving these important objectives, but always maintaining the balance between helping developing countries and protecting eu producers.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the economic agreement between the union and the countries of southern africa. the instrument offers few real advantages to african countries, since it replaces the logic of non-reciprocity that has existed so far in the epas with one of reciprocity. in other words, it forces the least developed countries to open their markets to european products and thus further increase competition, which has serious repercussions in some sectors such as agriculture. in addition, there has been unfortunate pressure on african countries to speed up the signing of the agreement.
in writing. ‒ i am opposed to ratifying this agreement, not because i am opposed to its laudable objectives of helping the economic development of southern africa, but because its implementation has suffered from certain elements which i consider essential to make a sound decision. in particular, no impact study has been carried out on the consequences of the agreement on the community market in the specific case of extending the period for duty-free export of south african oranges by one and a half months, until 30 november each year. this extension coincides with the start of the marketing year in the south of the european union. the european citrus sector has been experiencing difficulties for several years in trying to ensure the profitability of its producers. the new concession for south african orange exports is also in line with the sector's dissatisfaction with the european commission's inaction in dealing with the threat posed by black spot disease affecting south african citrus fruit. the commission is not only not addressing that concern, but has also recently relaxed its on-the-spot checks.

in writing. ‒ i abstained in this report on the economic partnership agreement (epa), which has already been signed and is in the process of ratification by all african partners, will provide these countries with access to new markets. it responds quite satisfactorily to the objective of bringing the union's policies as closely as possible together by coordinating our trade policies with those of development, fisheries and agriculture. by signing the agreement, all participants commit themselves to act in accordance with international social and environmental standards. the agreement provides for a series of flexibilities and asymmetrical deadlines to allow the southern african countries to gradually and partially open up to union exports. but the lack of a separate human rights clause, that they do not contribute to regional integration, that many national parliaments have not participated in the negotiation process makes this agreement incomplete. and while the agreement includes a commitment to foster dialogue with civil society, unfortunately it does not incorporate a formally structured mechanism for its follow-up, and we are not failing in our efforts to call for the full inclusion of civil society in the process.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the economic agreement between the union and the countries of southern africa. the instrument offers few real advantages to african countries, since it replaces the logic of non-reciprocity that has existed so far in the epas with one of reciprocity. in other words, it forces the least developed countries to open their markets to european products and thus further increase competition, which has serious repercussions in some sectors such as agriculture. in addition, there has been unfortunate pressure on african countries to speed up the signing of the agreement.

in writing. ‒ i have always been in favour of free trade, and will continue to be in favour of free and fair trade. however, i cannot vote in favour of trade deals that will be hugely detrimental to the farmers in my constituency, in particular orange producers. in this specific case, the orange from south africa will invade our markets in huge numbers without the sanitary checks and strict rules eu farmers are subject to. these south african oranges will enter eu markets even before the european producers start harvesting their oranges. the european union should have made a detailed analysis on the potential negative effects on the agriculture sector.
in writing. i voted against the economic agreement between the union and the countries of southern africa. the instrument offers few real advantages to african countries, since it replaces the logic of non-reciprocity that has existed so far in the epas with one of reciprocity. in other words, it forces the least developed countries to open their markets to european products and thus further increase competition, which has serious repercussions in some sectors such as agriculture. in addition, there has been unfortunate pressure on african countries to speed up the signing of the agreement.
in writing. ‒ i voted against as the greens/efa group rejects the eu-sadc epa, as it continues to believe that economic partnership agreements (epas) are not the right means to foster regional integration, sustainable development and respect for human rights in the acp region. the eu-sadc epa singles out six economically very different countries from the 15 sadc member countries. this is likely to bring about the disruption of the still precarious regional integration and regional trade. cheap imports of european products and inputs might well wipe out infant industry and manufacturing potential.
in writing. ‒ i am opposed to ratifying this agreement, not because i am opposed to its laudable objectives of helping the economic development of south africa, but because its implementation has suffered from certain elements which i consider essential to make a sound decision. in particular, no impact study has been carried out on the consequences of the agreement on the community market, in the specific case of extending the period for duty-free export of south african oranges by one and a half months, until 30 november each year. this extension coincides with the start of the marketing year in the south of the union. the european citrus sector has been experiencing difficulties for several years in trying to ensure the profitability of its producers. the new concession for south african orange exports also joins the sector's dissatisfaction with the european commission's inaction in tackling the threat posed by 'black spot' disease affecting south african citrus fruit. the commission is not only not addressing that concern, but has recently relaxed its controls on the ground.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because fishermen need special protection. it is a sector characterized by high numbers of accidents at work, risk of illness and highly precarious conditions. it is also a sector in which workers lack a clear delimitation of rest and working time, with the consequent detriment to health and reconciliation. the resolution is a proposal for a council directive implementing the cogeca-etf-europe agreement on the implementation of the ilo convention on work in fishing 2007. while we regret the long delay in the submission to the council of the agreement with the social partners submitted in 2013, we consider that there was a need to develop the provisions on wages, social protection and social security with a view to ensuring adequate income for workers and their families and that this agreement puts the union in a better position to promote its implementation in partner countries around the world, thus fostering a level playing field in the global fisheries sector.
in writing. ‒ i support this resolution for the adoption of a directive which will undoubtedly improve working conditions for fishermen throughout europe. i am glad that this regulation has been drawn up with the active participation of the sector concerned and that it is being incorporated into the provisions for applying it to selfemployed persons working on the same vessels or in fishing enterprises with employees.
‒ 100 000 people work in the eu fishing industry, often in difficult circumstances. the accident and injury rate can be fifteen times higher compared to other sectors. in 2002, the ilo began discussions at global level for a comprehensive and updated set of international standards for the fisheries sector, with a view to ensuring adequate protection for fishermen worldwide. this led to the adoption of the ilo convention on work in the fisheries sector in 2007. so far, france is the only country in the union which has ratified this convention. on 29 april 2016, the european commission presented a proposal for a directive aimed at improving the working conditions of workers in the fisheries sector. the commission proposal is based on the request of the social partners to implement their agreement on the 2007 ilo convention on work in the fisheries sector. i support the ratification of the ilo fisheries agreement and have therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report so that the council can decide in favour of adopting ilo convention 188 on work in fisheries, as agreed by the european social partners. i have done so in order to support the european social dialogue and, above all, the adoption of ilo standards, in order to provide minimum standards of social protection, rest, wages, compensation and health and safety at work for fishermen on european vessels. i also hope that the adoption of convention 188 by the union will open the door to its ratification by third countries, thus serving as a global reference.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution, considering that the agreement concluded by the social partners and the commission proposal is limited to establishing minimum requirements, thus allowing member states and the social partners to adopt measures which are more favourable to workers in the sector. it is also important to note that this agreement also applies to selfemployed fishermen who work alongside salaried workers on the same vessel. we must develop the provisions on wages, social protection and social security, with a view to guaranteeing adequate income to workers and their families, including in the event of injury, accident or death.
in writing. ‒ this resolution concerns a proposal for a directive on the implementation of the 2007 international labour organisation convention on work in fishing. the aim is to ensure protection for fishermen worldwide and more specifically within the european union. this protection covers the working and living conditions of fishermen working on board vessels flying the flag of a member state of the european union: minimum age, medical examination, number of fishermen on board, rest periods, crew list, repatriation, payment method, accommodation on board, medical care, food, safety, etc. at the moment, only two eu countries, france and estonia, have ratified this convention, but its incorporation into european legislation should better protect our fishermen, while avoiding possible distortions of competition. that is why i voted for this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the human rights situation in poland, because it emphasises the importance of defending fundamental rights as something fundamental for a european country which must comply with the charter of fundamental rights of the union. in addition, our group added four amendments to the final resolution which stressed the need to protect the rights of women and sexual minorities.
in writing. ‒ we would like to emphasise here our vote in favour of the six amendments which have fallen and which criticised the restrictive laws on abortion, anti-muslim rhetoric, asylum, freedom of expression in debates on historical events and other aspects which merely confirm our concern about decisions which may be the exclusive competence of the polish institutions but which degrade fundamental freedoms and rights in that country and, therefore, throughout the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the degradation of the rule of law and the quality of democracy in poland. the european commission has been investigating for months the recent reforms of the polish constitutional court and state control over the public media. the commission has also noted a lack of cooperation from the polish authorities and will therefore proceed with the next phase of the phased process provided for by the mechanism. finally, another matter of real concern is the absolute ban on abortion that the government is planning and which is incompatible with the rights of reproductive autonomy. in addition, the venice commission has raised questions about the use of eavesdropping and monitoring practices of citizen communications included in the new police law.
in writing. ‒ i share the deep concern about the situation of fundamental rights in poland, which, like other eu countries, has seen a sharp decline. the growing xenophobia, the attacks on the rights of women and lgbt people, or the imposition of ultraconservative profiles in different instances of the state, are realities that call into question the self-proclaimed democratic and plural character of the union. however, this resolution puts the guarantee of these freedoms in the hands of european authorities who do not protect them in states where their political interests do not allow it. it also presents women's rights as something separate from the rest of the fundamental rights, which have a basic pillar in their indivisibility. as is often the case, the right to dispose of one's own body becomes an accessory and secondary element. for all this, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution, considering that the eu is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and human rights, values which are common to all member states and which must therefore be respected. despite intensive exchanges of views with the polish authorities, the issues threatening the rule of law in poland have not been satisfactorily resolved and the commission considers that there is a systemic threat to the rule of law in poland and, in line with this situation, has made a number of specific recommendations to the polish authorities on how to respond to the concerns of the institution as a matter of urgency.
in writing. ‒ the law & justice party won the presidency of the republic in august 2015 (andrzej duda) and the parliamentary elections in october 2015. this new government, because it is conservative, is attacked by the eurocrats on two points: on public television, where a reform aims not to renew the mandates of the heads of public television and radio. it is an exaggeration to talk about control of the media: it is simply a matter of renewal of the governing bodies, as is also the case in france in the event of a change of government. the new government has appointed a few judges to the constitutional tribunal. but the former ruling party, the europeanists, had itself appointed new judges to the constitutional court in may 2015. he wanted to keep control of the institution, even in the event of an electoral defeat, without the european commission and parliament being outraged. the resolution they are presenting therefore supports the government of the judges and the media against the government elected by the people. we therefore voted against this resolution with the patriotic members and tabled a counter-proposal in favour of poland.

in writing. ‒ since the ultra-conservative pis government came to power, poland has undertaken a real purge of existing counter-powers, similar to what has been done in hungary. many journalists in the public media have been sacked, the heads of the main state administrations have been replaced by supporters of the government, and the constitutional court is being reformed to bring it into line. at the end of july, the commission sent poland an official letter on respect for the rule of law, denouncing the machinations against the constitutional court. the resolution supports the commission's letter and is concerned about other moves, including the media law, changes in the police and administration and amendments to the criminal code to facilitate prosecution. i support this text, but i also call for more firm measures to ensure that the constitutional balances are not changed to the will of the majorities. the manoeuvres of the populist forces in poland and hungary to lock down the powers while maintaining democratic suffrage must be fought, otherwise they will become an example for all the autocratic apprentices on the continent.

in writing. ‒ i abstained in the vote on this report on poland because i feel there are differences of attitude in europe depending on the political majorities in place in different member states. in particular i would mention amendment 2, referring to problems of other countries with regard the rule of law and respect for democratic principles, which reads: ‘whereas other countries have had a deteriorating rule of law situation that would need to be investigated by the commission, considering that the rule of law represents a common standard that should be respected and applied equally by all member states’. in particular, i would like to see the same attitude on the part of the commission with regard the independence of the spanish constitutional court and the independence of the media in spain.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the human rights situation in poland because it emphasises the importance of defending fundamental rights as a fundamental right for a european country which must comply with the charter of fundamental rights of the union. in addition, our group added four amendments to the final resolution which stressed the need to protect the rights of women and sexual minorities.
in writing. ‒ although the report did not include our group's amendments on debt (in favour of an audit, restructuring and partial debt forgiveness) and the agreement on the readmission of migrants (which is a violation of human rights), it is a positive report in that it supports the eu's support for the democratization process in the country. however, we do not support the inclusion of a favourable clause in the opaque free trade agreement (fta), which, like all similar agreements, would end up hurting the weaker party in terms of terms of trade, both economically and environmentally, as stated in the manifesto signed by 29 tunisian and french civil society organizations. the effects of liberalisation on certain spanish products such as olive oil must also be analysed. finally, we believe that agreements of this kind, because of their major social, economic, labour and environmental implications, should be the product of a broad and informed debate in the societies involved prior to their signature. i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i support this motion for a resolution, which seems to me to be a correct expression, based also on an objective assessment of the situation, of the obligatory support that tunisia deserves from the european institutions for its democratic commitment to a real opening up of its institutional, social and political structures. it is also an expression of the issues on which we can contribute more than words: experience, means and concrete instruments of cooperation in critical areas such as innovation, security, etc.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which aims to boost relations between the union and tunisia in the current regional context. tunisia is a democratic success story in the arab world and its consolidation is of paramount importance for the stability of the whole region. the union should continue to support tunisia's socio-economic, political and security transition. we welcome the efforts of the tunisian government and encourage the union to support the reform of the judicial sector and the rule of law in the country, the reform of the criminal code and we call for increased assistance to tunisia through the european neighbourhood instrument, among other issues. we also stress the importance of respect for human rights and the development of monitoring mechanisms in respect for fundamental freedoms, gender equality and the strengthening of the role of civil society organisations.
in writing. ‒ this report reaffirms the union's support for the process of democratic consolidation in tunisia and underlines the problems that could jeopardise it: debt, unemployment, security, rule of law, etc. the report generally takes a more progressive approach than the european parliament usually takes to dealing with relations with other countries. however, there are some elements with which i do not agree and which made it impossible for me to support the report, and as a result i abstained in the final vote: one of the main problems was that the report supports the eunavfor mission, and on the other hand it talks about deepening the negotiations on the free trade agreement to which our delegation is opposed, although the text is about giving it a focus on the environment and consumer protection, i cannot vote in favour of the document which supports free trade and which also praises the macro-financial aid of 500 million euros without denouncing its neoliberal conditionalities, nor does it make any reference to a necessary audit of tunisia's odious debt.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, considering that the peaceful process of transition to democracy in tunisia is a success story in the arab world and that its consolidation is vital for the stability of the whole region and for the security of the eu. to help consolidate it, the eu and the member states need to mobilise and better coordinate a significant volume of technical and financial resources to provide tunisia with targeted support.
in writing. ‒ although the report did not include our group's amendments on debt (in favour of an audit, restructuring and partial debt forgiveness) and the agreement on the readmission of migrants (which is a violation of human rights), it is a positive report in that it supports the eu's support for the democratization process in the country. however, we do not support the inclusion of a favourable clause in the opaque free trade agreement (fta), which, like all similar agreements, would end up hurting the weaker party in terms of terms of trade, both economically and environmentally, as stated in the manifesto signed by 29 tunisian and french civil society organizations. the effects of liberalisation on certain spanish products such as olive oil must also be analysed. finally, we believe that agreements of this kind, because of their major social, economic, labour and environmental implications, should be the product of a broad and informed debate in the societies involved prior to their signature. i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it aims to boost relations between the union and tunisia in the current regional context. tunisia is a democratic success story in the arab world and its consolidation is of paramount importance for the stability of the whole region. a new government has just started its work, with a very young prime minister, whose main objectives are the fight against corruption and economic recovery. the text stresses the need to support tunisia's socioeconomic, political and security transition. our group has insisted on: the importance of respect for human rights and the development of monitoring mechanisms on respect for fundamental freedoms, gender equality and other human rights issues, that the free trade agreement should contribute to the stability of tunisia and that it should be a progressive and asymmetrical agreement, from which the economies and societies of tunisia and the union can benefit, and finally, the strengthening of the role of civil society organisations.

in writing. ‒ tunisia was the country where five years ago, the so-called arab spring began. the democratic transition began in january 2011, the only one of the so-called arab spring in which the process culminated in the approval of a constitution and the holding of democratic and transparent presidential and legislative elections. the commission notes that the union has provided financial assistance to tunisia in the form of loans to finance the construction of a new airport in the country. the fear now is that the economic situation will derail the political gains. the eu-tunisia association council held in april last year stressed the importance of tunisia's implementation of the structural reforms still pending. in the european parliament we have started work, taking a first step in this direction, through the creation of the eu-tunisia joint parliamentary committee. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that spain and europe should regard tunisia as a priority partner in the strategic maghreb region and we must support it in political reforms, economic development and the fight against terrorism.
in writing. ‒ in the european parliament, we have committed ourselves to renewing our commitment to the tunisian people and their political transition process, which began in 2011. my support for the resolution calling on the union to support your government in the face of the challenges and threats facing the country in consolidating the democratic process, implementing the necessary reforms for its social and economic prosperity and guaranteeing its security. in the motion for a resolution which we have supported, we express our support for political and institutional reforms, which will make it possible to move forward on the path of democratic consolidation, and for economic and social development measures to be implemented as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ the report we voted on represents a renewed commitment to tunisia following the election of the new government of youssef chahed. the process of transition to democracy in tunisia is a successful example in the arab world and the stability of the region depends to a large extent on its continuation. despite all this, we must continue to work together to advance the social and economic development of the country and to encourage investment. that is why i congratulate the commission on its proposal to allocate some eur 500 million in aid and to convert tunisian debt into local investment projects. i voted in favour of the report in the hope that democracy and development in tunisia will continue to take hold.
