in writing. ‒ i voted for, as i welcome this sound and comprehensive report, which is long overdue: the remarkable political transformation and efforts of the tunisian people since the overthrow of ben ali in 2011 have regrettably fallen off the eu/ep radar. tunisia faces mighty challenges – from terrorism to deep and persistent socio-economic inequalities and political fragility. the eu should substantially step up its efforts in support of this unique, effective democratisation process in the arab world. it should remain vigilant to ensure that human rights and the rule of law are upheld in the challenging security and political context. support to tunisian youth, women and civil society should be a priority for the eu.
in writing. ‒ in this report, the european parliament urges the union and its member states to better mobilise and coordinate technical and financial resources to support tunisia, while expressing support for the democratization process in the arab country, taking into account in particular the challenge of strengthening stability while deepening democratization in a volatile regional context. given that tunisia was the country where the so-called 'arab spring' began - which brought with it the beginning of the democratic transition - and, in fact, the only one where this phenomenon culminated in the adoption of a consensus constitution (which came to enshrine such relevant aspects as freedom of conscience, equal rights for women and the civil character of the state) and the holding of democratic and transparent presidential and legislative elections, i share the need to reiterate european support for tunisia, so i have voted in favour.
mr president, the deterioration of working conditions and social rights due to social dumping is the fundamental problem of the european union. the erosion has been constant for decades, making european workers more vulnerable and impoverished. europe has the instruments to combat this practice, but we find that the directives that are adopted, as in transport, are not applied, or are distorted, as in the case of legislation for posted workers. as the report calls for, we demand equal rights for every worker in every place in the union; that inspections, fines and penalties be applied to the last person responsible; that the mail-order companies and the fictitious subcontracting chains be combated; that collective bargaining and social dialogue be strengthened. because the laws and fundamental principles of this deeply devalued european union demand it. by refusing to act, the european union is denying itself any chance of a democratic europe.
in writing. ‒ the fight against social dumping, which could be defined as the race to the bottom in social, labour and wage standards within the union, has been a priority for the socialist group since the last parliamentary term, as it leads to the abuse of workers and erodes national social protection systems. with this report the socialists have sought to improve labour inspections and controls in the union, to increase the penalties for companies which do not respect the rules, to improve cooperation between national authorities in order to improve the fight against social security fraud, false selfemployment and shell companies. we also call on the commission to set up a european road transport agency and to review the posting of workers directive. in short, i voted in favour of this report because it is a huge step forward in the upward social convergence of the union and in the struggle to equate social rights with economic freedoms. only if we guarantee the principle of equal pay for equal work and fair competition will we be able to protect workers and smes, which are the real engine of job creation in the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a progressive report which denounces unfair economic and social competition resulting from social dumping. dumping promotes a reduction in labour costs and leads to a reduction in the social protection of workers, which in turn reduces the resources available to the state to protect its own citizens. the report proposes a harmonisation of social rights and includes positive measures such as strengthening labour inspection at national level and the creation of a body at union level to combat abusive practices; the development of a single digital document guaranteeing the social rights of all workers; the obligation for companies to have an official address to combat the existence of shell companies; a revision of the posted workers directive to ensure fair competition, with particular emphasis on the transport sector and the adoption of a social protocol ensuring the primacy of social rights over economic freedoms, as well as the introduction of minimum wages that can be extended at union level in some sectors.
in writing. ‒ i have supported the main lines of this report because i share the view that strengthening the internal market must go hand in hand with harmonising social rights in the internal market. otherwise we will be seeing cases of social dumping leading to practices which we have repeatedly denounced in sectors such as transport and construction, which distort competition and are degrading basic aspects of working conditions such as the purchasing power of wages and, especially, the safety of workers. putting an end to this threat is also key if citizens are to realise the usefulness of the european project. i agree with the need to activate the commission's commitment in this field.

in writing. ‒ this report not only takes a clear position on the problem of social dumping, which the right and other european institutions refuse to even mention, but also calls for measures with which i strongly agree: better implementation of existing labour regulations, reinforcement of sanctions and inspections and the extension of responsibility to the chain of subcontracting, coordination of social security systems, equal rights for workers in the same place, etc. i am sceptical that the constitutional architecture of the treaties, especially when the union is not considering joining the european social charter or even the echr, will allow us to overcome the current subordination of labour rules to the 'market freedoms' used by the big groups to force workers to compete with each other, and in this respect i consider proposals such as the 'social pillar' or the current reform of the posted workers directive which the rapporteur likes to see as insufficient. i have nevertheless voted in favour of this as a step in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ europe has been defined as a democratic area with an efficient economy and a high level of social protection. however, if market liberalisation is not linked to the harmonisation of social rights, the principle of fair competition between undertakings and the promotion of a social market economy may be jeopardised. the increase in abusive practices and unfair social competition are undermining the principle of the internal market and undermining confidence in the european project. the european parliament is committed to 'fighting social dumping' by closing the legislative and regulatory loopholes which favour the development of unfair competition currently existing in the internal market, such as reinforcing controls and inspections, both at national and european level, among others.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, as i noted that the european union was built, first of all, by the liberalisation of economic trade between the member states. however, there has been no harmonisation of social rights and, apart from certain principles laid down in the treaty and in certain directives, member states retain competence in social matters. there is therefore an asymmetry between the reality of an internal market in the process of being completed and very heterogeneous social rights. this paradox creates competition between firms, since european workers do not have the same social rights and obligations. in this regard, on 15 july 2014 the president of the commission made a commitment to the european parliament to 'fight social dumping' during the current legislature. we must therefore continue to work and legislate within the european institutions to achieve greater harmonization in social matters.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection to the commission's delegated act, which would delay the entry into force of the new regulation on the information that financial undertakings must make available to the consumer when selling insurance-based investment products. the reason is that the current proposal includes a risk forecasting system which has been pointed out by independent research as being too optimistic, i.e. tending to hide the real risk from the consumer. this regulation is part of the commission's policy of favouring the capital market union as a means of financing for companies and individuals, favouring the securitisation of all types of assets and favouring speculative markets.
in writing. ‒ given the implications of safe regulation for the users of these funds, we agree to ask the commission to improve its proposal. we played a lot. these retail funds consolidate a market in which 10 trillion euros are traded. its users move basic own resources for their income and mostly aspire to generate income from them to meet basic needs such as education or paying a mortgage, so eliminating the risk categorization calculation of insurance products is the surest way to mislead investors.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it raises an objection to the delegated act presented by the commission on the information requirements for insurance investments. the commission proposal contains serious shortcomings in the calculation of the risks which retail investors should be made aware of before purchasing any of these financial products. that is why i share the shortcomings identified by the european parliament in the commission's delegated act and why i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.

madam president, we need to reindustrialise europe because having a strong industry means having sustainable growth, and because industry is also linked to having good wages, to having better social protection and more stable jobs. but to re-industrialize europe, the first thing we must do is protect the industry we have today. i am tired of meeting in my constituency in catalonia with companies, with works councils, with trade unions, with workers' representatives who are facing restructuring, plant closures due to merger processes, such as alstom's - we also have a plant - because of a very aggressive labour reform or because of the greed to seek unlimited profits. i know that commissioner thyssen shares this sentiment, but we have to take action on this matter, and what we have to do is to put in place common rules to protect workers against any restructuring processes we may undertake and common rules for information and consultation of workers in companies.
mr president, we were saying this morning that europe is at a crossroads. europe is chained by crises, and crises are chained by europe. nationalism and populism are on the rise and so is public discontent with the european union. and this has to do with the increase in inequality, with the wage gap, with the loss of rights and, of course, with the loss of employment. the european union as a whole needs to relaunch an industrial policy. and if we do not do this, we will not meet the european commission's objective of increasing the gross domestic product of industry from 15 to 20 per cent. we must move from words to deeds. we must invest in new niches of employment and new opportunities. and of course we must avoid social dumping and unfair competition, which are also taking place within the european union's own states, as is the case, for example, with the steel industry. and that is why we need to create a european fund to compensate energy-intensive industries, so that each member state cannot do as it pleases.
member of the commission. – thank you, madam president. i welcome the debate we had today and i have taken note of your recommendations. i would like to stress once more that our immediate priority now is to support those directly affected. the european union will continue to show solidarity with the workers and regions affected by major closures, and we are ready to offer our support through the european funds, the legal acquis and any other relevant policy instruments. i can announce that today the commission has adopted a proposal to prolong the derogation for needs beyond 2017. this prolongation that is foreseen in the regulation on the globalisation fund in article 6(2). to support job creation we must keep improving the framework conditions for jobs, growth and investment. we do this via the european semester, recommending, clarifying and simplifying rules and regulations, ensuring that tax systems encourage, and not discourage, employment reducing the scale of undeclared work. we must also act directly to help create jobs by deepening our internal market in all its dimensions. the crucial tool is the investment plan for europe, which has the potential to bring investments back in line with historical trends. structural reforms in the framework of the so-called third pillar of the investment plan will nurture the economic recovery and can provide further basis for sustainable growth. there were some reactions on the stability and growth pact. it should first be noted that the closure of the caterpillar plant in gosselies and the stability pact are of course two different things. the stability pact is critical to preserve sound public finances in the european union and to stimulate sustainable economic growth. the rules of the pact should not therefore be holding back investments, as president junker also said this morning in his ‘state of the union’, and here we see a common responsibility for member states and for the european institutions. there was also something said on the european parliament’s resolution on the competitiveness of the european rail supply industry. we are aware of this resolution. we know it. we are preparing a draft reply, and i can tell you that we are taking due note of parliament’s resolution on the competitiveness of the rail supply industry. we welcome the emphasis on our common effort to maintain a thriving industry. there were a lot of remarks on the international trade agreement. i can tell you that commissioner malmström is a good negotiator; she is negotiating hard and she has the next item is the debate on the commission statement on the apple state-aid decision (2016/2879(rsp)).
member of the commission. – madam president, on 30 august the commission adopted a decision that apple’s tax benefits in ireland are illegal state aid. i am thankful for the european parliament’s interest in this case and happy to be here today to inform you about the decision. it is an honour. this decision follows an in-depth investigation into two tax rulings that ireland had issued to apple. we concluded that they gave apple a selective advantage over other companies, artificially reducing apple’s tax burden over two decades. this is illegal under eu state aid rules. apple now has to pay the unpaid tax of up to eur 13 billion plus interest. member states cannot give unfair tax benefits and thereby selectively favour certain companies. eu state aid rules keep the level playing field in the single market and ensure that companies can compete on equal terms, thus protecting european taxpayers. the state aid decision on apple does not call into question ireland’s general tax system or its corporate tax rate. the investigation concerned two irish tax rulings from 1991 and 2007. they gave selective tax treatment to two irish companies in the apple group. the ruling endorsed an internal allocation of profits within apple sales international between its head office and branch. the bulk of the company’s profits were allocated to the company’s head office. the thing was that apple sales international’s head office had no employees, no premises and no real economic activity. it existed only on paper. therefore, there was no factual or economic justification for allocating almost all of the company’s profits to the head office. under the irish tax law applicable at the time, the head office was not subject to tax in ireland or anywhere else. the rulings therefore allowed apple sales international to pay very little tax on its profits. in fact, the effective tax rate for apple sales international was as little as 0.005% in 2014. this means that apple paid less than eur 50 in tax for every million euros in profits, giving it a significant advantage over other businesses in breach of state aid rules. to restore fair competition the decision now orders the recovery of apple’s unpaid taxes back to 2003. it is for the irish tax authorities to calculate the exact amount. we estimate that it could be as much as eur 13 billion plus interest. apple and ireland have announced that they will appeal, and they of course have the right to do so. we have a robust decision and will defend it in court. once agreed by ireland, we will publish our decision for all to see, and i hope that this can happen as fast as possible. the published information may also be relevant to tax authorities in other jurisdictions. this is because apple decided to record most of its profits from european sales in ireland. this is not an issue for the eu state aid rules, but as soon as the decision is published, tax authorities will be able to read across the information provided by apple in ireland and in their jurisdiction, and of course assess whether this updated information is relevant under national tax rules. in addition, if the us tax authorities consider that apple should have paid a higher contribution for research and development to its us parent, it could lead to a higher taxable amount in the us. looking ahead, the goal is that all companies, big or small, should pay taxes where they generate their profits. to that end, the eu, the us and the international partners as such must work together, and significant steps have already been taken by the oecd and endorsed by the g20. in the eu, under the responsibility of my colleagues valdis dombrovskis and pierre moscovici, we are pursuing a strategy towards fair taxation and greater transparency. firstly, european tax authorities will next year start to exchange information on tax rulings, a real change for the better. but we should go even further. transparency is very important in an open, democratic society. it is important that basic tax information on multinational companies becomes public. the public should see the number of employees, what activities a company has in each country, what profits they generate and what taxes they pay. this is the objective of the commission proposal on country-by-country public reporting. these reforms and even-handed enforcement of our competition rules contribute to a fairer investment environment, and a single market where companies can compete on merit, as reflected in the quality of their products, prices, and the services they can provide, and not on the basis of their tax arrangements. a single market of more than 500 million potential customers: that alone is a very good reason for companies to invest, and it is a top priority for the juncker commission to make europe even more attractive for investment for the benefit of all european citizens.

in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work on this report, which i supported, on the european travel document for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals. in this case, i have also deferred from my group and voted in favour of amendment no 35 by the gue/ngl group which requires that the european travel document for return be drawn up in the official language or languages of the member state adopting the return decision and in a language which the returnee understands. i have been advocating this since the last parliament, when we were discussing the european protection order.
in writing. ‒ the european procedure for returning irregular migrants who are subject to a return order is currently not effective. in 2014, less than 40% of the total number of return decisions issued by member states were implemented. however, in around 60% of cases, facilitating such return, even when it is voluntary and desired, cannot be carried out because the country of origin refuses to accept that person back into its territory due to, among other things, the lack of documents or the recognition of these documents. this regulation, which i supported with my vote, establishes a uniform european travel document to facilitate the return of third-country nationals who are subject to a return decision. the document must contain a passport photograph and be issued in an official eu language, with a translation into english and french and, where possible, into the language of the country of return. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment.
in writing. ‒ the expulsion of people who have fled wars, misery and exploitation generated by the west is one of the key elements of the fortress europe that we reject. we believe that this is a measure contrary to the rights of migrants, who are being forcibly and against their will expelled, and it should be remembered that forced displacement is recognised in international law as a crime against humanity. we have therefore voted against this proposal, the sole purpose of which is to speed up these deportations and to reduce the limited guarantees and rights that migrants may have.
in writing. ‒ the european travel document, intended for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals, should speed up the return of illegal immigrants who do not have a passport or identity card. this is now a widespread situation, as illegal immigrants have realised that the absence of these documents makes it difficult for member states to identify countries of origin and therefore to return to them. the best solution would therefore be to conclude genuine readmission agreements with third countries, so that illegal immigrants can be expelled despite the very "timely" loss of their identity papers. but it is not the european union that is actually still very pro-immigration. i therefore voted against this report because i am convinced that it is being applied effectively and that it is effective. i would also like to note that the rapporteur himself stresses that to be more effective, the union would need to conclude stronger readmission agreements with third countries. i would add that for these agreements to become a reality, the member states must restore their national borders and regain their sovereignty in immigration matters, in order to conclude and implement these agreements themselves.
in writing. ‒ we vote against this report because it is a text that legitimises the mechanism for the regulated expulsion of migrants, which is part of the repressive and security logic with which the eu has decided to deal with the humanitarian crisis caused in part by its irresponsible foreign policy. none of our group's amendments, which focus on the need to respect the rights of migrants and data protection, were included in the final text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because this regulation will establish a common model and the technical and security specifications of a harmonised european travel document for the return of third-country nationals who are staying illegally in the territory of the union. this document will only be valid in cases where the identity and nationality of the returnee are established and never in cases of unknown nationality. the document must contain a passport photograph and be issued in an official eu language, with a translation into english and french and, where possible, into the language of the country of return. the document is valid for one journey only, ending on arrival in the country of return. the text stresses the importance of respecting human rights and the principles recognised in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, in particular human dignity and access to the right of asylum. return, expulsion and extradition should be a last resort subject to an effective remedy.
in writing. ‒ the expulsion of people who have fled wars, misery and exploitation generated by the west is one of the key elements of the fortress europe that we reject. we believe that this is a measure contrary to the rights of migrants, who are being forcibly and against their will expelled, and it should be remembered that forced displacement is recognised in international law as a crime against humanity. we have therefore voted against this proposal, the sole purpose of which is to speed up these deportations and to reduce the limited guarantees and rights that migrants may have.
in writing. ‒ the eu's return policy has a lot of room for improvement. their average efficiency is less than 40%. in times like the present, when the eu is under very strong and growing migratory pressures, enhanced return effectiveness is one of the key elements of migration policy. i believe that the importance of this report lies partly in the fact that, in order to improve the efficiency of returns, it is crucial to have a european travel document which meets safety standards and is accepted by third countries. and although this document has been around for years, its use is uneven, in part because of its safety deficiencies. i am voting in favour of the adoption of this report, since it is necessary to promote the use of the document mentioned above, especially with third countries to which people who are in the eu illegally are returned.
in writing. ‒ a long-term solution is needed to stabilise the current migration crisis, to relieve the pressure on member states and union agencies and to increase our capacity and resources in this area. for that reason, i support the proposal for a regulation on the european travel document for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals. we propose that this document be a requirement of any future agreement concluded by the union on cooperation and readmission and that the necessary measures be established to ensure the functioning of the system, while protecting the human rights of these persons.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the regulation on the prospectus to be published when securities are issued, as it harmonises the conditions in all member states, thus helping to strengthen the single market for financial and capital services. the internal market is still one of the fundamental elements for making progress in the federal sense in european integration in the economic, political and social dimensions. i am also pleased that the report has taken up our proposal that no purchaser of allowances should be excluded on grounds of nationality or residence, even if the allowances are covered by the quantitative exemption which allows the information leaflet or prospectus not to be published. at the same time, the report makes clear that if the issuer publishes the prospectus and may have benefited from the quantitative exemption, the issue will not have to meet additional requirements in member states other than where the issue takes place.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this proposal for a regulation, which sets out the rules that financial companies must follow when informing consumers about the financial products they put on sale. on the one hand, it seems to us that this regulation, like all the others included in the draft of the commission on capital market union, promotes a financialized economy with a high tendency towards financial instability and speculation, with an increasingly limited capacity of the states to direct the flows of financing towards activities and projects of general interest. the commission has also proposed that the regulations on leaflets be too lax and not sufficiently detailed to warn consumers of the risks and responsibilities involved in buying these products.
in writing. ‒ i would like to congratulate my group colleague petr jezek on his work on this report on the prospectus to be published in the event of a public offer or admission to stock exchange listing. the purpose of this document is to define the requirements for the preparation, approval and distribution of this brochure. it is a good step towards transparency and clarification.
in writing. ‒ the current directive 2003/71/ec on the obligation to publish an information brochure understandable to the average investor has become outdated as a result of market developments and, in particular, the uneven application of the directive by the member states. for this reason, the commission has chosen to replace it with this regulation, which i voted for, which simplifies the reporting obligations for smes and allows national exemptions for emissions below eur 5 million, as well as ensuring uniform application. i also welcome the socialist proposal that voluntary compliance with the regulation may be possible even if it is below the threshold, which will allow the issuer to benefit from the cover provided by the regulation, i.e. to be able to operate within the internal market with the authorization of a single member state.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the regulation on the prospectus to be published when securities are issued, as it harmonises the conditions in all member states, thus helping to strengthen the single market for financial and capital services. the internal market is still one of the fundamental elements for making progress in the federal sense in european integration in the economic, political and social dimensions. i am also pleased that the report has taken up our proposal that no purchaser of allowances should be excluded on grounds of nationality or residence, even if the allowances are covered by the quantitative exemption which allows the information leaflet or prospectus not to be published. at the same time, the report makes clear that if the issuer publishes the prospectus and may have benefited from the quantitative exemption, the issue will not have to meet additional requirements in member states other than where the issue takes place.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it represents a step forward in the financial integration of the business fabric of the european union, adopting a model similar to that of the united states to promote speculative financing methods for companies linked to the real economy, mainly smes. this proposal, which lays down the information requirements for such companies, is a necessary step within the capital markets union, to allow financial funds to short-circuit bank requirements and to be able to speculate directly with sme financing. this will result in the destabilisation of the real economy and the outsourcing of financial sector risk to smes. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.

in writing. ‒ disclosure of information in the event of public offerings of securities or admission of securities to trading on a regulated market is vital to protect investors by eliminating information asymmetries between investors and issuers. harmonisation of this disclosure allows for the establishment of a cross-border passport mechanism facilitating the effective functioning of the internal market in a wide variety of securities. we cannot forget that the differentiation of approaches leads to a fragmentation of the internal market. i therefore consider it necessary that the rules on disclosure in the event of an offer to the public or admission to trading on a regulated market take the same legal form as those laid down in a regulation, in order to ensure that the provisions imposing direct obligations on those involved are made in a uniform manner. i am voting in favour of this report because i also believe that this regulation will increase confidence in the transparency of markets across the union, reduce regulatory complexity and the costs of research and compliance for businesses.

in writing. ‒ in this legislative resolution, parliament gives its approval to the conclusion of the agreement with the member states of the community for the development of southern africa (botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, south africa and swaziland). this agreement seeks to increase cooperation with this region of africa. it contains provisions to promote trade and development, promote regional integration, and contains clauses on respect for the values and monitoring of the implementation of the agreement. however, this agreement poses a threat to the spanish agricultural sector, especially citrus, because of the unfair competition it allows and the lack of reciprocity. i share the objectives of encouraging interregional cooperation and helping the economic growth of southern africa, but not without transparency, at the expense of the spanish agricultural sector and without taking into account its demands and its possible impact, nor of providing for compensatory measures.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of a report opposing the eu-turkey agreement and the readmission scheme proposed by the commission as part of its human rights-abusing migration policy. we share the criticism of the member states for their petty behaviour in accepting people in need of international protection on their territory and the need to act in co-responsibility with greece and italy in dealing with the greatest humanitarian crisis in europe since the second world war with sufficient resources and in a spirit of solidarity.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur and the rapporteurs for their work and commitment to reaching an agreement on the provisional measures for italy and greece in the area of asylum. i also supported the amendment concerning the fact that many applicants in need of international protection currently in these two countries cannot benefit from the relocation scheme as they are subject to regulation (eu) no 604/2013 and support the idea that member states should apply without delay the right to family reunification provided for in that regulation and thus expedite vulnerable cases to allow for reunification as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ decision 2015/1601 indicated that refugees were to be relocated from italy and greece to the territory of other member states. so far, the member states have not managed to mobilise the planned resettlement places. the need for member states to fulfil their obligations and the resettlement agreement to be respected is therefore present. it is imperative that member states respond in solidarity to the challenge posed by the refugee crisis as a basis for developing a genuine european asylum system. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ we are faced with a proposal which does not question the root of the current situation of migrants or face the logic of a fortress europe. however, a whole series of concrete measures are being proposed to improve the situation of these people. the abolition of the shameful eu-turkey agreement or the extension of the right to asylum to more nationalities, in accordance with the geneva convention which the eu does not comply with today, are elements that we value very positively. we also share the need to overcome the current quota system, which has failed because of the lack of political will on the part of the states, and to impose a system which is really based on solidarity and on freedom of movement and the right of choice of the asylum seeker himself. that is why, although it is not the model of migration policy which we are advocating, we voted in favour of the report, in the understanding that this proposal would bring tangible improvements in the situation of people who are forced to flee their countries.
in writing. ‒ this resolution concerns the application of the migrants' relocation plan throughout the european union. this relocation, presented as aid to italy and greece, is aimed primarily at forcing the member states and the peoples of europe to take in asylum seekers, even if they are in most cases economic refugees. the european commission therefore wants to use 54 000 of the 120 000 places in the relocation plan agreed by the european heads of state in september 2015. the plan provides for the start of relocation - distribution among member states as of 26 september 2016. unfortunately, this is not all, since the agreement concluded on 18 march between the european union and turkey provides for the resettlement of one syrian to one of the member states for every syrian readmitted by turkey. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body. i therefore voted against this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because so far the member states have mobilised only 7% of the relocation places planned. as of 5 july, only 793 persons from italy and 2033 from greece had been effectively resettled. the commission, in its first report on relocation and resettlement of 16 march 2016, states that member states need to achieve a monthly relocation rate of at least 5,680 persons in order to meet their relocation obligations within the envisaged two-year timeframe. the report stresses the need for member states to fully assume their obligations in the field of relocation in order to help alleviate the pressure on frontline member states under the decisions taken last year. responsible member states where resettlement should take place should rapidly and substantially increase their efforts to respond to the existing humanitarian situation. it is imperative that member states respond in solidarity to the challenge posed by the refugee crisis as a basis for developing a genuine european asylum system.

in writing. we voted in favour of a report opposing the eu-turkey agreement and the readmission scheme proposed by the commission as part of its human rights-abusing migration policy. we share the criticism of the member states for their petty behaviour in accepting people in need of international protection on their territory and the need to act in co-responsibility with greece and italy in dealing with the greatest humanitarian crisis in europe since the second world war with sufficient resources and in a spirit of solidarity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour as the eu system (highly costly and scarcely effective) to enforce the return of irregular migrants seems not to be sustainable in the long term. for instance, in 2014 less than 40% of the total number of return decisions issued by member states have been enforced. however, the establishment of a dedicated eu travel document for irregular migrants for the purpose of removal will not ensure an automatic increase in the effectiveness of returns and no impact assessment was carried out by the european commission in the context of this proposed regulation to prove otherwise.
in writing. ‒ this proposal aims to improve european council decision 2015/1601 on the relocation of persons in need of international protection from italy and greece. within the framework of the existing commitments forming part of eu-turkey cooperation in the area of migration, the proposal responds to the need for further action in favour of resettlement in turkey. the 54,000 places provided for relocation will be available for the relocation of syrian nationals from turkey to the eu through the 1-1 scheme. under this amendment, member states can implement their commitments by admitting syrian nationals into their territories directly from turkey. the number of syrians relocated will be deducted from the fixed resettlement quotas and each of the countries using this route will receive 6,500 euros. given the increased efficiency of the process that these measures imply, i thought it appropriate to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ we abstained on this report because we considered it a matter of priority that the content of the report should be taken into account by the council in a binding manner and not as an appendix without any effect. we consider the content of the report to be generally positive and most of the recommendations are positive, but we find that special emphasis is placed on the promotion of entrepreneurship in contrast to the recommendations on how to reduce longterm unemployment and ensure quality work. as we do not oppose any part of the report and as the committee's amendments cannot be voted on separately, we shall abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution in which parliament denounces the lack of attention paid by the council in october last year to its proposals, adopting guidelines which completely ignored any of the recommendations made by parliament a short time before, an approach which is contrary to the spirit of the treaties and which weakens cooperation between the institutions of the union. parliament expressed its concern about the achievement of the objectives of the 2020 strategy, in particular the employment and social protection objectives and the education objectives, with particular attention to the growing divergences between different countries. the resolution also stresses the need to introduce the social dimension, alongside the financial and fiscal dimension, into the european semester process in order to improve the results of macroeconomic policies in the social field.
in writing. ‒ in this case, i have spoken in favour of the amendments to the eu proposal tabled by the employment committee because, despite their shortcomings, they at least broaden the focus to passive employment policies and macroeconomic policies to combat the current mass unemployment. the commission proposal, which i voted against, is nothing more than a battering ram to reduce social benefits and pensions and to blame workers for their unemployment situation - positions serious enough that i did not vote for the final resolution.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a council decision aims to stimulate demand for labour, improve labour supply and skills and the functioning of labour markets. it also aims to improve the quality and performance of education and training systems at all levels, and to ensure social justice. therefore, these guidelines are in line with the main objectives of europe 2020, which are, inter alia, to raise the employment rate for women and men aged 20 to 64 to 75% by 2020; to reduce the school drop-out rate to below 10%; to increase the proportion of 30 to 34-year-olds completing higher education or equivalent to at least 40%; and to promote social inclusion, in particular through poverty reduction.
in writing. ‒ we abstained on this report because we considered it a matter of priority that the content of the report should be taken into account by the council in a binding manner and not as an appendix without any effect. we consider the content of the report to be generally positive and most of the recommendations are positive, but we find that special emphasis is placed on the promotion of entrepreneurship in contrast to the recommendations on how to reduce longterm unemployment and ensure quality work. since we do not oppose any part of the report and the committee's amendments cannot be voted on separately, we shall abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that last year the council adopted guidelines for employment policies which completely ignored any of the recommendations made by parliament a few months earlier. the report also expresses parliament's concern about the achievement of the 2020 strategy objectives, especially the employment and social protection objectives, as well as the education objectives, with particular attention to the growing divergences between different countries. the report also includes the need to introduce the social dimension, at the same level as the financial and fiscal dimension, into the european semester process with a view to improving the results of macroeconomic policies in the social field. it also literally reintroduces the position expressed by parliament on 8 july, as a way of reiterating the role that parliament must play in this institutional framework of the union.
in writing. ‒ in this case, i have spoken in favour of the amendments to the eu proposal tabled by the employment committee because, despite their shortcomings, they at least broaden the focus to passive employment policies and macroeconomic policies to combat the current mass unemployment. the commission proposal, which i voted against, is nothing more than a battering ram to reduce social benefits and pensions and to blame workers for their unemployment situation - positions serious enough that i did not vote for the final resolution.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to strengthen cooperation between national parliaments, as well as with the social partners and civil society representatives on employment. the employment guidelines cover the economic and labour market sectors. the adoption of this report is important as these guidelines boost labour demand, improve labour supply, skills and the functioning of labour markets, ensure equity, combat poverty and promote equal opportunities. for the reasons described above, i vote in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ my support for the proposals made by this parliament to improve the guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. this is an important decision at a time when, after years of crisis which have done so much damage to job creation, the eu needs to take action to help ensure that throughout europe measures are taken to ensure harmonious development which leaves no one behind, including the most vulnerable sections of our society.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution in which parliament denounces the lack of attention paid by the council in october last year to its proposals, adopting guidelines which completely ignored any of the recommendations made by parliament a short time before, an approach which is contrary to the spirit of the treaties and which weakens cooperation between the institutions of the union. parliament expressed its concern about the achievement of the objectives of the 2020 strategy, in particular the employment and social protection objectives and the education objectives, with particular attention to the growing divergences between different countries. the resolution also stresses the need to introduce the social dimension, alongside the financial and fiscal dimension, into the european semester process in order to improve the results of macroeconomic policies in the social field.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which contains a number of guidelines for the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), to be held in johannesburg, south africa, from 24 september to 5 october. all the guidelines are designed to meet environmental objectives and promote sustainable development policies. poaching and the alarming situation of elephants and tigers are other highlights. cites' main objective is to ensure that international trade in wild animals and plants does not endanger their existence. from its creation in 1963 to the present day, you can see how the species have declined while trade has increased. it is therefore all the more necessary to stress that only international cooperation between the various governments will make it possible to combat illegal trade, the mafia and to protect wild animals and plants. we are facing a global trade that knows no borders, and therefore all the actors involved must have a determined will to put an end to this practice that constantly threatens our environment.
in writing. ‒ we have voted in favour of the key objectives for the 17th meeting of the cites committee in johannesburg as the union's accession to cites is fundamental; considers it a key step to ensure that the eu can achieve the wider objectives of its environmental policies and the regulation of international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, promoting the sustainable development policies of the un 2030 agenda.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this resolution on the key objectives for the 17th meeting of the conference of the parties to cites in johannesburg. it welcomes the accession of the eu to cites and considers such accession as a key step to ensure that the union can achieve the wider objectives of its environmental policies and the regularisation of international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora by promoting the sustainable development policies of the united nations 2030 agenda.
in writing. ‒ wildlife trafficking has become the fourth largest black market after drugs, human trafficking and the arms market. the eu is a major transit and destination market for illegal trade in wildlife of birds, turtles, reptiles and plant species that are subject to high levels of protection under the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). an increasing number of illegally traded exotic species are kept as pets in the eu. in view of the 17th meeting of the conference of the parties to cites, i voted in favour of this resolution which calls, among other things, for more measures to combat corruption and tackle organised crime involved in wildlife trafficking, more effective measures to combat illegal trade, the full use of effective sanctions, and joint international cooperation and the highest conservation status (cites, annex i) for african elephants, so as to send a strong political signal for an indefinite ban on ivory trade in the future.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this joint resolution of all parliamentary groups in the environment committee of the european parliament as it makes several positive recommendations for the forthcoming conference of the parties (cop) on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) to be held in south africa. since the text emphasizes the importance of transparency in decision-making and in the adoption of measures to combat wildlife trafficking and to combat corruption and trafficking in hunting trophies, with particular emphasis on measures to protect the african lion, the folidoto or the white rhino, i have voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ cites is an international convention whose object is the protection of fauna and flora, in particular protected species. france is of course a signatory to this convention, as are all the other member states of the union. the objectives of the union are certainly laudable, but this text takes advantage of the good intentions to further undermine the sovereignty of the states by substituting the union for the member states in this convention, which was not the case until now. beyond the attack on our sovereignty, this substitution will not increase in efficiency. on the contrary, the fauna and flora are so diverse that the state is precisely the right scale for action. the danger to many species and the inefficiency, if not the nuisance, of european policies convinced me to vote against this text.

in writing. ‒ this report reviews the implementation of the postal services directive, adopted in 1997 and amended in 2002 and 2008. the commission's preliminary work has enabled us to include in the text a number of important points advocating a universal, accessible, long-term sustainable public postal service capable of maintaining quality jobs. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the european union, including the countries of central and eastern europe, the former soviet union and the former soviet union. so, to reflect the balance between the positive and negative points of the report, we have abstained.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work on this own-initiative report on the implementation of the postal directive, which is always conflicting because of the different systems in the member states. it promotes universal service by enhancing the independence of national regulatory authorities, allowing fair competition with well-defined access, quality of services and user needs. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the internal market. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ parliament's response to the commission's report on the implementation of the postal services directive five years after its entry into force. the report is positive and concludes that, despite the crisis and the fall of the letter-mail market by electronic substitution, the directive and the single postal service are functioning relatively well. the main contribution concerns the regulation of the parcel sector which is not covered by the postal services directive, an area on which the commission has submitted a proposal for a regulation. the report proposes a balance between free competition, consumer demands, the sustainability of the universal service and its financing, and the preservation of jobs. the postal sector is called upon to ensure the sustainability of universal service, with low prices for consumers but at the same time high quality, with fast 'track and trace' services open to all operators, transparent commercial services to all other operators and at the same time with workers with good working conditions, trained and guaranteed stable employment. for these reasons, i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this report is positioned in such a way that the liberalisation of postal services appears to be more or less inevitable. so, although it contains a whole series of recommendations on the improvement of working conditions and the protection of the universal service, with which i could agree, it serves in essence to legitimize the reforms which have allowed the terrible degradation of working standards in the postal sector, the ruin of public operators and the loss of quality in the service to the final customer. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ good postal services are a vital part of communication in the eu's internal market. the eu postal sector remains a key factor for social, economic and territorial cohesion and for the development of the digital single market. affordable and reliable postal and parcel delivery remains crucial for the single market. the 2008 postal services review achieved the objectives of the liberalisation of european postal services. in this regard, in february 2008, the european parliament and the council adopted directive 2008/6/ec, which introduced the legal basis for the completion of the internal market for postal services and provided the final legislative step in the process of gradual market opening. the third postal services directive also strengthens the roles and powers of national authorities
in writing. ‒ postal services are facing increased competition from the development of online shopping, which has revolutionized the market by introducing new players such as parcel delivery companies. the aim of this report is to promote greater competition in this sector, in order to increase growth. the report thus aims to bring domestic prices in the member states closer to international prices by raising domestic prices to compensate for the fall in international prices. this proposal is surprising, given that the fight against greenhouse gas emissions is presented as a priority by the european institutions. the report also claims to defend universal service, i.e. the minimum public service, but at the same time it opposes the public subsidies necessary to maintain this service. the report also calls on the commission to combat social dumping and poor wage conditions in the postal services, but without questioning the intensified competition which is precisely what is driving the massive use of precarious contracts, posted workers and even clandestine workers. i therefore voted against this report which does not provide any real solutions to the contemporary problems of postal services, particularly in social matters.

in writing. ‒ the overall objective of this own-initiative report is to address specific issues related to crossborder parcel services and to present parliament's opinion on amending the postal services directive. parliament reiterated the importance of more efficient functioning of markets, increasing the consistency of regulatory supervision of parcel markets and promoting competition. it also stresses the need to increase price transparency in order to reduce unjustified price differences and the fees paid by individuals and small businesses, especially in remote areas. i am voting in favour of this report because i agree with the guidelines set out here. at imco, as the epp rapporteur on the legislative report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on crossborder parcel services, i will be working to achieve these objectives. we need new legislation to develop the digital single market and increase cross-border e-commerce and digital inclusion. more and better europe for business is about regenerating jobs and growth.

in writing. ‒ smes are a key component of the european economy and a key lever for its effective recovery. to make this possible, the union must support smes by supporting their creation and growth, guaranteeing their access to capital and their internationalisation. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which contains a detailed list of measures to boost european smes. in the present situation, in order to continue to advance the project of european integration in a federal way and to defeat the resurgence of nationalisms which would condemn europe to repeat the nightmares of the past, the union needs to regain the confidence of broad sections of society, in particular that of the entire working class, including precarious workers, and the small selfemployed. it is essential that the european economy, in which smes play a key role, grows sustainably and creates quality jobs. this report can help to achieve this objective, together with an extension of the investment plan for europe, which must be endowed with new own resources and the capacity to issue european public debt in order to double the available financing.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report on access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises. we believe that the approach he advocates, based on the consolidation and expansion of the capital markets union, is wrong and harmful. firstly, because it has not been demonstrated that liberalization of access to the capital market in any way reduces the cost of financing for smes. secondly, because we think that you are wrong in your diagnosis, since access to finance is not the main problem facing smes today, but rather the low level of demand.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report on access to finance for smes and increasing the diversity of sme finance in a capital markets union. smes and midcaps are an important part of the eu economy and in this context access to finance is, and must remain, a key issue on the political agenda. it is important that such funding is provided throughout the life cycle of the sme, where the transfer of activities is an important step for an enterprise and where appropriate measures should be taken to support smes in preparing for the transfer of activities that entails tax incentives.

in writing. ‒ the objective of this report is to increase the diversity of sme financing in a capital markets union. while it is inclined to continue to encourage the bank credit channel for financing smes, it supports measures that can be taken to improve its effectiveness. i believe it is important to diversify the financing options for smes in order to allow them to be better connected with other financing options. some of the key elements reflected in the report are improving the public availability of financial information on smes, reviving the securitisation market, simplifying listing on the stock exchange, collective microfinance or peer-to-peer lending. i also believe that we must strive for a fair and simple tax system, which guarantees a level playing field for all companies, because this is the best way to guarantee the development of smes. given the importance of smes, both as job creators and as a key part of the industrial and economic fabric of the eu, i support the adoption of this report.
in writing. ‒ in the eu we need to do more to ensure access to finance for smes and to increase the diversity of sme finance in a capital markets union. the crisis has reduced the access of these companies to bank loans, which must be solved and other complementary sources of financing must also be sought, as we propose in the resolution i have supported.
in writing. ‒ smes are a key component of the european economy and a key lever for its effective recovery. to make this possible, the union must support smes by supporting their creation and growth, guaranteeing their access to capital and their internationalisation. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which contains a detailed list of measures to boost european smes. in the present situation, in order to continue to advance the project of european integration in a federal way and to defeat the resurgence of nationalisms which would condemn europe to repeat the nightmares of the past, the union needs to regain the confidence of broad sections of society, in particular that of the entire working class, including precarious workers, and the small selfemployed. it is essential that the european economy, in which smes play a key role, grows sustainably and creates quality jobs. this report can help to achieve this objective, together with an extension of the investment plan for europe, which must be endowed with new own resources and the capacity to issue european public debt in order to double the available financing.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report on access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises. we believe that the approach he advocates, based on the consolidation and expansion of the capital markets union, is wrong and harmful. firstly, because it has not been demonstrated that liberalization of access to the capital market in any way reduces the cost of financing for smes. secondly, because we think that you are wrong in your diagnosis, since access to finance is not the main problem facing smes today, but rather the low level of demand.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because the proposals it proposes will not solve the problem of access to finance for smes, but will expose them more to the risks of financial speculation. the report points out the difficulties faced by european smes in accessing credit, but instead of proposing a sound retail banking system to finance these types of businesses, which form the backbone of the european economy, it argues that the solution must be the capital market union. this proposal will only increase the risk borne by smes dependent on complex financial products of a speculative nature. it is because this report does not propose solutions for smes but for financial capital that i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report on access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises. we believe that the approach he advocates, based on the consolidation and expansion of the capital markets union, is wrong and harmful. firstly, because it has not been demonstrated that liberalization of access to the capital market in any way reduces the cost of financing for smes. secondly, because we think that you are wrong in your diagnosis, since access to finance is not the main problem facing smes today, but rather the low level of demand.
in writing. ‒ the access of smes to the capital markets is a fundamental step to increase the potential economic growth of europe and its resilience to global shocks. the eu is still too dependent on banking credit and it must move forward with the capital markets union in order to improve this situation.

in writing. ‒ this report provides a wealth of excellent recommendations for better exploiting the job creation potential of smes. that is why i voted for it. i would like to highlight some of the recommendations, such as the growing importance of self-employment and micro-enterprises, which are of fundamental importance in boosting innovation and entrepreneurship, and the disproportionately higher administrative burden on self-employed people and micro-enterprises. the report also highlights the important value of cooperatives and social enterprises, which provide employment for more than 14 million people, representing approximately 6.5% of the eu's workforce. it also proposes a favourable tax treatment for smes and a regulatory framework to encourage investment in smes and social enterprises.
in writing. ‒ this report seeks to identify the problems that hinder smes from achieving an effective growth rate and creating jobs. the report focuses largely on reducing 'administrative burdens' on smes and, although improved in the employment committee with some progressive content, its basic premise remains neoliberal: that laws and regulations, including workers' pay and working conditions, health and safety, are administrative burdens and must be reduced in order to promote growth. although he does not directly call for the elimination or reduction of minimum wage standards, he says that "high labour costs" are one of the most important constraints on job creation in the sme sector. it implicitly calls for an exemption from regulatory rules for smes and suggests a move from direct to indirect taxation, which is clearly regressive. it also stresses the importance of temporary employment in the sme sector and 'urges the commission and the member states to support all forms of temporary employment'. that is why we voted against.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work on this report on how best to harness the job creation potential of smes. we must identify what we mean by false selfemployed, as this growing phenomenon is a cause for concern. the administrative burden on the selfemployed and micro-enterprises must be reduced, as they are often overwhelmed by bureaucracy.
in writing. ‒ small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are the backbone of the european economy, accounting for 99% of enterprises and 67% of employment. a proper regulatory framework, access to finance and skills are key to ensuring its momentum and the creation of stable and quality employment. thanks to the work of the s&d group, the report emphasises the need to boost social protection and occupational health and the creation of quality jobs, as well as tackling the problems of precarious work, the so-called self-employed, unfair competition and wage and employment inequalities between men and women. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because its aim is to reduce the labour protection of workers in smes and the selfemployed, including employees and the pseudo-selfemployed, under the mantra of improving their competitiveness. in this way, smes are used to open a gap in the interests of big capital against the working class. i believe, on the contrary, that the problems of smes (lack of demand caused by falling wages and public spending; extreme volatility and financial dependence caused by the growing power of the banking oligopoly) should serve to create an alliance with the popular classes to put an end to neoliberal policies.
in writing. ‒ migration flows and the high unemployment rate are challenges that must be overcome by strengthening the conditions for job creation in all the central and peripheral member states of the union. the european economic structure is based mainly on small and medium-sized enterprises as a source of new jobs and a driving force of the economy; smes should therefore be the focal point in shaping the union's enterprise policy, and all necessary measures should be taken to strengthen the job creation potential of this sector on the basis of an in-depth diagnosis of existing constraints. this report provides an analysis of the problem - both at eu and national level - to tap the job creation potential of smes in the european union. the commitments proposed by the rapporteur are in line with the promotion of the conditions for the development of smes and the reduction of administrative bodies, as well as the burdens and difficulties experienced by smes.
in writing. ‒ with unemployment remaining at historically high levels, the european union is beginning to recognise the contribution of smes to job creation. over the last ten years, smes have created 85% of new jobs in europe. it is therefore vital to help smes by removing the obstacles to their development. these include inadequate or inappropriate vocational training, uncertain regulations, administrative overload and taxation. the report also stresses the importance of addressing the financing problems of smes and ensuring a level playing field with large enterprises. the report also calls for better tax treatment of smes. the multinationals are currently the beneficiaries of preferential treatment, particularly in france, where they pay less corporation tax. i regret, however, the dubious references to the promotion of labour mobility and especially to the integration of migrants into the labour market. despite these marginal references, the text correctly identifies the problems faced by smes and proposes some solutions to overcome them. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it must ensure fair competition, access to finance, an appropriate regulatory framework, s.xxi skills and good social dialogue in order to enable smes to create quality and sustainable jobs. the report introduces elements such as social protection and occupational health, social economy enterprises and cooperatives, quality job creation, the problems of precarious work, letterbox companies, the self-employed, unfair competition and wage and employment inequalities between men and women, the fight against tax evasion and the shadow economy, the impact of trade agreements on workers' rights, wages and jobs, or the impact of the digital single market. the reference to 'unjustified burdens' for smes instead of simply burdens is also retained. in addition, support has been given to the focus on the potential of smes, 21st century skills, dual education and continuing training to overcome skills shortages, access to finance and support for smes (including european funds and programmes), corporate social responsibility and specific support for young entrepreneurs.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this own-initiative report is to boost job creation and the workforce: through a favourable and stable regulatory framework, facilitating access to finance, with an investment plan for europe, with public procurement, improving investment and innovation capacity and fostering the digital economy. in this report we stress the need for a regulatory framework that encourages investment while promoting sustainable economic growth and quality employment. i believe that one of the key factors which can influence the competitiveness of smes is labour costs, but unemployment should not be tackled at the expense of protecting workers, but by increasing the value of training as a necessary element in preparing the working population to take up jobs, and by adapting the demand and supply of labour. finally, i would stress that we must reduce the administrative burden of regulation, as it is disproportionately higher for the selfemployed and micro-enterprises than for larger enterprises. for all the reasons stated above, i vote in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ as the engine of our economy, smes play a key role in job creation and we, the institutions, must do everything we can to facilitate business development and increase their job creation potential. i support the report on how best to exploit the job creation potential of small and mediumsized enterprises, which should serve as a reference for the commission to establish immediate measures to provide an appropriate framework for the growth of these enterprises and their protection in order to ensure a level playing field with respect to large enterprises.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it assesses the implementation of the employment equality directive since its adoption and draws up recommendations for further improvements in the future. it takes a balanced approach to the most important aspects, such as discrimination on grounds of sex, racial or ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. it also stresses that although some member states have gone further in implementing the requirements of the directive, and that europeans are tolerant of groups at risk of discrimination and are also better informed about their rights, challenges to the implementation of the directive still exist. the s&d amendments strengthened aspects relating to age and disability discrimination, on reporting, data collection, multiple discrimination, continuing training and apprenticeship. a paragraph on work-life balance (maternity, carers, paternity leave) was also added, and another defending the 'quality' of employment for people with disabilities and the elimination of discriminatory language against migrants and refugees.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the weber report on the implementation of the employment equality directive. in the face of those who insist on denying fundamental human rights on the pretext of the principle of subsidiarity, insist on the idea that human rights are universal and indivisible. we must move forward with european rules that regulate and prohibit discrimination on grounds of sex, religion or race. the prohibitions on certain religious symbols are not always in line with international human rights standards, as they are not limited to well-defined and delimited circumstances or pursue a legitimate aim. states do not always take appropriate action against these restrictions when they are not in accordance with international human rights standards. in the face of prohibitions, freedom of speech. in the face of intolerance, education and promotion of diversity and mutual respect.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report as it is positive in that it identifies the main problems and challenges in the implementation of the directive and proposes recommendations to the commission and the member states, with which we agree, to eliminate discrimination on grounds of sex, religion, belief, disability, age or sexual orientation and to ensure equal treatment in employment. amongst others, some highlights that we find very positive are: the commission's presentation of a directive on carers' leave; an improvement and mainstreaming of available data on equality, including harmonised and homogeneous statistics; providing ongoing training for stakeholders on employment legislation; strengthening and supporting civil society organisations working in this area; measures to make the private sector take responsibility for creating an environment free of discrimination; the adoption of a european framework of national strategies to combat anti-semitism and islamophobia; recognising social clauses in public contracts or the effective enforcement of legislation (ged review) to ensure the protection of trans people, amongst others.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report assessing the implementation of the employment equality directive as it recognises and identifies the fundamental problems in the implementation of this directive, such as the lack of data on equality, the lack of information and support for victims, or the barriers to access to justice and redress in the event of breaches of the directive. the report also makes a number of recommendations which i consider to be positive, such as the need to adopt a european framework to combat islamophobia at national level, among other things, or the need for member states to implement legislation to ensure the protection of transgender people, as well as to enable mutual recognition of all types of unions, marital arrangements and parental rights. in supporting these recommendations, my vote has been in favour.
in writing. ‒ the employment equality directive, which was adopted 15 years ago, is key legislation to ensure equality and combat discrimination in employment. since then, the situation has improved a lot, although it is far from ideal, especially for some groups such as the disabled. the report proposes appropriate measures to combat discrimination in the workplace against these people. in addition, the use of the european structural and investment funds should play an important role in achieving greater equality and employment inclusion for these people, for example by adapting workplaces, implementing universal design, providing the necessary assistance and advice at work, improving education and training and creating programmes targeted at companies that employ people with disabilities.

in writing. ‒ we consider that, with regard to the first part of amendment no 21, it is precisely the principle of subsidiarity applied to the states and social intermediary bodies which generally guarantees compliance with international human rights standards, which are otherwise difficult to apply, at least until a supranational justice system is fully effective. without prejudice to the need to promote a balance between the unity of human rights and the diversity of the cultural and political contexts in which they are applied, we believe that states and employers may indeed retain legitimate reasons for banning symbols which are patently oppressive and which cannot be excused in their religious nature. with regard to the second part of the amendment, although it does not clearly specify the criteria by which certain symbols repress women's rights, which may give rise to some misinterpretations, we consider that the risk that the text will be used today to justify the repression of symbols legitimately protected by religious freedom is significantly lower than the risk that the text will abstain on the need to repress the public use of oppressive symbols, or that it will pose obvious security problems.
