in writing. ‒ we have promoted and voted for this resolution on syria because of the worsening humanitarian situation, especially in the aleppo region. and because of the resounding failure of the truce agreed between the united states and russia which has been operational for only a few days. the latest attacks by syrian government forces on aleppo. these operations are pushing away the hope of a real ceasefire. the war crimes allegations that have been made against russia in the security council focus on the widespread use of anti-bunker bombs and firebombs on the 275,000 civilians living in eastern aleppo. aleppo will go down in history as a shameful place like dresden, gernika or sarajevo. we must put an end to this destruction which is already practically total. despite all this, the only way out for syria now is to renegotiate, to put down the weapons and to secure humanitarian corridors so that relief can reach the civilian population. that's the most important thing right now. the union must become even more involved in these two priorities.
in writing. ‒ this resolution is another example of the unidirectional propaganda campaign we are engaged in, which presents us with a single 'guilty gang', russia and the syrian government, a rather hypocritical stance when some member states of the union, in collaboration with the usa, trained and financed terrorist groups operating in the middle east and europe. the us strategy of unilateralism and the eu's accomplice foreign policy have already had consequences in the case of libya. we have to decide whether we want to return to that path, or whether we want to position ourselves as a facilitator of dialogue and political resolution of the conflict. the union must demand that the united states resume dialogue with russia in the context of the conflict in syria in order to bring about a ceasefire that will give way to a negotiating table for peace with all non-terrorist political actors. we must not forget that the failure of the last truce was the cause of the us bombing of syrian army positions in deir azzor. as long as the european parliament's resolutions continue to present a single culprit in the conflict, and continue to evade its own responsibility in the conflict, i will vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution welcoming the eu's emergency humanitarian initiative for aleppo, which, in addition to mobilising funds to meet urgent humanitarian needs, aims to ensure the medical evacuation of the wounded and sick, in particular women, children and the elderly, from the eastern part of aleppo. it is now essential to consolidate the cessation of hostilities agreed in september by the us and russia. if it is achieved, it will be possible to allow humanitarian aid access to the whole country. the international community, represented by the united nations, must be involved in this process. their role is essential in facilitating this dialogue. i therefore support the work being carried out by the unsg special envoy for syria, mr de mistura. i would like to end by highlighting paragraph 3 of the resolution, which calls on all parties to the conflict, and in particular on russia and the assad regime, to stop all attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, to take credible and immediate steps to end hostilities, to lift all sieges and to allow unhindered access for humanitarian organisations to people in need.
in writing. ‒ despite supporting the bulk of the content of this resolution on syria, which calls on all parties to cease bombing, open humanitarian corridors and reopen negotiations for a ceasefire, podemos voted abstention, considering that the resolution lacks the intended equidistance, pointing out greater responsibilities to one of the parties in the conflict and, therefore, placing the debate in the key of a bipolar choice between two powers to which we oppose from our conviction that it must be the syrian civil society that leads the way towards peace, democracy and social justice that none of the parties in conflict seems to be interested in achieving.

mr president, i abstained on the proposals for cop 22 because they do not seem ambitious enough for the marrakesh meeting. but i would like to address this house to warn of another element which should not go unnoticed, and that is the propaganda use being made of this event, cop 22, by the moroccan regime, trying to give itself an international pedigree and a green halo with which to conceal its occupation of the saharawi people. as parliamentarians we must not forget that the host of cop 22 is responsible for the expulsion of minurso, the violation of the ceasefire in guerguerat, the repression of sahrawi protesters in the occupied territories. let not prudence make us cowards before our hosts. i would like to end by remembering the prisoners of gdeim izik, who are now illegally confined in rabat after six years of torture, harassment and ill-treatment for demanding a right which morocco must respect if it is to become a respected member of the international community. and it is the right of the saharawi people to self-determination.

in writing. ‒ i have decided to abstain from voting on this report because, although i believe that the ratification of the paris agreement by each member state is essential to ensure the fight against climate change, i believe that this report is only a first step. the paris agreement is totally inadequate to achieve the long-term objective it sets itself: not to exceed 2°c of temperature rise by the end of this century. the report is based on false solutions such as the emission trading system (ets) whose exchange of emission bonds contributes to the financialization of nature and allows the one who pays more to pollute more. the redd+ system also puts biodiversity at risk and leads to land grabs that endanger indigenous peoples. this report is only a first step in this struggle, since it leaves out important issues such as the modification of the production and agri-food system. the paris agreement makes no mention of agriculture. industrial agriculture is among the main drivers of anthropogenic climate change, and at the same time climate change is one of the biggest food security problems i was.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution, considering that the fight against global warming cannot be seen as an obstacle to economic growth but, on the contrary, should be seen as a stimulus to generate new economic growth and new jobs that are sustainable. the ratification and entry into force of the paris agreement is a very important step in this direction, but we must continue to work towards the objectives set to mitigate the effects of climate change, which is why the preparation of the one conference in marrakech is of great importance. we need to move forward with the negotiations and respect the commitments made under the paris agreement, in particular those relating to the union's contribution to mitigation and adaptation, as well as its support in the form of financing, technology transfer and capacity building.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution which aims to define the european parliament's position in view of the cop22 climate conference in marrakech, morocco, in november. the proposal addresses issues such as the urgency to ratify and implement the paris agreement, pre-2020 ambition and the kyoto protocol, priority negotiation points at cop22, the role of non-state actors, the global effort of all sectors, the reduction of non-co2 emissions, climate finance, climate resilience through adaptation and climate diplomacy, among others. the resolution welcomes the paris agreement as a historic achievement in the fight against climate change and for multilateralism, as it represents an ambitious, balanced, equitable and legally binding agreement. the resolution also welcomes the commitment of all countries to keep the rise in global average temperature below 2°c compared to pre-industrial levels and to continue efforts to limit the temperature rise to 1.5°c.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution encourages countries to accelerate the transition to zero greenhouse gas emissions to avoid the worst consequences of global warming. it also called on the member states to ensure that the commission's proposals are implemented in a timely manner. the european union, as a leader in the fight against climate change, while well on track to go beyond its 2020 greenhouse gas emission reduction targets and meet its 2020 renewable energy target, must adapt to the requirements of the paris agreement and continue its efforts to reach safe emission limits in the poorest countries, which will be the most affected by climate change because they do not have sufficient resources to prepare for and adapt to the changes that are taking place. i am voting in favour because we are facing a global challenge which requires effective and concrete action, and the union must set an example by immediately setting itself to work towards achieving the objectives mentioned.
in writing. ‒ the historic paris agreement reached in december 2015 was a landmark achievement for the fight against climate change and for multilateralism, representing an ambitious, balanced, equitable and legally binding agreement. the adoption of the agreement and the submission of the envisaged nationally determined contributions by 187 states parties has marked a decisive turning point towards comprehensive and collective global action, and once implemented, will represent a major step in the transition towards a climate resilient and climate neutral global economy. the next climate conference in marrakech will need to address the urgency of ratifying and implementing the paris agreement, the pre-2020 ambition and the kyoto protocol; the details of a global inventory; more guidance on planned nationally determined contributions; a mechanism to facilitate implementation and promote compliance; shaping the 2018 facilitation dialogue, which will be a key opportunity to close the mitigation gap, given current national contributions; and expanding the mobilisation of climate funds to achieve the common goal of usd 100 billion per year by 2020, issues covered in this resolution, which i voted in favour of.

in writing. ‒ the paris agreement is a before and after in the fight against climate change at global level, paving the way towards a low greenhouse gas emissions development model. the implementation of the agreement must be promoted at this stage, and this requires ensuring that climate change is on the political agendas of world leaders beyond cop21. in this sense, cop22 will be a benchmark to integrate the paris agreement with the implementation of concrete actions to combat climate change. the leadership shown by the union in paris must be maintained and, for this, early ratification of the agreement is key in the first place. i have therefore voted in favour of the resolution setting out the european parliament's position in view of the marrakesh conference and calling on the council to approve the paris agreement on behalf of the union without further delay. rapid ratification by its member states will consolidate the union as a leading actor in the fight against climate change.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the union must seek appropriate regulation for all types of materials and articles intended to come into contact with food, including the prohibition of the use of endocrine disruptors and other substances of very high concern. the current union legislation on fcm allows chemicals that are prohibited under other union laws. many substances in materials and articles intended to come into contact with food are not being evaluated. this is the case for so-called 'non-intentionally added substances' (nias), which are impurities of substances intentionally added or substances resulting from chemical reactions (such as decomposition products or by-products formed during the production process), which are present in the finished material. it should also be noted that the european food safety authority (efsa) does not take into account the so-called 'cocktail effect' and multiple exposures (resulting from chemicals - even in low doses - from different sources) in its risk assessment procedure. all of these should be addressed by efsa as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ food contact materials may behave differently and transfer their components to food. in such cases, the chemicals emitted from these materials may endanger human health or adversely affect the composition of food products. action at union level is therefore necessary to address the lack of specific union measures and the shortcomings in risk assessment, traceability, compliance and control. the rapporteur calls on the commission to review the current regulatory framework on the basis of the policy recommendations. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of this report. i think it is important that the union should gradually draw up legislation on this subject. this is a first step and although i do not think it is enough, it does propose specific measures at european level on materials and articles intended to come into contact with foodstuffs such as plastic, ceramics, cellulose, etc. which i think are of paramount importance. the report also mentions the importance of member states being able to take specific measures in cases where european legislation does not mention certain materials that may be considered toxic.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for her work on this report on the application of the regulation on materials and articles intended to come into contact with food. in this case i also voted in favour of an amendment which states that the numerous reassessments by efsa over the last decade have not effectively addressed all health concerns, and that efsa will reassess the risks of bpa again in 2017, following the publication of a report which shows that the current tolerable daily intake does not protect foetuses or infants from the effects of bpa on the immune system and recommends that consumers be advised to reduce their exposure to bpa from food and other sources, and urges that bpa be banned from all food contact materials.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report. food contact materials are used continuously in daily life in the form of packaging, kitchen utensils, tableware, etc. when coming into contact with food, different materials may behave differently and transfer their components to food according to their composition and properties. in such cases, they may endanger human health or adversely affect the composition of foodstuffs. the legislation aims to maintain a high level of consumer protection while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market for products containing materials intended to come into contact with food. one of the main challenges we face is the demand for greater harmonisation in the area of food contact materials (especially non-harmonised materials) by the majority of stakeholders across all sectors. it is also necessary to strengthen and improve the current traceability legislation to ensure the traceability of all materials in contact with food.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of this report. i think it is important that the union should gradually draw up legislation on this subject. this is a first step and although i do not think it is enough, it does propose specific measures at european level on materials and articles intended to come into contact with foodstuffs such as plastic, ceramics, cellulose, etc. which i think are of paramount importance. the report also mentions the importance of member states being able to take specific measures in cases where european legislation does not mention certain materials that may be considered toxic.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the regulation lays down the general safety requirements which apply to all possible materials and articles in contact with food. member states may take specific measures at national level, and some have already done so, for the most widely used materials such as paper and cardboard, metals and alloys, glass, coatings, silicones, rubbers and printing inks. but for some specific materials the specific measures taken by one member state may be different from those of another member state, i.e. different standards for product safety have been created. however, the report highlights that it is essential to adopt specific union measures for the remaining non-harmonised materials, and to improve the reuse and recycling properties of these materials to improve their absorption into the circular economy. testing should be based on uniform standards and the overall 'cocktail effect' of materials should be examined, which would help to identify and prevent the use of endocrine disrupting substances. overall, there is an emphasis on the need to greatly improve traceability measures as well as the implementation and strengthening of controls.

in writing. ‒ this report recalls that regulation no 1935/2004 lays down general requirements to prevent certain materials, when in contact with food, from transferring substances in such quantities as to cause problems for human health or to alter the composition of food or to impair its organoleptic characteristics. to that end, it establishes a list of 17 materials and articles in contact with food which may be subject to specific measures. the problem identified in the report is that only four materials or objects on that list are subject to specific measures by the european union, while the rest are subject to the possibility for member states to adopt national provisions. the legislation on these national measures is therefore disparate and the principle of mutual recognition does not work, so that neither the effective functioning of the internal market nor a significant level of consumer protection can be guaranteed. i am voting in favour of the report because, as it says, greater harmonisation in the european union is needed to address the shortcomings in the application of regulation no 1935/2004.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the implementation of the regulation on materials and articles intended to come into contact with foodstuffs, because the chemicals they emit can sometimes endanger health and adversely affect the composition of foodstuffs. regulation (ec) no 1935/2004 lays down the safety requirements in this respect. annex 1 lists 17 materials for which member states are required to take specific measures, and it is necessary to harmonise such measures in order to avoid obstacles to the internal market. uniform rules should also be laid down as regards the tests to be carried out on those materials.

in writing. ‒ this report presents the european parliament's position on the thirty-second annual report of the commission on monitoring the application of union law. the report states that the correct and timely transposition of union legislation into national law and a clearly defined national legislative framework should be a priority for the member states. in this connection, the importance of improving transposition and the need for member states to clearly communicate and indicate national measures complementing european directives are emphasised. it is emphasised that, in applying union law, member states should refrain from adding unnecessary obstacles to union law. the correct application of the union contributes to strengthening the credibility of the institutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on monitoring the application of union law, which contains very important and interesting information on the effective transposition and practical application of union law. the annual report also underlines that the number of formal infringement procedures has decreased over the past five years. the report, however, points to spain as one of the member states which is most in breach of european legislation. it should be borne in mind that the european commission has received 533 complaints about possible breaches of european regulation in the case of spain. we must therefore urge the spanish government to comply faithfully with european legislation in order to protect the interests of all citizens and groups.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to check whether the european directives have been properly applied in the member states and to take stock of the measures taken against those who have allegedly misapplied them. it therefore attests to a large number of the negative observations we make against the european union: a desire to bring the internal law of each state into line, an obvious interference, retaliatory measures in the event of non-compliance. this report comes from the commission on the enforcement of eu law, for which the sovereignty of nations is not a concern. for these reasons i opposed this report.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this resolution because it contains very positive elements. the resolution calls for strengthening eu law to protect consumer rights, health, the environment, mobility and transport. there are many infringement cases initiated by the commission which are still open, and this report calls for parliament to be able to have appropriate access to this information in order to make the processes more transparent.
in writing. ‒ eh bildu voted in favour of the annual report on monitoring the application of union law, including a separate vote on paragraph 10. despite being a paragraph that eh bildu does not consider completely convincing, our vote was based on the following sentence: ‘stresses the importance of enhancing transposition and the need for member states to provide notification of, and clearly indicate, national measures that supplement european directives.’ the spanish state has often been warned or punished for not implementing eu law correctly. more specifically, the spanish government tried to hide the notification of framework decision 2008/675/jai, after having transposed it more than four years late. thanks to a parliamentary question addressed by josu juaristi mep, we were informed that the spanish government was one year and a half late notifying the transposition law. we have no doubt there is an intentional delay in the notification aiming to avoid the european commission´s analysis of the national law. eh bildu wishes to recall that if the national law complied with this framework decision seven prisoners should be immediately released. eu law is often our only safeguard when dealing with basque politically motivated prisoners and thus we voted in favour of paragraph 10.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which aims to 'monitor monitoring' by the commission, from a political point of view, and the interest in ensuring that legislation adopted in the union actually becomes a reality applied in the member states. the commission's annual report shows that the environment, transport and the internal market and services remain the areas where the highest number of infringements occurred in 2014. according to the report, the number of formally infringing procedures has decreased thanks to the effectiveness of the informal eu pilot procedure procedure. however, the report also points out that, as parliament still has only limited access to information on this procedure and to pending cases, it is difficult to assess to what extent the reduction in formal procedural infringements reflects the true degree of compliance by member states. the report, thanks to the socialists, stresses the joint responsibility of the commission and the member states in the event of improper or incomplete implementation of european legislation.

in writing. ‒ this annual report once again provides interesting information on the effective transposition and practical application of eu law. the report concludes that compliance with eu law is still not sufficiently transparent. parliament considered that the commission should propose, where possible and proportionate, more regulations and fewer directives to ensure a level playing field between member states in legislation, especially in the case of union legislation relating to the single market, bearing in mind also that the form of legal texts should correspond to the aims and objectives of the proposals. the single market is the driving force of the union, and i am voting in favour of this report because i agree with the proposals it makes in this area.
in writing. ‒ one of the major problems of european legislation is its relationship with the laws of the member states. for several years now, the european parliament has been pointing out that one of the biggest problems in the implementation of community legislation is 'gold-plating', which often hinders the objectives that the legislation is intended to achieve. in this report, and in the reports on the application of union law in the years to come, we will continue along this path of denouncing and trying to put an end to this practice by the member states. we also mention some instruments which have proved useful (such as the eu pilot programme), but i think we must not forget that there are still many obstacles to be removed if the application of european legislation is to be precise and effective.
in writing. ‒ under article 17 teu, the commission monitors the actions of member states and ensures that their legislation is in line with european law. articles 258 to 260 tfeu authorise the commission to take action against an infringing member state. the european parliament, in turn, 'monitors the monitoring' of the commission and must ensure that legislation adopted in the eu effectively becomes a reality applied in the member states. this annual report on the application of eu law shows that the environment, transport, the internal market and services remain the areas where the highest number of infringements occur. the number of procedures has decreased thanks to the effectiveness of the eu pilot procedure. however, given that parliament has limited access to information on this procedure and on pending cases, it is difficult to assess to what extent the reduction in formal infringements reflects the true degree of compliance by member states. i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this resolution because it contains very positive elements. the resolution calls for strengthening eu law to protect consumer rights, health, the environment, mobility and transport. there are many infringement cases initiated by the commission which are still open, and this report calls for parliament to be able to have appropriate access to this information in order to make the processes more transparent.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this report because the report concludes that the enforcement of eu law is still not sufficiently transparent and open and that the discretionary power conferred by the treaty upon the commission in dealing with infringement procedures must respect the rule of law, the principle of legal clarity and the requirements of transparency and openness and that nothing must jeopardise the basic purpose of that power, which is to guarantee the timely and correct application of union law. absolute discretion coupled with an absolute lack of transparency is fundamentally contrary to the rule of law. the enforcement of eu law is proclaimed as a priority by this commission, but it is far from being achieved.
in writing. ‒ the new administrative law working party set up within the european parliament's committee on legal affairs has drawn up proposals which, as this report argues, can serve as a valuable inspiration for the commission in monitoring the application of community legislation in the different countries of the union. the report notes, on the basis of the conclusions drawn from the 32nd annual report on the monitoring of the application of union law prepared by the commission, that an initiative to regulate the administration of the union's own administrative procedures would be both useful and feasible to enact. i voted in favour of this resolution because i want to give the european parliament (the only community institution directly elected by the people through their vote) greater access to infringement procedures which the commission initiates against member states, with the aim of assessing the extent to which progress is being made towards better compliance with the acquis communautaire by the 28 or whether, on the contrary, agreements are being reached with them after the rule has been breached.
in writing. ‒ the resolution contains many positive elements, such as the reference to the charter of fundamental rights of the european union in the application of union law or the recognition of organised civil society in the legislative process. i have nevertheless abstained, considering that the application of union law is not a technical but also a political debate: it is not for nothing that legislation relating to the protection of social and civil rights is systematically disregarded, while its application is immediate when it goes against the interests of the working classes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection to the marketing of seeds of genetically modified maize bt11 (tolerant to the toxic herbicide glufosinate ammonium), because i am totally against genetically modified organisms and therefore against new authorizations of them. in addition, the current procedure for authorising genetically modified food and feed is clearly not working properly. i therefore support this and any objection that is put forward in relation to the authorization of gmos, and i have voted accordingly.
in writing. - i am neither for nor against gmos. i'm standing up for science. in the union we have created an agency for this kind of task: the european food safety authority (efsa), which reflects the opinion of independent scientists who monitor and guarantee food safety in the union. just a few months ago, more than a hundred nobel laureates were calling for the conclusions of the competent scientific institutions to be recognised and for the campaigns against genetically modified organisms to be abandoned without sufficient scientific support. the different products must be analysed on a case-by-case basis and the debate must not be generalized or simplified.
in writing. ‒ the use of gm seeds is part of a wider debate, which can be approached from three angles: health, environment and socioeconomic impact. i voted in favour of the objection because when we talk about allowing the marketing of genetically modified seeds we are talking about deepening this unsustainable model of abuse, of royalties, of dependence on agrochemicals; and socially perverse. we know that genetically modified seeds will not be marketed for the benefit of farmers, consumers, society, the environment but for the profit of a giant like monsanto. a giant whose merger with bayer will create a monster whose consequences for the world's food system we are not even able to foresee.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection because genetically modified organisms (gmos) are not succeeding in controlling pests and weeds, but have instead led to the emergence of superpests and superweeds. the new cap objectives include ensuring food security, protecting the environment and ensuring the economic and social vitality of rural areas. it is difficult to justify that the approval of monsanto's gm seeds meets any of these three objectives.

madam president, the vienna agreement on iran's nuclear programme has opened a new stage in that country's relations with the european union and the international community in general. the full implementation of the agreement must remain a priority for us, while its progressive implementation makes it possible to move towards a broader and more constructive bilateral relationship. the verification by the international atomic energy agency allows us today to work on new areas of cooperation and to take advantage of the opportunities that arise, from political dialogue to trade and investment, to energy and the environment. a dialogue in which we must not forget our principles, so human rights must also be present, as you yourself confirmed to us a few minutes ago, commissioner. the importance of iran in the regional context is also clear: its participation is essential in the solution of the various crises currently affecting the middle east. i am referring in particular to the conflict in syria and the fight against daesh. iran must take a more constructive attitude in the pursuit of peace in syria and also in the fight against terrorism; it must use its ascendancy over some of the groups and countries acting in the region to avoid further escalation of regional conflicts. we need iran to contribute to the security of the region and the countries that make it up, including israel. there are no exceptions. iran, on the basis of compliance with the vienna agreement, must continue to continue to win the sympathy of the international community and actively contribute to peace, overcoming religious clashes and struggles for regional hegemony that are tearing the middle east and the muslim community apart.
madam president, commissioner, the agreement with iran is a very important milestone, we agree. but this diplomatic success, ladies and gentlemen, let us not forget, has been achieved by dealing with a state, with a regime of terror. a fundamentalist regime, which continues to carry out systematic executions, which denies the holocaust, which executes children and which also perpetrates torture on a daily basis. i believe in the future of iran because i believe in the iranians. i know very well your love of freedom and your age-old courage and that is why i know that one day you will be free from the tyranny of the clergy. i support the initiative of high representative mogherini and applaud her excellent diplomatic work. but i am absolutely against any form of appeasement as the extreme left, like my podemos colleagues, is trying to propagate. how much money has your leader received from the mullahs? how much funding for television production do you receive each week from a state that funds terrorism? why doesn't your leader denounce the executions and torture in iran? why does your leader not condemn and publicly denounce the systematic violation of women's rights or the atrocious persecution and execution of homosexuals? there are those who are eager to accept the money of the iranian tyranny for their own ends. moreover, some have accepted it to finance their propaganda, but we europeans cannot sell our principles. no, your honours, we cannot.
madam president, the nuclear agreement signed between iran and the members of the un security council in 2015 is very good news. it was good news for international relations. but we have to compare how the weapons of mass destruction were dealt with in iraq - without diplomacy, without listening to the rapporteurs or the un investigators - and what has happened when diplomacy has been launched. it is also good news for the stability of the region and it is good news for nuclear non-proliferation - something that should also apply to israel, which has more than three hundred nuclear warheads, which also violates human rights, and nobody says anything to it. but in this report on the european union's strategy towards iran we are again making the same mistakes that are soiling international relations: we are not calling for the total lifting of the us sanctions - unilateral, extraterritorial sanctions, which also affect european union companies but which affect, above all, the iranian people. to put hezbollah on the same level as al nusra is either crazy or shortsighted. why would you do that? because hezbollah is a political-military organization that is part of the lebanese government has several ministers. and, furthermore, we have not included the political part in these terrorist organizations. and nusra is al qaeda. let's not forget that, please. when it comes to respect for human rights - refugees, asylum seekers - we can agree, but perhaps we should apply it to ourselves first before we give lessons. in short, mr howitt, it is not a bad report but, in my view, it falls short of what should be the basis for a good understanding between sovereign nations.
in writing. the european strategy for natural gas and lng should not be based on replacing coal with another fossil fuel which continues to emit co2 and especially methane, more than 80 times worse than co2 for global warming. the commission has for years sought to impose the use of gas throughout europe as a simple fuel change, inflating consumption forecasts without taking into account the improvement of energy efficiency or the penetration of renewables. this has resulted in over-investment in facilities used at 25% of their capacity in europe. countries like spain have plants that closed the same day they opened. the major climate agreements ratified by the union should be the basis of any energy strategy, where energy efficiency and the use of clean energy should be put ahead of any development of fossil fuel energy sources. natural gas could be a transitional backstop for the entry of renewables into europe's energy mix, but it will become a hindrance to the development of clean energy if it is promoted in a short-term way as a reduction in c02 emissions.

madam president, in the european union there are first-class laws, which the european commission is already ensuring are being complied with, threatening to expel us from the euro area; and there are second-class laws, which can be systematically broken by the member states without anything happening. for example, the first is the stability and growth pact, for which we in the spanish state have been suffering cuts in our public services for more than six years and for which we are now being asked to make a new sacrifice of more than 5 000 million euros. second, or even third, is the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and that is why there can be a 'law of the gag' in the spanish state; that is why there can be hot returns in ceuta and melilla; that is why there can be xenophobic laws in hungary, or restrictions on women's sexual and reproductive rights in poland or ireland; or that is why there can be homophobic laws in lithuania. they are more or less concerned about fundamental rights, and i believe that this is not because of a lack of mechanisms, but because respect for fundamental rights is contrary to their economic and migration policies.

madam president, i would like to thank sophia in 't veld for her realistic and feasible proposal to improve democracy in the union. an objective, independent and open annual report on the subject, as well as preventive and corrective measures, are essential, because there is much to be improved. i believe that with mechanisms of pre-emptive dialogue it would be more difficult for a european government to ignore recommendations from the united nations to compensate victims of its own dictatorship; for an interior minister to conspire to invent criminal cases against political rivals; or for a president to announce to a person on trial for illegally financing the party they share that he will provide him with trusted judges, and for that promise to be fulfilled. mr timmermans, all this is happening today in a member state which, moreover, does not respect basic framework decisions for the creation of a common area of freedom, such as the mutual recognition of sentences, something which could already be corrected with today's mechanisms. i thought in our union these things were impossible. we must at least get them to have some price, and correct them.
mr president, when in states such as spain and others the standards of democracy are manifestly lower than those which the european union advocates and theoretically defends, action is necessary. and this report, although it can be improved, is going in the right direction, for example when it proposes a large independent group of experts to analyse and monitor the member states. but let us not forget that the european institutions are also 'monitorable' and, of course, as my colleague mr spinelli has stressed, social and economic rights. it is time to abandon the double standard 'whether we look outside or inside the union', and the report sets the right course on this point. the same applies when citizens are given access to the court of justice of the european union. any mechanism which improves the functioning of the union in terms of democracy is a step forward. and, mr timmermans, if the present framework worked, this report would not be on your desk today.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the fences of fortress europe do not seem to be enough to stop the migration drama. attempts to reach us are far from diminishing, generating more and more deaths directly related to our border and security policy. a big business of xenophobia, from which the defense industry benefits equally on one side of the border and the human traffickers on the other. the miracle of the multiplication of border controls then takes place, and with them political statements are rooted which link irregular migration with organised crime, terrorism or human trafficking, encouraging punitive populism, as we have seen in this very house. fortress europe is not only a racist project that violates rights and freedoms but also a big business that has grown steadily in recent years: the business of xenophobia, which is fuelled by the security strategies of a europe that looks the other way in the face of this crisis.
mr president, the european union is threatened and must protect itself, it must activate preventive and repressive tools. repression is the way to avoid impunity. the security of europeans must be a priority in the policies of the union. terrorist attacks, organised crime, drug trafficking, money laundering, corruption, trafficking and illicit trafficking present us with deadly scenarios every day which must be faced with determination and subordination to our laws and our guarantees. we have put in place a whole range of instruments and tools - you have all referred to them - from the ectc to the ec3, prüm, pnr, entry and exit, and so on. i believe, however, that the so-called political cycle must be activated and updated immediately. the political cycle is five years old and needs to be updated. ladies and gentlemen, the challenges ahead are linked to the rise of terrorism. the more weakened the terror in the occupied territories and in the failed states, the more it will strike western targets. the security of a member state is the security of the union as a whole. so we must give a global response. but first of all we must tell ourselves the truth: we do not have a common security policy; we do not have an intelligence community; we do not have a common judicial space; we do not have a common defence policy. our borders are vulnerable. we don't have a tftp. long way to go. good luck with that, commissioner.
mr president, the eu has to ensure internal security and has to fight terrorism. this is undeniable, but in a democratic society this can only be done while keeping in mind the main goal of protecting and reinforcing civil liberties and the human rights of citizens. when we do not do so, we are falling into the trap set by terrorism, which plans to have us caught in fear, resentment and diminishing democracy. has the eu really evaluated which of the security initiatives taken against terrorism really work and which do not? i am afraid this has not been done so far. it is urgent to do so. a lot has been said on this during this debate, but i would like to insist that we should only accept more security measures if they mean a better protection of freedom, not a disruption of it.
mr president, i see an advantage in the appointment of commissioner king as security officer - there is already an immigration officer, commissioner avramopoulos - and that is to say that it is quite clear that the false identification that immigration is the cause of insecurity is false and deeply harmful to european integration. because those speeches that you hear here often, in this european parliament, are close to what we hear in the constitutional and political debate in the united states before the elections, starring donald trump, who claims that raising a border or a fence or a barrier against immigration is the guarantee against insecurity, while defending the second amendment, which causes 30,000 deaths a year by firearms in the united states. no, the cause of terrorism in europe does not come from immigration. the terrorism that has hit us hardest in europe was perpetrated by citizens who had european passports, who lived in european capitals and who lived among us. therefore, the security strategy has to be perfectly distinguished from the immigration strategy.
in writing. ‒ i have opposed and voted against all these data exchange mechanisms, because of the absence of effective safeguards to guarantee the fundamental right to privacy in this type of exchanges. the vote is intended to bring denmark into a system whereby the various security services in the member states exchange data on citizens without any control or judicial or political transparency, allowing the storage of private data and the storage of data on persons who have not committed any crime or are suspected of committing one. consequently, my vote is against.
in writing. ‒ the decision to establish automated data exchange with regard to fingerprint data in denmark is a step forward in strengthening crossborder cooperation in law enforcement in the union: the implementation of the prüm decision and the european model for information exchange. i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the moraes reports refer to the application to denmark of council decision 2008/615/jha (prüm decision); a legal framework to deepen cooperation between member states in the fight against terrorism, crossborder crime and illegal immigration. more specifically, it provides for the exchange between the contracting parties of dna profiles, dactyloscopic data, vehicle registration records and personal and non-personal data related to cross-border police cooperation. the purpose of the prüm decision is to intensify and accelerate the exchange of information between authorities. denmark has, in the council's view, fulfilled the requirements for the application of that legal framework (report and evaluation visit, and pilot trial) to conclude that it fully applies the general provisions on data protection. however, following the eug's view on the prüm decision, we voted against it because it is a treaty which was negotiated and adopted in a non-transparent way and without serious democratic control from the outset, and it deepens the conflict in which security is sought to be strengthened at the expense of freedom.
in writing. ‒ the fight against organised crime - not just terrorism, but also other phenomena such as human trafficking - requires that we optimise the possibilities offered by forensic science and criminology today. in this area of freedom and security which is europe, the automatic exchange of dna data banks, which facilitates this objective, is an obligation.
in writing. ‒ in accordance with article 25 (2) of decision 2008/615/jha, the transfer of personal data pursuant to that decision may only be initiated when the general provisions on data protection set out in chapter 6 of that decision have been transposed into national law in the territory of the member states participating in that transfer. on 29 july 2015, the council concluded that denmark has fully implemented the general provisions on data protection laid down in chapter 6 of decision 2008/615/jha. therefore, for the purposes of automated searching of dna data, denmark should be entitled to receive and supply personal data pursuant to article 9 of decision 2008/615/jha. i have therefore voted in favour of this report, which is necessary to approve the exchange of dna data with denmark in the context of crossborder cooperation in the fight against terrorism.

in writing. ‒ the decision to establish automated data exchange with regard to fingerprint data in denmark is a step forward in strengthening crossborder cooperation in law enforcement in the union: the implementation of the prüm decision and the european model for information exchange. i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the moraes reports refer to the application to denmark of council decision 2008/615/jha (prüm decision); a legal framework to deepen cooperation between member states in the fight against terrorism, crossborder crime and illegal immigration. more specifically, it provides for the exchange between the contracting parties of dna profiles, dactyloscopic data, vehicle registration records and personal and non-personal data related to cross-border police cooperation. the purpose of the prüm decision is to intensify and accelerate the exchange of information between authorities. denmark has, in the council's view, fulfilled the requirements for the application of that legal framework (report and evaluation visit, and pilot trial) to conclude that it fully applies the general provisions on data protection. however, following the eug's view on the prüm decision, i voted against it because it is a treaty which was negotiated and adopted in a non-transparent way and without serious democratic control from the outset, and it deepens the conflict in which security is sought to be strengthened at the expense of freedom.
in writing. ‒ the fight against organised crime - not just terrorism, but also other phenomena such as human trafficking - requires that we optimise the possibilities offered by forensic science and criminology today. in this area of freedom and security which is europe, the automatic exchange of data from fingerprint banks, which facilitates this objective, is an obligation.
in writing. ‒ in accordance with article 25 (2) of decision 2008/615/jha, the transfer of personal data pursuant to that decision may only be initiated when the general provisions on data protection set out in chapter 6 of that decision have been transposed into national law in the territory of the member states participating in that transfer. on 29 july 2015, the council concluded that denmark has fully implemented the general provisions on data protection laid down in chapter 6 of decision 2008/615/jha. therefore, for the purposes of automated searching of dactyloscopic data, denmark should be entitled to receive and supply personal data pursuant to article 9 of decision 2008/615/jha. i have therefore voted in favour of this report, which is necessary to approve the exchange of fingerprint data with denmark in the context of crossborder cooperation in the fight against terrorism.

in writing. ‒ regretting that this is a measure which only benefits a minority of people holding this type of diplomatic passport, i voted in favour of this agreement between the union and china, because we believe that the obstacles to effective access to the right of free movement must always be reduced.
‒ china is one of the countries whose nationals are required to have a visa when travelling to the schengen area. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the union holding a valid diplomatic passport or a union security pass, and for citizens of china holding a valid diplomatic passport, when travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a stay of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. with this report, for which i voted in favour, we welcome the agreement which will allow progress to be made in relations between the two countries. in order to ensure equal treatment, article 6 of the agreement states that china may only suspend or terminate the agreement with respect to all member states of the union and that the union may only suspend or terminate the agreement with respect to all member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because we consider that the visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports represents progress towards full reciprocity in the visa waiver for holders of ordinary passports. the importance of visa liberalisation is considerable, as its benefits are tangible, such as reducing waiting times at consulates and the costs associated with travel, facilitating contacts between citizens and fostering the stable development of relations. the agreement also has the positive side that it also includes holders of a union laissez-passer.
in writing. ‒ china is one of the countries whose nationals need a visa to enter the union. conversely, european citizens also need to complete the visa process to travel to china. in 2013, a dialogue on mobility was established, aimed at achieving mutual visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. the agreement reached with china provides for short stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period for european or chinese citizens holding a diplomatic passport. i voted in favour of this agreement because it is a first step towards the gradual abolition of the visa requirement. facilitation in this area is positive, because it allows for the removal of burdensome requirements for travellers and contributes to better contact between people, which in turn helps a flourishing of the economy, culture, scientific research and trade. however, progress towards full liberalisation will always be conditional on china's progress in human rights and public freedoms.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because its practical implementation helps to reduce somewhat the impact of the cuts applied in member states such as greece and cyprus, which have hit the most vulnerable socioeconomic groups hardest. this amendment to the regulation increases the payments for member states in budgetary difficulties. although it is an insufficient measure, it is a palliative, and this should be the approach taken by the institutions to mitigate the effects of the economic crisis and not the application of sanctions and suspension of payments with which the council and the commission threaten spain and portugal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this commission proposal, as it is a temporary solution to alleviate the liquidity problems of the member states, in particular the commission proposed to amend the regulation on the financial management of member states experiencing serious difficulties with regard to their financial stability. the financial and economic crisis has put pressure on national economies and member states have adopted austerity measures to balance their budgets. as national budgets are under strain, it may be difficult for countries experiencing budgetary difficulties to find sufficient funds for national co-financing of regional policy projects.
in writing. ‒ we agree with this specific and budget-neutral solution to the temporary liquidity problems facing greece and cyprus. at a time of great pressure on the budgets of these states, every effort must be made to ensure that their restrictions do not affect their ability to participate in european programmes, especially those focused on development policies.
in writing. ‒ the financial and economic crisis has put pressure on national economies, and states have resorted to austerity measures to balance their budgets. in this context, it is essential to ensure that the european funds are used in the best possible way. with national budgets under pressure, it can be difficult for countries experiencing budgetary difficulties to find sufficient funds for national co-financing of projects. article 24 and article 120 (3) of the european funds regulation were created to help those states experiencing transitional budgetary difficulties. greece is currently the only country to benefit from a financial assistance programme. since the economic situation in greece remains very fragile, the commission has proposed to extend the provisions on the supplement. the commission has also decided to extend the co-financing rate of the union contribution to the eligible costs of the cohesion fund for the period from 1 january 2014 to 30 june 2017 by an additional amount of eur 300000000 (eur 300000000 for the period from 1 january 2014 to 30 june 2017). i voted in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ noting the budgetary and financial difficulties encountered by some member states in co-financing regional development projects, the report proposes to increase payments to member states under an adjustment programme after 30 june 2016 and to extend the exceptional co-financing rate of 85% under the erdf and esf in cyprus until the closure of the 2014-2020 programmes. it appears, however, that these measures do not solve the structural problems facing greece and cyprus, but may make them even more dependent on the european structural funds. the other member states may also have to bear the consequences of these increases. for these reasons, i abstained on this report.

in writing. ‒ in this draft legislative resolution, the european parliament endorses the council's position at first reading on the proposal to amend regulation (eu) no 1303/2013. the amendments aim to help those member states experiencing transitional budgetary difficulties and receiving financial assistance to make the most of the investment opportunities provided by the european structural and investment funds in the 2014-2020 programming period. in this sense, it is possible to increase the co-financing rate, which can lead to positive results such as improving budgetary consolidation and investment efforts. i am voting in favour of this because it is a concrete solution which will help member states in difficulty.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of jean-marie le pen, who has been denounced in france for his clearly nazi-fascist statements. although le pen herself has wished to invoke her parliamentary immunity, the facts have nothing to do with her parliamentary work, since they are nothing but the expression of her deplorable ultra-right position. i have therefore voted to lift his parliamentary immunity so that he can be tried for incitement to racism and hatred.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative resolution, by which parliament approves the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the regulation amending regulation (ec) no 91/2003 on rail transport statistics, as regards the collection of data on goods, passengers and accidents. after lengthy negotiations, the council and parliament agreed that the most efficient and cost-effective way to avoid duplication of work between eurostat, the commission and the european union agency for railways was to strengthen cooperation between these institutions and to ensure that statistical data relating to union policies are easily accessible to citizens and stakeholders, which resulted in the signing of two memoranda of understanding between eurostat and the commission (27.4.2016) and between eurostat and the afe (12.5.2016).

in writing. ‒ i abstained on this report which seeks to create a legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions. i support some of the commitments in the report, as they significantly improve on the commission's bad proposal. however, several issues remain concerning. firstly, i do not support the complete harmonization which was the result of the final vote. the list sets out minimum and maximum penalties and lists possible aggravating and mitigating circumstances. the text also contains a comprehensive list of infringements and sets out how the fines are to be calculated by the judges. the effects of this proposal on national criminal systems have not been sufficiently studied.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur, mrs kallas, for her work in bringing this report to the fore. a very important report on the legal framework of the union for customs infringements and sanctions. our single internal market is one of the pillars of the union and it must be further strengthened. that is why i voted in favour of the agreement.
in writing. ‒ the report on the union legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions sets the objective of closing the gap between the different legal regimes of the member states by creating a common platform of rules for the application and imposition of sanctions, in order to avoid unequal compliance costs and administrative burdens that differ between member states. this will improve the level playing field between economic operators in the union. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, considering that the customs union is one of the foundations of the union and the backbone of the single market. however, despite its importance, there is still no integrated approach to the enforcement of customs legislation, including sanctions. this means that the rules are the same but, when the rules are broken, the penalties applied differ significantly. customs union and trade policy are exclusive competences of the union, so only the union can develop a common approach to the implementation of customs legislation. without an integrated approach to enforcement, including sanctions, it is not possible for the customs administrations of the member states to act as a single entity, particularly in view of the significant differences between the sanction systems of the different member states. the union customs code requires member states to establish systems of customs penalties which are effective, proportionate and dissuasive. the directive should therefore aim to improve the convergence of member states' approaches to comply with union customs legislation.

in writing. ‒ although the customs union is considered to be one of the foundations of the union and the backbone of the single market, there is still no integrated approach to the enforcement of customs legislation, including sanctions. this is particularly important in the context of the growth of electronic commerce, which requires greater legal certainty and greater transparency in the handling of infringements by the various customs authorities. we therefore support a common legal framework, which would allow customs administrations to interact and function as effectively as if they were a single administration, ensuring that checks are carried out with equivalent results and supporting legitimate business activity, as well as protecting the financial interests of the union.
in writing. ‒ the report on the union legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions sets the objective of closing the gap between the different legal regimes of each member state by creating a common platform of rules for the application and imposition of sanctions, to avoid unequal compliance costs and administrative burdens that differ between member states. this will improve the level playing field between economic operators in the union. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this report which seeks to create a legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions. i support some of the commitments in the report, as they significantly improve on the commission's bad proposal. however, several issues remain concerning. firstly, i do not support the complete harmonization which was the result of the final vote. the list sets out minimum and maximum penalties and lists possible aggravating and mitigating circumstances. the text also contains a comprehensive list of infringements and sets out how the fines are to be calculated by the judges. the effects of this proposal on national criminal systems have not been sufficiently studied.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because it ultimately represents a boost to the internal market through the harmonisation of tariff barriers. the report seeks to improve the functioning of the sanctions applied, to avoid different types of dumping on the european market, by selecting the importing country according to its sanction regimes. this is technically fully justified, but in a context of the development of ambitious trade agreements, this directive can be a boost to the implementation of trade agreements which run counter to the interests of european workers. that is why i have decided to abstain on this report.

in writing. ‒ at present, customs legislation is common to the whole territory of the union. however, in the event of non-compliance, the applicable rules correspond to the 28 different frameworks that govern each member state. in order to establish a common framework for european criminal law, this text is a further step towards harmonisation in this area. since such harmonization will mean that foreign trade operators will have a better understanding of the legal consequences of their actions throughout the customs union, i have voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ while welcoming the partial internalisation of the security service of the institutions, i reject the view that these changes should be conditional on a linear target of cuts and new outsourcing affecting all the staff of the european parliament. i also believe that the discretion with which security measures are being taken in parliament should be reviewed and i have therefore voted against this proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this draft amending budget, which seeks to allocate a heading for the recruitment of 35 new armed security staff after the attacks in the european union. although security is necessary, i think there are other measures to guarantee it without having to resort to the militarization of all institutions. as the report says, this recruitment process was done without proper involvement of parliament. in addition to strictly adhering to increased security only by increasing the armed personnel to monitor the european institutions, without taking into account the rest of civil society which is also exposed to these attacks, or security in infrastructures. that is why i do not support this report because of its exclusively security-related approach, and i believe that these dangers must be tackled from a more inclusive approach and that conflicts should be prevented and resolved at their source, and not result in a militarization of our environment.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which represents a further development of eu-iran relations one year after the nuclear agreement between the international community and iran. the report outlines areas of possible cooperation with iran, such as trade, environmental protection, aviation safety, academic exchanges, etc. and it deals extensively with the regional situation in the middle east, sending the message, especially to iran and saudi arabia, about the need to de-escalate tensions and to carry out a diplomatic normalization. the report also covers the human rights situation in iran, emphasising the union's opposition to the death penalty, and criticizes iran for the very high number of executions and other human rights violations, such as detentions of eu-iranian dual nationals, gender discrimination, minority rights, freedom of expression, etc. the report specifically calls on iran to cooperate fully with un human rights mechanisms.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to define the union's strategy on iran following the nuclear agreement signed in 2015, a permanent agreement between the parties to lift the sanctions imposed on iran by the united states, the union and the united nations, and for its part, iran limits its long-term nuclear programme. the report has positive elements, but also negative ones, such as the fact that it does not call for the total lifting of the us sanctions or that, as is usual in reports and resolutions of the union, it is hypocritical to call for the human rights of refugees and asylum seekers to be respected, when the union systematically violates them on its own territory. i have voted in favour of this report, however, because it supports a return to active diplomacy and cooperation with iran, based on mutual respect for international norms and principles, and recalls that 'it is not intended to interfere in the internal political choices of a country'. furthermore, the report argues that iran can act as a mediator in seeking a peaceful solution to the syrian conflict. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has refused to include in the report the defence of the main values and principles which represent the union. parliament has refused to include paragraphs expressing concern about the high number of executions or calling for the release of political prisoners. it also failed to include a call for the expansion of economic relations between the union and iran to be accompanied by improvements in the field of human rights, women's rights and freedom of expression, as well as the abolition of the death penalty. these principles are essential and they conditioned my vote. that is why i voted against this report. the nuclear deal with iran is a very important milestone. but we cannot forget that we are still dealing with a regime of terror. a fundamentalist regime that practices systematic torture, denies the holocaust and executes children. i believe in the future of iran because i believe in the iranians. but i am absolutely against any form of appeasement with the regime and against renouncing the defence of the fundamental values which represent the union, the defence of human rights, the defence of the rule of law, the defence of human rights, the defence of the rule of law, the defence of the rule of law, the defence of human rights, the defence of the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of a text which i consider to be in the direction of building a common and standardised agenda between the union and iran, based on respect for sovereignty, multilateralism in the settlement of disputes, the joint pursuit of processes leading to progress in respect for human rights, the sustainable and sustainable development of the iranian people and peace and security for all the peoples of the middle east. i am, however, opposed to the view of iran as a source of regional instability, to the establishment of relations guided predominantly by commercial criteria, to the presentation of trade liberalization per se as a panacea for the achievement of the development of peoples like the iranian (who participate in asymmetric and subordinate conditions in the global market) and to the use of fossil and nuclear energies as the basis of the productive and energy matrix of any country.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank mr howitt for his work in getting this resolution voted and passed today. the sign given by parliament today is very important. i am a signatory to some amendments calling for respect for human rights and an end to the harassment of women and children. but i also think that we must help iran in its steps to put aside isolation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the eu's strategy towards iran following the nuclear agreement reached a year ago with the international community, which highlights the joint comprehensive plan of action as an important achievement for multilateral diplomacy and for european diplomacy which will not only allow for a significant improvement in relations between iran and the union, but also promote stability in the whole region. in addition to recognising the successful role played by vice-president mogherini, the resolution addresses the human rights situation in iran from a broad perspective, taking a position against the death penalty in the country and against the multiple human rights violations committed in the country: detentions of persons with dual eu and iranian citizenship, gender discrimination, failure to respect the rights of minorities, constraint on freedom of expression, etc. we call for a moratorium on the death penalty, while supporting full cooperation by iran with all un human rights protection mechanisms and calling for the release of all political prisoners.

in writing. ‒ organized crime, money laundering and transnational corruption are criminal phenomena on the rise in the union. the ferrara report is important because it looks at which recommendations of those identified by the european parliament's anti-corruption commission (crim) have been implemented and which are pending. the report is very comprehensive and consists of eight sections. each of them addresses a specific aspect of the fight against corruption and organised crime and calls for specific actions to be taken to achieve this. these include monitoring the transposition of existing rules and their degree of application, the operational structure adopted to combat organised crime and corruption, the need to strengthen the legal framework to combat corruption, more effective judicial and police cooperation, the confiscation of assets of criminal organisations, preventing organised crime from penetrating the formal economy, the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office as a tool to combat this phenomenon and the identification of areas requiring further regulatory development. the report sought to identify specific areas of failure in the legal system for preventing corruption in order to take measures to remedy it as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ despite my opposition to the creation of a european public prosecutor's office which would create a parallel justice system without even the physical resources to support it, i voted in favour of this resolution. i have done so because i believe that it contains very positive proposals in the fight against corruption and organised crime. the commission proposes that the member states and the union take effective measures to prevent various crimes which are committed by the laxity of administrations, such as tax crimes, human trafficking and environmental crimes. in addition, specific punitive measures are proposed, such as the prohibition of persons convicted of corruption or money laundering from working in public institutions, which i regard very positively, hence my vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ this report contains a number of measures of vital importance to fight corruption and organised crime. from a call for greater cooperation in the criminal field to open support for the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office. we call for urgent and decisive legislative action at community level to equip the security forces with the necessary tools. highlight the establishment of a comprehensive union-wide electronic public procurement system to reduce the risk of corruption. the drawing up of 'blacklists' of companies with proven links to organised crime or involved in corrupt practices. mandatory rules to disqualify those convicted of activities related to organised crime, money laundering, corruption, both from running for elections and from working for administrations, including union institutions and agencies. a common system for confiscating assets from criminal organisations and extending their use for social purposes, such as compensation to families and businesses affected by criminal or corrupt practices. we must move towards more europe, because crime knows no borders.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it incorporates important amendments on issues of transparency, environmental aspects of corruption, better communication by judicial authorities, the need to address labour exploitation of migrants and other relevant issues. the final text is balanced in its final wording on the most sensitive points such as the use of the internet or the links between organised crime and terrorism. among the most positive aspects of the report, they highlight: 1) a call on the union to become a member of greco and on the european commission to publish its anti-corruption report (including a section on the union institutions) and to propose appropriate legislation; 2) the need for legislation that strengthens the rights of suspects and guarantees for a fair trial; 3) a call on the commission to present a legislative proposal on the protection of witnesses and whistleblowers before the end of 2017; 4) calls on the union and the member states to strengthen measures to locate, freeze and confiscate the proceeds of crime and to firmly prohibit fraudulent companies from accessing european public procurement procedures; 5) a statement against tax risks for prosecutors.
in writing. ‒ we support this report because it provides a european vision of the fight against corruption, one of the most destructive traps in some member states. it sets out guarantees for the correct transposition of european legislation, sets out priorities, provides for improvements in police and judicial coordination against corruption, preventive measures to prevent infiltration into the legal economy and common methods for the seizure of assets obtained as a result of corrupt operations, all in line with our proposals presented in previous reports on the state of fundamental rights in the union.
in writing. ‒ organized crime, money laundering and transnational corruption are criminal phenomena on the rise in the union. the ferrara report is important because it looks at which recommendations of those identified by the european parliament's anti-corruption commission (crim) have been put into practice and which are pending. the report is very comprehensive and consists of eight sections. each of them addresses a specific aspect of the fight against corruption and organised crime and calls for specific actions to be taken to achieve this. these include monitoring the transposition of existing rules and their degree of application, the operational structure adopted to combat organised crime and corruption, the need to strengthen the legal framework to combat corruption, more effective judicial and police cooperation, the confiscation of assets of criminal organisations, preventing organised crime from penetrating the formal economy, the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office as a tool to combat this phenomenon and the identification of areas requiring further regulatory development. the report sought to identify specific areas of failure in the legal system for preventing corruption in order to take measures to remedy it as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, considering that organised crime, corruption and money laundering pose serious threats to the union's economy by significantly reducing tax revenues of the member states and of the union as a whole. we must develop effective, cutting-edge european legislation to combat organised crime and corruption. the phenomenon of organised crime, corruption and money laundering generally has a cross-border dimension requiring close cooperation between the competent national authorities and between the national authorities and the relevant union agencies.
