in writing. ‒ this report highlights the seriousness of corruption, which is adapting to new activities, different geographical, economic and social sectors and new markets, and is wreaking havoc on the economy. in particular, it is recalled that in 2014 1 649 irregularities were identified as fraud against the european budget, amounting to eur 538.2 million. in this context, we call on the commission in this report to review existing legislation to establish effective, proportionate and dissuasive sanctions, to clarify common definitions of crimes and, as an example of transparency, to include the european institutions in its report on the fight against corruption. i am voting in favour of the report because to put an end to the scourge of corruption it is essential to promote a culture of legality and to encourage greater exchange of information on fraud between member states.
in writing. ‒ the eradication of organised crime, corruption and money laundering are priority issues, and i therefore vote in favour of the implementation of measures to make progress along these lines. to do this, we must work on the transposition of the existing rules in order to assess their effectiveness. we also call for the fight against organised crime and for this purpose we call for the creation of a specialised unit within europol to combat organised crime groups active in different sectors. we also want more effective judicial and police cooperation within the countries of the union, and measures to prevent organized crime and corruption from gaining access to the legal economy.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it calls for the effective defence and protection of the human rights of all people who are forced to migrate for various reasons. the text finally adopted - despite the opposing vote of right-wing groups - places particular emphasis on special protection measures for the most vulnerable, in particular women and children, and calls for improvements to the integration of migrants in host countries and their access to basic services and the labour market. it also specifically addresses the situation of refugees and internally displaced persons - more than 65 million people today - whose dignity and human rights are flagrantly violated, and insists that there is no better way to prevent trafficking and human trafficking than by opening up safe and legal pathways for migration. the report also calls on the union and its member states to set an example in promoting and protecting the human rights of migrants, especially within their borders, if they are to have credibility in the debates on migration and human rights with third countries.
in writing. ‒ although the right wing has tried to impose on the report the whitewashing of systematic violations of the human rights of migrants in the union, such as returns to the country of origin against the will of the migrant, this has been rejected and i have been able to vote in favour of the report. it contains a number of positive elements, pointing to the systemic causes of migration and the need for a migration policy based on human rights and legal and safe pathways of access. i also voted in favour of the report because it is critical of the current eu model of outsourcing of borders and of migration management by third countries, a model which i completely reject, and it proposes effective measures for free access for migrants to social and labour rights and public services in the countries in which they reside. that is why i support the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, of which i was a co-rapporteur. the report stresses the importance of integrating migrants in host countries and ensuring that their most basic rights, namely health, education and housing, are respected. in this respect, the report speaks of the importance of avoiding discriminatory practices in access to the labour market. on the other hand, there are paragraphs that refer to gender-based violence and the situation of special vulnerability of some groups, such as children and women. finally, i would like to highlight the paragraphs dealing with the mobility of migrants. the report advocates legal and safe immigration channels.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of an own-initiative report by our group which addresses in a necessary and urgent way the humanitarian crisis facing the union as a result of conflict, violence and repression in countries of origin of forced mobility flows. the report calls unreservedly for compliance with international conventions, especially those on human rights, asylum and refuge, and for the member states and the community executive to address in a comprehensive, urgent and adequate manner the range of problems and vulnerabilities of various kinds faced by people moving to and within the union, from a human rights approach.

in writing. ‒ i abstained in this report despite considering that human rights are inherent in all human beings, without distinction. migration is a global and multidimensional phenomenon, which has its origins in multiple causes such as economic, social and political conditions, working conditions, violence and security, as well as the progressive degradation of the environment. this phenomenon must be tackled in a coherent and balanced way, within a global perspective which takes account of its human dimension. we must bear in mind that according to the united nations, there are currently about 244 million people who are considered international migrants. it is therefore essential to have effective mechanisms for monitoring and controlling the entry and exit of foreigners, as well as analyses and forecasts of the effects of migration, as a basis for the development of any policy for managing the migration phenomenon.

in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of an own-initiative report by our group which addresses in a necessary and urgent way the humanitarian crisis facing the union as a result of conflict, violence and repression in countries of origin of forced mobility flows. the report calls unreservedly for compliance with international conventions, especially those on human rights, asylum and refuge, and for the member states and the community executive to address in a comprehensive, urgent and adequate manner the range of problems and vulnerabilities of various kinds faced by people moving to and within the union, from a human rights approach.
in writing. ‒ i support this resolution and want to make reminder that this text calls on states to recognise their obligations under international law with regard to asylum and migration and to enact national laws for the effective implementation of those obligations. it recalls that migrants have the right not to be sent to countries where they risk ill-treatment and torture; recalls that collective expulsions and push—back are prohibited under international law; expresses concern at the treatment of migrants who are forcibly returned to their countries of origin or to third countries without adequate follow-up of their situation. it calls for the eu and the international community to identify specific measures that governments can take to increase the potential of legal migration as a development enabler; stresses that political leadership and strong advocacy are required, especially in destination countries, to combat xenophobia and to facilitate the social integration of migrants.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which constitutes the first real attempt by the pe to contribute to the eu-wide, vivid debate on the issue of migration (following a recent droi report on trafficking in human beings). it aims to focus on the rights of migrants in third countries and on means to uphold these rights in eu policies and broader international efforts.

mr president, the corrado report should go much further in promoting binding instruments to monitor and sanction companies which violate human rights in the world. the existing mechanisms are based on voluntary work and are not sufficient. it is essential to ensure consistency in the policies of the european union and not to sign trade agreements which contain private judicial mechanisms for settling disputes between investors and states, as ceta (aecg) and ttip (atci) do and contain them. we also lack a greater reference to the responsibility of financial institutions that support transnational corporations in tax havens dotted with scandals such as the panama papers. the second session of the working group is currently taking place at the united nations, where it is working on a legally binding international instrument to establish responsibilities for transnational corporations and to control corporate power. i have been able to participate and i believe that the european union and, specifically, parliament and the commission should take note of the work of this group and support its recommendations and proposals, and not continue to throw stones at the wheel.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because the text recognises the responsibility of companies and expresses concern about human rights violations in third countries, and calls for continued, effective and coherent action at all levels, including national, european and international, to combat effectively human rights violations by international companies. it also makes explicit calls on european and non-european businesses to respect human rights and calls on the union and the member states to guarantee and protect human rights. it specifically requires the union, the member states, third countries and all national and international authorities to adopt, as urgently and as widely as possible, binding instruments aimed at the effective protection of human rights, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour, not without recognising that it should have gone much further in promoting binding instruments to monitor and sanction companies that violate human rights. the existing mechanisms are based on voluntary work and are not sufficient. it is therefore essential to move towards joint responsibility for parent companies along the entire value chain; it is necessary to ensure consistency in union policies and not to sign trade agreements containing opaque and para-judicial mechanisms for resolving differences between investors and states. we are missing a greater reference to the responsibility of financial institutions, which support transnational corporations and the need to specifically address the right of access to justice of the most vulnerable. we should also, as we proposed in amendments, promote the creation of a union agency to monitor the activities of transnational companies in third countries, and sanction procedures in the event of crimes, so as to put the protection of human rights and the environment at the centre of union action, rather than corporate profits.
in writing. ‒ we support most of the measures in this report to ensure that there is an effective system of control and sanctions against companies that commit human rights violations in the course of their activities in third countries. in particular, we underline our agreement to the creation of labels that will ensure consumers that what they buy is free from this type of behaviour and that will help to extend the social debate and awareness of this problem.
in writing. ‒ although some progress has been made in recent years (united nations guiding principles on business and human rights), there is still no binding regime to address the defenselessness of business in cases of human rights violations. the globalisation of economic activities makes it increasingly necessary to establish common standards. this report addresses the necessary responsibility of companies for respecting human rights in their international activities, regardless of the level of compliance where they are present. in this connection, we support the working group set up within the united nations to prepare a future binding international treaty on business and human rights. we call on the eu to increase coherence and the development and effective implementation of international commitments in this area, and for companies to do more to implement human rights due diligence and to be more transparent in their activities. for these reasons i have voted in favour of this report.

mr president, we are opposed to this report because we are opposed to the interests of the big gas companies who want to speculate with our territories, our energy bill and our climate. in my country, spain, there are many open conflicts because of european plans to bring american gas extracted by hydraulic fracturing or liquefied gas from qatar to our territories. we have the examples of castor, which we are all going to pay for, and doñana, where a very important agro-environmental heritage is in danger, a matter on which the commission has washed its hands this week, to play the game with gas natural. but also gas pipelines like the midcat, storage infrastructure in urban areas, the overcapacity of power stations like castejón. all of these are dangerous and useless infrastructures that only add another fictitious cost to energy bills for the benefit of the large energy oligopolies and to the clear detriment of the people.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because this strategic commitment of the union to liquefied natural gas is a reinforcement of energy dependence and environmental destruction. instead of stepping up its commitment to renewable energy and indigenous sources of energy production, the union is continuing to pursue the path of global resource hoarding, the same logic of oil applied to gas. another aspect is the importation of gas through destructive techniques such as fracking, but it is no more serious than the international conflicts developed around this resource, whose liquefaction allows its transport through smaller infrastructures. gas is a fossil fuel with high levels of emissions and only benefits the large multinationals that control its distribution. because we need a balanced transition from energy production in the union to renewable energy, i have therefore decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ the global liquefied natural gas (lng) market is in a phase of strong dynamism. global lng supply is expected to increase by 50% by 2020. the union can benefit from the expansion of the global lng market to strengthen its security of gas supply and its competitiveness. but always with the utmost respect for environmental protection and gas independence. this report therefore contains a number of measures to this end. among the amendments i have advocated, i would like to highlight the incorporation of the need to meet the objectives of reducing greenhouse gases, energy efficiency and renewable energy expressed in the paris agreement and the energy union roadmap. at the same time, the call to raise awareness in global free trade forums of the environmental, climate and social effects of lng. the report also expresses the potential benefit that the atci could have for energy security, as the removal of import restrictions can significantly increase the gas supply options of the union. the report is complete and that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the own-initiative report on liquefied natural gas (lng) and gas storage, because it promotes, on the basis of the functioning of the market, the construction of new lng terminals, gas pipelines and gas storage. the commission has also concluded that the measures in question are in line with the union's climate objectives. the energy security of the eastern and baltic countries does not mean replacing russian gas imports with gas from other supposedly safer countries (even sometimes from fracking), but a clear commitment to improving energy efficiency and developing renewables.
in writing. ‒ this report stresses the need to rationalise infrastructure investments for this alternative energy source, some of which are now over-scaled, and points to the potential of this fuel to alleviate dependence on the european market and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. we also agree with the special mention of the usefulness of this source in maritime transport. we also share the need to emphasize the role of the union as the second largest purchaser of this fuel on the world market.
in writing. ‒ i share the balanced view on the eu liquefied natural gas strategy that we adopted in the itre committee. the report reflects both the situation and the potential of lng, taking into account its contribution to the security of energy supply in europe and the benefits of a more competitive market. in addition, the lng strategy is particularly relevant from the perspective of its qualities in reducing current environmental impacts, as an alternative fuel in transport, heating and electricity. i believe that lng, as an energy source with far lower emissions than other fossil fuels and other natural gas sources, should not be penalized with labels that cast doubt on its clean character, questioning the opportunities and advantages of our companies globally, although the possible import of lng from hydraulic fracturing deserves more detailed attention in the framework of our international agreements. in short, i believe that europe must make a firm commitment to lng, as a source of energy which is beneficial for the environment, the economy and european society, and that is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ an internal energy market that fully integrates liquefied natural gas and storage facilities will make a significant contribution to the union becoming a world leader in renewable energy. that is why i support the union's strategy for liquefied natural gas and its storage, which will enable a rapid transition to a sustainable, secure and competitive energy system and end dependence on external gas suppliers. to do this, we will need to complete the infrastructure that is still lagging, strengthen the internal gas market and focus on the use of liquefied natural gas as an alternative fuel for transport, heat and electricity production.

in writing. ‒ the global liquefied natural gas market is in a high-dynamic phase, with global supply of this form of energy expected to increase by 50% by 2020. in addition, supply conditions are changing from long-term contracts indexed to the price of oil to spot and benchmarked markets. the expansion of the gas market can benefit the union, in order to strengthen its security of supply and competitiveness. to realise its full potential, the document suggests completing the community's gas infrastructure so that all member states can access it, and working towards the completion of the internal gas market, while promoting free, liquid and transparent global markets. in full recognition of the potential benefits of market integration for security of supply as well as for convergence of regional energy prices, i support with my vote the move towards a fully functional and integrated internal gas market.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it draws attention to the need to harmonise fisheries controls in the union, by establishing a single reference framework and by promoting the application of the same penalties in all member states for the same infringements. fisheries control in the union differs from one member state to another, with differences in the procedures and types of sanctions applied for the same type of infringements - in some cases administrative and in others criminal - differences in the level of resources used, lack of specialised inspectors, databases not always interchangeable between member states, etc. the lack of a standardised approach to fisheries controls creates a feeling of inefficiency and injustice in the sector. the report proposes that common control criteria be adopted, the role of the european fisheries agency be strengthened, more resources and more modern means be used to make inspections more effective, and that european training for inspectors and fishermen be promoted.
in writing. ‒ the report submitted by the committee on fisheries for approval by the european parliament's plenary contains many positive aspects: recognition of discriminatory treatment in the conduct of controls within the sector, the failure of some european rules to adapt to reality, the defence of regional or autonomous community inspections for inland waters, national inspections of maritime fisheries in waters up to 12 nautical miles and union inspections for the rest of the waters. however, i abstained because the report has several aspects which raise concerns and ambiguous interpretations, such as those relating to the use of new monitoring technologies; the introduction of a points-based penalty system with implications for fishing licences. at the same time, the report reflects a high degree of centralisation and definition at community level of technical and political measures relating to controls rather than cooperation between member states, which is why i could not vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i understand that the report calls for simplifying and improving the union's legislation and reducing the administrative burden, a historic demand of our seafarers, and points out that closer cooperation between the member states requires that, in this review, the european institutions and the fishing sector work together, especially the coastal, artisanal and traditional fishing sector, whose protection and promotion must be the aim of any new legislation. the commission is also proposing to introduce a new system of penalties for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and to include the impact of recreational fishing in the revision of the control regulation, all of which are objectives for our fishermen. it also calls for effective control of the traceability of our products throughout the chain and greater control of imported fish, in line with the union's parameters.
in writing. ‒ this report addresses one of the gordian knots facing european fishermen: the lack of rules, the heterogeneity of controls and sanctions, the need to improve statistics in order to be able to prevent the most common or harmful illegal behaviour with inspection campaigns and the need for everyone to be sanctioned in the same way for the same infringements. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a good example of the need to ensure that the safety of workers is not compromised.
in writing. ‒ fisheries control in the union differs from one member state to another, with differences in the procedures and types of sanctions applied for the same type of infringements - in some cases administrative and in others criminal - differences in the level of resources used, lack of specialised inspectors, databases not always interchangeable between member states, etc. the commission is proposing to tackle this problem by adopting common control criteria, strengthening the role of the european fisheries control agency, using more resources and more modern means to make inspections more effective, and promoting european training for inspectors and fishermen. i would like to say that i support the rapporteur's approach to the harmonization of fisheries controls in the union by establishing a single reference framework. and, in particular, that the same penalties be applied in all member states for the same infringements, thus putting an end to the feeling of inefficiency and injustice that is generated in the sector.
in writing. the report, which was submitted by the committee on fisheries for approval by the european parliament's plenary, contains many positive aspects: recognition of discriminatory treatment in the conduct of controls within the sector, the fact that some european rules are not adapted to reality, the defence of regional or autonomous community inspections for inland waters, national inspections of maritime fisheries in waters up to 12 nautical miles and union inspections for the rest of the waters. however, i abstained because the report has several aspects which raise concerns and ambiguous interpretations, such as those relating to the use of new monitoring technologies; the introduction of a points-based penalty system with implications for fishing licences. at the same time, the report reflects a high degree of centralisation and definition at community level of technical and political measures relating to controls rather than cooperation between member states, which is why i could not vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from voting on this report not because i do not agree with the approval of fisheries controls in europe, but because the differences between the fisheries in the atlantic ocean and the mediterranean sea were not taken into account when the approval was given. we cannot deal with such distant realities together, and we must bear in mind that the problems in both areas are far from being the same. the rules must be applied with the same rigor, but always bearing in mind that what is beneficial for fisheries in the atlantic does not necessarily have to be beneficial in the mediterranean.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i understand that the report calls for simplifying and improving the union's legislation and reducing the administrative burden, a historic demand of our seafarers, and points out that closer cooperation between the member states requires that, in this review, the european institutions and the fishing sector work together, especially the coastal, artisanal and traditional fishing sector, whose protection and promotion must be the aim of any new legislation. the commission is also proposing to introduce a new system of penalties for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and to include the impact of recreational fishing in the revision of the control regulation, all of which are objectives for our fishermen. it also calls for effective control of the traceability of our products throughout the chain and greater control of imported fish, in line with the union's parameters.

in writing. ‒ the present motion for a resolution aims to address different proposals for methods or solutions to improve the harmonisation of the control of the common fisheries policy and to identify shortcomings in the application of the rules of the common fisheries policy. at present, there is a considerable diversity in the areas of application of the control, procedures and strategies of the common fisheries policy. an example is the fact that the same offence is punished differently, as the sanction may have been classified as criminal or administrative. all this creates a feeling of injustice among fishermen and raises questions about the effectiveness of the regulations applied. i am voting in favour of the proposal because harmonising the scope of application strengthens the effectiveness of union law and therefore helps to achieve the objective of ensuring the sustainable exploitation of living marine resources and, on the other hand, the union's fight against illegal fishing on a global scale.
in writing. ‒ the common fisheries policy is one of the most integrated in europe but it still has shortcomings, such as those caused by differences between member states in the application of controls, which creates an unfair situation in the sector. i am in favour of a uniform approach to fisheries controls in europe, which will also make it possible to identify shortcomings in the application of the rules and improve the harmonization of controls, both in terms of procedures and in terms of training and penalties.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution for the creation of a union mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the founding values and principles must also be applied within our union. we do not currently have the instruments to do this in the same way that we demand compliance from the outside. given the weakening of democracy and the rule of law in countries such as poland and hungary, it is necessary to adopt mechanisms such as this one to strengthen the respect for fundamental rights and to prevent any kind of authoritarian drift within the union. the mechanism contained in this resolution contains various instruments and provisions to achieve the objectives mentioned. in particular, i would like to highlight the request to delete article 51 of the charter of fundamental rights (cdfeu) and to make the charter a declaration of rights of the union. this would strengthen the implementation of the eutf in all union actions and legislation. since my parliamentary activity i have always advocated the adoption of an application of article 51 which would enable the union to guarantee the respect of fundamental rights.

vice-president of the commission. – mr president, honourable members of the european parliament, as you know, the commission has tabled a proposal for mid-term review revision of the financial framework in mid-september. i would like to express our gratitude to parliament and especially to the two rapporteurs for the own initiative report, ms thomas and mr olbrycht, as well as for the work you have done to prepare a draft resolution, which we are pleased to see incorporates many of the proposals the commission has tabled. thank you for that. we all recognise that we are taking on this task at a time of multiple, successive and overlapping crises, and in that environment it is absolutely paramount for the european union to demonstrate the capacity to act. in our proposal we focused on two dimensions of this capacity to act: the financial dimension (additional financial resources) and the flexibility aspect. i will go through those two in some detail. in terms of beefing up our capacity to fund priorities with very strong focus on jobs and growth and dealing with migration, we are proposing to make eur 6.3 billion available. this is funding for very important objectives. for example, more young people in regions affected by particularly high levels of unemployment to find targeted support for integrating or reintegrating into the labour market. for giving more young people the chance to participate in actions supported by erasmus+. to allow the european research council to finance more high-quality projects in frontier research. they are also about achieving a more effective management of migration flows so we can help refugees to integrate in their host countries, secure a better control of our external borders, fight illegal immigration and address the root causes of migration. but in itself this amount does not reflect the full level of the proposed refocusing of eu spending, because we have also taken a very careful look at how we can realign financial resources, for example, in our support for the connecting europe facility, which has very broad endorsement here in parliament. we have topped it up with eur 400 million but we also are proposing to shift eur 1 billion from financial instruments to grants under the transport strand of this facility. a big share of the proposed top-ups goes to instruments that have a significant multiplier or leverage effect: cosme, efsi, the new european fund for sustainable development, the increased eib external lending mandate, the union’s instrument for macro-financial assistance to our neighbouring countries. and we have done that looking into every possible source, but within the parameters agreed in the 2013 multiannual financial framework (mff). secondly, on flexibility. given that we continue to face a particularly volatile international environment, opting for an extension of flexibility is the responsible thing to do so we can act swiftly in crisis situations. this mff runs until the end of 2020. this means more than four years still to go, with our existing flexibility already stretched to its limits. so for this reason we are proposing to double the size of the flexibility instrument and the emergency aid reserve, as well as to establish a european union crisis reserve financed from decommitments we have fully taken on board, and that is a proposal from parliament. and just to say that, if we had had this crisis reserve in place at the beginning of this mff, it would have allowed us to finance the refugee facility for turkey entirely. in other words, it would have avoided seeking complex, off-budget satellite solutions; we would have had the resources available to us. let me stress in closing that our proposals are not only about the tangible things i have described. we are making a very serious effort to simplify the rules by which the union’s programmes are implemented so as to reduce administrative burden for beneficiaries and public administrations, to make the eu funds more predictable and more flexible and the results of their deployment more visible to our people. we are, of course, at your disposal – parliament, the council – to engage so we can make the mid-term review a very prudent and helpful for the union exercise. of course, we look forward to the debate. we will be listening very carefully to all of you.

in writing. this package on corporation tax, which aims to harmonise and consolidate the base through two directives, should be welcomed. the original proposal, from 2011, has been blocked in the council by certain member states, which is truly unacceptable. the internal market cannot be built and tax justification ensured if some states continue to think of using their tax regimes to artificially attract profits generated in another jurisdiction. the commission is right to separate biccis into two directives, since the consolidation of the basis and the allocation formula are undoubtedly the most controversial elements. but it is enough to harmonize the basis (mainly deductions) because if the same calculation formula is not applied to settle the tax, the artificial transfer of profits will be maintained. it is also important to reduce the applicable threshold from eur 750 million to eur 40. we must ensure that the council does its job, so that one or two countries do not block these measures. for the spanish socialists, the fight against tax evasion and avoidance is an absolute priority, which must not be undermined by an anachronistic claim to national sovereignty.

in writing. with the adoption of this directive, known as the web directive, all public authorities' websites and mobile applications, including electronic and multimedia documents, in europe now have to be accessible to a wide range of users, including 80 million people with disabilities. this is a crucial milestone towards achieving an inclusive digital society, in which people with disabilities and other users have access to online services on an equal basis with others, which is a right enshrined in the un crpd. the union must ensure that it is implemented at national level and that the derogations provided for in the text are not abused. by monitoring and reporting to the commission and a group of experts made up of stakeholders at european level, the union can more easily address problems in implementation and work more effectively. in addition, further advocacy should be made for other relevant or complementary union legislation, including the european accessibility act and the revision of the audiovisual media services directive to ensure that what is not covered by the web directive is adequately addressed.
member of the commission. – madam president, i am very pleased to appear before the plenary here today with a view to successfully concluding our work on the regulation on protective measures against pests of plants, more commonly referred to as the plant health regulation. this is a very important piece of legislation. it is the result of a great deal of hard work by parliament, the council and the commission. its outcome is, i believe, a credit to all three institutions. we all share a deep and common understanding of the fundamental importance of plant health and its link to the protection of our people’s health, agriculture, food chain and environment. furthermore, we collectively recognise that outbreaks of plant pest will occur from time to time. this is inevitable due to the intensification of global trade as well as climate change. the case of the outbreak of xylella fastidiosa in italy, france and, to a small extent, in germany, is the most recent reminder of the serious threat that pests pose for our farmers, agricultural production, environment and the livelihoods of so many producers. another example is the pine nematode outbreak in portugal, affecting our forestry industry. we must ensure we are best prepared to deal with future outbreaks of plant pests and also make sure that our territory remains protected from the entry of non—european pests. the new regulation has been drafted and negotiated while taking into account all of those concerns. in this view it will introduce more protective rules for the early detection and eradication of dangerous plant pests, if found present in eu territory, and more proactive tools and actions such as the prioritisation of pest action plans for eradication. contingency plans and simulation exercises allow the european union to adopt a more proactive policy against the entry of pests from other countries and the import of high—risk plants and plant products; harmonise and simplify the rules concerning certification of plants and plants products, thus facilitating their production, marketing and controls; and specify the responsibilities of the producers through legislation and authorisation before they produce, market and certify the health of their plants. all those new provisions are based on the concept that we have to do more in order to suffer less from the devastating effects of some plant diseases. i take the opportunity to recall that member states remain responsible for import controls and surveillance in their territories to avoid the presence of those pests. therefore more resources need to be allocated by the member states to cope with those important tasks. otherwise this eu law will not bring the expected benefits. in the coming years the commission will focus its inspection programme on import control audits and will check whether european union plant health rules are implemented in the member states in an effective and harmonised manner. all the elements included in this new framework are well thought out and have been thoroughly discussed with all interested parties. i therefore look forward with both hope and expectation to a broad agreement and endorsement of this file. our work will, of course, continue with the development of dedicated and implementing acts and through the practical implementation of new rules once agreed.
on behalf of the ppe group madam president, commissioner, i would first of all like to thank the rapporteur and all the alternative rapporteurs and all those who have worked on this report because it was really the best agreement we could have come to. this regulation has a clear objective, which is to protect european production from harmful organisms imported from other countries. the history of plant pathology is full of examples of plants that are carriers without symptoms - carriers of diseases - but that, when imported to other latitudes, wreak havoc on other species and other genera. this risk is aggravated by the single market, as the commissioner has rightly said, because one country imports and another crop suffers the damage. as an example, we have the xylella fastidiosa - which you have also mentioned - which continues to affect italy, france and germany dramatically. all indications are that this pest was introduced into europe by an ornamental coffee plant imported through the port of rotterdam in the netherlands. that is precisely what we are trying to avoid with the preventive measures of the fight against imported pests. the new regulation introduces a new mechanism to combat emerging risks of epidemics unknown to the european union by means of temporary action applications. the text we are about to adopt is therefore a very important improvement and i ask all the members of parliament to support it, because it is the best possible text.
i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the future of the european union, but that we should be concerned about the future of the european union. xylella fastidiosa was just one example of what's happening. it is essential that plant material entering the european union is strictly controlled and monitored, and that is why we support this text. but we also need mechanisms to detect the presence and development of pests of invasive species that enter the european union with imports of other agricultural products, as was the case with the velvet wasp. that is why we are calling for a european strategy that counts on farmers for early detection, monitoring and investigation, and for establishing the necessary actions to prevent, eradicate and prevent the spread of invasive species. at the same time, we believe that it is necessary to define action protocols to combat pests and invasive species in order to protect health, the environment and water.
on behalf of the green group, madam president, the spread of the xylella fastidiosa bacterium is destroying the ancient olive trees in apulia and has now spread to corsica and germany. as you know, it is one of the most destructive plant pests to have come to europe from outside our borders, but it is not the only one. the regulation on the prevention of the introduction of pests needed to be updated and we therefore welcome this proposal on which we have worked, especially my colleague jordi sebastià, whom i am replacing, to make it as safe as possible. we are, however, calling on the commission to draw up the implementing acts of the new regulation within a decade to exempt low-risk seeds, farmer-to-farmer seed exchange and the conservation of genetic biodiversity. the consequences of pests such as black spot or citrus scab are incalculable and we are very concerned that the commission has recently tried, by means of an implementing act, to amend directive 2000/29/ec in order to limit controls on citrus fruit from third countries, which would leave our producers defenseless. i therefore ask that the intention of the regulation which we are going to vote on at this part-session be respected and that the commission not seek subterfuge to limit controls to the import of citrus fruit. don't forget we have to work to protect our producers. that is what they expect from a european union so that this time they do not fail.
madam president, i would like to add my congratulations to our rapporteur, mrs mcintyre, and to all the other rapporteurs, in particular my colleague mrs dancila, who have been working together to make this a good agreement, the best possible agreement. i would have liked to have been able to reach a positive list on plant matters, but i understand that a global agreement was needed for all the countries of the european union and therefore this is my agreement and this is a great agreement. the member states must now carry out the checks. to do this, means are needed. i do not agree with mr huitema on this, who says that this will cost us money; of course it does cost money, but it is for the protection of the european union's plants. i therefore hope that the member states will take account of this new regulation. and let me tell you something, commissioner: we are not going to amend, by means of annexes, certain criteria which are now being improved by this regulation. i am referring to the amendment to directive 2000/29/ec for oranges for juice. let's not change the rules of the game.
madam president, commissioner, i think it is important that we have a debate on trans fats, because both efsa and who have made recommendations to reduce their intake. the association between these trans fats and cardiovascular disease is a proven fact, and we should do everything we can to reduce their intake. but we must not forget that certain products of animal origin naturally contain these trans fats and that they are necessary products in our daily diet and therefore we should not in any case prohibit these fats which are natural and not added. the important thing is to have a varied and balanced diet. in spain, the food safety and nutrition act already requires economic operators to reduce these fatty acids in production processes. however, it is important to harmonise legislation at european level. it is essential that awareness, information and nutritional education campaigns on trans fats are carried out within a framework that encourages balanced diets and healthy lifestyles. the involvement of the agri-food industry is necessary to reformulate and improve products with the ultimate aim of eliminating or reducing the content of trans-fatty acids added to food. i know that the commission is aware of the need for action at european level to harmonize legislation on trans fatty acids and i believe that this motion for a resolution is a good way of doing so.
madam president, i agree with virtually all of those who have spoken on the need for harmonization of the rules to take action on hydrogenated fatty acids - trans fats - especially in industrial processes. it is recognised by international organisations and efsa that limits on consumption should be established. i therefore agree with mr häusling. so many environmental impact studies are not bad, but i think the result is clear. so let us take the initiative now and let the commission take the initiative. we have to be very careful about the way we use our money, and we have to be very careful about the way we use it.
madam president, i have to ask you. the conclusions adopted by the council in the last 18 months do not take up a hundred pages. eighteen months ago the council deplored the continued loss of life in the mediterranean and spoke of the need for an effective asylum policy and said it was waiting for mr juncker's plan. they talked about the migration crisis and the refugee crisis. a few months later, those words disappeared and we started talking about the migration crisis: immigrants and irregular migrants. for this council we have gone much further. now, we're talking about addressing other elements of the overall strategy. these other elements are women and children; people who are cold; children who are not in school in greece; a human plug: a situation that unhcr says is unbearable in lesbos. the council is responsible for negligence. and mr juncker, unfortunately - and i am very sorry, i would not like that to happen - is also an accomplice. today it has eluded all the people who are drowning in the central mediterranean. it's not like you. and the criterion of 'flexible solidarity' is the criterion of 'non-solidarity to the letter'.
madam president, after several years in this house, i have come to the conclusion that a semiologist, even if he is a mere amateur, is better able to interpret the council's findings than a member of parliament. if that semiologist goes to the spanish version of the council conclusions, he will find that the terms 'controls' and 'returns' appear up to fourteen times, and the term 'prevent' appears twice: a real blow. and it is true that we must try to organize and regulate the arrivals, but above all we must prevent the departure of the immigrants from their places of origin. and to prevent the exit, the european union has to strengthen its capacity as a global actor and its intervention through, of course, the global strategy, through the european pact on immigration and asylum, through investments abroad and through the development of our security and defence capacity. mr juncker has said, and the president-in-office of the council has also said, that initial steps have been taken along this road: some agreements with african countries. that's the way to go, but you have to go much faster and you have to go in a much more intense way. and the european union must play a relevant role in ensuring humanitarian access to the places where the real barbarity is taking place: the emergency medical evacuation of aleppo and the care of its suffering citizens, who are subjected to continuous bombardment. a final point concerns youth unemployment. it appears in paragraph 19 of the chapter 'other economic and global issues', but it is a fundamental issue for the union and we must not abandon or conform to this problem. we cannot simply wait until december or february next year for results to begin to show.
madam president, we are at our worst. brexit can become a method and a model. europe is showing that it is a project that can be reversed. and the refugee crisis has shown us that our solidarity is insufficient and, moreover, is waning. besides, we've now blocked the deal with decent canada. if we are not able to sign an agreement with canada, we will not sign a free trade agreement with anyone. free trade will continue, but we will be left out, and to be left out of free trade means less prosperity, means less employment and means less welfare. it is not reasonable for the interests of a region of two million people to block the interests of a continent of half a billion people. democracy works in reverse: the interest and opinion of the majority always trump the opinion of the minority. globalization is a fact; it is not an ideology. and those who oppose globalization and those who oppose free trade do so by using cell phones from companies whose employees are located in the united states, china, mexico, brazil, singapore, taiwan, japan, france, germany, israel, malta and belgium. it is a real contradiction. as i said, globalization is a fact; it is not an ideology. opposing globalization is opposing the advance of the times. populism is a reaction; it's not a response. complex problems require complex solutions and, of course, in an adult world, being in politics with childish attitudes constitutes a political pathology.
madam president, the latest european summit and the content of the bratislava declaration and roadmap could give rise to hope, but yesterday's debate on the budget and priorities for 2016 illustrates the difference between the big words of the states and their 'squieter' deeds in the effort to build a true european sovereignty. we need leadership, not a declaration of intent, because syria is still on fire and there is no common position on russia's role or the solution to the refugee and immigration crisis. because the unification of energy and digital markets, the resurrection of our social model with special emphasis on the youth guarantee and the fight against poverty, are still pending. because the states are not meeting the priorities which give meaning to the european fund for strategic investments or are hampering our trade agreement policy with the ceta crisis. because we're slow on the outside dumping. and to lead a europe that resolutely overcomes these bottlenecks is the best policy against walls, which even the populists who defend them know are useless.
madam president, i have paid particular attention to the immigration chapter of this european council and i am of course struck by the positive assessment of the infamous deal with turkey. has the council given any thought to the extremely negative assessment it received from this parliament? has the council given any thought to the situation after the coup, with thousands of journalists and judges in prison? has the council given serious thought to the negative view it continues to perpetrate on immigration, on foreigners and, in particular, on the arrival on european soil of very vulnerable people: women, helpless children drowning in the mediterranean as a result of the diversion towards the mediterranean of the migratory pressure contained in numbers in turkey? has the council made a commitment to strengthen solidarity with italy and greece not just the european border guard? and above all, has the council spoken about the infamous anti-european referendum that took place in hungary on 2 october?
madam president, it is not just wallonia, ladies and gentlemen. mr ska keller has stressed that the council has turned a blind eye to opposition in the streets and in some parliaments. i would like to add another fact: more than 2 000 towns and cities in europe have already declared themselves free of ceta and ttip, and this should also be taken into account. so no, it's not just wallonia. a note on the arrival of migrants and refugees in europe. the european commission welcomes the fact that fewer people arrive from turkey and therefore die in the aegean sea. but the commission is hiding the b-side of all this: the unacceptable limbo in which they are living at our external borders and in some places within the union, and the 3 740 people who have died since 1 january in the mediterranean sea.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the budget resolution because, although it is a less hardline position than that of the commission or, needless to say, the council, it still presupposes 5% cuts. although there are aspects which restore some of the points of interest (the youth employment initiative, although it is only applied by 7% of the member states), it also does so with others of a security nature, it continues to rely on the problematic juncker plan to promote investment, and i do not find a redistributive character in the model proposed.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution stresses the need to strengthen the european budget and give it greater social and environmental content, without calling into question its neoliberal drift. although i agree with these reforms, i consider them insufficient and have finally decided to abstain.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution stresses the need to strengthen the european budget and give it greater social and environmental content, without calling into question its neoliberal drift. although i agree with these reforms, i consider them insufficient and have finally decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the resolution reiterates parliament's priorities for the revision of the mff, endorsing the financialization of investments, the austerity conditionality of cohesion and development funds, the privatisation of research, the commercialisation of agricultural policies and the use of external funds to strengthen europe's strength and the geopolitical adventurism of european elites. i voted against to express my criticism of the current use of european funds, which have become yet another instrument of neoliberal policies.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has no powers to define the multiannual financial framework, which is the framework that structures and limits the evolution of the budget over 7 years. it's the council that decides. however, the pressure of the union's crisis situation has led to a parliamentary consensus on the need to strengthen european budgets to meet existing challenges (refugees, investment crises, security, employment, etc.). the resolution points to a number of positive aspects. the commission is also proposing to increase the resources, reform the own resources system, assess the new flexibility conditions for the new mff, criticise the council, and call for the withdrawal of 'rebates' (discounts on the contributions of more than 10 member states to the european budget), the possibility of reusing unused resources and the unity of the union budget against intergovernmental funds. however, the resolution seems to be a good-natured attempt to legitimize itself, because there is really no negotiation at stake in which parliament decides. in fact, the budget proposal for 2017 goes in the opposite direction, thus reducing the credibility of this resolution. that's why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the authors of this resolution on the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework, which underlines parliament's continuing concern about the insufficient resources available under the current multiannual financial framework. new crises and priorities that have emerged in recent years, in particular the migration and refugee crisis, external emergencies, internal security issues, the agricultural crisis, efsi funding and the persistent high level of unemployment, especially among young people, must be taken into account.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, to give a clear political response to the presentation of the revision of the mff package presented by the commission on 14 september. while i generally welcome the commission's decision to propose a revision of the mff, i stress the scarcity of resources available under the current framework to address the political commitments and strategic objectives of the union and, in this regard, we stress once again the responsibility of the member states to match the pledges with the means to ensure a response in line with the emerging challenges. i welcome the proposal on flexibility, but i regret that there is no proposal for an upward revision of the ceilings of the current mff, which is necessary if we are to meet the present and future challenges and meet our objectives. finally, i call on the council to start negotiating the financial framework urgently, as we cannot negotiate the 2017 budget without having a framework under which to negotiate.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament has no powers to define the multiannual financial framework, which is the framework that structures and limits the evolution of the budget over 7 years. it's the council that decides. however, the pressure of the union's crisis situation has led to a parliamentary consensus on the need to strengthen european budgets to meet existing challenges (refugees, investment crises, security, employment, etc.). the resolution points to a number of positive aspects. the commission is also proposing to increase the resources, reform the own resources system, assess the new flexibility conditions for the new mff, criticise the council, and call for the withdrawal of 'rebates' (discounts on the contributions of more than 10 member states to the european budget), the possibility of reusing unused resources and the unity of the union budget against intergovernmental funds. however, the resolution seems to be a good-natured attempt to legitimize itself, because there is really no negotiation at stake in which parliament decides. in fact, the budget proposal for 2017 goes in the opposite direction, thus reducing the credibility of this resolution. that's why i abstained.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament has no powers to define the multiannual financial framework, which is the framework that structures and limits the evolution of the budget over 7 years. it's the council that decides. however, the pressure of the union's crisis situation has led to a parliamentary consensus on the need to strengthen european budgets to meet existing challenges (refugees, investment crises, security, employment, etc.). the resolution points to a number of positive aspects. the commission is also proposing to increase the resources, reform the own resources system, assess the new flexibility conditions for the new mff, criticise the council, and call for the withdrawal of 'rebates' (discounts on the contributions of more than 10 member states to the european budget), the possibility of reusing unused resources and the unity of the union budget against intergovernmental funds. however, the resolution seems to be a good-natured attempt to legitimize itself, because there is really no negotiation at stake in which parliament decides. in fact, the budget proposal for 2017 goes in the opposite direction, thus reducing the credibility of this resolution. that's why i abstained.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mobilisation of this european globalisation adjustment fund, maintaining a consistent position with the other requests for mobilisation of this fund, as it may result in compensation for estonian workers affected by the impacts of capitalist globalisation. i am aware that this is only a bandage on a wound, and that these funds can bring relief to these workers, which is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted yes. the fund is intended to compensate, with mainly training measures, 800 workers laid off by four estonian companies, most of them russian-speaking, in the petrochemical sector, which has clear problems of competitiveness with china. as we often say, this fund does not solve the employment problem, which can only be remedied by new investment plans with sectoral transitions, but it is a mechanism that at least gives support to the victims of these processes. alternatively, companies using these funds should be monitored, because one of the risks is that they could in practice be facilitating relocation processes. doesn't seem to be the case. but it certainly begs to be reconsidered in terms of thinking of an alternative line to these funds.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank mr negrescu for his work on this report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund requested by estonia in the petroleum and chemicals sector. it is a response to a request from estonia to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant in three companies and will benefit 800 workers made redundant.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund: application egf/2016/003 ee/oil and chemicals. europe and the world are engaged in a profound process of globalisation which, while a source of trade and wealth creation, can also entail risks to which we must be very attentive. as a result of this process, there are sectors which are more exposed to international competition, and the union must therefore respond to those citizens who lose their jobs as a result of globalisation. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) provides support for workers who lose their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation or the global economic and financial crisis.

in writing. ‒ this request for the mobilisation of € 1 131 358 from the egf, the european globalisation adjustment fund, for estonia, seeks to benefit 800 workers made redundant in the coking and oil refining sector. it should be noted that the egf was created precisely to provide additional support for workers who suffer the consequences of major structural changes in world trade and that, in this case, these dismissed workers will be offered ten types of measures. these include, for example, reimbursement of training costs to employers, labour market training, practical work experience, psychological support and support linked to participation in formal studies. i am voting in favour of the request because the measures will promote employment and are compatible with the transition to an efficient and sustainable regional economy.

madam president, i voted in favour of this directive. i spoke yesterday in plenary, but i did not have time to say all my points, which is why i am using this institution. on the one hand, i very much welcome the fact that we are making public institutions' websites accessible to eu citizens and disabled people in general who want to work with the sites and want information from the public sector. on the other hand, and this is what i did not have time to say yesterday, i do not agree with the part which essentially introduces bureaucratic control of this directive, whereby the states will have to send a report every year on how the directive is being implemented to the commission and officials will evaluate it. i think it would be better if the state authorities only responded to citizens' complaints if there were any wrongdoing, rather than having thousands of reports gathered here in brussels and then evaluated by someone. so it's a good idea, but the controls, in my opinion, are not very fancy.
in writing. ‒ around 80 million people in the union have a disability. with the ageing of the population, the number of people with disabilities or age-related difficulties in accessing the internet will continue to increase. as a socialist, i believe that it is our responsibility as a society to improve the living conditions of our fellow citizens and to do this it is essential to increase accessibility to public sector information and services in the digital age. i have therefore voted in favour of this directive, which represents an important step towards an inclusive digital society. with the new rules, the websites and mobile applications of all public bodies - government agencies, courts, police, hospitals, universities or libraries - will have to meet common accessibility standards and, from this house we have also ensured that applications used on mobile phones and tablets will be subject to the new legislation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because accessibility to public services should be the priority of any public sector web application. i believe it is essential that the public sector should be at the forefront of both web application development and all kinds of accessible services to ensure access to and effective participation in the rights of all citizens. the diversity of functions should not be a limit to the exercise of the right, and it is essential that the public sector be the guarantor of this maxim which should be universally applicable. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on accessibility of websites, because it proposes the harmonisation of minimum requirements at european level to guarantee access to information on websites. the text is a second reading, for which the commission made its first proposal in 2012, in the context of the adoption of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities in 2006. this proposal was made in particular to increase the accessibility of public service providers' websites (websites and mobile applications) to all people, including people with disabilities. the directive aims to establish harmonised minimum requirements to ensure access for all, particularly in the area of access to information. parliament sought to extend the scope of the directive and to introduce additional measures in the field of monitoring, information and enforcement. the council reached agreement on second reading, which parliament supported without amendments.
in writing. ‒ i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs charanzová, on this report on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites and mobile applications. it is a recommendation for second reading which goes beyond the agreement reached by the two legislative institutions. it is essential that this directive be transposed within the time limits laid down in the text so that it can enter into force in the member states as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because accessibility to public services should be the priority of any public sector web application. i believe it is essential that the public sector should be at the forefront of both web application development and all kinds of accessible services to ensure access to and effective participation in the rights of all citizens. the diversity of functions should not be a limit to the exercise of the right, and it is essential that the public sector be the guarantor of this maxim which should be universally applicable. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a directive lays down specific technical provisions for member states to make the content of certain types of public sector bodies' websites (which provide information and services essential for citizens' participation in the economy and society) accessible. the directive aims to approximate the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states on the accessibility of the websites of public sector bodies by defining harmonised requirements. i am voting in favour of this important legislative instrument to promote the accessibility of websites and mobile applications, aware that there is still a long way to go before full accessibility is achieved.

i have been asked by citizens in my country, the czech republic, whether it is necessary for the ep to adopt such a regulation, whether individual member states should not regulate the problem of plant pests in a comprehensive way themselves. at first glance, it seems that this is perhaps a european unnecessary adjustment. i myself am not in favour of too much european legislation and too much extension of european legislation. i respect the principle of subsidiarity, but in this case i voted in favour of this proposal because it is clear that the fight against pests which are europe-wide cannot be carried out by individual national states alone. in short, pests do not respect or know any national borders and the fight against them can be effective if we work together and if the eu coordinates this. this proposal contributes to this. that's why i supported it, because i'm sure that the pest control will be more effective than if each state acted alone.
in writing. ‒ although there are aspects of this report that can be improved, such as the implementation of preventive measures and measures to combat and adapt to climate change, i voted against the amendment proposed by alde which calls for the rejection of the legislative proposal. i think it is important that this report is adopted and i am very pleased with the progress made in the negotiations, which have led to the regulation imposing strict controls on the importation of plant material into the union. this is essential to prevent future outbreaks of pests and plant diseases (such as the problem of xylella fastidiosa in olive trees).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of introducing new measures to stop the entry into the eu of plant pests such as xylella fastidiosa and to equip member states with the means to combat their spread. the new regulation introduces preventive and rapid response mechanisms for suspect imports, intensifies surveillance within the eu and requires all member states to have contingency plans for possible outbreaks. those measures serve to protect union citizens from pests that a plant, plant product or other object from a third country could introduce.
in writing. ‒ i vote against this amendment. i agree with this regulation because its aim is to prevent the entry and spread of two types of plant pests: quarantine pests and regulated non-quarantine pests. at the last agri committee meeting on 13 october, this report was approved by 28 votes in favour. thanks to the amendments made by the shadow report, this document on plant pests calls for the implementation of strict controls on the import of plant material into the european union with the intention of avoiding future plant pests and diseases (such as xylella fastidiosa that attacks olive trees and caused a 20% increase in the price of oil in 2015). after this second reading, we think it would be good if it were adopted, and that is why we think it is important to vote against this amendment proposed by the alde group. alde votes against because it considers the proposal to be too restrictive as regards the import regime, whereas we want a restrictive import regime to protect our plants and crops.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement on protection measures against plant pests, against my group and against the amendment tabled by my group against the agreement. the report calls for further measures to curb the entry into the eu of plant pests such as xylella fastidiosa and to equip member states with the means to combat their spread. the new regulation introduces preventive and rapid response mechanisms for suspect imports, intensifies surveillance within the eu and requires all member states to have contingency plans for possible outbreaks. this regulation will entail certain measures which will have to be put into effect as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the final adoption of the agreements reached with the commission and the council on the new european basic plant health regulation. the union plant protection regime is crucial for the development and competitiveness of european agriculture. the final agreement does not include the existing positive list system for animal health, which we would have liked to have applied also to plant health, but it does substantially improve the commission's initial proposal through a closed system for 'high risk' plants and vegetables. those classified as 'low risk' will continue under the current system of import controls but with the addition of the plant passport, now implemented at european level.
in writing. although there are aspects of this report that can be improved, such as the implementation of preventive measures and measures to combat and adapt to climate change, i voted against the amendment proposed by alde, which calls for the rejection of the legislative proposal. i think it is important that this report is adopted and i am very pleased with the progress made in the negotiations, which have led to the regulation imposing strict controls on the importation of plant material into the union. this is essential to prevent future outbreaks of pests and plant diseases (such as the problem of xylella fastidiosa in olive trees).
in writing. ‒ this report aims to combat new pests and diseases from third countries that threaten our crops and harvests. however, even if the text indirectly refers to the effects of globalisation on the proliferation of invasive species and organisms, it is content to respond to these threats simply by improving controls and traceability. this includes reducing the risks posed by these invasive species and organisms to an acceptable level. but the increase in controls will not stop these species entering the internal market and substantially increases the powers of the european commission. the commission will be able to decide on the eradication of affected plants, as it did this year with olive trees affected by xylella fastidiosa in puglia. i therefore abstained on this report, which does not tackle the causes of the problem, namely the opening up of frontiers without respect for environmental balances. in reality, the commission will not hesitate to completely eradicate crops, sometimes ancestral, which are very important for our lands, even though it is itself partly responsible for the proliferation of invasive species that attack these crops.

in writing. ‒ in order to protect european agriculture by preventing the entry and spread of pests into european territory, which cause serious economic problems, this draft legislative resolution of the european parliament endorses the council's position at first reading on the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on protective measures against plant pests, amending part of the existing regulation. i am voting in favour because parliament's position has been respected. this regulation will protect the health, the economy and the competitiveness of the union's plant production sector, while maintaining our policy of opening up trade.

in writing. ‒ although the pests of plants regulation as negotiated will impose strict controls on importing plant material into the eu, so hopefully avoiding future outbreaks of plant diseases (like the recent xylella fastidiosa attacking olive trees), there will be increased costs and unintended consequences for seed-saving operations by plant conservation charities under the restrictions on internet sales and distribution, and also on farmer-saved seed, whereby farmers breed their own seed varieties using seed exchanges. this is why i abstained in the final vote.
