in writing. ‒ the economic recovery in europe remains slow, fragile and, above all, highly uneven: growth is weak, unemployment rates remain very high in many countries and investment is at record lows. europe as a whole must strengthen the investment plan so that it is not just the sum of its parts but a genuine union policy, and countries with trade surpluses must invest more to balance their economies and improve domestic demand. we also call on the member states to take effective measures to ensure decent jobs with decent wages, adequate social protection and decent public pensions. we also need fairer and more severe taxation not only of average and working incomes but also of capital incomes. and finally, we need a european minimum income framework to lift the 120 million people living in the union today at risk of social exclusion out of poverty. only then can we overcome this long and painful crisis in a just and sustainable way. i have therefore voted in favour of this report and i am deeply sorry that the other left-wing groups have not joined in these calls.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because, despite the significant references to the social problems that austerity policies are causing in the member states of the european union, it continues to bet on austerity as the only way forward, even legitimising the possible sanctions on spain and portugal that are under discussion. i reject the imposition of austerity policies outright, because they are a complete economic nonsense, which only increases poverty and inequality. the same applies to macro-conditionality, which, if applied in the iberian peninsula, could have a serious impact, accelerating the destruction of our economy. the report is unable to propose an alternative, calling for more austerity. this is what we are fighting against and i have therefore decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this resolution on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies. although the resolution has a social vision which i share, many of the contributions and proposals put forward by my political group were not taken into account. however, i voted against my group's line to withdraw the paragraph welcoming the commission's focusing its priorities in the 2016 country-specific recommendations on supporting investment in innovation, growth and job creation, and urging the pursuit of socially balanced structural reforms, and the promotion of responsible public finances. i believe that these recommendations are particularly necessary for spain's economic recovery and progress. i also rejected the amendments in favour of leaving the single currency and strengthening the sovereignty of the member states, proposed by the eurosceptic political groups. i also voted in favour of an amendment by the greens calling for the creation of a european deposit guarantee scheme, which would make it possible to strengthen the banking union in the face of the weakness of the financial system during the crisis.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i am opposed to the european semester mechanism as a whole. the european semester is intended to subject the budgets of governments to scrutiny by the european commission, which ensures that certain macroeconomic objectives are met and that the so-called structural reforms are implemented. the facts show that the effect of the austerity measures has been procyclical, that is to say, they have worsened the economic crisis. although the rapporteur's work in the shadow of the gue/ngl has led to positive references to public investment, i still do not share the diagnosis, nor the solution.
in writing. ‒ i appreciate the work done in the econ committee on this report on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies and their implementation of the priorities for 2016, but i abstained in the final vote on this report as the key points of our group were not covered by the rapporteur. on the contrary, i voted in favour of two amendments calling for progress towards the establishment of a european deposit guarantee scheme and for the eu institutions to initiate and support a process of renegotiation of public debt in the most indebted countries.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report bearing in mind that the union's economy will grow less than expected according to the european economic forecasts, as euro area gdp is expected to increase by only 1.6%, to reach 1.8% in 2017. it is therefore necessary to improve growth, cohesion, productivity and competitiveness by improving sustainable investment and addressing the shortcomings in the completion of the single market which are preventing the union from reaching its full growth potential. we must support investment in innovation, growth and job creation, pursue socially balanced structural reforms and promote responsible public finances. similarly, it is particularly important to make labour markets more inclusive and to reduce social exclusion and widening disparities in income and wealth.

in writing. ‒ my support for the implementation of the priorities of the european semester for economic policy coordination, which emphasises the need to improve the union's overall capacity to grow, create and maintain quality jobs and thus fight high unemployment rates. another measure is to strengthen inclusive education systems, which encourage innovation and creativity and teach skills relevant to the labour market. we must also work on policies that promote sustainable development, including a real focus on research and development spending.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe it is important to regulate and set limits on the presence of industrial trans fats in food. consumption of these trans fats through industrially produced partially hydrogenated vegetable oils has been associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, infertility, alzheimer's disease, obesity and some types of cancer. it is therefore urgent that the commission should issue a legislative proposal setting legally binding limits for trans fats.
in writing. ‒ this proposal is timely and based on consolidated, updated and evidence-based eu and who health, consumer and market information considerations. the commission notes that the measures cannot be purely national and that measures at union level are needed to reduce the average intake of agw. a trans fat labelling policy may be the most difficult measure to implement effectively. the financial impact of the trans fat ban has been shown to be minimal in countries that have implemented it, due to the low costs of implementation and monitoring. the labelling strategy to inform would only affect certain foods, but not unpackaged or restaurant food. we also ask the commission to carry out a thorough impact assessment to assess the costs and benefits of different thresholds and to take specific account of the effects on smes. we also call on the food industry to give priority to alternative solutions such as the use of improved oils, new fat modification procedures or combinations of agt substitutes.
in writing. ‒ at the end of 2015, the european commission presented a report on the health problem of trans fats in food, but did not submit the corresponding legislative draft. after a year of waiting and continuous complaints from civil society, consumer organisations, medical societies and others, i have voted in favour of this report to achieve a single union legislation on this issue. the united states has banned the use of artificial trans fats in food products from 2018, so this legislation would accompany the european industry in its exports. the approval of upwards quality standards should be reciprocal and not as anticipated under atci. it is important to stress that the incentive for legislation should be to reduce cardiovascular disease as the main cause of death in europe and not the market, which i understand is not clear from the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on trans fatty acids because i believe that the eu should set mandatory limits for these industrially produced acids, as they can increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, infertility, alzheimer's, diabetes and obesity for consumers. the commission believes that only one in three eu consumers is aware of trans fats, which shows that the labelling measures are insufficient. i therefore voted in favour of the ecr group's amendment calling for mandatory labelling. unfortunately, it has not been approved. what is being asked of the european commission is to propose a legal limit in the eu to the content of these acids in all food as soon as possible, preferably within two years.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution, aware that the issue of agt is a priority for the european parliament because of the risks they pose to the health of european citizens. it has been shown that limiting agt can provide rapid and significant health benefits, as exemplified by the successful experience of denmark which in 2003 established a national limit of 2% agt in oils and fats. similarly, it is important to bear in mind that the majority of the union population, in particular the most vulnerable, lack information on agts and the health consequences of their consumption, which may prevent them from making informed decisions. the union institutions must therefore take measures to reduce the average intake of agt considerably.
in writing. ‒ trans-fatty acids are found in fats used in the food industry. these fatty acids are particularly involved in the development of cardiovascular diseases. in the face of these public health concerns, the european parliament has proposed legislation to limit the presence of these trans fatty acids in agri-food products. in the face of such technical issues, labelling alone cannot be enough. i have raised, in amendments with my colleagues in the envi committee, that such a proposal should in no way affect dairy products which can also be sources of trans fatty acids but whose health effects are very different from those of trans fatty acids from industrial fats. i also indicated in those same amendments that it would be better to support companies that are committed to reducing trans fats. several experiments in some member states have shown that it is economically and technically possible to reduce these trans fats. to facilitate the work of our many exporting smes and to protect the health of consumers, i therefore supported this motion for a resolution.

in writing. ‒ trans fatty acids (tfa) are a type of unsaturated fatty acid that have been widely used by the food industry since the 1950s. they are added to foods because they improve the texture of processed foods, increase their shelf life, or as a cheap alternative to other fats. there is now broad scientific consensus that high trans consumption significantly increases the risk of coronary heart disease, and may also be associated with more other diseases than any other nutrient per unit of calories. although the average consumption of these fats in the union is below the levels recommended at national and international level, this is not the case for all population groups. for these reasons, i have voted in favour of this oral question calling for legislative measures to eliminate the presence of agts in the union food supply chain in the long term, either by introducing mandatory labelling on the content of agts or by a legal union limit to the content of industrial agts in all food products.

on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – madam president, i welcome this timely opportunity to join you today. the military campaign to retake mosul is a critical step in defeating daesh as a military force and bringing an end to daesh rule, which has had such disastrous consequences for the people of the region and continues to pose a threat to all of us. the crimes and the atrocities committed by daesh, including the killings of innocent civilians in and around mosul over the past days, are a reminder, if a reminder was needed, of the complete depravity of this organisation. whilst over the past days there has been progress in the military campaign, we need to be aware that this is an extremely complex operation which will need endurance, perseverance and pressures. there are bound to be setbacks. many fears and concerns have been expressed about the conduct and consequences of the campaign. these are real and valid concerns, and they require all of us to watch the events on the ground closely. at the same time, there are two reasons that give me cause for cautious optimism, at least in this opening phase of the campaign, which i would like to share with you. the first is that the military campaign is based on comprehensive planning and coordination between the federal government, the government of the kurdistan region and the global coalition. this has led to improved political ties between baghdad and erbil. it has seen the iraqi army enter kurdish territories for the first time in 25 years with the full agreement of the kurdistan region. this was unimaginable even a few months ago. the second reason is that we are confident that the federal government, under prime minister al-abadi, has taken on board the message concerning the need to protect civilians and for the iraqi army to enter mosul as a liberator, not as an occupying force. not only that, it is now the iraqi government which is the most vocal advocate of the protection of civilians with government instructions to its forces and to the united nations and the humanitarian community, reflecting their approach. this helps to explain why the shia militia, with the pershmerga, have been ordered to keep out of the campaign for the city centre. it is the national institutions of the iraqi army and the federal police, backed by sunni tribes, that will fight for the city. again, a year ago this seemed an unlikely scenario but, as i said, we need to keep a watchful eye. you are all aware of the humanitarian situation and concerns about massive displacement. the way hostilities are conducted will have a huge impact on the safety of the citizens of mosul, on the perception of the campaign, on civilian infrastructure and on returns and reconciliation. we also need to bear in mind that the behaviour of both daesh and the militias is inherently unpredictable and will need to be managed as the campaign develops. currently, the european union is ensuring the delivery of principal life-saving humanitarian assistance for all civilians most in need, whoever and wherever they are. this is our top priority. to date we have allocated eur 134 million to respond to the needs of iraqi internally displaced persons. equipment is pre-positioned and humanitarian contingency planning has been done jointly with the iraqi government and the united nations. we are also ready to respond to stabilisation challenges that post-daesh mosul poses. stabilisation after the military campaign is as important as the military campaign itself. one area in which the european union is very proactive is the removal of improvised explosive devices, which is a precondition for the return of the internally displaced people. i am confident that daesh will be defeated on the battlefield, but we can only defeat extremist ideology by addressing root causes which have given terrorist groups a foothold. in iraq non-inclusive policies have allowed daesh to flourish. therefore, we need to help iraq in rebuilding an inclusive, peaceful, multi-ethnic and multi-religious society trustful of its state institutions. inclusiveness, national reconciliation and the rule of law are essential. on regional dynamics, iraq’s relations with its neighbours are crucial. we are strongly in favour of dialogue between all countries of the region. this is essential as we focus on the primary task of fighting and defeating daesh in an effective way. looking ahead, it is our collective moral responsibility to remain a strong partner of iraq during these difficult moments. iraq needs all the help we can give at this critical moment for the country’s stability. if we do not do our utmost to help now and ensure that mosul is both liberated and then stabilised, we will have a much worse situation to deal with, which will have knock-on effects for all the neighbours. the council has therefore been looking at what more the european union can do in iraq. i call on the parliament to continue to support all the strands of eu actions, to tackle in a comprehensive manner the multiple causes and consequences of the crisis. thank you very much for your attention and i look forward to our discussion.

madam president, it is estimated that there are over a million people in the city of mosul and since the military action began, only 10 000 have managed to leave the city. for those still trapped inside, the most important thing right now is safe routes out and reliable places to go. and so the first effort has to be to plan those safe routes, communicate them properly to the population, preserve those who leave the city and ensure protection along those routes. then we have to give a humanitarian response to avoid the mistakes of aleppo. i know that the european union has deployed resources and is prepared to do so, but it will be another very important humanitarian crisis and we have to make sure, in that humanitarian crisis, that we have learned from the mistakes in aleppo and other parts of syria and we apply international humanitarian law and the protection of the most vulnerable.
mr president, i very much welcome the progress made in the offensive against daesh in recent months by the iraqi armed forces, the kurdish peshmerga and the other forces of the international coalition. in this campaign, mosul is now a priority target, as already mentioned. the news of the rapid advance is encouraging, but caution is in order. in any event, i am confident that this complex operation will be successfully completed as soon as possible with the least possible loss of human life and in full respect of international humanitarian law. the entry into mosul should be led by the iraqi army, assisted by the forces of the international coalition, avoiding interference by third parties that could jeopardise the success of the mission and the subsequent stage. i think it is particularly important to avoid all kinds of sectarian revenge and possible mass exodus. in addition, military victory will then raise important humanitarian challenges of security, of access of the population to basic services, as well as of reconstruction and reconciliation, which must be tackled urgently, as was noted at the high-level meeting in paris last week. in short, the iraqi people must be able to resume, so to speak, their normal lives. finally, mr president, in mosul, as in the rest of iraq and in most of the middle east, sectarian clashes of a religious, ethnic or territorial nature must also be overcome. there will be no viable political solution, no peace and no stability unless political and social inclusion, territorial integrity and reconciliation prevail.
on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – mr president, let me start by expressing my thanks for the opportunity to discuss with you today the main elements of the joint way forward on migration issues. this document was signed on 2 october between afghanistan and the european union. it should be seen not only in the context of eu—afghan relations but, more importantly, in the context of the european union’s new partnership framework with third countries under the european agenda on migration. this initiative falls under the package of efforts to address the ongoing migratory crisis and was welcomed by the last european council. more than a year ago we adopted, as you will remember, the european union’s agenda on migration which this house has welcomed. the eu agenda on migration set out our common strategy on the basis of this principle. a common challenge demands a common european response. it demands a comprehensive policy, which includes both short and long—term solutions and a coordinated approach of our internal and external policies in order to address all aspects of this phenomenon. preventing irregular migration is one of the issues that demands a long-term policy and engagement with key third countries. our engagement, therefore, with afghanistan, along with other key countries of origin, is part of this comprehensive approach. it is in this spirit that the european union and afghanistan have decided to bring their cooperation to the next level. let me stress the overall picture. europe faced an unprecedentedly large number of irregular migrants of afghan origin in 2015 and during 2016 afghans continue to represent the second largest group of irregular migrants to the european union. a large number of them will most likely be eligible for international protection either because they belong to specific categories of persons or because they originate from certain areas of the country. i do not have to repeat that every asylum seeker goes through a due and fair process, respecting her or his rights according to eu laws. those who are not eligible for international protection will have to be returned. this is exactly the issue which needs to be addressed with the afghan authorities. the afghan authorities do not contest the international law principle of readmitting their nationals found in an irregular position. they are, however, concerned about the impact of their return on those who return and on their receiving communities as well. this issue has to be adequately and proactively managed. their concern, which the european union shares, is moreover amplified by the fact that other neighbouring countries, notably pakistan and iran, are already returning thousands of irregular afghan migrants back to afghanistan. these returns are happening without an accompanying measure in favour of those who return and of the communities that will receive and reintegrate them. until 2 october the european union did not have any cooperation framework with afghanistan. this situation had created mistrust with limited possibilities for dialogue and cooperation, but also uncertainty for the migrants. the only ones profiting from the lack of a cooperation framework were the criminal organisations dealing with migrant smuggling. now we have this framework for dialogue and cooperation to discuss the issues of return, readmission and reintegration of the irregular migrants in a comprehensive, balanced and sustainable manner. this will also help to address the concerns of the afghan authorities i mentioned before. i would now like to give you an overview of what the joint way forward is, what it is not, and what its key elements are. let me start by reminding you that the joint way forward does not refer to persons having been granted international protection status in the european union or whose international protection request is still being examined. it only covers irregular migrants – persons who either have not requested asylum or whose asylum claim has been rejected and they have no right to stay in the european union. in all cases the principle of non-refoulement will be preserved and respected. secondly, the joint way forward is not a legally binding international agreement. it does not set out new obligations. it represents rather a joint declaration in which are described the various initiatives which the european union and afghanistan, in accordance with their authority and internal procedures, intend to implement in order to organise the return, readmission and reintegration of the irregular migrants, while preventing further irregular migration flows. this declaration will enhance the mutual trust between the two parties. it proves that both the european union and afghanistan are committed to address the irregular migration phenomenon in a comprehensive, balanced and human manner. thirdly, i would like to underline that the joint way forward in fact goes much further than the return of irregular migrants. not only does it describe how member states and afghan authorities will organise an orderly return of the irregular migrants, but it encompasses several other initiatives helping to give to this challenge a sustainable solution in a spirit of partnership. for instance, it also covers measures aimed at preventing further departures of irregular migrants, such as campaigns to sensitise the population to the risk of irregular migration and capacity building to fight against migrant smuggling. it also underlines that, in line with eu legislation, the eu side will give the necessary consideration to humanitarian aspects to ensure that vulnerable groups of migrants receive adequate protection, assistance and care throughout the whole process. in this context, the joint way forward stresses the intention of the european union to support the country as much as possible with the challenging task of sustainable reintegration of those who return. as mentioned earlier, afghanistan is facing unprecedented migration challenges. it is in this spirit that the commission is developing an important multi-country programme to assist returning migrants, members of third communities and the local authorities. the interventions foreseen under this programme will include vocational training and skills development, strengthening of local communities and the improvement of migration management systems and policies. this programme comes in addition to the existing bilateral development cooperation which addresses some of the root causes of irregular migration, for example as concerns the availability of basic services or economic opportunities. it represents just one aspect of the much broader financial and technical support which the european union and its member states have been giving and, as reiterated at the brussels conference on 5 october, will continue to give to afghanistan to promote its overall stabilisation and development. the joint way forward represents the beginning of a dialogue and cooperation for the european union and the member states with the afghan authorities. nothing should be taken for granted. patient work and mutual respect in a spirit of partnership will ensure the effective success of the initiatives described in the joint way forward. from the commission’s side i can ensure you of our full commitment to make the joint way forward a success story with a positive outcome for the european union, for afghanistan and, in particular, for the afghan migrants involved. i can conclude by reassuring you that i am committed to come and inform you on the state of play of the joint way forward whenever you request it in the future.

its communication should be improved and its operation should be made simpler for those concerned. we also want to highlight the role of volunteering as a factor of social cohesion, personal growth of the individual, and even as a contribution to economic development. the work of volunteers in europe, as one colleague has said, contributes to the production of 5% of gdp. we also recommend that member states promote european voluntary service in academic education systems. in my country, spain, as in most european countries, volunteering is carried out mainly through individual and local community initiatives, but international volunteering programmes are not promoted in schools and the opportunities of european voluntary service are not known. i believe that greater cooperation between the european union and the member states through joint programmes and greater internationalisation of the offer could also help to improve this european proposal. when we think of volunteering, we also think of young people. volunteering is, in fact, one of the eight areas underlined by the european union youth strategy. but let us not forget the elderly and the fundamental role that volunteering can play in promoting a culture of active ageing, especially if we aspire to a society that includes all generations. we have come a long way since the european year of voluntary activities in 2011, and this is certainly a source of civic pride, but we still have a long way to go.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the management report on iter and the development of fusion energy because of the very high cost of this type of research. the european budget must be geared to solving the many problems facing the european citizens. i am not against the development of this type of research, but the union has a budget which must be geared to solving problems of a european nature. the high cost has been demonstrated shortly after its start; this is an ambitious project that must be financed at the expense of policies that are fundamental for the citizens of the union. i believe that the union needs a much larger budget. i cannot therefore support a project of this nature in this context. that is why i have decided to vote against this draft.

in writing. ‒ my vote shows the unquestionable socialist commitment to the fight against international terrorism by daesh, to the urgency of a rapid liberation of mosul and the surrounding populations, to the lowest possible number of civilian casualties and to the need to protect the most vulnerable in this crossfire. i make it clear that we do not support a struggle that breaks the rules of war, much less that violates international humanitarian law. the text, as proposed by the socialist group, reinforces our call on the international coalition to make the protection of civilians the focus of military action, to ensure evacuation through humanitarian corridors, to provide urgent humanitarian aid to the displaced and to launch an urgent plan for the reconstruction and development of iraq. we deeply regret that the representatives of the following parties in the european parliament did not join our call for protection and an end to terrorism: podemos, iu, eh bildu, alternativa galiga, nec and equo. once again, with your abstention, you are leaving thousands of people helpless. in this case, to the nearly 1.5 million iraqis who are being held in mosul.
in writing. ‒ i abstained because there are many elements that currently worry us in the offensive on mosul: that in order to destroy daesh, humanitarian law is left aside; the constant misinformation about what is happening in mosul; or turkey's role in the entire conflict, including its invasion of iraqi territory, and the corridor through which they allow terrorists to flee to syria and attack kurdish and syrian forces; we are concerned about the proposal to arm local militias, which will worsen the situation, while we do not provide sufficient funds to unhcr, a refugee aid organization. in the final vote i abstained, considering that while i disagree with many things, the resolution had some positive elements, such as expressing concern about the recent tensions between regional actors, calling for full respect for the territorial integrity and sovereignty of iraq and refraining from any military action in iraq without the consent of the iraqi government, and stressing the importance of promoting dialogue between iraq and the countries of the region in order to achieve a more secure middle east.
in writing. ‒ support the struggle and preservation of the independence, integrity and sovereignty of the iraqi people, as well as the self-determination of the most vulnerable peoples in their territory. however, from a perspective which advocates active multilateralism and peaceful conflict resolution, i am opposed to the introduction of military assistance into the territory as a measure of protection for ethnic minorities in the conflict, which will only contribute to the generation of more tensions in the region.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this motion for a resolution on the iraqi operation to liberate mosul from the jihadists of isis, which calls on the iraqi authorities to do everything possible to protect civilians, hospitals and schools as they advance towards mosul. the atrocities of jihadists and genocide against christians, yazidis and other minorities must be tried by the international criminal court, the text says. today, moreover, we celebrate the awarding of the sakharov prize to two yazidi women. the use by isis of children, the elderly, women and the most vulnerable people as human shields in the face of the military operation against them is very worrying and the extreme violence spreading across iraq must be condemned. furthermore, daesh is committing genocide against christians, yazidis and other minorities, and eu countries must be asked to take the case to the international criminal court. i therefore supported the motion for a resolution.

madam president, i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution which rightly condemns the increasing repression by the turkish government of journalists and the media. the drift of the turkish government is very worrying for those of us who defend civil and democratic rights, but it is also extremely worrying - and we must remember this - that the same european union which, here in this parliament, rightly condemns the turkish government, at the same time passes resolutions giving turkey the status of a safe country. turkey is not a safe country, neither for journalists, nor for kurds, nor for opponents. we must say this and we must say that alp altinors, for example, the vice-chairman of the turkish hdp, is still in prison and we are calling for his release directly from here. ladies and gentlemen, if you are worried about journalists in turkey, you should also be worried about what is happening to kurdish channels in europe, which have been deprived of the right to broadcast in their own language. let's worry, in general, about what's going on and stop looking the other way when we're interested.
in writing. ‒ the situation of journalists and press freedom has steadily deteriorated in turkey, especially since the attempted coup d'état last july, the resolution condemns the coup and supports turkey's legitimate institutions, but notes that the failed military coup d'état cannot be used as an excuse for the turkish government to crack down on the opposition, or to prevent journalists and the media from exercising freedom of expression, and calls on the turkish authorities to release all journalists and media professionals detained without strong evidence of criminal activity. the resolution deplores the fact that the turkish authorities have closed the offices of more than 100 broadcasters, newspapers and magazines, leaving more than 2 300 journalists and media professionals without jobs and revoking the press credentials of at least 330 journalists. the resolution calls for the release of all journalists and media professionals detained without strong evidence of criminal activity. finally, it recalls that a free and pluralist press is an essential element of any democracy, freedom of expression and of the press.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because it helps to denounce internationally the dramatic situation of human rights in turkey today, especially as regards the free and full exercise of freedom of expression. unfortunately, erdogan is taking advantage of the supposed coup against him, to carry out a purge against journalists, teachers, judges, doctors, among others. it is acting against anyone it suspects of being in opposition to its government, and it has launched an offensive against its own people who are de facto going unpunished, and it is a moral indignity for the union to remain silent and to be complicit by omission in these crimes of a state which should not be a reliable partner, nor be considered safe by the union. we would have liked to see the text express more forcefully and clearly the condemnation of the turkish government's behaviour, which is contrary to international law, but it is a good start to highlight the situation of violence against journalists in turkey.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a text condemning the cycle of increasing repression by the turkish government against journalists and the media, exacerbated after the attempted coup in july 2016, which has resulted in the closure of newspapers, the persecution and imprisonment of journalists and the establishment of a climate of authoritarianism and censorship that is absolutely incompatible with democracy and the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ i think it is essential to give this hint of attention to the turkish government, which has taken advantage of the operations to control the failed coup d'état of july 15 to carry out a real persecution against journalists and intellectuals critical of the current government by closing more than 150 media outlets and persecuting hundreds of critical journalists. we also insist with our support on the need for proper respect for minorities, especially the kurdish people. if this minority is routinely mistreated in turkey, the operations to control the failed coup have served to intensify the punitive operations against its members.
in writing. ‒ the situation of journalists and press freedom has steadily deteriorated in turkey, especially since the attempted coup d'état last july, the resolution condemns the coup and supports turkey's legitimate institutions, but notes that the failed military coup d'état cannot be used as an excuse for the turkish government to crack down on the opposition, or to prevent journalists and the media from exercising freedom of expression, and calls on the turkish authorities to release all journalists and media professionals detained without strong evidence of criminal activity. the resolution deplores the fact that the turkish authorities have closed the offices of more than 100 broadcasters, newspapers and magazines, leaving more than 2 300 journalists and media professionals without jobs and revoking the press credentials of at least 330 journalists. the resolution calls for the release of all journalists and media professionals detained without strong evidence of criminal activity. finally, it recalls that a free and pluralist press is an essential element of any democracy, freedom of expression and of the press.

in writing. ‒ a safer world requires that we take the disappearance of nuclear arsenals seriously and we must lead by example. the growing climate of insecurity may lead to a new episode of proliferation of this type of weapons of mass destruction. that is why we do not agree with any kind of operation in european countries with nuclear arsenals to manufacture new weapons or to improve existing ones. this is incompatible with the signing of the npt, which requires the reduction and/or elimination of arsenals and does not add to this new impetus the military doctrine of deterrence.

in writing. ‒ while i recognise the social value of volunteering, i could not vote in favour of this resolution because it advocates a mercantilist view of european volunteering (which amounts to 5% of gdp) as a substitute for social services which should be public. i consider the voluntary work of thousands of citizens and residents of the union to be commendable and as such to be socially recognised, but i am opposed to volunteering being used as a pretext for the state to disregard its responsibilities, for example in the reception of refugees, which is the line the resolution is aiming at. that is why i could not vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i consider it of the utmost importance to provide a legal framework which determines a volunteering statute with rights and responsibilities for volunteers and volunteering and facilitates mobility and recognition.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the jmr on the european voluntary service and the promotion of volunteering in europe as podemos defends the values of volunteering, solidarity, active citizenship and the mobilization of civil society in favour of the most vulnerable without cremation objectives. this jrc has highlighted issues that are key to us, such as that volunteering should not replace formal employment, that volunteering systems at european level still lack adequate coordination and need to be improved or that fair funding is needed for their proper development. the resolution also highlights the importance of the whole movement of volunteers during the refugee crisis, who have been able to react to challenges with great pragmatism, and envisages the possibility of recognising volunteer status and improving access to information, recognition of acquired informal skills and a better communication strategy. that's why i think it's a good resolution and i vote to consolidate this service.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this motion for a resolution on european volunteering, which calls for a clear legal status and adequate funding. the eu needs a more coordinated policy on volunteering, where volunteers should be given a legal status with clearly defined rights and responsibilities. we must also call for adequate funding for voluntary schemes to encourage participation and help young people develop skills and gain experience. many european citizens have volunteered in the educational, cultural or artistic fields, at sporting events, humanitarian or development tasks and, despite the clear economic and social benefits of volunteering for individuals and organisations, participation in the european voluntary service remains modest and the barriers that still persist need to be removed.
in writing. ‒ volunteering is one of the most visible expressions of solidarity, producing a transformative effect on society through the building of social capital and social inclusion, as well as being an expression of freedom and responsibility that puts european values into practice. this motion for a resolution, which comes in the wake of the 20th anniversary of the evs, calls for the support mechanisms and organisational structures to be strengthened by strengthening an appropriate legal framework determining the rights and responsibilities of volunteers. it also calls for a stronger local dimension and follow-up after a volunteering experience abroad by providing support to local communities. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the development of a coordinated european volunteering policy and the need for the institutions to give greater impetus to evs.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that this review report on the 2013-2015 youth strategy contains complex elements of analysis and lines of improvement which i believe are consistent with our training positions. however, there are elements in the report with which i do not agree, such as the creation of an 'erasmus for apprentices' or an exaggerated rhetoric of entrepreneurship, to the detriment of other active employment policies. however, i consider that the positive aspects outweigh the negative ones, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the cornerstone of the eu youth strategy is employment and the emergence of real opportunities to integrate young talent into our productive economy. that factor solves all the others, empowerment, participation, and requires decisive intervention in the field of education. maintaining and improving programmes that open up the world to young people in their own communities is another key factor in maintaining successful initiatives such as erasmus, reviewing and gaining effectiveness in programmes such as the youth guarantee and supporting entrepreneurship with a particular focus on the field of new business.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which assesses the eu youth strategy 2013-2015, a strategy focused on improving and addressing the main challenges facing young people: unemployment, poverty and social exclusion. for the next cycle (2016-2018) it is recommended to invest more in access to education, more mobility through erasmus+ and more involvement of young people in policy-making and decision-making. among the vulnerable groups identified in the report are migrants, refugees, minority groups, women and lgbtqi people. it also stresses the need to address the causes of youth unemployment, promote entrepreneurship among young people and invest in education, apprenticeships, apprenticeships and vocational training.

on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, i have just been told by the house's services that this is a record. i hope my colleagues will forgive me, because i really did not aspire to that and i would have preferred that yesterday, when we had the annual report of the court of auditors, i had been given a few more minutes, not these 15 minutes now. but anyway, i hope i didn't bore you and therefore i apologize in advance. it is true that, in the early hours of the next saturday to sunday - in the early hours of sunday - a change will occur, while we sleep, a change that we will apparently not notice while we sleep, but that, over the course of the following weeks, we will notice in a very important way. and it is precisely an accumulation of fatigue, because of that change in the social jet lag that we are talking about, via lack of sleep or the change that has taken place in sleep, which, of course, does affect the health of our citizens. the cost has even been qualified and quantified. between the direct and indirect cost, we are talking about 1% of these health problems that we carry over the following weeks and months. in some cases, it has also had an impact on road accidents, which we were already studying when directive 2000/84/ec was put into effect. and in fact, not even the accidents were going up in the weeks afterwards, but you could see the peak of the rise in road casualties a month after the time change. why would you do that? because what was building up was the chronic stress of the lack of sleep that i was causing that, to the month, was when there was a situation of greater vulnerability in transportation. in the spanish case we have even an added peculiarity. spain, in the 1940s, under franco, adopted the time of nazi germany in 1942 and has never changed it since. just as the rest of the countries returned to the greenwich meridian which is the one that would correspond to spain, in the spanish case it was not done. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the directive is implemented. and it is true that in recent days there has been a decision in the balearic parliament; there have also been decisions and debates, particularly on the part of the valencian community. these are regions, territories which live essentially on tourism, that is, services; they are very seasonal and have a lot to do with sunshine hours. the hotel industry in the mediterranean, in the spanish part of the mediterranean, has therefore even been able to quantify that, in the week following the change to winter time, up to seven points of hotel occupancy are lost, precisely because of the drastic reduction in hours of sunshine in the afternoon. i mean, it really does have an important effect and it is felt in the economic and industrial part, in the health part as well and in the part - as i said also - of road safety, which is so important. and although it is true that the commission did a study in 2014, the study was a bit of a status quo. and i think that right now, given the demographics that we have in the european union, with diseases precisely because of that chronic stress of poor work or poor sleep or because of age, which is also making us increasingly vulnerable, the health aspect is becoming increasingly important. and of course, a change twice a year, which is social jet lag twice a year, has significant health effects. and that is what any study tells us, like the one presented at last year's hearing, where precisely the fact that the european union does not need to add - that we are no longer particularly popular - is taken into account, an added stress for the effects of that change. it would therefore be important for the commission - as we have done in other areas - not only to study how it affects in a dispersed way, but also to include the effect of the opposite, that is, what would happen if there were no such change twice a year and, therefore, people could maintain this relationship with the biological clock but, above all, with the social clock. the commission has also not given us enough figures to examine the cross-border effects. because it is true that i was present, i was not a member of parliament, but i was in parliament working with my group when the directive was put into effect, which, in addition to the social, safety and health effects, suggested that harmonization - which is a good thing, as mr reul has very well said - had to have important effects on the cross-border side. in other words, this harmonisation would help transport companies - which were the most interested at the time, now even transnational companies, transport, energy or other services - which is why the 'harmonisation' aspect should take precedence over the 'change' aspect throughout the year. the commission should therefore be able to provide us with a study on the fact that there is no need to change, even if the situation is kept in line. it is true that it is more complex to get all the member states to agree to accept a single standard time and thus not to change it twice a year but to keep the one that is most beneficial for health, for safety, in short, for all economic aspects, but above all social and health aspects. and maybe that's the challenge; that is, once we've done the test and we've been harmonizing for quite a few years, to see how we could avoid an additional change that adds only chronic stress to social stress. and there we are too - and then i come back to the spanish case again - because the debate never ends because we never have enough studies, but of course, when we have been able to go to mars and go even further, for the commission to say that it does not yet have the evidence, the sufficient proof of this effect on health and how we could improve this situation, because it is a bit incredible. i mean, we have all kinds of studies now, and then, somehow, at some point, we have to have the evidence, the evidence in all sectors so that we can help those for whom it is most positive in some way, and where it is negative and where we see precisely that the health part is the one that prevails, of course to be able to take another decision that does not affect the health of european citizens so much. and in that sense, returning home again, returning to spain again, we have a rather complex situation in that debate right now, because, if the two time zones we have in spain - one for the peninsula and one for the canary islands - were not enough, the current debate is also joined by the third possibility of going to a third time zone, that is, that spain would have three time zones: one for the balearic islands, one for the peninsula and one for the canary islands. we have reached that stage precisely because of a debate which has not yet been given the proof we asked the commission to provide. commissioner, even if you are not the rapporteur, because we were waiting for mrs bullock, i think we need the commission to come forward, to take its responsibilities and to make a study of some kind; we agree, we agree with the council, however, to reach an agreement whereby citizens are not being shocked twice a year when it comes to adapting their biological clock to the european clock. and above all because it is certainly not in our interest as the european union that the changes induced or promoted by the european union and the institutions should be the ones that cause the most discontent among european citizens. so i would ask you very strongly, commissioner, that the commission should take, as mrs bulc told us last year, a really more systematic, holistic approach, and instead of giving us a study - which would be the umpteenth - on the various sectors, bits and pieces, etc., that it should be a really systematic approach where the evidence for reconsidering the opinion is definitive.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, we are talking today about the custom of changing the time twice a year, a custom already established by a european directive in 1981, as the spanish government recently reminded the parliament of the balearic islands, which this week voted to maintain the time without any change. as a curious fact, roosevelt referred to this change as "the wartime", because it was established in the period of the world wars, with the aim of saving on coal. of course, right now, in the middle of the european parliament's term, if the grand coalition continues to be re-edited - as is happening in spain - to set the clock back an hour will seem to us to be quite a bit. and i say this not by chance, but because this change of time is done with an objective, which is energy saving or energy efficiency. in addition, we already have an energy efficiency directive which, as you will recall, we recently revised and which, by the way, did not include binding targets for the countries. and, in addition to this, the governments of the member states are not doing enough to implement these energy efficiency measures either, which is what it is all about, after all. and this should be a top priority for economic reasons and to curb climate change. now, we have to think, does this measure really save energy? this argument was based more on the old heavy industry, but the reality today is that the most energy-intensive industrial sectors can be running 24 hours a day, so the savings are not so noticeable - again, this directive is from 1981 - but the savings are not so noticeable. the reality now is that the scientific community is not entirely in agreement about the savings that are being made with this, which could be 5 percent or even a meager 1 percent. some studies even say that this saving could occur only in the first few days after the time change, and then return to consumption similar to that before the time change. the daily reality for citizens is that the energy savings that families make in the morning could be spent in turn in the afternoon. and this is also important, because we obscure the natural light in the leisure and free time of most people, and this has to be linked with the need for more dignified and coherent schedules to reconcile and end the working day earlier, enjoying life with light. there are 50 million people in europe who are affected by energy poverty, and this is not discussed in this house. according to who, the fact that households cannot afford to heat their homes causes more illness, death, and even fire danger. i think that is also an important matter to be discussed in this house. we think that it should be examined whether the savings at present are sufficient, but above all, we must not waste time. there are many people who are not guaranteed access to electricity at cost and there are many ways of promoting energy savings which are not discussed or applied in the european union or in the member states.
blue card question. what is it? mr president, i just wanted to remind my colleague marc that i understand the nostalgia of the young, but that, precisely, the health studies tell us that the change - not the fact of having summertime, which is so pleasant to him, which is what we are proposing, that it be maintained - is what is also leading to obesity problems throughout europe and that is what we have been told by several universities and scientific institutes that were in parliament last year. i therefore ask you: would it not be better if we talked about keeping the working hours better for the health and morale of the citizens and thus perhaps being able to make the working hours more family-friendly, more social, something which is not achieved in some member states because of work?
rapporteur. – mr president, we live in times of uncertainty where future stability in our economies cannot be taken for granted any more. in this context, the biggest reassurance we can have for the future is the ecb’s safe pair of hands. ecb policies have been correct in general terms, and tomorrow i hope this chamber will clearly endorse them, as we did in the committee on economic and monetary affairs (econ) some weeks ago. ecb policies are subject to improvement and critique, of course. in this report you will find several ideas that may be of interest to you. we believe, for instance, that the asset purchase programmes (app) should be redirected away from buying public debt into investment assets related to the eib. the ecb should try harder to buy assets, such as a new wave of project bonds related to eu projects with clear eu added value, for example assets related to the building of the trans-european network of energy and transport, which is fundamental for the economy of the eurozone but lacking in proper investment in some member states. these european projects related to the energy union and the transport union were voted through by a large majority in this parliament during the last legislature. we need investment, but smart investment: no more airports without planes; no more high speed trains without passengers; no more roads without trucks or cars. i believe that the current app is being used by some member states to avoid necessary reforms in the fields of late payments, energy reform and public deficits. we also ask the ecb to study how it would impact the european monetary policy if member states issued debt directly related to public investment so that the ecb could buy it. this may give incentives to member states to increase their level of investment in research and education. we are also worried about the effects of negative interest rates in our banks and in our economy if they are maintained in the medium term. we know that the ecb is aware of these downside risks. i hope that negative interest rates will be the first measure to be unwound. we express also our concerns in the report on the creation of housing bubbles in many big cities in europe, such as barcelona, where i come from. the cities are more and more expensive due to international capital inflows. ultra-low interest rates are partly responsible for it together with, of course, local mistakes. income inequalities are also worryingly on the rise. finally, we call on the ecb to study in depth how small saving banks and big banks react differently during the crisis on the concession of new credit. so we ask: are healthy and well-managed, small saving banks a key part of the rapid recoveries in some countries of the eurozone? i also ask myself in this chamber, do we need to balance concentration at the big bank level, which is happening in some member states, with a new wave of small banks linked directly to their local territories? dear commissioner, dear colleagues, i really look forward to your views on all these issues.
i would like to thank the rapporteur, our colleague mr tremosa, for the work he has done in recent months and the group of alternative rapporteurs who have drafted and worked on this report, which i believe is a balanced document, which helps us to understand the work of the ecb's monetary policy, but which also sheds light on the direction in which monetary policy should be taken. the report, as i said, probably clearly supports the main measures that the ecb has been taking to achieve the inflation target, which is the main purpose of the european central bank. because we are still far from the target, despite all the expansionary measures we have taken, and therefore we encouraged and, in a way, illuminated some ways of improving access to credit for smes, as one of our colleagues who spoke earlier said: how small and mediumsized enterprises could also have a place within the monetary expansion programmes of the ecb. but the report also clearly says that monetary policy alone is not enough, that it is true that we need to make structural reforms in some sectors, and mainly in banking, because european banking, and in some countries causing greater difficulties, continues to restrict the ability of credit to reach all businesses and all consumers. but apart from that reform, we need a serious fiscal policy. in the next few days we shall be seeing the annual growth report drawn up by the commission, and here is commission vice-president dombrovskis, who must shed light on what tax policy should be. that fiscal policy has to go clearly alongside monetary policy, because when rates are so low, when private investors are not sure about their returns because growth forecasts are so low, because really the environment in which europe is moving is a very uncertain environment, we need the public sector to do its job. and so we need the public sector, which is ultimately the risk-taker in a society, to be able to drive demand to also facilitate the european central bank's meeting of the inflation target. and so in the coming months, also in the context of the european semester, we must define what that policy should be, which does not have to be just a country-by-country approach, but there has to be a holistic approach to macro policy, to fiscal policy, which accompanies the monetary policy implemented by the european central bank, with a reasonable result in a very complex environment, as i said before. in any case, i would like to spend these last few seconds insisting that the profits of the european central bank, the profits of the only federal institution, the institution of the currency of the union, which is the euro, should be returned to the budget of the union as a whole. and this debate can be carried on, it can be carried on without the need for a major reform of the treaties, and we should discuss it at some point in the coming months.
president of the european central bank. – madam president, first and foremost let me apologise for this delay, which was due to transport problems. i am happy to be back at the european parliament to discuss with you the european central bank annual report for 2015. this debate is an important pillar of our accountability. we take your comments and suggestions very seriously. at your request, last year, we began publishing the ecb’s feedback on your resolution on the ecb annual report. on 4 october 2016, the governing council also approved principles increasing transparency in developing ecb regulations on european statistics. these principles take into account the transparency practices of the european parliament, the council of the european union and the commission. in my remarks today, i will retrace the economic developments since our last plenary exchange in february. in particular, i will discuss the role of the ecb’s monetary policy in supporting the ongoing recovery. i will also review the policy agenda aimed at addressing current vulnerabilities in the euro area. let me say a few words now about economic developments and the role of the ecb’s monetary policy in supporting the recovery. the euro area recovery continues to proceed at a moderate but steady pace. it has shown remarkable resilience to adverse developments and uncertainties emanating from the global environment. in fact, euro area unemployment has been steadily declining. more than four million jobs have been created since 2013, when the situation was at its worst. domestic demand has also strengthened and positive figures for real gdp growth have been recorded for 14 consecutive quarters. since the beginning of the year, headline inflation has gradually picked up, moving from the negative rate of -0.2% in february to +0.5% in october. our monetary policy measures since june 2014 have been a key factor behind these positive developments. asset purchases, targeted longer-term refinancing operations (tltros, as they are called) and low policy rates have strongly supported the recovery. let me explain more in detail. first, the pass-through of our monetary stimulus to bank lending conditions has been remarkable. interest rates have fallen markedly across a broad spectrum of asset classes and credit markets since june 2014. as a result, euro area firms and households have experienced more favourable borrowing conditions. for example, bank lending rates for companies declined by more than 100 basis points between june 2014 and september 2016. bank lending conditions for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) – the backbone of our economy – have improved even more. since may 2014, bank lending rates on very small loans to corporations have declined by around 170 basis points. they are now converging towards those on loans to large-scale borrowers. evidence from our bank-lending survey supports this picture. banks report that our measures are contributing to more favourable terms and conditions on loans and are supporting credit creation. moreover, we see that banks are passing on the very attractive funding conditions of the tltros to their customers. lower borrowing costs for firms and households have stimulated both consumption and investment. for example, household income is benefiting from lower interest-rate expenses. likewise, investment spending benefits from lower financing costs, which are making more investment projects profitable. supported by our monetary policy, the recovery is sustaining its momentum. we also expect headline inflation to continue rising over the coming months. at the same time, we are not seeing a consistent strengthening of underlying price dynamics. much of the expected increase will be driven by statistical factors related to the stabilisation of oil prices. moreover, the return of inflation towards our objective still relies on the continuation of the current, unprecedented level of monetary support, in spite of the gradual closing of the output gap. it is for this reason that we remain committed to preserving the very substantial degree of monetary accommodation necessary to secure a sustained convergence of inflation towards levels below, but close to, 2% over the medium term. however, as your draft resolution on our annual report argues, our monetary policy support has to be accompanied by decisive action from other policy areas. in fact, we continue to face a number of structural challenges that are holding back a more dynamic expansion of the euro area economy. so the right policies need to be designed to address existing vulnerabilities and challenges and, ultimately, to secure higher sustainable growth for the euro area. as i argued before, the euro area economy has proved resilient despite the uncertainty caused, among other things, by the crisis in emerging market economies, the collapse in oil and commodity prices, and the consequences of the uk referendum. beyond the relevance of the ecb’s monetary policy, an important contributing factor has been the more robust financial sector which has emerged from the financial crisis. the decision to address the mistakes of the pre-crisis era through ambitious regulatory reforms is thus paying off. it has resulted in a european financial sector that is now stronger in terms of capital, leverage, funding and risk-taking. for example, common equity tier 1 ratios in the euro area have improved substantially, rising from less than 7% for significant banking groups in 2008 to more than 14% today. the welcome improvements in bank solvency – and the related improvement in asset quality – are a tangible result of our common work to create the banking union. the comprehensive assessment we conducted in 2014 – together with a deep asset quality review – encouraged banks to strengthen their balance sheets without delay. as a result, while the level of non-performing loans (npls) remains high in some countries, today this problem is not primarily related to the robustness of balance sheets. coverage ratios are close to 50% and much of the remainder is collateralised. a more resilient euro area banking system has been able to respond to the impetus originated by our monetary policy and facilitate the recovery in credit we have witnessed so far. however, a number of structural factors are still weighing on the ability of the financial sector to fully support the euro area recovery. notably, the profitability of euro area banks remains a challenge to be addressed. while bank profitability and the level of bank equity prices is not, per se, a matter for policymakers, insofar as it raises financing costs for banks, it could ultimately curtail lending to the real economy and hold back the recovery. we should therefore consider what factors are behind this and what we can do to address them. one factor is certainly the low-growth and low-inflation environment, which translates into low interest rates. by supporting the recovery, our monetary policy measures are supporting a return towards higher rates of return. in other words, low interest rates today are necessary for a return to higher interest rates in the future. but legacy and structural challenges are also important factors behind banks’ low profitability. where profitability is being affected by structural issues, such as overcapacity and inefficient cost structures, rationalisation and consolidation must form part of the answer. where the non-performing loans (npls) are at a high level, creating the conditions for a faster resolution of bad loans is an essential part of the solution. ecb banking supervision has presented its draft guidance on npls for public consultation. we have also conducted a stocktake of national supervisory practices and legal frameworks related to npls. with a view to creating liquid markets of distressed debt, efforts will be required to foster the development of an npl servicing industry, to improve data quality and access, and to remove tax and legal impediments to debt restructuring. the european parliament also has an important role to play in a number of key legislative dossiers. some relate to the banking union, with the proposed european deposit insurance scheme and the introduction of ‘risk-reduction’ measures in the context of the upcoming revision of the legislative pillars of the single rulebook for banks – namely the bank recovery and resolution directive (brrd), the capital requirements regulation (crr) and the capital requirements directive (crd). others relate to the capital markets union (cmu). in particular, the negotiations concerning the securitisation regulation need to be finalised soon. securitisation can play a very important role in increasing bank funding to the economy but regulatory uncertainty is detrimental to european securitisation markets. we consider that the commission has put forward a strong package that balances a revival of the european securitisation markets with the preservation of a prudent regulatory framework. progress needs to be made in other areas too, in particular insolvency law and taxation, as announced in the commission’s communication. it will also be necessary to address the financial stability aspects of cmu as part of the macroprudential review. a stable, profitable and competitive financial sector is essential for sustainable economic growth; but the reverse is also true. this is why we need more decisive action to raise the potential growth rate of the economy. first, let me echo your draft resolution. the implementation of structural reforms needs to be substantially stepped up. this concerns, in particular, policy actions to raise productivity and improve the business environment. we will soon discuss the annual growth survey 2017, which touches upon these exact issues. we should make the best use of the annual cycle of economic governance by ensuring that recommendations – including euro area recommendations – are really taken into account and effectively implemented. second, fiscal policies should also support the economic recovery, while remaining in compliance with the fiscal rules of the european union. for instance, a more growth-friendly composition of fiscal policies could boost growth. this leads me to my concluding point. during our last plenary exchange in february, i said that the cohesion of europe was being tested. since then, the challenges have increased. it is now, more than ever, important and necessary that europe responds cohesively and decisively to the challenges it is facing. i believe we should remember the words of a great european, carlo azeglio ciampi, spoken in this room more than ten years ago: ‘if we act alone we will be at the mercy of events bigger than us, events that threaten peace and european security.’ i am confident that the foundations on which the eu project is built are strong enough to achieve the objectives that have been entrusted to us by the people of europe. i am now looking forward to the debate.

vice-president of the commission. – mr president, let me thank you all, but first and foremost the rapporteur, ramon tremosa i balcells, for this debate. the ecb’s independence is a precondition for its effectiveness in safeguarding price stability. but so too is accountability, especially in difficult economic times, with monetary policy playing an important role in improving the financing to the real economy. to understand and debate monetary policy it is therefore essential for us to shoulder our part of the responsibility, first and foremost, as president draghi has outlined, regarding the implementation of structural reforms. this debate thus perfectly sets the tone for the discussions which will be held tomorrow on the european semester. it has demonstrated that there is much common ground between the commission’s and the european parliament’s views, so we count on your continued support in building the foundations for sustainable growth and job creation in europe.
president of the european central bank. – mr president, let me thank mr tremosa i balcells and his colleagues for the report. i would also like to thank vice-president dombrovskis, and let me thank all of you for the very relevant and useful debate, and also for the deep concerns that you have expressed on various issues and on the present situation. let me just present to you a few scattered
