better today than they were before. that is the first statement of fact that we should collectively keep in mind. and all this in spite of the serious geopolitical risks that are maturing and have matured especially this year. any available evidence suggests that the transmission of our accommodative monetary policy is effective. it has contributed, as i was saying before, to a significant easing in the borrowing conditions for firms and households – not for the large capitalists as such, but for everybody – and our policy has stimulated credit creation, and it is basically supporting the euro area recovery. there are two surveys. one is the bank lending survey where we asked banks what they are doing with their credit conditions, and they all say they have expanded credit, they have expanded the standards and their costs have been going down considerably for a long time. then we also asked the commission for a survey for smes, and similar questions were asked revolving around how they felt today with respect to credit conditions. the answers are unambiguously positive. the annual rate of growth of loans to firms has increased from -3% to +2% since may 2014. some of your points, and also those in the draft resolution, raised the issue of heterogeneity within the euro area, along with some other points raised before. that also has improved as well. development in lending rates to non—financial corporations point to a drastic reduction in the fragmentation of bank lending across the euro area, and i can give you all kinds of numbers about that. we have next to the asset purchase programme for the public sector a programme – and it was referred to in some of the interventions – where we buy corporate sector bonds. one lingering worry is that this programme actually benefits large corporates and does not benefit smes. nothing could be further from the truth. smes have actually improved their lending conditions a lot. there is one good reason for this, which is that if the large corporates borrow more on the capital markets they will free space in the banks’ balance sheets for smes. and, by the way, the corporate bond market has also experienced a significant increase in issuance. so funding costs and better access to finance have improved for both small and large companies, and this has and will have a positive effect on investment. having said that, i understand – from your words, of course, but also we are aware – that there are concerns as regards the risks associated with low interest rates and our unconventional measures. our measures still entail some medium—term risks and have side effects. however, do we see a bubble today? if we look at asset valuations we do not see that their valuations are somewhat high or stretched. also, any analysis would show that it is not a rise in asset prices per se that can create long-term damage to financial and macroeconomic stability, but it is an asset price boom which is fuelled by excess borrowing and leveraging, and this we do not have. in summary, financial stability risks related to our monetary policy measures are for the time being contained, but we will certainly watch them closely, and we are certainly aware that they have to be observed and monitored very, very closely. but we should also be aware that the right macroeconomic policy is the best safeguard of financial stability. on the low interest rates let’s be clear: low interest rates are a consequence of low growth and low inflation all over the world. they are not the creation of the ecb. in this situation, as i was saying i think in my introductory remarks, the policy rates by the ecb have to be low in order to stimulate growth and when you have higher growth and higher inflation, the policy rates of the ecb will also increase. by and large so far, the negative rate situation, when we weigh up benefits and costs, we see that the benefits are bigger than the costs. of course, there are many different considerations here, and you have all kinds of actors, but the impact of recent monetary policy measures on bank profitability so far has been contained. we are aware that this is not going to be forever. in the medium term, negative interest rates will certainly create a negative effect on banks’ profitability. on the economic outlook, as i have communicated before, at our next monetary policy meeting in early december we will assess the inflation outlook and our monetary policy stance. our assessment in december will benefit from the new staff projections extending up to 2019, and we will also take stock of the work of the eurosystem committees on the options that ensure a smooth implementation of our purchase programme until march 2017 or beyond, if necessary. we are committed to preserving an accommodative monetary policy stance that is necessary to bring inflation towards levels below, but close to, 2% over the medium term. and we are also committed to act if warranted by using all the instruments available within our mandate to achieve our objective. of course, other policies should also play a role, and i have commented on these several times in the past. let me now address some of the points – unfortunately in quite a scattered way – but, first of all, our monetary policy is by and large similar to the monetary policy that has been pursued in the united states, in the united kingdom and in japan. the policies of the large central banks do not differ very much today. second, the troika. there isn’t any sentence by any court that forbids the ecb to be in the troika. it is true that, over the years, in the last two or three years, the ecb has carved itself, in a sense, a much narrower role in the troika, closer to our own specificity – namely the financial sector and the banking sector. it does not have as much of a voice as it used to in the past on the macroeconomic programmes, where it is the commission which is the predominant voice. , i have already addressed the point that the large corporates benefit from our programmes while the smes do not. on our mandate, some of the statements were saying either explicitly or implicitly that we are overstepping our mandate. well, we went to court and that is not the view of the european court of justice. our policies generate inequality? that is not what the data shows. the creation of four million jobs has done more for reducing inequality than anything else. it is true that when the central banks’ buy assets, asset prices go up and the owners of the assets are usually wealthy, and you may have a worsening of distribution in the short term, but then the effect upon employment and upon economic activity reduces the major sources of inequality, which is unemployment, and that is what has happened in the euro area, where we have basically created four million jobs. a point was raised on ela which, by the way, is the prerogative of the national competent authorities – in this case, the national central banks of cyprus and greece – and this emergency liquidity assistance has to comply with the monetary financing prohibition laid madam president, i would like to report here today on a case which we have recently suffered in spain - in catalonia, in reus - particularly as a result of energy poverty, a problem which we have dealt with on a number of occasions here. rosa, an 81-year-old woman so was her name: rosa, died in a house fire because gas natural, a large spanish electric company, cut off her electricity after two months of non-payment. a candle that he used to light his house eventually caused a fire and his death. that is what is happening in european homes today: we have five million people suffering from energy poverty in spain and 50 in europe. and it is time for the european commission to take action, to take clear measures to ensure that companies do not cut off the supply and do not make citizens choose between eating or paying for electricity, to make clear controls on tariffs and to impose clear rules on companies to send the message that the european union is there to protect citizens.
madam president, 2016 is on track to be another black year for accidents at work in spain: accidents with dismissal increase by 7.6% and fatal accidents raise deaths by 1.5%: 461 dead victims of exploitation and greed, of the precariousness of the working class. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the european union is responsible, together with the spanish government, for the attack on collective bargaining and the cutting-down policies which have led to a rise in unemployment, temporary work and worsening working conditions, as well as cuts in health and safety resources. we demand that the role of inspections and recognition of occupational diseases be strengthened, with the involvement of european trade unions and organisations such as osha or the platform against undeclared work, and that in the future the european pillar of social rights, decent, safe and dignified work, be at the centre of the european norm.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, the economic and social priorities you are raising are completely inadequate. the recommendations reiterate measures which we have already seen fail year after year. in the field of employment, they are a new call for the precariousness of working conditions and the lives of workers. the incentives to recruitment are eventually converted into subsidies to entrepreneurs, which only serve to avoid paying their social contributions. the report calls for improvements in training systems, while at the same time making cuts in all public policies. the social protection elements are not yet in place. we've been waiting two years for a minimum-wage proposal. in short, these measures are a repetition of their mistakes. year after year we see in this parliament the failure of these measures, the same measures which have led us, among other things, to brexit, to the disaffection of the citizens, to the advance of far-right politics, as a result of precisely that disaffection. what they are proposing is not how to grow, but a dadaist manifesto, more structural reforms, flexibilization, and so on. have you learned anything since the beginning of this crisis? certainly not. make the big capital pay taxes. make an effective investment program. they power a sustainable production model. they improve productivity. make a real pillar of the community. this is not the way. they only want to benefit big business and dismantle social europe.
on behalf of the green group, mr president, thank you for your presence. i'm going to focus on your communication on the fiscal position. there are three statements in the communication which i think are correct: firstly, that the recovery is fragile - i think no one can doubt that - secondly, that basing our entire growth strategy on external demand is suicidal, given the context; and thirdly, that we cannot rely entirely on monetary policy as the solution to sustain growth. but then, one thing happens: you make an effort to put forward a proposal for an expansionary fiscal position, but i have to tell you that it is too little, too late and that it is inconsistent with the rules we have, which is something you do not recognise. too little, obviously, because basically what they're asking is to go a little bit beyond this year's fiscal position, not much beyond that. too late because the damage done by austerity policies over all these years is very high. and too inconsistent because it's a little bit difficult to see how a policy of this kind is consistent with the standards of governance that we have today. the whole process is lacking in coherence, i have to say. the strict implementation of the budgetary recommendations you made last year meant a regressive fiscal position of 0.3%, even though you foresaw that the fiscal position would be neutral. so the consistency of all the forecasts for the past year is absolutely clear. and that, for me, has three implications or demonstrates three things: first, the volatility and uncertainty of the whole process we are starting today; second, the endemic procyclicality of the stability and growth pact; and third, the persistent overoptimism of its forecasts. and then, in connection with the communication, i must also say something else, that they have not finished breaking a taboo which is very important: what geographical distribution of the aggregate fiscal position and the measures to be taken must be made. the calculations we can see would imply that, for example, germany, from the current surplus of 0.6% should go to a negative fiscal position of 0.5%; or if germany goes to a neutral fiscal position, that means that certain countries - for example, spain - would not comply with the very recommendations and forecasts you have made. but it would be good if you could indicate that geographical distribution. so, in conclusion, mr vice-president, i have to say that, although it is too little and too late, i hope you do well, but the signs are not very good. the german and spanish ministers have already said, incomprehensibly, that they do not agree. i think this parliament must send a clear message that it is important that the fiscal position this year is expansionary because otherwise the recovery will not come. we shall ask you to make further progress, as i said, on the regional distribution, to indicate which regional distribution there should be. and finally, you have to recognize that the current rules of governance are not working and that the whole economic policy strategy of the last few years has been a failure.
mr president, there are fellow members who are critical of the semester. i believe that in a monetary area, coordination of all other activities is not only appropriate but also highly necessary. but having the instrument, we have to get the policies right, the orientation and also the ambition. and i think it is very important, as the annual growth survey presented by the commission shows, that we need to have a more ambitious fiscal policy, that monetary policy is not enough. but what you are missing in your speech, mr dombrovskis, is something which is essential to me: having employment at the heart of european policy, not as a consequence but as an objective, a real objective. we need to increase domestic demand, and to do that we need to increase wages, which, according to eurostat data, have seen their purchasing power fall by more than 10% cumulatively over the last decade. we need to restore the dignity of employment to reconnect millions of citizens, workers, with the essence of their social model, because employment is much more than an economic policy, it is the umbilical cord by which many citizens feel part or not of a society. let us raise wages, let us increase the policies that coordinate quality employment and let us also give hope, within the framework of the european semester, to millions of citizens who want jobs, but they want quality jobs and decent wages.
in writing. i am glad to see that the european commission is slowly, but i hope surely, changing economic policy to match the real needs of the union. i hope that the 2017 european semester package will be the first of many steps in this direction. on the one hand, it has recognized, thanks to the efforts of the european parliament, that the structural funds for spain and portugal should not be suspended. otherwise it would not only have been irresponsible, but deeply unfair to a citizenry that has already suffered the unspeakable. on the other hand, the commission is finally moving to an expansionary fiscal policy for the euro area, asking countries with budget surpluses for more investment. and there's an even stronger bet on the investment plan. but unfortunately, one essential element is still missing: the creation of quality jobs with decent wages. we need to increase domestic demand, and to do that we need to raise wages, which, according to eurostat, have seen their purchasing power fall by more than 10% over the last decade. only by putting the fight against inequalities at the heart of the european semester can we build a stronger and more social europe from the rubble of populism and austerity.

madam president, i would like to reiterate to mr moscovici the support of all socialists for an agenda to combat tax evasion as ambitious as the one that is being put in place. in the wake of the luxleaks scandal, i would remind you, ladies and gentlemen, that automatic exchange of information on tax rulings, country-by-country reporting, has been introduced; that it has been proposed to limit the abuse of transfer pricing to ensure that profits are taxed where they are made; and, finally, that the harmonization of the corporate tax base has been resumed. it is a very ambitious agenda, certainly, and this directive which we are dealing with today in the report which mr maurel has presented to us is intended to guarantee the tax administrations access to information handled by financial institutions. but that is as far as i can go, so to speak, with my compliments, mr moscovici. i would also like to point out some criticisms which i think this directive in particular lacks. firstly, i think that there are a number of exceptions to the automatic exchange of information in this directive, which i do not think are justified, since the luxleaks scandals and the panama papers and in the context of the social alarm that is being felt all over the world. secondly, i believe that the list of actors involved in the information process must be extended, because it is not just the banks, but many financial actors, notaries, and many civil society organisations who also have to intervene in this information. and finally, it should be remembered that so many reforms to the directive on administrative cooperation would require a consolidated text, which it is time to be able to do. i should like to remind you that the council has to give its opinion on this matter and should not leave the european commission out of the question of fiscal coordination.
madam president, mr moscovici, my speech will be mainly political because my colleagues have already appreciated the gaps, the weaknesses, but also the good points of a text which my group and i will certainly support. because it is a text that is needed in the short term. it is a text of minimum, at least, and that meets one of the great demands of society. and that's where i wanted to go. you see, in this matter of tax evasion, tax avoidance and all related matters, but above all money laundering, even the democratic system itself is being compromised. and that's where an ambition to go much further is lacking. the cooperation will not last long and is very imperfect. we must force it, automate it and think about taxation, taxation surveillance, comprehensive and integrated, over and above voluntary exchange. madam president, never before has there been such widespread indignation against corruption and money laundering from illicit businesses, and never before has administrative cooperation to exchange information been so necessary. but above all, the shortcomings of the situation we are currently experiencing have become more apparent than ever before, after the panama papers scandal. the commission must therefore be required not only to take the initiative but to confront the council to ensure that all countries make this commitment to transparency as far as possible, including not only financial institutions but also notaries and trust holders in addition to registrars, by forcing them to pass on information to the commission regarding their tax rulings and, above all, by preventing large corporations from not paying taxes and by ensuring that, before the end of the legislature, the objective of companies paying money where they make their profits is met.
member of the commission. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, mr rapporteur, i would like to thank you all once again for your comments and for the impetus which this parliament has given to our joint action on taxation. i am once again confirming what has always been my conviction, namely that our two institutions, despite the differences in sensibilities and positions that may arise here and there, are on the same page in general, simply because we have the same objective: more transparent, more efficient and at the same time fairer taxation. i therefore welcome the level of ambition that some of you have mentioned and that mr maurel's report has perfectly translated. i can assure you that this directive will create the conditions for the establishment of a mechanism for crossborder access to information on beneficial owners, a mechanism which many of you are keen to see. in this way, brick by brick, we are building a strong defence structure against tax fraud and evasion in europe, a robust systemic response against external threats to member states' tax bases, a path to greater tax fairness for all european citizens and businesses. the political pressure, in the proper sense of the word, exerted by parliament, particularly by its econ and now pana committees, is decisive for the success of our initiatives. perhaps i should make a few more specific remarks in response to the comments made by the members. i have noted your request for automatic exchange of information and i share that objective. as i said, the commission will propose such an exchange in a separate proposal as soon as we have sufficient information, precisely on the best way to proceed. this will be done in coordination with the development of the anti-money laundering directive currently being discussed by this parliament, as well as by the council. many of you have pointed out that there are still activities or structures which are not transparent. i agree with you, of course. the commission is working on this and will continue to extend this transparency as far as possible with your help. several of you, including mr kofod, have mentioned the responsibility of the banks. the commission believes that not only is there a responsibility on the part of the banks, but that all those who facilitate aggressive tax planning must be included in the scope of our vigilance. we have launched a public consultation - i said it - on this to determine the best way to hold these facilitators of all kinds, backgrounds and origins accountable. as regards the agreement in the council, i take note of your remarks that the council did not wait for parliament's opinion to agree on a general approach to this particular matter. fortunately, we will continue to work towards greater transparency through other legal instruments. so there is obviously a major utility to the debates taking place here. i am happy, as always, to continue this work, happy to be able to do so in close coordination and partnership with the european parliament to achieve in europe the fairer taxation that our fellow citizens expect. in this respect, i am also very pleased to welcome this report, which is an important step in our common struggle, and, once again, the remarkable quality of this debate, which really moves things forward.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative resolution by which parliament approves the draft council implementing decision approving the conclusion by the european police office (europol) of the operational and strategic cooperation agreement between ukraine and europol. the agreement provides for an exchange of information to help europol further deepen its cooperation with ukraine. ukraine is a key eu partner and increasingly relevant in the fight against organised crime, specifically drug-related crime, trafficking in human beings, smuggling and organised crime gangs. the exchange of information with ukraine will enable the eu to combat organised crime, terrorism and other forms of international crime more effectively. in addition, the agreement also expands opportunities for cooperation in areas such as combating training activities and crime prevention. the signing of this strategic and operational agreement should foster greater coordination between the different strategies and action plans of the eu, its member states and ukraine.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of jean-françois jalkh, in view of the report drawn up by the committee on legal affairs, which finds that the prosecutor of the court of appeal of versailles has requested such a waiver in relation to an alleged offence of incitement to national, racial or religious discrimination following the complaint against him for statements made in a booklet entitled petit guide pratique de l'élu municipal front national (practical guide of the elected head of the national front), published on 19 september 2013 and posted on the official website of the national front federation on 30 november 2013, which encourages the candidates of the national front elected as councillors in the elections held on 23 and 30 march 2014 to recommend, from the first plenary session of the new mayors, the defence of the public interest in the issue of social housing to jean-françois jalkh, as director of the national front. since jean-françois jalkh was not a member of the european parliament at the time of the alleged offence and since the charges have no obvious connection with his status as a member of the european parliament, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of françois jalkh, since he has been denounced in france for his discriminatory and racist statements. the statements made have nothing to do with his parliamentary work, they are merely the expression of his deplorable ultra-rightist position. i have therefore voted to lift his parliamentary immunity so that he can be tried for incitement to racism and hatred.
in writing. ‒ under article 9 of protocol no 7, members of the european parliament enjoy, in their national territory, the immunities accorded to members of parliament of their member state. referring to the french constitution, article 26 states that no member of the french parliament may be prosecuted, investigated, arrested, imprisoned or tried for opinions or votes he has expressed in the exercise of his duties. given, first, that jean-françois jalkh was not a member of the european parliament at the time of the alleged offence and, secondly, that there is no link between his status as a member of parliament and the charges against him, the committee on legal affairs recommends that the european parliament suspend jean-françois jalkh's parliamentary immunity.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of lifting the parliamentary immunity of jean-françois jalkh because he is accused for his position as director of publications of the official website of the national front for the statements of jean-marie le pen, published on the website "frontnational.com" and later on the blog "jeanmarielepen.com" on 6 june 2014, in response to the mention, by a participant, of the name of the singer patrick bruel, who had stated that he could no longer perform in the cities that had elected a mayor of the national front: no wonder. look, next time we'll put you through the oven; considering jean-françois jalkh was the director of publications for the official website of the national front. these statements are clearly incitement to hatred and i think it is appropriate to withdraw his immunity, since for a member of the european parliament to be protected by immunity, he must have expressed his opinion in the course of his duties, which implies the requirement of a link between the opinion expressed and parliamentary duties. and that relationship must be direct and be clearly imposed. in this case, he is not responsible for any of these circumstances, since the actions were taken before his term as an mep.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this new cod plan, as it simplifies the landing of catches and updates the 2008 plan, which was hampered by the limitation of fishing effort which reduced the time that seamen could spend at sea. with the application of the discard ban, this limit became an unnecessary tool. the proposal is adapted to the new common fisheries policy and therefore introduces a provision requiring the council to set the total allowable catch (tac) on the basis of maximum sustainable yield (msy) and stipulating that the precautionary approach should prevail in the setting of quotas in cases of insufficient data. this update of the cod management plan and the fisheries exploiting it is necessary, although it is expected to have a short life until the approval of the north sea multiannual plan. this does not prevent the commission from treating with caution the impact that the landing obligation may have on the sustainability of the fishing fleets that exploit them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because there is ample scientific evidence that the four cod stocks in europe are at levels well below sustainable levels. the stricter rules that were established in 2004 (revised in 2008) have proved to be insufficient. pending the adoption of the north sea mixed fisheries management plan, this regulation constitutes an interim solution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i understand that it is a matter of adjusting and adapting regulations. delegated acts are introduced in the following areas: adaptation of fishing mortality rates and associated stock biomass levels to scientific findings, adjustment of fishing effort in case of exclusion or re-entry of a group of vessels under effort regime, specification of the rules on the method of calculating fishing capacity and adaptation of maximum capacity levels and, finally, the establishment of rules on a method of calculation allowing member states to adjust the maximum allowable fishing effort in relation to quota management and following transfers of effort.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank mrs doods for her work on this report on the long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting them. i have supported this report, which comes from the last legislature, because we have had to adapt it not only to the lisbon treaty but also to the reform of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. ‒ report referred to the court of justice of the eu (cjeu). parliament adopted its position at first reading on 11 june 2013, pending the outcome of the ruling of the ecj which on 1 december 2015 made it clear that fisheries management plans fall under the ordinary legislative procedure pursuant to article 43 (2) tfeu. the judgment annulled council regulation (eu) no 1243/2012 amending provisions of the plan in articles 9 and 12 to establish fishing opportunities in situations where data were insufficient to establish the status of stocks and maintained the effects of the annulled regulation for an additional year so that the new regulation could be adopted on the correct legal basis during that period of time. in this way, the co-legislators adopted a text by the ordinary legislative procedure within the time limit set to ensure legal certainty and a compromise agreement was reached in the first and only trilogue on 29 june 2016. the revised plan is fully in line with the principles of the cfp and, in order to ensure legal certainty for the fisheries sector, will enter into force on 1 january 2017. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒i voted in favour of this new cod plan, as it simplifies the landing of catches and updates the 2008 plan, which was hampered by the limitation of fishing effort which reduced the time that seamen could spend at sea. with the application of the discard ban, this limit became an unnecessary tool. the proposal is adapted to the new common fisheries policy and therefore introduces a provision requiring the council to set the total allowable catch (tac) on the basis of maximum sustainable yield (msy) and stipulating that the precautionary approach should prevail in the setting of quotas in cases of insufficient data. this update of the cod management plan and the fisheries exploiting it is necessary, although it is expected to have a short life until the approval of the north sea multiannual plan. this does not prevent the commission from treating with caution the impact that the landing obligation may have on the sustainability of the fishing fleets that exploit them.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution on the cod stock plan. the plan will be replaced, provisionally, by multiannual plans for mixed fisheries (i.e. fisheries where several species are caught) in all the areas concerned. pending these regionalised plans, the amendments to the 'cabillaud' plan simplify its application while ensuring better management of stocks. this means that cod fishermen will no longer be subject to time limits (days at sea) which have not allowed stocks to be restored. they can land all their catch, even unwanted ones, instead of throwing some of it into the sea. other changes are introduced to avoid disparities in member states' fishing effort calculations (which lead some states to fish more than the plan allows). it also reduces the administrative burden on fishermen by removing procedures for fishing activities in which insignificant quantities of cod are caught. it also exempts from the fishing effort management regime vessels participating in trials on fully documented fisheries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i understand that it is a matter of adjusting and adapting regulations. delegated acts are introduced in the following areas: adaptation of fishing mortality rates and associated stock biomass levels to scientific findings, adjustment of fishing effort in case of exclusion or re-entry of a group of vessels under effort regime, specification of the rules on the method of calculating fishing capacity and adaptation of maximum capacity levels and, finally, the establishment of rules on a method of calculation allowing member states to adjust the maximum allowable fishing effort in relation to quota management and following transfers of effort.

in writing. ‒ the draft legislative resolution approves the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the regulation establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting them. after a long debate on the powers of codecision, parliament approved the act, the aim of which was to restore cod stocks above levels which would allow maximum and lasting yields to be obtained. i am voting in favour because the amendment will be important in achieving the union's objective of ensuring the sustainability of fisheries.
in writing. ‒ report referred to the court of justice of the eu (cjeu). parliament adopted its position at first reading on 11.6.2013, pending the outcome of the ruling of the cjeu, which on 1.12.2015 made it clear that the fisheries management plans fall under the ordinary legislative procedure, ex article 43 (2) tfeu. the judgment annulled council regulation (eu) no 1243/2012 amending provisions of the plan in articles 9 and 12 to establish fishing opportunities in situations where data were insufficient to establish the status of stocks and maintained the effects of the annulled regulation for an additional year, so that the new regulation could be adopted on the correct legal basis during that period of time. the co-legislators thus adopted a text by the ordinary legislative procedure within the time limit set to ensure legal certainty and a compromise agreement was reached in the first and only trilogue of 29.6.2016. the revised plan is fully in line with the principles of the cfp and, in order to ensure legal certainty for the fisheries sector, will enter into force on 1.1.2017. i voted for the report.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this text is to amend the rules setting limits on catches, to amend the fishing effort regime and to strengthen the measures to deal with discards. the aim is to give fishermen more flexibility, and it removes the obstacles to introducing obligations in the plan. it also provides for a wide flexibility in the rules on catch limits and agrees with the need for member states to take appropriate measures to minimise and, where appropriate, eliminate discards. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this reform of the administrative cooperation directive to allow access to and exchange of information relating to money laundering, which in the anti-money laundering directive financial institutions are obliged to provide. while the consultation procedure has succeeded in incorporating the automatic exchange, the opportunity to extend the list of obliged to provide information beyond financial institutions, in line with the anti-money laundering directive, such as: notaries, agents, trusts, etc. has been lost. it is also very positive that, at the request of the psoe, the report includes the creation of a public register of companies containing relevant tax information, and reiterates that the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion is an absolute priority for the union. the spanish socialists hope that the council will take this report into account and incorporate these achievements, while continuing to call for the com munitization of tax policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it improves the requirements for tax authorities to have access to information. with the development of all the tax scandals that have occurred in recent years - luxleaks, panamaleaks, bahamaleaks - the public has become aware of the tax practices of the major players in the financial system. this proposal is born of the pressure of public opinion to act in this area and allow access to relevant tax information of tax evaders. access to information by the competent authorities is a necessary step in order to implement the principle of paying taxes where wealth is created and to take action against tax havens. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a further step towards eradicating tax fraud. in particular, this amendment will give tax authorities greater access to information on the active beneficiaries of intermediary entities in order to identify and tackle tax evasion more effectively.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report and in favour of the commission's proposal to make it compulsory for member states to exchange information on money laundering in order to combat money laundering and tax evasion. the final date of entry into force is 2017, considered more realistic by virtually all parties. the amendments tabled by parliament also require the exchange of information on the beneficial owners of companies, making it more difficult to evade the use of shell companies.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report on access to information by tax authorities against money laundering. more transparency, clarity and above all cooperation between tax authorities are needed. there are mechanisms that need to be put in place, and the fight against money laundering is fundamental in the union.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it improves the requirements for tax authorities to have access to information. with the development of all the tax scandals that have occurred in recent years - luxleaks, panamaleaks, bahamaleaks - the public has become aware of the tax practices of the major players in the financial system. this proposal is born of the pressure of public opinion to act in this area and allow access to relevant tax information of tax evaders. access to information by the competent authorities is a necessary step in order to implement the principle of paying taxes where wealth is created and to take action against tax havens. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to make the exchange between member states' authorities more agile and faster, and thus to combat money laundering more effectively. the report also stresses that the fight against tax evasion, particularly in connection with money laundering, is one of the main challenges facing the european union. the evidence is that recent events have confirmed that greater fiscal transparency is now indispensable, together with greater international coordination and cooperation. i am voting in favour of the report because the global nature of money laundering requires an effective and efficient response, which can only be achieved through international cooperation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report and in favour of the commission's proposal to make it compulsory for member states to exchange information on money laundering in order to combat money laundering and tax evasion. the final date of entry into force is 2017, considered more realistic by virtually all parties. the amendments tabled by parliament also require the exchange of information on the beneficial owners of companies, making it more difficult to evade the use of shell companies.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this dossier on the annual report on the activities of the ecb, as it supports the expansionary monetary policy pursued by the issuer of the euro. thanks to the socialists, the initial emphasis in the draft report has been lowered on structural reforms, which are described as socially sustainable, as well as the recognition of the federal nature of the ecb and the reiteration of support for the pledge made by its president in july 2012 to do everything possible to safeguard the stability of the euro. it is true, however, that monetary policy is not enough, and that the union must therefore pursue an expansionary fiscal policy to support growth and employment. the review of the european fund for strategic investments is an opportunity to issue long-term bonds, taking advantage of negative interest rates, to relaunch the financing of projects generating jobs in sectors such as energy, bio-industry, infrastructure and others.
in writing. ‒ i have voted against this report because it falls far short of criticising the functioning of the european central bank during the financial year 2015. it points out some substantial criticisms of the ecb's activity during this period, the role of super-low interest rates, the impact of quatitative easing, etc. however, the report continues to call for the need for 'structural reforms' to make monetary policy itself work. we need a different monetary policy that calls into question the independence of the ecb and allows it to function to finance public debt and not just debt markets, where the financial system blackmails the states. the report does not criticise the present structure or its undemocratic functioning, and that is why i have decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because of the important role played by the european central bank, but i would like to stress my concern about the effects that negative interest rates can have on savers. i would also like to stress the need to strengthen economic and monetary union, in particular to complete the banking union.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which i consider to be overly complacent with the activities of the european central bank. the commission notes that the greek authorities have not provided any evidence that the bank has engaged in a disproportionate or excessive conduct. in addition, the policy of quantitative expansion and the purchase of bonds through secondary markets has been a gift to financial institutions which has not brought benefits to society and has not succeeded in solving the economic problems it was intended to solve.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report in view of the consequences for the european economy that brexit may entail, as well as the disparity at state level in terms of economic growth and the reduction of unemployment rates. we must also bear in mind that despite the efforts made, some countries in the union are still above the deficit targets set. we must bear in mind that the single monetary policy alone cannot stimulate aggregate demand if it is not complemented by sound fiscal policies, ambitious and socially balanced structural reform programmes at member state level. in this context, we must complete the full implementation of the union, as this would be a decisive step towards improving the effectiveness of the single monetary policy and mitigating the risks arising from a shock to the financial sector.

in writing. ‒ in accordance with article 284 tfeu, the annual report of the european central bank is presented to the european parliament. the main themes of this meeting were the recovery of the euro area economy, low inflation, the effects of low interest rates and the ecb's decision to expand its asset purchase programme. the european parliament's analysis of this report is certainly valuable, as it focuses on the core elements of the ecb's own activities, such as monetary policies. 'this breaks with the practice of covering general economic policies which has in the past led to delays and complications in the parliamentary procedure.' the present text, which i voted for, provides a balanced assessment of the relationship between monetary policies, structural reforms and the risks of low interest rates; also of the ecb's asset purchase programme, not calling for its expansion but asking for a study of the impact it would have on public debt.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report, which reflects parliament's position on the green paper on retail financial services drawn up with the commission, as it proposes various measures to increase transparency, protect consumers and remove barriers to access, including those of a cross-border nature. it also includes a proposal on the creation of a european savings account to increase financing for green and sustainable investments. the commission has also adopted a number of amendments tabled by the spanish socialists, aimed at ending the practice of cancelling payment cards for moving residence to another member state, limiting excessive fees at atms and defending the euro as the main currency on the financial services market. this is a very progressive and pro-european report which can have a decisive influence on the commission's forthcoming legislative proposals on this subject. it is regrettable that the european right has tried to remove, both in committee and in plenary, the paragraph on defending the rights of payment card users, but i am glad that it has not succeeded.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it is a continuation of the financial deregulation which exists in the financial system of the union. this green paper presents the initiative to regulate retail financial products at transnational level. instead of seeking greater transparency and security for potential consumers, the report leaves it to the financial system to create all kinds of products. instead of simplifying, it is being left to do, allowing for a diversity and complexity of financial products that can undermine the interests of european consumers, as has already happened in the past with preferential shareholdings. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to support the development of retail financial services at european level. the approach of this report seems to me very timely, and the development of a more efficient market will allow for more innovation and promote the entry of new players into the market.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this proposal to liberalize retail financial services. while the aim of giving consumers more choice and lowering the price of products may seem to be commendable, the legislation is moving towards deregulation which favours the single market but does not offer guarantees of standardisation and transparency of the products placed on the market. in this way we can expect that the large multinationals will be able to sweep away the smaller suppliers, and that derivative financial products whose risk is very difficult to assess will prevail over safer products.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank olle ludvigsson for his work on this report on the green paper on retail financial services. initiatives based on this green paper should be compatible with the intensification of the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and avoidance and money laundering, including further efforts towards the development of a common tax identification number.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, bearing in mind that the green paper focuses on a number of elements where it might be advantageous for the legislation, currently in the implementation phase, to be completed in the coming years. for most retail financial products, we are still faced with 28 divergent national markets and not as competitive as one would expect. crossborder activities remain limited due to a multitude of barriers. this is not good for consumers, for innovative companies or for the overall functioning of the european economy. there is a huge potential that we have not yet tapped. the green paper is also timely because digitisation is opening up new possibilities at an accelerated pace. if tackled properly, digitalisation could provide exactly the momentum needed to start removing cross-border obstacles. we now have a real opportunity to link financial operators established throughout europe with consumers residing across the continent. this represents a new opportunity for the single market which must not be missed.

in writing. ‒ this report seeks to overcome the barriers that exist today in retail financial services, while developing them in the coming years. the union must meet the challenge of creating and maintaining a level playing field. any new legislative initiative based on this document should be based on technology and business model neutrality. the legislator, faced with a rapidly expanding market, must create a regulatory framework which allows, without manipulation, to create a safe and lasting growth environment, and then it must be the consumers who decide who wins or loses in this market. it is equally important to highlight the challenge of ensuring that there are no unfair or unnecessary differences between euro area and non-euro area member states and that no one is left behind. financial exclusion is a serious problem affecting the whole of europe and for the single market to be truly effective it is necessary that it also retains its integrity in this fundamental respect.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report, which reflects parliament's position on the green paper on retail financial services drawn up with the commission, as it proposes various measures to increase transparency, protect consumers and remove barriers to access, including those of a cross-border nature. it also includes a proposal on the creation of a european savings account to increase financing for green and sustainable investments. the commission has also adopted a number of amendments tabled by the spanish socialists, aimed at ending the practice of cancelling payment cards for moving residence to another member state, limiting excessive fees at atms and defending the euro as the main currency on the financial services market. this is a very progressive and pro-european report which can have a decisive influence on the commission's forthcoming legislative proposals on this subject. it is regrettable that the european right has tried to remove, both in committee and in plenary, the paragraph on defending the rights of payment card users, but i am glad that it has not succeeded.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this proposal to liberalize retail financial services. while the aim of giving consumers more choice and lowering the price of products may seem to be commendable, the legislation is moving towards deregulation which favours the single market but does not offer guarantees of standardisation and transparency of the products placed on the market. in this way we can expect that the large multinationals will be able to sweep away the smaller suppliers, and that derivative financial products whose risk is very difficult to assess will prevail over safer products.

in writing. ‒ the report is presented with the aim of being transmitted, once adopted, in the form of a resolution to the council and the commission. the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire in a building. it also advocates advancing the design and passporting of specific types of retail products and services that meet the conditions to be set in a harmonised way. i have voted in favour of this proposal, in the hope that it will improve and increase the use of retail financial services and instruments.

in writing. ‒ europe is facing threats and challenges unprecedented since the end of the second world war. the socialists have supported the union's continued progress towards integration, with security and defence being one of the main challenges to be faced. that is why we support moving towards a european defence union as an 'umbrella' structure to pool, improve and coordinate the union's preventive and reactive military capabilities. we are in favour of a european defence union which guarantees the maintenance of peace, the prevention of conflict and the strengthening of international security, in accordance with the principles of the united nations charter. to do this we need the member states to commit themselves to moving forward through permanent structured cooperation, ensuring reactive capacity and trained personnel, as well as sufficient means.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to develop common projects, and it is expected that the money contributed could mobilise up to €5 billion a year from 2017. in addition, it is intended to encourage research and development in military projects. until now, eu spending on innovation has excluded military uses, but in 2017 €25 million will be allocated and from 2020 €500 million a year. i rejected this report which seeks to strengthen the security and militarist perspective and which requires the states to allocate 2% of gdp to defence, at a time when the european population is sinking ever deeper into poverty and unemployment (the data tell us that in the spanish state 1 in 5 households are below the poverty line, and unemployment is close to 4 million). what the states should do is increase social investment and job creation, not contribute to militaristic escalation. according to article 41 (2) teu, there can be no military financing from the union budget. my vote against this report is opposed to the military line.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the european defence union because it proposes to give the union greater strategic autonomy in defence policies and greater coordination, but it does so by proposing measures which in no way guarantee that solutions will be found to the security problems that exist at global level. the report calls for specific resources to be allocated to military cooperation between member states, the creation of a european defence union, beyond the common security and defence policy, the convening of european-level meetings of defence ministers, and the creation of a union headquarters, among other measures. none of these measures is aimed at resolving the causes of the threats to security in the union, let alone contributing to creating a framework of stability, cooperation and peace between countries.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by my colleague mr paet. i support the creation of a european army, for which a balanced budget is needed, but i did not agree that the text should explicitly state that 2% of gdp should be allocated to it. we must continue to cooperate so that the european army is a fact in the future.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, fully convinced of the need to equip the union with the necessary elements to meet the challenges in the field of defence. at present, cooperation between member states is sporadic, and europe continues to place great reliance on nato and the solidarity of the united states. in the face of the deterioration of security in recent years, in europe and beyond, due to terrorism, hybrid threats and cyber and energy insecurity, the union must rise to the occasion and take decisive steps towards a defence union, as no country alone can meet the challenges we face. the union must be able to respond more swiftly and firmly to threats, which requires improved cooperation between the armed forces. it is of particular importance to consider the possibility of jointly procuring military equipment and of having an operational headquarters in the union in order to plan and conduct crisis management operations.

in writing. ‒ this report is part of an initiative by the epp group in the subcommittee on security and defence in response to the deterioration of security in our neighbourhood, which requires member states to take joint action, especially in the fight against terrorism. for these to be effective, the shortcomings in the development of security and defence capabilities need to be addressed and the possibility provided for in article 42 teu, which provides for progress towards a common defence of the union, needs to be further developed. the text considers that all resources should be mobilised to make defence cooperation systematic, in particular through permanent structured cooperation (pesco). the document stresses the need for closer eu-nato cooperation, which will improve synergies and compatibility between the two frameworks and allow for greater leverage of defence investment. i am convinced that the union must provide a more solid framework for its defence policy in the long term, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.

as i said in the debate in the committee on transport and tourism on this report, mr president, it is a first step which has some positive aspects, but which leaves unresolved certain elements which are fundamental to the construction of a good transport policy. firstly, it does not specify; and it is not the same thing to talk about a megacruise for mass tourists as it is to talk about a short-distance ferry used by citizens, which brings the territory together and stimulates the local economy. secondly, it is not the same thing to promote natural gas in producing countries as in member states which not only do not have this resource, but would have to bring it across thousands of kilometres, building huge infrastructures and spending millions of public money which could be used to promote renewable energy from local generation and thus reduce the european union's enormous energy dependence. however, this report deals with the introduction of gas into ports without taking these considerations into account. that is why we voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it does not add any political priority in the field of passenger transport by inland waterway and, moreover, it strengthens the presence of non-sustainable resources such as liquefied natural gas (lng). the report does not include specific references to the role that the public sector should play in the development of these channels, maintaining a market-oriented approach that has so far only inhibited their development. however, despite the lack of clarity, what it does make a clear reference to is the transport of lng by these routes, consolidating the great bet on this fossil resource and the strong impact it has on the areas of extraction or storage as is the case of the natural park of doñana. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because, although it has interesting elements, it lacks a critical approach to issues that are fundamental to building a good transport policy in the long term. for example, the evaluation of alternatives during infrastructure planning and management or the differentiation of ship types and lines according to their social function or environmental performance. it is not the same to maintain and improve the secondary port network as to build industrial mega-ports which then remain underused. a regular ferry service that stimulates the local economy and improves the mobility of citizens is not the same as a macro-cruise service for mass tourism. in addition, the report advocates the introduction of gas infrastructure at ten-t ports, which is a red line for us. in spain we cannot afford to spend on gas infrastructure and transport millions of public money that could be used to promote locally generated renewable energy, create sustainable jobs in the long term and reduce our enormous energy dependence.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank mr taylor for his work on the agreement on unlocking the potential of passenger waterborne transport services. i have supported this report but have not followed the line of my group on the mention of the limits applicable to sulphur emissions.
in writing. ‒ passenger transport by sea and inland waterways offers great potential in terms of using the excess capacity available, both in terms of infrastructure and vessels, and plays a key role in connecting the eu's regions (especially the outermost regions) as an important factor of cohesion. the cruise and ferry business also promotes coastal tourism, which is one of the main maritime activities in europe. the report encourages the member states, regional and local authorities and the commission to take account of passenger transport by sea and inland waterway and, in particular, to improve the associated infrastructure, both in the core and in the comprehensive network, within the framework of the ten-t and the cem, by strengthening its interconnection with inland railway infrastructures, among others, and by providing infrastructure and information that meet the mobility needs of all travellers. it also proposes a set of measures to make the sector more competitive and cleaner, such as improving connections with urban centres, reducing the environmental impact of ships, updating passenger ship safety regulations and connectivity with other modes and regions. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ passenger transport by sea and inland waterways plays a key role in connecting the different regions of the union. it is therefore an important factor in improving cohesion, both economically and in terms of efficiency. the cruise and ferry business, on the other hand, greatly encourages coastal tourism, one of the main maritime activities in europe. in the environmental field, inland waterway transport is an environmentally friendly mode of transport included in the white paper recommendations. in view of the desirability of these provisions, we in the european parliament support the unlocking of the potential of passenger transport services by inland waterway.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, bearing in mind that passenger transport by sea and inland waterway plays a decisive role in achieving a more sustainable and efficient european transport sector. better use of available capacity for passenger transport by sea and inland waterway could contribute not only to reducing congestion and co2 emissions, but also to improving air quality and providing better transport services in general. while maritime and inland waterway transport is already one of the most sustainable modes of transport, there is still more potential to make ships less polluting and more energy efficient through investment in research and innovative technologies.
in writing. ‒ the report calls for passenger transport by inland waterway and sea to be given greater prominence on the political agenda. the report lists a number of measures to promote this mode of transport, which, although minor in comparison with air, rail and bus, is key for certain regions, in particular the islands. the proposed measures aim to make the sector as a whole more competitive, but also cleaner and greener, and range from improving connections with urban centres, statistics, the environmental impact of ships, updating passenger ship safety regulations, and connectivity with other modes and regions. it recognises the importance of this mode of transport for certain islands which have no other alternative means of transport, in particular the contribution to territorial, social and economic cohesion it represents for the outermost regions. the committee regrets the lack of development of certain areas in coastal regions and islands due to lack of connectivity and calls for the improvement of passenger terminals (especially for those with reduced mobility) and for measures to achieve better quality ferries.

in writing. ‒ this report recalls the fundamental role played by passenger transport by sea and inland waterways in connecting the different regions of the union and is therefore an important element in improving cohesion. it stressed that more than 400 million people pass through eu ports every year, with 120 million passengers transported between ports in the same member state. the report seeks to exploit the great opportunities offered by this means of transport. it should not be forgotten that sea and inland waterway transport can be an alternative to congested access roads to urban centres. i am voting in favour of the report because by favouring a means of transport which has proved to be efficient we will be favouring european integration.
in writing. ‒ passenger transport by sea and inland waterways offers great potential in terms of using the excess capacity available both in terms of infrastructure and vessels, plays a key role in connecting the different regions of the union (especially the outermost regions) and is an important factor in improving cohesion. the cruise and ferry business also promotes coastal tourism, one of the main maritime activities in europe. the report encourages member states, regional and local authorities and the commission to take account of passenger transport by sea and inland waterway and, in particular, to improve the associated infrastructure, both in the core and in the comprehensive network, within the ten-t and the cem, by strengthening its interconnection with inland railway infrastructures, among others, and by providing infrastructure and information that meet the mobility needs of all travellers. it also proposes measures to make the sector more competitive and cleaner, such as improving connections with urban centres, reducing the environmental impact of ships and updating safety regulations for passenger ships. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because, although it has interesting elements, it lacks a critical approach to issues that are fundamental to building a good transport policy in the long term. for example, the evaluation of alternatives during infrastructure planning and management or the differentiation of ship types and lines according to their social function or environmental performance. it is not the same to maintain and improve the secondary port network as to build industrial mega-ports which then remain underused. a regular ferry service that stimulates the local economy and improves the mobility of citizens is not the same as a macro-cruise service for mass tourism. in addition, the report advocates the introduction of gas infrastructure at ten-t ports, which is a red line for us. in spain we cannot afford to spend on gas infrastructure and transport millions of public money that could be used to promote locally generated renewable energy, create sustainable jobs in the long term and reduce our enormous energy dependence.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it does not add any political priority in the field of passenger transport by inland waterway and, moreover, it strengthens the presence of non-sustainable resources such as liquefied natural gas (lng). the report does not include specific references to the role that the public sector should play in the development of these channels, maintaining a market-oriented approach that has so far only inhibited their development. however, despite the lack of clarity, what it does make a clear reference to is the transport of lng by these routes, consolidating the great bet on this fossil resource and the strong impact it has on the areas of extraction or storage as is the case of the natural park of doñana. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.

in writing. ‒ community legislation on maritime safety has been applied for 15 years and has improved the safety of travellers and facilitated search and rescue operations in the event of an accident. however, there is still scope for member states to step up the enforcement of existing rules and to simplify the current regulatory framework with a view to eliminating overlapping requirements. in this respect, the report proposes a set of measures on competitiveness, environmental sustainability, safety, security and quality and accessibility of services. in europe, geography offers extraordinary opportunities for passenger transport by waterways. in fact, more than 400 million people pass through the union's ports every year. in order to support all those proposals which contribute to the development of this type of transport and which go along the path of greater intermodality, social cohesion, environmental improvement and more sustainable and efficient socioeconomic development, i have voted in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it frames and legitimises development cooperation in the logic of the market, reinforcing the role of enterprises within development cooperation mechanisms. the call for the countries receiving aid to assume 'the introduction of market economy mechanisms', 'the opening of their markets to global competition' or 'the mobilisation of private capital' is a conditioning and an attempt to use development cooperation to interfere with each country's sovereignty in organising and regulating its economy. i reject cooperation designed to open the door to business for european companies in impoverished countries. we therefore reject this report which requires and makes it a condition for the 'effectiveness' of aid that third countries enable the private sector to do business with basic services such as infrastructure, health or education. on the contrary, i believe that the effectiveness of aid depends on cooperation and the strengthening of the role of the states in these impoverished countries, on the development of public services and on public control of strategic economic sectors.
in writing. ‒ i think it is important that in the gpedc 2hlm process we do a self-criticism of the poor results achieved compared to the effort put in. i voted in favour of this report because it seems to me to be balanced and sound.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which underlines the timeliness of the development effectiveness principles. i believe it is essential that the efficiency agenda is a key pillar of the implementation of the sustainable development goals. the resolution stresses the importance of all development policy complying with the principles of appropriateness and alignment with the national development strategies of individual countries, stressing the need to unlock aid and the importance of making use of the public procurement systems of partner countries as a first option. the resolution also notes that private sector actors should adhere to the principles of development effectiveness and corporate social responsibility throughout the project life cycle and stresses the need for the private sector to respect the principles of international law and social and environmental standards, as well as the un global compact on human rights, the un guiding principles on business and human rights, the ilo core labour standards and the un convention against corruption.
