in writing. first, i would like to express my full support for the commission's proposal to establish a capacity guarantee. if the proposal is effectively implemented in all member states, if it targets sectors with current and future potential and, above all, if it has the support and collaboration of the social partners, and in particular the education and business sectors, we can achieve that millions of european citizens with low qualifications improve their employability and access the labour market more easily, thus fostering greater social cohesion. however, many rural areas in europe and spain, such as my own, aragon, are regions with a strong problem of depopulation and population dispersion, which lack an adequate broadband network, which further hinders their business and economic development. i am not disputing the crucial importance of digital skills, but i wonder whether we have the necessary infrastructure for their training and business development. if we do not take account of these different territorial realities, we risk turning a proposal to improve the employability of low-skilled european citizens into a death sentence for many small european municipalities.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i am aware of the efforts made by the commission, but the truth is that the news and the signals coming from the last few rounds are very worrying. after two and a half years of negotiations, no agreement has been reached on what constitutes an environmental good, and i wonder how it is possible to negotiate an agreement on environmental goods without reaching agreement on what these goods are. the list of products has been progressively reduced. now they're down to less than 300. this list, as you have also pointed out, is limited to goods and does not include services. the commission is working exclusively on lowering tariffs and cannot include the removal of tariff barriers at the moment. and the truth is that the contribution to environmental protection of the listed goods is increasingly being questioned. i wonder what the environmental improvement might be in the case of a tariff exemption for vacuum cleaners or refrigerators, as one of the partners is proposing. i have the feeling that the negotiations have gradually abandoned the laudable objective they were pursuing, and that the environmental impact that this agreement is intended to achieve is being reduced to an ever smaller expression. i would clearly argue that our trade policy is a fundamental instrument for tackling one of the great challenges we face, which is combating climate change; but the truth is that its aim and scope have been decaffeinated too much. and i would like to ask you a specific question: given the election result in the united states and mr trump's upcoming presidency, how do you think you can affect the outcome of these negotiations, given what is mr trump's position on global warming and his lack of confidence that he can really be effective in the fight against climate change?
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in the framework of the geneva convention we have the gothenburg protocol, which sets specific targets for the reduction of transboundary pollutant emissions. the directive we are adopting today updates european legislation, the amendment made to this protocol in 2012, and sets specific national targets for the reduction of five pollutants. these targets have to be set by member state because the conditions in each state are different. it also foresees the control and monitoring of other pollutants and their review in 2025, to make the necessary adjustments. the agreement reached by the council is very positive and balanced for industry, transport and agriculture. the agreed targets for reducing ammonia emissions are realistic and the measures are very positive, and the combination of both will allow for reducing emissions in agriculture, which can sometimes have a strong impact on urban areas. it is also important that reduction targets for mercury and carbon monoxide be adopted in the future when comparable data are available. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs girling, in particular, on the result achieved and the efforts she has made in the negotiations. this new directive will not be ideal for many, but it is an excellent instrument for reducing pollution and its impacts, especially in the area of the health of citizens.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. madam president, i am afraid i will not be as optimistic as the rest of my colleagues. the marrakesh summit has not left us with a good taste in our mouth because we have not made any progress in implementing the paris agreement; rather we are left with the fear that steps will be taken backwards. i'm sorry to tell you, mr. cañete, that i'm not going to appreciate your role as commissioner. the european union's lack of weight in the negotiations has become even more evident and, given the new world scenario, more worrying. we still wonder what a politician with interests in the oil industry and ties to the brick giants - linked, moreover, to corruption scandals like acuamed or the panama papers - is doing representing the european union's position in the fight against climate change. you spoke at marrakesh about the energy transition as unstoppable, and yet your party did not even ratify the paris agreement in time, withdrew the incentives for renewable energy, and since the people's party came to power in spain, emissions have continued to rise. spain is the only country in the european union that has increased its greenhouse gas emissions since 2013. i don't think this is a good way to make the energy transition. mr cañete, the european union has been out, absent from many important negotiations. this should make you reflect on your role as commissioner, if you are ethically up to the job. i really think that out of respect for the citizens, out of respect for the other countries, out of respect for the european union, out of respect for europe in short, you should resign.
madam president, climate change is the main challenge we face. we're not just playing with what kind of future humanity is going to have, but the very fact that humanity is going to have a future. and we have no time to lose, we've already lost a lot of time. paris was a big step forward, but it's in the implementation of the paris agreement that our response to climate change is really at stake. marrakesh can be seen as optimistic, but there are some reactions, particularly in the united states, which cause us concern. but i wanted to emphasize the humanitarian aspects. climate change intensifies natural disasters, accelerates the destruction of ecosystems, causes prolonged famines, devastating droughts, and it is the most vulnerable who suffer from this reality. we need to accelerate financial support to those most vulnerable. as the unhcr has pointed out, some 27 million people become climate refugees each year. in a few decades there may be hundreds of millions in the world. as the red cross has pointed out, political climate change is the main obstacle to the fight against hunger. so we have no time to lose; we cannot accept brakes when it comes to curbing global warming; we cannot accept, much less, steps backwards.
madam president, mr cañete, i want to express our concern about the use that you intend to make of agriculture in the fight against climate change, and i want to tell you that we will not accept that you make agriculture a factor in maintaining or even increasing emissions. we don't believe in phony solutions like so-called climate-smart farming. we will not tolerate any pressure on agricultural land or the financialisation of natural resources. we must make progress in reducing emissions. and that is why we are advocating agroecological agriculture, giving priority to local markets and short-distance marketing as a key element for another cap which will have to be described in the framework of food sovereignty. we deplore the exploitation of cop22 by morocco, condemn the expulsion of the sarawak mp selma beiruk and support the decision of the pan-african parliament to withdraw from cop22.
madam president, i would like to express my satisfaction at the pace and timetable agreed at the marrakesh summit to complete the rules of the paris agreement and because, both in the moroccan city and at the summits in lyon, paris or quito, the regional and local role in the fight against climate change is being consolidated. cities and regions are the ones who know the environmental situation in their territory best, who have the power to design urban planning and mobility, and who, thanks to their proximity, are driving the cultural and behavioural changes that are essential to decarbonising the planet. i therefore hope that at european level, institutional consideration of key players will be deepened so that europe can be a global benchmark with low emissions. i would like to know, mr cañete, how the commission is adapting its methods to work with these types of organisations.

mr president, there are votes which are a matter of common sense and democratic decency. today we are faced with a treaty whose legality is questioned not only by many members of the european parliament and civil society, but also by the judges themselves and even by the german constitutional court. we have voted today in favour of a matter which, as i said, is a matter of common sense. we want the european court of justice to rule, to decide, whether ceta is legal or not. it is unacceptable that some of you who call yourselves democrats, social democrats and christian democrats voted against. you are voting no because you are afraid that the court will say what we all know: that ceta grants extraordinary and exclusive rights to companies and not to people, and that this is contrary to the equality of all before the law, which is a fundamental principle of the rule of law. and that's why it's illegal. it has been a vote of fear, of fear of the truth, and of legality and of democracy.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of this resolution meant that the vote on ceta in the european parliament was suspended until the court of justice of the european union delivered an opinion on the compatibility of the investment chapter with the eu treaties, which could take at least two years. this meant stealing the democratic political debate which members of parliament, as representatives of the people, must have on the content of ceta, and constituting a legal tool to avoid a political decision. that would not have been in keeping with the responsibilities of the socialist group in the european parliament. we socialists are in favour of legal clarity on all aspects of the treaty and, in particular, the compatibility of the investment chapter of ceta with the union treaties, and we therefore asked for the opinion of the legal service of this parliament on this point, which endorsed this compatibility. we also consider this resolution unnecessary, since the provisions of ceta on the investment court system will not be provisionally applied if the european parliament gives its consent to the agreement. for all these reasons, we have decided to vote against this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion because the canada-eu trade agreement (ceta) raises serious legal problems which the ecj should resolve before its implementation. as national authorities and courts have stated, ceta creates institutions such as arbitration tribunals (which allow foreign multinationals to obtain financial compensation for any regulatory change affecting them, putting their profits ahead of democratic rights) or regulatory cooperation bodies (in which multinationals directly intervene in the legislative process) that adversely affect state competences. it is therefore a legal requirement that the court of justice should rule on the legislative scope of ceta and that it should not enter into force until it has been voted in favour in each member state. ceta is a treaty which will have a very negative impact on the rights of european workers, on financial and economic stability, on environmental protection and on democracy itself. i deeply regret that for a majority of members of this house its approval, for the benefit of big business, is so urgent that they want to avoid even the most elementary legal debates and protocols.
in writing. ‒ the initiative to bring ceta before the court of justice of the european union is an attempt at obstructionism. if we did that with all the laws, it would be impossible to move forward, legislate and govern. in europe, in spain, in any city hall. the european parliament has its legal services with good professionals. there has been a democratic process of debate and processing. however, it is legitimate to go to court if a law or an agreement is considered to be unlawful. anyone who thinks that, report it. i am in favour of the excellent eu-canada trade agreement. i think it's good for europeans. i do not accept that it is a matter of delegitimizing and insulting those who think so. i believe that free trade is positive, because it brings prosperity and progress, and it is compatible with social progress and respect for human rights. and i know, because history has shown it, that protectionism and tariffs impoverish. however, of course, i respect those who disagree, from trump to podemos.
in writing. ‒ the compatibility of the ceta ics with the european legal order has been questioned by associations of jurists across europe. i voted in favour of asking the european court of justice to give an opinion on the matter. we believe that this is a matter of common sense, not just a matter of being for or against the treaty, but of giving the european court of justice its proper role and not risking the entry into force of a treaty containing an instrument which could be incompatible with our legal system.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution signed by a number of meps (mostly from groups on the left) to refer ceta and especially the investment court system (ics) to the european court of justice, to check its compatibility with eu law. ceta is the most progressive treaty the eu has ever negotiated. ceta and ics have been cleared by the german high court in hannover. both parliament’s and the commission’s legal services are in no doubt that ceta and ics are compatible with eu law. further, the ics in ceta is a major overhaul and improvement on the outdated investor-state dispute system (isds), which neither meps nor ngos ever tried to refer to the ecj in the past. ics is in fact the only way to improve the outdated isds, which our member states continue to use, even against each other. there are more than 4 000 existing bilateral agreements between eu member states with out-dated isds provisions. a referral to the ecj of ceta would lead to a case taking up to one-and-a-half years. this resolution is a clear attempt by the anti-trade camp to further delay the approval of ceta in the hope of sabotaging the entire agreement, and in the process, eu trade policy as whole.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because the final result of the trilogue negotiations has reduced the demands of parliament's initial position, making it easier for the member states to maintain the current situation. this directive has proved to be a missed opportunity to oblige the member states to take immediate measures to improve the quality of the air in their territory, especially in large cities. we are facing a critical situation where thousands of deaths are being caused by the poor quality of the air we breathe in the main urban areas of the union, yet despite a good starting position of the european parliament, in the negotiations with the council and the commission the mandatory nature of the measures has been reduced, leaving aside the real emergency we have to face. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the report because, although the european parliament and the commission had proposed much more robust measures, these have not been successful during the negotiations with the council. weaknesses of the agreement reached:- the council managed to remove methane and mercury from the final agreement. - flexibility for the member states. the council has managed to force parliament to accept several of the so-called 'flexibilities' of the directive, making the limits much more difficult to enforce. - there are no binding 2025 milestones. parliament called for binding interim targets for all pollutants except methane, but in the end accepted the council's position that these targets were only indicative. - the reduction of premature mortality by 2030. the original text as amended by the european parliament contained a legally binding commitment to reduce premature mortality by 2030 from air pollution by 52% compared to 2005. the council's proposal of 49.6% is finally accepted. while the agreed text aims to further improve air quality conditions, the text was significantly watered down by the council during the negotiations.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on the agreement reached on emissions of certain air pollutants. there has been a lot of debate, but what has been achieved is a firm step in the right direction which has led me to support it in this vote.
in writing. ‒ poor air quality is responsible for more than 400 000 premature deaths a year, and its economic cost to health is estimated at between eur 300 000 and eur 900 000 million a year. many vulnerable sociodemographic groups are particularly affected, and around 90% of europeans living in cities are exposed to levels of air pollution considered harmful to human health. the commission's air quality package (18.12.2013) includes a proposal to amend directive 2001/81/ec on national emission ceilings (nec/ned directive), which replaces the current annual limitation regime for certain air pollutants. the aim is to reduce emissions in order to address the health risks and environmental effects they pose. the proposal sets limits for each member state for five toxic pollutants: sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), fine particulate matter (pm2.5), volatile organic non-methane compounds (vocs) and ammonia (nh3). although i would have liked a more ambitious agreement, in view of the council's opposition, i voted in favour of the agreement reached in order to implement the important steps it contains in dealing with the high health risks and environmental impacts of air pollution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, considering that air quality is a matter of great importance for human health and the environment. poor air quality contributes to premature death, sickness absences, high health care costs, lost productivity, lost crops and damage to buildings. in europe, the external health costs to society from air pollution are estimated at between €330 and €940 billion per year. although efforts have been made to reduce air pollution across the union, many member states are falling short of the agreed benchmarks, leaving the union far from its long-term objective of meeting the pollutant limits recommended in the 2005 who air quality guidelines. the commission proposal is based on achieving 70% of the maximum technically feasible reductions in health effects as specified by the who. now, from the union's institutions, we must closely monitor the development of the legislation and the member states' compliance with it.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the report because, although the european parliament and the commission had proposed much more robust measures, these have not been successful during the negotiations with the council. weaknesses of the agreement reached:- the council managed to remove methane and mercury from the final agreement. - flexibility for the member states. the council has managed to force parliament to accept several of the so-called 'flexibilities' of the directive, making the limits much more difficult to enforce. - there are no binding 2025 milestones. parliament called for binding interim targets for all pollutants except methane, but in the end accepted the council's position that these targets were only indicative. - the reduction of premature mortality by 2030. the original text as amended by the european parliament contained a legally binding commitment to reduce premature mortality by 2030 from air pollution by 52% compared to 2005. the council's proposal of 49.6% is finally accepted. while the agreed text aims to further improve air quality conditions, the text was significantly watered down by the council during the negotiations.
in writing. ‒ air pollution in europe causes 400 000 deaths per year and the national emissions ceilings directive is a crucial piece of legislation which is meant to tackle this problem by placing appropriate limits on certain key pollutants which cause high levels of damage to public health. the agreement on updating this directive which has come out of negotiations between parliament, the commission and the council is unacceptably weak. it has significantly lowered ambition on a range of pollutants to the extent that it is now estimated that this weakened agreement will lead to an extra 10 000 lives lost every year, compared to the original proposal. intense lobbying from agri-business has led to a text which crucially no longer includes a cap for methane as well as a lowering of the limit for ammonia, two pollutants which contribute significantly towards premature mortality and adverse health outcomes in the eu. for these reasons eh bildu has voted against endorsing this weak first reading agreement and would have preferred the three institutions to return to the negotiating table to considerably improve upon this legislation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour as it is an important step towards addressing the high health risks and environmental impacts of air pollution. poor air quality is responsible for more than 400 000 premature deaths each year and its economic cost to health is estimated at between 300 000 and 900 000 million euro annually. around 90% of europeans living in cities are exposed to levels of air pollution considered harmful to human health, and many vulnerable sociodemographic groups are particularly affected. measures to address hazardous pollutants across all sectors are therefore needed. the main objective of the socialists is to urgently address the premature deaths as a result of toxic air pollution, which amount to over 400 000 in the union, so we believe it is necessary to raise the overall level of ambition of the directive, such as the modification of the nox ceilings and the setting of binding targets for 2025 to ensure the linear reduction of emissions.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because the final result of the trilogue negotiations has reduced the demands of parliament's initial position, making it easier for the member states to maintain the current situation. this directive has proved to be a missed opportunity to oblige the member states to take immediate measures to improve the quality of the air in their territory, especially in large cities. we are facing a critical situation where thousands of deaths are being caused by the poor quality of the air we breathe in the main urban areas of the union, yet despite a good starting position of the european parliament, in the negotiations with the council and the commission the mandatory nature of the measures has been reduced, leaving aside the real emergency we have to face. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ this text is a reminder of the effects of poor air quality. premature death, sick leave, and high health care costs are just a few examples. this text thus sets new national emission limits for the most significant types of air pollutants. it thus modifies the emission commitment for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, non-methane volatile organic compounds and ammonia, for fine particles of not less than 2,5 microns in diameter and for methane emissions. it also lays down new rules on public participation in the preparation of plans relating to the environment. i vote in favour because of the clear benefits to human health and the environment of good air quality.
in writing. ‒ poor air quality is responsible for more than 400 000 premature deaths per year and its economic cost to health is estimated at between eur 300 000 and eur 900 000 million per year. many vulnerable sociodemographic groups are particularly affected and around 90% of europeans living in cities are exposed to levels of air pollution considered harmful to human health. the commission's air quality package (18.12.2013) includes a proposal to amend directive 2001/81/ec on national emission ceilings (nec/ned directive) to replace the current annual limitation regime for certain air pollutants. the aim is to reduce emissions in order to address the health risks and environmental effects they pose. the proposal sets limits for each state for five toxic pollutants: sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), fine particulate matter (pm 2.5), volatile organic non-methane compounds (vocs) and ammonia (nh3). although i would have liked a more ambitious agreement, in view of the council's opposition, i voted in favour of the agreement reached in order to implement the important steps it contains in dealing with the high health risks and environmental impacts of air pollution.

in writing. ‒ this proposal for a directive on the reduction of emissions of air pollutants, known as national emission ceilings (necs), is an essential instrument for improving air quality. in addition to setting national ceilings for 2020 and 2030 (the agreement on the latter date is a novelty), it requires member states to draw up national air pollution control programmes and systematically monitor the impact of air pollution on ecosystems. the agreed figures imply drastic reductions in pollutant emissions, with the aim of achieving a significant reduction in the health impact measured in premature deaths caused by poor air quality (it is estimated that the 400 000 premature deaths per year in the union will be reduced by almost half). the implementation of this directive will mean that all community countries will have to assume very demanding but also very necessary obligations to alleviate a major environmental problem. i therefore voted in favour of this text because i am concerned that the poor quality of the air we breathe, especially in cities, has a serious impact on the health of citizens.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the international banking regulation process known as basel iii. the resolution calls for the financial position of banks to be improved but without significantly increasing capital requirements, and for the european banking model to be respected in the context of international competition. the report supports the risk-based approach to capital levels, but with reduced variability.
in writing. ‒ this resolution aims to water down the work of basel iii and limit capital requirements on european banks, one of the most speculative in the world. the financial system has amply demonstrated its inability to self-regulate and the serious risk it poses to the stability of the economic system as a whole: that is why our proposal is based on public banking and the prohibition of speculative activity. in the meantime, it is necessary to ensure that private banks take such basic precautions as providing themselves with sufficient capital so that their shareholders bear the financial risks they incur, rather than passing on their speculative losses to the states. that is why i cannot accept the content of this report and have voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i agree to tighten certain banking rules in order to find a fairer system for citizens. but the sector is crucial to the financing of the economy, and the different models of european banking must be taken into account when changing certain criteria. we will follow very closely the involvement of the european banking authority, the ecb and the commission in the basel committee.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution, in which parliament is hampering the revision of the basel directive on the capital requirements of banks. increasing capital requirements force banks to hold a larger amount of capital when making loans. this is a condition for reducing instability and vulnerability in the financial system. however, the position of the banking lobbies and the commission is that this would reduce the competitiveness of european banks vis-à-vis american ones. i think the high volatility of european banks and their disproportionate size is a very serious threat to european society and requires drastic intervention if financial institutions are to fulfil their social role.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr gualtieri, for his work on the report which underlines the importance of sound global rules and principles for prudential regulation of banks and welcomes the csbb's post-crisis work on this.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this resolution by the committee on economic and monetary affairs of the parliament on the international banking regulation process known as basel iii. with this resolution we call for the financial position of banks to be improved without significantly increasing capital requirements and for the european banking model to be respected in the context of international competition. in addition, the report supports the risk-based approach to capital levels, but with reduced variability.

in writing. ‒ this text expresses the european parliament's position on the discussion of a reform of the prudential framework for banks currently being carried out by the basel committee on banking supervision (bcbs). this reform aims to make the standardised approach more risk-sensitive, while restricting the use of internal models for certain portfolios and setting some levels for the rest of the products on the basis of the standardised approach. by voting in favour, i support the basle negotiations, considering it essential that their adaptation to the european financial regulatory framework does not lead to substantial increases in the capital requirements of institutions, and that it does not affect the different banking business models asymmetrically and contributes to the design and maintenance of a stable regulatory framework and equal treatment of all institutions.

in writing. ‒ this afet report is based on the annual report from the council to the european parliament on the common foreign and security policy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the report also calls for an eu white paper on security and defence and calls for a strong defence industry. it also supports further reforms to the security sector and training and equipping also the military financed by development aid (including the civilian instrument contributing to stability and peace), promotes the extension of the athena mechanism to finance all union military missions and tactical groups, escaping parliamentary control, and pushes for the deployment of union tactical groups for all types of crisis management. we reject military funding from the union budget, and give priority to the civilian approach to conflict resolution and stop contributing to military escalation, and advocate a total separation between the union and nato, while the report proposes greater cooperation. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ this report highlights the deterioration of european security in the face of the growing terrorist threat and the war situation in ukraine, syria and iraq, as well as new challenges such as cyberterrorism. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. it also called for greater facilities to finance international operations and for the urgent establishment of an economic fund for this purpose. it called for the strengthening of military research and the european arms industry with sufficient funding and industrial production aid similar to that received by north american companies in the sector. i voted against because it goes into the political and financial stakes of a strong army and arms industry in the union to combat external threats. although i understand that some of these threats are real, i believe that by increasing the climate of war we are not going to achieve a real solution to the problems and a framework of stability and peace in the union.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report by mr pascu on the implementation of the common security and defence policy. we must make progress on a european army, but i have refrained from referring to the allocation of 2% of the national gdp for this purpose. i think that a more thorough analysis is needed before any concrete figures are set, however much this was repeated at the wales and warsaw summits.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy, which assesses the implementation of policies in this area and the events of the year. the report calls for a review of these policies, as well as an eu white paper, a stronger defence industry and a european defence action plan. it also considered that cooperation with nato should be improved and extended. it also calls for greater intra-community coordination within the union to be able to adapt better to new threats.

in writing. ‒ this report highlights the deterioration of european security in the face of the growing terrorist threat and the war situation in ukraine, syria and iraq, as well as new challenges such as cyberterrorism. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. it also called for greater facilities to finance international operations and for the urgent establishment of an economic fund for this purpose. it called for the strengthening of military research and the european arms industry with sufficient funding and industrial production aid similar to that received by north american companies in the sector. i voted against because it goes into the political and financial stakes of a strong army and arms industry in the union to combat external threats. although i understand that some of these threats are real, i believe that by increasing the climate of war we are not going to achieve a real solution to the problems and a framework of stability and peace in the union.
in writing. ‒ this proposal is based on the evolution of the current strategic context of the union, characterised by deteriorated security, the mix of conventional and hybrid threats, the intervention of state and non-state actors and the emergence of new (less predictable) risks to the east and south. this requires that priority be given to preventing crises that occur beyond the community's borders, while intervening in the resolution and stabilisation phases of conflicts that directly affect the security of the union. conscious that europe must deal with a growing number of crises in its immediate neighbourhood (the most visible consequence of which is terrorist acts perpetrated on our own territory) in the most effective way possible - through joint action and closer cooperation - i thought it appropriate to vote in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ this afet report is based on the annual report from the council to the european parliament on the common foreign and security policy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the report also calls for an eu white paper on security and defence and calls for a strong defence industry. it also supports further reforms to the security sector and training and equipping also the military financed by development aid (including the civilian instrument contributing to stability and peace), promotes the extension of the athena mechanism to finance all union military missions and tactical groups, escaping parliamentary control, and pushes for the deployment of union tactical groups for all types of crisis management. we reject military funding from the union budget, and give priority to the civilian approach to conflict resolution and stop contributing to military escalation, and advocate a total separation between the union and nato, while the report proposes greater cooperation. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ this is yet another example of the russophobia of this parliament, which is constantly exaggerating the differences between russia and the union. the report is a frontal attack on the media, calling for the use of nato instruments, such as the centre of excellence for strategic communications (coe stratcom), to combat the russian media. it also calls for direct support for 'independent' media, which is paradoxical, since by sponsoring them from european organisations, these media would obviously cease to be independent. not content with this, the report, and following this paranoid anti-russian rhetoric, argues that 'the security and intelligence services conclude that russia has the capacity and the intention to carry out operations aimed at destabilizing other countries', continuing the militarist rhetoric and leading to an unacceptable escalation of tension. the report identifies two propaganda threats: a state actor, russia, and terrorist groups such as daesh, and focuses on giving the union the means to support its own strategic propaganda campaigns, mainly against russia, a un country which it places on the same threat level as daesh. my vote was clearly against.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from voting on the report because, although i agree with the content, i do not share the approach. it focuses on particular criticism of one country, russia, and one terrorist group, daesh. to equate and put a country on the same level as a terrorist group does not seem to me to be right and distorts the text. i share the criticism of the russian propaganda media policy aimed at disrupting the process of integration of the union. and in this respect, as the text says, i regret the support given by russia to anti-european forces in the union, as far as far-right parties, populist forces and movements that deny the basic values of liberal democracies are concerned. i also agree that the union should make strategic communication a priority and devote the appropriate resources to it. and i condemn without reservation the terrorist group daesh, and of course the systematic use and promotion of hate speech for political purposes. the union must develop strong and effective common policies to protect society from the processes of radicalisation which lead to terrorism and violent extremism.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on strategic communication of the union against propaganda by third parties, because it makes an analysis which leaves out many aspects of the geopolitical reality in which the union is currently situated. we believe that encouraging hate speech and fear is an ineffective way of putting an end to the threats to the union. the analysis and tone of the whole report is one-sided and untrue, and it is also on the opposite political line from ours in the field of foreign policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i do not agree with it at all. the only section i could share is number 6. it is not acceptable to vote for a resolution which equates russia and isis and the propaganda they both use. i completely disagree with the content of this report, which in my opinion should not have been written.
in writing. ‒ this parliament's own-initiative report deals with two external threats in terms of propaganda directed against the union: one from a non-state actor, the terrorist group daesh, and one from a state actor, the russian federation, and seeks to counter radicalisation through cooperation between member states and the european institutions. however, it does place a state, russia, on the same level as a terrorist group. although the need to react by means of strategic communication against propaganda directed at the union and its citizens is clear, the mixing of state and non-state actors at the same level is not an appropriate approach for a resolution of this parliament. i have therefore decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because it is an allegation rather than a report, far removed from the geopolitical interests of the union. it is unacceptable in my view that it resembles a potential ally as russia is with daesh.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, considering that the union, its member states and its citizens are under increasing systematic pressure to counter information, disinformation and poisoning campaigns and propaganda by non-state actors and countries, such as terrorist and transnational criminal organisations in neighbouring countries. freedom of the media, access to information and freedom of expression are cornerstones of the democratic system of the union. we must remember that strategic communication and information warfare are not only external to the union but also internal to it, and that the union must therefore give strategic communication a priority and devote the appropriate resources to it.
in writing. ‒ while i fully understand the essential need to counteract propaganda and disinformation by third parties that directly threaten the values and the stability of the union, i simultaneously believe that in order to achieve this goal, our strategic communication must meet some basic requirements: 1) it should observe fundamental european values, such as freedom of expression and freedom of the press; 2) it should be sensible to the different political natures of the parties involved; and 3) it must be effective – and at least not counter-productive. after a long and careful evaluation, i understand that the final report does not sufficiently meet these three basic requirements: 1) the idea of a free and independent media is hard to reconcile with the proactive training and support of these same media by the eu itself; 2) the report puts russia, a nation-state with a long history, at a same level as daesh, an accidental pseudo-state and a terrorist group; failing to recognize the long-term need of a peaceful cooperation between russia and the union, specially where our interests overlap; 3) i thus believe that the implementation of this strategy may unnecessarily escalate on going conflicts and don’t serve its own strategic priority.

in writing. ‒ this report addresses the issue of cybersecurity, in particular the attacks on the union by media and propaganda seeking to discredit it and its institutions. it also focuses on the fight against daesh propaganda on the internet. the report proposes, among other things, to study the sources of funding for anti-european propaganda, to increase the visibility of moderate muslim academics who have credibility to delegitimize daesh propaganda and to create a site, on social networks widely used to discredit the union and incite hatred, aimed at the general public, which brings together the various means of detecting disinformation and explains their operation. i am voting in favour of the report because it is important to put an end to disinformation which ultimately undermines something as important as the right of citizens to access objective and quality information, which is essential for the formation of a democratic society based on the rule of law.

in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution highlights the growing pressure on the union from third parties, both state and non-state actors, who are using propaganda to weaken it. in order to serve as a basis for evaluating the objectives pursued by the community's strategic communication plans, it points to the methods used by russia to discredit the union's institutions, to engineer a strategic separation of the united states and the union, to foster division between its member states and to call into question european values in terms of respect for human rights and the rule of law. it also looks at daesh's strategies for youth recruitment, the promotion of radical islam and the rise of hatred towards community principles and interests. the text calls for greater coordination between the relevant parties at both union and national level, so that work is based on an approach that is effective in combating disinformation and propaganda. i am convinced that strategic communication is one of the essential vectors in the framework of our foreign policy, and i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it is committed to the effective defence of the rights of deaf, deafblind and hard of hearing people and calls for a series of measures such as the official recognition of sign languages, both national and regional, in the different member states and in the institutions of the union. it also advocates for the professional recognition of sign language interpreters and advocates the incorporation of sign language into educational programmes in a similar way to foreign languages. it also considered that the inclusion of deaf, deafblind and hard of hearing people should be ensured in european programmes such as erasmus+ and that their integration into the labour market should be effectively promoted in the european institutions. conscious of the importance of promoting sign language in education in raising awareness throughout society and facilitating respect for the right to equality of the more than 52 million citizens and residents who are estimated to use different sign languages in the union, i have decided to support this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i fully share the spirit of non-discrimination against social groups such as deaf people, and we defend the principle of equality in the institutions. the resolution has been strongly defended and worked on by our parliamentary group, and it advocates the full integration of this group by facilitating the accessibility of all information, and by requesting european recognition of professional sign language interpreters.
in writing. ‒ i have supported the resolution on sign languages and professional sign language interpreters, as well as the four amendments to it. this resolution highlights the need for qualified and professional sign language interpreters which can be met by official recognition of national and regional sign languages in the member states and the union institutions, as well as by regulated university or similar training.
in writing. ‒ on 28 september, the european parliament hosted the historic conference on 'multilingualism and equal rights in the eu: the role of sign languages'. speakers stressed the importance of sign language recognition and the availability of interpretation for the full inclusion of deaf people in society. they also stressed that recognition alone is not enough: only full implementation of legislation can ensure that deaf people have access to interpreters, with a serious shortage of fully qualified university interpreters. this joint resolution by the s&d, epp, ecr, alde, greens/efa and efdd groups contains the basic principles on the qualification of sign language professionals and on access to such services for deaf, deaf-mutes and people with severe hearing impairments, in order to ensure equal opportunities and non-discrimination in areas such as education, the labour market and the european institutions. in spain alone, more than a million people have hearing impairments, of whom about 100,000 suffer from profound deafness. for these reasons i have voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ accessibility is a prerequisite for people with disabilities to be able to live independently and participate fully in society on equal terms. such accessibility is not limited to the physical accessibility of the environment, but includes accessibility to information and communication, including in the form of content presented in sign language. the professional status of qualified and professional sign language interpreters and the quality of subtitling on public and private television also vary considerably between member states. given that article 15 of the european social charter of 1961 states that every disabled person has the right to social integration and to participation in the life of the community, we in the european parliament support this resolution on sign languages and professional sign language interpreters.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution bearing in mind that as full citizens, all persons with disabilities, in particular women and children, including deaf and hard of hearing people, both those who use sign language and those who do not, enjoy equal rights and are entitled to inalienable dignity, equal treatment, an independent life, autonomy and full participation in society. therefore, there is a need for official recognition of national and regional sign languages in the member states and the union institutions, as well as for regulated training. all citizens of the union should have access to the same information and communication as others through sign language interpretation, subtitling, voice recognition or alternative forms of communication, including interpretation of spoken languages.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this objection because, given the fact that an active substance meets the requirements for authorisation, including the scientific report from efsa, i believe that the ec has acted correctly, especially given the fact that the possibility of providing new data which may confirm or interrupt such authorisation remains open. farmers need to have active substances to fight pests.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection because i am against the renewal of the active substance bentazone, one of the pesticides most frequently found in groundwater and deep water, as there is no scientific data to show that it is a safe substance, either for human and animal health or for the environment. the commission's proposal therefore breaches the precautionary principle and ignores the ombudsman's proposals to improve the commission's pesticide approval system (by restricting the practice of approving a substance while simultaneously requesting data that is expected to confirm its safety), so i voted in favour of the objection.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report for a number of reasons. firstly, because the draft commission implementing regulation does not implement the european ombudsman's proposals for a solution to improve the commission's pesticide approval system. but above all, i do not see the logic of the commission's decision to approve an active substance, while at the same time requesting data confirming its safety (a process known as 'confirmatory data procedure') would allow the active substance to be placed on the market before the commission had obtained all the necessary data to support that decision. we must therefore wait until we have this data before making any decisions about it.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of the objection in line with the precautionary principle to avoid the renewal of bentazone. in the absence of data to demonstrate the safety of a chemical substance, i understand that its use should not be authorised. the european commission exceeds its implementing powers as provided for in regulation (ec) no 1107/2009. the intended renewal of the authorisation of bentazone for 15 years is not compatible with the objective of regulation (ec) no 1107/2009, which is to ensure a high level of protection of both human and animal health and the environment.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank mr poc for his work on this report, which i voted against. i also voted in favour of the epp amendment which called for the authorisation of the product until 31 july 2024. as that amendment was not adopted, i voted against the report, which i consider to be an overreach by the commission of the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1107/2009. the agricultural sector needs this product for its crops and efsa has already said that it is not harmful and has the safety standards well covered.
in writing. ‒ commission implementing regulation (eu) 2016/549 of 8 april 2016 amending implementing regulation (eu) no 540/201 extended the approval period of the active substance bentazone until 30 june 2017. the european commission has also proposed to extend the authorisation of bentazone until 31 january 2032 in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1107/2009 concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market. i voted for a seven-and-a-half-year extension and against the abolition of the use of the active substance. i understand that bentazone acts as a post-emergent selective herbicide against broadleaf weeds on a wide range of crops, which allows control of weeds and is a fundamental tool for the management of various crops in spain, such as rice. the abolition of the use of bentazone reduces the plant protection tools of farmers, worsening their competitive capacity.

the istanbul convention on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence is the first instrument in europe to establish legally binding and specific rules on preventing gender-based violence, protecting victims and punishing the perpetrator. the convention covers a wide range of measures, including obligations ranging from awareness raising and data collection, to legal measures on the criminalisation of different forms of violence. although all the member states of the european union have signed the convention, only 14 of them have ratified it. the european parliament considers it essential to support the union's accession to the istanbul convention on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence.

the next item is the debate on the report by catherine bearder, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, on the eu action plan against wildlife trafficking (2016/2076 (ini)) (a8-0303/2016).
vice-president of the commission. – mr. president, there has been a dramatic surge in wildlife trafficking. it raises between eur 8 and 20 billion each year for organised criminal groups, ranking alongside trafficking of drugs, people and arms. it not only threatens the survival of some species, it also creates corruption, claims human victims and deprives poorer communities of much-needed income. it also threatens security in central africa, funding militia and terrorist group activities. the commission responded by adopting in february an eu action plan to tackle wildlife trafficking within the eu, and to strengthen the eu’s role in a global fight against these illegal activities. member states endorsed the plan at the june environment council. parliament already had an important role in developing the eu approach. your resolution of 2014 was an important contribution to the development of the action plan. this new resolution is comprehensive and ambitious. it is particularly encouraging to see that several committees – development, international trade and fisheries – have provided substantial input to the resolution, in addition to the environment committee. this reflects the multi-dimensional nature of wildlife trafficking as well as the need for a large spectrum of stakeholders and communities to take action and work together to address this trafficking. in the commission also, not only myself and carmen vella but also several other colleagues – federica mogherini, nina mimica and dimitris avramopoulos – were all closely associated in the development and adoption of the action plan, with the support of our services. we have now turned to implementation of the action plan, as requested in your resolution. it is too early to give a detailed report on this, but good progress has already been made since its adoption. the action plan helped the eu to get successful outcomes at the recent conference of the parties of the cites convention. the cites cop was a success and the eu was a major driver for that. my colleague commissioner vella was on the spot with the commission team to guide eu positions, and i know also that the rapporteur herself and several other members of this house were in johannesburg following the negotiations. the eu tabled a record number of proposals at this meeting. this included the inclusion of new species in cites, in particular rare and valuable reptiles and birds which are traded into the eu for the exotic pet market. the resolution was adopted, which for the first time in cites clearly recognises that corruption is a key enabler for wildlife trafficking and calls on cites parties and bodies to investigate and penalise it. the eu also pushed for targeted recommendations and sanctions to improve the fight against ivory, rhino horn and tiger trafficking. at international level, we have also succeeded in including the issue of wildlife trafficking on the agenda of the g20 and of the financial action task force, the main international body in charge of money laundering, so that the financial dimension of wildlife trafficking will be addressed. within the eu, the commission has been working with enforcement agencies from the member states, europol and european networks of judges and prosecutors, to raise the awareness of wildlife crime, especially through training sessions and the facilitation of joint enforcement operations. the commission and the member states are also developing guidelines on trade ivory to make sure that trade within the eu, or exports from the eu, do not contribute to international ivory trafficking. we will continue to work on many strands of the eu action plan to make sure that the eu delivers on its commitments and makes a real difference in the fight against wildlife trafficking.

mr president, europe must be decisive in the fight against wildlife trafficking in the face of its three worst enemies. first, the loss of biodiversity. the report estimates that we are facing a clear extinction of species which could upset the food chain of animal species and cause irreparable damage to some of the ecosystems that are unique to our planet. second, the financing of criminal organizations. the business of wildlife smuggling is worth approximately 20 billion euros a year. 20 billion euros are hidden, which neither tax the states, nor is it known where they come from, nor do they help to improve the economy of the countries of origin of these species; on the contrary, they destabilize it. third, impunity for environmental crimes. environmental crime has traditionally been considered a minor offence, with small penalties that rarely go beyond administrative sanctions. we must be aware that the damage we do to nature will be returned to us tenfold, one hundredfold or a thousandfold, and we must accordingly introduce coherent, effective and dissuasive criminal sanctions, as the report says. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat illegal wildlife trade, and it is therefore important that the member states and the commission and the european union should take the necessary steps to ensure that the measures are implemented.

in writing. as undeniable as climate change is the sixth extinction of species. overfishing, extensive cattle ranching in the amazon, or palm oil plantations in borneo and sumatra are eliminating animal and plant habitats. but the great cruelty that contributes to the extinction of species is the trade in exotic animals. bloody business that moves billions. according to a un report, more than 80 elephants are killed every day, more than 1,000 rhinos and 120 tigers are killed annually, and these species are dramatically on the verge of extinction. spain is the gateway to europe for many wildlife species from the illegal trade, which are confiscated and relocated to private wildlife centres or unfortunately are slaughtered even though they are threatened or endangered species. some 15 000 animals have been confiscated in spain since 2005, which like many other member states lacks its own rescue centres, leaving confiscated animals in private hands and with donors without an official protocol for re-adaptation to the environment. spain, because of its location, should have more support at european level not only for customs control but also for the direct victims of this illegal trade.

on behalf of the ppe group mr president, commissioner, rapporteur, apart from my personal wish to speak on this report, i represent mrs monteiro here, who apologizes for her absence, as the alternative rapporteur on behalf of the epp. i'll translate your criteria on her behalf, since she's absent. the report, according to mrs monteiro, analyses the new opportunities for the transport the connection between customer and company and are part of the unstoppable innovation. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the public authorities. the rapporteur also calls on the member states to update their national laws to include the idea of a collaborative economy. i will now make a number of personal judgments, not without saying that i agree with mrs monteiro on this point: the sharing economy can and should be an element of innovation and competition, provided that it respects the basic elements of transport, such as safety and consumer protection, and does not lead to unfair competition. the element of concern to the spanish delegation, however, is light industrial vehicles. small businesses cannot rely on transport modes that optimize economies of scale. in paragraph 37 of his report, mr riquet asks whether there are reasons for exempting light commercial vehicles from the application of european legislation. as its title 'new opportunities for small transport enterprises' indicates, the report is intended to facilitate the integration of small and medium-sized enterprises into the transport market. it is therefore inconsistent in our view to question the exemption for light commercial vehicles, since this would be contrary to the intention of the title of the report. we therefore understand and see it as an obstacle that the administrative conditions for smaller vehicles should be tightened up. light goods vehicles represent a on behalf of the alde group. mr president, commissioner, i would like to congratulate mr riquet on this report which suggests a powerful work programme to enable europe's small transport companies to adapt to two major challenges: the evolution which will lead this sector to make intensive use of new technologies and its adaptation to new business models which come with the sharing economy. these companies will thus play a decisive role in the fight against climate change, while being in the best position to solve the great challenge of integrating the different modes of transport into an intelligent mobility system, the solution to the 'last mile' challenge, both in non-urban spaces and in cities. to encourage current and future entrepreneurs to take advantage of this opportunity requires a proper boost to the transport market unit. the report also states that it requires a change in the philosophy of regulation to adapt it to the new reality, to encourage innovation and fair competition, and to guarantee consumer rights. it should also recognise and build on the momentum that many local authorities are already putting into promoting this transformation with small and local operators. if we get this right, the change will be a quarry of quality jobs. commissioner, i can only urge the member states once again to meet the investment priorities foreseen in the ten-t because they are necessary to enable this development. that is why they add value at european level and why they must be concluded.

mr president, commissioner, the negotiation of the many agreements which the european union has undertaken in the field of commercial aviation requires us to make an effort to be transparent, because the exercise of transparency is the basis of confidence. i believe that it is an obligation to disclose timetables, interests at stake, dates and objectives envisaged in these processes, and that the treaties are respected as regards the information that this parliament should receive and the time when it should receive it, as does the european council and before and after each round of negotiations. finally, we must ensure that agreements are only applied after the approval of this house. the protocol of clarity and transparency which this question raises i believe resolves any doubt about the progress of a negotiating process. it is clear that this does not guarantee that everyone will agree with the contents of an agreement reached under these conditions, but we will avoid criticism for opacity in the future.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, in this house there is a lot of talk about the security of energy supply, but rather little about the security of access to energy. in spain, more than five million people suffer from energy poverty. as the news tragically reminded us recently, more people die each year from lack of energy supply than from traffic accidents. a basic right such as access to energy is increasingly becoming a luxury. that is why we must recognize the right to energy as a common good and necessary for life and prohibit power cuts to people in vulnerable situations as the directives require. and of course, to fulfill this right, we have to secure the supply. but it is not a problem of gas coming from russia or from elsewhere, as the commission is suggesting, it is a problem of not wanting to assume that the european union must embark on a real energy transition which, on the one hand, improves energy efficiency and, on the other, allows the development of renewable energies. in fact, the european commission's own stress tests for possible gas supply cuts say it: the current infrastructure is sufficient and meeting the 2030 targets for renewables and efficiency would improve the situation and reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels. we therefore ask the commission and the member states to listen less to lobbies and more to the people for the winter package. and finally, these rich resources of the caspian sea make us accomplices of authoritarian regimes like azerbaijan's. mr president, commissioner, the geostrategic dimension of energy security is certainly crucial, but energy poverty cannot wait. commissioner bulc, tell the energy commissioner that he's not here today. we are talking about 50 million europeans, 5 million spaniards. what else has to happen for them to take urgent action? it is urgent to grant a winter break, give priority to a european framework for combating energy poverty, with reduced tariffs and a review of taxes and rates on electricity bills. the commission should focus european funds for efficiency and self-generation on citizens suffering from energy poverty, benefiting them with efficiency obligations, improvements in the retail market and promotion of self-consumption. this is about safety. we are talking about a vital right such as access to energy, which affects many, many people, many people of flesh and blood who cannot wait, madam commissioner.
in writing. the geostrategic dimension of the security of energy supply cannot blind us to the plight of more than 50 000 000 europeans affected by energy poverty. 60% of deaths in home fires are attributed to energy poverty. rosa died early monday in reus (tarragona), when her mattress caught fire. the 81-year-old woman had been without electricity for two months, lit herself with the candles that caused the fire. how many deaths must there be before the commission takes urgent action in the face of this tragedy? a european framework for combating energy poverty, with the promotion of reduced tariffs and the revision of taxes and turnover rates, is a priority. the commission should focus efficiency and self-generation funds on energy-poor citizens, while benefiting them with efficiency obligations, retail market improvements and promotion of self-consumption. a common definition, addressing data standardisation and collecting best practice is needed. in short, no one should have to choose between heating or cooling and food or medicine, let alone pay with his own life. we therefore urge the commission to take the appropriate measures as a matter of urgency.

the author. mr president, the situation of the guarani-kiowa indigenous community in brazil is dramatic: four hundred murders since 2003. it was therefore urgent for this european parliament to take a decision. guarani-kaiowa do not die of old age or rare diseases, but are murdered. and i'm right: they are murdered. who is the murderer? multinational corporations that violate human rights constantly. their ancestral lands, to which they are entitled under international and brazilian national legislation, are occupied by the soybean industry, a soybean and ultimately european multinationals. and how do they do that? through impunity the authorities of brazil do not commit to the delimitation of their lands and also through the increase of repression by the illegitimate president temer towards social movements, students, the trade union movement sin tierra. and if anyone dares to interfere with temer's anti-social reforms to the brazilian constitution, you get your headquarters stormed with gunfire. but for the european union and the popular party, brazil is now opening up to the world and to the business of free trade.
mr president, with the expansion of soybean and sugarcane monocultures, the guarani-kaiowá indigenous people have been relegated to very limited areas. he suffers from extreme poverty and has no access to land. the government's commitment to demarcate its 36 territories has not materialized and attacks on this community continue. after the coup against president dilma rousseff, criminalization, repression and violence against community leaders, indigenous peoples and social movements increased. in the context of this repression of the popular movement throughout brazil, i would also like to bring up the case of the landless movement, which is being criminalised and repressed for its tireless struggle for land reform, social justice and against the violence of agribusiness. i want to highlight the november 4th police raid on the florestan fernandes national school in são paulo, without a court order and shooting at students and mst militants. i would ask the european union to call attention to the urgent need for brazil to put an end to repression, to criminalization and to demand respect for human rights.

in writing. ‒ the 'macro-financial assistance' to jordan is nothing more than the union's intermediation in a private loan of up to eur 350 million as counterpart to an imf adjustment programme, which will impose further cuts in labour rights and the public budget of jordan's fragile economy. i believe that the imposition of new neoliberal policies will only increase instability in the region politically. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i abstained because i think the initiative itself is positive and necessary, but it has been approached from an angle that makes it very unlikely to achieve its objectives, and that involves a significant risk that the aid will, in fact, have a counterproductive effect. the aim of this aid is to provide a breathing gas to jordan, whose economy has been one of the hardest hit by the war in syria. the fall in income, together with the massive arrival of refugees, has contributed to a marked increase in external debt. hence the macrofinancial assistance initiative which we voted for. the reason why i doubt whether this aid will really support the jordanian economy and society is that the instrument is linked to imf loan programmes which, as a condition, impose the implementation of neo-liberal structural reforms. these reforms, coupled with a possible increase in debt, can have negative long-term consequences and were not the best option available.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive because it aims to improve the transparency and governance of institutions providing occupational retirement pensions (pillar 2), which are normally linked to social partners and common in countries such as germany and the netherlands. the commission proposal also aims at the creation of crossborder funds, which is a positive step in the context of a genuine internal market within the union.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains positive points which improve the current transnational functioning of pensions, it maintains the approach of treating them as mere financial products. there are many problems for crossborder pensions that this directive seeks to solve, especially those linked to the financial risk to which such funds may be subject. this report addresses many of these problems; it improves transparency and mandatory information to beneficiaries, it includes environmental risks in the scope, etc. however, the report maintains the focus on financing pensions, including the possibility of financing and participating in risk finance mechanisms such as efsi bonds. it is because of this basic approach that, although i share the need for some of the improvements that have been made, i have not been able to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in this report because it is a contribution by parliament to the process of recasting the directive on the second pillar of pensions. these pensions are those resulting from an agreement between the company and the employees, with the employer contributing to a fund set up specifically for this purpose. it is therefore a system halfway between the public pension system and private pension funds, a system which is more widespread in countries such as the united kingdom and the netherlands. while we understand that in some cases these funds represent a trade union conquest, and that it is good for consumers that there is progress in greater standardisation and the possibility of transferring rights from one country to another, we are opposed to pension funds being regarded as a mere financial service. we are also concerned that the solvency requirements for these funds are being relaxed in relation to others.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report by mr hayes on the activities and supervision of employment pension funds. the agreement states that the scope of application will be the employment pension funds. where, under their national law, they have no legal personality, member states shall apply the directive to the funds or to the authorized bodies responsible for managing them and acting on their behalf.

in writing. ‒ i abstained in this report because it is a contribution by parliament to the process of recasting the directive on the second pillar of pensions. these pensions are those resulting from an agreement between the company and the employees, with the employer contributing to a fund set up specifically for this purpose. it is therefore a system halfway between the public pension system and private pension funds, a system which is more widespread in countries such as the united kingdom and the netherlands. while we understand that in some cases these funds represent a trade union conquest, and that it is good for consumers that there is progress in greater standardisation and the possibility of transferring rights from one country to another, we are opposed to pension funds being regarded as a mere financial service. we are also concerned that the solvency requirements for these funds are being relaxed in relation to others.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains positive points which improve the current transnational functioning of pensions, it maintains the approach of treating them as mere financial products. there are many problems for crossborder pensions that this directive seeks to solve, especially those linked to the financial risk to which such funds may be subject. this report addresses many of these problems; it improves transparency and mandatory information to beneficiaries, it includes environmental risks in the scope, etc. however, the report maintains the focus on financing pensions, including the possibility of financing and participating in risk finance mechanisms such as efsi bonds. it is because of this basic approach that, although i share the need for some of the improvements that have been made, i have not been able to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ this text aims to encourage the development of occupational retirement savings plans in a context that is shaped by the recent economic and financial crisis which has put pensions under intense pressure in many member states. the demographic indicators (european society is ageing, life expectancy is increasing and the working population is declining) suggest that intergenerational solidarity is not working. in view of all this, more countries should consider the establishment of complementary second pillar pension schemes, which would result in more secure pension benefits. it also points out that good supervisory and governance standards are crucial to provide citizens with a high degree of confidence in their system and to encourage them to participate in it. i therefore consider it appropriate to vote in favour of this document.
