in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i am generally in favour of it, as it proposes changes and improvements in the way it operates, relating to simplification, speeding up the allocation of funds, reducing processing times, introducing greater transparency, increasing the amount of advances and reducing thresholds. however, i believe that an important opportunity is being lost to propose real improvements for the people affected by disasters. it would have been time to extend the objectives of the solidarity fund to include humanitarian disasters and not just natural disasters. a great opportunity to use community funds to alleviate the effects of the migration crisis which is causing so many deaths at our borders. finally, the introduction of gender equality policies and women's rights should have been considered as eligibility criteria for the proposals, as women are one of the groups that suffer most from the consequences of natural disasters. i voted in favour, although i am aware of the limitations in the evaluation of the fund.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the alternative resolution tabled by the gue and in favour of the alde resolution in the opinion of the court of justice on the compatibility with the treaties of the agreement between the united states of america and the european union on the protection of personal data in connection with the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences. our group has tabled an alternative resolution in which it considers that there is legal uncertainty as to the compatibility of the envisaged agreement with the treaties and asks that the court of justice be asked for an opinion on the compatibility of the agreement with the treaties.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this agreement is to protect the right to privacy in the context of cooperation between the united states and the european union in the fight against terrorism. however, the protection standards are not in line with the requirements set out in european legislation, and a number of exception clauses for the united states are maintained, perpetuating an asymmetrical relationship between the union and the us. it also regulates rights on the basis of citizenship, because it guarantees citizens of the member states of the union more rights than persons who reside or operate in them without being citizens. finally, by elevating this type of regulation to the status of an international agreement, the judicial investigations (many of which are currently under way) on this matter are being hindered, since this text is superior to the treaties on which the claims are based. for all these reasons, i have voted against this agreement.

in writing. ‒ the agreement adopted with my vote in favour covers the transfer of all personal data, such as names, addresses or criminal records, exchanged between the european union and the united states of america for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of crime, including terrorism. i voted in favour of this because it is a step forward for transatlantic data protection. from now on, there will be higher standards of binding protection of fundamental rights and strong controls will be applied when data is exchanged between the police and judicial authorities. the agreement represents the start of a new way of negotiating transatlantic standards on the protection of fundamental rights which will replace the fragmented and uncertain standards seen so far. the agreement guarantees that citizens on both sides of the atlantic will have the right to be informed if data security has been breached, that the information is correct and can be corrected, and sets limits on data transfers and retention periods.
in writing. ‒ the framework agreement aims to ensure the protection of the fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals, in particular the protection of personal data when transmitted and processed for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences, including terrorism, in the framework of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters, between the competent authorities of the european union and the usa. however, there are serious doubts, including from the european data protection supervisor, about the compatibility of the framework agreement with the charter of fundamental rights of the union and with secondary union data protection law, in particular as regards the right to judicial redress, access by police and judicial authorities, the limitation of the data subject's access rights and data retention periods, among others. doubts requiring intervention by the court of justice of the european union. as the motions for resolutions by the gue/ngl and alde calling for the opinion of the court of justice on the compatibility of the framework agreement with the treaties of the union were rejected, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in the vote on this recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the union, of the agreement between the united states of america and the european union on the protection of personal data relating to the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences. our group has tabled an alternative resolution in which it considers that there is legal uncertainty as to the compatibility of the envisaged agreement with the treaties and asks that the court of justice be asked for an opinion on the compatibility of the agreement with the treaties. that is why i abstained in this vote.

in writing. ‒ i have supported the interim economic partnership agreement with ghana (ipa) because:- it improves the legal certainty of ghanaian trade with europe (avoiding a possible loss of the tariff exemptions currently granted to it temporarily and unilaterally by the union), it improves the regulation of our trade (contains provisions on trade in goods, customs, trade facilitation, technical barriers, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, while maintaining the free access exception for bananas destined for the outermost regions). - it incorporates binding commitments on sustainability and human rights, such as the fight against illegal timber trade, corruption and child labour. - the ghanaian government has requested this agreement after consulting the stakeholders and its parliament has strongly supported its ratification. - a possible increase in tariffs, in the absence of the aaei, would be very damaging for a country which directs more than 20% of its external trade to the union. - the socialists will ensure that ghana's commitments are properly monitored, while continuing to work towards a good regional epa with all of west africa and demanding that ghana make further democratic progress and dialogue with civil society.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this consent report on the interim economic partnership agreement between the eu and ghana, because it reinforces an asymmetric logic and a peripheral-centre subordination of trade relations, condemning ghana to underdevelopment in the long term.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this recommendation on the interim economic partnership agreement between ghana and the european community and its member states on the other hand. this interim agreement will open the way to its provisional application. due to the delay in the signature of the eu-west africa economic partnership agreement (epa) in 2016, ghana and côte d'ivoire decided to proceed with the ratification of their interim epa with the european union concluded in 2007. the agreement provides a contractual safety net as it guarantees duty-free access to the eu market until the regional agreement is concluded. the interim agreement will be replaced in due course by an epa at regional level once it enters into force.

in writing. ‒ the objective of this decision is to provide an additional eur 1 906.2 million for the items 'security and citizenship' and 'global europe', which will have to be offset by the funds dedicated to 'sustainable growth' and to a lesser extent 'governance'. i am opposed to the global orientation of funds dedicated to the migration and refugee crisis, the so-called 'fortress europe', which has turned europe's borders into open-air prisons and graves for thousands of migrants. i call for the right to asylum to be respected and for a genuine development and peace strategy to be put in place for the countries of origin of the migratory flows, which requires a specific increase in the european budget instead of the proposed patches. that is why i voted against.
in writing. - i vote against it. it amends the european budget by upgrading the levels of security and migration resources, which, being insufficient, make it necessary to mobilise other instruments, such as contingency funds, and by reducing expenditure, for example, on the european medicines agency (based in london). it advances provisions to continue the juncker plan; it reduces appropriations for the agriculture and territorial cohesion items; and it makes advances to finance frontex staff. in total, this means an increase of 225.4 million in credits and, more importantly, a decrease of 7 284.3 million in payments. it also leads to a reduction in the member states' contributions to the budget.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report. it is a mechanism which reduces solidarity in the distribution of contributions to the budget of the european union. the report develops 'reductions' in the contributions of member states considered to be over-contributing. this is an attack on the principle of solidarity and territorial redistribution which the union budget must have. the mechanism approves these reductions retroactively, with the result that the countries concerned, including the united kingdom, sweden, germany, austria, etc., will recover part of their contribution to the european budget in the years where the economic crisis has been the most severe. we need a european budget which promotes solidarity between countries and that is precisely why i voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ having examined all other financial possibilities to respond to unforeseen circumstances within the 2017 expenditure ceilings of heading 3 (security and citizenship) and 4 (global europe) set out in the multiannual financial framework, and having mobilised the flexibility instrument for the total amount of eur 530 million available in 2017, it is necessary to mobilise the contingency margin to address the needs arising from the migration, refugee and security crisis by increasing the commitment appropriations in the general budget of the union for the financial year 2017 above the ceilings of heading 3 and 4. the decision, which i voted for, therefore mobilises eur 1 906.2 million for headings 3 and 4. this amount is offset by eur 575 million of the unallocated margin of heading 2 (sustainable growth) in 2017 and eur 507,3 million in 2017, eur 70,0 million in 2018 and eur 253,9 million in 2019 of the unallocated margins of heading 5 (government).
in writing. - i voted against it. the budget proposed by parliament was already accepting cuts, only partially compensating for the positions of the commission and the council, and finally after the negotiations we have one of the most austere budgets we have known for a long time, after the intransigence of the council and the richest countries. the budget will be left with eur 157 857.8 million in payment appropriations (pa) and eur 134 490.4 million in payments, representing a real cut of more than 6.4% and a further 1.7% in appropriations. the budget is given more flexibility to give more room and resources to security and migration measures. the main victims will be agriculture, the administration of institutions and decentralized agencies. it basically involves reducing member states' contributions to an already tight budget, mobilising contingency and flexibility margins to be able to address additional expenditure for the handling of migration processes, strengthening the european fund for sustainable development (a kind of juncker plan for the containment of migration in the border countries) and the trust fund for turkey (refugees).

in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument to finance immediate budgetary measures to deal with the current migration, refugee and security crisis. the amount to be mobilised will be eur 530 million in commitment appropriations and, we reiterate our view that without prejudice to the possibility of mobilising payment appropriations for specific budget lines through the flexibility instrument without prior mobilisation of commitments, payments arising from commitments previously mobilised through the flexibility instrument can only be counted above the ceilings.
in writing. ‒ the flexibility instrument is intended to allow the financing of clearly identified expenditure which cannot be financed within the available ceilings under one or more headings. having examined all possibilities for reallocating appropriations within the expenditure ceiling of heading 3 (security and citizenship), it is necessary to mobilise the flexibility instrument to supplement the financing available in the general budget of the union for the financial year 2017 by an amount of eur 530 million in excess of the ceilings of heading 3 in order to cover measures in the area of migration, refugees and security. by this decision, which i voted in favour of, the payment appropriations corresponding to the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument are to be distributed over several budgetary years, estimated at eur 238,3 million in 2017, eur 91,0 million in 2018, eur 141,9 million in 2019 and eur 58,8 million in 2020.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument to finance immediate budgetary measures to deal with the current migration, refugee and security crisis. however, it should be noted that the resources made available for this purpose may not be sufficient given the challenges facing the union in this field, and we must be prepared in case additional funds are needed.

in writing. ‒ the eu solidarity fund provides financial assistance to member states and candidate countries that have suffered a major natural disaster (over eur 3 billion or 0.6% of gdp); aid that can also be received by regions. in the past, i have criticised the administrative difficulties in accessing the fund and the rigidity in its implementation, as they make it difficult for the available amounts to be spent, despite the increasing frequency of natural disasters. the purpose of this decision is to ensure that 50 million of the total fund is immediately available for any emergency. i consider this a positive step and have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ if we are to take the refugee crisis seriously, foster growth and tackle the still unacceptable levels of youth unemployment, we need a well-funded and flexible eu budget. the budget we passed today is a step in the right direction. we have managed to raise an additional 500 million euros for the youth employment initiative, a priority for our group. this will ensure that millions of young europeans have the opportunity to continue their studies, training or find their first job. we have also managed to increase funding for programmes that drive development and address the root causes of the refugee crisis: an additional €700 million has been agreed to increase aid to neighbouring and developing countries, and we have secured increased funding to support palestinian refugees. for all these reasons, the spanish socialist delegation to the european parliament has voted in favour of the union's 2017 budget.
in writing. - we voted against it. the budget proposed by parliament was already accepting cuts, only partially compensating for the positions of the commission and the council, and finally after the negotiations we have one of the most austere budgets we have known for a long time, after the intransigence of the council and the richest countries. the budget will be left with eur 157 857.8 million in payment appropriations (pa) and eur 134 490.4 million in payments, representing a real cut of more than 6.4% and a further 1.7% in appropriations. the budget is given more flexibility to give more room and resources to security and migration measures. the main victims will be agriculture, the administration of institutions and decentralized agencies. it basically involves reducing member states' contributions to an already tight budget, mobilising contingency and flexibility margins to be able to address additional expenditure for the handling of migration processes, strengthening the european fund for sustainable development (a kind of juncker plan for the containment of migration in the border countries) and the trust fund for turkey (refugees).
in writing. ‒ i have supported the agreement on the budgetary procedure for 2017, after going through the conciliation process with the council, by voting in favour. the documents adopted are: the list of budget lines not modified in relation to the draft budget or the council's position, the summary of the figures by heading in the financial framework, a consolidated document showing the figures and the final text of all the lines which have been modified in the conciliation procedure.
in writing. ‒ if we are to take the refugee crisis seriously, foster growth and tackle the still unacceptable levels of youth unemployment, we need a well-funded and flexible eu budget. the budget we passed today is a step in the right direction. we have managed to raise an additional 500 million euros for the youth employment initiative, a priority for our group. this will ensure that millions of young europeans have the opportunity to continue their studies, training or find their first job. we have also secured an additional €200 million for programmes to boost research and innovation, support small and medium-sized enterprises, help to promote cross-border infrastructure projects and to encourage support for students to study in different eu member states. in addition, we have managed to increase funding for programmes that drive development and address the root causes of the refugee crisis: an additional €700 million has been agreed to increase aid to neighbouring countries, and in developing countries, we have achieved increased funding to support palestinian refugees. for all these reasons, the spanish socialist delegation to the european parliament has voted in favour of the union's 2017 budget.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which addresses the situation in italy following the earthquakes in august 2016, which were followed by several aftershocks and a strong earthquake in october, the most intense in recent decades, which leveled entire towns and caused multiple damages. calls on the commission, given the exceptional nature and gravity of this situation, to consider excluding from the calculation of national deficits under the stability and growth pact investments related to sustainable reconstruction and earthquake prevention, and to take all necessary measures to promptly analyse requests for assistance from the european union solidarity fund (eusf) with a view to ensuring its rapid mobilisation;
in writing. ‒ this is a motion for a resolution adopted in the context of the debate on the eu solidarity fund (established to respond to major natural disasters and provide european solidarity to the disaster-stricken regions of europe) following the devastating earthquakes that struck central italy in august and october 2016, killing nearly 300 people and injuring more than 400, with a possible displacement of another 100 000. it is intended to answer the questions whether the commission has received an application from the italian government to receive funding from the fund and has taken all the necessary measures to assess the application and to mobilise this funding rapidly, and whether the commission will consider requests for amendments to the italian national and regional operational programmes, in order to better address the issues of thematic objective 5 (promoting adaptation to climate change and risk prevention and management), and will study the existing procedures for evaluating funding applications with a view to simplifying them and shortening the necessary deadlines. i voted in favour of the resolution finally adopted.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution, taking into account the devastating earthquakes that struck central italy in 2016, which, according to various reports, caused more than 400 injuries and 290 fatalities. similarly, the recent earthquakes have devastated villages, seriously damaged local and regional infrastructure, destroyed historical and cultural heritage and affected economic activities, especially those of smes, agriculture, natural landscapes and the potential of tourism and hospitality. the union must therefore be ready to help through the european solidarity fund, bearing in mind that it is very important that the national authorities can have these funds at their disposal as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because, following the appointment process of the college of commissioners in 2014 and subsequent news concerning several commissioners, it is clear that the european commission needs to review its code of conduct, to ensure that commissioners' declarations of interests accurately reflect their financial situation and that of their family members. the declaration of financial interests must include current and two previous years' activities and interests, the commissioners will have to declare all their interests as shareholders, members of boards of directors, advisers and consultants, members of foundations, as well as the interests of close family members. in the event of a conflict of interest identified during the term of office, the president of the commission shall follow parliament's recommendations to resolve it, or the house may withdraw confidence in that commissioner and, where appropriate, deprive him of his pension and other benefits. the resolution also envisages extending from 18 to 36 months the period within which commissioners, once out of office, must refrain from working for the private sector in the area for which they were responsible.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because its purpose is to control the declarations of financial interests of commissioners, to ensure that they can carry out their mandates in complete independence and to ensure the utmost transparency of the commission. any change in the financial interests of a commissioner during his or her term of office, or any reorganisation of the distribution of responsibilities among the members of the commission, constitutes a new situation as regards the possible existence of a conflict of interest. the commission is also asked to urgently review the 2011 code of conduct for commissioners, to take account of the recommendations made by parliament in its recent resolutions. we believe that it is essential for an institution like the commission to increase transparency and to ensure the independence of the commissioners. that is why we voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the adoption of this report is intended to help clarify the role of the committee on legal affairs (juri) in examining declarations of interests. the report also proposes to the commission a number of amendments to its code of conduct and declarations of interests, to ensure that the latter include sufficient information to assess the financial interests of commissioners. the rapporteur also proposes that, in the event of a conflict of interest identified on the basis of the statement or additional information provided by the commissioner during his term of office, the committee on legal affairs could make a recommendation to the president of the commission to withdraw confidence in the commissioner concerned. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the european parliament, the council and the commission.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, bearing in mind that it is important to have the utmost transparency in relation to possible conflicts of interest of members of the european commission. we cannot allow the highest representatives of the european commission to be influenced by private interests which may be contrary to the general interest of the citizens of the union, and so we must always be vigilant, and we must establish the maximum possible controls and transparency to avoid possible conflicts of interest.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because, following the appointment process of the college of commissioners in 2014 and subsequent news concerning several commissioners, it is clear that the european commission needs to review its code of conduct, to ensure that commissioners' declarations of interests accurately reflect their financial situation and that of their family members. the declaration of financial interests must include current and two previous years' activities and interests, the commissioners will have to declare all their interests as shareholders, members of boards of directors, advisers and consultants, members of foundations, as well as the interests of close family members. in the event of a conflict of interest identified during the term of office, the president of the commission shall follow parliament's recommendations to resolve it, or the house may withdraw confidence in that commissioner and, where appropriate, deprive him of his pension and other benefits. the resolution also envisages extending from 18 to 36 months the period within which commissioners, once out of office, must refrain from working for the private sector in the area for which they were responsible.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because its purpose is to control the declarations of financial interests of commissioners, to ensure that they can carry out their mandates in complete independence and to ensure the utmost transparency of the commission. any change in the financial interests of a commissioner during his or her term of office, or any reorganisation of the distribution of responsibilities among the members of the commission, constitutes a new situation as regards the possible existence of a conflict of interest. the commission is also asked to urgently review the 2011 code of conduct for commissioners, to take account of the recommendations made by parliament in its recent resolutions. we believe that it is essential for an institution like the commission to increase transparency and to ensure the independence of the commissioners. that is why we voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it calls for greater clarification of the family relations of commissioners, their property and their contracts and for the resolutions of the european ombudsman and the ad hoc ethics committee on employment authorisations for former commissioners to be respected. unfortunately, conflicts of interest are a constant feature of the career of european commissioners, a clear example of the personal collusion between their politicians and the interests of big transnational capital. kroes and uber, cañete and his family's properties, barroso and goldman sachs etc. highlight the structural links between the european high bureaucracy and corporate power.

in writing. ‒ after the recent scandals of former commission president barroso and other former and present commissioners regarding conflicts of interests and moving to the private sector after leaving the job, these guidelines for the declarations of interest of commissioners is very welcome and much needed. i note in particular that: the code of conduct for commissioners adopted on 20 april 2011 regarding impartiality, integrity, transparency, diligence, probity, responsibility and discretion presents improvements over the preceding code adopted in 2004 as regards the declaration of financial interests in that disclosure requirements are extended to commissioners’ partners and the declaration of interests has to be revised when information changes or, at the least, every year. the credibility of the declaration of financial interests depends on the accuracy of the form presented to the commissioner-designate; considers that the current scope of commissioners’ declarations of interests is too limited and their explanatory content ambiguous; calls, therefore, on the commission to revise the code of conduct as soon as possible in order to ensure that the declarations of interests provide the committee on legal affairs with accurate information with which it can substantiate its decision unequivocally. the credibility of the european commission depends on the strict applications and respect of these basic ethic rules and code of conduct.

in writing. ‒ the report calls on the commission to assess the desirability of introducing new harmonised rules on liability, compensation and financial security in order to avoid further accidents with cross-border repercussions and to consider the establishment of a legislative mechanism for compensation for maritime accidents. it also calls for compensatory schemes capable of dealing with crossborder claims efficiently and quickly and covering both primary and secondary damage caused in all affected areas. member states are encouraged to develop financial guarantee instruments, covering compensation for damage, traditional arising from incidents related to general offshore oil and gas activities or to the maritime transport of oil and gas, including in the event of insolvency. i voted in favour because i believe that strict rules on civil liability for such accidents should be established to facilitate access to justice for victims.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on liability, compensation and financial security in the field of offshore oil and gas operations. the adoption of the directives on the safety of offshore oil and gas operations is supported. the member states which have not yet transposed the directive are also asked to do so as soon as possible. in addition, it is considered that stricter rules on civil liability for accidents at sea should be established in order to facilitate access to justice for victims affected by such accidents.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on liability, compensation and financial security in offshore oil and gas operations, which clarifies the offshore safety directive as regards the types of damage that must be compensated, the liability regimes of each of the parties and the financial capacity to meet this compensation, if they are liable. the aim is to harmonise and update the member states' liability systems, ensuring the 'polluter pays' principle. this would prevent a possible accident in european waters from adversely affecting future oil and gas operations, both in a member state and in the union as a whole.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, bearing in mind those affected by disasters in offshore oil and gas operations, such as those caused by the castor platform off the coasts of the terres de l'ebre and north of castellón. the report lays the groundwork for those affected by disasters due to offshore oil and gas operations, whether from direct, indirect or collateral causes, to be able to claim liability and compensation in the future (until now, only if they were from direct causes, such as a black tide). if the european legislation had been harmonized as we demand from the european parliament at the time of the events, neighbours would now be able to claim compensation for the damage they have suffered.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to clarify the types of damage that must be compensated in offshore oil and gas operations, the liability regimes of the parties and their financial capacity to cope with such compensation if they are liable. the report focuses on the importance of harmonising and updating liability systems in the member states to ensure the application of the 'polluter pays' principle not only in the case of environmental damage but also in the case of personal injury, property damage or net economic loss. the report is relevant for spain because it specifically mentions the case of the castor platform, being applicable to offshore fracking operations. it is also applicable to cases such as the 'prestige' case, as it does not only deal with damage from fixed infrastructure, but also with possible accidents during the process of transporting and distributing gas or oil.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on liability, compensation and financial security in offshore oil and gas operations, which clarifies the dsb as regards the types of damage to be compensated, the liability regimes of each party and the financial capacity to meet this compensation, if they are liable. the aim is to harmonise and update the member states' liability systems, ensuring the 'polluter pays' principle. this would prevent a possible accident in european waters from adversely affecting future oil and gas operations, both in the member state and in the union as a whole.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to introduce new regulation to minimise the damage of a possible accident in offshore oil and gas operations: all the more so when the union is promoting their development without taking into account their risks and impact. i share the need to establish a compensation mechanism to protect potentially affected sectors such as fisheries and tourism, to facilitate victims' access to justice and to ensure, through specific contributions, that the offshore industry actually pays, and i ask the commission to act on parliament's request. for these reasons, i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the drc is in a serious political crisis caused by the intention of the current president kabila to remain in power, by running for a third term which the constitution expressly prohibits. in recent months, dozens of people have been killed in the violent repression of demonstrations organized by the opposition and pro-democracy groups. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the time has come for the union to react and take concrete measures to put pressure on those responsible for the violence and the political blockade - by means of nominal sanctions - and to try to promote a genuine political dialogue in the country, involving all the forces and preventing the situation from degenerating dangerously into open conflict. the political situation is unstable, but there is also a serious humanitarian situation, particularly in the east of the country. in this text we call on the union and its member states to redouble their efforts to help improve the living conditions of more than 1 500 000 internally displaced persons and hundreds of thousands of refugees from neighbouring countries such as the car, burundi and rwanda.
in writing. ‒ i have abstained on this resolution on the situation in the democratic republic of congo because, although i agree with certain elements of the resolution, such as your concern about the human rights situation and the increasing deterioration in the democratic republic of congo, i believe that the responsibility of the union in the crisis is not addressed. i also believe that the resolution is a significant step forward in the country's upcoming electoral process.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution on access to energy in developing countries because, although i consider access to sustainable energy to be essential for the realisation of various basic rights, i believe there is a clear orientation towards the private sector. i understand that the role that the private sector can play in a strategic sector such as energy must be very limited and regulated by the state and this is an element that we are missing in the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution on energy access in developing countries, which also calls for the inclusion of the gender dimension in all energy policies. it also called for the phasing out of fossil fuel subsidies and encouraged the use of these funds for effective social policies and actions to eradicate energy poverty in developing countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which guarantees access to modern, sustainable, affordable and reliable energy for all developing countries, thereby meeting human needs and, in addition, promoting human development and economic progress. the main objective of these energy access programmes in developing countries, governed by the development cooperation instrument (dci) and the european development fund (edf), should focus on access to energy and ensuring the same access for those poor people in remote regions, on the elimination of energy poverty and on the need to increase transparency and accountability. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement on the conclusion of the agreement on the european economic area.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the grounds that sustainable access to affordable, reliable and secure energy is fundamental to meeting basic human needs and rights. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 21 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the application of this regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution on access to energy in developing countries because, although i consider access to sustainable energy to be essential for the realisation of various basic rights, i believe there is a clear orientation towards the private sector. i understand that the role that the private sector can play in a strategic sector such as energy must be very limited and regulated by the state and this is an element that we are missing in the resolution.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which guarantees access to modern, sustainable, affordable and reliable energy for all developing countries, thereby meeting human needs and further promoting human development and economic progress. the main objective of these energy access programmes in developing countries, governed by the development cooperation instrument (dci) and the european development fund (edf), should focus on access to energy and ensuring the same access for those poor people in remote regions, on the elimination of energy poverty and on the need to increase transparency and accountability. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement on the conclusion of the agreement on the european economic area.
in writing. ‒ this resolution contains positive references and proposals such as the recognition of the need to take special account of the gender dimension in energy access, the importance of renewable energies and short-circuited production. but this promotion of eu development policies to tackle energy poverty in the impoverished countries, will be in vain, as long as the current trade and economic policies are upheld. in addition, an essential element in ensuring access to energy is overlooked: the central role of the state and governments in a strategic sector. access to energy is essential to meet basic needs and human rights, but this access will never be guaranteed by promoting the logic of the market and leaving it in private hands. i could not therefore vote in favour of this resolution, since it promotes the current european model of privatising the energy sector, in whole or in part, for developing countries, to leave access to energy in private hands by emphasising the importance of the private sector and market conditions in ensuring access to energy.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to assess the implementation of the european order for payment procedure. the purpose of the european order for payment procedure is to facilitate the recovery of sums in cross-border proceedings. the procedure allows creditors to easily obtain an order to recover uncontested civil and commercial claims. i voted in favour of this report because it calls on the member states to implement the european order for payment better and to raise awareness among citizens, businesses, legal professionals and all other interested parties about the availability, operation, application and benefits of this tool in crossborder cases.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work on this report on the implementation of the european monitoring process which i supported. we welcome the successful operation in the member states of this procedure applicable in civil and commercial matters relating to uncontested claims and whose main objective is to simplify and speed up the procedure for the recognition and enforcement of the rights of creditors of the union across borders.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report assessing the implementation of the european monitoring process. the european monitoring procedure was created in 2006 for the payment of debts not rejected by a debtor, thus simplifying, speeding up and reducing court costs in cases where more than one european country is involved, and allowing the free movement, recognition and application of monitoring processes in all member states. it applies to all civil and commercial matters where one of the parties lives in a european country other than the country in which the monitoring order is sought. the report gives a positive assessment of the european monitoring process, but stresses the need for improved harmonisation in terms of implementation, as well as the need to provide a more effective and more efficient monitoring system.
in writing. ‒ the european monitoring procedure is designed to facilitate the recovery of sums in crossborder proceedings. the procedure is optional, which means that it is available in crossborder cases as an alternative to the various equivalent national procedures. what is proposed in this report is that the commission should adopt new versions of some of the standard forms, in order to take account of the various changes that have taken place over the years and to improve the clarity of the sections on the payment of interest. as regards the regulation itself, it is considered that some of the restrictions on the scope of the procedure could be lifted in the light of the progress made by union family law. the report also highlights that additional efforts are needed in relation to requests for revision of european orders for payment.

member of the commission. – mr president, thank you very much for the debate. i have listened very carefully to what you have said, so allow me now to address a couple of your concerns and comments. first, the regulation does not impose a one-size-fits-all approach. we know that every port in europe is different. the regulation respects this, including the public or private ownership of ports. it is really important to know that this regulation applies only to the ports of european interest, which were identified as such in the trans-european network by the european parliament and the council in 2013. this refers to 329 ports out of 1200 ports in europe. this is a very important message that needs to be taken on board. the regulation also includes tailor-made provisions to avoid putting unnecessary burdens on the smaller ports in the trans-european network with a more local dimension. second, on the point of private ports which do not receive public funds, let me stress that they do not have to apply the rules on financial transparency, and this has to be very clear. i would greatly appreciate if you can pass this message on clearly. however, private ports as private undertakings should apply the same rules on the provision of port services, including ensuring adequate training. on the other hand, we see no good reason to allow a private undertaking to potentially abuse its dominant position vis-à-vis others on the mere grounds that it is private. so let me add to this two more comments on social aspects: firstly, the regulation will improve the training of the employees of the port service providers; secondly, it respects the tradition and ongoing social dialogue in each member state. it allows – but does not impose – the transfer of the rights of workers from one undertaking to the new one in case of change of contracts. the discussion shows that the agreement of the trilogue between council and the transport committee strikes the right balance. as regards state aid the process is ongoing. i can reassure you that the commission will do as much as it can within its remit to integrate the latest comments made by the parliament and the interested parties, notably in the final version of the general block exemption regulation. maritime ports are vital for the competitiveness of the union and sustainable multi-modal transport. so that is why the eu is providing a substantial part of its connecting europe facility budget to support infrastructure investments in ports belonging to our ten-t corridors – eur 760 million since 2014 – or in infrastructure connecting those ports, railways, for example. the port services regulation will ensure that investors are adequately consulted. the momentum is there to create a european framework which provides a level playing field and creates legal stability for investors, port workers and users. so at the end, let me just wrap up. the port services regulation creates a stable framework in which ports will be able to: first, develop; second, attract private investors; third, improve their public spending; fourth, improve the quality of port services; and finally, contribute to more efficient logistic chains and sustainable transport. commission statement on recital 45 of the proposal for a regulation establishing a framework on market access to port services and financial transparency of ports the commission considers that recital 45 should not have been included for the following reasons. first, the recital does not relate to any of the enacting terms of the regulation and hence does not comply with the principles of the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making. in that agreement, the european parliament, the council of the european union and the european commission confirmed that they remain fully committed to the interinstitutional agreement on common guidelines for the quality of drafting of community legislation, which provides that the purpose of recitals is to set out concise reasons for the chief provisions of the enacting terms, without reproducing or paraphrasing them, and that recitals should not contain normative provisions or political exhortations. second, the commission recalls that the notion of state aid within the meaning of article 107(1) tfeu is an objective one, enshrined in the treaty and not at the disposal of the union legislator. it can only be applied as such by the commission or national courts in specific cases, subject to the control of the union courts. third, the wording of the recital may create confusion. having regard to the treaty notion of state aid, it cannot be claimed that public funding of all access and defence infrastructure accessible to all users on equal and non-discriminatory terms always falls outside the scope of the state aid rules. the commission's decisional practice shows, for instance, that public funding of certain access infrastructure located within the area of a port may constitute state aid.
member of the commission. – mr president, on behalf of the commission and my colleague, karmenu vella, i would like to thank parliament for its role in reaching the successful and balanced conclusion of the deep—sea access file. the commission fully endorses the compromise found between the co—legislators. deep—sea fisheries account for only one percent of landings from the north—east atlantic, but i know that the economy of a number of fishing communities depends to a certain extent on these fisheries. the compromise therefore reflects both the need to protect the marine environment and the interest of the fishing industry in continuing deep—sea fishing. the agreed measures, such as fishing within the footprint and the 800m depth limit for bottom trawls, the observer scheme and the control measures will make deep—sea fishing more sustainable and more environment friendly. deep—sea fisheries have only been regulated since 2003. before this, the fisheries were largely unregulated and partly showed typical symptoms of the ‘race to fish’ problem, resulting in the depletion of stocks. ensuring sustainable fishing is increasingly important for society at large, but it is fundamental for the fishermen that depend on these fisheries. we all have an interest in ensuring sustainable fisheries, and with the deep—sea regulation we have taken an important step to ensure a sustainable framework for deep—sea habitats and fisheries. in this context, i would like to give you an example of the roundnose grenadier in the celtic sea and the english channel. this is the only stock for which we have full scientific advice. as a consequence, in november this year the commission proposed to the european council to set the fishing opportunities for this stock at maximum sustainable yield levels. in the new year, the commission will start preparing proposals for the next steps of the implementation of the regulation, establishing the footprint for deep—sea fishing and identifying vulnerable marine ecosystems to be closed for fisheries. i started by thanking you all for making this agreement possible because such important steps are only possible through common effort. let me, however, end by giving special thanks to mrs thomas, as rapporteur, and her team and the shadow rapporteurs for their outstanding work on this file.

on behalf of the alde group. mr president, i would like to thank all those involved in the implementation of this agreement for the effort made to adopt this regulation on deep-sea fishing, and especially the rapporteur, mrs thomas. this is a balanced regulation, which combines the clear need to protect a vulnerable ecosystem critical to life at sea with the rational exercise of trawling in european waters. all available scientific reports indicate that the deregulation that existed until 2002 led to overfishing, and that the regulation adopted at that time failed to end it. this agreement is the result of negotiations which started in 2012. after a laborious and complex process, we are approaching the most demanding international standards of protection. the regulation concerns the activities of our fleet in european waters. activities in international waters are also covered by the north-east atlantic fisheries commission. the prohibition of activity below 800 metres for the trawler fleet, together with measures such as the establishment of fishing zones, the obligation to carry out impact assessments or the total ban on certain vulnerable marine ecosystems, forms a framework whose main objective is to ensure the protection of the environment, the basic pillar for any sustainable fishing activity. control measures have also been strengthened by requiring all catches to be declared and by establishing an observer programme to ensure that data collection is consistent and accurate. we hope that we will definitely move from words, from good words, to deeds.

madam president, next saturday the protocol for the guarantee of linguistic rights will be presented in euskal herria, specifically in donostia. it is a protocol drawn up after an exemplary exercise in democracy and the participation of experts, and especially of social partners from all over europe. thanks to their contributions, the protocol contains 185 measures to guarantee the linguistic rights of all europeans, rights which are not guaranteed in the case of minority languages. this protocol is a concrete and comprehensive instrument, covering all aspects of society, to guarantee linguistic rights in practice, but also to consolidate peace and coexistence in europe, because respect for linguistic rights also means respect for human rights.
madam president, i have to ask you. this is my last minute in this parliament. a moment filled with concern for the present, which causes us indignation and so often tempts us to revolt, but also full of positive passion because today, two and a half years later, i know that the european dream is still possible. that is why i would like to put forward five strategies for europe which this parliament is well aware of and to a large extent shares. one, we need to get out of the self-imposed recession to return to sustained and sustainable growth. secondly, it is urgent to recover the eurozone as an economic, monetary, fiscal and social area. third, we must lead from europe the change in the production model that we need to tackle climate change. fourthly, let us complete the europe which takes full responsibility for the central issues which require it: the economy, security, defence, etc. but also to know how to give back the maximum capacity for decision, for real power, to the internal diversity of nations and peoples. let us build the political space that will make europe the driving force behind the new global balance between democratic power and economic power. let's move from extreme inequality to maximum equity; from the state-authority to the empowered society. (speaks in catalan)
madam president, a few weeks ago i met josé antonio cuesta in asturias, a citizen who had suffered from polio as a child and who had managed to overcome the disease and lead a full life, like many of the sick people who suffered from it all over europe a few years ago. however, recently new effects, new symptoms of this disease seem to be complicating the life of josé antonio cuesta and many citizens throughout europe: muscle aches, respiratory problems, great difficulties in living a full life as they had done up to now. the treatment they are receiving from the different national legislations is very different, with support and recognition of the disease in some countries and with distance and alienation in others, as in the case of my own, spain. i therefore want to be the voice of these hundreds of thousands of sick people, of these hundreds of thousands of people who have suffered from polio and who have managed to survive a very complicated disease and who need the support and backing of all europeans at this time.
madam president, i have to ask you. today i want to report a very serious event that will take place in spain next friday. for the first time in a supposedly democratic european state, a court of justice, instigated by the spanish government, will call for the president of the parliament of catalonia, the honourable mrs carme forcadell, to testify. it is being accused, contrary to all reason and legal sense, of having allowed the outcome of a study committee, a study committee, to be debated and voted on on the independence of catalonia. the extreme gravity of this attack on the sovereignty of our parliament in the exercise of its freedom of expression, this attack on the people of catalonia who elected this parliament, demands not only my denunciation and my rejection but also that of the european parliament, where freedom of expression is always respected. i have no doubt that this democratic outrage will be followed by others. if spain is abandoning the principles that make up the european union, we catalans should leave spain, not the european union, because we defend freedom and democracy.
madam president, we welcome and support the donostia protocol on the guarantee of linguistic rights. stateless nations like galicia need instruments to make our governments fulfill commitments and also international agreements to guarantee our language rights, which are also human rights. in our case, it is the galician government itself that attacks our language, when it passes decrees such as the one that reduces its presence in education and that expressly prohibits subjects such as mathematics, technology or physics and chemistry from being taught in galician. the new spanish state education law makes this situation even worse. both institutions are clearly in breach of, among other things, article 8 of the european charter of languages. we must act now to guarantee linguistic rights. we want our language to be recognised and to be able to express ourselves in it in this parliament too. we also need commitments to increase the budgets for language policies, as well as support for cultural production in our language, its promotion and distribution, which will ultimately ensure language policies that guarantee the recovery and normalisation of galician in all areas.
madam president, we are facing a great opportunity. the transition to clean energy is an environmental necessity and an opportunity for economic growth and job creation. we need a single energy market, a more integrated, more transparent market, capable of providing affordable prices and meeting our climate objectives. it also overcomes the isolation suffered by the iberian peninsula. we need to drive the transition towards a model that is based on renewable energy, that encourages self-consumption and that is unquestionably committed to improving energy efficiency. and as socialists, but also as people, we demand definitive action against energy poverty. fifty million europeans and five million spaniards are waiting for a response to the challenge. the citizens, commissioners, must be the centre and the reason for the new energy policy of the european union.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used effectively. it is good that you have come to this house to discuss this winter package, because you talk about putting citizens at the centre of energy but what you are putting at the centre are fossil fuels. we know them by their deeds and not by their pretty words. it would be good if you explained why you are proposing contradictory measures in this package. the capacity mechanisms, first of all. covert subsidies to fossil fuels. it is estimated that 95% of the coal plants in the union will receive money; they will receive millions for continuing to pollute until 2026. secondly, a clearly insufficient energy efficiency and saving target. we should reach the binding 40% and without legal loopholes, facilitating public investment to reduce consumption and eradicate energy poverty. insufficient targets to meet the paris agreement and contradictory measures: this is what we see in this package designed to continue to hold back the democratisation of the sector and to maintain the power of the fossil fuel lobbies.
in writing. the transition to clean energy is an environmental necessity and an opportunity for economic growth and job creation. we need a single energy market that is more integrated, more transparent, that meets our climate objectives and is able to provide energy at affordable prices. we must move towards a model that is based on renewable energy and that is committed to improving energy efficiency. we socialists also demand definitive action against energy poverty. fifty million europeans and five million spaniards are waiting for a response to their needs. in addition to reducing co2 emissions by at least 40% by 2030, we are committed to a binding target of at least 30% renewable energy, as well as energy efficiency, thus reducing our dependence on energy imports. the union is well placed to turn this transition into an opportunity and generate up to 1% of gdp growth and 900 000 new jobs over the next decade. in addition, european consumers will need to have a wider supply, price comparison tools and the ability to produce and sell their own energy.
in writing. renewable energy production cannot be in contradiction with other activities that are fundamental to the life of the people, such as food production. in this context, it is necessary to demand the preservation and priority of the use of agricultural land for food production. in galicia we run the risk with the law of fiscal and administrative measures, annexed to the draft budgets for 2017 (which opens the doors to the creation of mega biomass plants) of increasing the pressure for the production of energy crops, including the afforestation of agricultural land; ending up becoming a real green desert and mortgaging the future of our small and medium-sized agricultural holdings, the rural environment and our sovereignty and food security for generations. we urge the commission to avoid such situations and to put in place effective measures to preserve the use of land for food production.
mr president, i believe that there can be no strong parliament without an efficient rules of procedure. i think this is an efficient regulation. i would like to thank the rapporteurs, especially mr wieland and mr corbett, who have done an extraordinary job, two words which are important in this matter: what transparency and exemplarity mean. transparency, because i think we need to be much more transparent than we are. that is why our group will support many of the amendments which we have to make in order to improve transparency and to inform the public. i am against an amendment which introduces the possibility that members may also defend lobbies. it is not possible to defend all citizens and lobbyists. we defend citizens, not special interests. i am also in favour of a reform of the statute which would make it possible to establish the criterion that our activity is exclusive. we can't work here and somewhere else. i think that change has to be made too.
vice-president of the commission, in writing. – the commission takes note of the fact that the european parliament has adopted today a revision of its rules of procedure which includes some changes concerning the relations with the commission. pursuant to point 21 of the framework agreement between the european parliament and the commission, the european parliament has taken the commitment to seek the opinion of the commission when it comes forward with such changes to its rules of procedure. by letter from president schulz of 9 december 2016, the european parliament transmitted for the commission's opinion, where relevant, the envisaged amendments to its rules of procedure brought forward for consideration of the plenary on 13 december 2016. the commission regrets that parliament did not respect its commitment for consulting the commission in a meaningful way, as the time left before the vote by the european parliament has not allowed the commission to provide a considered response or even discuss the matter in the college, and the parliament to take a commission opinion duly into account before voting on the proposed changes. the commission regrets that the parliament did not act in accordance with the principle of loyal and sincere cooperation and, despite its request, did not allow the commission enough time to express its opinion before adopting the revision. the commission wishes to highlight some of parliament's changes to its rules of procedure, in particular those relating to the proposed hearings in case of the appointment of a new commissioner during the commission's mandate or modifications in the portfolio of serving commissioners, as well as those relating to a possible conflict of interest of a commissioner. it must be borne in mind that those changes, if introduced unilaterally by the european parliament in its rules of procedure, cannot create a role for the european parliament which is neither provided for in the treaties nor in the framework agreement and which would affect the institutional position and functioning of the commission. the commission underlines in this regard that it will apply the treaties and continue to respect the terms of the framework agreement. the commission expects that the parliament will do the same.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation for the second reading as it ensures, to the greatest extent possible, the sustainable exploitation of deep-sea stocks, while reducing the environmental impact of these fisheries. the agreement reached maintains the ban on trawling beyond 800 metres only for community waters, an important aspect to ensure equal opportunities for community fishermen in external waters. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the north sea, including the north sea, and to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the north sea. deep-sea fisheries in the north-east atlantic are dominated partly by traditional coastal fleets (portugal) and partly by large itinerant trawlers (france, spain). although they account for approximately 1% of landings from the north-east atlantic, the economic viability of certain fishing communities depends to some extent on these fisheries.
in writing. i am voting against the amendment rejecting the council's position at first reading because i think it is a good thing that the deep-sea fishing trail is frozen and that specific sanctions are provided for vessels that do not comply with the rules. the negotiating teams of the parliament and the council reached an agreement on the commission proposal on 30 june 2016 establishing a depth limit of 800 metres for trawling, which is intended to ensure the protection of vulnerable marine ecosystems. the obligation on vessels to leave fishing areas deeper than 400 metres when in vulnerable ecosystems is also good news. the new transparency rules on deep-sea fishing and its impact, and the introduction of scientific observers on board 20% of vessels, should also help to move in this direction. for this reason i do not support the amendment which sought to reject the council's position at first reading.
in writing. ‒ deep-sea fishing is a major problem for the sustainability of our seas. i am in full support of this recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i see the recommendation as positive, whether it is for increasing levels of transparency, such as the control of high impact fisheries, or ensuring the depth limit is above 800 metres, except for vulnerable marine ecosystems, where a limit of 400 metres should be placed.
in writing. ‒ the general objective of this proposal for a regulation is to ensure the sustainable exploitation of deep-sea stocks, reduce the environmental impact of these fisheries and improve the information base for scientific evaluations. it is the result of intensive negotiation with the council, which came from the previous legislature. the european union will freeze the 'huella pesquera' in the area in accordance with a general bathymetric limit set at 800 metres, which is satisfactory for the industry and which, in turn, ensures the protection of vulnerable marine ecosystems. in addition, stricter transparency rules are introduced, a fair system of sanctions for non-compliance is introduced and scientific observers are ensured on 20% of vessels. in short, it is a good regulation for the sustainability of deep-sea fishing in the north-east atlantic, which is why i voted in favour of its adoption.

in writing. ‒ parliament hereby approves the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions for fishing in international waters of the north-east atlantic, and repealing council regulation (ec) no 2347/2002. this proposal, which was adopted by a very large majority in the committee on fisheries, has made a number of important concessions, such as the adoption of new and more stringent transparency rules, for example by recording all catches, the setting of a 800-metre limit to protect the most vulnerable ecosystems on the seabed, or the introduction of sanctions for vessels that infringe these rules, with no one being left unpunished in the case of several control rules. these are just some of the new measures which i believe will make a significant contribution to the objective of sustainable fisheries.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it is a clear effort to improve long-term sustainability of fishing. it is an acceptable compromise because:- the european union is going to freeze its fishing footprint by specifying the area in which deep-sea fishing will be allowed. that area includes the area in which targeted fishing took place between 2009 and 2011 in eu waters in the north-east atlantic. this geographical boundary will apply to vessels targeting deep-sea species, i.e. those whose deep-sea species catch makes up more than 8% of the total on at least one fishing trip during the year. - parliament has secured specific penalties for vessels breaching the regulation on deep-sea fishing and a stipulation that no exemptions will be granted to certain rules. - the parliament and council negotiators have agreed on a depth limit of 800 metres. this new measure is intended to protect vulnerable deep-sea marine ecosystems more effectively. - in an effort to ensure that scientific data is collected, 20% of vessels will be required to have a scientific observer on board.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i see the recommendation as positive, whether it is for increasing levels of transparency, such as the control of high impact fisheries, or ensuring the depth limit is above 800 metres, except for vulnerable marine ecosystems, where a limit of 400 metres should be placed.

mr president, i voted against these changes to our rules of procedure because, if we already had limited powers, we are now going to reduce our decisionmaking power, limiting the number of questions we can put to the commission, limiting the possibility of amending texts with which we disagree and limiting parliament's position vis-à-vis the council in the negotiations. at the same time, this is the reform of the grand coalition. a reform so that only the issues that interest the major political groups - the european people's party and the social democrats - are dealt with, and in the way that they are dealt with, which means blocking the work of the groups that are against austerity, against the loss of labour rights and against refugee policies. today is a dark day for democracy in the union and bad news for the citizens. it is their concept of democracy and respect for minorities that is clear today.
mr president, i said 'no' because the corbett report is an attack on pluralism, transparency and democracy which alienates this parliament from the european people. the big groups have agreed to censor the voices of critics, limiting our right to amendments, questions and parliamentary participation. to avoid leaving a mark, they also reduce the debate and the transparency of the votes. the new rules of procedure formalize what many of us have been denouncing for some time: that this parliament is nothing more than a theatre where agreements between the socialists and the right are represented before a muzzled public that watches in astonishment the destruction of its social rights and freedoms in the name of the market. the european union will not survive this democratic revolution if it continues in this way.
in writing. ‒ i believe that there can be no strong parliament without an efficient rules of procedure. i therefore voted in favour of this revision of the regulation which aims to improve its functioning, increase transparency and adapt its content to the 2016 interinstitutional agreement on better law-making. i welcome the fact that the reform adopted includes proposals to improve efficiency in practical matters such as question time, voting on legislative acts and roll-call votes, and to integrate the gender perspective and include topical debates in each part-session at the proposal of the political groups. the new regulation also introduces improvements in the area of transparency by introducing the legislative footprint in reports, limiting meetings to interest groups registered in the transparency register and prohibiting the pursuit of paid advocacy activities directly related to the union decision-making process. however, i regret that other reforms which sought to publish online meetings with interest groups or to ban members from holding paid jobs during their term of office have been rejected by the conservative majority in the european parliament.
in writing. i voted against this revision of parliament's rules of procedure because it will reduce the ability of small groups to influence parliamentary work, leaving this house at the service of the people's party and the socialists, who see their capacity to define working hours and speed up legislation of their interest strengthened, by blocking amendments and debates they consider hostile. and so will other forms of initiative, such as questions and statements, that small groups have been using to influence the political agenda beyond the agreements between the majority groups.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the general revision of the rules of procedure of the european parliament, as i consider it to be a very important text which means a greater centralisation of power in the hands of the large political groups to the detriment of the small ones. the afco working party on the regulation spent more than two years reviewing the regulation. the mandate of the working group was to 'identify possible inconsistencies, redundancies, overlaps and, where possible, simplify the rules'. many of the changes proposed by the working party were technical (simplification of the text, incorporation of interpretations, adaptation of the legal basis, grouping of provisions into new chapters, etc.). these changes are positive as they improve the legibility of the regulation. however, a number of substantial proposals could make it more difficult for smaller groups to express themselves, particularly at plenary level, while larger groups will have more scope to act both in the committee and in the plenary. in general, this means greater centralisation of power in parliament for the benefit of the larger groups.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the general revision of the rules of procedure of the european parliament. after much negotiation we voted today on a text which seeks to simplify some of the rules, but i also voted in favour of the amendments which called for transparency in the listing of the groups with which we meet during our parliamentary work.

in writing. ‒ i believe that there can be no strong parliament without an efficient rules of procedure. i therefore voted in favour of this revision of the regulation which aims to improve its functioning, increase transparency and adapt its content to the 2016 interinstitutional agreement on better law-making. i welcome the fact that the reform adopted includes proposals to improve efficiency in practical matters such as question time, voting on legislative acts and roll-call votes, and to integrate the gender perspective and include topical debates in each part-session at the proposal of the political groups. the new regulation also introduces improvements in the area of transparency by introducing the legislative footprint in reports, limiting meetings to interest groups registered in the transparency register and prohibiting the pursuit of paid advocacy activities directly related to the union decision-making process. however, i regret that other reforms which sought to publish online meetings with interest groups or to ban members from holding paid jobs during their term of office have been rejected by the conservative majority in the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ as has happened regularly, parliament revises and reforms its rules of procedure with the aim of improving them and adapting them to the new powers that are being conferred on it. the commission has also received comments from the three sampled union producers, which were not included in the questionnaire replies. the new rules of procedure include amendments to the agreements at first reading, under which approval by an absolute majority in committees of the opening of negotiations with other institutions must be announced in plenary, which will vote on it if one tenth of parliament's members are opposed. the commission has also proposed that the council should be able to adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling of foodstuffs for human consumption. i am voting in favour of these measures because they will increase transparency and the functioning of parliament. and there is no doubt that such an objective contributes to a stronger and better european union.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has its own rules of procedure. the reform was aimed at updating the internal rules, with two main objectives: improving the operation and transparency of the system and clarifying certain rules. these changes have been the result of extensive technical work and negotiations which have lasted almost two years. the aim has been to reduce the obstacles and simplify the internal decision-making processes, and to adapt the legislation to the new interinstitutional agreement on better lawmaking which aims to give, and we shall see if it does, more weight to parliament. finally, among the new measures is the new debate on topics of particular relevance and urgency in the union, which will allow parliament to assess what is urgent. we are slow. i am ashamed of our impotence in the face of the political and humanitarian crisis, and this regulation is not a miracle cure, but it is a little better.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this revision of parliament's rules of procedure because it will reduce the ability of small groups to influence parliamentary work, leaving this house at the service of the popular and socialists, who see their capacity to define working hours and speed up legislation of their interest strengthened, blocking amendments and debates they consider hostile. and so will other forms of initiative, such as questions and statements, that small groups have been using to influence the political agenda beyond the agreements between the majority groups.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it undermines the rights and activity of directly elected representatives of the people. this report does not improve but decreases transparency of the work of this house. the conference of presidents will continue to be the decisive non-transparent place for all important decisions in this house. it decides the agenda and topics to be discussed. members should not be limited in the parliamentary questions, which are an essential element to raise issues important to their constituency. the actual system is over-bureaucratic and the parliamentary questions are filtered by non-elected bureaucrats. i am in favour of the publication of the minutes of the trilogues and conference of presidents minutes; all citizens should have access to it.
