mr president, i was very hesitant about whether to support or abstain from the report. i was eventually delayed, so i'm taking this opportunity to explain why i made that decision. i personally consider the human rights agenda to be an extremely important agenda and whole sections of the report are in the spirit of how i would agree with them. it's about protecting human rights in the world, fighting the death penalty, and so on. on the other hand, there are certain passages in the report that ultimately led me to delay. these are passages that deal with human rights within the european union. in short, i think that in some cases the report is too intrusive in relation to the sovereignty of individual member states. i simply disagree with some of the points, such as the european commission's call for a uniform regulation on paternity, parental and maternity leave. i think these are things that individual states should be able to regulate themselves. and so i would find other things where we should respect the sovereignty of individual member states and not interfere in their legal environment.
mr president, first of all i would like to welcome the rapporteur's work on this report, which contains many of the amendments tabled by my group on such important issues as migration and asylum or the mass spying on citizens. but it is also true that we lack more decisiveness in some areas, or, for example, references to the impact of austerity measures. i would now like to focus on a specific aspect of the human rights situation in the union, namely in a member state. the spanish state. the report calls for all the fundamental rights of prisoners to be guaranteed. however, the spanish state falls far short of european standards, due, among other things, to its failure to comply with union law. framework decision 2008/675 requires the recognition of sentences served in other member states. a regulation which the spanish government took more than six years to transpose, and whose transposition it tried to conceal from the european commission for a year and a half. the aim was to buy time and to continue to consolidate in the spanish courts a situation which was contrary to european law and human rights. if the european standard were to be met, seven basque prisoners should be released immediately, as stated in the report drawn up by seven meps from three different groups in april this year. article 6 of the charter of fundamental rights includes the right to liberty. it is time for the union to activate all its mechanisms to guarantee this and other fundamental rights and not to have the strasbourg court come afterwards, as always, to chide the member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i think it gives a good picture of the serious deterioration of fundamental rights, both individual and social (although the rapporteur tried to censor references to the latter before voting in plenary). i believe, however, that a good diagnosis is not enough: the union must reverse its migration, economic and social policies if it is to put a stop to this difficult situation.
in writing. ‒ this report, which is produced annually, aims to present the situation of fundamental rights in the european union and to make recommendations. the committee on civil liberties has made important changes, such as eliminating the most problematic aspects and including many of our group's amendments, such as those on migration and asylum, the protection of whistleblowers, the evaluation of anti-terrorism measures, the condemnation of indiscriminate mass surveillance, etc. importantly, the report mentions aspects related to corruption, racism and xenophobia, gender equality and violence against women, roma rights, lgbt rights, as well as the rights of children, other minorities, people with disabilities, the elderly and digital rights. however, as a rapporteur for the epp, we have failed to get any reference to how economic policy, especially austerity measures, have affected the fundamental rights of european citizens. that is why we have made a new attempt by introducing amendments in this plenary session. since most of them were rejected, i have voted to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report, which is based on the need for the union to promote the values of dignity and equality, which are its foundation, and which do not allow any form of discrimination against any of its citizens. this report covers 40 commitments addressing key fundamental rights issues including rule of law, women's rights and violence against women, children's rights, migration, social integration and inclusion, human trafficking, xenophobia, freedom and security, the rights of persons with disabilities, lgbtqi rights, hate crimes, roma rights and digital rights, among others.

in writing. ‒ the union has a strong commitment to respect and promote fundamental rights. respect for these is one of the conditions for accession to the union. in addition, the union's external action must be based on the promotion of dignity and other fundamental rights. this report addresses a number of current issues relating to fundamental rights within the union. for example, it focuses on refugees with special needs and children, and includes a range of measures aimed at protecting children from trafficking and other forms of abuse. the report does not ignore the recent increase in hate speech, which the union should set an example for the rest of the world by combating in a real and effective way. i am voting in favour of the text because it will undoubtedly help to protect the rights of the most deprived.
in writing. ‒ i support the report by which the european parliament will call for the suppression of incitement to hatred against migrants and refugees. the countries of the union must refrain from inciting fear and hatred among their citizens against migrants and asylum seekers for political gain. the report perfectly summarises the main fundamental rights concerns in the union in 2015, focusing on migration, child protection and the internet, as well as the right to free movement and access to abortion in case of life-threatening conditions.
in writing. ‒ eu countries must refrain from inciting fear and hatred among their citizens against migrants and asylum seekers in order to gain and maintain power. it is horrible to strip human beings of all dignity, with toxic behaviors that recall the darkest historical times. humiliation is increasing at an alarming rate in some institutions, political parties and media, fueling the fires of fanaticism and extremism. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. when they have allowed the solidarity between equals to be diluted, turning their backs on a human drama that has cost thousands of lives, and which history will eventually judge harshly. human beings, children and adults, women and men, deserve our firm rejection of violent extremism. and this is fought with education and culture.

in writing. ‒ in this text, the european parliament gives its assessment of the council's work on the situation of fundamental rights in the union in 2015. the document contains a number of references to the protection of fundamental rights, ranging from recommendations in the rule of law framework to provisions on migration, integration and social inclusion; freedom and security; trafficking in human beings; discrimination and xenophobia; hate crime and hate incitement; violence against women; the rights of children, the disabled, the elderly; minorities or rights in the digital environment. particularly relevant is the need to promote the charter and to take action to promote awareness of it at national level. this year's text focuses on the analysis of hate crime, reiterating zero tolerance for the kind of language that fosters it and reiterating the need for national legislation to address this issue. the committee also calls for the commission to be given the power to adopt legislative acts to ensure that the rights of the child are respected. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains many positive points, it is a proposal which guarantees the participation of the major economic players. the development of cultural and creative industries depends on authors receiving a fair remuneration for their work, but without this implying any form of blocking the development of the industry and its services to citizens. the report contains positive references to the inclusion of creators' rights, but also ensures the concentration of intellectual property rights through their financialization. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this is a joint report by the itre and cult committees on the challenges and opportunities facing the creative and cultural industries in the union. among other issues, it highlights the need for active promotion policies, access to funding, the fight against piracy, better participation of authors and creators in the sharing of benefits, promoting intersectoral cooperation and mobility, improving the working conditions of workers in the sector and the gender gap, etc. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that these aspects are necessary to lay the foundations for a specific policy to make the sector more valuable and to enable it to grow in a sustainable way in all the member states.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report on a coherent union policy for the cultural and creative sectors. it is essential to ask the commission to propose effective measures to combat online piracy, in particular to ensure that online content services implement effective means to remove unlicensed content from their services and, once removed, act to prevent the reappearance of such content. in addition, we call for the promotion of 'protocols on intellectual property assets' which facilitate the valuation of intellectual property rights, and we invite the commission and the member states to adopt the necessary mechanisms to increase the financial attractiveness of intellectual property rights and the recognition of their full value as assets.
in writing. ‒ the cultural and creative industries are not just another industry. they are of crucial economic importance, generating more than 12 million jobs and more than 5% of the union's gdp. but their value goes beyond mere numbers: they are not only the basis of our cultural heritage but also our identity card to the world. in view of the paradigm shift brought about by digitalisation, it is necessary to provide them with the necessary tools for their development. as we have said in the report, for which i was a socialist rapporteur in the itre committee, it is urgent to strengthen its financial capacity, by improving its perception as an attractive sector for investment, but also by enabling public funds, which have been greatly reduced in these years of crisis. it is urgent to fight against counterfeiting and piracy and to ensure fair remuneration by stopping the transfer of value between creators and other actors in the value chain. and of course, it is urgent to ensure the highest social and labour standards for its workers. digitalisation cannot become synonymous with precariousness, but with development, opportunities and inclusion.

in writing. ‒ this parliament resolution calls for the establishment of a policy to support the cultural and creative industries at eu level. in fact, the cultural and creative sectors are important in the different member states of the union and form an undeniable heritage that must be kept alive in order to avoid the musealisation or even the disappearance of certain artistic professions in particular. these sectors are also powerful vectors of our culture and thus of our identity and values. it is therefore appropriate that each people should be able to express itself in accordance with its own traditions. innovations, especially in the digital field, have also brought new talents to light, particularly in france, a country that is particularly prominent in video games and animated films. this report suggests positive ways of working. however, the development of a coherent policy of the union would therefore be very risky, since it would tend towards a homogenization of productions and creations. this policy would necessarily be subject to the eu's ideology: immigrationist, globalist, even blaming our traditions. cultural diplomacy, a powerful tool for influencing people, is too important to transfer this competence to the union, so i abstained on this parliament resolution.

in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution calls on the european commission to develop a coherent, comprehensive and long-term framework for the cultural and creative sectors and to provide adequate funding for this industry, with the aim of increasing its competitiveness to enable it to reach its full potential in creating quality jobs and supporting economic growth. to achieve this ambitious goal, the report proposes to adopt a harmonised definition of the concept of cultural and creative industries based on data. the commission is also asked to establish a sound legal framework on copyright which will take account of the specific features of this sector. it also recommends that the commission cooperate with other sectors to improve the interaction between smes and universities, so that the educational branches of creation and entrepreneurship are better integrated. in particular, it calls on both the member states and the commission to open up the range of financial instruments available to small enterprises by supporting public/private consortia. i am aware of the need to promote this sector at european level and have therefore voted in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for her work on this report on women's rights in the eastern partnership countries. i am in favour of the introduction of compulsory quotas on the lists of candidates. the eastern partnership countries are also encouraged to ratify the istanbul convention on preventing and combating violence against women as soon as possible, as none of the countries concerned has ratified it, and the authorities are asked to put in place national strategies to combat violence against women and to monitor closely their effective implementation.
in writing. ‒ this report deals with the situation of women's rights in armenia, azerbaijan, georgia, moldova, ukraine and belarus, all of which are eastern partnership states. in these countries, de facto inequality exists and persists, even though equality between men and women is guaranteed. economic changes in recent years have negatively affected the situation of women, and these states are therefore urged to improve the situation of women's rights, to take measures to increase equality between men and women and to combat domestic and gender-based violence, including sexual harassment and trafficking in human beings. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this report, which looks at the situation of women's rights in the six eastern partnership countries of the union, recognises that despite women's rights being formally recognised by all constitutions of these states and gender equality being considered a strategic priority in the european neighbourhood policy, women continue to suffer discrimination and high rates of gender-based violence. it expressed concern at their low public representation and called for concrete steps to overcome the barriers women face on a daily basis, such as the wage and pension gap, which is as high as 50% in some sectors. despite her positive formulations, the rapporteur on the right does not go far enough when it comes to the recognition of women's sexual and reproductive rights. the text also falls within the framework of the european neighbourhood policy and its financial instruments, which interfere in the internal affairs of third countries and promote regime change, which i reject. for these reasons, despite your good intentions, i abstained in the final vote.

member of the commission. – further regulation will ensure greater transparency for the use of public funds in ports. many receive considerable financial support from both national and european union budgets. transparency will contribute to a genuine level playing field between european ports. it will also help make public funding more efficient. the court of auditors stressed the necessity to address this issue in a recent report. second, the regulation creates a common framework for the provision of port services. this framework brings legal stability for the tendering of port services. it will end today’s unclear situation where ports policy is not decided by eu legislation, but rather by judgment of the european court of justice on a case by case basis. third, it will ensure better training of port workers in line with the work undertaken by the social partners. finally, the regulation will contribute to our decarbonisation strategy. we need to green the shipping industry and promote short-sea shipping. this requires investment and the right type of investment in ports. many of you attach great importance to clear and simple state aid rules. the commission shares its attachment. we have been working a lot on the issue of state aid in ports over the last months. my colleague commissioner vestager and i are making sure that the views of european ports are adequately taken into account. replying last week to a preliminary question from mr fleckenstein, the commission clarified the framework for state aid in ports, including the general block exemption regulation. the situation is as follows: a new set of infrastructure analytical grids was published on 2 december. with this document, the commission explains which infrastructures are considered to be non-economic and therefore should not fall under state aid rules. these infrastructures include defence infrastructure, such as docks, and access infrastructure to ports, such as a river flowing through a port that can be used by anyone. last week, the commission also completed its second public consultation on the general block exemption regulation. its objective is to identify which public investments in port infrastructure are considered state aid but are unproblematic and therefore do not need to be notified. we are now analysing the replies to improve the text further and adopt the regulation in 2017. the result of the analytical grids and the revised general block exemption regulation will be more legal certainty and more clarity, but there will be no change in the decision-making practice of the commission. with this work, we are doing exactly what you have been calling for under recital 45 of the port services regulation. however, for institutional reasons and to recall the better law—making principles agreed between the commission and the co—legislators, we will record a statement from the commission to be inserted regarding this recital. the text is balanced. it is the result of three years of discussions with all stakeholders. all major organisations representing the european port sector stand behind it – the trade unions, port authorities, port terminal operators and port services providers. it received strong support in the transport committee and was accepted unanimously by member states. it is now time to conclude the legislative procedure at first reading. all the circumstances allow it. (loud applause and cheers from certain quarters)
member of the commission, in writing. – commission statement on recital 45 of the compromise agreement reached by the co-legislators on the proposal for a regulation establishing a framework on market access to port services and financial transparency of ports the commission considers that recital 45 should not have been included for the following reasons. first, the recital does not relate to any of the enacting terms of the regulation and hence does not comply with the principles of the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making. in that agreement, the european parliament, the council of the european union and the european commission confirmed that they remain fully committed to the interinstitutional agreement on common guidelines for the quality of drafting of community legislation, which provides that the purpose of recitals is to set out concise reasons for the chief provisions of the enacting terms, without reproducing or paraphrasing them, and that recitals should not contain normative provisions or political exhortations. second, the commission recalls that the notion of state aid within the meaning of article 107(1) tfeu is an objective one, enshrined in the treaty and not at the disposal of the union legislator. it can only be applied as such by the commission or national courts in specific cases, subject to the control of the union courts. third, the wording of the recital may create confusion. having regard to the treaty notion of state aid, it cannot be claimed that public funding of all access and defence infrastructure accessible to all users on equal and non-discriminatory terms always falls outside the scope of the state aid rules. the commission’s decisional practice shows, for instance, that public funding of certain access infrastructure located within the area of a port may constitute state aid.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it is a technical transposition of an amendment to the annex to the regulation concerned. a legislative amendment to the polish insolvency law entails a change in the abovementioned annexes and with that change the extent of the derogations which the united kingdom and ireland have with regard to that regulation should be specified. i have decided to vote in favour of this report because of the strictly technical nature of its contents.
in writing. ‒ in december 2015, poland notified to the commission a substantial reform of its national restructuring legislation, which would enter into force on 1 january 2016, and requested an amendment to the lists in annexes a and b to the regulation. according to article 1 (1), article 2 (4) and recital 9 of the regulation, national proceedings can only be considered 'insolvency proceedings' in the context of the regulation if they are listed in annex a to the regulation. the annexes to the regulation may be amended only by a regulation adopted in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure of the legal basis on which the original regulation was adopted. the commission examined whether the request of poland fulfilled the requirements of the regulation and made a proposal to the european parliament and the council to ensure that the scope of the re-established regulation was adapted to the legal framework of the polish insolvency law in force at the time of its application. in this context, the commission's proposal is purely technical. it does not contain any substantive amendment to the regulation. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on insolvency proceedings and receivers. we agree with the aim of the agreement and its content, but we believe that the three technical amendments, which reflect the position of the united kingdom and ireland on the commission's proposal in accordance with protocol no 21 on the area of freedom, security and justice of these two member states, should be adopted.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report amending the regulation on insolvency proceedings and receiverships. the annexes to this regulation contain procedures which are important and necessary to ensure that the rules are properly applied. the amendment is due to the reform of the insolvency law of poland and the request of poland to amend the lists set out in the annexes, which stipulate that national proceedings may only be considered 'insolvency proceedings' if they are listed in annex a, and that these annexes may only be amended by the ordinary legislative procedure. the commission examined whether the request from poland met the regulatory requirements and sent a technical proposal to the council and parliament without substantial changes to the regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a technical transposition of an amendment to the annex to the regulation concerned. a legislative amendment to the polish insolvency act entails a change in those annexes and with that change the extent of the derogations granted to the united kingdom and ireland from that regulation should be specified. i have decided to vote in favour of this report because of the strictly technical nature of its contents.
in writing. ‒ a minor technical amendment to annexes a and b to regulation (eu) 2015/848 on insolvency proceedings is proposed. the annexes to the regulation may be amended only by a regulation adopted in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure. this amendment is of a technical nature and is the result of a change in the legislation of poland. the commission examined whether the request of poland fulfilled the requirements of the regulation and submitted a proposal to the european parliament and the council to ensure that the scope of the re-established regulation will be aligned with the polish insolvency legal framework at the time of its application. in this respect, the commission's proposal is purely technical and does not contain any substantial amendment to the regulation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion because it is a technical text which simply extends existing legislation in this area to all member states.
in writing. ‒ this regulation adds to regulation (eu) 2015/848 of the european parliament and of the council on insolvency proceedings an amendment to the list of insolvency proceedings. this is the result of a request by poland after it had carried out a substantial reform of its national law on restructuring. the problem was that national proceedings could only be classified as insolvency proceedings if they were listed in annex a to the regulation. the commission has also included two amendments to the commission proposal under protocol no 21 on the position of the united kingdom and ireland in respect of the area of freedom, security and justice and one on the entry into force of the amending regulation. i am voting in favour of these amendments because they are purely technical and bring greater clarity.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of extending the eu-uzbekistan association agreement to bilateral textile trade, having seen that our rejection of it five years ago had the desired impact. in 2011, on the initiative of the socialists, the european parliament rejected the eu-uzbekistan textile protocol, until the country demonstrated progress on human rights and labour standards. today, the european union (eu) and the international labour organization (ilo) have reported clear progress in the required direction. among other measures, the uzbek government has taken the required steps to eradicate child labour - previously systematic and now almost non-existent in cotton fields - and to promote trade union dialogue, cooperates with the ilo under the decent work programme and has authorised international monitoring of cotton crops, further proof that the union's trade policy, accompanied by an appropriate external dialogue, is a key tool for the promotion of human rights and labour standards in the world. the socialists have also called on the commission to develop accompanying measures and an effective traceability mechanism for the textile sector.
in writing. i have rejected this proposal to accept an agreement seeking to deepen imports of textile products from uzbekistan into the union. the union is once again ignoring human rights with this agreement and legitimising as an economic partner a country where slavery, forced labour in the cotton fields and child labour exist. with this agreement, the union is once again ignoring human rights and is once again merely acting as an ambassador for the interests of the transnational textile companies and their multi-billion dollar profits, which are obtained by perpetuating labour exploitation and dumping.
in writing. ‒ i voted against giving consent to the signing of the protocol extending the provisions of the eu-uzbekistan cooperation and partnership agreement to the textile sector. we appreciate that since parliament postponed a decision on the acp in 2011, significant improvements have been made on the ground: not only have ilo missions been allowed in uzbekistan, but they have also shown very positive developments, especially in the eradication of child labour. however, the situation in the textile sector in uzbekistan is far from reaching the minimum level of labour and social guarantees which we consider essential for the approval of this agreement. both the ilo and other observers warn of the systematic use of forced labour in the sector. this is reason enough for us to oppose the union granting advantages to this sector, since such advantages would only encourage the increase in production and, with it, these practices.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur, mrs arena, for her work on this report on the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european communities and uzbekistan and bilateral trade in textile products. we fully support the work of the ilo to eliminate forced labour in the country once and for all and also that, should the uzbek authorities suspend their commitment to abolish forced labour, parliament reserves the right to ask the european commission and the council to activate articles 2 and 95 of the cwc to take general or specific measures for human rights violations.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, whose vote i asked to be postponed, because i believe that there are not enough guarantees that the minimum social standards (including ilo standards) necessary to address a bilateral textile trade agreement are being applied.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of the protocol amending the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european union and uzbekistan aims to extend the provisions of the agreement to trade in textile products, thereby bringing the textile sector within the scope of the 1999 partnership and cooperation agreement (pca). in 2011, the european parliament expressed its view that the conclusion of an agreement should be linked to an improvement in the human rights situation and working conditions in uzbekistan. since then the international labour organization has been closely monitoring conditions in the country. it concludes that child labour has been eradicated although doubts remain about forced labour in the textile sector. i voted in favour of the conclusion of this protocol because it favours the improvement of working conditions. in the event that the country suspends its commitment to abolish forced labour, we will undoubtedly have to activate suspension measures.
in writing. ‒ i have rejected this proposal to accept an agreement seeking to deepen imports of textile products from uzbekistan into the union. the union is once again ignoring human rights with this agreement and legitimising as an economic partner a country where slavery, forced labour in the cotton fields and child labour exist. with this agreement, the union is once again ignoring human rights and is once again merely acting as an ambassador for the interests of the transnational textile companies and their multi-billion dollar profits, which are obtained by perpetuating labour exploitation and dumping.
in writing. ‒ i voted against giving consent to the signing of the protocol extending the provisions of the eu-uzbekistan cooperation and partnership agreement to the textile sector. we appreciate that since parliament postponed a decision on the acp in 2011, significant improvements have been made on the ground: not only have ilo missions been allowed in uzbekistan, but they have also shown very positive developments, especially in the eradication of child labour. however, the situation in the textile sector in uzbekistan is far from reaching the minimum level of labour and social guarantees which we consider essential for the approval of this agreement. both the ilo and other observers warn of the systematic use of forced labour in the sector. this is reason enough for us to oppose the union granting advantages to this sector, since such advantages would only encourage the increase in production and, with it, these practices.
in writing. – i voted against, because this consent procedure should have been initiated after december, when the ilo report on the 2016 cotton harvest will be available. one of the conditions included in the interim report that the european parliament adopted in 2011 included the need to eradicate child labour and other forms of forced labour. even though there has been considerable progress in the eradication of child labour, the same result is likely to not have been achieved regarding forced labour. this is why the independent ilo assessment is a key tool to evaluate the possibility of giving our consent to this protocol.
in writing. ‒ this proposal aims to include the textile sector in uzbekistan in the scope of the 1999 cooperation and partnership agreement, since article 16 of the agreement excluded the textile sector from most-favoured-nation treatment obligations and the prohibition of quantitative restrictions, which apply to other sectors. this proposal can fill the gap left by uzbekistan's non-membership of the world trade organisation, as until it joins the wto it will not be bound by the most favoured nation clause and the multilateral rules which apply to all wto members. this report follows several years of efforts by the authorities to eradicate child labour, supported by a 2015 research report that reveals the virtual elimination of the practice and welcomes the measures taken to achieve this (out-of-school care, fines for promoters, and increased levels of accountability for parents, teachers and farmers...), which have resulted in the use of child labour being considered a socially unacceptable practice. i therefore consider it appropriate to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. i have rejected this resolution accompanying the agreement with uzbekistan as it legitimizes an agreement that i reject and washes its hands of human rights by focusing on the existence of a clause that allows its freezing in case of violation of human rights. in other words, an agreement with a country with flagrant human rights violations, such as forced labour or child exploitation, is justified by the fact that it will be frozen if human rights are violated.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the accompanying resolution because, although i agree with most of its points, the rapporteur draws the opposite conclusion, based on the diagnosis i share: that the european parliament should give its consent to the signing of the protocol extending the provisions of the eu-uzbekistan cooperation and partnership agreement to the textile sector. the report expresses concern that forced labour is still a common practice in the textile sector in uzbekistan. i share the rapporteur's view of the progress that has been made in the country and i support the request in the resolution that the commission should present as soon as possible the union's flagship initiative on responsible supply chain management in the textile sector. however, i do not share the main purpose of this resolution, which is to support a consent procedure with which i do not agree.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this resolution on the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european communities and uzbekistan and bilateral trade in textile products. following today's vote in favour of the agreement, this resolution underlines the importance of the measures taken by the government of uzbekistan to authorise the ilo to monitor the cotton harvest and to cooperate with the ilo under a decent work programme for each country.

madam president, i have asked to speak to explain the vote in favour of the agreement with ecuador because i think it is very important that the european parliament has approved this agreement so that ecuador can be incorporated into the agreement with colombia and peru. we are doing a great favor to ecuador and its people with this agreement. i do not see why we should oppose free trade with a country which can export a lot to europe and which can benefit the people of ecuador. ecuador is doing a very modern transformation of their country, and these exports of their products are key for them. we have worked very hard with them, we have ensured that banana exports do not harm other countries, in particular spain and the canary islands, and we have ensured that the relationship between europe and latin america through this new agreement is intensified and improved, something which i think is very important for europe too.
in writing. ‒ i have supported ecuador's accession to the european union's trade agreement with colombia and peru, whereby the union will continue the tariff preferences it has granted to ecuador until now and which, by becoming a middle-income country, it would have lost in january, burdening the exports of many people in this country. the socialists welcome the fact that this agreement includes ambitious commitments, unprecedented between the union and ecuador, in the field of sustainable development, human rights, labour and the environment, which should serve to promote fairer bilateral trade. in this respect, ecuador has already been undertaking some good reforms, which under the agreement should continue. we have also worked very hard with ecuador to ensure that its export capacity in the banana sector does not harm european regions which, like the canary islands, are very dependent on this crop. the agreement will undoubtedly help to intensify and improve the relationship between europe and latin america, as we spanish socialists advocate. we will monitor very closely the implementation of the commitments and support ecuador in its reforms, with all the instruments at the disposal of the union.
in writing. i voted against ecuador's accession to the eu-colombia/peru multi-party trade agreement on the understanding that there are no substantial changes in an agreement that is still based on the logic of free trade, deregulation, privatization or exploitation of natural resources. i opposed the eu-colombia/peru agreement and i still reject it. our model of relations is not free trade agreements which ignore economic asymmetries and seek only to open up new markets and benefits to multinational companies, but agreements based on complementarity, cooperation, sustainable and sustainable development and which have as their central objective the elimination of inequalities. we reject the blackmail to which the union subjects third countries through its current tariff policies and the conditionality of development cooperation funds linked to the signing of trade agreements such as this one. we support the policies of the government of ecuador for the development of the 'good living' model based on greater state control of strategic sectors of the economy, but we consider that social achievements would not have been possible under the logic established by this agreement.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which is in line with my position on ecuador's accession to the eu trade agreement with colombia and peru. i believe that in the current global context the union must strengthen its relations with latin america, being a preferential and reliable partner contributing to the economic and social progress of the region.
in writing. ‒ it is undeniable that the decline in oil prices and the appreciation of the dollar makes the economic and political situation in ecuador complicated. in this context, the loss of tariff preferences threatens ecuador's economy in the short term and also the electoral victory of the emancipatory project in february. however, while i understand the short-term interest of the ecuadorian government in getting the oxygen balloon that is the non-increase in tariffs on its exports, the agreement contains harmful elements in the long term because it could lay the foundations for an unequal trade relationship. in addition, with this agreement the union is once again promoting a system in which the basis is laid for trade to the benefit of the usual, which i will not defend in any case. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i have supported ecuador's accession to the european union's trade agreement with colombia and peru, whereby the union will continue the tariff preferences it has granted to ecuador until now and which, by becoming a middle-income country, it would have lost in january, burdening the exports of many people in this country. the socialists welcome the fact that this agreement includes ambitious commitments, unprecedented between the union and ecuador, in the field of sustainable development, human rights, labour and the environment, which should serve to promote fairer bilateral trade. in this respect, ecuador has already been undertaking some good reforms, which under the agreement should continue. we have also worked very hard with ecuador to ensure that its export capacity in the banana sector does not harm european regions which, like the canary islands, are very dependent on this crop. the agreement will undoubtedly help to intensify and improve the relationship between europe and latin america, as we spanish socialists advocate. we will monitor very closely the implementation of the commitments and support ecuador in its reforms, with all the instruments at the disposal of the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted against ecuador's accession to the eu-colombia/peru multipartite trade agreement, as i believe that there are no substantial changes in an agreement that is still based on the logic of free trade, deregulation, privatization or exploitation of natural resources. we opposed this eu-colombia/peru agreement and we continue to reject it. our model of relations is not free trade agreements which ignore economic asymmetries and seek only to open up new markets and benefits to multinational companies, but agreements based on complementarity, cooperation, sustainable and sustainable development and which have as their central objective the elimination of inequalities. we reject the blackmail to which the union subjects third countries through its current tariff policies and the conditionality of development cooperation funds linked to the signing of trade agreements such as this one. we support the policies of the government of ecuador for the development of the 'good living' model based on greater state control of strategic sectors of the economy, but we consider that social achievements would not have been possible under the logic established by this agreement.
in writing. ‒ a trade agreement was signed between the eu, colombia and peru in 2012. the council proposes that the european parliament include ecuador in the list. fisheries and agricultural products would thus be exported to the union with very low customs duties. dependent on oil exports, whose price has fallen sharply, and victim of a severe earthquake that has caused thousands of victims, ecuador is in a delicate economic situation. the earthquake is expected to cost reconstruction about 3% of gdp. this reconstruction certainly offers opportunities for the european giants of the btp. however, the country is no longer sovereign over its currency, as the us dollar is legal tender. the extra-territoriality of the dollar means that the markets conquered will be subject to american laws, which are regularly used to weaken our industrial leaders. the extension of the trade agreement to ecuador will also threaten our dom, whose banana exports to the eu will be strongly competitive. the agreement also risks placing local economic players in a very difficult situation (competition from more competitive european players), even as the country has to rebuild after this natural disaster. i therefore voted against this proposal.
in writing. ‒ it is undeniable that the decline in oil prices and the appreciation of the dollar makes the economic and political situation in ecuador complicated. in this context, the loss of tariff preferences threatens ecuador's economy in the short term and also the electoral victory of the emancipatory project in february. however, while i understand the short-term interest of the ecuadorian government in getting the oxygen balloon that is the non-increase in tariffs on its exports, the agreement contains harmful elements in the long term because it could lay the foundations for an unequal trade relationship. in addition, with this agreement the union is once again promoting a system in which the basis is laid for trade to the benefit of the usual, which i will not defend in any case. that is why i abstained.

in writing. ‒ ecuador's entry into this free trade agreement is proof of how europe uses trade treaties to force developing countries to be integrated in a peripheral way into world trade. by signing a trade agreement with colombia and peru, an agreement that has had very negative effects in terms of labor rights, land grabbing and productive dismantling of these countries, exports from ecuador were diverted, which in this way was pushed to sign this agreement to avoid a balance of payments crisis. however, the effects of this agreement will be very negative in the long term also for ecuador and that is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ parliament approves the accession of ecuador to the trade agreement between the european union and colombia and peru, concluded in 2012. at the moment, ecuador is in a difficult situation, stemming from the sharp fall in oil prices, the appreciation of the us dollar, the depreciation of other currencies and the tragic earthquake of magnitude 7.8 that occurred in april of this year. that is why accession to this trade agreement could be very beneficial for a faster recovery of the country. throughout the accession negotiations, the will to include ecuador has been evident. in november 2015, parliament adopted a resolution welcoming the opening of negotiations with ecuador and encouraging a swift entry into force of the accession. i am voting in favour because i believe that the agreement will enable ecuador to continue along the lines of policies of stimulus in the field of sustainable economic and social development.
in writing. ‒ the trade agreement between the european union and colombia and peru was signed on 26 june 2012. article 329 of the trade agreement provides for the possibility of accession to the agreement by other andean community countries. the union and ecuador therefore concluded the negotiations for such accession on 17 july 2014. ecuador is currently going through a very complicated economic situation, which is added to the terrible earthquake that recently hit the country and which at the end of the year will lose its preferential status of spg+. it is urgent that the trade agreement should enter into force as soon as possible. the economic, cooperative and friendly relations between ecuador and spain have always been fruitful and my support for this recommendation is part of my wish that their effects should be extended to the union.

in writing. – i voted against the ecuador accession for the main reasons my political group voted against the trade agreement in 2012, as the text has not changed. in addition, those sectors in the ecuadorian government which were responsible for the ecuadoran ‘buen vivir’ model, as well as environmental ngos, opposed this accession until today. with the fta accession, indigenous people, small farmers, environmentalists and grassroots activists fear a return to the previous resource depletion model, while the ‘buen vivir’ model had guaranteed them better redistribution of wealth, access to schools and health systems and a strong decrease of poverty rates. these factors were highly praised by cepal (un economic commission for latin america). national researchers and activists saw the ecuadorian model as a path to follow, which would lead away from dependence on mono-cultural exploitation. if they had voted in favour of the accession, it would have meant abandoning their support for the attempt to create a different economic model in a peripheral country. an additional strong argument against accession is that the agreement is fundamentally unchanged and is still open to tax dodging and money laundering. in the short run, export companies will win, of course. however, globally, labour rights in this sector are not said to be the best.
in writing. ‒ we are talking about an agreement that has been voted on in parallel with the safeguard clause and the banana stabilization mechanism. the trade agreement will thus not only bring economic benefits to the parties involved, but will also help to prevent the agreement's threshold for this product from being exceeded without action, as the new mechanism will include an early warning system which will oblige the european commission to formally alert parliament and the council in writing when banana import volumes reach 80% of the envisaged import thresholds. i therefore think it is appropriate to vote in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which stresses that access to the internal market of any third country must be based on reciprocity, and that in the case of norway's customs duties on food products, including fishery products, from the union must be in accordance with the agreement on the european economic area. the report calls on the commission to forward to the european parliament the minutes and conclusions of the consultations and a full report before the renewal of the negotiations. it also called on the commission and the council to keep parliament fully informed immediately at all stages of the procedures relating to the agreement and its renewal, as provided for in article 13 (2) of the treaty on european union and article 218 (10) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it implies consent to an agreement on the shared management of fishery resources in the skagerrak and the kattegat. these two straits are what separate the waters of the baltic from the waters of the north sea, this is a fishing zone where fishermen traditionally follow the fish shoals independent of the border line of the countries involved. as this is a fishing area shared with norway, it is the union's competence to develop such agreements with third countries. as this is an agreement to allow traditional fishing methods and to respect the principles of reciprocity and sustainability in these areas, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the skagerrak sea area has traditionally been a fishing area shared between norway, denmark and sweden. i voted in favour of continuing reciprocal access for these countries.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the new agreement on fishing activities in the skagerrak, the fishing zone between the north sea and the baltic sea. this agreement concerns two member states, denmark and sweden, and one third country, norway. it extends a 1966 convention, which was made necessary for practical reasons because this very limited area is at the confluence of the maritime areas of these states. norway has denounced this old convention in order to sign a new agreement better adapted to developments in fisheries law. the 1982 united nations convention on the law of the sea and the 1995 united nations fish stocks agreement have changed the game. the new agreement guarantees the maintenance of reciprocal access of the two member states concerned and norway to their respective waters in the skagerrak area. it also allows the implementation of fisheries conservation and management measures in this area. it also allows for the adoption of control measures in accordance with the principles of the normal jurisdiction of the coastal state.

in writing. ‒ the new reciprocal fisheries access agreement in the skagerrak and kattegat replaces the 1966 agreement, which had been extended until 2012. the former agreement, according to norway, was not in line with the existing provisions of the law of the sea, nor with the principles of the normal jurisdiction of the coastal state, nor with modern principles of conservation and management. all this was taken into account in the negotiations between the commission and norway which resulted in this agreement which, in addition to complying with the provisions and principles mentioned, maintains exclusive access for vessels of denmark, norway and sweden to the waters beyond four nautical miles from the baselines, while respecting the historical fishing rights in this area. i support the agreement because it will be beneficial for the common fisheries policy.

in writing. i voted against this agreement between georgia and the european agency europol on operational and strategic cooperation. i am opposed to this because i am in favour of extending the scope of europol's activities, and my position is against the existence of this agency, which does not act with the transparency and the guarantees required by an institution of this kind. serious concerns have been expressed about the lack of political or judicial accountability to which europol is subject. in addition, the lack of clarity on the issue of the exchange of sensitive data, including personal data, of european citizens with third countries is something that is impossible to approve, since the protection of personal data and the rights of citizens are at stake. on the other hand, from a geopolitical point of view, this agreement with georgia is part of the union's strategy of straining relations with russia, which i oppose, because i consider this neighbour to be a strategic and necessary partner.
in writing. ‒ the proposal refers to the approval of the conclusion of an agreement between georgia and europol on operational and strategic cooperation. as was the case in the november part-session with the proposal for a similar agreement with ukraine (although the chapter on the exchange of personal data is not included in this case), georgia, in addition to being a player in the geopolitical game between the union, the usa and russia, is still a country that is far from meeting the standards required by the eu's human rights legislation, a criterion which our group takes very much into account when approving any cooperation agreement. the european parliament has also voted for a new regulation for europol which will come into force next year, in which cooperation agreements will be established by a much more transparent procedure than the current one. there is no reason to rush into an agreement with a country which does not have sufficient democratic and legal guarantees. i therefore voted against.

in writing. this report concerns the contribution of the egf to individual support measures for the reintegration into employment of 250 workers made redundant at the bosal plant in sagunto, of which 25% will be direct income support measures and the rest training and job-replacement activities. these measures cannot in any way replace the need to develop an industrial policy to enable the economy of this region, with unemployment above 25%, to recover from this closure. nor do they exempt bosal from its liability in this particular case, when instead of using the subsidies received and the profits from its activity to invest in its plant, it decapitalised the company in a probably irregular manner. but at least they provide help for unemployed men and women, and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which calls for compensation funds and measures to encourage job-seeking in cases of relocation or closure of businesses due to globalisation. the aim of the project is to help workers who have been made redundant in the region of sagunto, which is already suffering from industrial restructuring and high unemployment. these are measures which, if they were not taken, would leave the workers concerned in a worse position. the vote in favour, however, does not hide our concern about the legal proceedings opened for alleged unfair management of the company and that these funds are used to make up for the relocation of companies that are profitable. we believe, as we have said in our amendments, that the globalisation adjustment funds should be set up in accordance with reindustrialisation strategies, with measures to support workers affected by restructuring due to the unfeasibility of production, with a greater share of public investment that makes the productive sectors of the regions concerned sustainable, contributing to changing the production model and guaranteeing the future of the productive sectors.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is a solidarity-based fund at a time when industries and the economy are facing some of the adverse effects of globalisation. with the economic crisis many of our companies and sectors have been forced to close. in other cases they have succumbed to the benefits of relocation to third countries. on this occasion we voted to grant €856 800 of european funds to 250 workers in the automotive sector of the valencian community who lost their jobs between june 2015 and march 2016. my vote and support are with the workers concerned, although i take this opportunity to ask that these funds be linked to the reindustrialisation of the affected areas and the re-training of their workers.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this proposal is to repeal council regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. this regulation authorizes member states to compensate railway undertakings for the costs of obligations which other transport undertakings do not have to bear. this is the case for compensation for accidents at work in this sector and for compensation for accidents at work in other transport sectors, which are paid by the state. however, this regulation does not respect the current legal environment, as it was drawn up in a context where there was a much more direct relationship between governments and railway undertakings and therefore the list of the regulation contains a list of state ownership, which has had to be extended to include the new member states. i am voting in favour of this because, in addition to being legally outdated, it discriminates between companies which are included in that list and those which are not.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of repealing this regulation on common rules for the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings because it was completely out of date. however, a transitional period is provided for level crossing facilities, as some member states continue to rely on this regulation for compensation for certain obligations that other transport sectors do not have.

in writing. ‒ this regulation repeals the regulation on common rules for the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings, which was adopted when organisations providing railway services fulfilled certain public sector responsibilities and has become obsolete. however, it is still used, in particular for the compensation of costs relating to the installation of level crossings. this justifies a transitional period for the compensation of those costs and for the adjustment of national legislation and administrative mechanisms to the new framework. all this with a view to the effective implementation of the system to be introduced, as this report advocates. i am confident that this amendment will adapt the present system to the modern organization of the railway sector, and i have voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ we have tabled an amendment rejecting this amendment and several amendments to the substance against this amendment to the regulation, which requires the management of lines operated under public service contracts, subsidised with public funds, to be put to tender. i understand that there was no reason to amend this text, which until now allowed each member state, according to its own needs, to choose which contracts it wants to open to public tender and which contracts it awards directly to the national public operator. we have also echoed the demands of trade unions throughout europe for the serious lack of protection for workers in cases of change of operator after a new contract. the only objective pursued by this new text is the obligation to ensure open competition between all operators potentially present on the market, competition which is likely to take place at the expense of public funds, essential elements of the public service and working conditions. i therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution rejecting the report.

in writing. ‒ through this agreement, public authorities retain a margin to define public service obligations in the railway area, which must be consistent with strategic transport objectives. the text includes the principle of proportionality, which is already enshrined in the community acquis. from an economic point of view, the new rules contain a number of provisions which seek to strike a balance between efficiency in the provision of the service and ensuring the long-term economic viability of the responsible undertakings. for all these reasons, and with the ultimate aim of helping to increase the efficiency and competitiveness of rail transport services in the union, i have supported this agreement by voting in favour.

madam president, i voted in favour of this motion. i think this is exactly the example of the european union showing that it makes sense. because the liberalisation of railways, the possibility for individual national carriers to carry out their business and services in other countries, that is to say to use the rail transport infrastructure in other countries of the european union, will only lead to transport services being more efficient and cheaper for the citizen. i'm a liberal on this issue. i am a little disappointed that some of the steps in this package will not be available until 2023, when individual carriers will be able to apply for public tenders in individual member states of the european union. i think it could have been a lot earlier. the package also contains a number of exceptions whereby the owner of a transport infrastructure will not be forced to let a foreign carrier onto its infrastructure. so going forward, it's going to take some of the problems to be removed and to liberalize the space even more.
madam president, i voted against the fourth railway package because it responds to the european commission's repeated interests in dismantling the public railway system in europe since the 1990s. in particular, the governance part sets out the obligation to open rail services to privatisation and to design a completely fragmented system. we know the disastrous consequences of rail liberalization because the united kingdom experienced them in the 1990s. free competition did not lead to improved quality of service and competitive prices but to higher prices, abandonment of infrastructure, increased insecurity and accidents, and economic bankruptcy, as well as deteriorating working conditions, to the point that the state was forced to renationalize and rescue some of the lines. we are therefore clearly committed to rail as a public service, as a mechanism for territorial integration and social development and as a more efficient and sustainable means of transport at the service of people.
madam president, what thatcher did not dare to do, this parliament will do: completely privatize the railway sector. if there is any doubt, the present european union is to the right of the most radical neoliberalism. the promotion of railways requires the integration of the territory with conventional railways, the promotion of affordable prices and the coherent planning of infrastructure. this is the only way to ensure that rail is an attractive option for the mobility of people and for the transport of goods. only a public railway can ensure decent work for railway workers and a safe infrastructure for all. what the european union will achieve, on the contrary, is to destroy the regional railway and to eliminate all lines except the most profitable ones; that private operators exploit workers and abuse travellers. let the train, in short, return to the 19th century.
in writing. as with the van de camp report, i have supported the withdrawal of the text. in this case, the regulations and control mechanisms are created to facilitate the liberalization and privatization of the railway sector with the resulting higher prices, less safety, lack of planning, reduction in the weight of the conventional train (especially in less populated regions) and precariousness of working conditions, with the recurrent intervention of public authorities to rescue the private companies that will be sharing the cake.
in writing. ‒ we have tabled a rejection amendment and several amendments of substance against this amendment to the directive which aims to make it compulsory to open up rail passenger services to private operators, through a system whereby any operator can provide rail services by renting the tracks on a given section and schedule. this reform, combined with the amendment to the public service regulation voted just before, is a waste of time both in terms of the coherence of the rail network as a whole (universal accessibility, promotion of social and territorial cohesion, etc.) and in terms of coordination and control in the field of safety. we already know the consequences where this liberalisation has been applied (the united kingdom, for example) and they have been disastrous in terms of worsening frequency and quality of service, price increases and serious safety failures. we will continue to oppose this market model and defend a public railway that serves the needs of citizens in each territory. i therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution rejecting the report.

in writing. ‒ the present proposal aims to establish a single european railway area, as regards the opening of the market for national rail passenger services and the governance of railway infrastructure. the success of the fourth railway package is beyond doubt. increased competition translates into a greater attractiveness of railways compared to other modes of transport. we can also take the opportunity to develop high-speed passenger transport, contributing to the achievement of climate change objectives. i am voting in favour of this because it will contribute to greater competitiveness in services, which will greatly benefit passengers, as they will enjoy more services of higher quality.

in writing. – i voted against the single european railway area proposal because the door is left open to ruthless competition between the cheapest providers, with little regard for quality of service. an opportunity to level the playing field between different modes of transport has been missed. while member states can introduce tolls on their roads if they see fit, member states are obliged to charge a fee for every kilometre on every track they use.
in writing. ‒ this directive is a further step in opening up domestic passenger transport services in order to increase the quantity and improve their quality and efficiency. it addresses the governance of railway infrastructure management with the aim of ensuring equal access to the companies concerned, allowing for the possibility of both separate and holding structures, and including the reversibility of the model chosen. in this way, it regulates potential conflicts of interest that may arise for those who have to make management decisions and seeks to eliminate any possibility of cross-subsidisation by enhancing the transparency of financial flows. it also introduces provisions on the crossborder coordination of infrastructure management, emphasising the role of regulators, who become guarantors of the application of the rules on conflicts of interest and financial transparency. finally, it includes points on information and transport tickets which aim to pave the way towards a multimodal passenger transport system. i therefore considered it appropriate to vote in favour of the text.

in writing. despite the commission's intention to use this legislative initiative to liberalise and privatise the european port sector, the negotiations between parliament and the member states have allowed the text to become, on the contrary, a mechanism to preserve working conditions in the sector and strengthen its rights to collective bargaining or in the event of transfer of the operating service. however, some of its provisions could be used to fragment the public management of the port system by accounting separately for those segments that could be opened to private competition. i have decided to abstain on the basis of the text as a whole.
in writing. ‒ this report on port services began with a liberalising proposal by the european commission which we strongly oppose. however, during the negotiations it was possible to turn the proposal around, omit the clauses on liberalisation and protect the rights of port workers. it is a satisfactory result that we do not usually see in the reforms of european transport legislation. however, i have decided to abstain because the final text calls for the promotion of decentralised management of ports, whereas in a country with a strong maritime sector such as ours, centralised management of the port network is one of the key elements of the system. although this decentralisation is not a matter of obligation, we wanted to be consistent with our position that each member state should be able to choose its own model of public administration, in accordance with its own trajectory and specificities.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr fleckenstein, for his work on this report, in which he puts forward a few amendments concerning port autonomy. i do not agree with the agreement reached on this point, but in line with the rest of the text, i voted in favour of the agreement with the council and therefore of the report.
in writing. ‒ the agreement reached with the council at first reading substantially changes the initial proposal submitted by the commission, by ensuring that ports can limit the number of operators on the basis of a multitude of criteria (public service obligations, safety or environmental concerns, etc.). the agreement also requires greater transparency of financial flows between public authorities and ports in order to detect situations of unfair competition between ports and covert state aid. in addition, the text has been substantially improved with measures such as the exclusion from the regulation of categories such as piloting, provisions on social dialogue and the reinforcement of staff subrogation obligations in the event of a change of port operator, while recognising the possibility of fixing fees for the use of port infrastructure by law, as is the case in spain. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i am disappointed with the outcome of this compromise at the end of trilogue negotiations because in the end the status quo in the port system in my country, catalonia, won’t change. in fact with this outcome, spain like other member states can and will maintain its centralised system of port management, avoiding therefore fair competition among ports in spain. this absence of real change, real reform, will be to the detriment of competition: therefore no reduction of prices for consumers, the companies using the ports. the result is less efficiency in port management as there is no autonomy de facto. the port of barcelona would very much like to compete with other ports of the mediterranean and of northern europe on an equal footing. with the current regulations, it is impossible. the port of barcelona is already connected and chosen as part of the core network in the ten-t program. it could really become a gateway for the european single market but spain will never allow it, it will never give it real autonomy. the centralised system in spain is constructed with disguised state aid to non-efficient ports.

in writing. ‒ this regulation aims to increase transparency in the financial relationship between the state, ports and their service operators. the text makes it possible to make the organisation of port services subject to minimum requirements for their provision, limitations on the number of providers, public service obligations and other restrictions on in-house operators. as regards the challenges facing labour relations in ports, it is committed to jointly developing provisions that improve everything from worker conditions to environmental health issues or the required vocational qualifications. the ultimate objective is, broadly speaking, to remove restrictions on the provision of port services and to increase transparency in port financing. i am convinced that this regulation will contribute to a better use of public funds and to a fairer and more effective application of the union's competition rules in ports, so i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the fica (fund for coal and steel research) is an important programme to make the coal and steel industries cleaner and more efficient. the fica programme provides around €50 million of funding annually for r & d and innovation in the coal and steel sectors. the new legal framework of horizon 2020, the union's research and innovation programme (2014-2020), requires a revision of the multiannual guidelines for the fica. this revision of the fica programme management rules harmonises the procedures and concepts used for horizon 2020 in order to facilitate the participation of the same beneficiaries in both programmes (fica and horizon 2020). the programme also aims to finance research activities in the bio-industry for the capture and management of co2 from coal, helping and supporting the sustainability of the sector and the economy of the regions that live off the exploitation of these materials.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of this report on the approval of the research programme of the research fund for coal and steel, because this amendment improves the operating rules of the fund. this research fund is a fundamental tool for the long-term functioning and viability of the coal and steel industries. this report includes provisions for the evaluation and follow-up of projects financed by the fund. i believe that both industries are fundamental to industrial activity and the energy transition of our production model and that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
